history.text: Its a morality play basically. The dialogue is so simple and obvious that this movie clearly was not intended for adults. It might be a good movie for kids up to the age of 8-10, but even older children are likely to see it as so obvious they would be bored by it. There are several subplots running: cruel rich rancher trying to expel an Indian family from his land; same rich rancher despises his preacher turned rancher son-in-law; his grandson befriends the boy in the Indian family the rancher despises, and his other grandson become critically ill. Somehow all of the evil running through these subplots is defeated - the assassination attempt on the half Indian father fails and he miraculously survives a deadly fall and even walks home after losing his horse, the two boys who are friends are saved from a wolf by the stray dog one of them has befriended and are miraculously found in the high plains late at night by the ex-minister son-in-law, the old Indian grandfather saves the life of the ill grandson who is near death with some magic native medicine, and the embittered rancher who caused much of the tragedy suddenly loses all of his bitterness and invites the Indian family he tried to destroy to Christmas dinner with his now highly respected son-in-law and everybody lives happily thereafter. Its as if Santa Claus, the tooth fairy, and the Easter Bunny all turn out to be real and all appear in the flesh at the same time! The actors in the movie did a credible job, making a valiant attempt with a script that would be expected to be seen on a Saturday AM children's show.

It a perception of a perception of a perception. The cover picture, as others have pointed out, is not Nat Turner, but Frederic Douglass. I think there is too much about Styron's book and not enough about the event itself. Whereas, it may be true that we know very little about Turner himself, and what we do know may not be true as it was originally presented by a white man with his own motives, we do know what happened. We know who was killed, how they were killed, and where they were killed. We know what the reaction of the white slave owning south was. We know what the conditions were for most black slaves in the South before and after the event. Rather than indulge in a back and forth about whether Turner himself was a madman - which whites prefer, or a revolutionary hero - which African Americans prefer, I would have preferred more history about the event itself. Was there much reaction in the North? Did it help bring more support for the abolitionist movement? How did it fit into the centuries' long struggle by African Americans for their freedom? Why did it fail whereas a decade long slave revolt in Haiti succeeded more than three decades earlier?

history.review_title: War is Hell - as told by those who lived that Hell at Kapyeong.
history.text: An excellent documentary. Very objective, very realistic. First, as an American, it is unusual that anything but American bravery ever is exemplified in war movies. I realize this is a documentary, and not a movie - but it is extremely well balanced. The compliments paid to the Chinese soldiers are also quite refreshing compared to the American genre about this war. I liked the personal interviews with the soldiers and officers on both sides. The "human wave" Chinese attacks were substantially overstated in most American historical accounts, and in fact, the Chinese military deaths were over estimated by a factor of ten for almost 5 decades. Yes, in key battles in selective circumstances, the Chinese amassed men in overwhelming numbers at key choke points. However, the myth of millions of Chinese soldiers screaming towards American lines is largely that - a myth. However, in this battle - as real. The Chinese had no air cover, no armor, and essentially no artillery. In fact, as was stated in this documentary some their soldiers did not even have arms - they used the arms of comrades fallen in battle. As the Chinese officer said - we didn't have all of those bombs - we had to fight a different way. The mistakes of Commonwealth officers, and the courage of those who bore the brunt of those mistakes is a refreshing honesty that, I am sure, took the passage of time to be told. But, it is a key contribution to this documentary. The personal accounts of the horror experienced is moving - and should make all of us consider strongly before supporting the choice of war. Hence - the title of my review "War is Hell - as told by those who lived in that Hell."

A wonderful story, highly romanticized, about one of the greatest artists of the Dutch Golden Age. Scarlett Johannsson's portrayal of the young servant girls is near perfect - in fact when you look at Vermeer's portrayal of such women (The Milkmaid for example), she is as much that subject in his painting as she is the Girl with the Pearl Earring. Vermeer was exceptionally kind and respectful to women in his paintings, given his era. Yes, he has one of a brothel scene, and he has three others that imply the seduction of a servant girl, but it is possible (as hinted in this movie) that he painted those themes to please the sponsor of a painting. Vermeer painted at least 35 paintings - women appeared in 33 of them, and appeared as the sole subjects in 28 of them. No other painter of his era, in France, Italy, Austria, - anywhere - painted more than 30% of their sole subjects as women. And so many of his paintings show women in quiet, reflective moments - indicating a respect for their private thoughts and concerns. The growing sexual awareness of the maid Greit (Johannson) in this movie parallels the sexual tension between the pretty young servant girl and her master. It does make a great movie plot, but in all of my studies of Vermeer and his paintings - consummation is unlikely to have occurred, and she was not likely the model for his most famous painting. The most likely model for this painting was his precocious thirteen year old daughter. I respect the movie greatly because they did not allow either character to sink into a tawdry sexual desire. The young maid was flattered to be painted, and wanted so much to be the object of her master's brush. Vermeer, seems in the end, in his unwillingness to support her - to have gotten what he wanted. The perfect model for a masterpiece. I loved this movie - I like sex scenes in movies - but that this director left it out is one of the strongest reasons for this being a great movie.

history.review_title: Some nice adventures, nice scenery, but not a lot of meaning
history.text: I give this three stars because some of it is 5 stars and some of it is one star. I enjoyed the scenery and the adventure scenes. I got a bit tired of the out of sequence flashbacks, and of his unwillingness to establish any kind of meaningful connection with anyone he met. If Penn meant to portray McCandless as a fearless adventurer who discovers the true meaning of life by giving up all of the privilege that he was born with, he failed to convince me. Google his name and find a documentary about his sister and two half sisters visiting the bus in which he died to learn a lot more about who McCandless really was. That documentary did not enhance his heroism to me, but it did reveal there was a lot more pain there than Penn managed to communicate in the movie. It also verified that he was in many ways, quite selfish and vain. I found the movie to drag in places, especially in the meaningless (to him) relationships he gets involved in - or rather refuses to get involved in. They all end the same way - people take to him, are friendly and helpful to him, and some even feel an emotional connection. He gives nothing in return except some platitudes about the meaning of life, and shares nothing about himself. He refuses advice - well he knows the meaning of life - why should he listen to these people who are willing to accept the "traps they are in" and just work for a living? He cannot even give hope to the woman who befriends him and plaintively wonders if she will see her son again. A simple white lie that he would contact his own mother someday would have given her comfort. He does not say it. He cannot give any real sense of worth to the young girl who is so hungry for affection, intimacy, appreciation that she throws herself sexually at him. Yes, it admirable that he does not take advantage of her that way, but he cant give her any affection, any sense of self worth that she so needs. A warm hug, stroke her hair, touch her face, utter some compliments about her, etc would have meant much more to her than sex anyway. Instead all he can do is spout out his "meaning of life" quotes. He dies within 8 miles of a highway and within 28 miles of a town - hardly out in the wild. However, he has no map, was totally inexperienced in living in such conditions, and underequipped. He did not die in the harshness of winter - he died of starvation in the warmest month of the year, failing to even survive 5 of the mildest months of an Alaskan year. I do not mean to vilify him, but simply cannot see him as a hero - an enlightened guru type who lost his life living it and to whom adventure was more important than death. In the end, his final diary entries show that he is desperate to get out of his situation, but does not know how. He is lonely, frightened, and desperate in the face of his death - not the brave philosophical adventurer Penn tries to sell us. From the documentary by his sisters, I do feel he was more of a victim than Penn managed to convey. His real father refuses to acknowledge in the documentary the kind of pain he caused his 7 children by two marriages. He takes credit for his effort to keep them all together emotionally as brothers and sisters, but cannot see any fault in himself. The fact that not one of hi six children have any contact with him now (22 years after McCandless' death as of the date of the documentary), nor with his second wife (McCandless' mother) suggests that he indeed must have caused quite a lot of pain in that family. What McCandless planned had he survived is not known. He took 600 photos of himself on this two year journey - almost all using the timer on his camera. He never communicated with his sister during his whole adventure - except to say before he graduated that he intended to cut himself off totally from his parents. It was all about himself. Was he going to write the great adventure story, or the ultimate book on the meaning of life? We don't know, but what he left behind did not show much skill at writing or any true enlightenment about the meaning he had discovered. He mostly quoted others. I spent not only the two hours watching this, but several hours researching his life online. In the end, all I can say is it is a story about a young man - pained, adventurous, brilliant, charming, selfish, and vain - who dies a needless and untimely death largely due to his own mistakes and not the uncompromising reality of the Alaskan wilderness. If I wanted to improve upon my personal understanding of the meaning of life, I would have to look elsewhere.

history.review_title: Very poor movie and a waste of time to watch
history.text: I did not care for this movie at all. Although the two main actors did not have a lot to work with in this script, neither of them captured my imagination, affection, respect, or even interest. I stuck with it to the bitter end thinking that it would get better or that somehow these two characters would come alive. The woman Claire is self-absorbed, selfish, cold, and a very good definition of "a bitch". She shows no warmth, feeling, concern (much less love) for anybody throughout the movie. Except for a couple of long stares near the end, she shows no feeling or attachment to the man (Thom). He is at least a bit likable, although its frustrating to see him stumble from one self imposed disaster to another. He is patient, far more than I can imagine any man being with such a selfish, bratty woman. Clearly, he needs approval, respect, and love in his lonely, failing life. Hard to imagine that he thinks he can get it from this woman. Therefore, the ending is simply ridiculous. The movie did not at all develop a blossoming relationship between the two based on anything other that their mutual need to get out of the several messes they get themselves into. Don't waste your time. It is not the impulsive adventure, with excitement and some fun, that pulls these two together romantically as we are led to believe by the storyline description. The dour, whiney music score adds to the drag that this movie becomes from the very beginning and sustains for 90 minutes. simply a total waste of time.

history.review_title: A story about a fascinating young woman
history.text: This is a documentary, not a movie. For those who expected something else and quit watching after 10 or 15 minutes – too bad. You missed a chance to see the incredible strength and total honesty of a very lovely young woman. She had no illusions about what she did or why she did it. Nor did she have any illusions about the limited choices she had to get out of it. At one point late in the movie when she was reading lines from the book she wrote about being beaten by a boyfriend, but being afraid for her life if she left him, she said “I don’t know how I got through all of it. I don’t know what held me together.” Nor do I. Yet, this was not a self-pitying whiney story at all. She was often smiling, even laughing when she told stories about her life, her struggles, her fears and frustrations. When she talked about her father who had totally abandoned his family, and she found him after 8 years and went to see him, it was almost as if she were talking about a scene in a movie rather than her own life. He cruelly dismissed her as his daughter because she was a porn star. She shot back her dismissal of him as a failed father and husband, and neither her voice nor her face portrayed bitterness or anger – she was almost laughing about it. She would be seen going to the porn set – a place that was nothing but grueling drudgery for her – but laughing and joking playfully. Her laugh was captivating and invited you to laugh with her. Her smile was simply pure sunshine. She also had an intellectual side to her. Quoting Shakespeare as she is walking to do a naked porn show; reading Chekhov, etc. In the final scene as she is walking on the beach away from the camera, I felt a sense of deep empathy for her. But it was not sadness, rather it was hope for her. I felt certain that she had the strength and the intelligence to find alternatives to porn, and that she would do that. This is a fascinating young woman, and I thank her for opening up her life to me so honestly, and yet so cheerfully. Far better to watch a documentary like this than most of the fiction garbage coming out of Hollywood.

Have Mescaline, Will Travel - pun on Richard Boone's Paladin. This movie was awful, and I can only blame myself. I don't like Vincent Cassel at all, and were it not for Juliette Lewis would never have even opened this movie. It was a boring naive good guy vs evil but clever bad guy plot that is so over done in westerns, gangster, war, and other action movies. Mikey (Cassel) foolishly takes on a gunslinger for the love of a whore he has known for 3 hours. She may indeed have been a sweet girl, but his naïve attempt at heroism only succeeds in getting her killed. He escapes miraculously with his life - of course he does, otherwise we don't have a long boring movie. He is saved by a band of Chiracahua apaches - mostly by their psychedelic drugs it seems. Ha - so Geronimo was a tripper????? And that's how his tiny band avoided 1000 troops for three years? Ha! yeah! Anyway, Mikey supposedly becomes hardened and wise in the ways of evil men and becomes a sheriff. When his nemesis shows up he stupidly slugs down a bunch of whiskey, goes for the gun that he had that tragic night so as to kill his enemy with proper romantic overtones, but is bushwhacked when he clumsily stumbles into the saloon with three of them in waiting. Ha, stupid number two by Mikey. He once again winds up being saved by the Chiracahua band, and in some kind of long, drawn out duel in psycholelia land kills his enemy. The physical dual is never shown - it is just minutes and minutes of centipedes, snakes, alligators, and spiders floating across the screen. Then he gets to make river love with Juliet Lewis. The photography, at least some of which appears to be in the Chiracahua mountains is very good. But not worth two hours of this miserable movie. If there was an intended tribute to the native americans - it gets lost in showing them to be stoners and incompetent warriors. In the pell mell ride by the bad guys they manage, while running away to shoot 5 pursuing apaches out of their saddles (I counted them!) while losing only one of their own. Typical John Wayne western where the stupid Indians get shot down in numbers by the superior white man. Yet, it was the native americans who learned to shoot from horseback, whereas the white eyes were taught to dismount, form a defensive line, and shoot while stationary. Terrible movie!

history.text: a documentary from the US point of view. Overall, a reasonable summary of the history of the war, but very shallow. Eastern Front was recognized, but not enough. Analysis of Hitler and his driving forces was shallow - as was the commentary on why the German people would follow this madman.

history.review_title: Vermeer is the artist, Tim is a brilliant technician
history.text: Brilliant. does it take away from one of the best artists of the Dutch Golden Era?. No. It explains him, perhaps. I love Vermeer. I still do. I am absolutely stunned that Tim accomplished what he did - but - fact is - he is no Vermeer and he even admits it. However, in today's world is a photographer an artist? Of course. If Vermeer used a mirror or a camera obscure - he was using technology to enhance his art - as photographers do today. Rather than see him as cheating, I would see him as advancing the frontiers of painting tremendously, since Tim just proved that he, an unskilled artist, could have painted the Music Lesson. But could he have imagined it in his mind, the layout, the theme, the colors, the placement and expressions of the characters? No. Tim has shown us that technique can be reproduced. Creativity cannot. Thanks Tim, but Vermeer reigns!

history.title: Spider-Man 3
history.text: I just paid $3.75 for this blu ray at Target, and I paid too much. Tobey Maguire's acting is atrocious; but then, who could tell when the rest of the actor's performances are just as horrible. Usually actors try to upstage one another, but this movie provides a rare example of actors trying to downstage each other. The screenplay and movie are so schizophrenic and devoid of any real emotion, that one suspects the studio execs, producers, writers, actors and director were more interested in snorting cocaine than making a good film.

history.title: Foul Play
history.review_title: A Dwarf and an Albino walk into a Bar.
history.text: I went with two friends to see this film in a Virginia Beach theater when it came out. One of these friends died in a plane crash three years afterwards, so I always think of him when I watch this movie. As to the movie, it would make a perfect double feature with High Anxiety. Both are comedic takes on Hitchcock genre films; however, Foul Play is less satirical than High Anxiety. In Foul Play, Goldie Hawn carries the movie and as a viewer, you fall in love with her because of her personality and incredible beauty (this was the first time I had seen her with long hair; before, when I was a small child and she was on Laugh In, she had short Edie Sedgwick/Twiggy haircut). This was to be Chevy Chase's star vehicle after being the first Saturday Night Live performer to leave the show for film stardom. I believe he turned down a role in Animal House for this film. It is probably the best Chevy Chase film (maybe Caddyshack, I can't remember if Fletch was good throughout). This film's plot has been explained by several reviewers and on Wikipedia, so I won't do a half ass job here. I will say the scene with Goldie Hawn meeting Dudley Moore and going to his apartment are probably the film's comedy highpoints. Taking place in San Francisco, the whole film dovetails into a The Man Who Knew Too Much climax at a Gilbert and Sullivan opera. It would be nice to have this movie released on blu ray. Since I bought the dvd, the price has escalated, but I would recommend buying a copy or at least watching the film on a streaming service.

history.title: Saturday Morning Cartoons: 1960s Vol. 1
history.text: Don't pay the inflated prices for this dvd when "4 Kid Favorites: Saturday Morning Cartoons: 1960's" has the same content, just a different cover. Amazon should ban sellers who try to gouge customers. So far as to what's on the dvd, it brings back childhood memories of getting up and watching cartoons on Saturday while eating Fruit Loops or Captain Crunch. The best part of this dvd is to get Quick Draw Mcgraw shows. I really wish that the complete series would be released.

history.title: Stalker (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I just got the Criterion blu ray and the picture quality is greatly improved, as well as the sound. I was disappointed in the supplements/extras and think my old Kino dvd version has better extra features. If you have watched any Tarkovsky movies, you are aware that he is one of the greatest directors ever; however, you have to be prepared to watch his movies. The films will drain you mentally and Stalker is probably the most brutal of Tarkovsky's films to watch. Stalker moves at it's own deliberate pace and you have to have patience or you will get bored; this is not a Hollywood blockbuster with hyper-pacing, loud explosions and throwaway dialogue. It doesn't help American viewers that the characters are Russian and come from different mindsets. This is not going to be a film for everyone, it has three unhappy ugly dudes talking philosophically while slowly walking. Stalker requires several viewings to start reaping it's rewards, but the film transcends the screen and takes the viewer on a journey that comments on spirituality (the Stalker), science (the Professor) and commercialism (the Writer). The ending shot with the child (Monkey) always leaves me wondering how it was pulled off. I think probably with magnets under the table, but perhaps it is best just to watch it and marvel at the brillance of Tarkovsky as a director and the difficulties he overcame during the making of Stalker, to give us one of cinema's greatest masterpieces.

history.title: The Marx Brothers Silver Screen Collection (The Cocoanuts / Animal Crackers / Monkey Business / Horse Feathers / Duck Soup) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: I Shot An Elephant In My Pajamas
history.text: I have bought these films in vhs, dvd and now blu ray formats. These films have been some of my favorite films since my childhood and are among the greatest comedies ever made. The new blu ray transfer greatly improves the picture and sound quality. The one thing I have to ask is why there is still missing frames/glitches in Horse Feathers during the couch scene with Groucho and the college widow. Is there only one surviving master reel of this film? As to the content of the films in this collection, these films are the Marx Brothers at the height of their talents. The lightning fast dialogue must have really shaken up audiences of the time who were just adjusting to the introduction of sound in the movies after thirty years of silent movies. The anarchy the Marx Brothers unleash on the screen during the time period of these films is relentless and nothing is sacred, especially the wealthy dowager. The only thing that slows the pace down is the musical numbers. While Chicho Marx is one of my all time favorite piano players and his numbers are great fun, and you can forgive Harpo's harp pieces, even though they drag the pace down; it's the singing musical numbers that are painful pace-killers (except of course Groucho's ie: Hello I Must Be Going, Hooray For Captain Spaulding, Whatever It Is I'm Against It, etc.) and really date the films. I guess even in the 1930's, film studios were trying introduce songs in films to sell records in stores; maybe audiences were expecting musical numbers after the introduction of sound into movies. These musical numbers are probably carry-overs from the stage versions of the show, when the Brothers were off stage changing wardrobe or taking a break. Animal Crackers is my favorite Marx Brothers film.

history.title: Ten Little Indians
history.text: I found this dvd at Amoeba Records for $3. The film versions of Agatha Christie's novel can follow one of two directions: The happy Hollywood ending or the ending faithful to the original novel. This 1974 version suffers from lackluster acting. Oliver Reed sleepwalks through the film, ruining another movie (the most notable example being Tommy, where his casting is the only dead weight in an otherwise exceptional film). Elke Sommer is another actor miscast in this film; since the whole storyline hinges on her performance, the film lacks any emotion (romance, suspense, humor) due her tepid acting and the lack of chemistry between her and Oliver Reed. It is a shame because I loved her in A Shot In The Dark. The only two things of interest in this movie are the location (which I thought was Egypt but is in Iran at the world's oldest hotel) and the casting of two early James Bond villians as murder victims. These Bond villains had me thinking this film would have been vastly improved if all the cast members had been Bond villans (Donald Pleasance, Dr. No, Lotte Lenya, Bruce Glover, Charles Gray) with Sean Connery and Honor Blackman (or Ursula Undress) as the fim's central couple; although I do like Herbert Lom (ie: Inspector Dreyfus) and Stephane Audran (who I love in Claude Chabrol and Luis Bunuel films).

history.title: Inspector Clouseau [Blu-ray]
history.text: I grew up watching and loving the Peter Sellers Pink Panther movies. Yesterday, I found a $3 Dvd of Inspector Clouseau at Amoeba Records. Obviously Alan Arkin is no match for Peter Sellers, much like George Lazenby is no match for Sean Connery’s James Bond. Arkin borrowed some elements of Sellers’ creation, but largely tries to add his own flourishes to the character. Missing are the ridiculous accent, the cat and mouse games with Cato, the rivalry with Chief Inspector Dreyfus, ane even Arkin’s bumbling and pratfalls are half-hearted attempts to mimic Sellers (who could masterfully develop a series of gags, like the interrogation of the house staff in The Pink Panther Strikes Again). All in all, this is not a bad movie, but it does not live up to the expectations set by The Pink Panther or A Shot In The Dark. Even the directing is flat; where funny premises are set up, but not fully fleshed out. Perhaps the best instance is when Clouseau mistakenly does audio surveillance of a tv set. In the hands of Blake Edwards, this scene could have provided a much funnier impact (even though Bud Yorkin did direct some great movies, particularly Start The Revolution Without Me). In fact, a lot of the movies ideas were presented but not fully developed; like why the main actress falls in love with Clouseau. Also, sorely missing is the music of Henry Mancini. There are some very good supporting actors in this film ( Patrick Cargill, Barry Foster, etc.), even if we are missing Herbert Lom and Burt Kwouk. I believe Inspector Clouseau is probably better than Steve Martin’s attempts (John Cleese should have been Inspector Clouseau), which I refuse to watch; therefore, I would say watch this movie and try not to compare it to the vastly superior Sellers/Edwards movies.

history.title: The Finest Hours

Characters are caricatures as if from a Disney cartoon. The description of "crossing the bar" is so unbelievable as to convince one that one is watching a cartoon or animation. Worst of all is the anachronistic excising of God from the film. In great concern about how the rescue might proceed without a compass and in the dark the lead character lowers his head but never utters a prayer or even a sound. He made me tihink of Peter Townsend's "Tommy the Pin Ball Wizard". Not once was God called out to by anyone, not once does a character pray. In the 50s people were more humble and realistic. Hollywood would convince us otherwise. What is it like to cross the bar that braces the bay from the ocean. Here is the poem I learned in public school in the 50s. Tennyson thought of crossing the bar from the bay out to the ocean as a metaphore for crossing from this life to the next. Perhaps the original men who went out into the ocean to effect this rescue did the same. "Crossing the Bar", Alfred Lord Tennyson Sunset and evening star, And one clear call for me! And may there be no moaning of the bar, When I put out to sea, But such a tide as moving seems asleep, Too full for sound and foam, When that which drew from out the boundless deep Turns again home. Twilight and evening bell, And after that the dark! And may there be no sadness of farewell, When I embark; For tho' from out our bourne of Time and Place The flood may bear me far, I hope to see my Pilot face to face When I have crost the bar.

history.title: The Best of British War Cinema: 10 Action Packed Movies
history.review_title: Morally wholesome, sometimes challenging and historically interesting British movies
history.text: British War Cinema (10 Movies). Worth the price as others have said. Here are some thoughts on each movie. I think it is important to have good - morally good - entertainment available. This group of movies meets that standard. Appointment With Venus (Island Rescue) 1951 2 David Niven, Glynis John, Kenneth Moore Silly humor. Some good acting. Tenuous stretched unrealistic plot. Neither the seriousness of war nor that of a relationship between a man and a woman is done well. The Wind Cannot Read 1958 2 Dirk Bogard, Yoko Tani, Ronald Lewis Corny play on interracial issues between English flier and Japanese teacher in Burma Operation Amsterdam 1959 4.5 Peter Finch, Eva Bartok, Tony Britton Very good acting. Plot is realistic taken from an actual event. Theirs Is the Glory 1956 [1946] 4 Stanley Maxfed, Thomas Sculion, Allan Wood, British 1st Abn Div Re-enactment of the Battle of Arnhem in Holland done just after the war ended by the actual survivors of that battle The Day Will Dawn 1942 Deborah Kerr, Ralph Richardson, male lead Richardson has a very short appearance in this movie. The male lead delivers a forgettable performance as a handsome loose living, wealthy society person who has become a newspaper reporter. He is a protégé of Richardson who help him to become the newspaper’s reported in Norway before the Germans invade. Incredibly the lead charater is talked into parachuting into Norway – without any prior training. Deborah Kerr is the romantic lead and is the daughter of a Norweigan fisherman (the powerful elderly Welch fisherman from I Know Where I’m Going). Long story short male lead saves the day and carried off Deborah Kerr to England with the expressed desire to return after the Nazis have been defeated. Seven Thunders (The Beasts of Marseilles) 1957 Stephen Boyd, James Robertson Justice, Peter Ustinov, a French actress This movie analyzes the moral corruption present in Marseilles, France in 1943 from the standpoint of 1957, when the movie was made. Moral values of every sort came under great strain during the War that took 60 million lives. The reverberations of this event are still with us. Two British soldiers have escaped from an Italian POW camp. They arrive in Marseilles and are awaiting a French fishing boat Captain’s offer to get them back to England so that they can re enter the fight. Boyd’d character (he exhibits the same character traits and tics here as he did in Ben Hur and The Man Who Never Was} becomes involved with a young woman abandoned by her mother. This is the romantic piece that holds the plot together. Unfortunately in the end the relationship seems to trivialize the monstrous events and behaviors the movie has shown un occurring in Marseilles in 1943 German occupied France. The analysis of moral climate here reminds me of “The Third Man” with Joseph Cotton and Orson Wells which analyzes the moral climate in Vienna just after the war. We see nihilism in flower after the events of the war in the Third Man. In Seven Thunders it is still germinating. Unpublished Story 1942 3 Richard Greene, Vallerie Hobson Slow starting until the thesis of the story begins more than half of the way through. Some good acting. Fifth column concerns in England. Two Thousand Women 1944 3.5 Phylis Calvert, Flora Robson Why would this be an interesting movie? Do women find a movie about 2,000 women in a French hotel under the police control of Nazis an interesting story line? In what ways? The movie dialogue is women’s chatter with a strong element of British propaganda. First to note about this movie is that it was made during the war in England. As someone else has said men are naturally interested in a movie with 2,000 good looking women in it. How did women feel about the loss of men at home in England during WWII? Probably they felt similarly to the way men felt when they were away from women in military service: they missed them. So this is a movie made primarily for British women during WWII. The characters include a social cross section of the possible female paths in life from the sacred to the profane; the upper class to the lower class. The relationship of the sexes during war time is a primary focus here viewed especially from the stand point of women. For that reason, the women’s point of view makes this film different and interesting. Secret Mission 1942 2 James Mason, Michael Wilding, Kurt Stapanek, male lead not mentioned on the CD jacket In spite of some good actors the screenplay is poor. The film quality itself is very poor. The Germans are made to seem foolish and silly and the British smart, brave and dashing. The German Admiral of the Bismark in the eponymous movie has a part in this movie as is convincing in his role. This movie includes a romance that is very unconvincing. The male lead is the same as that in The Day Will Dawn. The movie is in general silly. The Flemish Farm 1943 4 Clive Brook, Clifford Evans, Jane Baxter Plot and screen play is from a true story: the folding of the colors of the Belgian Airforce as the Nazis closed in on Belgium and the restoration of those colors. Very well acted. The drama is sustained, plot and character are developed, there is tragedy and reward. This is a good movie.

history.title: Wild Strawberries (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.text: What does this movie mean? For me it was a touching personal reminiscence of the process of getting old. Sjostrom is radiant as Professor Bork, an aging Swedish Doctor and Professor who is on the way to receive an honorary degree. Professor Bork’s journey to receive his award will take him about one day. As he travels he dreams about the course of his life and it’s end. He reviews the emotional pain of his life in its events as he daydreams. In the real world as he travels we see him honored and thanked by young and old for his contributions to the lives of others. He is not aware though of the many good things he has done. The sum of his life’s regret, Bergman seems to be telling us, is his ability to be detached and cold with respect to the events of life or to put that another way his inability to be passionate in the way that others are passionate. His punishment has been to be lonely. But the passion that Bergman shows us, the passion that Prof Bork lacked in his life, was an immoral, illegitimate passion. So I am not sure that Bergman has in the end said anything coherent in his comment about being dispassionate in life. Are immoral people not lonely at the end of their lives? Not in my experience. In my experience virtue is its own reward. Is this coldness, this loneliness, a Swedish, a Northern European problem that Bergman wrestled with himself? I am not sure this film says anything. In some respects this film is like Ozu’s films. It depicts ordinary life in an extraordinary and at times in a very beautiful way. Real life is extraordinary. It is not ordinary.

history.title: True Grit
history.text: This is the better film in comparison with the John Wayne version. Jeff Bridges is a more nuanced actor than John Wayne. To put that another way John Wayne brings very little acting nuance to his parts. The cast in a John Wayne film is expected to orbit John Wayne. In this 2010 Bridges film there are several very good performances. That of Bridges is just one of them. The plot does not suffer by being in service to one actor. The actors carry the story forward with ease in the 2010 version. The photography is great in the 2010 version. One character that is stronger in the Wayne film is that of "Lucky" Ned Pepper portrayed by Robert Duvall in the 1969 film. Pepper is the leader of the outlaw group to which Chaney flees after he has murdered Hattie's Father. Duval brings a level of character portrayal and psychological nuance to the chief of the bad guys that provides full counterpoint to "Rooster" Cogburn, the character portrayed by John Wayne, chief of the good guys. In the final analysis this movie is about vengeance in all of its remorseless monomania . Yes, the bad guy deserved justice. But the manner in which the bad guy receives the consequences of his action leaves the film with a sullen and cold ending. I am left feeling regret and pity for the heroes and heroine. I am not eager to see either version again.

I don't understand the release of these sets is a money making scheme & there is just going to be a more complete set that comes out later on, like the DBZ orange bricks but do you have to make it so obvious? I mean to come out with a set that only has 2 discs & only 13 episodes, I mean really? Rant over. Now to grade the episodes, when this set comes out most have already seen these episodes in one shape or another, whether that's through the Resurrection of F movie or the actually aired episodes. The story is as always great, yes its somewhat trying because Frieza coming back has happened a couple times now so its really not that special. The animation is in many episodes not to the same level as later seasons of DBZ, but this is to be expected considering the new animators they have working on it. In my personal view, DBS as a series as better than GT and thankfully most agree after all we are now 100 plus episodes into the series if you are watching it online like me, & GT only ran for 64 episodes. I for one hope the series goes for awhile like Z did. Its got a lot of the same feel with the action, but also throws in more humor more like Dragon Ball. So if you haven't already seen these episodes, definitely pick the set up. Personally I am going to wait for more substantial English dubbed episodes to come out first before I buy, but like I said if you haven't already seen it, go for it!

history.title: Live Without a Net (Tour Only) (US Release)
history.review_title: This is a fantastic DVD & concert
history.text: This is a fantastic DVD & concert, the concert is from the Van Halen 1986 5150 Tour & it really is Van Halen at the absolute top of their game. Even a fan of the Roth era will enjoy this DVD. The energy and the enthusiasm coming from the band on this will make anyone who is a fan of the band or even just good time rock n roll will enjoy this. You can really tell at this point in time the band was in some of their best spirits. Just wish they would remaster this & put it on a blu ray. But I guess at this point in time the band is almost trying to pretend like the Hagar era didn't exist, so I guess we just have to be thankful for what we have. Its too bad, there is no doubt Sammy was the man vocally, & this concert is documented proof. Sound is great, just wish the picture was a little better but still a great concert for any fan to have. Quality: Now with all that being said buyers of this need to understand the picture on this in my view is slightly better than VHS, so it could be better. The sound is good but could be great. We all want Van Halen to come back to this stuff & come out with a blu ray, but at this point its doubtful that's going to happen. So buyer beware, this is a fantastic concert but don't go into it without reasonable expectations.

history.title: DCU: Batman and Harley Quinn (BD)
history.text: Soooo just rented this from the library because of all the bad reviews...alrighty, so its not that bad. Its not as serious as Batman the Animated Series, its actually comical in parts (aka there is a scene with a fart joke, which is actually pretty funny lol). I think it can be considered unfocused in a lot of places, because we are looking at it through the lense of the animated series, which we cannot blame people for the animation style screams the animated series. Its hard to say exactly what's the tone they want to achieve. I wasn't bothered by Melissa Rauch from the Big Bang Theory voicing Harley or the different voice actress for Poison Ivy, although I don't know why they decided to make the switch. It may be because of scheduling differences I guess, but from what I have heard voice acting doesn't really take that long to do. Personally I think the film as a story isn't that bad, but that being said I would pass on buying this. Definitely a renter 110%!

history.title: Drone Wars
history.review_title: Just when you think they hit bottom, a new low bobs to the surface.
history.text: A marginal ID4 clone with little to call it's own. Grim infighting among the characters with Mad Max morality did not make up for the lack of a SPFX budget. I liked Corin better in his monster bug movies. He got to show more humor which is his strong suit in those low brow time burners. In this he just runs around shooting anything that moves. His lighter side was wasted. He might have shined better as the villain. Considering the script, I doubt it.The SPFX are passable but the story stole a lot from District 9 as well as a couple of others. If you are an incurable Sci Fi geek like me you will get it anyway. But get it cheap, guys. The less you pay, the better you'll feel about it. 90 minutes felt kind of long while watching this one. Should have been better. Could have been better. Wasn't. Sigh.....

history.title: Poltergeist - The Legacy - Season 1
history.review_title: What a delightfully horrific surprise! Like finding an old fiend, I mean friend.
history.text: Wow! I just finished the 90 minute premier episode of this series. There is no point in waiting any further before logging in this critique. If you saw the series in it's US release back in the 80s, you ain't seen nothin' yet! This is the European version of this show and is as R rated as any theatrical feature of the time. The scares are quite creepy with eye popping special effects and the sex includes a demonic seduction that leaves nothing to the imagination. Keep the kiddies in the other room, Mommy. This is Halloween for the grown ups! I suspect this film actually got a foreign theatrical release before launching its TV syndication. What ever the rest of the series has in store, I am sure it will be a monster mash worth watching, if you are so inclined. BTW, the show took itself quite seriously. So do not look for in jokes and characters mugging the camera. This is way beyond Tales From The Crypt. Deliberately horrific stuff,,,just the way we like it! Insert maniacal laughter here.

history.title: I Am Dragon
history.review_title: I was a teenage dragon heart throb.
history.text: The painfully low budget did not hurt this fairy too much. The costumes and other trappings looked sparse. But the cast was solid and the story and direction did not lack for the proper zeal. To keep it short I will simply say that this was an entertaining fantasy in spite of all the obvious short comings. It is easy to get spoiled by mega-buck master works and become jaded when other films do not measure up. But I cannot bring myself to degrade this film just because it does't look like it cost enough to pay off the National Debt. Once again Hollywood has spent many a misguided dollar on far weaker stories with far bigger stars and come up with nothing worth talking about lately. ( You know the dud I am talking about.) The words Dragon and Dinosaur are a film maker's ticket to profit if they can deliver the goods to their pre-sold public. And let's face it. Dragons and monsters of all kinds aren't just for kids anymore! And the special effects are first rate, even for a straight to DVD market. So keep them coming! You can never have too many monsters.

history.title: Arthur C. Clarke // Collection / Mysterious World 2
history.text: Back when the X Files was in first run. Or even before that, when Twilight Zone crawled over the airwaves, shows like A. C. C's Mysterious World were slipping between the cracks. They stretched the programming beyond Sit Coms and disposable detectives. With Mr Clark himself serving up the weirdness there was a creepy credibility in these stories. It was a kind of documentary deliberately designed to make you think and wonder about long after the show was over. And the best thing about it is they still do!

history.title: Sinbad: Season 1
history.review_title: Sinbad-light. Good to the last drop, er, episode.
history.text: A fun series that I begrudgingly give that fifth star. The premier episode is fabulous. But as the series wore on the scope of the stories shrank quickly. this was sad because the cast was great and the writing was consistent. Obviously the powers that were did not relegate the flow of the limited bucks in a way that maintained the level of the magic through out the first season. I very much liked the cast and the interplay between the inexplicable mix of nationalities ( and maybe even time periods). There was a part Ray Harryhausen, part Terry Gilliam feel to production and that may have been part of the problem. The first episode set a bench mark they never quite hit again. And that may have been their fatal mistake. But that doesn't mean that Sinbad Season One isn't fun. It stands on its own merits quite nicely. But I think if one pays attention, one can see why the show didn't last. For what ever reasons,the producers did not support their young Sinbad properly. Ultimately the production visually starved to death. Sinbad is traditionally about spectacle. And they ran out of funds long before they ran out of episodes. It was a shame. BUT!!! That only explains why there are not ten seasons. The first season listed here is over all well conceived, impressively produced, and populated with a cast of interesting characters, creatures, and situations. It is a shame they could not maintain it with a life span like Hercules. We could have used eight or nine more seasons. Season One is a lot of fun.

history.review_title: Quite a good movie, human interest story is what it was ...
history.text: Quite a good movie, human interest story is what it was to me. Wondered how much was true and how much was added to the film; would he have written about that in his century-later-found journals, about the wife not becoming pregnant because aspect? I don't think so. Also highly doubtful the queen would have been dropped off on an island with her teacher with absolutely no bodyguard or staff. ...., so in places like that, you wonder about the authenticity. However, his intelligence and manner was not in question and was certainly what must have won the Queen's heart and trust. As the telling of this written story, it was a good history film, presuming it was a mostly non-fictional rendering. In the end, there's a photo of the queen herself with a much heavier Abdul. The actor who played him was very loveable and Judi Dench simply excellent in this film. In today's milieu, this film is bound to stir up a few things; Muslim's called Hindu's due to ignorance just because they're from India would be offensive to anyone who is from either of those religions. For me, the full black burkas were just unbearable to see (even if it was a century ago) and the nose ring. But as a human interest story from a piece of actual history, and as a film, it was exceptionally well done. The cinematography was excellent.

history.title: History's Verdict
history.review_title: SURPRISINGLY PREJUDICED, ANGLO-CENTRIC PRODUCTION---MUCH TOO BIASED TO QUALIFY AS EITHER "BIO" OR "DOC"...
history.text: ....True students of WWII military leaders will first feel themselves perplexed upon viewing this series (as the "facts" presented in his series often differ so greatly from the facts learned elsewhere)....Gradually, they will become enraged (as "re-written" or omitted history = false history)... ---Thus, from this London-based production crew, we are presented with : Montgomery : Cool, calm, methodical, "the most brilliant military mind since Napoleon, etc..." The (VERY MANY) serious shortcomings of the man's character and leadership are glossed over, completely omitted, or only briefly presented (only to be quickly refuted by another "source")....Not a syllable is spoken about Montgomery's truly under-handed treatment of Eisenhower (particularly, the lies he told him in order to "borrow" his personal journal---only to use it against him in a scathing "autobiography"); nor, are we told about the appallingly cruel manner in which Montgomery treated his mother (forbading her from attending events honouring him, refusing to visit or communicate with her--even when she was dying, then refusing to attend her funeral)...His outrageous boasting---and the damage he personally inflicted upon the US-British relationship during the war are hardly mentioned---and noted historians' critical assessments of Montgomery as overly-cautious--to the point he cost the Allies many lives; and so irascible that the Americans often preferred not even coordinating critical battle plans with him (as they knew it would involve days of senseless arguing--thus, slowing operations considerably ---all are barely (if at all) mentioned.... ---Then, the "documentarians" get their hands on Patton....Whoa. Total sea change. Beginning with the first sentence: "In March of 1945, General George Patton committed what was arguably the worst of the many "crimes" committed under his leadership...." (It goes--very quickly--downhill from there)....Far worse (from a historical perspective), rather than use celebrated biographer's assessments of these leaders, the producers have chosen only the two or three "historians" whose (often biased) assessments agree with their own..... ----Hirohito is depicted as a peace-loving neophyte---tricked, by his far cleverer generals into all-out war (conveniently omitting solid historical research and recently discovered documents that prove that Hirohito was very much a prime driver of Japanese aggression---actually pushing for a co tinuation of the war long after any hope of victory was possible)....This series was a real eye-opener for me...Rarely have I found a series so nakedly biased....I would have given it "0" Stars for accuracy....perhaps, "2" stars for imaginative fiction, if I could have.....Simply awful.....

---I didn't have a clue what to expect when I "clicked" on this rather quirkily-titled, pseudo-film....but I very soon found myself laughing—in disbelief....The actor portraying the race-obsessed Lanz is hilarious. He resembles "Seargent Schulz" from "Hogan's Heroes" (sounds like him, too)...His description of Hitler ("This pointy-headed, black-haired, Ape-Man") is a hoot (Lanz believed Hitler was descended from the most genetically “inferior human stock”)......This little ditty is about as “un-PC” as anything you will ever watch, and definitely worth a viewing-- if only to hear a really fine actor ardently espousing his firm, rather shocking (and hilarious) theories on race ....

history.review_title: VERY INFORMATIVE---BUT FAR TOO EASY ON THE POPE...
history.text: ---While I very much appreciated the scholarship that went into this production (and it is profound), at the same time, I believe that the commentators cut the duplicitous, borderline-evil, Pope Pius XI far too much slack for his inaction in the face of genocide (unlike his predecessor, Pious VI, who, even BEFORE Hitler had instituted his "Final Solution" against the Jews, had heartily condemned “the DIRECTION” that Hitler was “heading in,” in a scathing speech that he demanded be read out in every pulpit in Germany).... ----Unfortunately, the "good" Pious died (under very suspicious circumstances), leaving this slippery, Italian replacement in his stead (a replacement who--even LONG AFTER the extermination of Jews was revealed to him by several sources--refused to even SPEAK OUT against the practice)....What a black stain this one greasy, little man left on the Church....I would have given my review at least another star, were it not for the almost (nauseating) display of "Catholic scholars" and others, excusing such a horrid, little man's actions -- and far worse: his LACK of action....

history.review_title: OMG --- YOU ABSOLUTELY MUST WATCH THIS VIDEO!!!!
history.text: ----I have written many reviews for Amazon, and, being an amateur historian, have viewed thousands of WWII documentaries produced in many different countries, but NEVER have I seen anything remotely like this (TRUE) story.....It literally blew me away......One of the most fantastic tales of wartime grit, ingenuity and raw courage I have ever seen..... ----No synopsis in this review at all (this is too stunning a tale for that). WATCH IT. You won't regret it......(And as an aside: I think I am IN LOVE WITH FRED MAYER)!!!!!

history.review_title: DISHONESTY (ON A FAIRLY GRAND SCALE) RUINS WHAT MIGHT HAVE BEEN A GOOD DOCUMENTARY
history.text: ----I WOULD normally have given a documentary so chock-full of fairly solid research on a little-known historical event a higher rating, but the dishonesty used (repeatedly) by the filmmakers (presumably to make the victims appear more sympathetic---and the US Government more Machiavellian) was really disillusioning..... ---Throughout the film, we hear : "These were just unemployed workers during the Depression. They would have worked ANYWHERE..." or...."They came to the USSR in order to feed their families..." or....”ANYONE in a similarly jobless environment would have done the same"....except....”everyone" DIDN'T. Despite the fact that whole swathes of the population were jobless--tens of millions of Americans---only a teeny, tiny fraction of a teeny, tiny minority heeded the siren call of the USSR (despite huge promises of riches and prosperity)...What actually drew that tiny minority to the USSR was NOT the promise of "jobs," so much as it was ideology (estimates vary that from 85-92% of the Americans who emigrated were members of the Communist Party --most often, very committed members)... ----One only need look at the film footage in this video of the Americans as they disembark from the boats and trains bringing them to the USSR : most are holding their arm extended over their head, hand in a tight fist (the Communist "salute"). These folks were hardly the "Dorothy-in-Oz", wide-eyed innocents, that the filmmakers would have us believe....FAR more dishonest from a documentary standpoint, however, is the filmmakers' insistance on calling members of this group who were imprisoned or executed, "Americans." They were not. Of the emigrants who were executed by the Soviets, virtually all were SOVIET citizens---they had relinquished their American citizenship -- either for ideological reasons, because Soviet authorities insisted they do so in order to keep their jobs---or, most often, a combination of both (at which point, the few Americans not ideologically wed to Communism, beat a quick retreat back to the States).... ----This being said (which the filmmakers certainly did NOT), these people obviously did not deserve the barbaric treatment meted out to them by the ever-paranoid Stalin...If there is one point this film makes very clear, it is the danger of ideological blindness (indeed, it was at times quite difficult to avoid yelling at the screen, "What the hell were you THINKING? Do none of you ever READ??")...One would think that if the bloody history of the Bolsheviks --only 15 yrs prior--didn't turn them off, What Stalin had JUST DONE to the Ukrainian people---genocide via starvation---which was widely reported at the time, would have)....And as for the "shameful failure" of the US Government not to "help trapped Americans,” all I can say is..."Huh?" These were FORMER Americans--individuals who EMIGRATED of their own free will---and jettisoned their citizenship, in the process .... ---Perhaps the truly saddest aspect of this doc, however, was the apparent inability of these ideologues to see---before it was too late--how infinitely better life had been for them, back in the despised "Capitalistic" country they had forsaken....

---If there is one thing that I know very well, it is Germany---and the German people. Having been born in the US to German parents, I spent a great part of my life living and studying in Germany (my parents sent me back to Germany for studies, from age 8-18, in order that I wouldn't become too "Americanized," and after university, I spent several years working in Munich).....I find this video most interesting --not due to the "Nazi father" revelation---but because of something the filmmaker, himself, can't even seem to see : that he is far closer to his father---both in motivation, complete conviction, and "communal beliefs" ---than he realizes (in fact, the only truly "non-Germans" in this film are the siblings DEFENDING their father)... ----Germans are, by their nature, "group thinkers." Individualism has not, traditionally, been either a common--nor a prized--trait amongst the German people. And so, whereas in Hitler's time, practically all of German society supported the regime, in today's Germany, Political Correctness reigns —and is just as enthusiastically enforced by the "authorities" as thought crimes were by the Gestapo (for example, even VERBALLY denying that the Holocaust occurred is illegal in Germany—and will earn you a jail sentence; a German GRANDMOTHER was recently sentenced to 3 years in Federal Prison in Stuttgart for the crime of “denying the Holocaust”)....And so, rather than a rightward-leaning nationalism, today's Germans--almost universally--embrace a leftward-leaning, ANTI-nationalism... ----The real shock in this film was seeing some German "holdouts" (VERY "un-PC" not to denounce all things "Nazi" in today's Germany)....By the way, I am not saying--at all--that the Nazis SHOULDN'T be "denounced"; of course they should--but they should have been "denounced" much earlier (like, at about the time Hitler came to power)....This “group think" atmosphere--combined with a heavy dose of self-deception — has allowed the German people to perform the mental gymnastics necessary to execute 360 degree changes in “convictions” without missing a beat (thus we saw even YEARS after the war, whole --LEFT-WING --university departments literally stuffed with former high-ranking Nazis---with ALL of their fellow academics aware of it—yet, all telling themselves that none of them ever “really believed in” National Socialism)....Yeah...you’d have to hear it, to believe it—and had I not been considered “one of them,” I NEVER would have heard it in the first place.... ---As for the "denying" siblings: anyone can tell that the father worship they profess DIDN'T come from a father these children were far too young to have known or become much attached to---but from the mother, who was a far more ardent Nazi than the father ever was. Listen carefully to her statements (like the time her husband had considered leaving the Party after the Night of the Long Knives--because a close friend of his was murdered on Hitler's orders---and she told him, "When making a good omelette, a few eggs must get broken...".. OR....Her utterly indifferent recitation of her husband's cover-up and involvement in the murder of an elderly Jewish man ....OR...Her obvious disgust with “the foreign Jews” who had "spread lies" about the Party)...It was the MOTHER who inflicted such emotional damage on her children — damage that slowly becomes evident to the viewer, as we are confronted with her deceptions and her own mental gymnastics..... ----My roots and family are 100% German, going back many centuries. There is much I admire about the German character and I am deeply attached to the country and its people...Even so (and though I was born several decades after WWII), I came to the conclusion that these often-brilliant, very industrious people have 3 fatal flaws —flaws that have resulted in the deaths of tens of millions of people, via the two World Wars begun by them. They are: Arrogance (the belief in their own superiority, via industriousness and invention) ; Group Think (wherein the entire populace follows the State-sanctioned Pied Piper); and Self-Deception (which allows this same populace to deny whatever actions/deeds/thoughts it once both eagerly engaged in and enforced—but which it now fiound to be unpleasant—and is able to alter its course, without deep reflection)...You see all three of these traits encapsulated, more or less, in those interviewed for this film... But the character in this documentary that I felt perhaps best represented all three German “flaws” was not the “mother,” .kor siblings—but the filmmaker, himself....I saw little deep reflection on his part as to his family’s true legacy (like his failure to confront his own mother’s obvious culpability in his country’s crimes; or the damage eww she had wrought on his siblings’ mindsets). Even worse — as in Hitler’s time (when the majority of German citizens were lecturing the rest of the world on the “correctness” of their race-based hierarchy) — there is more than a hint of arrogant superiority in this film; a kind of false outrage, combined with a “Look-How-Much-We’ve-Changed” mentality....I’m simply not buying the filmmaker’s premise (that he is doing something “brave” by denouncing his father, by “confronting” his mother/siblings with his father’s guilt)—it takes no great leap of heroics to denounce a father one was far too young to have had any deep emotional ties to ; it felt as though he were following a “Today's-Germany-Approved" quest to damn his Nazi father— a quest, incidentally, that he knew would be as applauded by “today's Germany” as his father’s views were applauded by yesterday’s....And yet, he cannot seem to recognize the mirror image that he, himself, is presenting of his own father....

history.review_title: QUINTESSENTIAL PBS: UNSURPASSED VISUALS OF THE 30s/40s —COMBINED WITH AN UTTER TONE DEAFNESS TO THE SOCIAL MORES OF THE TIMES
history.text: Like the majority of PBS “historical-genre” series of late (“Home Fires,” “Crimson Field,” etc.), our friends at Public Broadcasting must feel that “Today’s Audiences” are : 1) Dolts; either completely ignorant of the social mores and conventions of the 1930s/40s (the ‘30s, supposedly depicted in “The Durrells”) ...or, that 2) Factually depicting people as they truly spoke, behaved & dreamt during this era would simply be “too boring” to hold the attention of the 21st Century audience....(Of course, when supposedly working from an autobiographical source —as with “The Durrells”—, PBS writers COULD have done the unthinkable : in addition to inculcating items one & two above, as the author did in his trilogy, they might simply have FOLLOWED the author’s very engaging and hilarious tales—AS WRITTEN. Examples of present-day mores and values being substituted for historically accurate behaviours simply abound in The Durrells: the eldest son blithely sleeping with his girlfriend—with family members giddily “listening in” in adjoining rooms (a situation not only happily accepted by Mum—but applauded by her, as she celebrates her son enjoying “carnal delights”). Preposterous, utterly unacceptable behaviour during a time when less than 1.5% of middle-class females engaged in premarital sex (especially in ultra-conservative Greek society)....but, hey, why bother with historical accuracy—or with the author’s own tales—none of which included such gratuitous sexuality...We can also highlight the, by now, obligatory PBS inclusion of a prominent homosexual protagonist (note: PBS policy apparently doesn’t allow for homosexual ANtagonists, as their gay characters NEVER “play the bad guy”). In addition, this character’s sexuality ALWAYS garners the understanding/acceptance by the series’ other protagonists (again, in an era when homosexuality was almost universally viewed as being both deviant and immoral- in addition to being illegal)....AND (just to ensure that today’s audiences will be left with the smug conviction that the really “good” people of this era were, well, millennium-type progressives), an inter-racial romance is usually thrown in for good measure (with, again, acceptance by all protagonists on the show—this, again, despite the practically nonexistent statistics for interracial marriages in 1930s Britain....) My point is simple: if PBS wishes to portray “life” in the 30s/40s, they should do so accurately—no matter how much this may offend their modern sensibilities. Too many are historically ignorant as it is; a society can not trace the arc of its progress and/or its backsliding without being able to see the FULL picture— “warts” and all....

history.review_title: HOW DID I MISS THIS WELL-WRITTEN SERIES?
history.text: Most everything about this film : the cinematography, acting, directing, musical score—and especially the screenwriting, is quite exceptional. Dana Delaney simply dominates the film as the fiercely determined, tough-as-nails Sarah, who will do whatever needs to be done in order to survive against both Mexican nationalists and Comanche in the inhospitable Texas brush country she is determined to call home...The young actress portraying Euphemia is truly gifted, and totally believable.....Although the second half of the film lags behind the first half in storyline, it is the writers of this unusual, female-centric film to whom major “kudos” should go out to; they have captured not only the language—but imbued even the roughest characters with the dignity they deserved, imparting a heartfelt poetry to the words of men and women who risked it all to follow their dreams....Definitely worth seeing—especially for those interested in historically accurate depictions of the hardships faced by early settlers.....

history.review_title: WITH CIARAN HINDS AS CAPT. WENTWORTH, I’D THROW MYSELF OVERBOARD HIS SHIP—JUST TO CATCH HIS ATTENTION BEFORE DROWNING...
history.text: The most authentic Austen adaptation of them all — from dialogue, to direction, cinematography, to acting talent—even the costumes and the female, makeup-free faces — this made-for-television, BBC/PBS partnership rocked the film world by its surprising success when released as a theatrical movie (which just goes to show that excellence is far more dependent on the talent of a film’s creators, than the money spent on its production).....And did I mention Ciaran Hinds?... The players in Persuasion are all top-flight—many Old Vic alumni and OBE awardees (which translates into Britain’s best), and simply transition beautifully into their roles : Corin Redgrave, as Anne’s superficial and supercilious father, Susan Fleetwood, as the “persuasive” (and emotionally domineering) Lady Russell, and Sophie Thompson, as Anne’s consistently dissatisfied and hypochondriac sister....and, Ciaran Hinds? Not only one of Britain’s finest actors, but one who inhabits his role as both sea Captain during the Napoleanic Wars and proud, resentful—yet, long-pining suitor to Anne—with absolute believability.... The ONLY “negative” I would offer regarding this most excellent adaptation is the casting of Amanda Root as Anne Elliott....Although Root is undeniably an accomplished actress—one who can play both Shakespearean dramas or modern comedies with flair—I believe that both her physical presence and interpretation of Anne were lacking....Physically, Austen describes Anne as being “tall,” and although she has “lost her bloom” (due to her failed love affair with Wentworth), she nonetheless has “delicate features,” with “deep-set, dark eyes,” and a “full smile”...Instead, we are presented with Root’s near-dwarfish height, and a bushy-browed, slightly bug-eyed countenance—overseeing a pair of missing lips. Even so, I could overlook features so contrary to the author’s description, were it not for Root’s permanently “martyred” look (“buzz killer” would be an understatement) : unsmiling (when in smiling company), and with a permanently pained look—including a permanently gaping mouth, and a deeply furrowed brow (the thought of spending EIGHT YEARS with such a personality would have me grasping for a syringe of Botox with one hand, while the other was itching for a hard slap to “snap her out of it”)....Wearing one’s “heart on one’s sleeve” in such a manner was not only considered self-pitying in Austen’s time, but a sign of poor character/breeding —none of which were attributes of Anne Elliott (although Austen DID describe Anne as being “somewhat melancholy,” she also emphasized the fact that Anne was “adept” at “hiding her personal anguish” from others).... Such quibbles notwithstanding, Persuasion is a film made for repeated viewings— each one, opening another window into the human spirit and character.....Superb.

Get the DVD "Wages Of Spin" to get a further insight into what happened to Charlie back in the 1950's.
