history.title: Motown 25: Yesterday Today Forever
history.review_title: The Motown Family at their best
history.text: Although this is a 3 disk set you only need to watch the one disk of the actual show. It's unbelievable to see the talent pool that Motown was. There is nothing today that compares to this music and the presentations. Someone like Beyoncé, who is a talent, doesn't come close to these performances. Back then you didn't come on the stage via a trapeze or a rocket ship or some sort of distraction. You also didn't come out half naked which is also a distraction from the actual talent of the performers. You heard the Motown sound without any amped up productions. The music itself was great and still trumps most anything today when it comes to some sort of soulful music. The bonus material is plentiful and enjoyable to watch. You will not be disappointed with this package.

history.title: The Strawberry Blonde
history.text: Set at a time around the turn of the 20th century this is an entertaining movie topped off by the great acting of Olivia Dehavilland and James Cagney. Of course today this movie comes across at times as a little corny, but on the other hand it represents a time when you didn't need to have filthy language and sex scenes. Multiple stories wrapped into one overall plot that gets a good message across - be certain of what you want before you get it. Along the way there are many laughs that make this a completely enjoyable movie.

history.title: The Big T.N.T. Show
history.review_title: Great non-lip synced performances by a diverse group of artists
history.text: Great non-lip synced performances by a diverse group of artists. Ray Charles was spectacular and Tina Turner finished the show with a bang. It just brings back memories of the 1960's when there were a multitude of great groups and performers. This was raw talent at it's best that didn't require stage antics like today's so-called singers and groups. Joan Baez's version of "You've Lost That Lovin' Feeling" was actually pretty good. The Byrds and Lovin' Spoonful came in strong as well.

targets.title: Fuller House: The Complete First Season S1 (DVD)

history.title: Double Indemnity
history.review_title: One of my all time favorites!
history.text: Everyone does a great job, especially Edward G. Robinson as the insurance company investigator. There's a lot of complexity in this movie and you may have to watch it a couple of times to get it all. But don't think about it too much- the murder plot is half-baked and one that everything had to work perfectly for it to come off. Obvious things are overlooked, like the man sitting on the observation platform of the train, and who would be able to forecast that Neff would be able to jump from the train right were Phyliss was waiting?

history.title: Diary of a Lost Girl
history.text: A good movie, and I marvel at where they managed to recruit the creepy looking actors for the villains. However, it is somewhat muddled, mainly because of the lack of explaining dialog slides. You can follow the plot, but it changes tacks abruptly at times and it takes a moment or two to pick it up again. I also never knew Louise Brooks had such a rotund posterior! I thought she was a lot thinner.

history.title: Becker, Final Season
history.text: The final "season" is dismal compared to the previous ones. It's kind of like watching a loved one die, slipping away and there is nothing you can do. It looks like the writers just ran out of ideas, and the series lost its edge.

history.title: Feu: Crazy Horse Paris (3D & 2D) [ Blu-Ray, Reg.A/B/C Import - Netherlands ]
history.text: This is an odd DVD. I bought it because it was in 3D and there are so few movies (that aren't animated) in that format. Christian Louboutin, the guy who made the movie, introduces each segment, and after the first couple of parts I began to think "Who needs this guy anyway?" All he does it talk while birdcages with shoes float around in the background. I guess if I spoke French (or Dutch) it would make more sense. Anyway for the part everyone is really interested in, the naked girls. The 3D HD effect is wonderful- you feel as if you are sitting in the front row of a private showing. There are several good segments, but there are two where you see nothing but feet in heels. Okay, whatever floats your boat. There are some really good things. The "Final Fantasy," which is kind of a bondage thing, really shows the physical ability of the girl (billed as "Pshyko Tico") who performs it. It is also a well planned and intricate routine. In the segment "Purple underground" the girls shed their Louise Brooks wigs and we see how some of them really look. All in all, it's not a waste of time, but if you're not going to see it in 3D, then think about just downloading it from You Tube- it's a heck of lot cheaper.

history.title: Orgy of the Dead [VHS]
history.text: I didn't expect much, and was richly rewarded. I never could understand what the "plot" of this thing was. It has one, but it's unnecessary, and appears to be largely an excuse to work a series of unimaginative (and strangely non-erotic) nude dances into the movie. Criswell comes off as a dirty old man, and the two "victims" could easily escape this dilemma- only pretending to be tied up. You can escape it too, don't buy it. I only watched it because I wanted to see Ed Wood's work toward the end of his life, and I was happy that he continued to honor his same low standards The movie credits list the source of the screenplay as a novel written by Wood. I would love to read it- it must be about four pages long.

history.title: The Best of Court TV: Body of Evidence
history.text: I really do not understand the rave reviews this show has garnered. I think the show should be called "The Body of the Bleedin' Obvious." During most episodes, where apparently inept police departments employ Ms. Hinman to solve cases that Inspector Clouseau could have solved in minutes, she treats her audience to insights such as "the presence of multiple bullet wounds in the body suggested that a firearm had been employed", or "The fact that the subject had been bragging all over town that he had comitted the murder and had 8X10 glossies of the victim and crime scene led us to consider him a strong suspect." I've watched more than one of these shows and kept finding myself saying- over and over- "Like DUH!"

history.title: Viva Max
history.text: I loved the movie, but the quality of the DVD is atrocious. The sound is good but the picture is extremely muddy. There are dropouts throughout, and even one place where part of the same scene is repeated. There has to be a better print out there somewhere.

history.title: Sully (DVD)
history.text: A great movie- well worth the time and money to see it, but it is slightly flawed by the omission of explanation of some of the aircraft jargon used throughout. I used to work for an airline, so I know what an "APU" is and what "ACARS" does, but I'm not sure that the woman sitting next to me did.

history.title: Ellery Queen Mysteries
history.review_title: The big mystery is how this series came to DVD!
history.text: I thought more of this series than one star, but I know most people don't read the mid-range reviews. I have several issues with this presentation. First, the show is so full of continuity errors that you sometimes find yourself asking yourself "Was that intentional? Is that a clue?" Often it's not. Another is that the culprit often confesses at the end of the show- sometimes when all Queen has is one of his elaborate theories to fall back on- and no evidence to speak of. Another problem with the show is the constant references to items that were probably common knowledge in the late 1940's but not so much now, and the constant use of the SAME CARS in every episode. Finally, the acting is often lousy and wooden, with the actors seeming to be just going through the motions. Some of it isn't their fault though, the dialogue is often very poorly written.

history.title: Ghosts of the Abyss 3D (Three-Disc Combo: Blu-ray 3D/Blu-ray/DVD) [3D Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Should have been called "Ghosts of the BS!"
history.text: Way too much of stuff other than Titanic, which in 3D is amazing. Could have done without the phony shots of Bill Paxton looking out the viewing ports at the wreck making obvious comments (was there a diver down at 12,000 ft. with a camera?) The video also does a lot to perpetuate some of the falsehoods about the sinking. I also could have done without all the philosophizing about the people aboard and what they did. Were any of the people in this video aboard when the ship sank? The video could have been entirely of the Titanic and I believe nobody would have complained about anything.

targets.title: On the Buses // The Ultimate Collection

history.title: Christmas Snow
history.text: Order this only if you're desperate for a holiday movie you haven't already seen and you're willing to settle for extremely mediocre TV fare. I'll give it credit for not reworking holiday cliches, but that's about it. The production values are spotty, the script is mawkish, and the plot painfully unexceptional.

history.title: Justified: Season 5 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Up there with season three as the two best seasons!
history.text: After what I thought was an uneven fourth season, Justified came back with a high-octane fifth season that was so good I couldn't resist binge-watching it. In the past I've been able to limit myself to one or two episodes an evening to savor them and extend the delight, but this season was so relentlessly riveting that I couldn't stop until I'd watched three or four a night.

history.title: Dakotas, The: The Complete Series
history.review_title: One of the best TV series ever
history.text: Saw only a few episodes of this show as a small child but it left a searing impression on my brain that lingered through adulthood, when I tried to track down information and episodes of the series, finally hitting pay dirt briefly on YouTube before the episodes were blocked. Even better is this: a DVD with startlingly crisp resolution. If not for the public overreaction to the shooting of a pastor in episode 19, which caused its sudden cancellation, this series would have lasted and established itself as a landmark series along the lines of Have Gun, Will Travel. Well worth the money. Buy it, put it in the DVD player, and sit back and savor these gems. In an era when most heroes were kissing their horses and talking the bad guys to death, this show was a gritted precursor to the realist western era that arrived in the late 60s and early 70s in film. Best of all, Jack Elam got a chance to show a range of character he never got in other shows or movies, and what a lost treasure that was. But for 20 fantastic episodes, you can enjoy it.

history.title: M Squad: The Complete TV Series
history.review_title: Good show, better than expected quality of recordings
history.text: OK series, quality of DVDs better than you might expect. Based on others' reviews, I was hoping this series would be better than it is. It's not bad, but basic fare for the era. However, I feared many poor-resolution episodes (also based on others' reviews), but so far the ratio of great (for the era) resolution to poor resolution is about a dozen great episodes to one poor, high-contrast episode.

history.title: Ace in the Hole (Criterion Collection) (Blu-ray + DVD)
history.text: This gem was rejected by audiences not ready for a loathsome protagonist, but later generations have come to recognize it for the brilliant classic it is. Every line of dialogue sizzles, and the cast is spot on. Buy it and sit back for an evening of celluloid gold.

history.title: TCM GCF Legends: Robert Mitchum (4FE)
history.review_title: What a bargain for two of the best film noirs ever!
history.text: Though only two of the movies are strong, in my opinion, they're more than worth the price -- you can toss the other two and it's still a great buy. I'd always known Out of the Past to be one of the all-time great noirs, and it remains so (and was later remade into Against All Odds). But I'd never seen Angel Face, and what a superb noir that is as well. After watching it the first time, I then watched it with the commentary on and what an amazing back story (or back stories, there are so many) behind this impressive film! If you like noir, you'll love these two gems!

history.title: Checkmate: The Complete Series
history.review_title: A very overlooked classic from the early 60s.
history.text: I remembered this show fondly from when I watch it as a kid, and it's well worth buying. A nice cast, even if Anthony George is a bit stiff, and an amazing lineup of guest stars from one episode to another. They always had at least one major star, backed up by other great stars who hadn't yet made their names -- just very well cast. The majority of shows in the first season are strong, with some weak ones here and there, while the majority of shows in the second season are weaker with a few standouts here and there. It seemed as though they shifted in the second season from focusing on solving murders to solving people's personal dramas, more of the vein of those anthology shows like Route 66 where each week the characters inserted themselves into someone else's little drama. The show was said to fail in the rating in its second season due to a change in time slot, but I suspect it was at least as much due to the shift away from murder mysteries to personal dramas. Image quality is good -- there's no remastering or anything, it looks like a rerun you'd see on late night -- nothing special but nothing terrible either.

history.title: Coherence (2013) [ Blu-Ray, Reg.A/B/C Import - Sweden ]
history.review_title: A real, honest-to-gosh sci-fi story that goes where no one has gone before
history.text: Tired of today's formulaic, copycat movies where special effects are everywhere and an actual story is nowhere to be found? Itching for a real sci-fi story that surprises, baffles and impresses you? Look no further. The ingenious plot keep you constantly off balance, at times almost incomprehensibly, before pulling everything together in the end for one of those incredibly satisfying "Aha" moments, with enough humor sprinkled in at unexpected moments to stay real.

history.title: Man from UNCLE Season 4
history.text: UNCLE was a fun series that blew everyone away in its groundbreaking first season but then quickly lost its way after the producers spent seasons two and three diving headlong in non-stop camp. This was their attempt to return to the strength of the first season, restoring the action and thrills that had made it successful in the first place, but the results were uneven and by then viewers had gone elsewhere and the series was canceled midway through the season. Still, several episodes are well worth watching/owning, particularly The Survival School Affair, The Deep Six Affair, the two-part Seven Wonders of the World Affair, and The THRUSH Roulette Affair.

history.title: Brilliant But Cancelled - EZ Streets
history.text: My low rating is not because of the quality of the show but because you only get three paltry episodes. I probably should have read the reviews more closely and thus would not have ordered it, as the product description suggest you're getting an entire season of a show that was canceled after its first season. The show itself isn't bad, though I wouldn't give it the heady praise other reviewers did; I would call it better than average but not great, and I probably would have been happy to watch more episodes without complaining. But three episodes is a joke: it's over before it even gets started.

history.text: A Truly remarkable Film from the early 70s. This is also Michael Caine's unsung acting masterpiece as The Captain.

history.title: Serenity [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: It could have been a Contender, but they blew it.
history.text: It was a truly Fantastic SC-FI TV series, original, well thought out, with gritty developed Characters. The Movie is simply not very good. It is predictable, formulaic, and frankly just dull. Much of the plot makes no sense, and the " Climax" is just terrible. All that work and the only thing Joss could come up with was a utterly boring MMA smack down in which our hero improbably, but predictably, kicks the hell out of the bad guy. Just about everyone of the 16 episodes was better than the film. Sad.

history.title: Above and Beyond Complete Two Part Miniseries
history.review_title: 3 Hours of my life I shall never get back
history.text: How you can take a story this exciting and make it into a movie so dull is the question. There were several times in the Movie when it was so bad it descended into self parody. Lackluster cardboard characters, irrelevant and unresolved side plots, and complete lack of understanding of actual flying ( NO , the Dumb one should not get a break and be allowed fly, he would get the crew killed, Duh! ) , combined with poor special effects make for 3 hours of my life I shall never get back.

history.title: Deep Impact (Special Collector's Edition)
history.review_title: This film is so bad, so dumb
history.text: This film is so bad, so dumb, so scientifically illiterate , that is rates as fun in the same sense " Plan Nine from Outer Space " was fun.

history.title: Jerome Bixby's The Man from Earth
history.review_title: If you like your Sc FI cerebral and original, this stage play transfered to film fits the bill.
history.text: Essentially a stage play transferred to film with little change, this remarkable, and fun, film spends the evening with a group of Professors saying goodbye to a colleague who is more than first meets the eye. No action, all dialogue, all on one set, it is interesting film and truly different. I would have given it 5 stars but they blew the ending with a ridiculous coincidence and a serious inconsistency. If you like your sci fi cerebral and original, go for it.

history.title: Go Tell the Spartans (DVD)
history.text: Burt, playing the tired fought out but competent Army major again, in one of his finest performances. Set in Nam this clichéd filled " B" movie may not tell you much about Vietnam but it does tell you about the old U S Army circa 1964 , before it was destroyed by the War.

history.title: Aces High
history.text: This is an attempt to remake " Journey's End" by setting it in the Sky with Pilots instead of infantry officers. It did not work. it lacks the subtlety and Character development that made the original a stage hit in 1929. Quite a waste of a first class cast.

history.review_title: When was the last time you saw Sci-Fi Chartacters acting rationaly, operatives who are trained for their job?
history.text: One of the few Sci-Fi shows ever done to have intelligent well thought characters. The characters act like they actually have some training and motivation for their mission. When was the last time you saw sci fi characters acting rationally and as thought they were real operatives? Putting personal feelings aside and getting on with the mission as in real life, instead of obsessing over personal foibles. The plots are rational and fit together. This level of writing and execution is truly rare in Hollywood. Highly recommended!

history.review_title: An intelligent reimagining of Dick's classic mindbender.
history.text: An intelligent reimagining of Dick's classic. The writers have achieved the rare feat of expanding on the original without betraying it's origins or indulging in the usual sin of rewriting a classic in the mistaken belief it is being improved. Please tell me we get a Season Three ? This is the best Sci-Fi since Firefly. Why is it from a bookseller?

history.title: Deutschland 83: Season 1
history.review_title: The movie makes you feel like you are in 1983
history.text: Captures the period and place. The movie makes you feel like you are in 1983. I was a Marine Officer at the time and the filmmakers have made a real thriller that actually makes you root for the Commie Spy. Quite a feat. The film also avoids easy or trite answers and endings. Top notch Cold War spy thriller with a touch darkness reminiscent of Film Noir.

targets.title: The Vietnam Chronicle: A Rumor Of War

history.review_title: Excellent beginning establishing the main villain who is a really bad guy
history.text: All these complaints of the brutal violence of the opener are misplaced. It was no more violent, only a little more graphic than what you have been seeing for years. Only in this case it happened to main characters. Sure you feel it, hard to watch, but no more gory or violent than what you have seen. The opener was excellent. They left us with a cliffhanger about a character getting killed (no spoilers here), and if they killed one of the tangential characters everyone would complain. Now people have stopped complaining about the cliffhanger and whine about the violence. Were you folks watching the show for the past 5 years? Anyways, on to why the opener is great. (Possible mild spoilers). Rick and the group grew very confident over the years, always ending up on top. This episode is so good because it made absolutely sure the audience knew that they were not on top anymore. A brand new direction for the show that we have not seen before. Hopefully the new direction will be done well to keep the show fresh and exciting as always. Second reason the opener was so good is that it established the villain, Negan, with the audience in just one show. What I mean is for hero's to do heroic things, they need a good villain to seem heroic. If you villain is weak, then that make your hero's story weak. You cannot have a great hero without a great villain. Seems WD knows this and was able to establish that villain on one episode, rather than building it over a season like the did with the Governor. The fact that so many feel emotionally spent and recoiled at the violence and gore, which again is only mildly worse than stuff shown for years, means the WD did it right. We KNOW Negan is bad, real bad. And we can tell there will not be some sudden victory by Rick and the gang over Negan halfway through the season. This guy is somebody they are going to have to deal with for a while. They did a good job with Negan beyond the violence, good acting, good story supporting Negan's bona fides as being a very bad guy. And to naysayers on the violence: I didn't hear you complain when this was done to others, or all the extreme gore with the walkers. No you are feinting waif's? Please. You are not worthy to watch the show lol.

history.review_title: Bad acting, bad writing, implausible action, and a ridiculous villain
history.text: So they got some decent actors for the Enterprise crew, started building them up in the first two films, then this movie just stopped trying. The story is the space equivalent of an action movie with too many chase scenes, action movie dialogue (bad), and a Chris Pine who clearly does not want to be doing this part anymore. Pine as Kirk literally seems uninterested in what is going on around him and his acting shows it. Bad, really bad. Won't give anything away but as you might imagine bad things happen to the ship and crew and Pine's Kirk character doesn't even wince. Doesn't seem to care when much or all his crew are put in really really mortal danger. Same straight faced Pine not even showing any emotion at all. Then the plan to save things is just strung together as they go and appeared quite implausible. Hey we got this spaceship, been buried 100 years, rusting, broken..Scottie get it in running order in 10 minutes. And guess what, he does. I am willing to suspend a fair amount of skepticism to enjoy a fantasy movie like Trek, but this one asks you suspend your ability to think..completely..so that this movie would appear better than it is. I would need a lobotomy to think this was a good movie. Also all the comaradery among the crew is missing. To sum up, if you like action movies that are wall to wall chase scenes and dialogue that is much like that type of movie, you will enjoy this one. If you were like me you thought the first was good, the second slipped badly but was not a failure, if you agree to this point, then I don't recommend you see this movie as it is much worse than the second movie.

history.review_title: Good for kids, less so adults
history.text: This one totally lacks the originality and humor of the Finding Nemo. Also this one is probably more entertaining for the kids than adults. Namely the story line is weak. Kids might find some humor in this and the animation will entertain them. But for me, wasn't funny, boilerplate story, and geared too much for kids for adults to like it as much as finding nemo.

Excellent movie. I really had my doubts about them bringing a magical hero to the big screen and making it work. But work it did, and well. Then I wondered how might this hero will tie in with the rest of the Marvel universe? Well you find out at the end, and that should work well too and it makes sense. Also a visually beautiful movie as well. A rating from me. Not A+ as I thought the acting of Dr. Strange had some small, very small weak spots in the beginning, but nothing major.

Loving this show. I wasn't sure if they would be able to pull off a show like this but they have. Season one was great. Just started season 2 and it is even better so far. Lot funnier it seems. Ash is great. Well worth watching;

history.review_title: For the love of god can't anyone in Hollywood write a good script?!
history.text: The acting was much better here than the last 2-4 alien related movies including the predator ones.. The visuals were good except the various aliens are missing a certain realism to them, like bad CGI or something. The alien of the first two movies more or less were ambush hunters, here they are more stalking hunters. Not that there is anything wrong with that but it does affect how the tension plays out typically for the worse. It wasn't that scary really, and that is part of why this movie is not that good. It lacks any build up of fear, it is just kind of a movie where there a couple aliens killing people. This is the next problem: the writing. For the love of god, why can't Hollywood write a script that is plausible based on human nature. Some of the decisions made in this movie are mind numbingly stupid, as in I don't care how stupid somebody is, they still would not make those decisions. Without spoilers, the overall purpose for the events revealed in the movie don't make total sense. OK, they happened, but why? I guess they spent 200 million on the effects then hired junior high school students to write the script and story line. Also the characters are not developed here due to time and the number of characters introduced. If they could write a good script they could have given some depth to the characters so you actually care about them. They did that in the first movie why can't they do it here?

history.title: Salvation
history.review_title: This isn't what scientists and DOD are like
history.text: Watched the first half hour and couldn't take more. This may be unique to me given I am a scientist and actually did work with the government. So what is my problem? This is so far from reality that is impossible to watch (if you know about stuff like this). This is not even remotely how discoveries are made, how the information is transmitted, nor is this what it is like to work in DOD. DOD in this show is sort of a mish mash of DOD, CIA, and NASA. The second thing is the Hollywood dialogue. Nobody talks like this, it is just silly, can't stand shows with a Hollywoodized version of how people talk and interact. This never happens like this anywhere, and certainly not at DOD. If you know nothing about any of this then you might like it, so far their technical approach is reasonably accurate for diverting the asteroid (but in reality they could not do it in the time they have).

history.review_title: Good start for a new show.
history.text: Shows some promise. It is probably more of a 3 and a half star rating. Couple things right off. This is not Family Guy or anything remotely like it. I have seen reviews that complained it is not funny. As far as I can tell it is a serious sci fi show with some mild, mild humor thrown in. This reminds me of the original Star Trek in feel with just a little more real life banter going on between crew members. So if it is meant to be mostly serious then they need to make the show more exciting (but understand the first episode has to introduce everyone so it is going to be a little slower). So maybe it will work. I myself would go with the more serious format with some appropriate (but funnier than this episode) humor thrown in, rather than using it to spoof sci fi shows. Make the funny moments funny, but not so ridiculous that it becomes a spoof. So needs a little work and I think with some decent writing and the characters introduced it could work. Time will tell.

history.review_title: Didn't quite live up to the hype.
history.text: Given how so many raved about this movie I was kind of surprised I didn't think it was great. I am a sucker for superhero movies but this one seemed rather dull and Wonder Woman fighting the bad guys was just not that impressive. So to my own surprise only giving 3 stars.
Absolutely great show. Looking forward to season 3!

history.title: Big Combo, The - 1955 (Digitally Remastered Version)
history.text: Too bad because the cast is good, however, for anyone who has watched enough movies, they know that a good cast does not a good movie make.

history.title: Trail of '98
history.text: This is one of the best Silents I have seen. What makes it so good is both the acting for the time and the location filming. I mean, I can't see how the treks through that kind of weather could have easily been filmed in studio. It certainly looked authentic. It had to be Alaska, especially, the Chilkoot Pass scene. Also, I like Robert W. Services poems (The Shooting of Dan McGrew and The Cremation of Sam Mcgee, among others) and this movie is based on, I believe, the only novel Service ever wrote. The novel was written in 1910 and the movie was made in 1928.

Relatively interesting movie with a parched artistic flair. The anticipation of the outcomes of a noble victim, a fiery and passionate whore and a a fellow who never got out of the corner with his dunce cap (an allusion for those of the more mature persuasion) holds some surprises for you, the audience. John Hurt and Terrence Stamp make the movie.

Actually, my comments cover the episodes in the first 4 1/2 seasons, not just Season 3. Nice idea but a little too much political correctness in some episodes. Also, a little too maudlin at times, although mostly a balanced presentation, pretty good over all. I like Kyra and her crew. I enjoyed the fellow who plays Chief Pope and who also has appeared in the Coen Brothers movie, "Burn After Reading." He is equally as good here and you get to see much more of him in this series; he does a great job. I also was interested to see that in real life Kyra is the wife of Kevin Bacon. As to Kyra's boyfriend/ husband in the series, I had to keep wondering whether he ever goes to work or just mostly stays around the house, cleaning up and looking after the cat; not exactly a Rambo, more like the stereotype of the husband of Margaret Thatcher. Finally, it's a bit of US version of the 1990s "Prime Suspect" with Helen Mirren and, in its way, a nice, down-home kind of rival. Again, I like it enough to continue watching through the final 7th season.

history.title: Newhart: Season 4
history.text: Pretty good lines and nice characterizations. Annoyingly, over-the-top canned laughter, but still I like the characters in this series.

history.title: Rhapsody in Blue
history.text: Nicely done movie. The (nearly?) complete Rhapsody was inspiring. Great shadow work and impressive instrumentation

Great story. The attempts to give humanity to those searching for and killing the killers was a good idea but is much too overdone and significantly takes away from the movie. Steiger's role is interesting as the "bad" good guy.
Pretty hokey and a poor print.

history.review_title: Well done film Noir by the Coen Brothers
history.text: This is a great B&W film noir by some of the industry's best. Thornton reflects a desire to achieve something meaningful through others and the irony is pretty thick at even turn. No doubt the brothers have listened with a keen ear to the laughter of the gods at humanity's sure fire plans for themselves.

history.review_title: The Unequal Distribution of Being a Little Bit Pregnant
history.text: An enjoyable romp with some bizarre characters. The struggles of the haves and have-nots, the law-abiding and the criminal, the pure-in heart and the demons. Then there are just those who are getting by just fine and have more than their share. It's all in good fun and fun it is!

history.title: The Gamers: Dorkness Rising
history.text: I haven't read all the other reviews but I'll assume it's similar to what I'm about to write. I didn't have high hopes for this film because it looks cheesy but man, it delivered. It's a funny take on Dungeons & Dragons. I've only played the game once or twice but that was enough for me to get the "inside" jokes. The only thing I found boring was the "office" scenario. I don't want to spoil things for peeps but that sequence was just plain boring. I want many sequels or similar movies like this one. So good. I don't know why Scifi channel haven't bought the rights to this.

history.title: Wanted (Single-Disc Widescreen Edition) [DVD]
history.text: Yes, this movie has CGI and action. And that's about it. I felt the story just lacked in any credibility whatsoever. And if you're going to do fantasy/sci-fi stuff, then let's bring in a good story behind it. The whole narrative part doesn't work... see Fight Club for how 1st person narrative makes the movie interesting. I'll say this, the movie was interesting at first. I wanted to see him train and get to know his powers and get revenge. But once the training started, that's where they lost me. It didn't make any sense, how they trained him. Lots of BS posturing and very secretive. We're just going to torture you and that's how you'll learn BS. And it was really over the top gore and violence. Others have said this is like Matrix and some even suggested this is better than the Matrix. I disagree. It's not like the Matrix. The Matrix actually had a story behind it. And it was compelling. And it got cooler as it went along. This movie was not any of that. I suppose the best thing about this was the CGI. And even that was meh.

history.title: Pretty Ugly People
history.text: Maybe, I'm just not the right demographic for this movie. I mean, the title did explain what this movie is about. Pretty people on the outside, ugly people on the inside. And maybe I was fooled by the way the cover and opening sequence seemed to make this movie a bright, cheery, funny movie like Sandra Bullock or Hugh Grant. Possibly spoilers: This movie was rarely funny. And what I could not get past was how such horrible people stay friends with each other. I could not imagine being friends with most of them. Maybe the steward (who was a saint or an idiot to keep going back to that narcissistic new-skinny chick, and helping that gay dude), and maybe the small-penis dude, who seemed like a genuine guy. I mean, really, they are just ugly people and halfway through I just wanted a meteor to come down and wipe most of them out. And I started wishing Freddy from Friday the 13th would appear. And yes, I get it. People are like that because of their past and things that happened to them. But, c'mon, to make us sit through an entire movie of hateful people (except for 2), shoot, I get enough of that everyday. I don't need to see this and again, I don't think any of them would stay friends with each other. Here are the pros: nicely acted, there are pretty people to look at, nice cinema photography. I suppose the direction is good too. It's the story I hated. I would say pass on this movie.

history.title: Shelter
history.text: Just finished watching it. Great love story. In the gay genre it's at the top of the heap (the gay movies out there are really not so good). In the non-gay genre. It's still at the top of the heap. It's a fantastic film. Great acting. Great cinema-photography. Great direction. I wanted to fall in love and surf after seeing this movie. One small problem is at the end. They didn't tie up the loose end of who will look after a certain someone with back problems. -------- Jan 2011. Since I wrote my review, I've viewed a bunch of gay-themed movies. And it's really hard to find a nice, well-acted, directed, gay love story. This is more a coming out/love story but it's still sooooo nice. And tops the list of gay movies. I feel it's up there with Latter Days, Just Say Love, Thirteen or So Minutes (a short film), All Over the Guy and Antartica (I liked how straight forward the movie showed gay relationships). Thinking of Shelter and certain moments in the movie in particular, gives me just a nice feeling of warmth and love.

history.title: Brotherhood
history.text: This isn't a feel good movie. I'll be honest, I got bored after awhile and I felt the nazi story was distasteful. There is violence in the movie and it's not like Bruce Willis, lots of guns, and you know nobody gets hurt. This seems more real. The acting, the directing was good. The movie visually was dark... I don't know if that's just the landscape of the filming, but it wasn't beautiful. It was gloomy. I probably would have given this 4 stars if it wasn't enveloped in Nazi stuff. While there's a love story, it's not Pretty Woman / Julia Roberts love. It's more primal and hidden. I suppose, as another review posted, it is a little like Brokeback, 1 dude is more willing to dive in, while the other is torn and wants to stay hidden. But Brokeback was set in beautiful landscape where they were herders, this tale is, oh, they are Neo-Nazis. So one is surrounded by beauty, and this movie is not. I can't recommend it because I'd rather see an uplifting movie. If you want drama and don't mind evil getting punished then see this. Plus, the dudes aren't really out. The love is hidden. There's gay love but it's not a romance story. Or a traditional romance story.

history.title: Long-Term Relationship (Widescreen)
history.text: Based on the good reviews here I watched this movie (altho I was hesitant because Gone but Not Forgotten, another Matthew Montgomery movie, sucked majorly) and was disappointed. The premise seemed ok. But just ok. The acting was meh. Background music was a little weird. Direction... ok. As others have said, there was some nudity. But even that was boring. I couldn't help but start to surf the web after 15 mins. And really started surfing the web after 30 mins. I'm writing this review as the movie plays actually. Nothing in the movie holds your attention. The manufactured drama. The rare bits of comedy. Nothing. It's boring. And I'm not certain what would make this movie better. I don't want to be mean, but maybe better acting, scripting, direction, music, even cinematogrophy. Maybe if there were a few stellar things like acting, or the script or the location shoots, then one might be more interested. And I do realize it's low budget, but there are other low budget movies that held my attention better but were more bare bones in sets.

history.title: Children Of God
history.text: I have to add my review to the others that I didn't care about the characters either. So, while the acting may have been strong, something was missing. Also if you're looking for an uplifting, romantic gay movie... you won't find it here. What I will say was that other parts of the film seemed well done. There was success in the tying up of the pieces throughout the film, so kudos to the writer, director. The cinematography was shot decently. There was definitely lots of angst with all the characters. Yet, I felt nothing for any of them. Maybe it needed more character development. I was disappointed because I expected it to be wonderful. And it wasn't. Even in it's genre. I thought it might be a romantic film, which it wasn't. It was more docu-drama or just drama. But, I'm rating this more on the film itself and not my disappointment in wanting a romantic story and finding a depressing drama. SPOILER: The ending is NOT uplifting. IMO. And while probably close to reality in the Islands, it's not something I'd like to see.

history.title: Breakfast With Scot
history.text: Good production values. This is not one of those gay movies produced on a small budget or at least it didn't look like it. The acting was top notch all around. Direction was good. The story was good except for one small point... and it might be considered a spoiler. SPOILER POSSIBLY: If you read the review, you know most of the story and how the gay couple are closeted in public. What I found weird is how they seem closeted in private. And maybe this is part of Eric's journey of growth. But I found it hard to believe that the only gay thing they do together is "maybe" have sex (and I'm not even sure how affectionate that would be). I mean, this couple did not seem like a couple. That was the one thing that struck me odd about the movie. Overall, tho well done and I did like the main storyline of not conforming to gender roles and acceptance.

The acting was decent, hence the two stars. And production values decent as well. Storyline had some promise... the electronic aspect. But it was very contrived. And IMO, other than the main character, every character was bitchy, and irrational. It did seem 80s like... but at least the successful, 80s campy movies were funny. This wasn't funny. There were some cute guys to look at but that's not enough.

history.title: Longtime Companion [DVD]
history.text: Saw this years ago and it still affects me. It's sad, informative, well acted, directed. It shows different facets of gay people and how it impacted so many lives. Just well done.

history.title: Newhart: The Complete Fifth Season
history.text: I am a big fan of Bob Newhart in both of his shows. However, season 5 is a significant step or two down from the prior 4 seasons. The characters are the same, but the writers seem to have lost their way. Some of the shows are almost cringe worthy. The amusing characteristics of the gang in prior seasons have been repeated over and over again and exagerated to the point of them becoming cardboard characters. How many times do we have to see: "Hi, I'm Larry and these are my brothers . . . " Even Bob spends more time doing one-sided phone conversations, the routines that made him famous as a stand-up comedian. Buy it to complete your collection, but not for the enjoyment of prior seasons.

history.title: Masterpiece Mystery: Endeavour, Series 3
history.text: The first two series were fascinating with good character development and excellent plots. This Series 3 went far off track. Some of the stories were laughable they were so ridiculous. And, . . . characters had personality transplants and acted out of character. Seriously disappointing.

history.title: Beck: Episodes 25-27 (Set 9) [DVD]
history.review_title: ... prior episodes and these newer ones I feared the worst. Many (most
history.text: After the hiatus betwwen prior episodes and these newer ones I feared the worst. Many (most?) long running shows loose steam after many years and end with a wimper. These got better -- the plots and acting are first rate.

history.title: The Disappearance
history.text: If you liked Broadchurch (and you should) you will like this. Very well acted with many twists and turns (perhaps one or two too many). A good look at what a disappearance does to a family and friends.

history.title: Castle: Season 8
history.review_title: How Bad is this Season -- Very, Very Bad
history.text: A fine series comes to a sad end. As others have noted the most serious problem is the writing -- the plots are often so ridiculous that it is hard for the actors to do other than go through the motions. It would be unfair to say the many of the actors "mailed in" this season but I don't think the entire ensemble gave it their best at all times.

history.title: House of Lies: Season 1
history.text: First a bit of disclosure: I watched only episode 1 of season 1, and then only because it starred Don Cheadle. As others have noted it is crude and cynical with little true humor. What a waste of talent.

history.title: Newhart: Season Seven
history.review_title: Stephanie and Michael Dominate the Plots
history.text: I never thought the Newhart Show was quite as good as his previous The Bob Newhart Show. Bob is always great, but the supporting cast was somewhat weaker -- not bad, but not quite so excellent. Season 7 gets 3 stars because Stephanie and Michael dominate many of the plots and they are just plain silly.

history.title: Masterpiece Mystery! Grantchester Season 3
history.review_title: Where are the Mysteries -- Gone to Soap Operas
history.text: This once delightful series has taken a serious wrong direction. Mysteries have taken a back seat to soap opera relationships. The mysteries seem an afterthought and the various relationship are all seriously troubled.

history.title: Murdoch Mysteries: Season 10
history.review_title: A Big Step Down This Season
history.text: This once fine series took a step or two down this seaon. The show was always a combination of mystery, comedy, banter, and quasi science. This year much of the banter is absent as key characters are absent or appear minimally in several episodes. And the plots -- well many of them are just plain silly. Unfortunately the last episode, the one that prompted this review, is one of the silliest I have seen in any series. What were they thinking. I read in another review that many of the episodes this season were spoofs of movies, books, etc. I could recognize one or two of these, but many more escaped me and seemed just ridiculous.

history.title: Midsomer Murders: Series 19, Part 2
history.text: Yes, the price is ridiculous, but that is not the reson for this poor review. The two episodes in series 19, part 2, are truly weak and somewhat silly. The attempts to incorporate personal lives of the police are equally silly. And, somewhat late in the production the order must have come from on high: "more diversity." Gays and minorities have been inserted into these stories in rather artificial ways. At least you immediately know they won't be on the list of potential bad guys. All-in-all a sad release; the end can't be far off.

history.title: North America
history.review_title: Starts with an adorable funny segment containing mountain goats and nannies
history.text: Starts with an adorable funny segment containing mountain goats and nannies. After that, it shows fighting for survival in the wild. Our pioneer forefathers would be upset with the concept of "born to be wild" since many generations spent lots of time and money taming this country. Guess they are referring to animals only. The movie makers are REVEALED in the second DVD, when it becomes obvious that it was made by a bunch of AUSTRALIANS. The segment on Belize is hilarious. Obviously someone from down under smearing jungle plants on himself. (Why don't they know enough to wear tropical clothes for protection? Slacks, long sleeved top, jungle hats, pith helmuts)? The film includes Belize, Panama, Costa Rica, etc. in North America. They are Central American countries. Overall, scenery is gorgeous, doubt if that is original.

history.title: Peter Pan - Starring Mary Martin [Blu-ray)
history.review_title: This is a wonderful transfer of this classic 50's TV version of Mary ...
history.text: This is a wonderful transfer of this classic 50's TV version of Mary Martin's "Peter Pan. Two black & white versions are here. But I was very disapointed that it was not in color. A leflet describing the TV production says that a color version wasen't available. But I remembered that I had a VCR version I bought 20 years ago, but never played. Well on unpacking my Christmas stuff, I found it and stuck it in my old VCR Player just to see if it was interesting. And low & behold it was in color and very nice and clear and the sound was as good as to be expected from a VCR tape.. It was produced out by an a company called Goodtimes. Now I'm wondering why this colored version could not have been included in this newer set! For the price I originally paid for it - they should have. So if any of you folks still has their ole' VCR up & running I would advise you to try to get a color version on Goodtimes VCR version if you can find it.

history.title: Feud Season 1
history.review_title: And it was wonderful. Like them or not Bette Davis and Joan ...
history.text: This has got to be the most unique TV series in years. And it was wonderful. Like them or not Bette Davis and Joan Crawford were two of the most famous movie stars of all time. Their legend and movies will long live on long after we are gone. There is no doubt about that. Most female stars of today cannot hold a candle to these gals. They will be forgotten. In the beginning of this series I thought that Susan Sarandon was the best of the two portraying these two giants of the Golden Age of Hollywood, but as the series moved on Jessica Lange was getting better and better as Joan Crawford. I didn't think Jessica looked or had a speaking voice like Joan, but her performance as Joan Crawford was amazing and I actually got to feel sorry for the character which I never thought would happen. And I loved the actress wh o played Joan Crawford's aid "Mama Sieta". She deserved at least an Emmy nomination for her role. But as far as who should get an Emmy, Susan or Jessica - I say give them both the award. We will never see this lind of great acting again by such two good sports in tackling these demanding roles. Bette Davis has always been my favorite movie star and actress and always will be. I like Joan Crawford, but Bette is my all-time favorite.

history.title: Lady in the Dark - 1954 TV Production
history.review_title: "Lady In The Dark" is a good reminder of how TV used to be.
history.text: This is a wonderful, beautiful BLAST from the past. It makes me glad that I am old enough to have seen shows such as this. It is proof once again that TV was better in it's infancy than it is today. This disc is not in color as it was originally telecast back in 1954. Color television was just starting out and very few shows were in color. Max Liebman a great showman of the day would produce and direct a color special about every month in the 50's. And to chose such a sophisticated Broadway show as "Lady In The Dark" was probably very risky at the time. The Paramount motion picture version starring Ginger Rogers in the 40's was a disappointment. Mainly because they took out most of the musical numbers from the original B'way show. Even "My Ship" ! Now how stupid was that ! Ginger looked beautiful in the film and it was a chance for her to carry a musical by herself, without Fred Astaire or anyone else. But they ruined it for her. But Ann Souther who was a very popular TV star at the time was chosen for the lead as Liza Elliott and Ann did a sensational job. Her singing voice should have been used more often on other projects. Warning: this is a old show and it shows because of the quality at the time and maybe not as clear as you may wish for and it is in black & white, but none of that should matter for REAL nostalgia buffs. The book is by Moss Hart and the music is by Ira Gershwin and Kurt Weill. Carleton Carpenter almost steals the show in every scene he's in. Remember Carleton from singing "Aba Dabba Honemoon" and "Row, Row. Row" with Debbie Reynolds ? The production numbers are done beautifully. It almost reminds you of those glorious MGM musicals. I believe that most of the 'good old TV has been destroyed through the years, so this is a treasure. Paul Newman once said that he learned much of his craft through his television work like "Playhouse 90" and "Westinghouse Presents" and "Kraft Theatre" and such shows. The problem with a show like "Lady In The Dark" is that it reminds you of the actual poor quality of drama and TV productions that we have TODAY. Anyway I suggest getting this great musical and see for yourself how great television shows used to be in The Golden Age of Television.

targets.title: Love At First Bite / Once Bitten [Blu-ray]

history.text: I wanted to like this movie. I really tried to like this movie. Unfortunately this film has not aged well, and leaves one feeling like they just ate a bag of candy when they really wanted steak and potatoes! Most of the acting is weak, although Rip Torn and Cornel Wilde hold their own. But the use of lousy still photos to show flashback memories, and some wretched music detract from the message wow this film. Worse yet, what was considered in its time to be editing worthy a Academy Award nomination just looks abysmal in today's film environment, showing that we have come along way, baby, in regards to editing. Listening to poorly recorded voice overs while looking at still photo images that Grandma could have shot better, really gets old fast. There are very few portions of this film that hold up all these years later, and I say that as a huge fan of 60's films. While there may have been a story in there somewhere, it gets lost in the poor production work.

history.review_title: Solid Fun and Guns in Aussie Land
history.text: Tom Selleck has never thrilled me in movies or TV, and he still doesn't in Quigley Down Under. However, I found this to be a solid flick, with a good story, and elements of classic '60s and '70s westerns that I love. A bit "spaghetti", a bit traditional, but a lot different due to the overall subject matter, Quigley entertains well. Even though this film is a bit long, it never gets boring. The blend of the Aussie aspects, (aboriginals, Australian scenery, music touches), makes for an enjoyable cinema experience.

history.title: The Wanderers [Blu-ray]
history.text: Much more than I expected. Being a fan of vintage "gang" films, this one satisfied and surprised. Some good acting, good script and dialogue, and decent production. Not an award winner in my opinion, but plenty of fun to watch and fits with the timeframe of the story. I give it five stars because I would indeed watch this again, and more than once.

history.title: Vigilante Force
history.review_title: Not the Best of Two Actors I Usually Enjoy!
history.text: I remembered this as a much better flick...but this DVD let me down. Kinda poor quality, especially image quality lacking. I know this is a 70's film, and I keep that in mind...and in fact, I liked this in the cinema when I first saw it....but this has to be Kristofferson's worst acting job of his career. (I typically love to watch him, as well as Jan Michael Vincent...but wooden acting here and lousy direction combined with low film imagery forces me to only give it a 3 star rating. I like it for the collection value mainly.

history.title: Cracking Up (a/k/a Smorgasbord)

I love Jerry, but not this particular flick.

history.title: Dune
history.review_title: Great production design ruined by the worst casting since Firestarter.
history.text: Somehow I just can't picture Gurney Halleck, the lean hardened fighting man, as a lumpy Irishman. In fact, the casting director seemed have cast lumpy people in general aside from a handful of parts. Even the pretty people are terribly chosen. While I like William Hurt, he was woefully miscast as the dark, brooding Duke Leto. Seriously, aside from a few extra's nobody looked right for their part. While I don't expect a slavish adherence to the author's description I do expect at least an attempt to get things close out of respect for the author's vision.

history.title: Neptune Factor, the (1973)
history.review_title: Another guilty pleasure only made better by it being ridiculous.
history.text: I am pretty sure the genesis of this movie was a screenwriter stuck staring at a salt-water aquarium in some waiting room and thought "I can make a movie about this...". Most of the underwater footage was obviously shot in an aquarium, and the plot that gets us there is razor thin. I have to admire the fact that the movie feels no obligation to explain much of anything - you just have to take everything at face value. Still, I enjoy this movie despite its sheer silliness. The current DVD copy available is a pretty good transfer, so I am looking forward to the HD quality to see how that looks in comparison.

history.title: The Night Stalker/The Night Strangler (Double Feature) [DVD]
history.text: As a kid growing up in the 70's I loved these MTV movies and the series that followed. Watching these movies again decades later I can see some of its flaws, but the stories are still solid. The zeitgeist of the time was in full display: government's sole job was to keep people in the dark somehow resonates today, but with less conviction that doing the right thing is an obligation of the man who knows the truth. As for this release the transfers are decent enough quality, with only a little color loss, no noticeable scratches and clear sound. My only complaint about this, and the reason for my 4/5 stars is that they put this out on one double sided disk. My luck with keeping them scratch free is spotty and frankly I hate them.

history.title: Dr. Strange
history.text: I bought this mostly out of nostalgia, having watched it when it was first broadcast. It didn't disappoint: it still isn't very good. Watching it again I can see why it didn't make much of a splash. Frankly, the story is a lot of not much. If they had stayed truer to the source it might have stood a chance, but it was so watered down and anglicized it lost its mystery and the sense of other-worldlyness that made the comic so good. Also, the costume he wears at the end is really lame; he sort of looks like the seventh Village Person. The one he gets earlier from the villain is a lot better. Still, no regrets in having added it to my comic-book movie collection.

history.title: Story of Wales
history.review_title: Good, but just not quite good enough.
history.text: The host is knowledgeable and personable enough, but I could never quite get the same sense of drama that a Simon Schama, Neil Oliver or even a Bettany Hughes brings to their productions. The beginning and end episodes especially play out less as history and more as chamber of commerce infomercial.

history.title: Science Fiction Theatre
history.review_title: What you've just seen is fiction of course....
history.text: They really should have called this show "Irresponsible Science Fiction Theatre" so many of the plots involved experimental treatments & devices being used without fully being tested. That aside, this show is an interesting bit of nostalgia. For my part, I derived more enjoyment from seeing classic actors like Deforest Kelly, Vincent Price and some others in their younger days. The stories themselves are almost uniformly predictable and serendipity rules. Part of this is because the running time for the actual story is further reduced from a far too short half hour by having the host demonstrate some scientific principle (often only peripherally related and occasionally wrong). Then once the story is over the host has to remind the audience that they just saw something that was made sup (A sad irony considering our current state of fake news). Aside from a handful of episodes you really just feel unsatisfied.

history.title: Ulysses
history.review_title: Recommended only if you are desperate to sort of see it again.
history.text: I have fond memories of this film, but this particular transfer is abysmal. Very poor quality and the sound is even worse. I hope that someday a remastered version or even a better quality print can be found and this can be released again.

history.title: Return to the Planet of the Apes - The Complete Animated Series
history.text: This series is a must for Planet of the Apes fans & fanatics. I am of the former variety but I am also a fan of classic Saturday morning cartoons, and my local NBC affiliate didn't show more than a handful of episodes.I was really happy to finally see the whole series. Unfortunately the series obviously rushed into production and despite some really awesome still drawings the animation is substandard. The voice acting is also wooden and lifeless. One additional gripe: the DVDs are missing a "Play All" feature, which always ticks me off. After each episode you have to go back to the main menu, select the episode and then select play on the next menu. First world problems I know, but still - why not do it right?

history.title: NOVA: Search for the Super Battery DVD
history.review_title: Could have been better with a different host---a LOT better in fact
history.text: This had some really interesting information but overall it was ruined by the worst host Nova has had in recent memory. Sorry, I don't find his "schtick" all that amusing - in fact I find it annoying as hell.

history.title: Shaft Collection (Shaft / Shaft's Big Score / Shaft in Africa)
history.text: Love the movies, as I have since I saw them as a kid. This set however is another matter. The first two movies are on a single DUAL-SIDED DVD. If I had know that I would not have purchased this set. There is no excuse for cheap crap like this on a classic movie. Amazon should plaster a great big warning on all movies that come this way because the distributer doesn't care a damn about producing a quality product when they do this.

history.title: The Pillars of the Earth [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The Blu-Ray version is worth the few extra $$
history.text: This review will cover different aspects, but I'll comment on the Blu-Ray first: as of today, the Blu-Ray costs $4.50 more than the regular DVD. It's worth it, IMO. It has great image quality and sound. My wife had read the book, and then saw that a movie channel was running it (divided into 9 episodes). After watching the first two episodes, she ordered the Blu-Ray set. It got here quickly (Amazon's regular shipping), so we saw it before the movie channel had finished their nightly telecasts of the series. Both of us really enjoyed the DVDs. A lot. When we watch a movie based on a book, we rate the movie on its production, the acting, how engrossed we get in it, and how much we enjoy it, rather than how it compares to the book. I give this movie 5 stars. My wife gives the book 5 stars, and also gives 5 stars to the movie. The acting is first rate, the cinematography is outstanding, and the plot holds one's attention for the entire seven hours. That movie channel had me a little confused at first - they were televising 9 episodes, not 8. Was there a sequel that I couldn't learn anything about? The answer is NO, I think. It appears that channel put all eight episodes together, then divided it into 9 episodes. That way they could fit in more commercials. That's just a guess on my part, though. Even with them making 9 episodes, the TV version lacks some of the scenes that are on the DVDs. Bottom line: we're very glad we bought the DVDs, especially the Blu-Ray version.

history.title: Going My Way (Universal Cinema Classics)
history.review_title: Good image quality and it has subtitles
history.text: There's no need to add to the praise for the movie itself - enough has already been posted. (I agree with the positive reviews) My review will focus on the DVD instead. Amazon's product description didn't show the DVD having subtitles, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that it did have them. Image quality is pretty good - B&W with good tonal range, and sharpness was decent. Some film grain, but that is to be expected from movie film back in 1944. Audio quality? Not exactly hi-fi, but acceptable, considering the way they did movies back then.

history.title: The Caine Mutiny
history.text: I haven't seen this movie on regular DVD - only on TCM (HD). The Blu-Ray version is a lot better than the movie that was on TCM. The print is pretty clean, and the color is reasonably accurate. I've seen better sharpness in some Blu-ray discs, but this one was adequate. Aspect ratio was 16:9, and the DVD had subtitles. Bottom line: I'm glad I spent the extra $4.80 for the Blu-ray. This classic is worth it.

history.title: Larry McMurtry's Streets Of Laredo
history.text: I have 5 of the movies - I'd rate this one a little behind the original Lonesome Dove, and Return To Lonesome Dove - but I'd rate it higher than the two prequels Comanche Moon and Dead Man's Walk. (For what it's worth, I'd put Dead Man's Walk in last place.) James Garner wasn't quite as good in the "Captain Call" role as Tommy Lee Jones or Jon Voight, but he was sufficiently stoic and sometimes menacing. Sam Shepard was okay as "Pea Eye" (Timothy Scott was no longer available to play the role again - he died of lung cancer in '95). Alexis Cruz was the consummate sociopath / bad guy "Joey Garza". Bottom line: I'll give it 4½ stars. I'm glad we have it in the collection.

history.title: Above and Beyond
history.review_title: Tibbets himself had no complaints about this movie.......
history.text: I had seen this recently when TCM televised it. I liked the movie (even though I thought the acting was a little melodramatic), but I suspected they had taken many liberties with the facts - especially with Paul Tibbets' marriage. Well, I bought Tibbets' autobiography [[ASIN:0970366604 (this one)]] and found that he had devoted an entire chapter to the movie. Tibbets had no real complaints about it. Tibbets' book mentioned that Robert Taylor was a pilot at the time, and that he and Tibbets had become friends during the filming. The movie is black and white, but it has good tonal range - especially for a 60 year old movie. It is a DVD-R, with no special features except for a trailer, no scene selection, and no subtitles.

history.title: Tora! Tora! Tora! [Blu-ray Book]
history.review_title: 5 stars for the movie - but the packaging isn't wonderful.......
history.text: The movie is great (of course), and the Blu-Ray quality is outstanding. But I'm not in love with the packaging. There is no hard case - the DVD is tucked inside the back cover of the book (I posted an image). It kind of looks like an afterthought. The book will surely show some wear on the cover as it is slid in and out of the bookcase. I wish I had bought the regular Blu-Ray instead. To me, the book isn't worth the extra cost. Just my 2¢......

history.title: One Magic Christmas
history.review_title: “Write and tell me if you are really real.”
history.text: Incredibly disheartening, this secularized vision of Christmas as hell on earth, presents Ginny Grainger (Mary Steenburgen), a crabby disillusioned mother of two who of course HATES Christmas. At every opportunity she tries to ruin the event for her Christmas believing daughter Abbie. Pushing the boundaries of good parenting to the point where she is prepared to tell her daughter that there is no Santa!!! Ginny is cheerless and tyrannical and rides roughshod over everyone including her poor husband who has a dream of owning his own bike shop. Enter an extremely creepy “angel” (Harry Dean Stanton as Gideon) who stalks little Abbie while the family is about to lose their home. He tells the little girl that angels are dead people. He was, in fact, a cowboy. “I got myself drowned.” Death and destruction tramples its way through this depressing story that the late Roger Ebert called “a tactical miscalculation from beginning to end.” Why are so many Christmas movies completely devoid of joy!?

history.title: Snow Bride
history.text: This Christmas romance is about a gossipmonger (Katrina Law as Greta Kaine), who makes her living off of disparaging stories she writes about the rich and famous. She has no scruples, she doesn’t care if the stories are real or not. “These people don’t deserve our sympathy.” Her editor wants the dirt on a famous political family and encourages a competition between her and another sleaze merchant. Whoever gets the best dirt first gets to be the editor of the tabloid’s online magazine. Happily, Greta not only gets her foot in the door, she’s housed with the family in question, just waiting for an exposé to fall into her lap, no work required. Unfortunately, she is not the only ‘sneak’ in the house. An ex-girlfriend has shown up, switching from one brother to the other, intent on becoming a member of this family, or else! As presented, every character in this movie lies out of convenience. To soften what might be problematic, they’ve tried to present this as a screwball comedy. In which case, it works great if you don’t consider the fact that no one in this movie is virtuous.

history.title: A December Bride
history.review_title: “You have a good eye, it’s just not enough.”
history.text: Interior designer wannabe Layla (Jessica Lowndes) loses her fiancé when he’s introduced to her cousin, who promptly marries him. Said cousin whines to her mother that Layla won’t forgive her, so Auntie manipulates poor Layla at every turn, including coercing her into attending the marriage of her ex to her cousin! Apparently, Auntie believes backstabbing family members is permissible as long as they get something out of the deal. Who came up with this plot!? Fortunately, Layla gets fired from her crappy job and has a chance at a better boyfriend (Daniel Lissing as Seth Murphy) and a better job. If she will only stop pouting and look to the future instead.

history.title: Santa's Apprentice/Magic Snowflake Double Feature
history.review_title: “Christmas crackers, it’s worse than I thought!”
history.text: Two movies, two disks. The first movie introduces the dilemma. Santa has reached the age where he must start training an apprentice. The problem is, Santa doesn’t want to give up the job, doesn’t want to retire. All the ex-Santas convene, insisting that Santa pick a replacement. The requirements are: the boy must be named Nicholas, he must be an orphan, and he must be pure of heart. And in this case, he’s at the other end of the world, bullied by a monstrous oaf named Grincroch. The training doesn’t go well because young Nicholas is plagued with self-doubts and Santa isn’t that enthusiastic about the boy taking over. The sequel has Santa and his wife Beatrice leaving Nicholas on his own with just a bunch of elves, his pet, and a little girl from the orphanage, also conveniently named Beatrice. Without any adult supervision, Nicholas decides he needs to grow up fast and become responsible. Unfortunately, part of being Santa means remaining young at heart. With this new disaster, the magic snowflake in the basement starts to melt. In a state of panic, the Council of Retired Santas show up to rectify the matter, without knowing how. Bricks are involved! Both films are fun. I thoroughly enjoyed them. I hate to use this word, but they are cute. It was a happy find.

history.title: Christmas Melody
history.text: Mariah Carey’s footprints are all over this clunky Hallmark movie. She directed this less than sterling effort, snagged a bit part for herself, then insisted on rewriting the song that poor Fina Strazza had to sing. If she had been a real director she would have had enough sense to recast the role of Melissa. The woman misplaying that role was almost lifelike. The plot was rudimentary at best, a widow (Lacey Chabert as Kristin) takes her daughter home to Ohio after her business fails in L.A. She meets more than her fair share of ghosts from Christmases past. Apparently, most of her former classmates never made it out of that small town. The place is mishandled by Melissa, a woman who will brook no dissent from anyone, at any time, over any matter, without consulting her first, in which case the answer is always no. Melissa is played by a waxwork doll; her features never move. I believe she was animatronic. I almost liked this movie because of Lacey Chabert. Otherwise, it was remarkably bad. I blame that on the director.

history.title: Debbie Macomber's Mr. Miracle
history.review_title: “I like to play gin rummy and read.”
history.text: An amateur angel gets his first assignment on Earth, to help an indecisive student find her way in life. Unfortunately, this particular angel (misplayed by Rob Morrow) is a bit unorthodox, as in slightly demented. He is erratic and profoundly unstable. He blunders through his assignment with all the verve of a two-year-old. To say Morrow overacts limits the bizarre expressions he exhibits throughout this film. What’s worse, he’s supposed to be a teacher! Yet he acts like a halfwit. Morrow’s performance is shocking when juxtaposed with the normal characters that populate this simple tale of insecurity and self-doubt. And a lame romance was tossed in as well...as an afterthought. This is a complete misfire.

history.title: Lifetime Holiday Triple Feature [DVD]
history.text: Three so-called Christmas movies crammed together on one DVD. The first movie deals with a music hating mother who tries to stifle her daughter’s dream of becoming a singer. A contest is involved but actually has very little to do with this family melodrama. Dolly Parton almost sings Jingle Bells. The ending negates the reason for the plot in the first place. The second film also involves a faux contest. Twelve trees are decorated for Christmas. In this case no winner is announced, and no actual judging takes place. The contest is simply a ploy to save a building that a spoiled brat wants to tear down. The third film is about a party girl who travels back in time to visit her teen-self, so she can dispense useless advice to herself that she won’t follow. Again, another pointless exercise in futility. None of these movies are very Christmassy. A disappointing collection. Lifetime is no Hallmark.

history.title: Dragons: Gift of the Night Fury [DVD]
history.text: This brief “winter tale” concerns Berk and its population of dragons who inexplicably leave en masse. This migration excludes Toothless, incapable of flying without his rider, and Meatlug, held prisoner in secret. It is quickly revealed where the dragons went and why. Naturally, they return, if they didn’t it wouldn’t be much of a franchise. At best, this harmless tale is cute, but hardly Christmassy.

history.title: Piranha
history.text: Not quite a remake, this version of the classic film Piranha only has one thing in common with the original―the title. Otherwise, this is just another wild raunchy romp that relies too much on sleaze and base humor to get by. The plot is simplistic: spring break happens at the same time as a seismic event occurs, releasing a ton of prehistoric piranha into the lake they’re frolicking in. This movie made enough money to support a sequel that did not fair as well. If you’re expecting more than killer fish, plenty of gore, and bare breasts, you will be greatly disappointed. This is not the Citizen Kane of piranha films.

history.title: Piranha [Roger Corman's Cult Classics]
history.text: Signs, what good are they if no one pays attention to them. In this case, two hikers ignore the obvious NO TRESPASSING warning on a fence and go for a dip in something that clearly isn’t a swimming pool. They don't live to regret their mistake. And a classic was born. Enter skip-tracer extraordinaire Maggie (Heather Menzies), obligated to find the hikers, or what’s left of them. Instead, she unknowingly unleashes the voracious piranha, allowing them to snack their way to a summer camp filled with kids. Farther downstream is a resort, a smorgasbord of unwilling foodstuffs. The military gets involved, but not to help, to hinder. Perhaps the pesky piranha won’t make it that far. A sly rip-off of Jaws, it may take more of the little buggers to get you but get you they will. What’s one shark compared to these toothy devils? “People eat fish. Fish don’t eat people!”
