history.title: Hickok
history.review_title: Not historically accurate but reasonable action
history.text: I'm always bothered when Hollywood does a movie about historical figures because they rarely have anything to do with the person being depicted except this name. This movie starts with Hickok as a Union soldier attacking a Confederate gatling gun. The problem is very few gatling guns saw action in the Civil War, and they were all produced by the Union. The rest of the movie is similarly historically inaccurate. However, there is a lot of shooting and killing and so must be considered to be an OK Western

history.title: The Lost City of Z
history.review_title: Horrible film about an epic failure.
history.text: Absolutely horrible film. The story is of an English explorer who searches for a fabled lost city in the amazon. He has a lot in common with Spanish conquistidors, Sir Walter Raleigh and even Theodore Roosevelt after his presidency in that they all searched for a fabled lost city in the Amazon and didn't find it. The main character manages to get himself and his son killed in the process. There was absolutely no reason to make this prolonged movie about an epic failure. The movie states some ruins have been found in the present(21st century) but if they are the ruins with which I am familiar, they are a long ways away from where this turkey was looking. The story of a prolonged and epic failure.
Really dumb film about a woman who, when she prances around in a sandbox, she creates a giant monster that destroys Seoul, South Korea. Sounds dumb? It is.....
It's OK, but did they really need to make another spiderman. Also, spidey seems to be getting younger and younger. Now he is a freshman in high school. Maybe they should call him spiderboy

history.title: Wonder Woman (4K Ultra HD) [4K UHD]
history.review_title: Even though it is a comic book movie, it is well done.......
history.text: While I find it hard to endorse yet another movie about a comic book character, this one is at least well done, reasonably well acted and placed in a relatively unusual setting, World War I. Probably the best of the comic book movies.

history.review_title: Anyone who expects eight novels to be covered in a 90 minute movie is a fool..........
history.text: Having read the reviews before watching the movie, I can only ask, "Did we see the same movie?" OK, first I read the Steven King Novel(I believe there were eight of them, but it's been a while.). I never expect a movie to have all the details of a novel or a series of novels. One of my friends criticized a well done eight hour miniseries based on a novel because it didn't have all the details of the novel. My response, "Duh!!!!!!". Anyone who expects all the details of a novel to be incorporated into a movie or miniseries is a fool. Secondly, as much as I enjoyed much of the series, do the people with this complaint remember the last novel in the series, where the "crimson king" is a drooling idiot and the ending is a worst non-ending since the TV series "Lost" set an all time low for endings. Did these people even read the novels or are they just making a generic criticism? The Movie wasn't half bad for a 90 odd minute good vs evil sci fi type movie. Unlike many reviewers, I was disappointed in the casting of the gunslinger and imagine more folks would agree with me if it were not politically incorrect to do so. The casting of Jake and the Dark Man were good. The change in how the villains are trying to bring down the tower disappointed me at first, but I was able to accept the premise of the movie, and it was a decent adventure tale. One last complaint is motivation. You can understand the motivation of well done villains, wealth or power or such. Sauron wants absolute power over Middle Earth. I get it. However, these clowns just want to destroy everything. That would include themselves. What do they get out of it? Nothing. It doesn't make sense...... In conclusion, it is a decent good vs evil movie with a decent plot. Not great, not horrible. Better than most.

history.title: Dawson City: Frozen Time
history.review_title: Silent film clips from Dawson City. If this isn't something that interests you, don't get it.
history.text: Decided to watch this since I visited Dawson City a few years back. This film consists mostly of silent film clips found in an excavation of Dawson City. While some of the scenes are interesting, it is essentially one scene after another, presented in conjunction with some very annoying cacophonous music. Best to make it a true silent film and turn the sound off. While this film would be of absolutely no interest to the general population, for those who live in Dawson or have visited there may find it interesting. . It might be useful if you were a student writing a paper on Dawson. It essentially met my not very high expectations. It certainly didn't exceed them.

history.title: Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets
history.review_title: Movie is even dorkier than its name.
history.text: The first thing that hits you is the dorky title. Were they trying to make this film a box office flop? The intro wasn't bad where they start constructing the space station. Various humans pitch in and various alien come along and pitch in. Not bad. Then the intro music stops, and the movie dies in a deluge of bad acting, stupid plot and flashing lights that only a video game addict could love. The two main characters couldn't act to save their lives, stumbling over their lines. Then again, they didn't have much to work with. The movie is dorkier than its name.

targets.title: Once Upon A Time In America [Blu-ray]

history.text: I know everybody loves this film. The story that pulls at your heartstrings, about the poor little brown boy who finds his Mother after a very long time,and feels whole again. Its a Liberal's delight. And I'm a Liberal. I think this film would have been much better as a documentary, about the real story with the real people involved. As it is, its a manipulative, long -winded piece of filmmaking, that takes way too long to get to the point. Would have much better if it were about the time that Dev spent with his Mother and sister in India after he found them again, and not so much about poor Nicole Kidman in her red fright wig. and her kind of dysfunctional family way off in Tasmania. The acting by all the Indian characters in the film was wonderful, especially the little boy Saroo's older brother ,and their Mother. It gets kind of dicey however with Dev Patel's performance ,and why all the time spent with all his internal angst. He should have either accepted the support of his Australian family and girlfriend in his quest to find his birth Mother, or gotten off his behind, traveled to India and pursued his own quest. Way too much time was wasted getting to that point. I was glad I did not actually purchase this film and grateful that Amazon offered it for rent for only a buck. Thanks Amazon. That's about what it was worth.

history.title: Capital Games the Movie
history.text: Yikes! It's like they took a Sean Cody video, and made it into a terrible movie. So many problems here. Poor, unbelievable acting. Looks like everyone was reading their lines off of cue cards, a soundtrack that drowns out every salvageable moment, and really so many flip flops in how the two lead actors felt about each other, it was hard to keep track. Then there's the thing about the one actor that was supposed to be British, but he kept changing his accent, and has this gratuitous crotch shot that either proves he was Jewish or Muslim, or they just got it wrong all together. But they both do have pretty blue eyes. (Not nearly enough to salvage this turkey). This one is the Gay TeleNovella of the year ,where no one is actually expected to believe any of it. Its all done in fun as a parody, only the actors don't seem to know it. It should be listed as a comedy, of errors, and if you were watching it with a group of friends, have a game to spot everything that didn't make sense in the film. The winner would be tired because the list is so long, so he or she should get a good prize.

history.review_title: In the land of the twilight zone
history.text: What do living in Salt Lake City, the whitest people in America, chaste, non-sexual courtships, and living happily ever after, all have in common? Mormonism. It didn't dawn on me until a little into this film that that was the real theme of it. As presented in the film, it's not a bad thing at all to treat your love interest with respect and dignity, work hard to make ends meet in difficult situations,and wish for the fantasy of living happily after as the film states at the end. However, this movie borders on the twilight zone. Its a land where everyone is white, fit, hetro ,and smiles and laughs through every adversity. Two serious themes are presented ,and somehow just shucked off in the film. The Father, and breadwinner of the family, goes to jail for life for ponzi schemes, and the youngest daughter has a life-threading diagnosis of Leukemia. They are mentioned briefly and then just conveniently forgotten in view of the more serious story of hooking up the two eligible daughters with contestants from The Bachelor. I was scared, very scared after finishing this thing.

history.title: Free Fall
history.text: A very interesting and complex film. There is a prominent adage in psychology circles that what attracts people to either the military or police work as professions ,is an internal lack of order, and the need for rules from an external source. The adage seems to apply here. Mark, especially is a person who is looking for answers as to how to behave in society. He attempts to follow every rule presented to him, and mete them out, but gets completely thrown off by his attraction to his police classmate, Kay. I'm not at all convinced that Mark is gay. He is so self-centered that he seems to lack the capacity to engage emotionally with anyone ,and there is not much hope he will, even after deciding to leave the structure of his girlfriend and baby, and relationship with Kay. He'd best stay in the police department where the structure is clear, rigid and codified. Kay, on the other hand really has a chance to succeed in life. He may break away from the police department, is much more grounded about his sexual orientation and emotionally mature. The acting in the film and pacing is uniformly great. All the actors do a great job in their roles and it's interesting to see a slice of modern German society in action. An long known fact is that in societies where there are rigid cultural and gender rules, the incidents of homosexuality is much greater than in societies where the gender roles are much more relaxed. Germany has always been an overtly homophobic society and has had an underground of gay sub culture.It would be worthwhile to see how many gay folks there are in the German police department, nationwide. The other thing I enjoyed about the film is that not a scene in the movie was wasted. Even the small scenes seemed to be going somewhere and where there for a reason. Well worth buying the film to watch again at another time.

history.title: The Perfect Wedding
history.text: Fluffy, cheery, and everything but the kitchen sink. What were they thinking. This film can not make up its mind what it's supposed to be. A drama, a tragedy, a comedy, a dark comedy, a disaster movie? Maybe they thought up the story for this one in gay, teen summer camp, somewhere. While its supposed to be about finding love and celebrating it, its also about alcoholism, dementia, relationships going badly, miscommunication, adoption, and an endless list of other subjects thrown in willy nilly throughout the film. I just wished it would end, at some point. What makes it more tragic( there it is, that must be the genre) is that the actors really do try to do a good job in their respective roles. They mean well, they just don't know what they've gotten themselves into. Its really difficult for the viewer to know how they are supposed to feel about all the information that is presented here ,or what to do with it. The end.

history.title: The Perfect Family
history.text: A good film with a great message. Sometimes movies with a serious message are so heavy-handed that you're tired after seeing the film. This movie is a comedy/drama that deals with several serious issues,(divorce, faith, gay marriage, alcoholism, and love). The message of the film is ultimately that love trumps everything else. And the last scene of the film proves that. While on the surface, the film takes a well-earned go at the Roman Catholic Church, positive things are also presented about the church.When all is said and done, we are all flawed, and the quality that is always needed to overcome our imperfections is love. That's the overall feeling that The Perfect Family presents and succeeds at well.

history.title: I Wish
history.review_title: Let's get the folks back together.
history.text: Here's a story of some really nice kids with a dream. 7 young Japanese boys and girls from Kyushu get together in hopes of reuniting the mismatched parents of two of the children. The journey itself is the thing, as well as the relationships they have with various relatives involved in their lives. Of note, they are living in the grips of a very active volcano in Kagoshima, Kyushu, and I think that must have some symbolic significance to the lives of the children involved. If only more kids could behave as these children do, cooperating with each other, and having fun all the way.

history.title: Do You Take This Man
history.review_title: A failed attempt at a great theme.
history.text: This movie has a very interesting concept. Friends and family of two men going to get married, come to a heartfelt pre wedding party at the home of the couple. During the course of the evening, secrets are revealed that put a damper of whether the couple should go through with the wedding. Something really bothered me about the film, however, and I put my finger on it. There is no chemistry,whatsoever,between the couple, played by Anthony Rapp and Johnathon. They seem to go through the motions, say the right things,but the viewer doesn't believe for one minute that any of it is for real. Even the way they kiss. Also, they both have a very odd and heterogeneous group of friends. It would be difficult to see who these people they had chosen as friends would actually be friends in real life. Poor Macenzie Astin couldn't play gay if his life depended on it, and Hutch Hancock, was such a self centered narcissist, whose friend saw she? How Rapp ended up with the wonderful parents he and his divorced sister has is a mystery.They try to explain it themselves, but the great parenting is difficult to fathom. A wonderful and true conversations happens with Rapp and his old female best friend, 2/3ds through the movie. Had Rap been straight, the two of them sounded like a far better match than his marriage to Bennett. I can see that one ended in divorce. Anyway, an interesting attempt to portray a real story, but missing some important notes in credibility.

history.title: Advanced Ice Age Civilizations and Atlantis
history.text: This title has NOTHING to do with Graham Hancock or David Childress. It is entirely, fraudulently misrepresented, and full of very poor quality copied stock footage from very OLD unknown sources. The only qualified speaker "scientist" therein is Dr. Schoch. Having reviewed the unedited interview with him on disc 2, he repeatedly politely attempted to put straight several obvious misrepresentations presented him by the producers during his interview. Regardless, he was intentionally quoted out of context in the main presentation. This title is a very poor quality production, without academic, scientific, or factual foundation, put together by the producers/editors without valid understanding of their subject matter. Several completely irrelevant references are made to astronomical terms, geography, archeology and very well documented geologic time, ...all totally wrong, demonstrating a profound absence of logic and understanding by the producers and most of the non-scientist fringe authors being quoted as "experts". The "Ice Age" did NOT end in 1,500BC as presented herein. This absurd notion is pushed as if it were an accepted time frame. Dr. Schoch tried to explain in his unedited interview, yet they ignored him. Listening to them in the background of that interview, it seems that they were not even listening to him as they taped it. This title is entirely unrelated to the excellent research and interesting theories of Graham Hancock, David Childress and Dr. Schoch. I strongly recommend to NOT BUY THIS TITLE. We hope that Mr. Hancock will eventually release DVD's of his interesting programs on this subject as presented in his book Underworld.

history.title: Heaven's Gate (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.text: It is a shame that Amazon does not better separate reviews for different release versions and formats of the same title. Instead we see a jumble of reviewer analyses for different versions and formats, sorting them out ourselves by date and internal references. Perhaps they might sort reviews by ASIN. The new (2013) Criterion DVD & Blu-Ray release is stated as "remastered", color adjusted to improve natural color balance, Widescreen 2.40:1 (according to Criterion, listed by Amazon as 1.77:1) , NTSC, w Surround Sound (Dolby Digital 5.1 according to NYT), Subtitles: English (only?). Plus, several new featurettes and a booklet, 2 DVD discs, 216 minutes. The (2000) MGM DVD release is original sepia toned color balance "direct transfer", Letterboxed 2.35:1 (not anamorphic), NTSC, Dolby Digital 5.1 (surround). Subtitles: Spanish, French. The only special feature seems to be the Trailer, 1 DVD disc, 219 minutes. The (1997) MGM LaserDisc release matches the later DVD release (yes, some of us still have LD collections), except audio is Dolby Digital 2.0, and AC-3, and Analog (mono); uncompressed digital audio is outstanding, 2 LD discs both sides, 219 minutes. The movie was filmed in Panavision® & Technicolor®. Therefore I have concerns regarding change in color balance and widescreen ratio. If accurate, the ratio 1.77:1 would be achieved via "unmasking" the top and bottom of the original Panavision® frames. "Letterbox" 2.35:1 is achieved simply by masking those areas. Criterion lists the current release ratio as 2.40:1 but Amazon lists the ratio as 1.77:1 and online video clips seem to be the latter. It is unknown at this time which method was used to change the ratio. IF unmasked, this is very good, we see more of the original frame. But more usually, the sides of the wider format are just chopped off to fit the narrower ratio; this is a very bad loss of the original Panavision® frame area. Being "anamorphic" makes no difference, it just adjusts whatever ratio is used to better fit modern 16x9 wide screens as if full frame. I understood the concept of original sepia toned color balance first used. I reserve comment on any color change. Yes, I would like to get the new featurettes & booklet. But, I am uncertain of the changes in widescreen ratio, color balance, and less running time than the 219 minute release. As to the movie, it is both very good and tiresome simultaneously. Overall I like the 219 minute original version. I would have preferred this new release to have been a longer Extended Version, with the new featurettes.

history.title: Godzilla (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.text: Thank you Criterion for making available this wonderful quality release (2012) with the ORIGINAL 1954 version of "Godzilla". After years of seeing only the re-cut 1956 USA version with Raymond Burr inset, it is wonderful to see the original film as created. My gosh, what concepts: ...Character Development, original Plot, proper timing in delivery of the Story, and the atomic sub-plot in full play (fully removed from the USA version). Further, that sub-plot and its ancillary effect is central to the main characters in the film, explaining WHY they do what they do. The original 1954 film is SO MUCH BETTER. It is a 5-star film (the re-cut version ranks by me as only 2-star cult film). Why is it that for so many years, we could only see the USA cut versus the original? The shame is that the censored atomic sub-plot deemed unacceptable in a Japanese made movie, was central to the entire series of mutant radiation USA sci-fi films of the fifties ("..Beast..20,000", "Them", "..Incredible Colossus", "..Shrinking Man", etc.). I leave it to the cultural historians to discuss the merits, politics and foibles. With the sub-plot in place, the original movie works at many more levels than just a stomp and burn monster film. DVD transfer is good, best available, digitally enhanced, 1.37:1 original frame, audio remastered. Subtitles are good. Supplemental material is outstanding, very interesting both for the making of the film and its special effects. The booklet is a wealth of information, worth reading. Yes, the 1956 is also similarly enhanced. Ignore the thirty plus sequels and derivative monsters. For the best, the most interesting, the most factual (a dubious term for a fictional story), always go to the Original source. This original is well worth seeing. Note: the booklet explains the original name "Gojira" is a combination of the Japanese word for whale (kujira) with the adopted English word for gorilla (gorira). Seems fitting.

history.title: The Questor Tapes
history.review_title: The Questor Tapes, finally on DVD-R
history.text: I am a surprised that my original review under "The Questor Tapes" failed to be forwarded into this new DVD listing. Good news is the DVD-R suggested has now been released. Thank you. But I guess this also means the revival of the story as a new series is dead. Here follows my original review: New Questor series in the works?, April 23, 2010 It would appear that Roddenberry Productions has entered into a deal with Ron Howard's Imagine Television to develop "The Questor Tapes" into a new TV series, according to TrekMovie.com (Jan 2010). Should this pan out, we might expect a respectable quality DVD of the original 1970's pilot TV program to be released at some time leading up to the new production. If not, we can only hope to be able to eventually get it as studio DVD-R like the rest of the mid-1970's Roddenberry titles. In the mean while, the TrekMovie site has some clips from the original and states that entire TV movie "The Questor Tapes" is available on YouTube.

history.title: Sunshine
history.text: Fabulous CGI effects. No viable plot. Worse science. Young actors too young for their character roles. At least the effects and visuals are very well done. I can't believe how much money was spent producing this terrible story. Let us start with the science: human ego aside, NO AMOUNT OF EXPLOSIVE delivered by a silly primate species could have any effect on the fusion processes of the sun. If the entire planet earth were converted into hydrogen and rocketed into the sun...no change. The sun is an exceptionally large object, thousands of times bigger than the earth. The writers of this plot apparently never took a science course in school, read a book or even verified any part of their idea online. This primary unbelievable premise makes the whole film completely unbelievable. Next, every actor is too young for what they are supposed to be, supposed to know, and every one of them is emotionally unfit and seems bent on suicide. More unbelievable. Bad guy is on a wrecked previous voyage we only learn of half way through the film. And then finding and docking with that vessel is treated no differently than pulling a car into a parking lot. Unbelievable. It is impossible to spoil this film. If you like the special effects, play it, sound off, ignore the unbelievable. Just watch the picture and try not to follow a viable story line. If one existed.

history.title: Northern Exposure: Season 6
history.review_title: Some gems therein, but a dismal end to a fine series. **Warning: Spoilers**
history.text: Spoilers herein, be warned. Season six is a dismal end to what was a wonderful series. Characters long known to us are deconstructed and completely changed from their long known personalities and traits. The worst example of this is what producers and writers did to Chris in several episodes, changing him from his well known character as an intelligent, well spoken, spiritual mentor to the community, into a whining selfish boob. And worst, setting him up with Maggie, who is suddenly interested in this whimpering uncharacteristic dis-interesting repulsive version of Chris? Yet, in other episodes, Chris is back in character, not involved with Maggie, and enjoyable to watch as was usual such as "the Graduate". The inconsistencies are maddening. The last final episode is terrible. Meant to be a homage to the series it does the opposite. Nearly all the characters are changed and modified beyond belief, stuck in a script without a plot, off in some new set supposed to be a "new summer lodge" for Maurice. This is not surreal, it is bad writing and destructive. What happened to Cicely? Were they kicked out of Roslyn, WA? Of the episodes on disc 5 of the set, only "Ursa Minor" is worth watching. Hidden within the year are the few remaining gems of episodes well worth watching, primarily those on discs 1 through 4 still including Rob Morrow as Dr. Joel Fleischman, and others such as "The Robe" with Shelley meeting the devil as a spa salesman. The episodes with Joel and Maggie are still magic, especially the actually surreal episodes "Dinner at Seven-Thirty" when Joel experiences an alternate realty in NYC and "The Quest" with them on treasure hunt for the "lost city" which should have been the finale to the series. Buy the set, but beware. The new doctor and his wife never fit into the series and you may wish to skip watching episodes primarily on disc 5 which are inconsistent with the fine history of the show.

history.title: Ancient Aliens: Season 8 [DVD]
history.review_title: well done, well presented, what if it were true?
history.text: Despite occasional gaffs of presenter's personal "opinion' being presented as "fact", the series does a wonderful job of presenting the huge volume of otherwise overlooked and ignored archeological evidence worldwide that suggests more than traditional scholarship admits. Whether this evidence is due to extra terrestrials from where ever, who may have arrived by who-knows-how, or due to ancient human civilization better developed and advanced than now recognized, the series brings forward a great deal to consider. An "open" mind does not mean empty or "vented". The worldwide volume of similar mythologies, legends, pictographs and very ancient physical constructs proven by geological science to be older than traditional scholars will accept, is overwhelming. Just statistical considerations suggest many of the opinions may have merit. Series programs are well done, well presented, and usually have adequate disclaimers regarding "what if it were true?" Maintain skepticism. Observe the presentations. Evaluate for yourself the documented evidence of there being more to history than we've been taught. And remember, scholarship is only advanced by the next generation of scholars out living their teachers.

history.title: The Flight of the Phoenix
history.review_title: Classic film, great cast, new hi definition release with special features deserved.
history.text: This film is a legitimate classic survival story, well directed, well acted, well cut, not cheap, with the best actors. A better hi definition DVD & Blue Ray release would be well received. Existing DVD has stimulated controversy over widescreen aspect. IMDb lists original aspect as 1.85:1 I see technical no references to wider aspect. Upon receipt of my DVD I too was concerned about the obviously cropped Fox logo at the begining. However, I compared the LaserDisc version 1.33:1 (scan & pan) and confirmed the DVD is indeed wider aspect. DVD cites 1.85:1 Widescreen. This seems correct. Quality of DVD imagery / resolution is vastly better than the LaserDisc which unfortunately was done to only 480i video TV quality. I would love to see a new DVD release with full special features. This film is a classic with an interesting history and outstanding cast.

history.title: Spectre (DVD)
history.review_title: End of the Franchise "Good Bye Bond"
history.text: This film IS the worst James Bond 007 ever. Despite attempts to reprise the types of spectacular scenes from past films, this movie has No script, No plot, No humor, poor cinematography, bad music, a hideous title song by an ameteur who should NEVER have been let near a microphone. What was Barbara Broccoli thinking? She, Sam Mendes and their minions have used their "license to kill" on the franchise. history.title: Doctor Who: Deep Breath (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: From a huge, long time fan... disappointment.
history.text: Disappointment... disappointment mostly with the new doctor. Capaldi is a well established actor. He currently is playing an excellent Richelieu but, to me so far, a terrible Doctor Who, second only to William Hartnell. An older doctor is OK (I'm older than him) but you need the soul of the character. I don't see it with Capaldi. If you wanted old, give it back to Tom Baker. Since all the regenerations have been used up and this starts a new countdown, the writers could have come up with some reason to revive #4. Bottom line, I believe it was a bad call. Another gripe is the new opening. I prefer most all of the older ones, especially the music, which has gone downhill since November 23, 1963. TARDIS interior stinks. Looks like the inside of a 1970's dance club. Carla seems a bit less than she was. Bad writing or is it just me? Yes, the writing. Not bad, not so good. I own every episode available (as far as I know). 'Deep Breath' is better than many of the 'classic' ones but falls short of most of the modern ones. T-Rex opening was big but quickly turned to a vehicle for the doctor to become introspective. Poor dinosaur. Regeneration gets a C-. I prefer seeing the transition and waking up process in one episode. Bottom line on 'Deep Breath', it did It's job in kicking off the new Doctor and giving us new characters. My hat is off to reviewer Allan M. Lees who pointed out that death has become a resting point in recent outings - shown here when a bad guy is impaled to death but awakens in 'paradise'. In episode 2, it happens again. Please write your Congressman or Member of Parliament and demand an impeachment of Capaldi.

history.review_title: Seasons 1-4 were great en all departments
history.text: Seasons 1-4 were great en all departments; story; characters, acting, special effects, etc. Most people seem to agree. They take all of that effort and diminish it by such such a skimpy, derailed, 3rd class, pulp comic quickie ending. After all this it comes down to a single winner-take-all fight to the finish between a man and a queen bee. Bug dies, all her soldiers and mechs die and/or stop. War over! Mankind wins! Might remind you of War of the Worlds where all the Martains catch cold suddenly die. Sad.

history.title: A Christmas Carol
history.text: Dickens' novella is one of my absolute favorite stories. I have pretty much every theatrical version, and love them all. This one, however, is utterly dreadful. I couldn't even finish it. From the terrible acting to the horrible presentation of the ghosts, it is unwatchable. Even the 1930's versions had better acting and effects. The scene with Marley's ghost was so irritating I had to fast-forward (repetitive, nonsensical wailing that went on and on).

history.title: The Maze Runner
history.review_title: It's OK, all but a little hokeey
history.text: This is a decent enough action flick (although it does steal a lot from Lord of the Flies), but the concept behind it makes no sense. SPOILERS: A cure needs to be found for a disease. So, what's the solution? Put a bunch of children through brutal challenges, like the maze. Um, what??? What a bunch of nonsense. The author clearly is in need of some education in how real science works.

history.title: Disney's A Christmas Carol
history.text: I have many theatrical interpretations of Dickens' book, and I will add this to the collection I watch every year. It is very well done. The only thing that bothered me was actually the special features. In the "making of" featurette, they have this college professor touting how faithful this version is. She lists a few examples of things from the book that are in this movie, but none of them are actually in the book! For example, she talking about Stooge getting chased through the streets of London by a couch, and being shot up toward the moon. Neither of these things are in the novella. I think if you are a literally professor you should get your facts straight, especially if on camera.

history.text: Suppose you wanted to pander to the basest desire for violence--buckets of blood and guts. But you wanted to give the whole effort the sheen of a Masterpiece Theater piece. How? You construct a thin historical story about the Irish in New York in the 1860s, give it BBC quality production values, weave in a bit of Gaelic piping at the critical moments, and then blast away. Copper Season has almost no storyline, weak dialog and no reason for being other than a leering interest in violence.

history.review_title: ONE OF THE BEST WRITTEN TV SERIES, EVER
history.text: The dialog in Suits is just extraordinary, with the characters, like swordsmen, literally dueling each other to the ground. The thrust and parry is something to see, and to extend this metaphor, they do it with rapier wit. It brings to mind Who's Afraid of Virginia Wolfe, some of the Mamet plays, heck, even Taming of the Shrew by the master himself. There's not a single episode that has been a dud, and my wife and I savor every moment. Great acting, of course, and whoever cast the various actors has not missed the mark once. Bravo!

history.title: A Colbert Christmas: The Greatest Gift of All!
history.review_title: Offensive, stupid, and--Stephen--this is not even funny!
history.text: We are big Colbert fans, but this is terrible, offensive trash. It begins with Colbert singing a song about making money off Christmas. Fair enough. Next comes Toby Keith-- carrying an AK-47 assault rifle. He sings a song about shooting people who don't share his views on Christmas. Then he sings about bombing them. The song's finale comes as atomic bombs with mushroom clouds explode in the background. I am not making this up. This is Colbert's Christmas show. Stephen---it's not even funny!! Next comes Willy Nelson, who sings a song about (surprise) smoking dope, and we now we see the baby Jesus in the manager enveloped in smoke. It goes on from there. Colbert needs to take his vast wealth, buy all these DVDs, and bury them.

history.title: The Decade of Discovery
history.review_title: How do prosecutors find evidence in hundreds of thousands of emails? The answer is not through word search.
history.text: If you've ever wondered how the feds tracked Hillary's emails--or how a prosecutor can find evidence in thousands and thousands of emails, The Decade of Discovery provides the answers. Let me say that I'm not an attorney, nor have a background in computers. But I've always wondered how prosecutors can indict corporations and individuals when the most damning evidence is often hidden in thousands and possibly hundreds of thousand of emails. If you're saying "Word Search," you're wrong. As the film explains, word searches are just not that good, leaving many critical emails undiscovered. Joe Looby does a fine job of explaining this complicated subject so that it finally makes sense. The interviews are good, the graphics are good, the music is good--it even has a sense of humor that makes what seems like a dull subject a pleasure to watch.

history.review_title: Sitting at JFK's elbow during the Cuban Missile Crisis
history.text: Do we learn from our mistakes? This film examines how several US presidents learned from their mistakes--and then went on to historic achievements. The most captivating segment covers JFK, who fumbled the ball during the Bay of Pigs invasion, but then handled himself superbly during the Cuban Missile Crisis. In the JFK segment, Mr. Looby, the producer, has found the historic black and white film clips and the actual recordings of JFK's phone calls made and received during the missile crisis. The feeling he has created puts you right inside the Oval Office, just feet away from Kennedy as he is trying to make the right decisions, with the clock ticking and the world creeping towards nuclear war. I can't tell you how chilling these film clips are. This is a masterful look at a series of Presidents, and their most important decisions.

history.title: Two and a Half Men: Season 12
history.text: The show died when Charlie Harper "died," but I bought the entire set so I'd have a Two and a half Men collection. I realize that the ending was ridiculous, but having written for TV in the eighties (and having taught script writing on campus most of my adult life), I probably would have ended the show in a similar way. Charlie Sheen had bounced off the wall so badly, Ashton Kutcher made such a mess of the Walden character, Jon Cryer ended up doing dumbed-down slapstick (when he's so much more capable) . . . . where do you go from there? You end the show just like the writers did. You make it absurd. I absolutely loved the inside jokes, and how the entire cast delivered one-liners and then looked right at the camera. I watch seasons one through four most of the time (didn't like the Chelsea episodes), and do watch the two final episodes for a good laugh. Worth it just for those two shows and to complete a collection.

history.title: Walter
history.text: Since mumblecore films became popular (why?! how?!), I've been suspicious of independent films, but Walter has soul (both the character and the film as a whole). It's not in-your-face like most things released lately, and allows you to follow Walter around, wondering what's going to happen to the poor schmuck. The ending is beautiful (no spoilers here). Absolutely worth owning.

history.title: Shriek If You Know What I Did Last Friday the 13th
history.review_title: A Teen Spoof for Thinking People
history.text: I'm old. I like the classic style horror movies (as well as classic style comedies). But this is just priceless. It's done with finesse. The acting is solid, the writing strong, and the laughs very real. I hesitated to watch it the first time because most modern horror films (and their parodies) are full of bad lighting, ad libbed shrieks and other unnecessary noises and gestures, and are otherwise just annoying. This, however, is clever and actually funny. I'm glad I bought it because I can watch it over and over and still get a laugh.

history.title: Madam Secretary: Season 1
history.text: This was recommended by someone I really trust and have known forever, so my husband got Season One. I taught drama and scriptwriting most of my adult life and in my opinion if Tea weren't the producer, this show wouldn't have gotten on the air. As a feminist and a woman, this may sound odd, but Tea's character is just too much of a spoiled soccer mom and she would have been stomped into the ground her first hour on the job. It just doesn't work. And the girl who plays the older daughter? She cannot deliver one line properly, making her completely unbelievable. I haven't watched the whole season, but as much as my husband loves it, I just don't. Too bad, because there are some strong actors and a great idea here.

history.title: Frequencies
history.text: I'm so sorry I couldn't get this on a DVD that would play on my all-American machine, but I did nab it from one of the movie channels via DVR. This is a smart film produced in a time of some insultingly stupid and uninspired movies. It hooked me (and everyone I've shared it with) from the opening through the credits. The ideas presented are inspired and all of us were left with that "what if this were true" feeling that led to a number of great discussions. (I won't give a synopsis -- that's already been done.) And having been a drama professor during my working years, I appreciate the casting and the performances. All around one of the best films I've seen in a long long time.

history.title: Mistress
history.text: I have this on VHS and it still plays fine (and often). I don't understand the mixed reviews -- especially the negative ones. The cast was excellent, the humor subtle and clever rather than in-you-face, and the plot just a lot of fun. I prefer it to The Player because it doesn't try to be a smart-and-stuffy film; it is what it is and all of us here love it.

history.title: Rolling Stones: Shine a Light
history.review_title: Next Best Thing to Being There
history.text: I typically avoid concerts on tape (or disc), but the Stones have been my favorites since sixty-four, and they pull through this one with flying colors. Their energy has always amazed me and they're on the top of their game with Scorcese. There's not a glitch in the production. The songs flow (as always), and the guys are amazing. The shots are great, with no choppiness. Of course it's not like being there, but it's the next best thing. If you're a Stones fan, you just can't go wrong with this DVD.

history.title: American Loser
history.text: This movie is one of those brilliantly-done little gems that comes along maybe once in a decade. I realize it's not the type of film that will appeal to the not-so-bright, and that's okay. It doesn't have to -- it has its audience. Seann was an adequate choice as the lead, although there are others who would probably have done a better job. The script could have been somewhat more even, but the structure breakdown almost adds to the genius of the production. I don't want to make a comparison between this and a literally-brilliant film, but this movie blows light and dark the way American Beauty does. And because it addresses the human condition on a base level, brighter people will "get it" and others won't, which is part of its beauty. If you're into offbeat films and indies, you'll probably love this. If, however, you're looking for slob humor or other frat-boy mentality fare, you'll probably want to choose something else.

history.title: Nature: Why We Love Cats & Dogs
history.text: A thoughtfully laid out and entertaining video. My husband and I enjoyed it immensely. I'd recommend it for children and adults, even for those who don't have pets (yet). I'll be watching my copy again soon.

history.title: Grace and Frankie: Season 1 [DVD + Digital]
history.text: I got this as a Xmas gift from my adult daughter who, I'm convinced, bought it to irritate me. No one my age looks like Jane -- not even my high school prom queen. And much as I loved Jane's workout videos from thirty years ago, she still cannot act. Lily has been great in some things, but playing an old hippie doesn't work in this show. Those of us who really were hippies are now feeling a backlash. The men are adequate actors but their characters are not believable. The stories are vapid and there is no way anyone my age is going to relate to them. This is easily the worst drivel I've seen in years. If you're "older" and expecting to relate to this show, forget it. And if you expect to get a laugh, you won't. This is just awful.

history.title: Have Gun Will Travel: The Sixth and Final Season, Vol. 1
history.review_title: Season Six is a huge dissappointment.
history.text: Season One unveiled a unique and most interesting character and format. Paladin, the Carlton Hotel, Kam tong's 'Hey Boy'- a sophisticated gentleman hires himself out to do the difficult and dangerous and usually interesting. But with all that potential, the show never explored itself and by Season Six, there's nothing of interest. The Hotel and Kam Tong are rarely seen and Paladin turns into nothing but a saddle tramp getting into a lot of fights. They just let this series die and that's a genuine shame. Ricahrd Boone wanted more from the show and obviously never got it.

history.title: Wu Tang Clan
history.text: I don't ask for much from a kung fu film but this film gave me nothing. But worse than that is that I bought the film so as to add to my small collection of films featuring some of the girls of kung fu and I had heard that Shih Szu was the 'Queen of Asian action films'. So I purchased the film expecting to see the 'Queen of Asian action films' featured and showing her style over and over again. So where's Shih Szu? There were a couple of girls that had a few lines but no action scenes with girls in them. So where's the'Queen of Asian action films'? Some guy kept a bunch of guys in a prison or someplace and he kept fighting or torturing them and that was the film. But if you want to see the best of the girl kung fu stars at their best, this film isn't it.

history.title: Midnite Angels 3 [DVD]
history.text: I purchased this dvd so as to have a sample of Moon Lee's work and I want my money back. Well, maybe half of it. Moon Lee, who started as a ballerina, took to Kung Fu extremely well and can deliver some of the best Kung Fu action and she does dominate the early going. The climactic scene in the early going comes whe she is discovered coming out of a room where she isn't supposed to be in and a massive battle takes place between her and about a hundred guards and she is superb. (She also does the Bruce Lee thing from 'Chinese Connection' where Lee has a climactic battle requiring extensive agility and flexibility and then suddenly, from out of nowhere, he has nunchakus- like where was he hiding them? Moon Lee has a wild battle and then reaches into her belt and has nunchakus. How do you flex with those things in your belt behind you?) She then escapes- after throwing he nunchakus at her pursuers with no ill effect- and jumps through a window maybe 50 feet off the ground but of course, she's unharmed. This was fine action and I waited for more but then Moon Lee disappeared. The rest of the story focused on the others in her group and I found that I couldn't care less. This is not a Moon Lee film but rather Moon Lee opens the film and then moves out of the way. Buy it so as to enjoy maybe the first 20 minutes of it but then say 'Goodbye' to Miss Moon and sadly at that.

history.title: The Crane Fighter
history.review_title: A disappointing film is ruined by one stupid scene
history.text: I rather like Judy Lee (Ling Chia) and was very impressed by how the movie started. She was learning the 'Crane' style and did fantastically well with it . I thought that she might continue through the film showing the same style and I'd watch the lovely Judy Lee using 'Crane' with superb showmanship. But the movie then sorta changed directions and shifted gears and there was a strong male lead and the story seemed different but still, it was alright as there was a strong 'chemistry' between Ling Chia and the male lead and it was still alright although the combat scenes no longer featured Judy Lee and 'Crane' and that was a disappointment. The young man marries Judy Lee but she won't bed him unless he defeats her in a Kung Fu fight which he can't do so he sleeps outside. And then comes the disagreeable (sick) part. There is a comic character that follows the young man around and in the morning, the comic character walks outside and pees (with the camera doing a close-up of a flow of something) and he's actually peeing on the young man who then pushes the comic character into a water-filled barrel. And this ruined the film for me. I'm just not into body-fluid humor and I don't need a closeup of some guy peeing on another guy. (I think the late George Carlin referred to this as something like 'scataholic' humor and I don't like it.) The rest of the film is a minor bloodbath and you can have my copy if you want it.

history.text: There's way too much fighting and simply not enough character development and that's not just a shame, it's a crime when you've got Cheng Pei-Pei and Shih Szu. It's poorly done and wastes the 2 main female leads but if all you want is a bunch of swordfights, it'll do.

history.title: Sherlock Holmes
history.text: Please be advised that this is an odd assortment and not a Basil Rathbone collection. There is only one Rathbone movie in this set- '...Secret Weapon'. Rathbone fans are not getting a Basil Rathbone filmfest. There are some early classics including a silent film from 1900 billed as the first Sherlock Holmes film and it is nice to see a bit of a variety just to see some others in the part and Holmesian history but there are 3 Ronald Howard T.V. episodes (to me, a very poor choice for Holmes) and radio shows and Nigel Bruce audition films and it is this oddball collection that seems to make up a huge portion of the 12-plus hours. If you're into just anything Holmes and love to collect, then buy this set. If you want Basil Rathbone, this ain't it. Good for a collector though. Maybe very good for a collector but not for the casual.

history.title: The Classic Sherlock Holmes Collection
history.text: I'm not thrilled by the collection but I don't want a refund and I do play several of the films. I like Basil Rathbone as Holmes but there are 2 discs with 4 Rathbone films on the first and 5 films from the 30's- preRathbone-on the second. On 1st disc: 'Woman in Green' is a waste of time with girls murdered and their fingers cut off-probably a vague attempt to associate Holmes with Jack the Ripper. I'm not a fan of mutilation. Have Holmes solve a jewel theft or find out who the solitary cyclist or something such as that but leave out mutilating young girls if you would. And who's behind it but Prof. Moriarity. Not again. ' Terror By Night' is about my favorite Rathbone film but I have noticed that in this one, Holmes seems a bit detached and cool acting and Lestrade is too bossy. 'Dressed to Kill' isn't bad and '...and the Secret Weapon' has Holmes fighting Nazis. The film isn't bad until who shows up but- you guessed it- Moriarity. Is Moriarity everywhere? The film loses its luster at that point. Disc 2 is for collectors and true fans. Three Arthur Wortner films and he isn't bad although not the definitve Holmes and the Watsons are all alright or barely noticeable but Ian Hunter puts in a fine performance in 'Sign of Four' although he does seem a bit young to be Watson to noticeably older Wortner's Holmes. There is a fine performance by somebody as Moriarity in one of them-almost defining the character- and these three films are 'Murder at the Baskervilles' which is a renaming of a not bad version of 'Silver Blaze' renamed to take advantage of the success of Rathbone's 'Hound of...' when it was released in the west in 1941 some 6 years after release as 'Silver Blaze' in Europe. There is a confusing and not very interesting version of 'Sign of Four' and a weak film called 'Triumph of S.H.' which is based on 'Valley of Fear' and Holmes does little more than stand there and listen to somebody else tell a long story. Raymond Massey does a fair job as Holmes in a nice version of 'Speckled Band' although the snake appeared to be more of a python than a poisonous serpent; the serpent was a good actor though, very well-behaved and well-coached and didn't wear too much makeup- and Reginald Owen does a nice job in a nice version of 'Study in Scarlet'. Don't hesitate to purchase it if you want to add to your S.H. collection and you get a good price. It's not perfect but it's not well-packaged nothing that lures in suckers. Good-enough purchase.

history.title: Queen Boxer [DVD]
history.text: I have a small collection or rather a 'sampling' of films showcasing the female stars of wuxia and Judy lee is probably my favorite and this is her debut film or at least her first big role. She appears very early in a restaurant that is under attack by some hoodlums (she does not fight them) and then she leaves not to be seen again until about the midle of the film. Once she shows again, she shows with a sonic boom but where is she for the first half of the film? It's a rather routine film about something or other-what difference does it make? This is wuxia and a typical wuxia script reads 'start fighting' and a dedicated wuxia fan might enjoy watching the men fight it out until Judy Lee takes over but it is a long and not very original wait. The ending is almost legendary where Judy lee-Chinese name Ling Chia and sometimes referred to as Chia Ling- takes on the place and she takes on the whole place- like 50 of them. Of course they're all polite enough to wait their turn and fight her single-file but still there are 50 or so and she does a nice job. Her kung fu is only so-so (if you want better, watch Moon Lee or early Michelle Yeoh or Angela Mao) but she is about as pretty as it gets and as an actress, she is very convincing. In 'Brave in Kung Fu Shadow', when her father is murdered, she actually seems to be overwhelmed with grief and this is her Chinese opera training and experience showing through. Her opera training also gives her a little flair and she does hold your attention but she wasn't the best at kung fu but still was alright. If you watch the film, watch the first half to see yet-another beat-em-up story and then watch the second half to watch Judy Lee and then there's the big ending. Moon Lee taking on 20 or more in 'Midnite Angels 3' was more convincing but still, Judy Lee is an eyeful and keeps your attention. She just never had the best scripts to work with.

history.title: Fantomas: Five Film Collection

history.text: This is a good 5-film collection for the collector. Not the smoothest and most sophisticated film-making by modern standards but good for the collector and actually rather entertaining although far from perfect. Each film is long- maybe an hour- and you get 5 so you get plenty for your investment. if you.ve an interest in film's early days. don't hesitate.

history.title: Hobbit, The: The Battle of the Five Armies (3D Blu-ray + Blu-ray)
history.text: First let me say that being able to watch this trilogy in 3D in the comfort of my living room was amazing. I had never read the book, so it was all new to me. Parts I and 2 were outstanding. Sadly the same can not be said for the third part. Yes I understand that it was all about battling armies but it was a shame that it had to be at the expense of interaction between the actors who barely seemed to have any dialogue. It reminded me of the Matrix trilogy that really shouldn't have been a trilogy. The entire second disc The Matrix reloaded was totally unnecessary. It was just repeated fight scenes ad nauseaam. The same is true of The Battle of the Five Armies. It simply got boring and confusing. They went overboard with the cgi affects. It also got boring to watch take after take of Thorin having gold lust. Now about the ending, Bilbo goes through hell and back with the dwarves and it's a one minute goodbye? What about a burial scene for Thorin? That would have been so touching and heartfelt. Do you really believe that Bard would have handed his children's safety over to the movie's biggest coward? NOT ! I could go on and on about the deficiencies of this third part of the trilogy, but I wouldn't want to bore you. The one shining example throughout this trilogy is Sir Ian McKellen. What ever character he plays, in whatever movie he is in, you can count on a bravura performance. I wish the rest of the cast had the superb diction that he displays. All in all, if you have watched the first two parts of the trilogy, you do have to watch the third, but be prepared to be disappointed.

history.title: Dirty Dancing
history.review_title: You'll have the time of your life
history.text: "Dirty Dancing" is an American romance-drama released in 1987. The movie is set in summer 1963 and tells the story of Frances"Baby"Houseman as she and her family are heading to a Catskills resort. While there Baby expresses an interest in dancing, but she finds herself falling head over heels for the attractive dance instructor Johnny Castle (Patrick Swayze). However, her father disapproves of their relationship due to Johnny's partner needing an abortion (which was not legal in the '60s). Featuring hit songs like "Wipeout", "Be My Baby", "Hungry Eyes" and "(I've Had the)Time of My Life" With Jerry Orbach, Cynthia Rhodes and Wayne Knight as cast members. This DVD features a good amount of special features, but if you want to dig a little deeper then you ma want to track down the 2-disc DVD released in 2007. The only issue I have with this particular release is it is recycled from 1997 and the video quality is mediocre. Overall, "Dirty Dancing" is a wonderful film and musical but I feel that this DVD release does not do the film any justice.

Unfortunately, their plea falls on deaf ears and they are suspended from school, but break in when one of them needs her art and accidentally cause a fire. The girls become known as Foxfire, but their friendship and hard-earned freedom becomes a trap when the local jocks try to teach them a lesson. The girls find themselves in a violent trap. Overall, not a bad movie. Great script, Angelina Jolie is a great actress and the tattoo scene albeit showing nudity was beautifully acted. The only issues I have with the DVD is they neglected to give this movie a 5.1 surround audio track and the only supplemental feature is a theatrical trailer. history.title: Radioland Murders [DVD]
history.review_title: A wonderful love letter to classic radio programs of the '30s.
history.text: "Radioland Murders" is 1994 comedy-mystery film, and it went through development for twenty years. It is an homage to the 1930s radio programs and screwball comedy films. The movie is about a husband and wife Roger and Penny Henderson (Brian Benben and Mary Stuart Masterson) with a troubled marriage who work for a radio station. On the opening night of the radio station a series of murders occur and with the bumbling police force around it is hard to tell who has killed the people. At one point all clues point to the script writer Roger (Benben) but he is innocent, and is determined to find out who is the suspect. Eluding the police in various ways Roger relies on the page boy, Billy to get information to Penny and send the actors the scripts. It all boils down to one individual who is also like Roger an unlikely suspect. With slapstick violence, musical numbers and romance "Radioland Murders" is a nice little homage to the 30s and I highly recommend it.

Pressure from their director, a bumbling alcoholic cast member and their personal lives get in the way. There is a lot of humor and slapstick in this film, and if you loved watching "Three's Company" or "Carol Burnett" then you'll love this movie.

history.text: :Surviving Christmas tells the story of a wealthy man who rents himself a family for the holidays. He goes back to his old house growing up and decides to toss a burnt piece of paper after mentioning his grievances. He then finds himself in the house, and offers the family a fortune to be his family for Christmas, in order to impress his girlfriend. However, his zany Christmas traditions and advice turn the household upside down. To make matters worse he begins to fall for their attractive, but sarcastic daughter who comes home for Christmas. Despite a PG-13 rating there are heavy sexual references and a photoshoot that ends up becoming very raunchy. Best suited for 14+

history.title: Forces Of Nature
history.review_title: Not a bad movie, but not a great one either.
history.text: "Forces of Nature" tells the story of a man who tries to get to his wedding, but natural disasters occur.. Ben Affleck and Sandra Bullock play the two main characters. Ben (Affleck) is engaged to a woman named Bridgette (Maura Tierney) and the day he lives for Savannah his plane experiences technical difficulties when a bird is caught in the engine causing it to crash. Along the way he meets Sarah (Bullock) a divorced woman who is on her way to see her son for his birthday. As they try to get Ben to his wedding, he begins to wonder if he should stay with Bridgette or let fate pair him up with Sarah. Affleck's acting is somewhat dismal, and Bullock and everyone else show him up at times. Nevertheless this is a cute movie and people may be upset with how it ends, but I won't tell.

history.title: Mean Girls (Widescreen Edition)
history.review_title: A must see for anyone entering high school.
history.text: Based on the book "Queen Bees and Wannabes" by Rosalind Wiseman, "Mean Girls" is an American comedy film that explores cliques and the damaging effects they have on girls in high school. The film stars Lindsay Lohan, Rachel McAdams, Tina Fey, Lacey Chabert and Amanda Seyfried. "Mean Girls" tells the story of Cady Heron (Lohan) and how she enters the public school system her junior year in high school. Previously being home schooled in Africa, Cady has trouble fitting in until she meets two people named Janis Ian (Lizzy Caplan) and Damian (Daniel Franzese) It is then Cady learns about the school's cliques and the cruelest group of all: The Plastics. Cady one day befriends them, and is a hit with the queen bee Regina George (McAdams) until she learns Cady likes her ex-boyfriend Aaron Samuels (Jonathan Bennett) After Regina betrays Cady and makes out with Aaron she is heartbroken and along with Janis and Damian she plans to ruin Regina's life. This movie is full of lots of laughs, hijinks, and shows viewers just how bad high school cliques are. Written by Tina Fey the film features cameos from Saturday Night Live alumni including Tim Meadows and Amy Poehler. Anyone who has a teenage daughter needs to let them watch this as it will give them a good idea of what to avoid in high school.

history.title: Cruel Intentions
history.review_title: A compelling and brilliant modern day adaptation of Dangerous Liasons.
history.text: In the game of seduction there is one rule you must follow: Never fall in love! "Cruel Intentions" is a modern day retelling of the classic Les Liaisons dangereuses, written by Pierre Choderlos de Laclos in 1782. The film stars Sarah Michelle Gellar ("Buffy the Vampire Slayer"), Ryan Philippe ("I Still Know What You Did Last Summer") and Reese Witherspoon ("Sweet Home Alabama") In upscale Manhattan wealthy and popular Kathryn Mertueil (Gellar) plans to take a newcomer named Cecile Caldwell (Selma Blair, "The Sweetest Thing") under her wing at the request of her mother (Christine Baranski, "Mamma Mia!"), but she intends to use Cecile to get revenge on her ex-lover who dumped her for Cecile. She asks her stepbrother Sebastian (Philippe) to seduce Cecile, but he plans to seduce Annette Hargrove (Witherspoon). Annette is the daughter of their school's headmaster, and is considered a paradigm of chastity and virtue because she is saving herself for marriage. Kathryn then insists on a bet, if Sebastian fails to seduce Annette then she gets his vintage Jaguar. If he succeeds Kathryn will sleep with him, he happily agrees. However, the bet takes a deadly turn when Sebastian genuinely falls in love with Annette. The movie itself is a little cliche as far as the plot goes, the chemistry between Gellar and Philippe is extremely good and despite the use of drugs, sex and heavy profanity it makes for a good romance-drama film. Overall: 7.5/10

history.review_title: Step Into This Master Painting Come to Life!
history.text: I'm not sure I have enough over-the-top adjectives to describe what a fabulous series Downton Abbey is! Numerous friends raved about it for several years but I had no interest in checking it out until recently when I had some time on my hands. Four seasons of the show are available now on Amazon Instant Prime video, I began with season 1, episode one and was immediately hooked. The filming, the cinematography of the show is captivating. The style in which it's done, including slow, sweeping pans of the camera from side to side showing the Downton estate and its grounds, brings a majestic quality to the show right from the start. The muted tones and coloring of the scenes make you feel you're viewing a master painting come to life. Beautiful music, at times haunting and melancholy, adds to the feeling of the story, moving it along. I watch this on my laptop with headphones and am entranced. The costuming in all its detail, hair and clothing, as well as jewelry, shoes, hats, ties and other accessories, is exquisite. It is a continual visual feast. The casting of all characters, from the main ones to even the smallest roles, is phenomenal. Dame Maggie Smith, oh my gosh! She is breath-takingly spectacular! Elizabeth McGovern brings a unique, magical quality to her character of Cora, the countess of Grantham. Michele Dockery, who plays eldest daughter, Mary, is mesmerizing on screen with her plain and pristine beauty. That's another thing I love about the show: the actors and actresses are all a delight to the eyes, not because they are glamorous but because they are all gorgeous in graceful simplicity and I do mean every one of them. The acting is seamless, you truly feel transported to this era in the early 1900s. The storylines become more intricate the longer you watch and can have a marvelously sudden and surprising way of developing new wrinkles to them just when you thought they'd finally been resolved. I watched the first season in two days and am happily on to season two. My pleasure. Downton Abbey is the crowning jewel of Masterpiece Theater.

history.title: Saving Mr. Banks
history.text: I'm writing my review before I read any others that might influence my opinion. I remember "Mary Poppins", the movie, from when I was a child. When my son was small, it was the first movie he watched over and over and over, which meant I did too, thus my interest in "Saving Mr. Banks". "Mary Poppins", from the casting to acting, writing and music along with a timeless story line, is flawless, sheer perfection, something I say about few movies. It was interesting to see "Saving Mr. Banks" to get behind-the-movie insight into the making of Mary Poppins. I think I read there was some artistic license to the story, and I plan to check that out. But this movie did a great job of taking us back to the early 1960s, always fun to see when it's done well. I loved all the Disney stuff. Emma Thompson, Tom Hanks and supporting actors and actresses were great. At first, I didn't know if I could stand Emma's character, P.L. Travers, but as the movie continued, I liked how things worked out. I did love Tom Hanks as Walt Disney, a very convincing portrayal. For some reason, I loved seeing Kathy Bates as Walt's secretary, even tho its a very minor role. All in all, a good movie and definitely one I plan to watch again.

history.title: The BIG C - SEASON 04
history.text: These episodes were an okay way to end the series. I started watching the show because I also have a cancer diagnosis. Despite a number of things I didn't like about The Big C, I still found it entertaining. In the final episodes, Cathy's life seems to come full circle. The reality of her situation finally seems to hit her and she can't try to run away from it the way she has before. If you've watched the series up till now, you will find parts of these last four shows somewhat predicable and some things may catch you by surprise. This show is beautifully filmed. A few things about season 4 didn't quite click for me. For instance, Cathy's hair is always greasy looking, but her clothes are immaculately ironed. The son who's supposed to be 16 looks much older so it was a stretch to really think he was a kid in high school. Some new characters were briefly introduced but most seemed to clutter up the storyline. However, Kathy Najimy has a guest appearance throughout this season and I very much liked her character. Overall, I think the whole series was bizarre and unrealistic but it held my interest.

history.title: Ethel
history.review_title: Amazing Account of An Amazing Woman
history.text: The legacy of Ethel Kennedy has always been overshadowed by the mystique of Jacqueline Kennedy. I'm a big fan of Jackie, and yet Ethel's story is remarkable and unique and just as poignant. Do they make people like Ethel these days? She is a class act, having been full of energy, sparkle and optimism, faced to endure countless tragic events in her life all the while adapting with style and grace to the new challenges those events brought. We forget the many roads she's walked down, the things in her life she has witnessed and everything that she's accomplished, so it is important that this documentary about her has been made, and in such a loving way. We were robbed of so much when Ethel's husband, Robert, was killed; the United States missed out on the leadership of him as president but also did not get the opportunity to experience Ethel Kennedy as First Lady. I found this account of her life to be fascinating.

history.review_title: This is not usually my favorite kind of movie
history.text: This is not usually my favorite kind of movie, no real storyline, just some average people moving through life; nothing earth-shattering. But following the fictional lives of this boy and his family, seamlessly told by using the same actors and actresses over a twelve year period was actually fascinating. So, because of its uniqueness, I loved it. I also liked that the characters weren't all glammed up. They all looked like anyone you might find in your own everyday life.

history.title: They Came Together [DVD + Digital]
history.text: I'm a huge Amy Poehler fan, but this is one of the worst movies I've ever seen. As I continued to watch it, the jokes got progressively worse to the point of disgusting. It's too bad, because the premise of the story is good, and if they'd just written jokes in a more intelligent fashion and not catered to the absolutely lowest common denominator, this could have been a really good comedy. It seems like they intentionally tried to write the worst possible screenplay to see if it worked. Welp, it doesn't!

I started watching this because the White House was the backdrop. It started out realistically enough and then as the story progressed, it became ridiculous. Maggie Gyllenhaal's character was a joke, not much emotion there, acting like the local library caught on fire instead of the attempted total destruction of the White House and execution of so many top officials. The movie was too long and too intense. And then, after horrific events, the ending sees the characters acting like they are in a Disney movie. Just too silly.

I really didn't get the point of this movie. Tho Annette Bening is stil gorgeous, I was distracted by her wrinkles...and Ed Harris, always a favorite actor of mine, has a face riddled with wrinkles. There is way too much oddity in the film. Annette's character, Nikki, doesn't even seem to have a life, no friends, and there are just way too many scenes where there are big misunderstandings yet there is no conversation to clear anything up. It's weird. Even the ending didn't make much sense to me.

This was an interesting documentary. I am mildly fascinated with stories of the kind of alcoholics who are the high achieving types with so much going for them yet they cannot see it themselves and are riddled by addiction for whatever reasons. I guess I am always trying to make sense of it. My father, in his later years, was a recovering alchoholic who was able to overcome some the damage he did to some of his relationships, but of course scars remained. This is a very honest portray of Bette. I am giving it four instead of five stars because I would have liked the narration to have had more emotion. It was a monotone throughout, making it feel like listening to a long commecial about the hazardous effects of excessive drinking rather than a personal commentary told by Bette's daughter. Still, it was worth watching and held my interest.
