history.title: Restrepo
history.review_title: Is this the Army of Today?
history.text: I read the book and saw the video. Having spent 30 years with the Army, initially as a Light Weapons Infantryman and two years in a combat zone, I have to say I have very mixed emotions about the video. What I saw were many basic mistakes that combat infantrymen should not be making, things that they should have been trained to avoid, such as standing up in full view of possible snipers, bunching up close together on patrol, and many other things that get soldiers killed or maimed. Somehow not expecting their buddies to be killed. I got the idea they were high school freshmen in uniform with M-4's. They seemed to have forgotten, or not learned, the basic survival techniques I learned in Basic and Advanced. One wonders where their officers and senior NCO's were. During contacts with indigenous civilians, they did the interpreting incorrectly--Army talkers droning on and on in English, then expecting the interpreter to interpret the long speeches exactly into Afgani, and constant use of "he said," as a prefix to the interpretation from Afgani to English, rather than just interpreting it exactly as said. Paraphrasing often makes for misunderstandings. Then again, using combat infantrymen in a civil affairs role is an incredible misuse of them. They are trained to defeat the enemy with the use of force, not in political affairs. A great many other things went on than just what we saw in the video and read in the book, such as messing, R&R, administrative activities, and more. One suspects it was cobbled together to present a certain biased picture of US combat involvement in Afganistan, and not a realistic depiction of combat soldiers in Afganistan at all. It seems to me that the author was not familiar with Army units in combat.

history.title: The Road
history.text: There is little I could add to the scores of previous reviews. To me, the movie was all-engrossing and scary. I constantly wondered what was going to happen next. What I didn't like was Viggo's characteristic muttering and mumbling, which for me was hard to understand. As many others, I wondered what I would do in various circumstances, and would have done else-wise in some. I wondered when he saw the beached ship, how he got up the side of it, and that all he salvaged was a flare gun and one flare, rather than a floating bag of food, clothing, weapons, etc. Obviously many things were plot contrivances, but in any event, it is a movie to see for an enlightening glimpse into a post apocalyptic world, even tho it is not very realistic in some areas.

history.title: The Hurt Locker
history.text: Well, I spent 32 years on Army Active Duty and was a Lt Weapons Infantryman, among other specialties. I also completed the Army Mines, Demo and Boobytraps school. I found the DVD to be incredibly unrealistic in virtually every respect and apparently written and directed by people totally unfamiliar with the actual Army. There are so many discrepancies I could include, but just read the reviews by "A Kid's Review," and "Maskirovka." they pretty much say it all. I cannot understand how this movie was given 6 academy awards and rated highly by critics. Must be politics and PC involved. I hate these kinds of movies.

history.title: Jericho
history.text: Having missed it on TV, I just bought the whole series. Having had some military and political/ public administrative experience, I couldn't believe how naive the writers were in the various plots--just not realistic in the present world. People just don't act that way. Just a daily soap opera plot in the world without electricity, dwindling food, deadly threats, etc. Sort of like a 1930's cowboy movie updated to modern times. The characters don't say what would be common sense or appropriate under the circumstances, just look at each other, apparently they can't think. But I suppose it is the writers conception of an interesting, dramatic plot line. Instead of directly dealing with wrong and evil, the characters let their convoluted sense of moral right screw things up even more. They don't know that you can't make deals with or ignore evil. The former mayor seems to be the only one able to make rational and wise decisions. The follow-on mayor doesn't seem to be up to the leadership task, where you always ask for ideas and recommendations, not just making instant, arbitrary decisions. As we have found out in the present reality, training, experience, and achievements count for future success, not just a great speaker with wonderful promises. Perhaps that was the plot's teaching point. Many times I wanted to yell, "no! Don't do that!" But mistakes happened. All to teach viewers the wrong ideas; but it made the plot go 'round again and again.

Ouch! Save your money and time. My qualification for rating this movie one star is my 30 year study of Spiritual Warfare/Demonology. The movie is based on the book of the same name by Matt Baglio, which is based on real people and events. Let's get our definitions straight: "Demon" is a fallen angel, disloyal to God, a subordinate of Satan. They are intelligent spirits without a body. All are evil and have varying powers. They hate God, the Heavenly Host and Humankind. "Possession" is when a demon is able to influence the body and mind of a human person whenever they want. Many are very hard to exorcise from a human person and much work and prayer (and fasting) is needed. "Exorcism" is running the demon(s) out of a human person by an authorized priest using the authorized Ritual ("Rite") of prayer. Sometimes it can happen almost right away, sometimes it takes years of sessions with really tough demons. While the young priest in the book had a way to go to strength his faith, the movie young priest didn't seem to know why he was a new priest, much less have faith in his God! As such, a very poor candidate for exorcist, as you need very strong faith and belief in God and Jesus Christ, and no unforgiven sin on your soul (otherwise the demons will just tell you to get lost, or hurt you as in the Bible). The first third of the movie roughly follows the book, but then goes off on a tangent all its own. the rest of the screenplay seems to have been done by a non-Christian or an Antichristian. Many scenes in the movie are not in the book and digress from the theme or are there only for sensational effect, such as the singular case of a young, possessed woman being pregnant by her father, and dying in abject suffering near the end. The worst part of the movie is the Master Exorcist (Anthony Hopkins), Fr. Candido in the book, becoming possessed himself, hitting a little girl, and looking like some kind of monster, while our apprentice neophyte priest exorcises him. Garbage!! Never happened in the book! This is serious stuff and not to be diddled with. Again, not recommended. Save your money. .

history.title: The Trigger Effect [DVD]
history.text: The movie is about what happens to a young family when the electrical power goes out in their city. It is a good instructional movie for those who are not prepared mentally or materially when a power outage happens. Normal, law-abiding people and lawless people immediately lose their cool and start doing lawless things. Our hero goes out to buy a shotgun for self defense of his family. The next thing is that his wife, who is deathly afraid of guns, tosses it and the shells to the bottom of their swimming pool without telling him. Then they need it for self defense, but the shells are water-soaked and totally worthless. Then they decide to drive 500 miles to relatives in this lawless situation. Whatever they can do wrong in an emergency situation, they do. In this, it is a great primer for "what not to do, if you want to survive."

So give it a shot of you like Blair Witch style stuff, this beats Blair...but they're grasping at straws..along the yellow brick road.

history.title: Lord of War
history.text: I thought it was a good movie.i saw it for the first time when it came to theaters, so it's been awhile. Just finished it & I still dig it ! Nicholas Cage & Ethan Hawke in the gun running business,with Hawke running off the rails (coincidentally by doing lots of em) with a drug problem,causing friction between brothers and potentially ruining Cage's business. He is soon pitted against some of the fiercest enemies that he deals with. Lot of story telling,lots of action. All in all of you like war movies then get this,it's an excellent film. The vast cast is good,acting is top notch,and man...theres So many gorgeous weapons. Buy it,I got mine for 4$(including shippi mg)

George Carlin - What Am I Doing in New Jersey?
George Carlin Double Feature: Complaints & Grievances / Doin It Again
George Carlin Double Feature: Life Is Worth Losing / It's Bad for Ya'

history.title: Avalanche Alley
history.review_title: terrible is too good a word
history.text: This is one of the worst movies I have seen. And I like cheesy diaster movies! I look forward to the Saturday SyFy movies. I enjoy them (yes, I realize there should be a 12-step program for that). But this...horrible. It just stinks. The acting was stilted, the script was lame.. I could go on and on. I was really suprised by how bad this really was. The scene where the Snow Patrol officer warns the snowboarders about the danger - ugh! Cringe worthy. Even Mega-Piranha had better acting than this. I don't care if this movie is on sale for $1.00 don't blow your money or time on it. It isn't campy, it isn't semi-good, it is just full on crap.

history.title: The Original Nancy Drew Movie Mystery Collection (Detective / Reporter / Troubleshooter / Hidden Staircase)
history.review_title: Wanted so badly to like these
history.text: I would have found the movies more enjoyable if they weren't supposed to be Nancy Drew movies. There is very little connection with the books, other than Nancy's name, her fathers profession, and a mystery is involved. The movie Nancy is kind of ditzy, the maid is not Hannah and is played as a nervous dimwit. The chemistry between Mr. Drew & Nancy, and Nancy and 'Ted' is great though, and I thought they were much better actors than the material they were working with . The portrayal of the black handyman in "Trouble Shooter" is hard to watch. Yes, I realize this movie was filmed in the 1930's but that doesn't make the scene where he is dressed in a long white night-shirt and white pointed sleep cap as amusing as Nancy and Ted seem to think (they may as well have printed "Klan" on the shirt pocket). These movies would be fun as generic Saturday morning TCM programming, but for those of us that love Nancy Drew books - well, these just don't cut it. Although, the Emma Roberts remake is far worse!

history.title: Signed, Sealed, Delivered: The Complete Series (Hallmark)
history.text: I just adore this show. It definitely has the "Touched by an Angel" feel, and both Della Reese and Valerie Bertinelli have guest starred (yea!). The cast has a nice chemistry, and the stories always have a feel good ending. I recommend the Christmas movie, too. It can be a little goofy and predictable...but I don't care. Against my initial hesitation to watch it, this series has captured my heart. I'm really upset with Hallmark for not renewing this as a series, but instead as an occasional 2-hour movie. I know so many people that just love this show, how could Hallmark not see the value in this as a series?? I ordered this because I know I will watch it again and again.

history.title: Sphinx
history.review_title: I gave it two stars for the beautiful location. They made the lead character (played by ...
history.text: This was awful. I gave it two stars for the beautiful location. They made the lead character (played by Lesly-Ann Down) so stupid. She is supposed to be the best Egyptologist (which she talks about in a little speech) and all she does is scream. I remember reading the book when it came out, and I don't remember her being so stupid. Saving grace of the movie is Egypt itself, and of course Frank Langella. What a let down.

history.title: HALLOWEENTOWN HIGH
history.review_title: and it still is a fun movie for the entire family
history.text: My daughter's watched this on the Disney channel when they were younger, and it still is a fun movie for the entire family.

history.title: They Call It Murder Film Chest Restored Version
history.text: It feels like you are back in the 70's watching this on TV. Jim Hutton is great, and gets in some practice for his perfect future role of Ellery Queen! Leslie Nielson is a little hammy and Jessica Walter looks like she hasn't eaten in a year, but overall a fun flashback to watch.

history.title: Masterpiece Mystery!: Inspector Lewis 8 (Full UK-Length Edition) (Blu-ray)
history.text: While the stories are good, the music excellent - as always, and our beloved Lewis, Hathaway, and Hobson are all at the top of their game, I only gave it 4 stars because there are only 2 stories (one is extended). As this is the last of the Inspector Lewis series (Inspector Hathaway? Please?) it really feels like this was a way to let the fans know this time they really mean it's the LAST ONE. Enjoyable, but short.

history.title: The Golden Girls: Season 2
history.text: Seasons one, two and three were the best of the series (although even the 'meh' episodes were better than most other tv shows). The ladies were all perfect in their roles, and the writing was brilliant. No one can deliver a line like Bea Arthur, and the chemistry was untouchable. Even though it is still being shown on 4 different TV networks, I really recommend you buy your own set. The years don't diminish the laughs or the amazing talents of these ladies.

history.title: The Golden Girls: Season 1
history.text: This season is worth buying just to watch Dorothy confront Stan after their daughter's wedding! Even though it is the first season, there aren't any growing pains and runs smoothly from the start. Watching the first season does make you wish the quality of the writing had held up through the end, but the acting from the very first episode is stellar. God know where they found the ugly outfits Dorothy always wore! Best first season of any t.v. series ever.

history.title: Agatha Christie's The Witness for the Prosecution
history.text: Boy is this dark! Both story line and filming are dark and dreary. It was like the production team and writer wanted to just pound the Dietrich/Laughton/Power movie version out of your head. Just not very good. I had high hopes for this after watching the same teams "And then there were none", which was also very intense and noirish. But unlike this movie, it was actually very good. The actors are all very good - so I give this 3 stars. As for the writing and production - Zilch.

targets.title: Baa Baa Black Sheep: Season 1, Volume 2

history.title: The Wicker Man (Widescreen Unrated/Rated Edition)
history.text: I'd give this movie half of a half of a star (if I could). I was watching it on HBO, and I was laughing too much to turn it off. Reading some of these reviews, I laughed even more. This movie deserves every bad review it gets. Nicolas Cage looks like a fool in this. Anyone in their right mind would have been on the island for a few hours and take off running. He acts like a one-man army, and all of the actors in The Wicker Man should be wondering if they just needed the money. So many scenes in this movie are so lame that it is embarassing. Often, it can make you crack up instead of sitting on the edge of your seat. Like most of the other bad reviews here, I would agree--don't bother. I say don't bother with this movie unless you want to see an accidental comedy (instead of good thriller).

history.title: The Darjeeling Limited
history.review_title: Offbeat + Quirky + scenic = a good movie
history.text: I enjoyed this movie with its quirkiness--three brothers with serious, yet goofy looks on their faces, and silly antics, is fun to watch. Francis nearly died in a motorcyle accident (Owen Wilson), and now is examining the importance of his life. Forever playing the role of bossy, big brother, he convinces his younger brothers to join him on a spiritual journey in India to reconnect and become close, like they used to be. He also has a hidden motive to reconnect to their vanishing mother who lives as a nun in India after their father's death (Angelica Huston). Much of the movie happens on this train called the Darjeeling Limited, winding throughout the exotic countryside of India. Jack (Jason Schwartzman) always walks around barefooted, in a suit; Peter (Adrian Brody) wears his deceased father's sunglasses, with the prescription still in them; Francis walks around with a head full of gauze bandages, with one fancy, black shoe on, and one street-bought, moccasin-like shoe on (after getting one of his $3000 shoes stolen from an Indian shoe-shine boy). Their journey is one of forever getting into trouble on the train, and glimmers of self-discovery--one heroic deed, resulting in life-and-death, offers the brothers a good look at themselves. The tossing away of the precious, yet burdensome luggage seems also symbolic of lugging around "extra baggage". In the end, the brothers toss it all behind themselves, showing the importance of freeing oneself from ludicrous amounts of materialistic excess. Like the brothers, we are all on that long, winding journey of figuring out who we are and why we do the crazy things that we do. In the end, maybe the brothers have tossed out extra junk, mind-dulling drugs and all, but still--the goofy bad boys that they are--go out for a smoke and a drink. Seemingly more trusting, the brothers seemed to have a new appreciation of each other. Was this trip a great awakening and life changing experience? Perhaps, but the ending is not "happily ever after" which is OK by me.

history.title: Waitress (Widescreen Edition)
history.text: This movie was well written, by Adrienne Shelly, who also acts in the movie as the waitress who marries her nerdy and obsessed boyfriend. I just found out that the actress was recently murdered. I will never see the movie again without thinking of her tragically, shortened life. This story is more than a slice of pie, but a slice of life...with a mixture of quirkiness, humor and serious dilemnas. Can the pregnant waitress leave her abusive and controlling husband? Can she find the courage to make it on her own? Will she really ever come to love her baby? Should she run off with her doctor, even though she knows this would hurt his loving wife? I liked how the pie making recipes of the waitress coincided with the concocted recipes of life...a bit of this, a bit of that...hoping it will all blend together and work out.

history.title: Talk to Me (Widescreen Edition)
history.text: I think I liked the first half of the movie better, but the acting was terrific. If anything, you have to see it JUST for Don Cheadle's performance. And his girlfriend is hilariously good in it, too. Martin Sheen has a great part, too, and also the guy who played Dewey. If you don't like the raw language, not recommended.

history.title: Juno (Single-Disc Edition)
history.text: When I first saw it in the movies, I thought that Juno was a strange girl, and really she was. But then again, she was supposed to be. Ellen Page gave a good performance of a extroverted teen with quick-wit, a snappy tongue, and still much growing up to do. Yet she also was naive, sweet, and quite tender at times. I like that she had enough wisdom not to be selfish concerning her baby. Even though she wanted to, she did not abort her child....so the rest of the story goes from there. Her equally offbeat, and immature, boyfriend and her aren't ready to be parents, so she finds a couple to adopt her unborn child. Her father and stepmother, don't crucify her like she worried they would, but they help her out inspite of their shock and immediate disapproval. Her friend--who bugged me--came along her side, too. The unique part is that Juno and the baby's father, Bleeker, remained friendly to each other, and solidified their relationship.

history.title: Doubt
history.text: I had to watch this movie twice to figure out if I liked it. The three main characters: Meryl Streep is wonderful in it as she is a wonderful actress. At first, you would be expected to dislike her character as a hard-boiled, stringent nun, and principal, with no desire for laughter and fun, music, ball point pens, sugar or candy, or deviation from her rigid, age-old beliefs. But then you begin to doubt if she is as mean as she appears to be. Is she simply someone who demands lifeless rigidity in her routine, stricking horror in the Catholic students, or is she relentless in her need to protect the children and demand the truth? Father Flynn (Philip Seymour Hoffman)leaves you doubting, as well. Is he a progressive, caring priest to his students, especially the downtrodden, or is he really a sexual predator? You could come to either conclusion. Sister James (Amy Adams)is another one who has two sides...she is sweet and gentle, yet she is aware enough to suspect possible wrongdoing in Father Flynn. She wavers from suspicion to understanding.

history.title: Grey Gardens
history.text: I saw parts of the documentary, catching it by accident on TV years ago. It was both fascinating and disturbing. I wondered, and still wonder, how people of such high society and prominent upbringing could end up so "bottom of the barrel". They looked like a couple of crazy, odd women who have lost touch with the real world. Seeing the film helped bring the story together for me. I thought it was well made and well acted. Drew Barrymore and Jessica Lange brought these two women back to life. I can see the humanity in this mother and daughter duo, even if I don't understand how they could have stooped so low to end up living in a decaying, isolated environment.

history.title: 12 Angry Men (50th Anniversary Edition) with Special Features
history.text: Why I love this film is it really is simply made, but keeps you interested and thinking. In that hot, little room in the courthouse, 12 White guys hash it out over the innocence or guilt of a 18 year old on trial for murdering his father. I think he is supposed to be Puerto Rican, and all jurors, except one, think he was guilty. Henry Fonda stands against all opposition to defend the boy. At first, everyone is ticked that he stands alone, and holds them up from leaving, but then things change. Juror #1 is the head juror, a high school couch. He is orderly, leads the discussion table, and tries to keep peace in the room. He eventually loses his calm due to all the fighting and stress. Juror #2 works at the bank. He is teased at by juror #7 because he seems so nerdy and wimpy to him. He is attentive and considerate. Juror #3 owns a "Beck and Call" service. His feelings are biased, based on the fact that his son has hurt him by not talking to him in 2 years. He can't wait to "slap down those tough kids". Juror #4 is a broker. He is all logic and not guided by emotions. He is fact driven, and when asked if he ever sweats he says, "No, I don't" (funny!) Juror #5 grew up in the slums. He soon finds himself defending his background when others knock down slum kids as pure trash and a menace to society. He is more shy than vocal. Juror #6 is a hard working, blue collar man who paints places for a living. He feels there must be a motive for someone to be guilty. He defends the older juror, respecting the elderly. He has no tolerance for rude remarks. Juror #7 is a wise-cracking, smart alec who loves baseball. He sells marmalade for a living. He has no real convictions except to leave the courthouse and go to the baseball game. He is only driven to a conclusion of guilt or innocence by his own selfish needs. Juror #8 is the lone juror who holds out on a guilty conviction. He is an architect, and he has cool and calm in the face of opposition. He is also compassionate and caring towards the accused, wise and reasonable. Juror #9 is the old man. He is so sweet and so wise that he is my favorite. He thinks he knows the old man, who was a witness in the case, better than anyone else...a man who nobody ever listens to. Juror #10 is the bigoted, loud-mouthed juror who has "lived among them all my life" and thinks "those people" are natural born liars. He also is an owner of garages and is impatient and grouchy. Jurror #11 is the European watchmaker. He has no respect for the wise-cracking, baseball nut who has no convictions. He knows why America is such a great country because of the fair trial system. Juror #12 is the youngest of the bunch, who works in an add agency. Due to his youth, he has a hard time concentrating on anything but the add business and cannot fully make up his mind.

history.title: A Christmas Carol [DVD]
history.text: I loved George C. Scott's version of Scrooge. I grew up with the 1938 version, and I still like it, but I like this one better. Usually, the depiction of Scrooge is as a feisty, mean, old man, one who can intimidate and scare people as he comes there way. Scott portrayed him as a cold businessman, an Ebeneezer Scrooge that was more business than he was hot-tempered and mean. His coldness of heart evenutally transforms, but the change is believable. Scrooge still has the same temperment, but he is a much more compasionate man. I also liked Jacob Marley's ghost. This Jacob Marley truly is a ghost you can believe has been cast into the depths of hell. His ghost was deeply tormented and had much remorse and regret for the selfish life he lived of hoarding money for selfish ain and greed. A great performance that deserves recognition. The 1938 version of Jacob Marley cannot compare. The other characters were portrayed well, too....Bob Cratchit, his wife and children,especially Tiny Tim, the other ghosts, etc.

history.title: The Walking Dead: Season 7
history.text: I am late to watching this show, so I watched seasons 1-7 within a month. I rented it on cable, and was intrigued, at first. The way I watched the series gives me a different perspective than if I had watched it as it came out, bit by bit. TWD is by no means meant to be a cheery look at life. After all, a zombie apocalypse has destroyed much of the world as we know it, leaving the survivors to eek out a bleak existence that ensures that only the strong and resilient ones survive. But to become the best of them seems to be to become the worst of them, and Season 7 shows it. Personally, I think the ones who died are the lucky ones. I mean...what's the point? Like other critics, I see the same pattern of dodging decaying zombies, though hideous and terrifying, are not nearly as a threat as human beings who are becoming more savage by the season. It seems that Season 7 is trying to out-savage all the other seasons, but we are supposed to think of Negan as a cool and interesting bad guy. How someone didn't bash his head in a long time ago, with a bigger weapon than his stupid, barbed wire bat, is beyond me. He's like Al Capone and Hitler rolled into one, but I find no charm in him or desire to watch him from his first appearance to his last. By now, viewers are supposed to assume that most people have lost their humanity and will do anything to survive, stooping lower than previously. Again, the lucky ones aren't the survivors. The ones who have been killed off - both major or minor characters - reveal a pattern that just becomes mind numbing and hopeless to the characters. How about the viewers? Some will disagree with me, but some see it just as that...pointless. You had the "Governor", a man of the same caliber of Jim Jones. He was the first villain who could con people into following him, a guy who has charisma and savvy on the outside, but was truly sinister. Though there was plenty of violence, there was a good story behind his character. The aftermath of the battle at the prison - when the Governor seemed utterly defeated in his life but then joined up to lead his new group - was well done. It shows that a leopard doesn't change his spots nor does does a zebra change his stripes. The cannibals at Terminus gave Hannibal Lecter a run for his money. Last of all, there was Alexandria, but peace was only an illusion. But you then have the likes of Morgan, reoccurring after disappearing from the first season, but no longer a crazed victim but seemingly a Zen master wannabe who wields his stick with flair, having the mindset of Martin Luther King, advocating complete nonviolence. What are we supposed to believe by a guy who convinces Rick to see his enemies as possible allies, only to find the allies were double crossers? Then there are the group of women by the water and the one says that, "There are no evil people...only people who forget who they once were". Tara insists she has seen evil people. It is laughable that Negan goes to Rick's home and makes spaghetti. How charming is that? Rick and Negan aren't cut out of the same cloth, though Rick's decisions can be questionable, the comparisons are asinine. I have been invested in Rick's character from the start. I don't really care what life was like for Negan before the apocalypse. Gutting people, using a hot iron for punishment. bashing heads into mush as a way to terrorize others... I just wish he would go away from the screen - period. I just fast forwarded through much of him. Okay, we get it! Don't cross this guy! Yet Daryl, Carl, Rosita and Sasha all try to take him on single handedly, and fail badly, and he we are supposed to believe that he thinks that Daryl and Sasha will turn to the dark side, realizing he is the better deal. Puke! I hope this old, familiar pattern breaks: Life for Rick, and his group, flee from one bad place to another, but end up like hamsters on the wheel in a never ending pattern of being chased off from one shakily held piece of turf to the next. The scene becomes more and more disturbing. How more disturbing can it get? The only breath of fresh air was the settlement called The Kingdom, Season 7, and King Ezekiel. Things need to get away from being more graphic and senseless to a different viewpoint. It seems all is hopeless, and the writers pounded that theme into the script time and time again, this time going overboard. After watching all 7 seasons, all in one block of time, I can understand why many are turned off. .

history.title: P.D. James - Shroud for a Nightingale
history.text: 12 of P. D. James books about Adam Dalgliesh have been made into movies: Death of an Expert Witness (1983), Shroud of a Nightingale (1984), Cover Her Face (1985), The Black Tower (1985), A Taste of Death (1988), Device and Desires (1981), Unnatural Causes (1993), A Mind to Murder (1995), Original Sin (1997), A Certain Justice (1998) - these 10 played by Roy Marsden - Death in Holy Orders (2003) and, finally, The Murder Room (2005) - these 2 played by Martin Shaw. The movies were not made in the order that P. D. James wrote them. The order of the first 10 books are: Cover Her Face (1962), A Mind to Murder (1963), Unnatural Causes (1967), Shroud of a Nightingale (1971), The Black Tower (1975), Death of an Expert Witness (1977), A Taste of Death (1986), Devices and Desires (1989), Original Sin (1994) and A Certain Justice (1997). The last 2 books that were made into movies were Death in Holy Orders, (2001), and The Murder Room (2003). These last 2 were filmed in order. P. D. James wrote 2 more books about Dalgliesh but to date have not been made into movies. They are: The Lighthouse (2005) and The Private Patient (2007). I have enjoyed all these movies with both Roy Marsden and Martin Shaw but I must admit I like Marsden better as Dalgliesh. Martin Shaw is an excellent actor and I have enjoyed him in Judge John Deed and George Gently. My least favorite movie is A Certain Justice. Dalgliesh is shown spasmodically throughout this movie. The main character is a very disturbed young man who terrifies the young daughter of the attorney who recently represented him in a murder case. I just didn't enjoy the characters or the storyline. I watch the Dalgliesh movies again and again except for ACJ but as a Dalgliesh fan, I had to have it for my collection. I wondered why this was Marsden last movie and, finally, learned that he was simply tired of playing Dalgliesh. The producers had no choice but to find another actor for the final 2 movies. Hopefully they will one day make movies out of P. D. James last 2 Dalgliesh books but probably not with Martin Shaw because of his involvement in George Gently. If you are a P. D. James fan or even an Adam Dalgliesh fan, I think you will enjoy all these movies. You owe it to yourself to watch them and judge them for yourself.

history.title: Kavanagh Qc Set One: Men of Substance
history.review_title: Correct Information for the complete Kavanagh Q.C. series.
history.text: For future customers I would like to give the following information on this excellent series. As listed at IMDb.com and Wikipedia.com the following is the order the shows when aired: Set 1 should include: Nothing But The Truth, Heartland, A Family Affair, The Sweetest Thing; Set 2 should include True Commitment, Men Of Substance, The Burning Deck, A Sense Of Loss, A Stranger In The Family, Job Satisfaction; Set 3 should include Mute Of Malice, Blood Money, Ancient History, Diplomatic Baggage, The Ties That Bind, In God We Trust; Set 4 should include Memento Mori, Care In The Community, Briefs Trooping Gaily, Bearing Witness, Innocency Of Life, Dead Reckoning. Set 5 should include Previous Commitments, The More Loving One, Time Of Need, End Game; Set 6 should include The End Of Law (this is the end of the series). When I first watched these on TV, I watched them in this order and know this information is correct. HOWEVER, when purchasing these sets separately I noticed a discrepancy I would like to pass on. Set 1 includes the 4 episodes I previously listed as well as True Commitment and Men Of Substance from Set 2 - these are all included in 1 box; Set 2 includes (again) True Commitment and Men Of Substance as well as the 4 episodes I previously listed above - Set 2 includes 3 episodes each in 2 boxes (separate purchases); Set 3 includes the 6 episodes I listed above but again 3 episodes each in 2 boxes (separate purchases); Set 4 includes the 6 episodes previously listed but again 3 episodes each in 2 boxes (separate purchases); Set 5 present mistakes in 2 areas: the first being it includes the last 3 episodes from Set 4 and it does not contain 2 episodes entitled Time of Need and End Game. Set 6 is correct. The was the end of the series. The only way I know for someone to own all 27 episodes is to buy the complete series as one unit. I hope this information will be helpful. These mistakes have nothing to do with John Thaw's acting ability - which I always enjoy - but rather the producers of this DVDs.

history.title: Brokenwood Mysteries, Series 2
history.review_title: It's slow - it's boring - it takes entirely too long to be solved
history.text: Something must be wrong with me! I've read several reviews and just don't see where all the "great and good" comments are coming from. It's slow - it's boring - it takes entirely too long to be solved. I watch many other Australian and British shows (and have even bought several series) but this show I just can't get into. I haven't bought the series - I've only seen it on PBS - and I won't be buying it. But for those who do, I'm happy for you truly. I know I always like it when I find a new series to watch. Anyway, these are my 2 cents for whatever they're worth.

history.title: THE COMMANDER, SET 2
history.review_title: According to IMDb and Wikipedia, Set 2 is supposed ...
history.text: According to IMDb and Wikipedia, Set 2 is supposed to contain the episodes "Virus" and "Blackdog". I received Set 2 today (9-3-16) and it contains "The Devil You Know", "Fraudster", "Windows of the Soul", and "Abduction". I am totally confused!!!

history.title: Masterpiece Mystery: Endeavour, Series 3
history.review_title: I am a great fan of anything "Morse"
history.text: I am a great fan of anything "Morse"; the original Inspector Morse, then Lewis, and now, Endeavour. I think in season 1 & 2 the writers did a great job in introducing us to Morse. He's young, unsure of himself as regards to other people but quite obstinate when he knows he's right - and sometimes even when he's wrong! I think the writers are growing him up slowly and not turning him into the grown up Morse in just a year or two. I watched and watched again season 1 & 2. Originally excited about season 3, I was deeply disappointed!!! What happened? Did the show change writers? They went so far off from the Endeavour of season 1 & 2 I had grown to like. I had a very hard time in watching all of season 3 but kept hoping, rather than believing, they'd finally get the old Endeavour back. It's a bitter pill to swallow after being so satisfied with Inspector Morse, Lewis and the first two seasons of Endeavour. Season 4 - well, let's only hope wisdom sets in!!!

history.title: Sherlock: Season Four [DVD]
history.review_title: I have LOVED this series - all episodes
history.text: I have LOVED this series - all episodes, excluding "The Sign of Three". I think it could have (should have) been done much better. I waited anxiously for the Christmas Special - "The Abominable Bride" - honestly, what were Gatiss and Moffat thinking? Then I waited for Season 4 - and what a disappointment. I just didn't like any of these episodes at all. I don't know if the way they ended Episode 3 marks the permanent retirement of "Sherlock" but it needs to be unless Gatiss and Moffat can regroup - go back to Season 1 and regain the magic they showed when writing "Sherlock" at the very beginning. Such a letdown from what was promised to be an excellent series.

history.title: Messiah - The Complete Collection 2001
history.text: Although this series is dark - very dark indeed - the actors are superb. I really enjoyed the performances given by Ken Stott and Neil Dudgeon. If you like the dark side of crime, this series is for you. The storylines are varied but constantly keep the plots moving. You'll find yourself griped in suspense.

history.title: Silent Witness - Series 19
history.review_title: Now here I am watching Series 19 and am truly amazed after all these years that the storylines are still ...
history.text: I first began watching "Silent Witness" when Amanda Burton was the main star. I found myself constantly entertained episode after episode. Now here I am watching Series 19 and am truly amazed after all these years that the storylines are still fresh - still entertaining. High praise for the producers, directors and writers of this show as well as Emilia Fox, Tom Ward, William Gaminara, David Caves, Richard Lintern and all the host of guest stars throughout these years. There aren't many shows like this one. (For those of you who may not know - Emilia Fox is the daughter of Edward Fox and Joanna David, both well known British actors. She is also the niece of James Fox - another great British actor and the cousin of Laurence Fox who stars as James Hathaway in the superb "Inspector Lewis" series.)

history.title: Criminal Justice Complete Collection
history.text: This is a review of Criminal Justice - Season 2 only. I have only just finished watching this long and torturous mini-series. I gave it 3 stars for the storyline and the all-star cast. However, this mini-series was sooo s-l-o-w to watch. It could have been made, easily and more watchable, in 2 hours instead of 5. If you have nothing else to watch and a few hours to waste, then this is the show for you - otherwise, avoid it like the plague.

history.title: Criminal Justice: Series One Region 2
history.text: This is a review of Criminal Justice - Series 1 only. I have just finished watching it on Prime Video (after watching Series 2 earlier in the day). The difference in these 2 mini-series are like night and day. I would gladly watch this one again. The storyline - the cast was so good. It moved quickly through each episode. My only negative comment is the Judge telling the defense they needed not only to find evidence that they client didn't do it as well as discovering who did. (This is not the defense's job.) So if you haven't watched either mini-series, I suggest watch 1 first! They don't relate to each other so if you decide to watch 2 first, you won't have missed anything - except the wasted hours of watching it. (IMO)

history.title: The Christmas Ornament
history.text: Poorly Written, Poorly Acted, and no chemistry between the main characters. Also, unbelievable script. For example, the female lead has a failing business that she is trying to save, yet she takes an entire day off to help a guy she hardly knows deliver Christmas Trees. Also, what seller of Christmas trees would include FREE delivery AND SETUP?
I was bored to death. The lead actor is painful to watch. Hated everything about it.

history.review_title: Worst Elvis Impersonator in the World. Couldn't be any less believable.
history.text: Worst Elvis ever. So bad, I couldn't think of anything else. Terrible choice. Doesn't look like Elvis, talk like Elvis, or act like Elvis. Also, the story was unbelievable and boring. Terrible writing as well.

history.title: School Of Rock, The (2003)
history.text: A terrible movie in every way. The Jack Black character is obnoxious and offensive throughout the entire movie. Totally irresponsible and irritating. The music wasn't even any good.

history.title: The Hollars
history.text: I love Margo and Richard and was glad to see such great supporting actors get a staring role. Everything else about this is terrible. The theme is strong women and weak men. The writing was terrible. There was no attempt at character development. At the end of the movie, I still had no idea who these people were. At one point the mother (Margo) says that she regrets marrying the father (Richard). With decent writing this could have been a very profound moment. It was the perfect setup for discussing the ups and downs of a life spent together. Instead, the topic was side-stepped twice and no insight was offered. The characters of the oldest son and the male nurse were both creepy, immature, and irritating. The musical score was exceptionally bad. Rrather than enhance the movie, it was just irritating. The most amazing thing about this movie is that some people found it hilarious. It wasn't even humorous. Any average person has a life with much more humor than this. To show Richard and Margo laughing on the cover is just false advertising.

A pleasant surprise. I love the actors but wasn't expecting much. This is an exceptionally well written movie. The lines were great and very funny at times. Overall a movie worth watching over and over again.

history.title: Monster-in-Law (New Line Platinum Series)
history.text: Poor writing. I very much enjoyed seeing Jennifer Lopez and Jane Fonda in the same movie. Personally Jane never impressed me when she was young, but she has aged exceptionally well. I've never seen her look better than in a few of the scenes in this movie. Her strength as a mature woman is undeniable. Jennifer Lopez is an amazing, multi-talented woman and her character in this movie reflected some of that. Basically a very upbeat and energetic person with a lot of inner strength and integrity. The problem — Jane's character is so over done. Not even close to realistic. Marie in Everybody Loves Raymond was a believable Monster-in Law. Viola in this movie was just crazy and unstable. The male lead was just vanilla and that would have been OK if Jane's character was more realistic.

history.title: Annapolis
history.review_title: Annapolis was irrelevant — a bad boxing movie.
history.text: Terrible! Nothing real about it. The outline follows and parallels an "Officer and a Gentleman" but poorly. Raised by an unsupportive father after mother's death Not really qualified — only determined Angry loner who doesn't understand teamwork Assaults a superior officer Defiant of authority Best friend attempts suicide after being dropped from Academy Way behind class in Academics Causes trouble for class mates Publicly fights superior officer who appeared to be the enemy but ultimately makes him an officer. Also poor versions of themes from Rocky, North and South, Coach Carter, and other good movies. Not filmed at Annapolis. There are no ship yards anywhere near Annapolis — the movie shows the lead character sitting and looking at his home — a shipyard in Philadelphia more than 90 miles from Annapolis as the crow flies. The main topic of the movie is boxing. The parts about the Naval Academy are totally unrealistic and unimportant to the movie. The boxing scenes looked like 3D animation. Mostly showing closeups of fast and furious punching. The lead character gains 35 lbs in a few days by eating junk food while training vigorously so that he can fight his superior officer as a heavyweight. Get real!!!

history.title: How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days
history.text: Terrible script. Boring / unrealistic . About half way through, I began to wonder why anyone would find either character appealing. I am at a total loss to understand what people see in this nonsense.

history.title: Runaway Jury (Widescreen Edition)
history.text: Another great Grisham story extremely well done.

history.title: Ghostbusters 4K UHD
history.review_title: 4K Ultra HD really not much of an improvement.
history.text: This review is only referring to the quality of the 4K Ultra HD remastering. The 4K Ultra HD treatment really didn't improve the visual presentation of Ghostbusters over the 4K remastered blu ray. If you already own Ghostbusters on blu ray you're better off sticking with that version, in terms of visual presentation only.

history.title: The Lego Movie (4K Ultra HD) [4K UHD]
history.review_title: Not worth upgrading from blu ray
history.text: There's very little improvement beyond how the blu ray looks in comparison to the look of the 4K Ultra HD version, other than some better textures here and there. Definitely not worth paying $30 bucks.

history.title: The Huntsman: Winter's War
history.review_title: Huntsman: Winter's War looked amazing in 4K Ultra HD!
history.text: The video was very crisp, the colors were rich and picture quality overall was amazing! I saw Huntsman: Winter's War in the theater when it opened, and it didn't look anywhere near as good as the 4K Ultra HD version.

history.title: Batman: Assault on Arkham (Blu-ray + DVD)
history.review_title: Better than the suicide squad movie.
history.text: The story in Batman Assault on Arkham was infinitely better than that of the suicide squad movie in theaters. But be warned this animated movie is definitely not for kids! But it is an excellent story and animated action movie.

history.title: Wabbit Season Part 1 (DVD)
history.text: Being a huge fan of the classic Looney Tunes cartoons, I wasn't sure about Wabbit at first but after watching just a couple of episodes, I became a huge fan of it as well. Wabbit is rapid fire off-the-wall lunacy at its best! I hope this show gets more seasons in its future.

history.title: Ghostbusters
history.text: I really enjoyed this movie! They didn't try to simply remake the classic original, the actors made this movie a complete original take on the classic franchise. This movie received a lot of unfair criticism way before it even debuted in theaters, you should really give it a chance before coming to a conclusion. All the actors and actresses in this movie were great in their roles, and brought their A games to the movie. Definitely worth seeing in my opinion.

history.title: Alice Through the Looking Glass (BD + DVD + Digital HD)
history.text: I saw Alice Through The Looking Glass in the theater and it was a really enjoyable movie, But when I watched it on blu ray, the movie just felt dull and bland. I don't quite know the reason for this, since I thought it was really great the first time. I really looked forward to seeing this movie again especially upconverted to near 4K quality, but sadly, it just fell flat.

history.title: Black Adder
history.text: Having been a Mr. Bean fan for many years and seeing Rowan Atkinson in several different film roles, it was great to watch another of his small screen roles. Black Adder is hilarious! Though I wouldn't recommend this for young children like I would Mr. Bean, Black Adder is more geared toward teens to adults. The humor's a more subtle and slightly more mature, and at times it's definitely not age appropriate for anyone below the age of at least 10-12. But you will definitely laugh at Black Adder, another great Britcom!

history.title: Van Helsing [Blu-ray]
history.text: I've enjoyed this movie ever since the first time I watched it in a theater way back in 2004, and it's still just as good today. The 4K up conversion is superb, except in the early scene when Van Helsing's battling Mr. Hyde the CGI used to create Hyde looks extremely dated now. But other than that this movie's awesome in 4K!

history.title: Dr. Seuss' How The Grinch Stole Christmas - Grinchmas Edition 4K Ultra HD + Blu-ray + Digital [4K UHD]
history.text: I've had this version of the Grinch on DVD, Blu Ray and now on 4K Ultra HD and I have to say it looks great in 4K! But like all movies of at least a certain age the remastering process of a movie that's this age also increases a slight graininess in the picture quality that's sadly unavoidable. But the movie was just as much fun as it was the very first time I saw it. And it's still a favorite of mine, and now so much better in 4K!

history.title: The Polar Express [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Adults can't "act" like children....use child actors!
history.text: I wish directors would understand that no grown up actor can naturally move like a child, so some of the scenes just looked forced since Tom Hanks provided the motions. Billy looked the most natural, but some things just can't be replicated by an adult. Caribou do not make that sound---elks do. And with the exception of the Michael Jeter elf, I found the elves the most annoying and not really attractive or charming in any way. I'm sure they were patterned after the people who worked on the film, but I would've preferred loveable jolly elves...especially if they are going to speak Yiddish then make them sweet, not obnoxious. Didn't need the Steven Tyler song or scene. Beautiful score, but the hobo character was creepy. We always skip the marionette sequence as it's just too much for young ones... love the hot chocolate scene! The best part of this movie is the utilization of "old time" Christmas music with Bing and Frank and Perry and the Andrews Sisters and Kate Smith etc... But kids want Santa to be fun and merry, not stiff and weird looking...couldn't they hire an actor who looked like Santa instead of Tom Hanks and his low voiced rendition? I feel the animators spent so much time on some details but forgot obvious ones like the fact that most children have a full set of eyelashes and people blink a lot compared to what these CG characters did. Children squirm and rub eyes and noses etc.. they are not as robotic as these "kids"... I think the falling snow and the train were the best animated things in the movie. Oh yes and the screaming engineer thing...all I can say is I thank God for the mute button!!!!

history.title: Highway to Heaven - The Complete Series
history.review_title: For entertainment purposes only..no sound doctrine here!
history.text: It's a "hit and a miss"...a hit show when it was on, but a miss when it comes to leading you to the truth that matters. Many things are alarming about this show. I don't remember there being so much swearing when this show was on NBC, but here you would be hard pressed to find an episode without the "d" word and the "h" word they use ad nauseum! Most disturbing is how they seemingly joke about using the Lord's name in vain, but they do it all the time... You will find no sound doctrine in this series. What it lacks in Biblical truth it overflows with humanism... It treats God as a generic "boss" and never points to Jesus Christ as the only way to God, which is Biblical truth. Michael Landon had a chance to really point people to this truth but instead pointed them to the errant teaching that all good people go to heaven and only bad people go to hell. Actually this show seemed to think nobody would go to hell. And their view of the devil was completely in error. Satan is not in hell, nor does he rule there. He will be there someday but not to rule, no be eternally punished. What is the truth about heaven? Believers on Christ and who He was,is, and will alway be who believe in Him as their Saviour are in heaven as are little children who die before the age of reason and people who aren't able to ever reach the age of reason. Good or bad has nothing to do with it. Christ is the only bridge to God the Father and to heaven. I wish this show had taught that instead of a lot of sappy stuff that sounds good, but is untrue. Angels are created beings just like humans are...But angels were never human and humans never "turn into" angels. This fallacy has been around for a long time (Frank Capra's "angel" Clarence Oddbody from Its a Wonderful Life for example was a dead human who was working up the ranks of angeldom to earn his wings).... Though you might like to think Granny is your personal guardian angel since she died, truth is, she isn't and she never will be. Yes God uses angels for many reasons, they have always been angels. They were never human. The angels who rebelled with Lucifer (himself once a very high ranking beautiful angel) were thrown out of heaven with him and are now what we call demons. And no they don't reside in hell yet either...but they will one day. If you want to spend some time being entertained, and don't mind swearing and unsound doctrine, then maybe you will like this. But please consider that Jesus loves you and He died for you so you could be with Him in heaven one day. That is the truth that will last forever. This series will only fade away into nothing, as all earthly things shall one day. Do you just want to be entertained, or do you want to know God's true Love forever? Please choose.....He loves you, beloved...

history.title: The Good Dinosaur DVD
history.review_title: Preview what you will be showing your little ones!!!!!!
history.text: This movie is proof that parents need to preview what they will be showing their children...once they see something, they are stuck with it for life and that all could be avoided.... There seems to be a trend in moviemakers to attack the family and tear it apart...Disney has always told stories of dead parents (Snow White, Cinderella, Fox and the Hound, Bambi) or inept parents too self absorbed to take care of their own kids (Mary Poppins, Aladdin--Jasmine's dad etc...) They love killing off one or both the parents, or having them be separated. Is it against the Disney/Pixar "religion" for any of their characters to come from a functioning 2 parent household? We have our conflicts too, ya know...it isn't all white picket fences and pearl necklaces.... And somebody at one of these companies has major dad issues that keep coming out in the movies... Enough of this trash! Just because you can animate, doesn't mean you can tell a story.... well, back to the storyboard....

history.title: 20 Family Adventures - Storybook Treasures: The Classic Collection
history.review_title: Best for older kids and not toddlers...
history.text: As a parent, I try to preview whatever the kids will be watching... Though I really enjoyed these, I feel they would be most appropriate for ages 7+, since a lot of them are lengthy and wordy and the subject matter is more serious. Don't get me wrong, they are lovely stories, but only a few of them a 3-4 year old would sit long enough for. The better ones for younger ones were Max's words, ish, the napping house, Pete's a pizza, spoon, and the one about the fly guy... kids can grow into the rest of these, and the only clunker in the lot was Uncle Elephant. I couldn't stand to watch the whole thing..my children are better off without that one altogether... For the most part, these are very quiet stories---good for sick days or rainy days, but best for older children who can possibly better grasp segregation and slavery and war and hunting etc... Isn't as useful as I had hoped right now, but will be someday....

history.title: Molly's Pilgrim
history.text: Hopefully your local library will have this for you to view as 30 bucks for a short story movie is way overpriced!!! Why are all of the best, clean movies always so pricey???? Crazy fallen world...

history.title: Great Performances: Driving Miss Daisy
history.review_title: Boyd Gaines best part of the show!
history.text: I rented this instead of bought it, and was glad I did. It was not something I would find myself watching again...once was enough. James Earl Jones on stage lacks the depth and warmth he portrays in movies. The subtle nuances into a character cannot be revealed in a stage production. I felt his rendition of Hoke to be brash and stiff and distant, thus making the ending scene not nearly as touching or important as it was portrayed in the film. Angela was good, but again it just lacked something that I easily found in the film version. Boyd Gaines was the best part...he was more natural and flowing with the character whereas James seemed like a yelling General devoid of emotion... I enjoy all these actors in many films and TV shows, but honestly prefer the film much more and watch it several times a year. I gave it 2 stars because, like the movie with Morgan Freeman and Jessica Tandy, this show used a lot of the Lord's name in vain dialogue which I do not find funny nor do I find it necessary. The English language has plenty more options than just blaspheming God. Thank you.

history.title: The Shack [DVD]
history.text: If this is anything like the book, it is total blasphemy.

history.title: David Suchet: In The Footsteps of St. Paul
history.review_title: Where is God the Father and the Holy Spirit in this?
history.text: I checked this out of the library and was hoping for something much more than this was. If you do not come from the belief that the Bible is God's Word and that the Holy Spirit inspired all the writers who wrote in it, you will end up with a production much like this one... All the questions asking who Paul was and why he was what he was are summed up in the Bible...because God (the Holy Trinity) found in Paul a usable vessel. How Paul spoke and believed and got through all the trials was simple...He believed on Jesus Christ and the Holy Trinity Who never left him nor forsook him... The "incident" on the road to Damascus is a key part, but it does not get the attention it deserves, nor does the fact that the Risen, Glorified Christ taught Paul himself. You would think that a production on who Paul was, would delve more into the spiritual as opposed to psychiatrists and the like...Paul did not have an identity crisis. Read a good authorized King James Version Bible and you will get to know the man named Paul whom God used in a mighty way. I give it 3 stars as I enjoyed the location shots of places I will never be able to visit in this lifetime and for the attempt on David Suchet's part to try to get to know Paul. Actors feel they must dissect a person they are studying to find motive and personality etc.. and that is what David is doing here, but unfortunately, with very little Biblical insight, which ultimately hurt the production for me. It had potential, but I really question some of his sources of information. Perhaps too politically correct? Something Paul never would have done...Bow to the political liberal dictates of the day. Spread the Gospel is what he did WITH GOD'S HELP...something this production never really gets around to saying...like they are afraid to say that Jesus is/was/always will be the Messiah, and He is God and He Himself used Paul to bring the Gospel first to the Jewish and then to the Gentile... But you won't hear that here on this DVD, but the good news is every KJV Bible tells you all about it. Look to God's Word, not actors to tell you the truth. God's only begotten Son will save you, if you believe on Him and who He was/is/and alway will be and repent of your unbelief, just as Paul did. That's how Saul became Paul, thru Jesus Christ the LORD.

history.title: Christy - The Complete Series
history.review_title: Like a soap opera with love triangles...gag..
history.text: Wishy washy preachers who don't even know what they believe in let alone having no ability to console the dying...that was the character of David...a man who seemed to be ticked off every other minute, and impotent when it came to anything spiritual... Christy's character was a do gooder who felt she knew what was best for everybody without even asking them, causing a lot of feuding and conflict. Though she supposedly wanted to help people, she seemed to do as much harm as good... Got tired of all the bs about pagan stories and evolution and whatnot shoved in from the doctor...For a supposed Christian series there seemed to be more superstition abounding than true Christian beliefs...and the Christian beliefs never seemed to be strong in the main characters, but only in the supporting cast on a rare occassion. I liked the supporting cast of neighbors as well as LeVar Burton and a lot of the children. I didn't need to see characters in their skivvies or bathing, thank you very much. There are better series out there. I would rather recommend the Sarah, plain and tall series. Honestly I have never read the Christy series, but I can tell you I wouldn't even bother to watch the last episode once I saw where it was heading... I hope the books are better, but after watching this, I doubt I would even bother with them.

history.title: Decoy: The Only Package with ALL 39 Episodes Available!
history.text: UPDATE: After trying to watch the last 2 discs of this series i finally had to just stop as i really wanted a show that was less raunchy and more befitting the time era as opposed to all the loud, fast, profane things that put out on tv now. After seeing a woman almost being raped or the title character being beaten up in an alley by a bunch of street thugs, I gave up on this show. I prefer a quieter type drama/mystery show where you get to know the main character (think Foyle's War-- first four seasons,or the early Dragnet episodes when Friday's partner was Frank Smith, or even Margaret Rutherford 's wonderful portrayal of Miss Marple)... I don't need smut to get the storyline across, I can figure out clever innuendo. To me there was nothing satisfying about these episodes and I can see why there were only 39 episodes made. I'm sorry I purchased it and just ended up throwing it out so as to not pollute anyone else's eyes, ears, hearts, and mind. Life is too short to be wasted on shows like this. Original review when first bought.. I am not writing as a fan of Beverly Garland, as I haven't seen her in anything else... However, that much being said, she does a pretty good job as police woman Patricia "Casey" Jones... My favorite part of this series though is not the stories, but the character actors you recognize as such or those whom later went on to bigger and better things, such as Edward Asner, Al Lewis, Colleen Dewhurst (thank goodness her acting improved over time!!!) The one thing I did not like though was the screeching, piercing music throughout that made trying to watch it quietly at night difficult as it was much louder than the dialogue. Though this was interesting to watch for real footage of NYC in the fifties including all the great cars they had, I much prefer the Dragnet format for a crime show where the main characters, or partners, play off each other and compliment the storyline...in this you have Beverly going solo most of the time and it is hard to get to know and like her character. It's not a good show, and the episodes aren't worth my time of watching again since I am not a film noir fan nor an avid Beverly Garland fan...I like mysteries most and these are just a trifle bit too campy...and, as it turns out, raunchy...if you are looking for something more clean to watch then today's debauchery, keep looking as this is definitely not it...you definitely end up feeling tainted when ur done watching this depressing fare...
Just awful and dated. Automatic audience laughter. Boring

history.title: Winter's Tale
history.text: Ignore the fact that the movie did not do well in the theaters. I sought by chance on a flight back from Europe and then saw again on DVD. You really don't want to miss this time traveling movie with the white horse, the villains, and the eternal hero played by Colin Farrell. The other actors both acknowledged and in cameo were all wonderful. It's a great winter's movie.

history.title: A Place to Call Home, Season 1
history.review_title: They do it better in Australia. Not to be missed
history.text: Superb show. It's been streaming for some time on Acorn.TV. My review from Amazon.UK follows: It will be curious to see how long it takes for the PBS System in the United States to wake up and put on this very interesting production. My guess is they will miss it entirely and it will end up going to Netflix or Amazon prime. We loved the first series, which we watched on a multi-region DVD player in the United States and then also bought the second series from Amazon.UK. You can imagine my amusement when I learned that the second series was being shipped by air from Australia. Yes, someone has commented it is a high-level soap opera that is such a much higher order and the programs we have that I really beg people to watch it. Also I have heard that there is a third series to be produced by another Australian television organization and possibly even a fourth so cheers for that.
