history.text: Everyone by now knows about the Suchet Poirots. They are fine but I still prefer Joan Hickson's Miss Marple. Not Mr. Suchet's shortcoming - I've never been 100% crazy about Christie's creation of the arrogant, narcissistic, moustache-plastered Poirot.

history.title: Parsifal: The Metropolitan Opera Orchestra and Chorus
history.review_title: Great performance of the greatest opera ever
history.text: The one and only authentic DVD performance of this arguably greatest work in all art, not just in opera and not just in music. Avoid the newer Met performance with Jonas Kauffmann, as well as all the other Regietheater junk.

history.title: Wagner - Tannhauser (remastered)
history.text: Beautiful rendition of Wagner's earlier work, later revised to this "Paris" version. The only authentic available DVD.

history.title: Psycho
history.text: One of the greats. Probably Hichcock's best, maybe tied with "Dial M for Murder", way ahead of all his others. Always shocks at first, but then the moral of the film becomes predominant: once having committed a crime, there is no going back. Poor beautiful Janet Leigh ... wonderful acting by her and of course the infallible Anthony Perkins.

history.title: Inside Job
history.text: This is THE documentary exposing the massive corruption in our present society, focusing on Wall Street of course but extending even into formerly pristine academe. I used to think we have just dumbed down, now I know we have been stabbed in the back. Be sure to read director Charles Ferguson's 'Predator Nation' also.

history.title: The Ramrodder / Revenge of the Virgins (Special Edition)
history.text: Unspeakable trash, not the original.

history.title: Prokofiev - Cinderella / Sibley, Dowell, Royal Ballet
history.review_title: If you want to hear an excellent and complete performance you have to go to CD's
history.text: It's been remarked elsewhere that an important portion of act 3 is omitted, namely when the prince travels abroad. This is a serious omission musically and it reinforces my suspicion that ballet companies care little about the music and everything about the dancing. Now, in most ballets this is perhaps tolerable since most ballet music is trivial to begin with (Adam, Delibes, Mendelssohn, Tchaikovsky et al) but this is anything but the case here with Prokofiev's marvelous music. If you want to hear an excellent and complete performance you have to go to CD's. I like the Ashkenazy/Cleveland Orch. one.

history.title: Sergei Einstein's Ivan the Terrible
history.review_title: Superb flicks but not for the Hollywood-loving, braindead set.
history.text: Superb flicks but not for the Hollywood-loving braindead set. If you like Hollywood garbage (which is quasi a redundancy since practically all Hollyywood films are garbage) you will not like this superbly artistic production. Be forewarned and watch "Rambo XIV" or similar instead. The soundtrack is inaudible (sad since music is by the great Sergei Prokofiev no less), picture quality is primitive - in fine, nothing to recommend to you action-loving, violence-revelling types.

history.title: Berg: Lulu (Metropolitan Opera)
history.review_title: ... person at the Met and this dvd redoubled my great admiration for the opera
history.text: I saw this performance in person at the Met and this dvd redoubled my great admiration for the opera, the score and the conducting. The greatest opera of the 20th century in a nearly perfect rendition. It's true that this package is not as appealing as the many DGG Met issues; it's basically a tape of the pbs presentation; but that is a minor concern compared to all the bad alternatives out there, most recently one with the Barcelona Opera with The Ripper somehow ending up as Santa Claus ... no kidding!

history.title: Berg: Lulu [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Colorful, eccentric, erotic, esoteric, busy, excellent singing ... but not Berg's Lulu.
history.text: Starts with Lulu not dressed as a shepherdess as intended, but in the buff, briar patch and all - and ends with The Ripper as Santa Claus and Lulu, stabbed yet just standing there seemingly trying to decide whether or not to drop dead. Inbetween so much stage alteration motion that you never knew what belongs in the opera & what doesn't. And the Barcelona orchestra is no match for Jimmy Levine's ensemble. OK, many of you like regietheater and here it is for you. Me, I don't. There is a new Met performance that may be available on dvd by now & it's very good also. Again, a bit phantasmagorical but still within the bounds of good taste and credibility.

history.title: W.
history.text: I can't believe such high caliber actors would embarrass themselves to this degree. Josh Brolin...Richard Dreyfuss...James Cromwell...Jeffrey Wright...Toby Jones...Ellen Burstyn, etc. I literally felt embarrassed for them. And you know some of them probably did this for free just for the chance to "show the Bush administration." There are movies that are bad...then really bad movies...then bad "made for TV movies" and bad movies barely show on TV. This movie is the toilet paper in the dirty bathroom of the gas station where bad movies barely shown on TV buys its cigarettes.

history.title: Gone
history.text: I highly recommend this movie. I saw it when it hit theaters last year and had a good time on a cold, February afternoon. It's suspenseful, well written and well acted. You no doubt have read the plot summary by now and either buy-in to the premise or not. If you do, then don't worry about plunking down your $12 for this movie. I liked the cinematography - shot on location in Portland, Oregon. And the music is on target as well.

history.title: Black Dynamite
history.text: Most period movies and TV shows, trying to go for that retro look, never authentically pull it off. Not with "Black Dynamite." "Black Dynamite" is the only period movie I've ever seen that looks like it was actually filmed in its portrayed era. It's a masterpiece. Perfection.

history.title: Roseanne: The Complete Series
history.text: FINALLY! Roseanne in one package. Now...about that package...here's what I've done. My "M*A*S*H" collection (and everyone knows how bad that packaging is) resides in a smaller "two up" zip binder and holds the entire collection of discs. Sits right on my shelf on top of my other TV DVDs, with the booklet inside. Every season...every DVD easily accessible. No muss, no fuss. I will do this with the Roseanne set.

history.title: The Long Goodbye [DVD]
history.text: Altman at his best is on parade through this entire movie: the slow moving camera ... overlapping dialog ... dialog that sounds improvised ... all the hallmarks that Altman fans appreciate. Then there's Elliott Gould and his approach to playing Philip Marlowe, which is an obvious riff on Bogey. I love Gould's performance in this movie. Slow moving, unshakable, cool. Add to that the cinematography and on location LA scenery. And then we get to the John Williams/Johnny Mercer penned score "The Long Goodbye", which permeates the entire movie, from the opening score, to a grocery store to even a doorbell. Magnificent and will leave you humming this song for days to come. One other thing...if you have never smoked a cigarette in your life, this movie might convince you to take up the habit, even more so than watching an entire season of "Mad Men."

history.title: Hill Street Blues: The Complete Series [DVD]
history.text: With the "Hill Street Blues: The Complete Series" collection, and with "Family Ties", "Cosby" and "Cheers" already on hand, my Thursday nights will feel like Thursday nights again...(might have to pick up "Night Court" too). There was nothing like that original Thursday Night NBC lineup in the 80s. This is fantastic!

history.review_title: Very disappointed. Shakespear's language has been altered and scenes added/deleted
history.text: Very disappointed. Shakespear's language has been altered and scenes added/deleted. Not a fan. Got ten minutes in and couldn't take it any longer. I'm afraid this movie comes highly NOT recommened.

history.title: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull (Single-Disc Edition)
history.text: "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull" is a fantastic movie, whether watching as part of the larger "Indy" canon, or as a stand alone. It truly doesn't get the credit it deserves. 1). The complaints about the refrigerator scene. Pretty sure the elaborate cave system and rolling boulder in "Raiders" is just as unrealistic but just as fun. 2). The aliens. The aliens. The aliens! "Skull" took place in the 50s when UFOs and aliens were all the rage. B-Movies were aplenty. "Skull" is both a nod to the era and to those movies. If the complaint is unrealism, again I point back to "Raiders" and the final scene. Here's why I loved this movie: +The lighting. "Skull" is lit in a classic, three dimensional style. High key hot lights. The cinematography is amazing. Watch it again and pay attention to how well every scene is lit. Amazing. +The sets. Big beefy sets: the warehouse, jail cell, cemetery, the Incan Temple, all of them. Nice and detailed. +The minimal CGI. Of course there is some CGI, but it's kept to a minimum. Thankfully. +The opening scene. Places us squarely in the world of what we're about to watch. Elvis' "Hound Dog", the roadster, the authentic looking teens, "The Atomic Cafe" sign. There's no escaping that we're in the 1950s. "Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull" hits on all points and, for me at least, is as classic an Indiana Jones adventure as the rest of them. Matter of fact, I place this second behind "Raiders of the Lost Ark."

history.title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (50th Anniversary Special Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.text: 5 stars for the movie, of course. 4 stars for Kino Lorber's 50th anniversary release of this classic. This is a long movie and it needed more chapter selections. That's only a minor complaint. 1 star for the extra features only because the frame rate is very ganky (that's a very technical term, by the way). The features look like a Real Media video stream from 1998. Its real inexcusable.

history.title: Happy Days - The Complete First Season
history.text: You all know about Happy Days, so I can't add anything more about the show that you don't already know. So let me skip the gristle and get right to the bone: when this DVD set first came out, "Rock Around The Clock" had been replaced by the "Sunday Monday Happy Days" theme. Much to my shock and surprise, "Rock Around The Clock" is indeed the theme song used for Season 1 again. This alone is worth the price of admission.

history.title: Batman: The Killing Joke [DVD]
history.review_title: For comic book or Batgirl fans only
history.text: This was supposed to be the bomb the best of the best, and perhaps to someone who owns all the comics and is an extreme fan of the comics it is. However to a fan who has none of the comics, but all the movies, series, and animations it is probably the worst one they have produced in a long time. It is extremely boring and there is little joker, action, interesting story, or even anything to even really earn it that r rating. If you are a big comic book or batgirl fan get it, otherwise I would advice passing on this one.

history.title: Hunter x Hunter Set 1 [DVD]
history.review_title: Great show for nostalgia or new viewers.
history.text: I have never seen Hunter X Hunter before, so I am fresh new eyes on an older classic.I found this well animated and paced with a great english voice cast. The story appeals to all ages, it has a refreshing almost whimsy to it for an adult viewer. I think that the way violence and death is handled also allows it to be appropriate for youngsters as well. My one complaint is part three is still almost two months away from release.

history.title: Ragnarok - The Complete S.A.V.E.
history.review_title: A study in the wrong way to do an anime
history.text: Kidsy, stupid , boring , and with terrible annoying voice actors. These are the high points.

history.title: Evangelion: 1.11 You Are (Not) Alone
history.text: High points: 1: good animation.2: really cool robot/alien fights. Low points: 1: One fight per half movie lasting less than 10 minutes. 2: when there is no fight scene BORING! All talk no doing anything.

history.title: Black Lagoon: Roberta's Blood Trail [Blu-ray/DVD Combo]
history.review_title: Not as good as the series
history.text: Not as good as the series. They tried to recreate the feel of it but it just didn't happen.

history.title: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them (DVD)
history.text: The way this was advertised I think I had too high expectations. It was always being compared to the Harry Potter's and it just didn't measure up. As a way to spend a couple of hours and be entertained it's fine. If, however, you are coming into this expecting the story or acting to pull you into another world you will be disappointed.

history.title: Alice Through the Looking Glass
history.text: Tried to recapture the magic and wonder of the first. Fell flat on its butt and started digging a hole. Even returning actors couldn't save lousy story, non-existing plot, and some of the worst movie decisions I have seen.

history.title: ROGUE ONE: A STAR WARS STORY
history.text: Let us start with this isn't set very long before Star Wars A New Hope like days before. Acting well it isn't great. This follows the path of the people who steal the Deathstars plans. There is an unnecessary romance involved, simply nonexistent story ( they take all of that from the other movies), it does not make any sense until almost the end. Lastly has an ending similar to the Titanic, you know where everyone dies.

history.title: Goku Midnight Eye Complete OVA Series
history.text: If you like anime like Cyber City, Wicked City, or Ghost in the Shell this is a must. A nitty gritty p.i. with an eye that makes him special trying to win the babes and catch the badies in a world where good isn't always so good and things aren't always how they appear. This show has a real old school detective feel to it and it is really good.

history.title: Darkside Blues: Complete Collection
history.text: Artwork is good. Story isn't really there though. It really comes down to it's too much for a movie. Mystery stranger possibly from another world, don't have time to flesh that out so he will just wander in and out mysteriously. Beautiful woman running darkside of Tokyo, no time for that she will just claim to run everything while not accomplishing anything. Evil organization trying to control the world (why? that's just what they do) and kill everybody(why? again, just what they do), is sending deadly assassins to kill a rebel. The assassins come with extreme abilities some are enhanced humans(not explained) and others have psycic or magical powers(again not explained). Lone surviving rebel of a group that tried to take down this evil corp.,his group is unexplained, reasons untold, he is there to bring the characters together for a common goal, and we've run out of time ending the struggle continues. Feel satisfied? I don't.

history.title: How to Fall in Love
history.text: Very cute and fun. Love Eric Mabius. One to relax and watch whenever in the mood for light romance. Mabius has created a personna that is very shy and endearing.

history.title: The Decoy Bride
history.text: SO QUIRKY!! This movie is really really funny. But off-the-wall kind of funny. It really reminded us of that Irish movie - Waking Ned Devine. I could easily have believed that they were written by the same author. Love the main girl in this - she was very cute and endearingly bumbling, and funny and sweet. she worked perfectly with david tennant. have seen 3 times now, and laugh more each time. (she was the voice of 'merida' in 'brave')

history.title: The Good Wife: The Final Season
history.text: sometimes it seems like writers are competing to end their series badly. I know there will always be those who disagree, but this series ended horribly. watch the other seasons, and give the end a miss.

history.title: A Respectable Trade VHS
history.review_title: A Masterpiece Theater that deserves to be seen
history.text: Why is this Masterpiece Theater not on DVD? It deserves to be. It deserves to be seen. It stayed with me and I wanted to see it again, just wish I could have a better copy. Its' subject is as relevant today as it has ever been. It is hard to watch in places, but it was very well done and moving and worth seeing.

history.title: Baby's First Christmas / Bride for Christmas
history.text: Bride for Christmas was fun. Baby's first Christmas was amazingly random and badly written. We give it a quarter of a star.

history.title: Collision Earth
history.text: It is a typical 'disaster' movie and i really liked it. it was exactly what i expected and i have watched it several times now.

history.title: Paranoia
history.review_title: A really good movie that deserved to be better known
history.text: A good movie with actors i like. it holds up to re-watching too.

history.review_title: If you tend to like disaster movies, you'll like this one.
history.text: It was just what you expect. I liked it. It was a typical 'disaster' movie, and it was good.

history.review_title: Everyone's favorite aunt should be Auntie Mame
history.text: Everyone's favorite aunt should be Auntie Mame. Rosalind Russell is a one woman tour de force in a colorful and epic drama/comedy in stunning Technirama. Wow and many thanks to WAC for remastering this one to perfection. The movie is golden. The Blu-ray no less. Enjoy. For those never having seen it, this one is a blind purchase. It will warm your heart.

history.title: Hangover Square
history.review_title: Poor Linda Darnell will not have a good time of ...
history.text: Bizarre, brooding and diabolical with a real cliffhanger of an ending; Laird Cregar, in his last role before his untimely death, plays a psychopath killer suffering from crippling bouts of amnesia. Poor Linda Darnell will not have a good time of it. But you will love this disc. Newly restored, Hangover Square has never looked this good on home video. A great movie and a solid Blu-ray. Wow and thank you!

history.title: My Blue Heaven [Blu-ray]
history.text: Featherweight fluff with Steve Martin as a Mafioso and Rick Moranis as the FED assigned to keep his whereabouts under wraps. I love this movie, despite its silly plot and idiotic conclusion. Martin is one of cinema's treasures. Moranis comes pretty close to achieving a like-minded classification. WAC's Blu-ray is solid. Enjoy this for what it is. Good fun.

history.title: Starship Troopers 4K UHD
history.review_title: the best this movie has ever looked
history.text: Starship Troopers has not aged very well. Too much blood and guts with a little Nazism thrown in and some gratuitous nudity. It came across as ground-breaking in its special effects back in the day. Today, it's just another rather pointless actioner with a lot of taut flesh thrown to the slaughter or Ginsu-ed by some horrendous CGI bugs. Yuck! The 4K presentation is, of course, the best this movie has ever looked. But with so many better movies in Sony's Columbia/Tri-Star cannon, why did this one get pushed to the front of the line. How about The Remains of the Day, Little Women, Sense and Sensibility, Annie, A Man for All Seasons, Tootsie, Steel Magnolias...the list could go on and on. Bottom line: ultra-violent to the point of anesthetizing, Starship Troopers is not the movie you remember it to be. The disc is perfect. The movie...anything but.

history.title: They Shoot Horses, Don t They? (Special Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: This isn't a feel good but a 'whoa
history.text: Darkly disturbing and poignantly acted, They Shoot Horses Don't They is given a royal release on Blu-ray and it is about time. Too many surprises along the way, but suffice it to say, Jane Fonda is doing some stellar acting here, along with Bruce Dern and Red Buttons. The 1080p transfer looks marvelous. Just buy it and prepare to be shocked by what you see. This isn't a feel good but a 'whoa...how on earth did something like this get made in the first place?' Great movie making like this was rare back then. Today, it's all but nonexistent. Regrets there.

history.title: Since You Went Away (Roadshow Edition)
history.review_title: A great cast and an important story to tell
history.text: Since You Went Away is the sort of wartime weepy that deserves far more recognition than it has received in the years since WWII. A great cast and an important story to tell. Kino's Blu-ray is a mess; riddled in artifacts, noise, a barrage of age-related damage. Why this release was not given the necessary clean up it deserves is beyond me. Buy for content. The disc will definitely not win any awards!

history.title: Suspect - 30th Anniversary - Blu-ray
history.review_title: Suspect has Cher's mesmerizing performance to recommend it. It's not enough to save the film
history.text: Cliched and silly, Suspect has Cher's mesmerizing performance to recommend it. It's not enough to save the film, but it yields some fairly solid scenes between her and co-stars, Liam Neeson and Dennis Quaid. The plot starts off solid but then devolves into dreck. By the end you'll be left saying "oh please" - words, effectively to describe any Blu-ray marked as a 30th anniversary edition that offer virtually no extra features and a 1080p transfer that is only marginally appealing. Bottom line: Suspect is highly suspect as an entertainment. Cher gets top marks. But even she cannot save this turkey.

history.title: Lost Horizon
history.review_title: Even the less than perfect 16mm inserts look exceptionally clean
history.text: Frank Capra's towering achievement gets a royal Blu-ray release from Sony, restoring a minute and a half to a movie that, regrettably is still piece work of the original release. Will other materials resurface in years to come. We hope so. What's here has been given utmost consideration by Sony. Even the less than perfect 16mm inserts look exceptionally clean, with image stabilization applied. This is a classic beyond most and deserves top shelf consideration in any collector's collection. Buy today. Treasure forever.

history.title: Brigadoon [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Lerner and Loewe's melodic masterpiece looks almost perfect on Blu-ray
history.text: Lerner and Loewe's melodic masterpiece looks almost perfect on Blu-ray. WAC has done a lot to preserve the flawed AnscoColor. We give them top marks. This transfer looks a little weak in its saturation, also its contrast. The story is timeless; two pals from the jaded present stumbling across a mythical Scottish village that materializes once every hundred years from the highland mists. Gene Kelly and Cyd Charisse dance to perfection. Van Johnson is sublime as the cynical best friend. Great performances and a superb score, regrettably missing one of my favorite songs, "Come to Me, Bend to Me" filmed but cut from the final release. It's here as an extra. Were that it belonged to the film proper. Oh well, it never did. What's here is going to impress. Prepare for a delightful night at the movies.

history.title: Miracle On 34th St (bw)
history.review_title: Disgusting that Fox should reissue its severely flawed Blu-ray from ...
history.text: Disgusting that Fox should reissue its severely flawed Blu-ray from a decade ago with different cover art but the same digital anomalies afflicting this disc. The image is too dark and riddled in heavy-handed DNR and edge enhancement. If you already own Miracle on 34th Street on Blu-ray there is NO GOOD REASON to repurchase it here. Skip and send a message to Fox. A new transfer is in order for something claiming to be a 70th anniversary! Bah, humbug!

history.review_title: Not for us and we were fans of Janet King Series 1 & 2
history.text: We enjoyed Series 1 & 2 but this one we found quite dull. For our liking, it had too much to do with her family life, girlfriend problems and trying to create a relationship with her father whom she had not seen in 20 years. Won't be buying Series 4 if there is one. The ending couldn't have been worse. All that work they put into trying to bring criminals to justice. Won't spoil the ending but don't know how they do it.

history.title: Bad Day at Black Rock
history.text: We went to the Cowboy Museum in Lone Pine, CA and I ordered this from Amazon right away. What a star-studded cast: Spencer Tracy, Lee Marvin, Walter Brennan. Kept waiting for a story...and nothing emerged.

history.review_title: You're in for a pleasant surprise!
history.text: What a wonderful combination of police detective work and an undertaker! They can go hand in hand and to think we'd find humor was a pleasant surprise. Sorry the show didn't continue. Very well done & excellent stories & acting.

history.review_title: Well done just find it a bit slow going.
history.text: I'm not a big fan of Midsomer but my husband is and he would rate it a 5. Bit much, in my opinion, to have so many murders in one episode. In real life, just how many times does that happen. I do miss Jones and this new guy's just a kid. Barnaby needs to buy some new suits - every episode he is wearing a blue suit. I appreciate the hard work that goes into these shows and the scenery is just breathtaking. Getting a bit pricey - only two episodes per disc now and the price remains the same.

history.title: Great British Baking Show Season 4 DVD
history.text: What a lovely show - The Great British Baking Show - pity that Paul Hollywood went his way and left the great Mary Berry behind. Though she, Mel and Sue are on another show now. Very entertaining and fun to watch them follow instructions and produce some magnificent bakes...in such a short amount of time.

history.title: Inspector Rex: Series 1-5 [PAL/0]
history.review_title: Don’t hesitate to buy this marvelous series - one of the best we have ever seen.
history.text: Inspector Rex - what a delightful series. We had Season 1 and so sorry when it ended and I searched every where looking for more seasons and I found it here. What a gorgeous dog Rex is - the amount of time the trainers must have put into this series. The comraderie among the actors, the acting, scenery, stories - all get our vote as a 10. Pity we didn’t know about this treasure until just now but we’re sure enjoying it. Lovely Rex, Inspector Rich and the other two main characters turn in a remarkable performance. A gem from Austria, in German with English subtitles.

history.title: Hetty Wainthropp Investigates: The Complete Collection (reissue)
history.review_title: A wonderful series - thoroughly enjoying them.
history.text: Oh Patricia Routledge turns in a marvelous acting performance (Keeping Up Appearances fame). Her sidekick, Geofrey and to husband, Robert, all have a great chemistry. What great little mysteries as Hetty has opened her own dectective agency and they go about solving them. Nonviolent and based on a book when Ms. Routledge was tapped for the part. Each episode is about 1 hour long and they close out each case, Highly recommend. British English with subtitles.

history.title: Out of the Furnace
history.text: There were so many good actors in this movie I thought for sure it was foolproof and would be awesome. I really anticipated a great action movie. It was just okay for me. I think most of the movie was a little slow-paced, and it didn't really pick up until the end. Sadly, not soon enough though. The idea of it being loosely based on the old adage, an eye for an eye, wasn't for me either. It's been done too many times to count, so in order for it to stand out it needs to be impeccably done. The ending as I said was different and what I liked most about the film. Don't think it was because it was finally ending, though honestly, that helped too. I was over it at that point. The last of the movie was really gritty, and if you read my blog regularly, that's kinda what I'm into. I don't want fluff, I want blood and gore. What can I say?! My mom claims I should have been a boy. Will I recommend it? Probably not. I probably won't think about it again.

history.title: Birdman
history.review_title: I'm the one who didn't like it!
history.text: It's me. I just didn't enjoy it or get it, frankly. I also don't get how this film stole all the awards' (nominations - left out this word initially... sorry to the people who couldn't figure that out.) at the Oscars. I get it was a sophisticated story, but maybe too sophisticated for me. I felt the degrees of separation were just too far for my tastes. It was so hard to decipher what was real and what was fantasy. Was he crazy, suicidal or both? I feel like I will never know. In the end, I feel like this is two hours of my life I can't get back.

history.title: Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children
history.text: The hubby and I have both read the book. I also read Hollow City, the second book, so I have a great understanding for what the film should be about. I said after reading Miss Peregrine's that Tim Burton would be the guy to make this book come alive, and I was right! He did such a great job at creating what I had in mind for the film version of the story. The kids were so well cast, they literally blew me away. I wasn't a fan of the actress that played Miss Peregrine, but that is because, in my mind, Miss Peregrine was much older than her. Still, she played her well. I did think a couple of the scenes ended rather abruptly... and even the hubby was like, "What the hay?!" The film was a great adaption though, blending both the first and second book in the series. If you read the book, or books, then you will enjoy the movie. If you haven't, you may find it too peculiar for you. I suggest reading the book. Even if you think you won't like it. I love when people are surprised.... Then watch the movie.

history.title: Masterminds
history.text: The hubby and I had so many laughs watching this one. Based on a true story of one of the biggest heists in history, the director pulls you right in with hilarity. It took real finesse choosing how to make a serious event into a riot of laughs, but this guy did it well! A great cast of characters also helped make this film great! Zach Galifianakis is so funny, I could actually watch this one again. I was surprised by how much I enjoyed Mike McKinney too, played by Jason Sudeikis. This guy kinda stole the show for me! His part was jokes! I highly recommend watching the bloopers at the end too. Hilarious!!!

history.title: X-MEN: APOCALYPSE
history.text: Out of all the XMen movies I have seen, and I have seen most of them if not all, this was one of the best. Staying true to the comic in every way, blended with an exciting, edge-of-the-seat story line, I was hooked from the beginning. I watched it with the hubby and even he was blown away. He also thought it was better than some of the others. I can't wait to see more now! At least, provided they make them, which I'm sure they will. 4.5/5

history.title: Assassin's Creed
history.text: The hubby and I watched this together. I had seen him play the game a few times, but my knowledge of the game is slim-to-none. I didn't know the story or the characters, other than the role he played as the assassin. This is where the hubby could fill me in, knowing the game inside and out. The first thing he noticed was how much story they added to an already existing story, though that was minimal to begin with. There were a couple of moments that he was lost at what was happening, since it didn't happen in the game. It made the movie better though. The story got quite exciting, full of action, and pulled us in deep. The actors were well cast in this film too. They played the scenes well, which were also very vivid and brought it all to life. It was so interesting, even if you had no knowledge of the game or its existence. For those that know the game will agree some of the scenes are spot on! It was such a good movie!

history.title: Immortal Life of HenriettaLacks(DHD/DVD)
history.text: I wish I had read the book first, but the story in the movie was pretty epic. Henrietta is singlehandedly the reason why so many people have lived on. Her cells have been used in so many diseases, trying to combat or prevent them, that she should be cannonized. Oprah was the perfect choice as Henrietta's daughter, the reason the story is told in the first place. Her studios also paid for the film, so it is well made. Rose Bryne played a good part. She got to tell Henrietta's story. I'm so glad I've seen this. Learned her story and I still wamt to read the book too. Remember there is some emotional scenes but they make the story. 4.5/5

history.title: Big Little Lies: Season 1 (Digital HD + DVD)
history.text: This series takes you to a place that might make you uncomfortable at times. It also takes you into a lighthearted group of friends and their lives. I love how the cast of actors made these characters come alive. Getting immersed into the whodunit at the playground was fun too. It was not what I was thinking at all, but in retrospect, I'm not surprised either seeing where Max comes from. It hits hard at the end. Bring some tissues for that one. Seriously. Can't wait for season 2 now!

history.title: The Boss Baby
history.text: I loved hearing my favorite Beatles tune! When it played, I realized how much kids would love it too. The way they sang it geared it more to a child but it was good. A great family movie is one that can capture the child and adult alike. This movie definitely did that. Even the dog got up to the screen a few times to watch closer. More when puppies were involved, but still. Well-made and fun for everyone. This animated film is surely to be a favorite for many for a long time. Being the Elvis freak I am, there was a special treat while watching! I love, love, loved it! Made my day!

history.title: Captain Underpants: The First Epic Movie [DVD]
history.text: This was a movie that I watched while home bored and alone. As I was watching it, I did laugh a few times, but quickly realized it was a film geared for small kids. Even the jokes were too immature for just me. I liked it though. I remember reading some books year ago and the story here is much of what I would have in mind when thinking of Captain Underpants. So kiudos for bringing the book to life! Still, this is for kids.

history.title: Father Ted: The Definitive Collection

history.title: Noah's Ark - The Mini-Series Event
history.text: I remember when I was young I saw what I thought was Noah's Ark with my parents. It must have been a segment of another Biblical movie that I remembered about Noah. It was VERY WELL done. I thought maybe a Charlton Heston played Noah. Who ever it was, was a major movie star back then. I remembered as Noah was summoned by God to build the Ark, all the chaos going on with orgies and strange violent people around him when he was building the Ark not taking what he tried to warn everyone about seriously and what was going to happen. It was REALLY intense as I remember. I only wish I could find WHATEVER Movie I seen originally in my youth, because it sure wasn't THIS MOVIE. This REALLY is a bad rendition to say the least. I honestly was doubting if this wasn't a spoof. John Voight is Noah and God sounds like Woody Allen. I started laughing so hard I couldn't take it. Emily Mortimer is in the movie and I should have been tipped off by that alone, because she is way to young to be in the movie I seen years ago (and I LOVE Emily Mortimer, That's the reason I bought this in the first place and being smitten by her, I made this choice with my heart not my head!). I know this shouldn't be taken lightly, but as I said, if you have a good sense of humor, you'll love this. This is in the same class as a Monty Python style movie, like the "Holy Grail". I guess it's really not supposed to be a comedy, but I'm going to set this movie aside for a rainy day or when I'm maybe down in the dumps. This will lift my spirits and give me another good laugh. It's a movie that is hard to take seriously but, if you have a goofy sense of humor, you'll LOVE IT!! I gave it a 1 star because IF it's supposed to be taken seriously, it stinks, BUT, if you take a light hearted view, it may be a 5 star to you. I think it's HILARIOUS!! Is Woody Allen the voice of GOD? You be the judge.... hahahahahahaha

history.title: Iron Man (Single-Disc Edition)
history.text: Iron Man breathes new life into the Marvel movie universe.While most marvel movies nowadays involve some young hero out trying to find himself while trying to save the city at the same time,Iron man takes a more sophisticated and more adult approach.While there is a considerable amount of time dedicated to Tony Starks's Ingenuity i.e. building suit prototypes,weapons aand ect, good filmaking and an excellent script make this a rather enjoyable process.Any doubts about Robert Downey's acting are put to rest by this movie,as this by far is one of the strongest performances of the year.Very suprising was the lack of sexual content and graphic violence which usually defines movies as "good" nowadays.Iron Man is a rare breed of action film in many respects,a lack of pointless and graphic material ensures that anyone in the family can enjoy this film and a good script and plot round out any beliefs about this film being yet another hormone driven teenage flop.

history.title: Transformers
history.text: Having grown up watching the original Transformers cartoons, it's hard to admit certain things about this film.True there are a few well made action scenes and the CGI work is some of the most intricate on celluloid yet.However,the films achilles heel is both the script and CGI.There has obviously been too much time and energy invested on the films teenage chracters.This is not American Pie or an episode of High School Stories...this is Transformers.Also,the CGI work is so advanced that yes,though every little part moves and operates individually,the final shot is one of thousands of undecernable pixels smashing into each other.Though the humor was suprisingly good and present throughout the film,the directors choice to over-modernize a good series with yet more Linkin Park songs and irritating teenagers may turn off fans of the original series.It's a decent film,it's just not about the bots.

history.title: Rocketman

history.title: The Best of Times
history.text: Though not widely known nowadays,this film has become a fall tradition in households around the country.Best of Times is the hilarious tale of one mans quest to correct a highschool football failure that plunges his small town into "lethergy" and haunts him well into adulthood.Robin Williams and Kurt Russel unite to lead the old team to victory and redeem their towns dignity and pride in this football classic that's packed with tons of heart and soul.This is one of those rare comedies that delivers in every department,so suit up and join the tradition by enjoying one of the most treasured and heartwarming comedies that has brought families together since the real best of times. "In conclusion I'd just like to say...Bakersfield must be destroyed!"

history.title: The Matrix Reloaded (Widescreen Edition) [DVD]
history.text: Reloaded is the second film in the Matrix trilogy.Following the events of the first Matrix film,Reloaded brings back the original cast to continue their fight against the "system" known as the Matrix.With the machines digging ther way towards the last surviving human colony,it's up to Neo and his comrades to bring down the system before all is lost.Just as the original Matrix set the benchmark for visual effects,Reloaded sets it twice as high by using the latest CG tools to create some of the most mind-blowing and visually stunning fights and chase sequences ever seen,along with more of the same extraordinary character depth that these films are famous for.Though not as strong in storyline as it's predecessor,Reloaded provides a refreshing and intellectual movie experience and sets the stage for the war to end all wars.

history.title: Walk the Line (Widescreen Edition)
history.text: Walk the Line tells the story of Johnny Cash,one of the greatest musical legends of the 20th century.The film follows The Man in Black as he grows up/serves in the military/discovers music/falls into depression and then in love.Joaquin Phoenix and Reese Witherspoon have wonderful on-screen chemistry and provide some of the most accurate voice and physical portrayals of the real music legends found on film to date.The cast,acting and cinematography are top-notch.Furthermore,the choice of songs performed by the actors during the film could not have been better.It should be said,however,that while this movie does chronicle most of Mr. Cash's life and show specific events that inspired some of his most famous songs,those looking for a History Channel style documentary need look elsewhere.All in all,Walk the line succeeds in telling one of the greatest stories in music history.Joaquin Phoenix and Reese Witherspoon have given us a glimpse of these great musicians bound by love and music that will not be soon forgotten.If you are a musician or enjoy music in general than you should see this film.

history.title: Ghost Rider (Widescreen Edition)
history.review_title: GO BACK FROM WHERE YE CAME
history.text: Ghost Rider is one of those films who's entertainment factor is truly limited to the viewers own interests. Basically,if you don't like motorcycles or flaming skeletons...then you won't like this film. The only real pros for this movie are it's near 2 hour length/good special effects/the hell cycle/ and Peter Fonda's portrayal of satan.Conversly, the film suffers from a weak plot that is chocked full of "CHEESY" dialogue and features less than stellar acting by many cast members.The single disc version of the film contains few "special features", with only basic commentaries/2 short documentaries and some trailers for other movies. Bottom line, if you like motorcycles (like I do) or have to own every movie ever made then you might enjoy this film. Barring those criteria, you're libal to find the film version of this great character to be no more appealing than if it were being done as a high school play.It's altogether too watered down with acting and dialogue that's way too cheesy and a main character that just isn't meant to be pg-13 material.

history.title: Van Helsing (Widescreen Edition)
history.text: Van Helsing was one of those rare occurences in our modern film industry, it succeeded in taking us back to the good ol' days of monster movies where even the bad guys had personality and weren't merely mutated/brain eating/thoughtless ogres or zombies. The film was cast perfectly,with most all of the actors demonstrating great chemistry and keeping their characters believable and well out of "cheese" territory.The sets and action sequences within them are wonderful and highly reminiscent of the old-school style of filmaking.There are many famous old-school villains such as: (The Wolfman/Frankenstein/Mr. hyde/Dracula/ect.) The film's CGI and Special Effects are some of the best in the industry and add significantly to the story.The plot of the film is very well written and does an excellent job of balancing such a large variety of classic characters and effectively connecting them to each other.Add on a length of slightly more than 2 hours and a pulse-pounding musical score and you've got a truly epic film.Bonus features include: (several documentaries/bloopers/movie trailers for Van Helsing and Shrek 2/an xbox compatible demo of the Van Helsing Videogame/commentaries/ect.) Van Helsing is one of those films that deserves a spot in every movie lovers dvd collection.If you enjoy watching movies at all, then you must see this film.

history.title: Last Man on Earth
history.text: While the film is as excellent as it always was, this "Alpha Video" dvd is somewhat dissapointing. (I realize this is an older dvd, but as the restored version is now out of print, and no longer available, this is the edition amazon is offering, and therefore is the basis of my review). The back of the disc is the same bare and purple style one sees when dvdr's have been used for the "made to order" films online. The picture is decent, but some pixilation is noticeable here and there. The picture is shrunken, and sits in the center of the screen. This may not be an issue for people running older dvd players and RCA cables, which tend to stretch the image to fit the screen. However, this will be an issue with modern equipment such as Blu-ray players, which is how I viewed the film. There are occasional instances of picture jump or digital lines appearing and going away (something obviously not related to the original film, but to the transfer itself). The menu is stationary and basic, with the standard "play" "index" "catalog" and "trailers" buttons. (Note: when you enter the scene index menu, there is no way to navigate back to the main menu. You must choose a scene; hitting the menu button during the film merely returns you to the scene selection. You must forward to the absolute end of the film to be returned to the main menu screen). I do gladly say though, that the film played from beginning to end, without any skips or stoppages of any kind. I remember several years ago (I believe in 2008) a new edition of this film was officially released that featured restored b&w and in-color versions. I have watched this film online several times, often in exceptional quality, which I can now only guess was from the restored 2008 version. Having neglected to purchase that version before it went out of print, I settled for this version, as it came from amazon. While I am grateful that I'll finally be able to watch it on Halloween without internet issues, having to view this film in such a low level of quality is unfortunate; as it can and has looked significantly better. That said, it's still a remarkable film for its time, and if you can't find a used copy of the 2008 version , this is still better than nothing.

history.title: Jaws [Blu-ray]
history.text: I purchased the Blu-ray to replace my aging 25th anniversary dvd version. Without a doubt, it is a significant improvement in both picture and sound quality. Fine details such as sand granules, cloth, pores, etc. are very pronounced. The film honestly looked like it had been made recently. All of the original special features in the older dvd's were included as well as some new behind the scenes featurettes, such as "the shark is still working" and a detailed look at the restoration process used for the Blu-ray release. My father, who had seen the film several times when it was originally released in theaters, was very impressed with how well the film had been restored. Suffice to say, this is the best that Jaws has ever looked. The picture and sound quality were well above what I was expecting, and I can't recommend it enough.

history.title: Primeval: Series 5 (DVD) [Region2] Requires a Multi Region Player
history.review_title: Not great, but when you have to own the complete series...
history.text: Primeval lost its way in this final series. The characters were separated on their own adventures, and they just seemed "off" as a team. The show managed to find its way back to the "old" style, but it was too litte, too late. Still, it completes the set.

history.title: Fringe: Season 3
history.review_title: Liked it so much, I bought it twice.
history.text: I lost my original set of this season, but had no qualms about replacing it. It's a fabulous series, even if it did sort of lose ground toward the end.

Just another anti big business sermon. Just like "Avatar" this is another propaganda film whereby big business exploits the friendly alien race for profit. Lots of pretty effects, but there's no pretense about the real "message" of this poor imitation of the original trilogy. I hear it's continuing with the same lame cast, but I hope the writers can lift the sequel above Age of Extinction; otherwise, please let the franchise die a dignified death. They need to do a prequel with the original cast. Aliens and humans fighting the baddie alien invaders. Shia LeBeouf can be a civilian consultant to NEST, and Josh Duhmal can be a general who's just "too damn old for this s***," as so many others have played such roles in many other blockbusters. I'm just not certain even the Autobots can save a second dismal parody. Furthermore we're back to the "helpless female" ("help me" screams the teenage daughter). Will the stereo types never stop?

history.title: Ffolkes
history.review_title: One of the best movies you've never heard of...
history.text: A wonderful character-driven action movie with a great cast. Not as bloody as today's flicks, this one is well-write, superbly acted, and remains current despite its age. I highly recommend you give it a try!

history.title: Z Nation: Season 1 [DVD]
history.review_title: Great start to an ever-improving series
history.text: I'm not a huge fan of the zombie genre, but I was looking for something new in the action arena. Started with that "other" zombie series, gave up due to the poor writing. Z Nation is a great action romp that goes from humor to horror in an instant. I write this review after seeing the next two seasons, so I'm trying to be fair about those first impressions (each season is better than the last, and the series has really hit its stride). The characters are complex, and the writers handle them deftly. Even Murphy, the self-centered, egotistical "bad" guy of the group, is constantly evolving. The series concept is simple..the zombie apocalypse...but don't mistake simple for simplistic. Within its framework, the show is character driven and always showing us new facets for every one of them. I love it: humor, action, gore, and great characters rolled into one amazing package. Just wish the DVD came with all the extras common to other tv releases.

history.title: Z Nation: Season 2 [DVD]
history.text: I think this excellent mix of comedy and horror is really coming into its own. Once again, the characters drive the story within the framework of the series. The season ended on a very upbeat note, possibly because no one was certain about renewal (SciFi is clearly clueless and seems to be more business driven than some of the other networks, which sometime show enough faith in their products to give them a decent chance). Anyway, if you like your zombies with a dash of humor, you can't go wrong. It's also good that the character of 10K is showing up more...he's liable to be the breakout character of the show.

history.title: Z Nation: Season 3 [DVD]
history.review_title: A tough transition after the cancellation jitters
history.text: Okay, maybe it's not quite as good overall as the other two seasons, but there are several fantastic episodes here. I blame SciFi for the inconsistencies. Two of the episodes are nothing but running around and fighting, clearly fillers for a season that needed time to get back up to speed. In a show with such complex characters, these throw-away episodes were a shame. Some of the episodes followed particular characters, which is fine for me since I like every one of them, but which may have created problems for those viewers who like only one or two. But the show is at its best when all the characters are together, where the episodes are balanced between action and humor and the characters get to interact with one another. There is brilliance in these characters, and my heart-felt kudos to the actors and writers who bring them to life. Bring on season 4! Still wish the DVD releases had more bonus features; really, who needs the DVD when the episodes are available on Netflix? I buy DVDs for the extras.

history.title: The Walking Dead: Season 1
history.text: In my search for more action/adventure in my tv viewing, I stumbled across this series on Netflix. I'm not a big fan of the zombie genre, but was willing to give it a try. The start was very promising, with good characters and action sequences. But as I progressed through the seasons, I became disenchanted with the writing. The characters began waffling to fit into the writers' intended outcome. I began shouting at my tv in frustration when characters on the edge of disaster suddenly turned into complete idiots just so some plot complication could happen. The final straw was when the (apparently) long-awaited introduction of the super badass villain occurred. Yes, this show may be based on a comic book series, but the writers didn't have to bow down in homage to those roots. The villain's speech was so long-winded and overblown, I was reminded of Vogon poetry (Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy) where to hear it was to be driven mad. I never made it to the end of the speech, nor have I watched since. The writing is just too deplorable to hold my interest.

history.title: Murdoch Mysteries: Once Upon a Murdoch Christmas
history.text: Another excellent entry into the Murdoch Christmas episodes. Hope the whole series stays around for a long time!

history.title: The Mummy (2017) [DVD]
history.text: Silliest movie I've seen in a long time. I suppose it was supposed to be action/adventure, and it was certainly full of action leading nowhere except what looks like a sequel. Please spare us! Stick to the first two Brendan Fraser mummy pictures. They're funny, scary, full of great characters, and a much better plot. This one tried too hard, and ended up a mishmash.

history.title: Darwin's Dilemma
history.text: If you enjoyed this or found it adds to your knowledgebase, you might enjoy: National Geographic: Lost Tribes of Palau - this documentary talks about how fast genetic changes can happen in humans. Also a book: Nutrition and Physical Degeneration - learn about how nutritional changes in ONE generation affect the next offspring in profound ways. Heck, changes in the SAME generation (Yourself and your diet). The assumption that changes only happen gradually...is false. With sustained stimulus, changes can happen very quickly. With that said, I found this doc interesting in flipping evolution on it's head.What if these guys are right (in some way), but they are more/less totally wrong about their Christian beliefs / thoughts about God, etc...? (Just assuming they are mainstream Christian based on earlier readings). On that note: check out, National Geographic: Lost Gospel of Judas. that turns Christianity as most know it, on it's head. Also PBS: First Christians: From Jesus to Christ. Also, about changes in our mind and body: search on Youtube for: 60 Minutes Endless Memory - Dutch Iceman - BBC Iceman takes a cold dip - Orlando Sorrell - Tarahumara Indians - human calculators - Rudiger Gamm - Scott Flansburg. Watch those videos and see that we are clueless about who we really are....

history.review_title: Insights into a subject not frequently talked about
history.text: Great documentary on a material that is all around us but that seldom gets talked about in any meaningful way. I especially enjoyed the incredible footage from the Amazon / Brazilian rainforest of the bauxite mine - and later footage in Europe which shows the entire production process more/less. The flood in Hungary is interesting too, I'd never heard of that. I'd heard about aluminum and alzheimer's / dementia, but never saw any documentary on it. I had no idea that such a large mining concern / large company was a Norwegian firm - Norsk Hydro. I have never used deodorant - one reason which scared me was the ingredient list a long time ago. Since then I've reduced sweating by diet modification. For many years I haven't used any shampoo or creams. I've never used antacids. How much aluminum is in my diet? Good question.This documentary may get one thinking. Aluminum cookware - I used to use that, no longer. But, if I sometimes go out to eat, do they use that? Good thing I don't eat out so much anymore. When I was young I ate plenty of kraft cheese slices and velveeta - no longer, but does my regular non processed cheese have it? After some web searching I learned more. I don't eat pickles, and I've been allergic to shellfish my entire life. I don't smoke. I don't drink soft drinks in aluminum cans (used to a lot). Nor coffee (used to), and almost never - herbal tea. I used to eat steamed buns (Chinese). I used to eat cake. I used to eat more bread products. I used to drink hot chocolate made of cocoa powder, maybe a few cups a year now? i used to eat chocolate (95-%+ gone now - pretty much only peanut MnMs!) I've almost kicked the habit of eating any canned foods. I almost never eat pretzels. Well..there's more potential sources out there according to certain research I've seen. Are we all suffering from dementia? Check out a video - 60 Minutes - Endless Memory. Maybe we are.... I'm staring at my new laptop which is encased completely in aluminum which is flanked by portable HDs made of same. I used to own an aluminum framed bicycle. I still use aluminum foil sometimes, though I have recently changed to wax paper coated with ??. I fly in airplanes made of aluminum. This documentary has made me think more about this material and our world. 5 stars! For another expose on a material in our lives, check out the documentary PLASTIC PLANET. Also EVIDENCE OF HARM for mercury in dental fillings. One may also enjoy a book called MATERIAL WORLD. Also any documentaries on ANDREW CARNEGIE will give insights into STEEL.

history.review_title: Had higher expectations, but not quite what I thought
history.text: I somehow managed to watch this to completion. I had much higher expectations, but should have realized otherwise once I saw some of the names of the people speaking as I had seen them speaking in some other videos. A significant part of this video is just "The Secret" repackaged. Something - which just inflates the ego and promotes a me-me-me culture. Anytime people start talking about "The Universe" too without being specific, I get very weary. Several of the speakers do that in this video. People use this term when they don't really understand what is going on. It's a very nebulous term. The video is basically just a bunch of talking heads with some animations and a "love" dramatization. Some of what they say is valid and enlightening for many when it comes to emotions, and if that is what it was just about, I might give this 4 stars, it's what they say you should do which gets me. The guy with the cowboy hat and arch mustache is the most annoying. He is definitely consuming way too much caffeine or some other upper -- you can hear it in his voice. He claims to not take drugs, never been to a doctor, talks about ancient wisdom, etc...yet here he is expounding the benefits of dark chocolate - which is very high in caffeine. Caffeine is a pain reliever, but it also paralyzes our muscles over time, and contributes to adding emotional baggage - which the video is saying is no good. Short term gain, long term pain. The dead giveaway for the credibility of some of the speakers is to just to look at their faces. They almost all have pinnochio noses. Do you know what that means? And if they are so stress-free, why do they have so much gray hair? Why do their voices sound stressed?

history.title: Idaho: The Movie
history.text: Amazing. Having lived in Western Washington State for a good chunk of my life, Idaho always seemed like this place in the boonies, who the hell would want to live out there? Who would even want to visit. On a multi-month cross country road trip, I drove through parts of Idaho on the way to Montana - the most memorable experiences being bugs on my truck windshield, a potato museum, and the Craters of the Moon park. Turns out I missed the most interesting parts! I would have never imagined such beauty and raw landscapes - even after traveling the world over and them some. I think the fame of Yellowstone certainly draws attention away from Idaho. Perhaps for the better.

history.review_title: Sheds light on one of those things most don't ever think about.
history.text: Sheds light on an aspect of our built environment that relatively few stop to think about. Even though I have visited Grand Coulee and Hoover Dam and perhaps a few others, I had no idea there were so many dams in the USA (if not world). Perhaps creating a dam is like eating too much of certain foods and having a blocked artery in our body. The documentary talks alot about fish runs, but perhaps there is much more to consider, some aspects of which are highlighted in the documentary. If we consider our entire planet as a dynamic system, what is the impact of impeding the free flow of water from one part to another? If you enjoy this, you might enjoy a documentary called Copy and Comprehend Nature. It discusses the research of a Viktor Schauberger on what healthy water is.

I seldom give such low reviews, but this movie was so confusing, I never finished it. I accept the premise, but it was done horribly. And this was the 2nd time I tried to watch it. I gave up 30-40 minutes into it or so. For a better example of past lives, try the movie I, Origins. The people who wrote this screenplay were trying to say too much.

history.title: What's With Wheat?
history.review_title: so, what should I eat and drink?
history.text: After you watch this you might think ok, I need to get rid of wheat products, which sounds hard enough. (But you learn *sourdough rye* might be ok for awhile) Then you watch KING CORN and you realize I need to get rid of corn (and products which contain it - HFCS for example) - which is also in many products, like wheat. Ok, this is complicated. Getting rid of corn and wheat....I'll eat more seafood, meat, fruits, and vegetables, no grains. But then you ask, is corn a vegetable, ok, maybe it isn't, it's a grain. Ok, whatever. You are thankful for eating less grains because they often have aluminum in the leavening. You remember that from watching the AGE OF ALUMINUM and doing some other research. You remember to not use DEODORANT because it often has this metal in it. But WHAT'S ON WHEAT shows you how grains are in makeup too...why do we smell and sweat anyway? Then you watch FORKS OVER KNIVES which advocates a vegetarian based diet (Or was that vegan?), so then you eliminate all meat (Many of which also eat grains unless you buy 100% grass-fed). And then you watch GMO-OMG and THE WORLD ACCORDING TO MONSANTO and then you realize you should eliminate all GMO foods, often unlabeled. So, this further complicates your selection of...what's left...some vegetables and fruit and seafood. Then you watch THAT SUGAR FILM and you learn that sugar including in the form of fruit (Fructose) is detrimental for you - so you think should I be eating eggs and bacon, but doesn't that contradict with FORKS OVER KNIVES? Then you watch FOOD, INC and then you learn than industrial food production is something to avoid - but supposedly you already got rid of a lot of that., ok, I can't just buy any regular eggs, I need not cage-free, but free-range. Whew! Then somewhere you learn that organic doesn't necessarily mean "good." So, what's left? You are totally confused and stressed out. This assumes you aren't sidetracked by the claims of the paleo crowd or any number of other diets being promoted. South Beach, Raw, Zone, etc... Seafood, but did Forks Over Knives say that was bad? You don't remember. At least I still have my vegetables. Then you learn about overfishing and mercury in many fish after watching END OF THE LINE and a few websites, then you think, ok, most fish is suspect. Nevermind that most fish is factory farmed and not wild. Do the wild ones eat plastic contamination in our oceans? Then you learn about how TOMATOES and SOY (a grain or a vegetable?) modify our ESTROGEN levels ..ok...no tomatoes. So much for eating non-meat processed products. No more tomatoes on salad. So, now you are at CERTAIN KINDS OF WILD FISH (The ones that don't have a lot of PCBs and mercury, and generally, lower on the food chain, and not canned) and some organic vegetables, with maybe some sourdough rye now and again. Then you think more and realize some people say eat RAW MILK and CHEESE, but this conflicts with something else you watched earlier (FORKS OVER KNIVES?)...besides maybe you are lactose intolerant, but you can't drink soy milk either. Now you are totally stressed out with all the conflicting rules and emotions and "scientific analysis." Then you watch NatGeo: STRESS, PORTRAIT OF A KILLER, and you think, maybe I should just eat whatever I want, to heck with all these rules and doctors and studies. Then you somehow hear about the documentaries EAT THE SUN and IN THE BEGINNING THERE WAS LIGHT and the BOY WITH DIVINE POWERS, and then you realize, maybe one doesn't have to eat anything. How the heck is this possible? Isn't sunlight bad for us, all that evil UV, I need sunglasses. But what about Vitamin D? Is more than just Vit D created when we get sunlight...yeah, you learn about PHYTOPRODUCTS. So many conflicting arguments from PhDs and attractive looking people on both sides of the fence. Who can you trust? Then you learn that we "eat" other forms of energy (EMF) too, not just "food." So you start watching documentaries like FULL SIGNAL and RESONANCE - BEINGS OF FREQUENCY. Out goes your smartphone and wi-fi that you used to learn about all this stuff - also shown in WHAT'S ON WHEAT. Then you think what about just good old water? Then you learn about acidic vs alkaline water...man, my head is ready to explode. Then you watch TAPPED and you learn about chemicals in all bottled water. Dang it. It's not so simple. I'll just drink good ol' tap water. And then you learn about CHLORINE and FLUORIDE in lots of tap water. Good grief....water isn't just water. Nevermind you might have contamined well water from fracking or some other pollution. Oh, we forgot about the detrimental effects of caffeine, so coffee, tea, and soda (But you got rid of that after watching THAT SUGAR FILM) are out. So, what's left? Then you learn about air quality, which also affects our health. Is there a documentary about that? What is it ok to die from these days? Then you learn about how certain individuals in the Bible (Which as a science loving person you think is totally ridiculous, but maybe part of you is still religious in some way) lived hundreds of years long. What did they eat? Rather what did they not eat? Why did they die? Who was this serpent anyway? Then you learn that the word hungry is made up of two parts - hun-GRY. Maybe we eat because we CRY? Because you realize C~G, like Cat = Gato in spanish. Doesn't the word hungry kind of look like AN-GRY? And then you see that the word DIET is has the word DIE-t in it. Along with DInner, DIning, and many others. Can something D(i)Elicious be bad for me? So, then you think...are you still thinking? Does the word EAT spelled backward, also mean DIE? TAE. D~T. So, what should I eat and drink? Then you realize, somebody opened Pandora's box a long time ago....and the root solution is something else...but what... you'll just have to wait, or maybe not. Maybe you should read an obscure book called QUIET FREEDOM. And you think - what does a search for a wild polar bear have to do with anything.....

history.title: Take Back Your Power: Investigating the Smart Grid
history.review_title: Excellent documentary for those who want to learn about smart meters and EMF emissions in general
history.text: awesome. Didn't know anything about smart meters before this......director/editor knows his stuff...especially when I saw a video clip about radar effects from a documentary - Exploring the Spectrum by John Ott. An obscure but profound documentary. Wireless madness. If you watch this yo may enjoy FULL SIGNAL, MOBILIZE, and RESONANCE - BEINGS OF FREQUENCY, and RADIANT DAY, the latter being on Youtube only. These docs are all about EMF related issues...but if you really want to fix the "root" problem...read a book called QUIET FREEDOM by WC PEACE. The root problem isn't money, emf, or anything else that is talked about, it is how we think about ourselves, other people, and the world around us.

history.review_title: this is what passes for popular in our world today?
history.text: silly movie. If this is what is popular, I'll just look forward to the apocalypse.

history.title: The Great Culling
history.review_title: Amazing comprehensive documentary on harmful effects of fluoride
history.text: Wow. Since 2010 I've mostly drank water that has been through a home reverse osmosis system then remineralized to create high alkaline water. I already knew fluorIDE (Anagram of DIE - like pesticIDE, chlorIDE, homicIDE, infanticIDE, suicIDE, pesticIDE...) was bad, but this documentary puts it all together and then some. I never really thought much about the fluoride that is in the food I eat - now I am. Nor in beverages I drink, though other than water I've mostly cut those out anyway. I've used fluoride free toothpaste for a long time now. Most recently, something called Earthpaste. A documentary called TAPPED you might find interesting. Also PLASTIC PLANET. This documentary reminds me to go upgrade my shower filter, which only does chlorine. I enjoyed the director's testing of bottled water and common drinks. Those fluoride testers are pricey compared to pH and TDS testers. I didn't care for the first 1 minute of the documentary where the director talks about the Georgia 10 Commandment stones, but after that, the documentary captivated me and held my attention. Comprehensive in scope of people interviewed and locations. Phosphate fertilizer mines in Florida was fascinating. The things we don't know. Didn't know much about fluorosis, I do now. Didn't know much about the different sources of fluoride. The title of the documentary would be better if it was just labeled with something more descriptive identifying it with fluoride or something more descriptive, rather then "the great culling" IMHO. On another note, there is a certain irony with the author using closeup shots of his cell phone, for the EMF from cell towers, mobile phones and wi-fi is polluting our air.....but maybe the director will touch on that in the future. You might also enjoy a book titled QUIET FREEDOM, which addresses the root cause of why we are collectively in this situation to begin with, a world where health takes a back seat.

history.review_title: A Bloody Good Sequel With Lots of Dolls Too!
history.text: Playing With Dolls: Bloodlust is the 2nd entry in this series. I’ll have to say, I really liked this one. More characters this time and even more carnage! It’s a very brutal movie and at times had me turning my head. One scene in particular is very hard to watch! The special effects are very gory, just like the others in this series. They don’t hold back at all, that’s for sure. If you enjoyed the first movie, I’d recommend the sequel. For a low budget horror movie, this looks amazing in HD. It’s a very visual looking movie and has some really well done music. My only complaint the rushed ending again, like the first movie. Other than that, a gory good sequel. I don’t think it’s been released here in the USA either on dvd/bluray, just on digital only. I’ve heard the UK dvd is uncut though. The German dvd/bluray releases are of course censored from what I heard.

history.title: Alien: Covenant
history.text: I can see now why Alien:Covenant flopped in theaters. Way too much cgi and it’s awful. I admit it had a few moments, but overall this stunk. So boring and incredibly slow, not enough alien action either. Stick to the original, it's a million times better. Much better special effects too and actually scary. Why they continue to cover up practical effects with cgi is beyond me. Really ruins the movie. None of the characters in this are likeable either. I don’t know what Ridley Scott was thinking. One of the worst sequels I’ve seen this year. A massive disappointment!

Wesley Snipes is back once again! He’s fought blood sucking vampires, now he must save earth from the deadly alien invasion! Not the best alien movie ever, but I enjoyed it for what it was. I would say check it out if you like action/scifi movies. The aliens look great when you finally see them. It’s nothing out of this world, but it’s dumb fun. 3/5

Cookie the elf is back with another horror story for us all. Cookie’s commentary is hilarious in this! He says some of the funniest things during this zombie movie. His comments and jokes about Locked Away had me laughing hard. If you enjoy horror comedy, this is a must see! I look forward to seeing what Cookie has planned next year for us.

history.title: 47 Meters Down
history.text: 47 Meters Down is a pretty boring shark movie. Not much shark action at all. The sharks do look good; the cgi is actually well done. The movie is just not exciting or very thrilling at all. They needed to make the sharks more vicious! This just felt too tame for a killer shark movie. The pop up texting stuff is annoying too! They did the same thing in The Shallows! Stick to Jaws or Deep Blue Sea. 47 Meters Down is not worth diving into. You may like it though, but I'd recommend renting if you must see it!

history.title: Cult of Chucky [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Chucky Is Back For The 7th Round!
history.text: Cult Of Chucky may disappoint longtime Chucky fans. If you’re hoping for a big battle with Andy, you can forget it! Don’t get me wrong, I liked some scenes in Cult. The problem though is not enough Chucky to go around! The 3 Chucky doll sequence was great, but doesn’t last long at all! It's good to see Chucky look the same now too, in the last movie he appeared different throughout the movie. Cult is well shot for a direct to video effort, has a real slick HD look. The music is good, but also some of the same music from Curse again. Yes folks, I notice stuff like that in movies. The cast in this is pretty horrible to be honest; most of the characters are not memorable at all. Nica is probably the only character that keeps this movie going along with Chucky. One character in particular from Curse Of Chucky is only seen for maybe a few seconds…Cult is entertaining, but definitely not the best Chucky movie in the series. The ending will leave fans either very angry or very confused. Just make sure you watch the Unrated cut. 2.5/5

After a very long delay, Leatherface is finally here! This is another prequel, but this time follows the original Texas Chainsaw Massacre & Texas Chainsaw 3D. Leatherface ignores the later sequels as well. This film has nothing to do with the 2003 remake and its prequel either. I know very confusing! This movie does share the same visual dark dirty look though of the remake. Leatherface is definitely a brutal movie and pretty graphic at times. I thought the characters and story were pretty decent. We actually get to see some of the Sawyer family members when they were younger too. The reveal of who becomes Leatherface is really poorly done though. Chainsaw fans will definitely shake their heads when they see the so called twist….It’s definitely an improvement over Texas Chainsaw 3D, but really doesn’t offer much new to the chainsaw franchise. If you’re a long time fan of the series definitely check it out. It’s nothing new, but not a bad addition to the Sawyer family tree. 4/5

history.title: Better Watch Out [Blu-ray & DVD Combo]
history.text: I haven’t seen a decent Christmas Horror movie since Krampus & A Christmas Horror Story. I wasn’t expecting much from Better Watch Out, but I was quite surprised. This movie was not bad, had a nice twist too. It’s basically a Horror version of Home Alone. I’d definitely say check it out, worth a rent. I wouldn’t say it’s the best Christmas Horror movie, but it’s pretty entertaining. Has the same kids from The Visit too. 3/5

history.title: Bunnyman Vengeance
history.text: Yep they made a 3rd Bunnyman movie. This is supposed to be the last one and I’m pretty glad to be honest. This movie is really poorly done. Feels unfinished! The sound is really bad, the effects, the acting, the story is even confusing. If you're going to end a series, do it right! This movie is a rushed mess! I will say one good thing, the haunted house looked great! It’s a shame the rest of the movie is a bunny turd. 1/5 I'd recommend the other 2 Bunnyman movies though, they were actually fun to watch.

history.title: War for the Planet of the Apes [Blu-ray]
history.text: I loved Dawn Of The Planet Of The Apes, but War is just not as fun. The movie is just very slow paced and takes awhile to get some ape action. I wouldn’t really call it War, more like Prison Of The Apes. Some really great computer effects though, definitely the way cgi should look! At times I really thought those were real apes running around. It’s not a bad movie, but definitely not my favorite in the new trilogy. 3/5

history.title: Laggies [DVD + Digital]
