history.title: The Abbott and Costello Show: The Ultimate Collection
history.review_title: You Hear the Laughter, and You May Cry.
history.text: A reviewer on here stated that this show was constant laughs. It may appear that way, because the laugh track is going practically non-stop, and to hear the same track over and over really detracts from it, so you have to put your mind on something else. I just watched the first episode and there are definitely some laughs to be had, and if you can ignore the laugh track there can be a number of laughs in a row, such was the style of A&C. This is a dream come true to me, and wouldn't had known of this show had it not started running on a retro station here recently. The dream of what I saw of A&C, was based on their movies. Their movie comedy was very good in many places, but detracting from it was all the lame singing often by people I never heard of. Nonetheless, when I watch a comedy movie I don't want it turning into a variety show, which is precisely what A&C movies pretty much were. This tv show, to all appearances, was that dream to me, to get A&C comedy without the distractions of baloney singing. Unfortunately the laugh track is almost as bad as the singing was, but at least it supports the material, rather than an abrupt aside. The video on the first episode is very good, if not excellent, considering the age of the show. If all old shows were re-mastered this well, you would be one happy camper. Right now, just based on one episode mind you, the comedy is pretty much your usual A&C. The video is as good as you could expect from old SD. The only drawback is the gross over use of the laugh track and it varies very little. I guess I would give this 4.50 stars if I could, as it's a little better than an 80% satisfaction. I really don't expect it will change much from the first episode, so that it has a big letdown later. Yes, the discs are held on placard holders, which as I predicted, do NOT scratch when being taken out, even if continually used that way, they inevitably will. Edited to reflect new data: I'm into the 4th episode now and am amazed that the pathetic repetitive laugh track on episode one has completely vanished. True, there is more laughter than the material often justifies, but it really isn't any more annoying than any sitcom you know of. I am quite smitten by this comedy. From what I know of future episodes through IMDB, Hillary Brooke is in about half of them. But what is a bit fascinating about this show, is you might call it what it would be like living in the neighborhood of these two comics, as they refer to each other by their actor names, in this case Lou, Abbott, and Hillary. I have seen the same neighborhood cop, along with a few other characters, especially their landlord more than once. I'm not sure I've ever seen a sitcom done like that before. Here is a not-so small excerpt from the show (as I heard it). Lou merrily skips down the street a small bit, and a lady approaches which is dressed similarly to a night dress. Lou says hello, tips his hat, and is fixing to continue on his way when she turns him aside and starts talking to him in an angry manner. Lady: Were you addressing me? Lou: I wasn't addressi.... Lady: Why I don't even know you. You have some nerve. How dare you speak to a single girl you don't even know? A nineteen year old who lives all by herself, at 106 Maple Street, on the second floor, apartment 23, and doesn't even have a steady boyfriend, and loves to go dancing, and is almost every evening all by herself, and whose phone number is Cresent 6 4805. (gives Lou her card) My card! Fresh! (she storms away). edited - Just a little followup comment. A&C get pretty old in the second season, and Hillary Brooke has all but vanished. The only thing I found of much good in the second season was an episode called Amnesia, which may be the best episode overall.

history.title: Cimarron Strip - Complete Series
history.review_title: Three Discs In and It's All Gold
history.text: I have just finished the third disc, and am surprised how good this series is. Dulsey provides eye candy, while Marshall Crown provides quite a bit of being unpredictable. In fact unpredictableness I would say is this series strongest suite thus far. In The Search, for example, the last two minutes there had at least two unpredictable actions, which it's timing is even more a surprise, because most series of any kind are just wrapping things up instead at the end. So far this third disc has provided my two favorites episodes, that being The Search and Whitey. IMO, the video is in pretty good shape, however the series does do some odd things at times, such as having night scenes that are so dark you can't see anything. It does have one of the odd quirks, as well, of having some night scenes where you can easily make out large white clouds in the background. I'm not sure I've seen that anywhere else, but it almost gives sort of a Twilight Zone effect, which of course rarely has a place in westerns. I am not a big fan of westerns, but I do think that it is a series different enough from most westerns, that even a western devotee would find quite a bit to interest them.

history.title: Laurel & Hardy: The Essential Collection
history.review_title: L and H, Captioning, and Foreign Film
history.text: I absolutely love this set, which I bought almost 4 years ago. Just the fact that loading a disc and seeing several scenes playing at once in the disc menu is quite enjoyable, and you get to hear their theme constantly during it. Another massive bit of value of this set, besides the picture greatness. is the availability of captioning! IIRC, there is no true captioning, but the foreign versions of some of the films have sub-text which is done excellently. Hard to believe sometimes when you see a foreign version, which is actually spoken in that language by the boys, just how almost mirror-like the performances are to the original English versions. Normally, I would never think to buy a non-English version of any film, but the boys show that it is possibly to get sub-text equating to getting captioning from films that have never had captioning. I am curious for those who absolutely need captioning, if they had ever thought this sort of thing through like that, that there may be an entire treasure trove of foreign sub-texted material out there? I just lost my Mom Saturday, and I only got into captioning interest because she was completely deaf. Too bad I hadn't figured this out earlier. Heck, hard to believe I had this four years and it is only now that I thought there might be an entire world of English spoken film, made for a foreign audience, then subtexted in English!

history.title: Decoy: The Only Package with ALL 39 Episodes Available!
history.text: I have only seen the first two episodes thus far, but am quite pleased. Two things are apparent. One, the video is in very good shape, and the stories aren't fluff and are in the noir attitude. You may not see a lot of happy endings in this series, but seem true to life. The first episode surprised me right off the bat, as I saw one of my favorite almost unknown actresses in a large role, that being JoAnne Linville, whom played the mini-skirted Romulan in Star Trek TOS. She always seemed a sweet lady, but you see quite a lot of bite out of her in that episode. I think it safe to say that this set is actually under-priced. How many people know of this show though? I had heard the name before, nothing else. Perhaps the best I can think of, of the general spirit of the show is that it is Dragnet type noir, but with a very unique female viewpoint. I would say it has a much heavier female viewpoint than even the Policewoman series with Dickinson. It's a nice bit of fresh air. (edited) Update. I saw much of this series again while doing some screenshots on it, and it's apparent my previous review neglected one thing I would like to emphasize here. Beverly Garland does a very good job with all the things she has to do, and makes her ole as a policewoman entirely believable. But the one thing that really stuck out to me, despite me mentioning before that it's pretty realistic, is the fact that the episodes seem very, very thorough for thirty minutes, and I don't mean compared to shorter modern shows. I mean compared to any television you have seen. It's really hard to believe how much tension there is to this show. You feel like you've just seen a tense 45 or 60 minute show. I don't think I have ever seen ANY show that just has so much substance to it in a mere 30 minutes.

history.title: The Avengers - Complete Series 3 [DVD]
history.text: I have seen only the first episode thus far. I have a refurbished region-free Blu-ray player, so what problems I describe, while particular to this disc, also aren't exactly unheard of from this player. I also have a BD player on the computer, but I'll lay off of that for a while. IMO, this set looks visually better than I expected. The closeups are as good as any from the season 4 dvd set, but I noticed that that is the case where the focus for the camera is. Where the focus is not, the blur is more noticeable, if for no other reason than you're just not that used to that sort of background blur (sometimes in the foreground, should the focus be elsewhere). I would also say the shadows seem to be more noticeable as well, but I suppose that is common to old live productions. I also had a problem where the player completely froze up and I had to bounce it. There is also a tendency for there to be a thin white horizontal line of pixels, at lightning speed, at times. I was expecting this dvd set to be at a level 3 satisfaction level, and instead it's a 4. Naturally if every episode freezes on me at some point, this will drop it another point at least. I must say that thus far the picture quality is making up for the lightning and freezing, anticipating that the freezeups will cease. Assuming freezeups are few, I am likely to buy the season 2 set as well. A word of slight caution. While there is acting, there is NO music, and this can seem odd at times. As well, I'm pretty sure there will be little if any convincing fight scenes, not that it was ever a staple of the Avengers, but in live action it will be even more noticeable. (edited for additional info) I have just now finished episode 2 now, and I have found some of my observations were perhaps incorrect on the first episode. First of all, there is music, but it's mainly when nobody is talking and during scene change, though there are at least a couple of exceptions to that in episode 2. I'm not sure if episode 2 was that distinctively different with the music, or more likely that it was there all along, it's just that it's markedly less than what latter seasons of the recorded venue presented. Watching live does take a little getting used to. In episode 2, up to the 40th minute, the lightning pixels did not reappear in their thin horizontal line across the screen, but after that time, there were a number of them, though they seemed weaker. There were no freezing whatsoever, gladly. So, at this stage, my overall assessment hasn't changed, and it continues the 4 rating it seems to deserve. If the series continues with the lightning streaks, I'll just consider that part of the old film, as it's not so consistent to be too terribly annoying. Freezing, however, I simply won't tolerate without shooting this rating ever downwards. Should it continue with the lightning at the rate it has show, plus no further freezing, I will consider this to remain a 4 rating and my interest in buying season 2 will remain. I have never bought a live action show before, but from what I've seen of stills of this show, plus the occasional youtube clip, I would have expected a considerably worse picture than what you're getting here. One additional comment on the show itself, though after just two episodes. Their is a distinct lack of comradeship, or playfulness if you will, between Gale and Steed, unlike what came so easily for Peel and King, with Steed. Perhaps it's just a bad combination of episodes to show such a trait, but as I treasured the interaction between the two latter girls with Steed in the series, Gale seems to be much more serious with Steed and I'm guessing this was by design for their original girl Gale. This does affect the humor, subtle though it may had been later, quite a bit. In episode 2, Gale kicked Steed as sort of a friendship tap, and it then occurred to me that it may had been the only playfulness I had seen so far. (edited) I am deeper into the season now, and everything seems to get better a bit, but I have added this to make this comment. On the episode called Number Five, around the 10 to 11th minute, there is a poster on a wall which you can't miss. Being a big Linda Thorson fan of the series, it immediately makes you think the girl on the poster is her. The resemblance, which I assume isn't her, is quite close, as this lady has a bob haircut and very similar face. I presume Linda must has been around sixteen years old at the time. Is it possible she was doing modeling at that age?

history.title: Lost in Space: The Complete Series [Blu-ray]
history.text: This is better than the BD job I seen dome on Star Trek TOS. It's also nice to hear the whole living crew (absent June Lockhart) in commentary. Too bad, like the old Dr Who series, they didn't offer commentary for every episode. Now the main reason I write. I only got into interest in captioning, because my mother was totally deaf and depended on captioning or subtitles to enjoy her video watching. Mom died over four months ago, but CC still has interest for me, and it really should for a lot of us, even if we think we'll never go deaf and don't care about those that do. The selfish reason one should consider CC (or subtitles) in a product is because it can be used at times to clear up dialogue you cannot hear, even if your hearing is excellent, or dialogue that is drowned in other sounds on the video. I will say, that fairly often CC and subtitles are pretty poor or completely wrong, so commenting on CC type media can be quite important to some. So I will mention here that after perusing an episode using the subtitles, it really is excellent, though I did see one mistake. It is excellent because it often will put the name of the speaker on the line given, should the speaker be off camera. It also will jump the text around, to often show directly who is doing the speaking of the lines. It's not limited to two lines at a time, and it isn't limited to the bottom of the screen. Having seen a lot of CC material in my life with Mom, it's interesting to see the text, because though it usually will slide underneath whom is currently speaking, it will at times go to their chest or face, which in comparison to the usual method of CC, is almost hypnotic; sort of like following a ball at a tennis match. It's not as maddening as following a tennis ball, but it is almost entertaining, as though it's alive. The one mistake I saw for the 3-4 minutes I watched it with subtitles, is it at one point went to Major West's face when Robinson was actually speaking, but otherwise it was flawless and it didn't misspell or even leave one word out. When it showed the robot say WARNING 8 times, that's precisely how many times he said it; quite excellent. It also has the habit of showing an entire sentence at a time, all at once, which to me makes it easier to read. It also seems to only disappear when the next sound occurs, although it doesn't display forever if there is silence. LIS can be pretty fast paced dialogue at times, but at least there's always the rewind and then pause to pick up the missed bits. Don't think that there aren't foreign films you wouldn't want CC or subtitles for. I have found them fairly indispensable when watching british shows on disc. Incidentally, each season has a different menu to go through, and season three may be the best one. I think the BD treatment of S3 may be the best too, unless it's all the same and I'm just imagining it.

history.title: CHiPs: The Complete Sixth and Final Season
history.text: This is a steaming pile. Not only are the two main stars constantly posing like a couple of girly men, but it's just awful all the way around. See these two idiots in close formation on their cycles, going down a freeway. Also see how they seem to be in slow motion and nobody is passing them. No, that's incorrect. They aren't in slow motion, they are literally driving 20MPH down the highway, and you figure this out by two things: 1) they aren't talking in slow motion. 2) The traffic in the background, like those crossing bridges at street speed, is going faster than they are. What makes that worse? Every single episode thus far involves at least one scene, usually more, where at least one car flips up into the air and falls on it's side (obviously running cars up off-camera ramps). So they show you a ridiculous amount of vehicular violence (cars don't go flying over each other IRL), and then the cops drive 20 MPH on a freeway! I can't imagine the earlier seasons could had been any worse. The music is terrible, but the audio/video of the show is pretty good. Any Adam-12 season is ten times better than this schlock!

history.title: Hazel: The Complete Final Season
history.review_title: Better Than I Thought It Would Be
history.text: The season starts off with almost every episode mentioning the missing parents in passing. It's painful enough that two of the three big stars on the show are gone, and the replacements seem wooden a lot of times, but that's mostly because I wasn't used to them much. However, once the season got some steam behind it, I didn't find them all that much worse. Why? Because while the battles were going on between the three main stars in previous seasons, this season took a much more cooperative feel to everybody involved. And while it wasn't a good sitcom in the final season compared to other sitcoms, somehow it worked quite well within the Hazel universe, almost a breath of fresh air. I never would have believed it, and I always hated this season previously, because I was all so turned off against the new Baxters and the old crew given the air, so naturally I just saw it in clips and didn't really invest in it like buying it on dvd can do. If you hated it like me, and therefore hardly watched it, I think you'll be surprised that it's quite a bit better than you always thought. I would put it as a pretty close match to the other seasons for just the enjoyment aspect. It's different from before, but compared to all the years of skullduggery on previous years, it is quite nice. It does have the convenience of color too. Finally, I would imagine that the early years were more true to the Hazel comic strip, so from that aspect this may seem almost an abomination, but the change in tone does show you what it could be like without all the fussing going on, sans the early Baxters.

history.title: The Donna Reed Show:Season 3
history.review_title: Is MPI Digitally Remastering Of Any Use?
history.text: Let me say from the start that I do not own this set. I do, however, own sets 4 and 5 which MPI made. There seems to be a general consensus among commentators here, that the "digitally remastered" sets 1-3 are a reason to double dip and buy all over again. I almost got suckered into double-dipping for that reason. MPI claims they remastered, Virgil did not. So I got out my set 3, a Virgil product and compared it to my MPI set 4. There is no difference in the picture quality I can tell, as both are quite good. Ironically enough on the first freeze frame I did to better compare, on the MPI I had come across a very large blotch of black, which ought to tell you if MPI digitally REMASTERED set 4, they did a quite lousy job, and in fact I would take the Virgil even without that, for a very slight edge, if any.

history.title: Paul Blart: Mall Cop 2
history.text: 2.5/5 stars. This Paul Blart has about 25% of the laughs (if that) of the original. One of the worst things about the movie is that two of the main characters are out of the movie right away (his mom and Amy) and Amy divorcing him just basically undoes everything that he worked to get in the first movie. No spoilers because it happens right in the beginning of the movie. I get that he's a geeky guy that things don't go well for, but couldn't they have written her out of the script in another way, like having her on a business trip or something? Now for the rest of the movie. Most of the jokes fall flat. Paul doesn't give any "fun facts" for anyone which was pretty funny for the first movie. He again shows off his segue skills, and there is a heist or attempted heist going on. You might recognize the main villain from Band of Brothers. Probably the funniest part of the movie was when Paul gets in the fight with the peacock and the piano player just keeps playing. The main fight scene between paul and the security guards and the henchmen is also entertaining if not flat out unbelievable. Let's hope there's not a Paul Blart 3, but I'm sure it made enough on the box office for there to be one. One last thought, the commercialization of this movie was much more obvious than in the first Blart. You could easily count at least 5 items that are blatantly advertised. Sort of reminds me of Minority Report except without the quality movie attached.

Good, compelling movie. I thought it was a pretty interesting story and I happen to be a chess player as well so that didn't hurt. I didn't realize just how crazy Bobby Fischer really was. He was an amazing chess player and won a world championship when America sorely needed a victory. Recommended.

history.review_title: Disappointing but at least Todd Packer's in it
history.text: Very disappointing movie. Started off semi-promising, in the vane of Trick 'r Treat (also by same director), although instead of good special effects and some genuine scares, this uses cheap practical effects and has virtually no real scares. It was a $1.50 rental from redbox, good thing we didn't pay more or (God forbid) see this one at the theater. This is kind of like a poor man's Gremlins. I own both Gremlins 1 and 2 and they are a couple of my favorite movies. This is like Gremlins, but without the heart, entertainment factor, or scares. The only reason I gave it 2 stars instead of 1 was because the grandma was funny, and they had a lot of nice Christmas decorations. And Todd Packer from the office (bald guy) is in it and gives it some life. Overall disappointing and only watch if you can for free and there's nothing better on.

history.title: La La Land [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD]
history.review_title: Fantastic fun, catchy music, memorable and worth owning
history.text: My wife and I saw this at the theater on New Year's Eve last year. What a spectacular movie. While not perfect (Gosling's vocals leave something to be desired), it's such a fun movie with very catchy music that I still find myself listening to the soundtrack. This movie hits all the right notes. It takes place in LA and since I love visiting California it makes it that much better. We visited Los Angeles this year and had a wonderful time. We got a chance to visit the Warner Bros lot for a tour (WELL worth it if you're in the area!) and they had a mock La La Land coffee shop where we had a photo op (see picture). In the movie, Ryan Gosling goes to visit Emma Stone, who works at the WB Lot coffee shop. They showed us on the tour where they were walking when they filmed that scene between two soundstages. Other aspects of the movie include J.K. Simmons as the restaurant owner who fires Ryan Gosling in his trademark style (think Whiplash but not as intense). Emma and Ryan have a fantastic on-screen chemistry and are funny as well as heartfelt and of course the music is great. Gosling's vocals are not as good as Stone's but I can forgive that given how much I enjoy this movie. Some may not like the ending but it is what it is and is a memorable 7 minutes. I bought this in 4K Blu-ray even though I don't have a 4K TV yet because it included the regular blu-ray as well. The soundtrack sounds great on my system, and video is high quality. I would highly recommend this but rent it first as it's a polarizing movie!

history.title: The Walking Dead: Season 3
history.text: Ordinary people having to deal with extraordinary situations. This is the stuff of great entertainment. Series like Jericho, Invasion, Falling Skies. Overcoming adversity. Bringing out the best in people, at least most of the time. And the worst in others. These are the villains. In The Walking Dead, it is not the zombies who are the bad guys. It is certain members of the human race. Of course this has been historically accurate in our history. The brilliant writers of The Walking Dead capture this extremely well in season one. Also Rick, Jim and Dale desperately trying to cling to doing the right thing in situations that defy our moral experience. Yes there is brutality everywhere, but for the most part the characters hold on to valuing life. Fragile as it is. There is plenty of action and excitement. And gore for those who want it. Ultimately this is a drama based on the inner journey of the characters more than the external journey looking for safety. In season two there is more friction between the characters. And the gradual awakening of characters like Herschel to the reality of their situation. All very inspiring. By season three, all of the characters are becoming increasingly flawed. And there is a growing callousness among all of them. Probably very true to life. The violence and gore also become more gratuitous. However to truly be entertaining and for all of the cliffhangers to work, you have to care about the characters. And for this they need to have some redeeming qualities. By season three the writers had diminished our heroes to being only slightly better than mass murdering, sociopathic villains that they are pitted against. Surely to keep watching this is to put oneself at risk of becoming overexposed to brutality and being entertained by people with no conscience. I found myself being inspired often in season one. Somewhat less in season two. By season three it was just depressing. Difficult to care anymore to what happens to the characters. Season 1 was like the movie The Edge, triumphing over adversity. Season 3 is more like The Grey. Probably more realistic but hard to get emotionally invested in the characters. BUT...if you can get through season three, season four is the best! So hang in there, despite the low's of season three, there is inspiring stuff to come.

history.title: Alias Smith & Jones: Special Edition [Import USA Zone 1]
history.text: Some of the TV shows from the '60s and '70s don't stand the test of time. This show comes across fresh and not dated. Our two lovable rogues are trying to earn amnesty by "going straight for a year." This proves quite challenging and many interesting predicaments occur. Most of the scripts are inventive and fun. More light hearted than the "Butch Cassidy and The Sundance Kid" movie, which inspired the series. There's a fair bit of action but the violence is toned down. The best part of the show is the on screen chemistry between the two stars, Pete Duel and Ben Murphy (though off the set they were not close friends). I took off one star because.. A. The picture quality is decent, but not great. Certainly better than VHS. B. There are no chapters or scene selections per episode. Feels like it was knocked out quickly and cheaply. C. There are no commentaries or extras apart from a disc in an envelope inserted in the box which is a short series of reminiscences by Ben Murphy and Roger Davis sitting together and chatting. Davis had known Pete Duel for longer, was closer to him and actually narrates the opening of the show. He appeared in one episode as a sort of hybrid of the two characters. After the untimely death of Pete Duel, he was hurriedly made the replacement. However, the show never was quite the same and finished at the end of that year. Not much is said about Pete Duel, a very talented but troubled young actor who apparently shot himself due to depression. More about this including interviews with Murphy and Davis when younger, along with family and crew members is available on YouTube by searching for "Pete Duel documentary." EMysteries, have a nice 21 minute documentary. Too bad this was not included and the other deficits addressed. Then it would have truly been a Collectors Version. Nevertheless all the episodes are here and are very enjoyable.

history.title: Hawaii Five-O: Season 3
history.review_title: The show hits its stride in season 3
history.text: Season 3 of this fictitious police dept, Hawaii 5-O (so named because Hawaii is the 50th State) is probably the best of its 12 seasons....the longest running cop show. Jack Lord really inhabits his part and you can see his real life warmth towards the people and places of the island coming through. The episodes come up fresh, with up-and-coming talent making guest appearances. No real violence, but the pace and action move along with good plot twists. We often know more than the police and it's fun to see them unravel the clues to catch up with the audience. Lots of great locations. FYI, after his death, Jack Lord's estate of $40 million went to Hawaiian charities. Good on you Jack.

history.title: Red Sun
history.text: Until recently, this was selling for hundreds of dollars!! This version is a knock off from overseas, but plays great. The appeal is the unusual cast combo...Charles Bronson, Toshiro Mifuno, Ursulla Andress and two french actors...Alain Delon and Capucine. The last two have very small roles and their considerable talents are wasted here. Mifuno steals every scene. Andress also has a small role which adds little other than sex appeal. Bronson is miscast. He does great in brooding, laconic roles like "Chato's Land' and Once Upon a time in the west." This part is more of a likeable rogue with charm. Burt Reynolds would have been so much better. The plot premise is sound, but the script is mediocre and despite the talents of director (Terence Young-who did Several of the Sean Connery 'Bond' films) the film is rather forgettable, except for the final 5 min action scene. The great Maurice Jarre film composer (Dr Zhivago, etc) fails to capture the mood correctly, despite a laudible attempt to combine western and oriental themes. The somewhat Disney-type theme is just an annoying distraction. Altogether, quite misseable, I'm afraid.

history.title: Ant-Man (1-Disc DVD)
history.text: Although not a fan of the ant man character, the movie received enough positive reviews that I decided to take a chance on this. From start to finish, the movie is an extremely fun ride. The whole cast is excellent. And the script is just enough tongue in cheek to set it aside from most superhero films. As with the dark Knight, civil war and the wonder woman movie, this one stands out because it is simply a good movie. Lots if likeable characters, simple plot that works. Very clever writing. Special effects are fine. But it is the character writing that pulls you in. It just happens to also be a superhero film. Just a word about the seller. The movie arrived three days early, and in perfect condition. Many thanks to BuybacksMansfield.

history.title: Batman
history.review_title: Great movie. Influential. See photos though.
history.text: This is the movie that influenced all the Batman iterations since. Michael Keaton's performance as Batman has many subtle aspects that actors in other Batman movies have not been able to replicate. Director Tim Burton alternated from shooting Batman with the eyes in shadow, then lit so the eyes really jump out with intensity. This version of Bruce Wayne made the most sense. A troubled soul who cannot connect with people since his life was traumatically derailed. You feel much more sympathy with this Bruce Wayne than any other. Nicholson plays Jack Napier with the controlled energy of a cat, converted into a demented dragon after his "accident...." But did Batman drop him in the nuclear waste vat by accident, or was there a moment of recognition. Many interesting nuances and hidden meanings in the performances and the script. Very strong support from Jack Palance, Pat Hingle and especially Michael Gough, who really set the standard for an unflappable, devoted Alfred....insightful enough to reveal Batman's identity to the right person. Also the most stylish Batmobile. Not just a Frank Miller tank. Love the "shield." The ONLY unfortunate part was the seller, jim-s-08, advertised this DVD as in "Like new" condition. I've tried to capture a few of the MANY scuffs and scratches on the case and the disc with my phone camera. The movie played alright, but it should have been advertised as "Good" condition.

history.title: Pilates Complete for Inflexible People
history.text: I bought this DVD because of the great reviews, and now as I reread them, I'm trying to figure out what they thought was so great about it. The instructor who demonstrates the Pilates is solemn and wooden, as is the woman who does the voice over. "Pilates Complete for Inflexible People" doesn't seem to have one thing, specifically, to do with inflexibility. I'm 61, active, and in great shape (size 6 jeans), but I'm getting some stiffness in my calves and thighs, as well as my shoulders, so I was really eager to get this one, but when I tried the very first set, I was already wondering what this had to do with specialized moves for inflexibility because they're some the very same moves I was doing at the fitness center where I exercised with people from 18 to 80, only much more repetitive, and full of incorrect transitions that could actually do harm if you follow them through. Always the optimist, I thought, "Well, there's a lot more to this DVD than that little bit." So, I began opening other segments, and they're all the same moves. I do know that there are hundreds of Pilate moves and positions, but this instructor seems to have gotten hold of 3 or 4 moves and made a career on them. They seemed more aimed at my stomach muscles than areas of inflexibility. I wanted a routine that would stretch and limber up my whole body,one that might be a little challenging in the beginning but that I could work up to, but that's not what I've got, and the whole setting with its dark, forboding background would have been depressing if I'd stuck with it much longer. There is nothing challenging, helpful, or inspiring about this DVD, and I would return it, but I got it here at Amazon.com when it was $9.99 w/ free shipping (I luv Amazon.com), and it would cost almost that much to return. Other exercise DVDs that I have and would recommend are "Ageless Mobility"; "The Anti-Aging Method"; and Louise Solomon's "Yoga & Pilates". I'll keep looking for more; I've decided I enjoy working out in the privacy of my own home, rather than going to the fitness center for classes, and I want a library of at least half a dozen DVDs to alternate.

history.title: AGELESS MOBILITY: Pain-Free Wellness For Longevity
history.text: The format of this DVD is unassuming and very easy to follow, but it's also challenging. Along the way, Scott recognizes that some people will be able to take the moves further than others, but he advises you to stop when the pain level is at 3 because some pain is necessary and causes the muscles and joints to flood with much needed moisture. (The pain-Free part comes after the muscles and joints are in good working order.) After 2 workouts (a few days apart) I already felt strength and fluidity in my movements that wasn't there before. This is what I was looking for. I'm 61, in good shape, but have some stiffness that I'm determined to deal with; I don't believe that getting older means we should just sit down in a recliner and give up. From the cover, I expected to be viewing a class of several people, but it's just Scott in a big empty room, which isn't a problem; I like his quiet, assured manner. As I progress, I expect to use this DVD several days a week, but for now, I need a few days in between to let the soreness work out. I don't vegetate during those days; I'm using other workout DVDs and Wii Fit. Yes, I would recommend this DVD for anyone looking to stay or get in shape. I've learned some things about how my muscles work together, about where my stiffness originates, and about pushing myself, just enough, feel better later.

history.title: The Girl Who Kicked The Hornet's Nest (English Dubbed)
history.text: I gave the other two movies in this trilogy 5 stars. This one, for me, was painfully plodding, and I'm sure I missed out on some of the interwoven politics, but it's the necessary denouement. I must admit to fast forwarding through a few scenes of this one, but I'm so glad to have seen all 3. While I knew where it was headed (unlike the first two), and at times I was thinking, "C'mon, already, and just do it!" this is the one that ties up all the loose ends. A definite must see.

There's not much on TV for me these days, and I didn't begin watching this series on TV. I didn't even know about it, but I was looking on Amazon for a series with which to fill my winter hours and decided to give this one a try, not feeling very hopeful that it would capture my interest. But it did immediately. It has something so much of today's programming misses, it immediately drew me in with well-rounded characters whose lives I care about, and it's intelligent viewing. That's it, simple enough ingredients sadly lacking in all the flash, bang, whiz, boom filling up our hundreds of TV channels. I'm well into the fourth season now. Seasons 2 & 3 are my favorites, but the first season sets up all the premises for future episodes. Season four seems to lose focus now and then, but once I got that far, I wasn't stopping because I cared about what happened to the characters and their unlikely worlds. If the series were to be picked up and resumed, I would have my DVR set so I wouldn't miss another episode. Thanks, Amazon.com, for making it possible for me to enjoy this unique series.

I'm a Jake Gyllenhaal fan, but I'm not a fan of this movie. I was also a literature and psychology major, so deep, elusive symbolism excites me.... this tale offers nothing but dark, uninteresting, disjointed segments with a few oddball, meaningless "symbols" thrown in to keep us thinking we're onto something if we just stay with it long enough. Not. I had to pause it about halfway through to make dinner, and afterwards realized I didn't care enough about how it came out to resume. There are just too many flaws in the plot to entice me to go along with it. I kept thinking that if I discovered someone who was my exact double, I'd be freaking out but in a good way, and I'd be telling family and friends, but these guys immediately panic and go all covert and secretive as if disaster has befallen them.......Why? Jake couldn't do much beyond the script he was given.

When he's good, he's very good, and when he's bad.......not so much. There are a few of his movies like Bad Santa that I could not, would not watch, just silly and profane. This time Billy Bob is excellent! The writing is fun, the characters are fully developed, and he is just so masterful in his role. I hope there are many more seasons of Goliath.

I saw the blurb, read Collin Farrell, but my mind said Collin Firth, and I thought anything he does is good. Even when I realized my mistake, I watched about half the movie, thinking it would surely turn into something watchable. It didn't. I used to teach/counsel in public school, and the whole way I kept thinking that if my third graders had a brain storming session, this is what they would co-write as a novel. Not one of the characters is likeable, so at some point you'll realize you don't care how it ends. It's offered as edgy, though provoking, and one review said you'll be talking about the holes in it long after the final credits roll. There's nothing to discuss. It's a movie which simply didn't happen.

history.title: Peter, Paul and Mary - Carry It On - A Musical Legacy
history.text: for ANY PETER,PAUL& MARY fan!!! There are lots of clips from their earlier years 1961-1970, and clips from 1978-2004.....keep in mind..I'm sure you know by now that Mary Travers left this world in 2009,and so there are no clips that go all the way upto now, if you want that you will have to wait until Noel, and Peter come out with something. They are still singing together afterall. Um....THIS documentary here includes a 2003/4 rendition of their very first song ever sung together as a trio....Mary had A Little Lamb in 1961. I wish however, that there was actual footage of them singing that song THEN, and lots more clips from their early years as that is when they were such a smash success. When I see clips from their shows, like at the March On Washoington 1963, and 1969,and on Jonathan Winters in 1969 and I see the floweredress Mary's wearing, I'm reminded of the flower children, I wasn't born until 1967, so that was a generation or two before my time!! But if you take an interest in the Sixties, and politics, social, political activism, oh yeah and folk music too, this is a great beginners start. It's also good if you're older and want to take a stroll down memory lane. But PP&M were always a current folk group, who didn't want to be labeled as a "nostalgia act," in the early 2000's they came out with a tear-jerker called "Jesus Is On The Wire," which I'm surmising is not only about homosexuals and the need to respect their rights to live their lives the same as do straight people, I also think the title is suggestive of the horrendous murder of Mathew Shepherd was beaten to a bloody pulp, hung on a barbed wire fence, and left to die...when asked why they did that to him , they said it was because he was gay. I think it's wonderful that PP&M, straight as they are, rose to the occasion in this very sad but important song. Last but not least, I enjoy clip from Peter Paul& Mommy Too, a heart warming footage of Mary with her grand daughter, Wyllie on her lap looking up at her, in the rocking chair quietly, and proud as ever listening while proud Grandma Mary Travers sang For Baby For Bobby. Just for her. The light just sparkles in Wyllie's brown eyes...you can tell she is in absolute heaven!! She adores her grandma!! And Noel is his wacky old self on The Old Lady Who Swallowed A Fly. He gets all the kids excited, and laughing histerically as always. Anyhow, I hope you consider this product,I've been a serious PP&M fan since 1984 and so I ought to know a good PP&M documentary when I see one.....THIS HAS OODLES AND OODLES OF COMMENTARY BY MANY PEOPLE including Pete Seeger, Phil Ramone,Tom Paxton, Ronnie Gilbert (of The Weavers.) Bob DeCormier (their director), as well as by PP&M THEMSELVES. And that makes this very good indeed. Trust me.

history.title: Saint Joan of Arc
history.review_title: Not Great But Adequate For A Joan of Arc Beginner.
history.text: If you're looking for something that shows all the places Joan of Arc lived and traveled viewing this video will probably NOT be up your alley. This video is done by Bob and Penny Lord, a couple who are known to thousands who watch them on Mother Angelica's network EWTN, do usually film their pilgrimmages to put them to DVD, which is why I bought this. It is NOT a live pilgrimmiage, and though you do see Rouen where she was burned, you don't see much of anything else. This is more for those who have either never heard of her, or do not know much about her life. If you are one of these and visiting Joan's home and homeland, from your your livingroom doesn't matter, than this should be up your alley.

history.title: Dr. Quinn Medicine Woman: The Complete Series
history.review_title: For All Us Dr. Quin Fans These Are Wonderful
history.text: I just love these dvds because the quality of mine are very good, they don't have any scratches, and they play very nicely on any dvd player. I watched this show from beginning to end back in the 1990's and I think Jane Seymour was well cast, as was Joe Lando (Sully), the kids, the towns folk....everyone!! Oh, yes we can't forget Cloud Dancing (Larry Sellers). My only complaint is that there is absolutely NO EPISODE GUIDE anywhere with this set.....it's not even writtten on the insides of these seasons! An episode guide for a set like this is necessary to find the episodes you are looking for, because they usually contain television log lines that tell you about each episode. So I am taking two stars off for that.....shame on you A&E channel! A&E? You tried to appease us by adding a list of Episodes in the cover of the First Season....that is not enough!!! You mearly, copied what is already written on the backs of each season in this set. That's another reason this product is getting only three stars. I liked the price of this set, it used to be much higher, but this price resembles the product a lot more....a good deal considerring there are six seasons plus two movies, and a few good extras. Like the A&E Biography on Jane Seymour, interactive menues, and tidbits about the real Colorado Springs in the 1860's. I wish there were interviews with Joe Lando and Jane Seymour....instead they have voice over commentaries on favorite episodes.....Joe was absolutely gorgeous!! This series teaches youngsters high moral values in my opinion. It doesn't have eveything I want in it, but I am still enjoying myself when I watch these. And I hope you do too.

history.title: Touched By An Angel: The Ninth and Final Season
history.review_title: Season Nine is both wonderful and dissapointing
history.text: Today,I received my first copy of the Touched By An Angel Season 9 dads. It's such a wonderful show I gave it four stars, but I've waited for so many years, and there are absolutely no extras.....you'd think they would include at least one or two interviews of cast and crew that are not on the first season. (I have that already.) I mean they made us wait for ten years, and probably would never have got these released had it not been for the millions of loyal fans bugging them. Still I am a big fan of the show. I love Roma Downey, I think what she's doing with the new theatrical movie,Son of God, is wonderful. I wish her and the whole cast of Touched By An Angel (minus John Dye, who died in 2011) well and lots of love and blessings in the future.

history.title: Waltons: Season 4
history.review_title: My Little Rant About These DVDs
history.text: I remember the nights I sat glued to the tv, watching The Waltons, sitting on my mom's or dad's lap, or discussing an episode, at school.....I remember The Walton's Doll House my Grandparents gave me, or favorite Waltons show.......I just wish these Season Four DVDs, had been packaged so I could flip through each one until I get to the disc I want, INSTEAD, they are all crammed together in one round space with the button in the middle, if I want to get to the LAST DISC, I have to take them ALL out, why can't they let us go straight to the disc we want? I give The Waltons a high rating because there aren't many shows like that anymore, I take off ONE star for the packaging!

history.text: I was a young adult when this series first aired, I liked it then, and I still like it now, I watch it on Nick At Night, everyday, Yes I know, this show has been dubbed, "this generation's Brady Bunch," because it's so light hearted......but it sure is better than what the network's have to offer, I.e. I never ONCE saw D.J. and Steve getting it on in Danny's living room, when we watch these we are not treated to dead bodies with heads cracked open laying in a pool of blood, on the sidewalk! history.title: The Mothership Connection Live 1976
history.review_title: Only took 40 years for me to see what I've always imagined ...
history.text: Wow! I don't know what to say... I didn't know this existed. It's everything I imagined was going on (and more) when I was a kid in the 70's listening (in particular) to Mothership Connection, Dr. Funkenstein and Motor Booty Affair, just how I pictured the live show, but it took 40 years for this "youth" to actually see it. If you are a fan of that period or this band, you will not be disappointed. Yes the sound is very good and the video is somewhat limited by a "network TV" look, but not distracting or too dark for me. Blu-ray probably wouldn't have made much difference, the DVD is great quality and there's a nice 3-page synopsis inside the case. "You won't believe how they party"!: There are a lot of people on stage - all amazing, apparently even some of Sly and TFS and Bootsy's Rubber Band members joined them for this and future shows on this tour (Sly bowed out after a couple more dates.). Everyone sings. And well. Everyone. I didn't know Mr. Clinton used three very gifted guitarists on this tour, including one who is also my favorite band vocalist Glenn Goins - hard to believe he was only 22 years old here and would pass away just two short years later of Hodgkin's lymphoma. Sad, but I am grateful to have this audible and visual memory of him and the whole P-Funk 1976 experience.

history.title: The Drop (Blu-ray)
history.text: Love this movie... It 's not a gangster movie but deals with criminal elements in an East Coast town, very realistic and believable. If you haven't seen Tom Hardy lately other than in the current Mad Max movie, this and The Revenant are good ones to see.. his range is amazing. All great actors - James Gandolfini, Nooni Rapace (from The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo) and the entire cast. Twists and suspense til the end, I showed this to my parents and they both loved it. Rated R for some language and violence, but nothing extreme. Bargain price and a Digital HD copy, too!

history.review_title: Highly recommend all Jeff Nichols movies...
history.text: I have seen 4 of the 5 movies that Jeff Nichols has written and directed, I would highly recommend seeing them all. He is becoming my favorite modern director/writer, a great storyteller in the mode of Spielberg. "Shotgun Stories" is more Indie than the others, but he still creates amazing characters and a great story with minimal resources. It is slow paced and brilliant. "Mud" is probably his most well known, Michael Shannon has been in them all, looking forward to "Loving" that comes out this November.
Brilliant! "An aggressive mouse", "They're starving for hot fudge?" ... I'm rolling off the couch with each episode. A great companion to his movies. Thank you Woody and Amazon.

history.title: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
history.text: No question this outing in the franchise is worthy of all the praise heaped upon it in these posts, and I agree with most so I will only comment here on something technical that was very annoying. I took this BR disc to more than one player and display thinking that the problem might be my system, but no, it followed the disc. I found that the convergence of the subtitles was way off; my eyes/brain couldn't converge them properly and it was so bad that I wound up having to close one eye when the subtitles appeared so I could read them. I had no problem with the 3D with the movie itself, just the subtitles. In fact, the 3D depth was so realistic that at one scene I remember saying outloud to the others in the room, "Damn, THIS is why I love 3D!" Subtitles are a separate file on BluRay so it could just be that they were not authored correctly, I don't know, but it does get minus marks in the technical department for this glitch. I have no idea if this was just a bad disc that I got or if anyone else has experienced the anomoly. Let me know if you have. That said, it was a small negative that barely impacted the great affection I have for everything about this film -- (oops, not "film;" digital).

history.title: The Martian [Blu-ray 3D + Blu-ray + Digital HD] [3D Blu-ray]
history.text: Matt Damon meets MacGyver -- or how to survive by hook or crook. Much less science fiction than it is a page out of Science Mechanic. The fact is, this could have taken place in the middle of the Mojave desert or the Sahara and it would have been just as entertaining, only difference there being that in either of those places, a helicopter and a rescue team would have come by in the first 20 minutes and plucked our hero out in a simple rescue -- end of the movie. On Mars, it's a bit more complicated, and everything wouldn't have had that omnipresent red tinge over-cast to it. Sure, we are routing for our hero because he's got a great sense of humor and that unstoppable American pluck, but in the end, his survival pretty much depends on luck, which he seems to have a carload full -- some of which REALLY stretches credulity. The 3D has plenty of depth and adds that sense of involvement that I happen to enjoy big-time but which always seems to be a matter of subjective taste...some love it, some find 3D adds little. I saw it in the RealD 3D format and found that so dull and lifeless as to be a constant distraction -- my brain saying, "Hey...someone turn on a few more lights!!" I can understand how watching THAT kind of poor 3D would put anyone off the 3D version, but then I want back with friends to see it in IMAX when they added for a week after THE WALK was pulled. IMAX uses dual digital projectors to double the light on the screen and there it was a totally different film -- the 3D was spectacular; it was bright and immerse -- a totally different, MUCH better experience (an IMAX experience if you want to use their marketing jargon). All I can say is, IMAX does it 3D right and the RealD 3D presentation is a much more inferior version. Here's hoping the 3D Blu-ray will be much closer to the IMAX 3D version.

history.review_title: There are MUCH better Dracula movie versions...pick any one OTHER than this one.
history.text: So let's see...as if Amazon charging 3 bucks for a nearly 25yr old movie is not enough, insult is added to injury when your are roped into this mishmash of film by the big name actors and of course the uber-well-respected Francis Ford Coppola's name. But that is where your being impressed in any way about this film will abruptly end -- that and possibly the superb cinematography, but there is not much else. Pretty (or pretty gruesome) photography on its own can't hold a movie together, and this one starts falling apart amazingly fast. Of most terrible note -- Anthony Hopkins' bizarre interpretation of the Van Helsing character; it is just so incongruous and out of place with the entire tone and Gothic feel of the rest of the movie. Well, wait, I take that back -- when did you ever see a Texan with a Texas drawl wearing a 10-gallon hat and touting a shotgun in ANY of the many Dracula incarnations up to now? Well, one is thrown in this version for no apparent reason whatsoever. What relationship any of this has to Van Helsing in poor Bram Stoker's novel is beyond comprehension. On top of that, Hopkins doesn't seem to know what accent he is trying to master -- sometimes it's British, sometimes it has a German twang, sometimes maybe Ygoslavian?? ("Yah") and worse, if he is supposed to be playing the very serious Van Helsing, that vampire expert and killer, and a man who has the responsibility of saving all of human kind from this evil, then why at times does it seem like he's mimicking Jerry Lewis in THE NUTTY PROFESSOR? This, unfortunate out-of-tune character blunder has to be laid at the feet of Coppola himself and probably with a nod of scowling disapproval at the screenwriter as well, because his dialogue at times is laughable. And not to take anything away from Gary Oldman's acting ability, but as Dracula, he is really miscast here. He has neither the mystery nor seductive good looks need for the sexual underpinning that Dracula must have. Mina pants "he's irresistible," and everyone in our home theatre said, "Who is she talking about?" Oldman simply can't pull that off look of irresistible perverted evil. In fact, he seems like he is actually bored with the role and just walking thru his lines, waiting to pick up his paycheck; and then there's his silly dark granny glasses and geeky long stringy black hair which makes him look oddly like Captain Hook in Disney's Peter Pan. When he is transformed into the decrepit old version of himself, he does the tongue quiver that Hopkins made famous in SILENCE OF THE LAMBS (sans the "..fava beans and a nice Chianti" line ). Watch this DRACULA trailer and catch that iconic Hopkins bit of business at 1:05. To sum up.....how can I put this kindly...hmmm...OK, you hear that loud barking? It's this awful DOG of a movie!

history.title: The Black Stallion [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: PURE CINEMA...imagery that is a beauty to behold.
history.text: Total, whole-hearted agreement here with the rest of the 5 star praises, but let me just add, when you watch this magnificent film, take special attention to the horse taming sequence where Alec (Kelly) and Black gain each other's trust and friendship. The sequence is, brilliantly played so naturally and genuinely by Reno and the horse (named Cass-Ole), was as good as any human actor -- kudos to its wrangler. This sequence is PURE cinema...a concept is fully conveyed only with visuals, not a word spoken, much like what needed to be done in silent movies. The spectacular images accompanied by Francis F. Coppola's dad's (Carmine's) powerful score couldn't be a more perfect marriage. Turn the music up LOUD for that sequence; throw anyone who talks during it out of the room!

history.title: Metalstorm: The Destruction Of Jared-Syn (3D Bluray / Bluray) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Enough has been said about the silly story, the stilted dialog made worse by the terrible acting -- if Hollywood has a C list of actors, they are all assembled in this film. And of course the direction is stiff and unsure. That aside, and believe me, it is bad enough to be laughable, I really want to comment on the 3D. I happen to be a 3D fanatic; loved it from the very first time I saw it as a kid in a movie theatre in NY (the then Century Fresh Meadows -- flagship of the chain in Queens) when I watched HOUSE OF WAX. I was hooked; forced my poor mum to sit thru it a second time). Saw every 3D film that came out after that, including the real clunkers, and back then, there weren't many that rose to Academy Award winning quality, but I loved the process, the feeling of depth and space in the image I was watching. To me it was stereo for the eyes. Imagine my delight when technology today allows me to show my kids that same HOUSE OF WAX in my living room on a curved, 65" OLED 3D TV. It's come full circle. BUT as much as I will watch almost anything in 3D that they release on BluRay, the 3D in THIS particular title is so bad that I actually had to stop watching it only a third of the way through. This was shot in SpaceVision 3D, a process that uses literally half the 35mm frame, one half for each eye. That limited film geography on the negative reduces the effective resolution and increases the film grain size to the point that even on a relatively small tv screen (compared to the theatre screen) gives the image a weird, textured look. The fact that the grain is not part of the 3D perspective, it sort of just sit there at the screen frame making the picture seem like it is superimposed on a bed of rice. But that is just the quality of the original source...you know, OLD film. BUT -- and this is where it crashes and burns -- many of the shots are soooo badly converged in the original negative that they are just impossible for your eyes/brain to resolve and you get this terrible feeling like you are seeing double. This happened to be the case with the SpaceVision process which, possibly because of physical spacing of the lenses in what they called the Trioptiscope attachment on the camera, the depth that the viewer experiences is very severe and very unnatural, not like the films shot and shown in dual strip 35mm (all the 50's so call "golden age" of 3D). The severity of the SpaceVision system to start with, then any shot where the cinematographer increases that convergence quota, can make the image unwatchable. This same problem is present in the other SpaceVision 3D film I saw -- Andy_Warhol's_Frankenstein. Many shot are impossible to converge and you see double. LOTS of shots in METALSTORM give that same "Damn, I am going blind" feeling, starting with the very opening credits where the starfield behind the Universal logo is impossible to converge and you say, "Geez, this is not a good sign!". Next you are treated to a "futuristic" vehicle, i.e., a Jeep that has been outfitted with a painted plywood shell over it, driving aimlessly over hill and dale for no apparent reason for what seems like 20 minutes, with half the shots having that very difficult convergence problem, and you ask yourself, "Why am I watching this plywood covered Jeep riding over dirt roads?" Everyone in the room complained. I even went into the 3D settings on the TV menu where the 3D "depth" can be adjusted (really just overall image spacing control) which was set at 50% and I reduced it to down zero (the mildest depth adjustment) in the hopes that would make the images easier for the eyes to converge, but everyone in the room complained that they STILL couldn't deal with some of the images. So as far as the 3D imagery, this gets the extra star only because I love 3D,but really, combined with the awful story and acting, it really deserves 1 star, sorry to say. Others have pretty much reviewed the rest of the quality of the film, which in my mind they are a little to forgiving, but it's obvious this is low budget so pretty much with low expectations so I will leave it at that, but I will add just on additional observation, that the two lead actors, Jeffrey Byron and Kelly Preston are particularly weird -- Preston because his singular expression is that of someone who just gotten tazzed; his eyes are fixed wide-open and bulging. Then there is dear Kelly who must have fell asleep under a hair drier for an hour -- her hair is so frayed and frizzed that it looks like she has one hand on a Tesla coil; Preston on the other hand looks like his hair was dipped in liquid plastic. Add to that the silly dialogue these actors are forced to say and you've got another reason to hit the EJECT button. My advice -- get this thing for free at your local Library or wait until you find it at a flee market or for a couple a bucks used because guaranteed, you won't watch it more than once (and if like me, not even once), but certainly don't be sucked in as I was and shell out list price for this dog of a 3D title.

history.title: Luna (1979) La Luna
history.review_title: A Bertolucci masterpiece finally available, but the Bluray has a serious technical flaw.
history.text: This probably is one very unjustly maligned Bertolucci film that back in 1977 was considered quite controversial but quite honestly, today it really is pretty tame except for the taboo subject matter (Oedipus has been around long enough that we should be over it by now). But this is to report on a very serious technical flaw in this Bluray release by Kino Lorber. For those purchasing this incredible Bertolucci masterpiece in this current release (finally!) be aware that the audio is seriously defective. All the sections that have music are so distorted that it's painful to listen to. Luckily the film has very few moments where music is actually playing, so at least that is a blessing -- dialog is fine, but where the opera music is mixed in, it is atrocious -- full on distortion. How it could be remastered this badly and no one noticed is beyond comprehension. Even the front menu audio is totally distorted. Didn't anyone at KL check this before it was mastered? Anyway, that is just a technical mishap -- KL should remaster this very worthy title and offer to replace the defective discs already sold. That said, this technical flaw shouldn't dissuade anyone foregoing this visual and psychological feast. It is a stunning film that grips you and will keep you intrigued for the full 2 hours. Not to mention it is probably Jill Clayburgh's best work.

history.title: Passengers
history.review_title: Thoroughly enjoyable, intelligent; beautiful use of 3D.
history.text: Story is intelligent, the actors are beautiful to look at, the 3D is spectacular. It does not so much focus on science fiction as it does on the human dilemma and a very deep moral and ethical situation. Lots of food for thought. Highly recommended.

history.title: It Came From Outer Space (2-D / 3-D Blu-Ray)
history.review_title: Historically interesting film, with less a less than intelligent storyline.
history.text: More of an historically significant film than it is anything special in the way of story-line (filled with plot holes and cliches) or serious content. It was, along with CREATURE FROM THE BLACK LAGOON Universal's foray into dual projection, polaroid 3D. The "alien creature," such as it, was pretty hokey, and certainly watching this film, you are very much aware of the technical limitations of what could be done with special effects in the 50s. That said, also in that same year (1953) came a major leap forward in much more realistic special effects (and quite frankly, much more of a coherent story line too) with the release of George Pal's WAR OF THE WORLDS (Paramount) which raised the special effects barre by light-years in the same way Kubrick's 2001 did in the 60s. IT CAME FROM OUTER SPACE still is what today we would consider a "B" movie, although at the time it did very good business for Universal. More interesting than the movie itself is the very informative commentary that is part of the added features with this BluRay release. BTW, THE WAR OF THE WORLDS and IT CAME FROM OUTER SPACE both start with a metior hitting the earth, out of which both spew aliens, nasty and benign (sort of) respectively.

history.title: American Mummy [Limited Edition Blu-ray 3D + 2D Versions]
history.review_title: How many ways can you say EFFIN AWFUL?
history.text: Don't be snuckered in by the professional looking DVD cover-art. It makes it look like it's a real movie, doesn't it? It's not. Or by the fact that it's a mummy movie, maybe like me, it a favorite genre of yours; with one new one about to hit movie screens as a potential blockbuster - this certainly is NOT THAT! There used to be such things as "B" pictures; this would be an "F" picture. Terrible acting by fairly unattractive people with a disturbing sexual undertone that constantly there to creep you out, this actually would be considered sexual harassment to women by any standard. Then there's NO story line, NO direction whatsoever; for the first half hour, you don't even know who the characters are, why they are there or what they are doing other than some gibberish about Aztecs and sacrifice . There no exposition, so you have no idea what the relationship is between any of them. The sets, if you could call them that, consists of a few tents and a rocky hill in Cougar Buttes California. And there in the rocky hills (filmed BTW, in almost monotone sepia -- the whole film has the look of faded 35mm stock) these half clad women are running around in short-shorts, legs totally exposed with no protection from snakes or scorpions, for no logical reason other than the director is tuck back in the 50s thinking bare legs in rocky terrain are titillating -- its not, it's just stupid and sexist. Also the gratuitously exposed breasts thrown in are wildly sexy to the point that they will distract from the gawd-awful acting -- THEY DON'T. By the way, those exposed tits are, for some inexplicable reason, immediately smeared and covered with what looks like road tar -- I ask you, how sexy is that?!. Believe me, this piece of garbage shouldn't have even been released directly to DVD, as that would have been a waste of plastic, but it seems it actually was released to cinema screens. Really... a theatre somewhere actually played this thing?! The only reason I bought it was because it was in 3D and I am a big 3D fan, but and even that couldn't save this dog of a movie. The 3D, btw, is nothing to write home about, those old hackneyed, in-you-face, cliche effects, like a shot of a spear coming at you is done with no subtlety whatsoever, with the camera lingering on it way too long as if the director is saying..."Do you get it? We're filming in 3D...see that spear sticking out of the mannequin and into your face? See....3D." I thought adding another 3D title to my 3D library would be a good thing because I am almost sure they are going to stop releasing 3D titles sooner or later now that LG and Samsung are no longer making 3D TVs. Buying this was NOT a good thing; don't make my mistake.

history.title: Brigadoon [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: This is no MY FAIR LADY
history.text: Lerner and Loewe at their not so good. Gene Kelly as a choreographer at his, well, let's just say, he dances better than he choreographs, and even his dancing we've all seen before. There are even some retread moves stolen right out of the SINGIN IN THE RAIN rain sequence. And Mr. Minnelli spent way too much time on set minutia...he seems to have forgotten that he needs to direct his actors...keep them from looking silly. And silly this whole 2 & half hours certainly does look. Thing is, I remember kind a liking this movie years ago -- used to book it in our retrospective art theatre and thought is was sweet. I don't know, maybe I am getting jaded in my old age, but damn, it certainly doesn't woo me now. Now it just seems cloyingly saccharin, with a much too short dose of witty sarcasm for relief that Van Johnson supplies. Yah, the signature Minnelli sumptuous sets are spectacular, but in that effort he has created a world that instead of looking "other-worldly and magical," it look like exactly what it is, a big MGM sound stage set. Everything looks too fake, even for Brigadoon. When I ran it in the theatre, I caught something I couldn't believe got by the editor -- in the big dance scene, there on what is supposed to be dirt ground, were yellow X marks to help cameras and actors land on their marks. I couldn't believe what I saw so I grabbed the binoculars that are in the projection booth to assist in focusing and I watched the sequence carefully and very "close," and yes, there were the stage cue marks. Not that this is a big deal, but it just added to the overall suspension of the "suspension of disbelief" that I get now from this ill-advised musical. I looked for them in the BluRay and either the frame was cut just a little more than the 35mm film frame, or they were digitally removed in the transfer, but there is no doubt that I saw them on the film. You hear people who don't understand musicals (or opera for that matter) say, "it makes no sense...people all of a sudden busting into song with a full orchestra." And I always respond, but you have no problem accepting Transformers and zombies and Klingons and freaking galaxy guardians, even SPIDER effin MAN? Either you go with the genre or just stay home when you see the word "musical" and leave the rest of us alone. But in this film, I found myself saying exactly the same thing about the dancing -- it all seemed so out of sync...just thrown in because, well, it's a musical and you need dance numbers. The dance sequences come abruptly out of nowhere and seemingly without motivation...AND they go on for WAY TOO LONG; the worst thing about them -- they don't move the story along at all, it's just --"Hey, stop the story, here's a dance number...Gene's gotta show off." And show off he does...it's embarrassing. I understand, Kelly at the time was a humungus big star and evidently Freed pinned the movie on his name and popularity. Thing is, he's totally wrong for the part. He's too old, he's much too slick, and nary a hair on his head ever moves or gets tousled. He certainly doesn't look or even sound like the idealistic, tousled-hair young romantic that the part calls for. And while we are on Kelly, let's take a look at the lack-luster choreography, sadly there is nothing new here. It's repetitive, it's all been done before, he steals almost identical movements from Agnes DeMille's CAROUSEL choreography (watch Louise's dance sequence -- ballet, actually -- with the Starlight Carousel barker) and then he steals Astaire's tap moves as well, and for good measure, he retreads a lot of his moves from SINGIN IN THE RAIN, but without the rain or the freshness. Move along...nothing to new to see here other than Gene Kelly designing dance sequences for himself that are too long and so obviously vanity vehicles for himself. Evidently Minnelli was too afraid to reign in the superstar. Then there is Ms Charisse -- yes, the woman is statuesque, and in this film, that's about it. Oh yah, the statue had with WAY to much rouge (who was her makeup artist? Should have been fired it's so badly done). Either it was Minnelli who just wasn't giving her any direction or the woman simply can't act, but thru the entire movie she either over-acts to the point of comedy or she does nothing but stare into space looking like a dear caught in headlights. There is one sequence where for what seems like a good 10 minutes, that's exactly what she does -- sits there, motionless staring off-set, looking at nothing...perhaps searching for motivation? She also walks with her arms unnaturally far out from her sides as if she's trying to avoid touching her dress; perhaps it was just pinned up by wardrobe and she's afraid it will come apart? I got the feeling she had no idea what she was doing and unfortunately Minnelli didn't clue her in. Oh, yah, let's not forget to mention how absurd this "Scottish" dialog starts to sound after about 5 minutes, all these Californians trying to get "Now dunna, ye worry the wee lassie" to sound authentic. And of course the songs; for me they are not very memorable, none followed me around for days after viewing like so many other good musicals songs do except maybe "Heather on the Hill." And I might add, like the dance numbers, the songs also didn't come naturally to the story line and worse, did they move the story along. Like I said, this is no MY FAIR LADY or CAMELOT. The only bright spot for me in this whole mishmash is the Van Johnson character's dialogue. There were some lines where I laughed aloud and heard the old super clever Alan Jay Lerner dialogue breaking thru. But that's countered with the forced attempt at mystical magical romantic sweet-talk he gives Kelly...just give me a barb bag along along with the BluRay. This sappy stuff was drawn out and so unpleasant that I actually grabbed the remote to see if I could skip ahead. Hey, it was a big hit for MGM so who can argue with success and it seems to get plenty of 5 stars here. But what seems painfully obvious to me is just a studio trying to hold the decline caused by TV at bay, recycling their aging, big musical stars and bigger, more lavish productions. There certainly was that over-the top effort to provide a sumptuous "look" that only Hollywood was capable of and that TV back then would never be able to give an audience. But in this instance, it was so overdone that it simply looks too fake...in Ansco Color? Ansco Color is a poor man's Technicolor and an even poorer man's Eastman Color. You can see how much the studios were trying to best TV -- the wide screen process name (CinemaScope) is put BEFORE the picture title or even the stars' names! Problem for me is, it just doesn't work for me any more. My suggestion, like in Brigadoon, see it once, then put it on a shelf for the next 100 years.

history.title: The Wall
history.text: I recently purchased the Kindle edition of the book that this movie is based on, [[ASIN:B00B6U090O The Wall]] by Haushofer Marlen. I noticed that there was a movie based on it so I went and rented it. The DVD doesn't have any extras, just the trailer for the film and an English language audio track and subtitles. I haven't read the book yet, so I can't compare the movie to it. The movie is about two-hours long and very slow paced - the majority of dialog spoken is a voice over describing what the woman has written in her report journaling the events of what has happened to her and how she has survived till now. This is a very dreary movie - which depending on whether you like that sort of thing or not , that is a good or bad thing. Personally, I liked the movie. I was constantly imagining what I might have done in a similar situation. The end of the file is a little unresolved, but I think that only adds to the sadness and ambiguity of the story.

history.title: K - The Complete Series (Limited Edition Blu-ray/DVD Combo)

Vibrant colors with richly detailed environments are the main in every episode. It was lacking a little on some explainations but none the less still a very likeable show. Shiro is suspected of being a murderer...there is even a video of the killer and it looks just like him. Yet Shiro swears he was at school at the time of this murder meanwhile there are people out to kill him because of this video. One such person finds Shiro and until he can prove that Shiro is or isnt the murderer he will not let him out of his sight. If Shiro is indeed quilty...he will kill him on the spot. So while trying to evade those who are after him...Shiro tries to piece together the puzzle of whom this person is in the video.
