history.title: Shangri-La: Complete Series - S.A.V.E
history.text: This is just a brief about the "SAVE" edition. I payed almost $70 for parts one and two...Part one I bought the "Limited Edition". Well much to my surprise...when I bought this version as a gift, it was the Chipboard box like my limited edition. Basically it IS the "Limited Edition" Chipboard box with Part Two included. It is the Limited Edition box...."That people are trying to sell you for $60 - part one" with both parts. If you were to buy both parts as of now - Part 1 "Limited Edition" = $60....Part 2 = $37. With this version you get the Chipboard box - Parts 1 & 2 = $20. No....it does not have SAVE plastered all over the front of the box. I really wish all SAVE Editions were like this. It is the best edition I have seen and truly lives up the word "SAVE". I hope to see more like this!!! As far as the animation goes.....it is done by GONZO and as a whole is above average. Kuniko Hojo is your main character and is the heir apparent to rebel group known as Metal Age. Kuniko and her almost ever present Tranny friend "Momoko" are a great team. Even during the heat of battle Momoko always drops lines...she grabs one soldier and while she is surrounded by more Soldiers she'll say "Patience boys..You all get a turn"...then proceeds to drop them. Two very likeable and inseparable characters. Yet there are three more that the story centers around and all are headed in the same direction. Whom will lay claim to Atlas, a haven amoung their ruinous existence...a city free of the strife endured by the masses aournd it. After the second great Konto quake - Tokyo is left to be reclaimed by nature. Hence the premises of the story. Their economy is carbon based and the more your nation pollutes the worse your econmy is...so Tokyo was left to be reclaimed by nature hoping to cool the planet and lower carbon emissions. In my opinion this is a sleeper and at least worth watching.

history.text: This was a very interesting story. This disc is not what I am talking about. On Netflix there is a movie that is about 1 hour and 40 minutes long. As far as the animation goes...think Ajin, Knights of Sidonia and Kingdom or Vexille come to mind. This is something I will definitely buy when the movie is released. Unfortunately I have not heard anything about a forth coming series. Sure the story has been done before with slight variations. This is about a futuristic city where computers or Netsphere were past of the daily life. Spoiler --> A contagion infects the mass population and the Netsphere suddenly deems humans as an illegal tenant of the city and you can guess from there. This is about the remaining individuals trying to survive...then they find someone with a possible solution and the story takes off from there. Very much worth watching!!

history.title: Ajin
history.text: Ajins have been discovered and they are immortal or are they. They are called Ajin and you only find out that you are one after you die. Which is what happens to our main character...Ajins are locked up, tortured and looked down upon by society. Generally people are afraid of them and are asked to turn them in if they discover one. Slight spoiler.....guess what happens. Kei is daydreaming and is killed in the process on the street. While everyone stands around looking on in horror something begins to happen to Kei and he gets up and realizes what he is. At that point he is scared and takes off......... That happens in the first 5 or 10 minutes so I did not give you to much to go on but alliances are formed and he is just a kid wanting to live his life in peace but will society let him? Animation style is great...think Knights of Sidonia, Blame...along those lines. This is an adult oriented story and there is no nudity..no harem comedy and I honestly do not remember any language issues. I found this series to be excellent and perhaps even with underlying tones of acceptance for others whom are not like you. There already is a second season to this on Netflix and all are in English or Japanese if you prefer.

history.title: Tales of Zestiria the X: Season One [Blu-ray]
history.text: This is a visual treat. There were several parts that reminded me of watching a Disney movie...the bright colors of El Dorado or style of Atlantis. Cg is awesome and the storyline is solid. You follow the Shepherd a person that can call upon the power of the Seraphim, which normal people can not see. Combined with their strength they battle Hellions and search for the reason why the world is out of balance, so to speak. Voices are done very well and the story moves forward at a solid pace. I streamed it off of Funimation and they have both parts one and two. This is a series I would recommend....there is violence but never over the top blood and guts. It is not a fan service series and I do not remember any foul language. If this is the future standard of animation then the bar is set high. Very very pleased with this series from start to finish.

I watched this movie years ago. I only remember the ending. Now I know why.

An all star cast makes this a really great movie. If you like mysteries you will like it. Surprise ending (I like that).

history.text: What a great movie. Anthony Hopkins I'm very familiar with. Ryan Gosling is a new comer to me. They worked very well together. I love a good mystery and this is one. You won't believe the ending.
Ashley Judd (what a lady). Her and Hugh Jackman are priceless. Every scene between them is worth watching over and over. The chemistry is so good. Not much of a story (who cares).

history.review_title: One of the best war movies ever
history.text: What a fantastic cast. The action never stops. I think this movie is based on actual events. Very realistic. They don't make good war movies anymore.

history.title: The Expanse: Season One [Blu-ray]
history.text: I'm always a little uneasy buying a movie or TV show I've never seen. But this show has been exceptional. After the first episode was over, I immediately wanted to watch the second. When watching the third or fourth episode, it suddenly ended. "Why was that only ten minutes long?" I asked myself. It wasn't, it just seemed so short because it held my attention so well. Don't worry about the comments about multiple story lines. I've only counted three major story lines thus far, and anyone can keep up with that. Looking forward to buying next season, after the price goes down.

history.title: Life [Blu-ray]
history.text: Go to your nearest home improvement store. Buy a sheet of plywood, paint, and a paint brush. Paint one side of the plywood sheet. Pull up a chair and watch the paint dry. Congratulations! You've just done something more productive with your time than watch this movie. Seriously, I've seen all kinds of movies, but if a movie doesn't end the way you want it, you should at least have a modicum of satisfaction at the end. This is the most unsatisfying movie I've ever seen. If you must watch it, rent it, don't buy it. But if you need not watch it, don't. You'd be better off painting the other side of the plywood.

history.title: The Middle: Season 1
history.text: To be honest, I bought this show for one reason: Neil Flynn. And if we're all being honest, he was the funniest character on Scrubs. While that type of character doesn't completely translate in this series, I have, nonetheless, enjoyed his acting. Like most brand-new shows, the first few episodes are a little uneven. But as the series progresses through the first season, the quality greatly improves. And I like the idea that I have eight more seasons to enjoy the show, though it was recently announced that the ninth season will be the last.

history.title: The Lost City of Z
history.text: Like so many other contemporary films, The Lost City of Z has potential, but ultimately ends in an unsatisfying and disappointing way. Save your time, save your money, and skip this one.

history.title: xXx: Return Of Xander Cage
history.text: I don't know where to start. To say this movie was horribly clichéd would be a compliment. I can't even articulate how bad it was. Is it just me, or are movies these days that are funded by the Chinese particularly bad? I like Vin Diesel, which is why I bought the film in the first place, but man, this is so bad. Did you really need a paycheck this badly, Vin? If you like Vin Diesel, I'd suggest any of the Chronicles of Riddick films.

history.title: Kong: Skull Island (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: Could have been a straight-to-DVD film
history.text: Yet another bad movie funded by the Chinese. Kong proves, once again, that throwing a bunch of big names into a movie does not a good film make. This film is completely directionless, introducing characters and plot lines that lead absolutely nowhere. The *only* thing that kept this movie from being a complete washout was John C. Reilly. No, I really mean that. There's also an Asian woman in the film who has about five lines, and was apparently only added to appeal to Asian audiences. She has no memorable presence in the film. And for goodness sakes, please stop throwing Samuel L. Jackson into every fourth movie created these days. You're killing the guy, and we need him for the Avengers movies. Someone wake me up when they start making good movies again for American audiences.

history.title: Brooklyn Nine-Nine: Season Four [DVD]
history.review_title: It was good while it lasted.
history.text: This show has definitely lost steam fast. I thoroughly enjoyed the first three seasons, but...what happened? I can deal with the mild gay references, but after one of the characters suggested that one of the other characters needed to "bone" his husband, I'm done. If you're reading this and you enjoy boning another man, whether you are also a man, hey, whatever. But I don't watch TV (and I certainly don't pay) to hear this kind of stuff. Permanently dropping this show would be more difficult, if this season weren't so bad. And I didn't get back the first disk.

history.title: Fences [BD/Digital HD Combo] [Blu-ray]
history.text: Maybe I take some movies too personally, but I don't like to see actors I generally favor (Denzel) portraying jerks. I did find some interesting similarities between Denzel's character in this movie and his character in Training Day: both were abusive, both cheated on their wives, and both died at the end. Of course, in his movie, Denzel's character doesn't die in a hailstorm of bullets, but if he had, I would have been okay with that. I'm honestly not sure why I watched this to the end. In some movies which portray a difficult character, the writers give you an out, explaining why the character is so unlikable. Not so here. Considering the course the movie takes, the photo on the cover is completely misleading. Bottom line, Denzel's (and he is the reason I watched it in the first place) character is a reprobate with genuinely no redeeming characteristics of which to speak. Skip this one. But if you are looking for a good Denzel movie, I recommend The Equalizer.

history.title: Going in Style (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: Oh, Zach Braff directed it? That explains it...
history.text: I loved Scrubs, but I would have been okay if Zach Braff hadn't been in every season of the show. But this isn't about Braff's bad acting, it's about his bad directing. You would think with this level of star power, this movie would be pretty amazing, but instead, it shows once again that great actors can only do so much with a weak story and script. Just before the bank robbery, one of the supporting male actors says that, "There is always another way." Why? What was the point of this line? The characters were going to rob the bank, no matter what. And I'm supposed to be happy about the movies happy ending? They still stole millions of dollars from innocent people. This movie could have been so much more, and had it not had the actors it did, I would have given it a one or two star rating. This isn't worth the money.

history.title: Fixer Upper Season 1
history.text: At this point, you would think the whole house-flipping genre would be as exciting as day-old bread. But I love watching this show, I have rarely seem a couple as perfect (or more precisely, adorable) as Chip and Joanna Gaines. But they also get the job done, turning plain (or nearly condemned) houses into lovely homes. I only wish Season Two and forward were available on DVD.

history.title: The Right Stuff
history.text: When "The Right Stuff" was first released in theaters back in 1983, it was not a box office success. It was perceived as a political story with a strong emphasis on the life of John Glenn and the movie-going public stayed away, flocking instead to more mainstream, easy-going fare as "The Big Chill", among others, for entertainment. I remember seeing it during its first run, along with about five other people in the theater that evening. I also recall what a memorable & impressive presentation it made on the big screen that first time & I thoroughly loved everything about it. It reminded me so much of that fabled, peaceful time in the early 60's some of us remember as "The Age of Camelot". Of course, it has long since become a great American classic with its inspiring, true story about the seven military pilots chosen for the early 1960's Mercury Space Program, along with the legendary test pilot Chuck Yeager (who was not.) Based from the best-selling 1979 Tom Wolfe book of the same name, "The Right Stuff" was adapted, written, & directed by Philip Kaufman. It took five years, according to Kaufman, to create the film as he envisioned it. He & his incredibly talented team (with a special acknowledgement to cinematographer Caleb Deschanel) had to develop convincing special effects from scratch and well before computer imagery became the norm. Actual NASA documentary footage was interspersed with brilliant and stunning effect. Pilot jargon such as "pushing the envelope", "screw the pooch", "spam in a can", and "that old demon in the air" were brought to the forefront. "The Right Stuff" has a run time of just over three hours, and Kaufman's direction makes it seem like less than two. It's a beautiful film with storylines and plot that flows smoothly in its focus on the pilots' individual and group journeys into becoming astronauts for the United States' first attempt with manned spaceflight. Great performances abound, with Scott Glenn, Ed Harris, Sam Shepard, Dennis Quaid, Fred Ward, and Barbara Hershey. The real Chuck Yeager (who makes a cameo appearance) was hired as a technical consultant for some of the flying scenes. Film composer Bill Conti was brought in toward the completion of the picture to write a new score for it, as Kaufman felt the first composer's score was not right. Conti's marvelous score for "The Right Stuff" got him an Academy Award for "Best Original Score". The film also won three other Academy Awards including "Best Sound Effects Editing", "Best Sound", and "Best Film Editing". It was nominated, as well, for "Best Actor In A Supporting Role" (Sam Shepard as "Chuck Yeager"), "Best Art Direction-Set Decoration", "Best Cinematography" (Caleb Deschanel), and "Best Picture". For myself, I believe it should have won "Best Picture" that year - many film critics feel the same way. The late Roger Ebert called "The Right Stuff" the best film of 1983. He wrote, "It joins a short list of recent American movies that might be called experimental epics: movies that have an ambitious reach through time and subject matter, that spend freely for locations or special effects, but that consider each scene as intently as an art film". Ebert would later call it one of the best films of the 80's decade and #2 behind Martin Scorsese's "Raging Bull". Ebert's co-host on their "At The Movies" tv show, Gene Siskel, also called "The Right Stuff" the best film of 1983, and put it at #3 on his best films of the 1980's list. Newsweek said, "When 'The Right Stuff' takes to the skies, it can't be compared with any other movie, old or new: it's simply the most thrilling flight footage ever put on film." I've owned the double VHS tape set, the laserdisc, and the standard dvd of "The Right Stuff", but they all pale in comparison to this 30th Anniversary double blu-ray disc set, which also includes a fabulous booklet inside the case containing bio's, beautiful photographs, production notes, and historical quotes. I've waited longer than I can remember for a proper presentation of this epic, historical, and glorious film, and now it's here. What a magnificent HD upgrade this is with gorgeous sound & stunning, perfect color, along with the second bonus disc containing special features, interviews, and documentaries on the film, NASA, the astronauts, & the historical significance of "The Right Stuff". It has quickly become one of my favorite blu- ray's. A timeless masterpiece about a long-gone era that totally deserves its status as a classic.

history.title: Something Wild
history.text: I remember reading about the 1961 film "Something Wild" years ago, but only recently learned it was released on dvd in 2011 by MGM's limited-edtion collection division. I've had the fine Aaron Copland cd soundtrack for years that was released on Varese Sarabande in 2003, but always wanted to see the film. A stark, grim, and poignant examination of a young girl's (Carroll Baker) experience with violence and despair in New York City, "Something Wild" is based on the Alex Karmel novella "Mary Anne" and was directed by Baker's then-husband Jack Garfein. It was filmed in black & white entirely on location in New York City. The dominating themes in the film are human loneliness & hopelessness. Baker is marvelous in the role of "Mary Ann", a young Brooklyn college student who is brutally raped in a park early in the story and is unable to deal with the harrowing trauma from it. Mary is about to commit suicide on a bridge when a mechanic (Ralph Meeker as "Mike") saves her at the last second. His own life is bleak and empty, as well. He invites her to come with him back to his drab apartment to rest and sleep for the night, but decides to keep her captive as she "is his last chance" at finding love. After he comes home drunk one night, he physically comes on to her, and she kicks him in the face causing the loss of one eye. In their strange relationship, there is not alot of dialogue between them. It was this particular aspect of the picture that really appealed to composer Copland, as it opened up many avenues for him in his expressive & dramatic writing. Aaron said, "The lengthy stretches of silent action invite musical comment in a way that imbues the whole film with a certain musical 'tone'. It goes, without saying, that one must have an absolute free hand in these matters and this was assured me by Jack Garfein and George Justin, respectively the director and producer of the film." A brilliant composer for contemporary urban settings, Copland's score for "Something Wild" would be adapted later for his piece, "Music For A Great City". On first viewing, one is truly guessing trying to see where the film's story is headed, as it seems there is absolutely no chance for ANY type of normal relationship between the two characters. Heartbreaking and unforgettable, "Something Wild" is a stunning, emotionally charged film that was called a "lost indie classic" when it was screened at the New York IFC Center in 2007. The on-location NYC shooting that Garfein used in the picture, particularly the night downtown scenes, reminded me of Stanley Kubrick's NYC scenes in his 1955 film-noir classic , "Killer's Kiss". The brilliant German director of photography on "Something Wild", Eugen Schufftan, would go on one year later in 1962 to win an Academy Award for his work on "The Hustler". The opening titles in the film, matched with the NYC skyline, were done by the legendary Saul Bass with remarkable effect. "Something Wild" was truly a labor of love for Jack Garfein & Carroll Baker -- both paid their own $ to get it completed. When United Artists subsequently demanded payment for IOU's on postproduction costs and refused to pay for Copland's scoring fee, Baker completed a deal with UA, as she & Jack had exhausted their funds, to "pay" them by doing another picture which would be "Mister Moses". $ debt on "Something Wild" would then be deducted from her "Moses" fee. "Something Wild" would be Garfein's last film, though. A timeless statement about the human condition in the urban jungle, it was controversial when it was released in 1961, as it dealt with a brutal rape and contained brief nudity. Powerful and direct, "Something Wild" would also be Aaron Copland's final film score. Kudos to MGM for getting this work finally released on dvd (in full-frame, with no special features or trailer).

history.title: Under the Volcano (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.text: It had been several years since I last viewed my 2-disc 2007 Criterion dvd set of director John Huston's fine 1984 production of English writer Malcolm Lowry's novel and masterpiece, "Under The Volcano", so I decided to examine it again one recent evening. It's a set I treasure not only for Huston's film but also for the marvelous documentary on the second disc called, "Volcano: An Inquiry into the Life and Death of Malcolm Lowry", a 1976 Academy Award nominated work from filmmaker Donald Brittain w/excellent narration by Richard Burton. John's movie was his 34th in his long, distinguished career, and features Albert Finney as the doomed alcoholic British consul Geoffrey Firmin, Jacqueline Bisset as his estranged wife, Yvonne, & Anthony Andrews as Firmin's brother, Hugh. Called "unfilmable" because of the novel's intense and difficult penetration into Geoffrey's alcohol-induced state of mind, "Under The Volcano" had been approached & abandoned by other filmmakers (Luis Bunuel, among others) before Huston did it at the age of 78. I'll give John high marks for attempting such a challenging subject, where others had backed off. Finney gives a tour-de-force performance in his portrayal of the alcoholic consul. One watches this and WONDERS how a human being could take this much liquor (and in only one day). "Volcano" is probably my favorite work from Finney - he's just astounding. Bisset and Andrews are outstanding, as well, but this is Albert Finney's showcase. I have no qualms with some of the liberties Huston took in adapting Lowry's novel to the screen. I have admiration that a quality production WAS finally achieved. Written over a period of 10 years and published in 1947, Malcolm's "Volcano" has been called one of the "100 Best Novels of the 20th Century." It was also derived from Lowry's own life and experiences as a chronic alcoholic - he started drinking at age 14, and died at the age of 47 from vomiting, excessive alcohol consumption, and barbiturate poisoning. I first read it while in college, but it's taken subsequent re-reads to get a firm handle on it. (For a detailed view into Lowry's life, check out Gordon Bowker's extraordinary 1993 biography, "Pursued By Furies - A Life of Malcolm Lowry", which I got several years ago & plan to read again this summer.) John's film was beautifully shot by legendary Mexican director of photography Gabriel Figueroa, who had also worked with Huston on his classic 1964 film, "Night of the Iguana", starring Richard Burton as an alcoholic minister and set in Mexico, as well. The remarkable and unique opening title sequence in "Under The Volcano" was done by Huston's 21 year old son, Danny, who was in London film school at the time. Alex North's evocative score for the film garnished his 13th (and final) career Academy Award nomination for his superb work. Finney received a total of 5 "Best Actor" nominations for "Volcano" (including Academy Award) and won the London Film Critics Circle and Los Angeles Film Critics awards in that category. Bissett was nominated for the Golden Globe "Best Supporting Actress" award. The film, itself, was entered and nominated in the 1984 Cannes Film Festival, and selected by The National Board of Review as a "Top 10 Film of the Year." After 6 attempts by other film directors who bailed from it, John Huston successfully completed the film adaption of "Under The Volcano" and did it in brilliant fashion. Bravo to the Criterion Film Collection for this wonderful & rewarding dvd presentation, along with spectacular documentaries, interviews, an informative booklet about the film, the book, all the principal's involved, and gorgeous photo stills.

history.title: Holiday Affair
history.text: They sure don't make them like this anymore. Great little Christmas film from 1949 starring Robert Mitchum & Janet Leigh in a love story that never is complete until the final scenes on the train. On first viewing, it seems these two characters never will get on the same wavelength with each other (as in real-life relationships, sometimes). Being a collector (and operator) of Lionel trains, I love the story involving Mitchum's character Steve buying a Lionel train set for Leigh's little boy in the film and the wonderful shots of the train in action from the opening scene and through the rest of it. It's heartwarming and keeps you guessing if Mitchum and Leigh are going to finally hook up, which they do. Fine performances from everyone & a funny bit from actor Harry Morgan as a police judge. "Holiday Affair" is definitely a seasonal Christmas film, but can be enjoyed anytime of the year. In black and white standard format. Wonderful.

history.title: Sorcerer (1977) (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.text: In 1956 when legendary film director William Friedkin saw the classic 1953 Henri-Georges Clouzot French movie "Wages of Fear" about four reckless men hauling nitroglycerine in two trucks over crater-filled dirt roads to put out an oil-well fire, it stuck with him. In 1976, he decided to update the story to the present era (then 70's) with different characters but same premise. Freidkin acquired the rights from the author of the original story, Georges Arnaud, since Clouzot didn't own them and so began his first picture for Universal Studios who gave a green light. I remember when I FIRST saw William Friedkin's extraordinary 1976 action film "Sorcerer" after it was released in theaters in its brief run before it was pulled due in large part to its inability to compete with the blockbuster "Star Wars" released a month earlier and obliterating the market. I saw it at an evening showing with about five other people in the theater that night. It was Friedkin's first movie since his own landmark blockbuster fright fest "The Exorcist" four years earlier. Many people had the misconception that the title "Sorcerer" meant this picture was going to be another horror shocker from Freidkin. It couldn't have been farther from the truth and word-of-mouth along with undeserved bad reviews (and the previously mentioned "Star Wars") pretty much killed it. But when I left the theater that night, I found it brilliant, refreshing, and STUNNING. I loved it. At long last, this magnificent film is now being properly presented in a glorious HD widescreen blu-ray with remastered sound the way it should be. Over the years, I've owned the VHS, laserdisc, and washed-out god-awful standard full-frame dvd of "Sorcerer" that were all simply adequate, but really didn't capture the jungle beauty and marvelous soundtrack Friedkin used by the techno band Tangerine Dream and incredible pipe organ work from jazz legend Keith Jarrett (from his 1976 ECM album "Hymns/Spheres"). Friedkin knows a thing or two about using unusual music for the scores in his films and "Sorcerer" is no exception. According to him, the title "Sorcerer" originated from the classic Miles Davis album of the same name, but he did intend it (regretfully) as a reference to "The Exorcist". The original title was going to be "Ballbreaker", which didn't go over too well with studio executives. Along with Tangerine Dream & Keith Jarrett, Miles' tune "So What" can be heard as well as Charlie Parker with strings. To watch this movie, one wouldn't have a clue as to the chaos, turmoil, dissension, frustration, and difficulties in its making. With "Sorcerer", it's legendary. So many workers were fired by Friedkin during filming that star Roy Scheider joked, "I was the only guy he couldn't fire, because I was the leading man. I said to Billy, 'You gotta stop firing these people, 'cause I'm getting tired of going to the airport and saying goodbye to them.'" Scheider was already somewhat bitter with Friedkin, as he had been turned down for the major role of Father Karras in "The Exorcist" after co-starring in "The French Connection" with Gene Hackman. Cost overruns & delays blew the original $2.5 million budget up to a staggering $22.5 million. Friedkin called "The Bridge" sequence in the movie, which took months to film, the most difficult thing he had ever attempted. It lasts only 12 minutes in the picture, and it's considered the key, pivotal showcase in the story. At a cost of over $3 million ALONE (most not budgeted), it has to be seen to be believed. Even now, it's still one of the most astounding things I've ever seen in a film. Friedkin was totally hell-bent on getting this done his way, and he pulled it off. In the introductory note that comes with the blu-ray book, Friedkin writes, "Despite all the problems and setbacks, the cost overruns, bruised egos, and shattered friendships, I felt then and still do that "Sorcerer" is the best film I've made." Quite a statement from the man who brought us "The French Connection" & "The Exorcist". Like alot of his pictures, "Sorcerer" is in-your-face, relentless, brutal, and uncompromising without a happy ending. He remains one of my favorite directors, living or dead. Kudos to Warner Bros. and those responsible for the great restoration & presentation of this new blu-ray of "Sorcerer", which is housed in a marvelous book containing photo stills, a letter from Mr. Friedkin, and notes adapted from his fascinating memoir, "The Friedkin Connection", which is highly recommended, as well. It looks and sounds better than ever. Welcome back.

history.title: No Way To Treat A Lady
history.text: The 1968 film, "No Way To Treat A Lady", has always been one of my favorite's. The subject matter concerning a psychotic master of disguise brilliantly played by Rod Steiger is certainly disturbing, but any graphic violence is not displayed, nor is there gratuitous nudity, sex, or profanity as would most certainly be present if this film were made now. It's also my favorite movie starring Steiger, as he gives an absolute tour-de-force performance as a serial killer of women in New York City gaining entry to the victims' homes under the guise of various roles (priest, plumber, gay wig-seller, policeman, older woman, & food delivery man). In the movie, he's a prestigious theater owner with an obvious mother-complex with subtle indications he, himself, may be gay. George Segal is wonderful as the detective on the case with Lee Remick playing his new-found love interest & coming very close to becoming a victim, herself. It's a fascinating cat-and-mouse black comedy directed by Jack Smight and based on the novel by William Goldman. The musical score by Stanley Myers, who was only 30 when he did the picture, deserves special mention. It not only features haunting vocals by legendary British singer Barbara Moore, but is a great example of a score capturing the classic sound & vibe of the late 60's urban scene. (Myers composed the dramatic music and theme for the 1978 Academy Award winning movie "The Deer Hunter".) The American Breed, a popular 60's singing group, provide a marvelous tune in the film called "A Quiet Place" featured in a sequence highlighting the blossoming romance between Segal's and Remick's characters. Myers' orchestrations PERFECTLY reflect the story's suspense, the eeriness of Steiger's weird behavior, & the immense urban scenery that is New York City. "No Way To Treat A Lady" is a haunting time-capsule from a long-gone era that is available now only in standard, widescreen dvd format but with fine, vivid colors in the transfer. A timeless film, both dark & funny, along with an exquisite musical score from Briton Stanley Myers and great acting, "No Way" is a winner.

history.title: Whiplash [Blu-ray]
history.text: I found "Whiplash" unpleasant, weird, and even bizarre. I DEFINITELY won't be watching this one again. What I really couldn't take was the foul-mouthed, narcissistic, crude, abusive puke portrayed as the instructor. Excellent acting, but I wouldn't want to see it again. I did like the music, particularly the Hank Levy title-tune but played against a background portraying a viscious cut-throat atmosphere, I can watch other more pleasant films. I had heard about "Whiplash" and wanted to see it - glad I got to on a free Dish pay-per-view offer and didn't have to pay anything. I actually thought it was well made for what it is but just too harsh and abrasive with the language, screaming, & berating tone. If you want to hear a marvelous version of "Whiplash", check out the late trumpeter/bandleader Don Ellis' cd called "Soaring". I also found the ending contrived, corny, and unrealistic. Pure Hollywood and a one-timer. I'll stick with my heavenly "Jazz on a Summer's Day" dvd, thank you, which I never get tired of seeing over and over - the real stuff.

history.title: Fear and Desire [Blu-ray]
history.text: In 1952, legendary film director Stanley Kubrick was getting ready to make his first feature film based on a screenplay written by a poet friend, Howard O Sackler, (at Kubrick's suggestion) who attended the same school he did, Taft High School in NYC. It was first called "The Trap", then "The Shape of Fear", and finally "Fear and Desire". Of the future film, Stanley said, "Its structure: allegorical. Its conception: poetic. A drama of "man" lost in a hostile world, deprived of material and spiritual foundations, seeking his way to an understanding of himself & of life around him. He is further imperiled on his Odyssey by an unseen but deadly enemy that surrounds him; but an enemy who, upon scrutiny, seems to be almost shaped from the same mold....... It will, probably, mean many things to different people, and it ought to." Even at this young age of 24, Kubrick had well connected and talented friendships. Sackler would go on to win the Pulitzer Prize for his landmark 1969 play "The Great White Hope" and he also wrote an early draft of "Jaws" (1975). Stanley Kubrick is my favorite director and has been since I first saw his amazing, mind-blowing masterpiece 2001: A Space Odyssey on a huge screen (and ice cold theater) in 1969 when I was 13. I had heard and read about his first feature film "Fear and Desire" for years, but had never seen it until this blu-ray was recently released. On a $53,000 budget that he raked & scraped together to make the picture, it's not that bad. Of course it doesn't have the flawless polish and performances of his landmark work to come, but for a 1953 debut effort with limited resources, a viewer has to take this into account. Shot with a rented 35mm Mitchell film camera (with four lenses), he had no previous experience with it. Kubrick recalled, "I went to the Camera Equipment Company at 1600 Broadway, and the owner, Bert Zucker, spent a Saturday morning showing me how to load and operate it. So that was the extent of my formal training in movie camera techniques." In a striking hint of Kubrick's future methods, a NEW YORK TIMES journalist (Thomas M Pryor) who interviewed Stanley before filming started wrote, "The one requirement is that the cameraman must agree in advance to follow the blueprint laid out by Stanley, who will direct and produce the film." But on "Fear and Desire", Kubrick would do all of the camera shooting, himself, even using a baby carriage to move the camera for certain shots as there was no dolly track available. In his 1999 autobiography, "Show Me the Magic", actor Paul Mazursky (who played Sidney in the film) wrote of Stanley, "Conditions were never easy. No matter what the problem, Kubrick always seemed to have an answer. To me, there was never a question that Stanley was already a master of his universe." The video quality on this new blu-ray of the restored "Fear and Desire" is simply outstanding with remarkable black and white clarity. I've read that Kubrick tried to obtain and destroy all copies of "Fear and Desire", as he was not exactly proud of it: "The ideas we wanted to put across were good, but we didn't have the experience to embody them dramatically. It was little more than a thirty-five millimeter version of what a class of film students would do in sixteen millimeter." Kubrick offered to HORIZON magazine (in 1960) that it was, "a lousy feature, very self-conscious, easily discernible as an intellectual effort, but very roughly, and poorly, and ineffectively made." Thankfully, some copies did survive giving us witness to the early work of a true genius just getting started. "Fear and Desire" is probably the only movie one will see Stanley's first wife, Toba, who appeared in the scenes where the three women are wading in the water. I recognized her from several books with photo's about Kubrick & his films that I've collected. (She's not the one who is later kidnapped & held hostage). The blu-ray also contains another early long-lost Kubrick effort called "The Seafarers", a short subject documentary that he made before this first film . Great to have it now available, as well. At a running time of one hour, "Fear and Desire" gives us a quick glance at the seeds of how a master film-maker thinks. His next picture, "Killer's Kiss", would gradually reveal even more of what was to come. Kudos to all those involved in the restoration and availability of "Fear and Desire" on this glorious-looking blu ray. P.S. Two tracks from composer Gerald Fried's score for "Fear and Desire" ("A Meditation on War" and "Madness") totaling more than nine minutes can be found on a 1999 Silva Screen cd called "Strangelove: Music From the Films of Stanley Kubrick". Recommended listening from this rarely heard music that was re-recorded by the City of Prague Philharmonic Orchestra.

history.title: The Seven-Ups [DVD]
history.text: The 1973 gritty cop film "The Seven Ups" tries hard to be an action thriller set in New York City. Following on the huge success of 1971's Academy Award winning "The French Connection", producer Philip D' Antoni decided to direct a cop picture using several of the actors and people associated with "Connection" (actors Roy Scheider, Tony Lo Bianco, Benny Marino, Bill Hickman, police technical advisor & screen- writer Sonny Grosso, editor Jerry Greenberg, & composer Don Ellis.) It would be the only movie he ever directed and would come from the same studio that produced "The French Connection" with 20th Century Fox. In "The Seven Ups", he would even include an extended chase sequence (like "Connection"), only this time it would be with cars & not an elevated train with a car. When D' Antoni produced "The French Connection" with the brilliant director William Friedkin, the story, characters, pace, and action all blended to perfection which is why it won 5 Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Director. Even "Seven Ups" Jerry Greenberg, who edited the chase scene in the film, won an Academy Award for editing "The French Connection". So the talent and depth was certainly all there for "The Seven Ups" & the chase scene itself, which is the action centerpiece of the movie, is the best part. But for me, there's something definitely missing with "The Seven Ups". Roy Scheider is excellent, as usual in the lead role but the other characters are stiff & dull, particularly Bianco as Scheider's boyhood friend who is actually a traitor. Many of the scenes in the picture lack tension and cohesion along with the characters having little to no chemistry with one another. I've watched "The Seven Ups" several times over the years and see these same things lacking time and time again. The car chase looks like it's based on the one that was so revolutionary by director Peter Yates when he made "Bullitt" in San Francisco and the film's sequence, as well, CLEARLY lifts the classic car chase audio sound from Steve McQueen's Mustang GT so effectively used in "Bullitt", which D' Antoni also produced in 1968. Antoni may have thought nobody would catch it, but HOW can a Pontiac Ventura with an automatic transmission (driven by Scheider) sound like a 4-speed manual being double clutched, as McQueen did with his GT? It just doesn't cut it for realism in a major motion picture. Jazz/film composer Don Ellis does the best he can with what's given him & contributes a nice score with screeching strings (but comes nowhere near his fabulous, riveting soundtrack for "The French Connection"). Johnny Mandel was the original composer on "The Seven Ups", but his score wasn't accepted. I've always felt that if William Friedkin could have directed "The Seven Ups", it would have made a monumental difference in the result. Friedkin is a director, D' Antoni is a producer and not a director. As it is, we can only imagine what COULD have been with "The Seven Ups". A classic example of all the ingredients but the wrong chef.

history.title: LISA STANSFIELD - LIVE AT RONNIE SCOTT'S [NTSC/MULTI-REGION DVD. Import-Latin America]
history.text: The dvd copy of this release that I originally picked up back in 2005 was a region 2 PAL version that I, fortunately, was able to see on an all-region player that I have, but it has apparently since been released in an NTSC format compatible with U.S. region 1 dvd players. "Live at Ronnie Scott's" was Lisa Stansfield's beautifully filmed appearance captured late one evening during a 2002 week-long sold out stay at the upscale London Soho jazz club that was first opened in 1959 by jazzman Scott who died in 1996. But the great venue has successfully carried on and is very much alive and kicking right up to today. I, like so many others, first got hooked on Lisa's voice & style when her smash debut album "Affection" came out in 1989. I've loved her music and video concerts (especially the 1990 Japanese laserdisc "Live: All Around the World" and the 1992 U.S. released laserdisc "Lisa: At Wembley Live") ever since. So it was really cool to see her in this late-night intimate club setting performing so many of her hits ("The Real Thing", "So Natural", "Change", "All Woman", "Live Together", "People Hold On", "Never Gonna Give You Up", and "All Around the World", just to mention a few), as well as some jazz standards ("Don't Explain", "They Can't Take That Away From Me"). Lisa's performances (along with her backup musicians, some of whom also appeared on her concert videos) are magical, gorgeous, and pure perfection. This is one dvd that never fails to refresh and stimulate. And, as mentioned before, it was beautifully filmed as well as recorded. Lisa said of her Ronnie Scott's show: "That was hard work but I'd like to do more intimate performances like that. You're up close and personal to the audience and so it's very real." In addition, a 19 minute interview with Lisa is included at the end where she reveals her feelings about attempting a performance challenge like the Ronnie Scott show along with her future musical plans and even a possible straight-ahead jazz album which I, for one, would love to hear from her. Good show, indeed, Lisa!

history.title: The Cyclops [Remaster]
history.text: A widow, a scientist friend, a pilot, and a land speculator go into Mexico to search for her husband that crashed three years ago. They travel in a Stinson Voyager and land in an area with radioactive ore everywhere that causes abnormal giant growth in animals and humans. They encounter the disfigured and brain damaged husband that only has one eye left, and kill him to finally escape. Now that you know the plot, don't waste your time with this. Amazing Colossal Man that came out this year and probably inspired this quickie is more worth it..

history.title: The Salzburg Connection [VHS]
history.review_title: Involved plot with lots of characters
history.text: The Americans, the Austrians, the British, the Chinese, the Nazis, the Israelis and the Russians are all after a box and it's contents for different reasons. Realistic spy thriller that requires concentrating on who is revealed to be who as the story progresses. A thinking man's mystery/thriller.

history.title: Glass Bottom Boat VHS
history.text: A scientist trying to interest the government in a gravity controlled environment space station has a chance meeting with a widow on the weekend, who also happens to work as a guide at his NASA facility. He chooses her as his biographer for his own personal reasons, but complications result from a security check that cast doubts about her being a spy or not. What could have been a clever comedy gets bogged down in silly scenes, some of which go on for too long. I'd pass on this movie unless you like a mix of slapstick and innuendo. There are a couple of scenes of engine tests at JPL, the scientist exiting an early Apollo capsule, an Alouette 2 helicopter with floats taking him away in an emergency, and full size satellite mock-ups in the lobby of what might be JPL. There are references to a Titan 3 and a Gemini space capsule in the animated credits, but this isn't really worth your while if aerospace is your thing,

history.title: the Wild Geese [VHS]
history.text: Surprisingly good film about mercenary operations in an emerging Africa. The officers are more developed characters, but the some of the motivations of the NCOs and enlisted are interesting in the hiring sequence. The opposition uses what appears to be a Beech Twin Bonanza in a strafing and napalm drop role! The unit evacuates in a modernized DC-3 "Dakota".

history.title: John Goldfarb Please Come Home [Import]
history.text: Comedy that moves along without any flab in the editing. Nearly a visual or verbal gag in every scene, if not every shot. Even if the story is a bit silly, there are topical references to the times. A sheik blackmails a downed pilot into coaching his boy's football team, while a female reporter sneaks in to write an expose on harems. There is also a running gag with the father's obsession with toy trains. We see one shot of an F-86 being towed across the tarmac. As the pilot prepares for flight, he stands before an RF-84F painted half black to look like a U-2, which is seen in flight in correct form as a model. See this for the comedy instead.

history.title: Journey Into Fear [VHS]
history.text: Engineer businessman played by Cotten tries to get out of Turkey without being killed by the Nazis. This sort of film was done better by Hitchcock, and could be tighter. I'm not sure what the original director's cut looked like, unless it was to develop backgrounds for the other characters even more than they are. The lead character is hard to root for, as he never gets involved more than he has to, and the tension doesn't build enough to the climax. The slipcase advertises a 15 min. "vintage short subject", which is Decade For Decision from maybe 1960, describing the push for more college grads through the development of new urban universities, like Buffalo NY. I'm not sure why this was chosen, except to round out a short movie, and RKO owned it.

history.title: The Big Parade
history.text: Spoilers! Well to do American leaves family and sweetheart, goes to war, makes friends, falls in love with a French girl, loses one buddy and is wounded himself, returns home, confesses where his heart is and returns to France to be with her. Long melodrama is well staged. There are brief shots of MB-2 bombers and DH-4 trainers in formation, a Jenny playing a German plane getting shot down, some other aircraft passing overhead as they move to the front, a ride along shot of the country side, and a strafing shot. Otherwise, this is primarily an infantry film.

history.text: The catalog number for the 2 disc Special Edition as listed on spine is G76044. The catalog number for the single disc standard edition is 75027. The second disc intended for a Windows XP computer also contains the Making Of feature, as well as a Uncharted Territories Challenge Game, and High-Def Wallpapers.,

history.title: Deadman's Curve: The Jan and Dean Story
history.text: My rating is for the Interglobal Home Video release. This is my second experience with a tape from them and they have to have the worst quality control and durability that I have ever seen in VHS. Movie skips to glitched areas throughout as others have said, and it sometimes loses it's LP speed for SP. The fact that the record tab is still present is also a sign of cheap manufacturing. Another tape title that I bought from them had it's surface disintegrate as I ran it through my machine. Guess I'll have to look for the GEM SP recording.

history.title: The Angry Red Planet by MGM (Video & DVD)
history.text: Spolier alert! A bit of a plodding science fiction film that is more horror oriented. There is a great deal of time spent in the ground station and on the ship. Some of the male/female interaction is typical of the period. The forays onto Mars are red tinted and solarized, and become irritating after a while. The crew encounter an octopus plant, a spider rodent, and a giant amoeba, all of which are under Martian mind control to test the astronauts and destroy them if possible. They are sent home with a warning not to return to Mars uninvited, as humans are viewed as merely advanced children.

history.title: Dogman
history.text: (Moderate Spoilers) Okay, get a few drinks in you first, and this movie just might be tolerable, the key word being "might" since it never really rises above a TV-movie scale. But I've seen worse movies and worse acting, although I know that's not exactly a glowing movie review. "Hanklin" (Larry Joe Campbell of TV's "According to Jim") and his wife begin to notice strange goings-on around their rural homestead, with similar events simultaneously occurring to his nephew and their small town. Apparently the Indian legend of a "Dogman" (think Bigfoot but with a dog head...and smaller feet, LOL) has awakened in the area, but we find out that it's actually not a male after all (I guess "Dogwoman" didn't sound terrifying enough, LOL). But, make no mistake, she is a meanie! ;) Oh, and if an animal is scratched by it, it may die, but you may live if you're human and only get scratched (not eaten), though it's not really clear, consistent with other vague aspects of the movie. And, ironically enough, the least scary part of the movie is when they show the Dogman itself...well, sort of, since it's hard to see. Maybe the producers should've steered away from ever showing it at all because, in this case, as in most scary legends, imagining it would have been scarier than actually (sort of) seeing it. But preteens may go for it, and at least there's no grisly violence or provocative scenes (just a little cursing), so it fits the bill at least in that way and is otherwise harmless (that's why it earned 2 stars). It must be said, though, that it's very interesting how we have yet to see "Citizen Kane Part II," yet the door is left ajar for a "Dogman" sequel! ;)

history.review_title: Only marginally suspenseful by American-movie standards.
history.text: (Minor Spoilers) With all due respect to our United Kingdom ally and friends, by American-movie standards, this little-known British film about 26 people taken hostage at the Iranian embassy in London in 1980 is marginally suspenseful, at best. There are recurring scenes of commendable English actor Jamie Bell ("Billy Elliott") attempting to lead his SAS (Special Air Service) group of terrorist specialists, on the Queen's direct orders, to aggressively thwart the responsible gunmen, only to be told to keep waiting until the right time. Then, when it's finally time, it's not much more riveting than a made-for-TV movie, though there is also the lovely Australian actress Abbie Cornish (as a BBC reporter who seems to be stationary for the entire movie), who looks like she could be Nicole Kidman's daughter. Only recommended for obsessed Jamie Bell fans (LOL) and/or if you have British ties, but Bell deserves higher-profile roles than this. [Viewer warning: There is more violence than expected, probably the reason for the R rating.]

history.title: Blood Father
history.review_title: All politics aside, Gibson reminds us why we love him as an actor.
history.text: From the get-go, this movie cuts to the chase and wraps it all up in about 90 minutes. Note to Hollywood: That's how it's done! I got things to do! (LOL) Mel Gibson plays "John Link," father of "Lydia," who has made some bad life choices, we'll say, played by the very impressive and able Erin Moriarty (who looks like she could be actress Ellen Page's sister). Lydia may be wanted by underground thugs in the drug trade, led by Diego Luna (practically a veteran Hollywood actor already), and before you can say "Just say no to drugs," Lydia and her Dad (an ex-con himself, interestingly) are on the run. I don't know the details of Gibson's surely regretful words and wrongdoings in the news of late, but the matter at hand here is Gibson's intentions of returning to form as a much loved Hollywood actor. And in that department, Gibson delivers, bolstered by William H Macy and Luna in supporting roles, with the bow on this present being Moriarty. Though not quite as good as Gibson's "Edge of Darkness" (also a father-daughter film), "Blood Father" doesn't disappoint and is highly recommended for Gibson fans and movie fans in general.

history.title: Daybreakers
history.text: I'm not one to go for anything vampire-related like "Daybreakers" (2008) but gave this a shot because of Ethan Hawke, Willem Dafoe, and Sam Neill and was pleasantly surprised (though I'm not sure "pleasantly" is the right word for a horror movie). Vampires have all but taken over the world in the not-too-distant future (2019, believe it or not), but they are running out of fresh human blood, with only a tiny percentage of the world's population remaining who are human. Is there a sufficient substitute for the blood? But, more importantly, is it possible to become human again after you've already gone over to the other side? Though some gore does come with the territory, "Daybreakers" is well paced, intelligent, not overlong (appx 95 minutes), and impressively stylish with just enough scares for a generally entertaining cinematic experience.

history.title: Into the Grizzly Maze
history.review_title: Basically a slasher movie...with the killer on all-fours!
history.text: Getting down to the nitty-gritty, what we basically have here is Jason Voorhees, if you will, reincarnated as a killer grizzly, and it's, without a doubt, beneath Billy Bob Thornton and James Marsden. But, if you go for slasher movies without much imagination, it may be sufficient and tolerable, and the Canadian scenery is actually quite nice, though it's definitely a shame that Oscar-winner Thornton has gone from his "Sling Blade" heights to something inferior like this. Viewer warning: Not for children, with grisly (or perhaps I should say grizzly, get it?) violence and gore.

history.title: Let Me In
history.review_title: Atypical but effective little horror film, set in the 1980s!
history.text: (Minor Spoilers) Here we have a somewhat atypical horror film in that the two main characters are preteens, one a mortal human (Kodi Smit-McPhee) and, oh yeah, the other a vampire (Chloe Grace Moretz), living at the same middle-class apartment complex...in New Mexico! The favorable reviews I've seen are mostly deserving, yet the film wasn't quite as scary as advertised in terms of shocks and suspense, with some predictable elements and the special-effects sequences being noticeably weak. But, interestingly, the viewer gets to see a kinder, gentler side to vampires, to the point where you may find yourself caring or rooting for them. It's not quite "The best American horror film in the last 20 years," like Stephen King apparently said (I actually found "Daybreakers," another vampire flick, at least as compelling, though that's not to mean that I dwell in this genre), but the upper-level acting, the timely anti-bullying message, and the film being set in the 1980s, including the music, were clear-cut positives! Filmed on location in New Mexico.

history.title: McFarland, USA
history.review_title: An undeniable sense of hope prevails!
history.text: Kevin Costner plays Jim White, a teacher and cross-country coach at a mostly Latino high school in McFarland, California, based on a true story and set in the 1987-1988 school year. There is a minor tendency towards schmaltz and over-length (15 to 20 minutes should have been trimmed), as well as some undernourished dialogue, and as in other movies based on true stories, there are the expected tweaks to the Hollywood story line. But what prevails is an undeniable sense of unity, loyalty, brotherhood, and, most of all, hope, sure to be a favorite in the underdog genre and easily living up to Disney studio standards and expectations (in fact, there is an underdog member within the underdog team itself, which I will not give away). And make sure to watch the closing credits all the way through for true-life pictures and accounts.

history.title: 6 Below: Miracle on the Mountain [DVD]
history.review_title: Sorvino and Hartnett hold up their end of a questionably true story.
history.text: (Major Spoiler Alert) Okay, I'm a little torn on this one. When I first saw the cover of the DVD/Blu Ray ad, I thought this movie was about a romantic couple struggling to survive a plane crash in the mountains, not the most original Hollywood plot but still seeming somewhat interesting. Come to find out, former Oscar winner Mira Sorvino plays the mother (yes, mother, not girlfriend or wife) of Josh Hartnett, who plays the role of Eric LeMarque, a real-life former pro hockey player-turned-snowboarder (and meth addict) who gets lost while snowboarding alone in the California mountains. If you can find it in yourself to get past that glaring casting flaw (Sorvino is only 11 years older than Hartnett in real life), then this otherwise lightweight movie (which could have been done for TV) is sufficient entertainment in that Sorvino and Hartnett know their trade and know what to do with their opportunities (though seemingly both have made only rare recent movie appearances). You may also wonder how Eric managed to get so lost when he was so close to a ski resort, but apparently meth (or his withdrawal from it) clouded his judgment. Just think of the film as similar to having a main course at dinner without any sides; it will suffice, but you may be looking around for the dessert tray. Then again, purportedly, both the movie and book (which I admittedly have not read) aren't true to the real-life story because apparently it was the stepmother, not mother, who instigated a search for Eric. Moreover, it's alleged that Eric was ultimately not exactly husband of the year post his ordeal, with his wife filing for divorce at the time of this writing with many (unproven) accusations. While those circumstances are, of course, out of the hands of Sorvino and Hartnett, therein lies my dilemma: If you know the truth beforehand, do you root for someone to survive who you know may ultimately become an abusive person later in life?

history.title: Something Borrowed
history.review_title: Not just another rom-com; it's well-produced and quite satisfying.
history.text: (Minor Spoilers) At the outset, when you realize that there may be some indiscretion and backstabbing going on between best friends as the premise, you may be inclined to skip this one. Resist that inclination, as I also fought to like this film, probably for that reason (as well as it seeming just like another rom-com). But, discrete from the book (which I admittedly have not read), this film will likely incrementally pull you in. "Rachel" (Giniffer Goodwin) and ""Darcy" (Kate Hudson) are the aforementioned best friends, and "Dex" (Colin Egglesfield) is the man who may break their seemingly unbreakable bond. Even the soundtrack and supporting cast (John Krasinki of TV's "The Office," as "Ethan" here, and Steve Howey of TV's "Reba," as "Marcus" here) fulfill expectations, and the ending may surprise you, though the door is actually left ajar for a sequel (since the novel apparently has a sequel). All in all, it's a well-produced and quite satisfying film, thanks to a very capable and good-looking cast and conscientious script. (Then again, it may be a tad awkward to watch this with your best friend if your spouses are also in the room, and maybe I liked it more just because I'm single and saw it alone, LOL).

history.title: Lucky One, The (DVD)
history.review_title: Mostly pleasant...but in a Big-Pharma-commercial kind of way.
history.text: (Minor Spoilers) To call a spade a spade, this otherwise well-shot and well-acted film is undeniably a consummate chick flick, no? ;) "Logan" (Zac Efron) returns to the States from his third Tour of Duty with the picture of a woman ("Beth," Taylor Schilling) he doesn't even know that was dropped by a fallen soldier, and he makes it his mission to find her and thank her because, according to him, she's the reason he finished his Tour. There's an unexpected war connection with that picture and that mystery woman (which I won't give away) that goes hand-in-hand with an expected simultaneous romantic connection on his return, all while Schilling and Efron seem to vie for who's the prettiest (and it's a tough call, LOL). And the film has more than its share of seemingly overly sentimental scenes (i.e., the church and tree house scenes), but its merits dwell in Efron, Schilling, and Blythe Danner (Gwenyth Paltrow's real-life mother), who make it all mostly gratifying, though it's in a Big-Pharma-commercial kind of way.

history.title: Hamish Macbeth - Series One
history.text: I am a big fan of the Hamish Macbeth murder mysteries and was expecting something even a little like the books. One of MC Beaton's books has a character who is a murder mystery writer very disappointed with the filming of her works. I wonder if this is where she got the idea.

history.title: Dumbo
history.text: When I tried to play this DVD on my bluray machine it says "DuD" When I tried to play on another combo DVD/VHS machine it says "Incorrect Disc" When I play it on anohter combo DVD/VHS machine it plays. This should play on all machines. It says it is "enhanced" so you would think it would play on my newest machine and not on the oldest.

history.title: Androcles And The Lion [DVD]
history.text: I always loved this film. I do wonder though why one of the most profound of Shaw's lines was cut from this film. The centurion tells Livinia that her death will mean nothing. She answers "then, why kill me". Not in the film.

history.title: Friendly Persuasion (DVD)
history.text: This could have been a good movie with a message. But as remarked on by other reviewers it was too slow And IT DROVE ME CRAZY that the producers and director didn't know, or care to know, the correct usage of "thou" and "thee". Thou is the nominative. Thee is the objective as anyone with even a passing knowledge of the KJB would know. there is no excuse for being this sloppy. Almost as bad as Amazon with their listing of languages on certain movies: The Pathfinder (in Saami, Amazon says Norwegian); Repentance (in Georgian, Amazon says Russian); The Cuckoo (in Finnish, Saami and Russian; Amazon says only Russian).

history.title: The Big Bang Theory: The Complete Fifth Season (Blu-ray+DVD+Ultraviolet Digital Copy)
history.text: The blu ray version is not user friendly. You cannot go to the menu by pressing the menu key. At least, unlike the DVD versions, the no subtitle is the default, selection of the episode you want is very frustrating. To stop an episode and go on you have to shut it off, reload and then go back to the main selections. I still can't figure out how to get to any selection other than the first.

history.title: Birdman
history.text: How did this get chosen as the best picture? Probably because it is a film about actors. Michael Keaton pulled off a great job in a role outside his comfort zone but other than that it is disjointed, incomprehensible, and unpleasant. You have to wonder about the Academy and its choices. Like in 2012 another year of unfathomable selections.

history.title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
history.text: Disjointed, silly and hard to follow. Once again, how did this win all those oscars? My wife (a member of SAG) and I had trouble even watching this to the end.

history.title: ESPN Films 30 for 30: I Hate Christian Laettner
history.text: Having attended Duke and having a daughter who had a crush on Christian Laettner,I found this documentary to be very well made and brought back many memories for me. I remember that within seconds of what is still remembered as "the shot" I had a phone call from a Russian friend and basketball fan who had been watching the game. The film shows how inaccurate prejudices creep into our thinking. For one, the idea of Duke students all being posh spoiled kids. Neither of my parents graduated from high school and my father was blue collar. I had to work and borrow to go to Duke. Two things were left out that should have been in the program. One, when Laettner went off to the Olympics, he was short one hour for graduation. Coach K told him if it wasn't made up by the beginning of the next school year, his jersey would come down and the NCAA banner would come down. Also the story of Bill McCafferty is left out. One of the highest scoring shooting guards at Duke he could not take Laettner's bullying and transferred to Vanderbilt. This should have been covered.

history.title: Resistance
history.review_title: I enjoyed the movie very much except for the horrible direction
history.text: I enjoyed the movie very much except for the horrible direction. I hope Mr. Gupta will not direct any more. His pregnant pauses in the movie really seemed like a full nine months. But I had read the book so could follow the plot though more should have been invested in the symbiosis between the German soldiers and Welsh women (take time from the long, long pauses). We did a showing for our Welsh society and no one who had not read the book could follow it. My wife, a member of the Screen Actors' Guild (and a big fan of Owen Sheers) could not stand it. I guess you chalk part of it up to the low budget.

history.title: Silence
history.review_title: Watched this on an Air France flight from Washington. ...
history.text: Watched this on an Air France flight from Washington. I had not known about the historical case and was very surprised at the ending. Historically it did hit me that these events are taking place in 1640. The priests are shocked by burning people alive, torture for the faith and the inquisitor when they get to Japan. And pray tell who was burning people alive and torturing them for their faith in 1640? Who were the inquisitors then? The view of the priests that only they have the answers when they don't know squat about Japan, the people or their language is reminiscent of the views of the Jesuit in "The Black Robe".
Crappy script, If this was comic relief I'd rather put my finger down my throat and cause me to puke.

If the Yurt stands up to 75 mph winds wonder what a circular home would do in a hurricane. You'd have to really trust your neighbors to live and leave that home but for a camp set up for say the summer it be cool and the show is well produced. Look forward to watching more. Of course Mililani was my home for 6 years it's fun to see how the islands are developed... Like to see more tropic and tents than stone city, Honolulu.

Being former active Navy and owner of many GSD's I can relate to the movie that a civilian can't. We use to tease the Air Force at Clark AFB about how bad their training was with their dogs. The drug dogs hit on hot tennis balls, food, and everything else but what it was trained to do. The Air Force zoomies really didn't know how to train back then. Having trained many myself, you have to be connected to the animal to sense what it thinks. The training now a day is much better, but then war always brings out the best in a handler and dog. Excellent film.

history.title: The Legend of Hercules
history.review_title: I grew up with all the tv Hercules movies, this one is pretty good.
history.text: I heard people say it wasn't very good. It's a mythological character and the film is pretty good. Not the best but I thoroughly enjoy it as another mythological movie and I loved the action.

Now this is the side of dracula that makes you cheer for him. A great love story and if the story of the Turks is true than I can see it happening of why he was called Vlad the Impaler. But then none of us lived back then. Most drac movies want to scare the stew out of the audience. This one shows you strength, vulnerability, respect for God and I'd love to see a sequel. Excellent casting, excellent story line. I don't care for scary movies and this one was a man trying to save his family and people. Makes you think, did we over blow the history books about the real dracula?

history.review_title: eye opening experience to the way the Garden of Eden was and can be in our lives
history.text: I have not read the book but the movie portrayed an eye opening experience to the way the Garden of Eden was and the peace we once had. The answer to many questions is filled with how well this movie was done. history.title: Foundations of Western Civilization II: A History of the Modern Western World
history.review_title: Pleasant ride through the centuries... with a disgraceful fall at the end
history.text: Let me start by saying that I really appreciate Prof. Bucholz presentation style and knowledge, which are really put to the test in a long, complex course like this one. He manages to keep you interest alive in this long ride along the centuries without ever coming out as pedantic or monotonous.. which is quite a feat for a history professor :) His pragmatic, "typical american", no nonsense approach to the subject is always interesting and pleasant, and a great consolation for those of us who had the misfortune of suffering only boring and insignificant lecturers in our history hours at school. Your knowledge , culture and "peripheral vision" will come out of this course very well enhanced,both on the historical fact and on what can be learned from them.. So why only 3 star in my review? Well.. I have been forced to realize that prof. Bucholz as a (unfortunately classic....) good and loyal american citizen grows exponentially biased as his historical ride through the centuries nears contemporary times..The first symptoms appear in his discussion of world war I, when he blissfully ignores the consequences and responsibilities of the US financial speculations on the war, and from then on it just goes downhill.. When treating the end of world war II prof Bucholz has the stomach of calling the crime against humanity of using the atomic bomb on Hiroshima and Nagasaki "a controversial moral choice".... Controversial????? CONTROVERSIAL???? And to add insult to injury he manages to say: "I am not a sufficient expert to sove the controversy for you.. it would take a theologian or a philosopher to weight the balance here" No, prof. Bucholz, it would not take a theologian or philosopher, an historian would actually do fine, but a professor who is more committed to professing the truth than afraid of jeopardizing his privileges , rich salary and consideration from the establishment... Needless to say, no more than a couple of words are spent on american imperialistic policy, the horros,abuse and exploitment brought by unregulated capitalism ad finally the "preemptive strike" on Iraq. Before the course is over he manages to dedicate just less than a minute to the phenomenon of islamic terrorism, attributing it to the "mainstream fable" of a vague contempt for decadent moral habits and "reasons which are well beyond the scope of this lecture". Again, no, the are not..they are actually at the heart of the scope of that lecture and of a course on western civilization... Beyond the scope of what I dare say would have been more honest, prof. Bucholz...

history.title: The Great Courses: Oceanography: Exploring Earth's Final Wilderness
history.text: This is one of the most enjoyable TTC video series: the subject is fascinating and gets little attention in a non specialistic education. Prof Tobin is very pleasant to listen to, and quite gifted to guide the student through such an ocean of topics without resulting boring but with a calm, relaxed pace. It is true as the ocean is the less explored part of the planet , oceanography is the less known subject to the general public. To give you an idea of the enormous vastness of the material covered I have to cite the table of contents: Explorers and Navigation Mapping the Sea Habitats, Sunlit Shelves and the Dark Abyss The Spreading Sea Floor and Mid-Ocean Ridges The Plunging Sea Floor and Deep-Sea Trenches The Formation of the Earth and Its Ocean Marine Sediments - Archives of the Ocean Offshore Oil and Gas -Resources and Risks The Enduring Chemistry of Seawater How the Physics of Water Controls the Ocean Waves - Motion in the Ocean Rogue Waves and Tsunami Tides in Theory and Practice Marine Life, Energy, and Food Webs Tiny Plankton--The Most Abundant Life on Earth Soft-Bodied Life in the Dark, Open Depths Swimming - The Many Fish in the Sea Marine Birds, Reptiles, and Mammals Whaling, Fisheries, and Farming the Ocean Where Sea Meets the Land and Why Coasts Vary Where Rivers Meet the Sea - Estuaries and Deltas Coastal Erosion - Beaches and Sea Cliffs Tidal Life, Sea Forests, and Coral Reefs Deep Bottom Life and Hydrothermal Vents Trade Winds -The Circulation of Heat and Wind Heavy Weather - Storms and Hurricanes The Gulf Stream to Gyres - Vast Surface Currents Upwelling, Downwelling, and El Niño The Deepest, Slowest River - Polar Bottom Water The Ocean and Global Climate The Warming, Rising Sea Marine Pollution - The Impact of Toxins The Future Ocean Isn't that a true ocean of fascinating material? :) It's sad that so little of this fascinating material is taught at the high school level... Anyhow.. prof Tobin does a great job of navigating through all these subjects, but he cannot be a marine geologist, marine biologist, physical climatologist and meteorologist at the same time.. I think this video series would have been better taught by a team of authors, say a marine geophysicist like Tobin, a marine biologist and a climatologist. These would make the presentation more engaging, varied, deeper and would remove some defects like the annoying lack of environmental concern in such a crucially "environmental subject". It 's quite shocking for me to see an "oceanographer" treat natural disaster like the Deepwater Horizon oil spill so lightly, and continually gloss over the criminal and autodestructive nature of overfishing , global warming and pollution of the ocean...or coming out with demented lines like "whales should be very grateful to the oil drilling industry because without petrol they would have been probably all hunted down for their oil" ....until you realize that prof Tobin is mainly a geologist, who goes himself drilling around in the ocean, and gets it kick from plate boundaries, earhquakes and seismic waves..and beig a "loyal citizen" of a nation owned by oil drillers is probably not fully capable of grasping and appreciating the beauty and fundamental importance of life in the ocean.. And I think it is the responsibility of the teachers of courses like this, addressed to the general public, to enable a clear understanding of the criminal nature of the acts of their political leaders when these "leaders" are refusing to partecipate in binding agreement on greenhouse gas emissions reduction in order to continue to speculate with their business (Bush, anyone?). There's a reason why the ozone layer hole is being fixed, why nobody seems to care about global warming: the small percentage of people who owns much of the world resources and money can easily survive the consequences of global warming, maybe even speculate on them, while ultraviolet radiation and cancer and not discriminate on the basis of income ... An oceanography class that fails to address these concerns is a missed occasion, not to mention the myriad of other improvement that could have been brought with the contribution of a professional marine biologist and a climatologist...
