history.text: Most TV shows have 1 good episode in them, some have 1 good season before it all goes to pieces in very predictable ways, and then there are shows that survive for quite a while against all odds - such as Charmed. How this show managed 8 seasons, I'll never know, guess they successfully tapped into the Witchcraft/Wicca craze of the late 90s/early 00s, despite the fact that the show has basically nothing whatsoever to do with either Witchcraft or Wicca, never mind real Paganism. I don't know about you, but if some 'prophecy' or family legacy tells me one fine day that I'm a witch, the first thing I would do is read that Book of Shadows front to back, back to front, over and over again, until I know the bleedin' thing by heart. Which is not what the sisters Halliwell do, they'd rather be put on the spot each and every time some new demon or warlock or grimlock or whatever comes to kill them for their newly acquired powers, rushing to the Book for help only at the last possible second. I suppose the script writers (.....) thought that makes for 'good TV'...... Aside from the fake witchy stuff, you get the usual; soap opera-esque parade of hawt guys who would willingly die for the girls 5 minutes after meeting them - they are just that special..... The cat (Kit ? original...) is also severely underutilized, refer to the script writer comment,. above. Alyssa Milano did make one very sexy witch, so it's not a total loss.

history.title: Sabrina, The Teenage Witch: Season 1
history.review_title: This could have been a really good show
history.text: Perfect example of a great concept ruined by Hollywoodism. The movie that came before the series was a fairly lame and very typical 'Cinderella' story type thing with a little bit of magic thrown in as a gimmick, the TV series was actually a little bit livelier than the movie, but so 'schlocky' and 'schticky', it's actually a little hard to watch, or, more precisely, hard to listen to. Which isn't the fault of the actors, they do a fine job (for the most part), the blame lies squarely with the script writers. Supposedly, a reboot of the movie is in the works, but I fear they'll screw that up, too, and in the usual, very predictable ways.

history.title: The Worst Witch [Import anglais]
history.review_title: Age groups up to 10 might like this
history.text: Kids' movie from the 80s, which quite obviously had a major impact on the imagery in Harry Potter. Very cheesy and embarrassing in parts - I'm sure Tim Curry and Diana Rigg would rather forget this episode of their careers - but ok for children.

history.title: Krampus [DVD]
history.text: Most movies about the holiday our badly misled world knows as 'Christmas' revolve around money - and how it makes everything all right in the end. Very, very rarely do we get a cinematic glimpse into the TRUE folklore origins of Winter Solstice celebrations, and when we do, it's usually been twisted and falsified in the usual movie ways. Krampus isn't entirely free of the latter, but it does have some good moments, especially those with Austrian stage actress Krista Stadler, who plays Omi (grandma), she's decidedly the star of the show. It's ot a great movie, but it is unique and entertaining enough to earn a spot on the December rotation. For those interested in the background, I suggest looking into the Norse God Thor and his goat-drawn chariot (which makes the thunder), the Scandinavian Julebock (Yule Goat) who accompanies Juletomten (the Yule Dwarf)....starting to sound familiar?....good.....you're on the way. Btw, in German-speaking Alpine regions - Krampus country - he appears on December 5th, usually with a rod made from branches (to punish the bad children) and a jute sack full of dried figs, dates, plums and nuts to give to those who were good.

history.title: Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Super Shredder
history.text: After going through a bit of a rough patch 'Earth's Last Stand' got the series back on track, and this 2-disc set does not disappoint. Some of the episodes get pretty intense.

targets.title: Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Final Chapters
King of the Hill - The Complete Second Season

history.text: The Found footage sub-genre of horror movies was striking at first when the Blair Witch producers really promoted it in the right way and even created a buzz with faux tie-in documentary. The Paranormal Activity series provided more laughs than scares, but given that I'd offer up more stars for them than this, in fact, I didn't mind a trip to the theater for P.A.3, provided I had cohorts on hand to riff it with me. But, Apartment 143, lacks even those fleeting opportunities for enjoyment. I'm an open-minded fan of bad movies, but this mercifully short (1hr 20min) hand-held visitation with attractive but unlikable parapsychologists on a case is pretty lacking. By 2012, filmmakers should have thought longer about making another haunted apartment release with a widower dad, a cute kid, dog and angry foul-mouth teen girl. I watched free with my Prime membership but I'd have been pusses if is been charged $4 for a rental....Who ya gonna call? ... Someone else!

history.title: Untamed Youth
history.review_title: Cat fights, cotton pickin and surprisingly great acoustics for a farm
history.text: Another cautionary tale about hitchhiking and cotton empires. A pair Hitchhiking hotties take farm life gig over serving 30 days of jail. There they encounter Pinky, an erudite talent scout/dishwasher and work for the original monopoly hoarding Mr Trump. Inspire of the backbreaking field work the titular untamed youth still have time for jitterbugging and several impromptu jive numbers that may lead them to fame in the city. Okay, It's no Manos but this delightfully bad teen exploitation fare can make a fair drinking game film if you drink each time "cotton picking" is said or someone is called a square.

history.title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, Ultimate Edition
history.review_title: Dug the film but could not get Ultimate BluRay to play on XBox
history.text: I dug the movie, even with Snyder's (consistently) darker look at superhero genre than the MCU. I loved Ben's Batman; he looked liked he'd come right off the page of a Frank Miller graphic novel. His Bruce Wayne was pretty on point too, he felt more cohesive than he'd been in Nolan's take on the character. I was not thrilled with the take on Lex Luthor, nor was I ecstatic about his baffling scheme. But ultimately what is worth the price of admission (or this set) is the 20 or so minutes including Wonder Woman, Gal Gagot is simply perfection and this appearance has me unbelievably stoked for the solo film for June 2, 2017

history.review_title: Terrific! Amazon please make this available for purchase!
history.text: Please make this available for purchase! A brilliant tv adaptation of DC VERTIGO classic! Sadly NBC never give a it a proper shot but John made return in an Arrow crossover ep last season, it should have been on CW to start anyway... But why not use some of those original tv/movie bucks Amazon and bring us season 2, please.

"Must maintain finesse." The Tick returns in all his empty-headed glory! ...It's hard to top the cartoon and live-action series based on the Tick comics because they hit the mark on so many levels; but Amazon Studios has hit the right tone with the pilot ep., I hope we get more of these ASAP

history.title: Batman: Return of the Caped Crusaders [Blu-ray]
history.text: Adam West, Burt Ward and Julie Newmar return to the 1966 Batverse in this epic animated feature! Not only does it tribute all the camp of the 60's series but it's full of tongue-in-cheek humor too. A super villain team up ends up with a batty rocket to space, multiple bad-Batmen and even a Robin/Catwoman team-up! This is a must have for any Bat-fan. Good news they've already green lighted follow up to this featuring Shatner as Two-Face.

history.title: Daredevil: The Complete First Season
history.review_title: Perfect take on the "Man Without Fear"
history.text: Amazingly good series (season 2 just as outstanding), on screen translation of some Frank Miller's work on the character. Although clearly set in the MCU it is a very different style and intensity Than anything Marvel as done on screen before. The violence is glorious and the portrayals next level good. Ronnie Cox is terrific and Blind Lawyer by night/ Vigilante by night & Vinnent D'Onofrio is phenomenon as Fisk, one of the best Marvel villain portrayals to date (at least until David Tennant's turn on season one of Jessica Jones!)

history.review_title: Rifftrax vs Shatner vs Spiders FTW
history.text: Thank Amazon for returning this to streaming (and making it part of Prime Member free movies). I remember watching this TV movie as a kid because Capt Kirk was in it (my excuse for TJ Hooker viewing too), but this is infinitely more fun to watch with Mike, Bill and Kevin there with hilarious comments and zingers. The Boys are sharper than ever and (dare I say) even funnier than their Mystery Science Theater 3000 days. Shatner is a country vet along with a pretty "expert" figuring out why animals are mysteriously expiring, did I mention there is a giant unconnected hill full of spiders?

history.title: RiffTrax Live: MST3K Reunion
history.text: Must have for all MSTies! Buy this NOW (Unless you already own it on your RIFFTRAX.com account for streaming). Lots of SHORTS, lots of MST3K former cast members return for this RIFF-a-POLZA, including Rifftrax refs: Mike Nelson (the old new guy), Kevin Murphy (Tom & Professor Bobo), Bill Corbett as (Crow2 & Brain Guy), Bridget Nelson (Wife & MST3K alum) and Mary Jo Pehl (Pearl), the Old Guy Joel Hodgson (TVs Joel), Frank Coniff (TVs FRANK), Trace Beaulieu (Dr F & original CROW T ROBOT) and even the new new guy Jonah Ray from upcoming NETFLIX MST3Krevival Lots of fun, sadly no puppet sketches but all the great voice over Riffs of shorts, PSAs and Terrifying anthropomorphic automotive life lessons, especially Bridget & MJ's "A Word to the.Wives" hilarious 50's gender role propaganda. Filmed live in Minneapolis' own State Theater June 28th this is the least awful thing to happen in 2016!

history.review_title: Easily the best of the franchise, possibly best of the genre
history.text: Saw it twice in the theater! A journey of 17 years comes to a powerful close through "Logan." Loosely drawn from Graphic novel "Old Man Logan" this finally ends the tale of two characters introduced to FOX's X-universe in 2000. So rarely does an audience have such an investment in characters outside of a tv series. But Wolverine and Prof X are like family in what is a third act and possibly a new beginning. Logan long life is nearing its end, not before he has one final fight. He has strayed from the samurai path he was on when we last saw him in The Wolverine (same director). He and the Prof fall in with a mutant child (and one of my favorite characters of recent X-history) and a wacky road trip ensues filled with cyborg mercy and an Oscar-worthy performance for Sir Patrick. Thanks to Deadpool, this was conceived as a Rated R project, which meant a pay cut for Jackman, a budget cut over all that give the film a raw indy pic feel, but more importantly it allows Logan to snikt his way through the baddies in a manner truer to the graphic novels than ever before! Powerful! Intense and brilliant must see!

history.title: The Aztec Mummy Collection [DVD]
history.text: Good, not great image quality. Some of it looks pretty smeary. It would be nice if somebody found the negatives and made better prints, because these are fun pics to watch.

history.title: Berberian Sound Studio
history.text: You should know that this film is anti-horror film. It is explicit in the dialogue from the male characters (who are all jerks), and if you doubt it you can find more proof in the extras, where the production team basically say that horror films are about taking pleasure in the misery of others, specifically women. I doubt you could find many horror fans who would assert that these films advocate violence against women. Violence is the horror film's subject, not its argument. Here the main character is driven mad by giving voice to the cruelty in a film about witchcraft - a ridiculous premise, as is the idea that a tech would be imported to work on a film he doesn't want to work on. The most pointlessly sadistic scare films usually aim at the lowest common denominator - cheap thrills - and fall off the radar, since even 'monster movie' fans can spot junk. An argument could be made that sadism is connected to the field of horror, but you won't find it here. This film just states that men who make horror films hate women, and brings down the curtain. But they want to celebrate the pretty ladies and cool fashions of the '70s 'giallo' at the same time. Better make up your mind if you love or hate these films next time. This is a film about horror films by people who don't understand horror films.

history.title: Chernobyl Diaries (DVD )
history.text: I'm suprised by the negative comments about this film. It avoids a lot of the mistakes others make. It's just a solid creepy film set in a unique location. It doesn't deliver over the top 'set pieces' like a Hollywood mega-production, but it's very watchable. I suggest watching it straight through, the pace with TV commercials would be too slow. Best of all, no crummy CGI effects to ruin the mood. And the handheld camera isn't utterly obnoxious for once. It's probably worth a watch, and I think its reputation will improve with time.

history.title: See No Evil 2 [Blu-ray + Digital HD]
history.text: If you wished Halloween 2 had come out just a little better (the sequel to Carpenter, not Zombie), your prayer has been answered. But there is still too little context to make this more than a hunt in the dark. Where is the meditation on the nature of evil? Where the blackly comic statement on the cruelty of fate? Where the O. Henry zinger to make it all "deep" and meaningful? It isn't there - but as it is, it's still a decent viewing experience. I have nothing against a walk through a haunted house, and this is a pretty good one. But it would also be nice if Horror could take credit for delivering some of the higher quality cultural flotsam in our day to day jetsam once in a while.

history.title: Shock Waves [Blu-ray]
history.text: Not terribly scary, this is still a watchable film. The blu-ray shows the 16mm film stock's grain pretty plainly in some shots, but it looks alright. This may be the most bloodless horror film ever. Nice ultra minimal synth score too. They should've written Cushing a grand little speech - he's almost wasted here. The extra interviews are good, maybe an hour of content. And Ms. Adams has three things to do: wear bikini; scream; run. All in all a nice package, but tame and predictable story, and an absolute minimum OF story, will keep this from your top ten list. Especially when the tagline could be "you'll never go in the ankle-deep water again..." For reanimated-fascist completists only.

history.title: Godzilla vs. Biollante (Blu-ray + DVD)
history.text: I'm pretty sure this is not a proper transfer from the original negative, or even a good scan of a print. It looks like they took the same materials used to make a dvd and just put it on a blu-ray. There is normally an obvious improvement in picture sharpness, and I don't see it here. I got the version with the two additional films - I don't know if the other blu-ray released by Lions Gate looks the same. I would suggest not buying this version and looking for an authentic blu-ray version.

history.title: I Bury the Living [Blu-ray]
history.text: I urge you to see before you buy - this is one of the dullest, worst films I know. Watch "Macabre" by William Castle instead - possibly his best film, a nasty piece of business about a child buried alive, and an underrated film for sure. I can't think of any reason this junk is coming to blu-ray...

history.title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, Ultimate Edition
history.text: After Sucker Punch, I was worried this would look over-processed and be another guilty pleasure at best. But I'd have to say this is not bad at all. Few of the Batman and Superman films have gotten it right, with Batman (and his Tankmobile) becoming more Iron Man-like all the time, and Superman having the usual problem of being too powerful for any but the most absurd enemies. This film takes an unlikely premise and makes it work pretty well. Also, it looks great. Thank your lucky stars that it isn't another stale origin story either! True, it's a bit dark thematically, but you can blame the comics for that - they started this fad for killing off Superman...

history.title: Crypt Of The Vampire
history.text: This is an above average gothic horror from the sixties, very similar to the sort of thing Barbara Steele did so often. Ignore the people who say it lacks atmosphere, they apparently didn't watch it. The film only hints at vampirism, however. One scene is really quite intense - taking into account the passage of time. I was very happy to find this obscure gem. It should be restored (along with The Blancheville Monster). See it.

history.title: Rammbock: Berlin Undead (Bloody Disgusting Selects)
history.text: Many horror films treat characters as an afterthought. This film is the exception. Very intelligent script, good characters. Some nice scary bits. This is not a film to pass because it was made in German with a smaller budget. See it if you like very good horror with some touches of comedy and pathos. Can't guarantee you will like the ending - these zombie things often end on a dark note - but this film will gain a following, mark my words.

targets.title: Pirates Of The Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales
Texas Chainsaw [3D Blu-ray + Blu-ray + Digital Copy]

history.review_title: A Compassionate and Complexly Real Film
history.text: Superb, complex, moving, compelling, and utterly convincing, this movie is one of the best films of the last year or so. The dialogue is keen-eared and sharp, the acting wonderfully accomplished by every person on screen, even by the minor characters who may appear in only one scene, the story rightly troubling, disturbing (as it must be), and deeply touching. This is a film that restores humanity and a profound, searching, observant realism to American movie making, similar in this sense, say, to Moonlight or Manchester by the Sea. It is of similar caliber and importance. It is a finely written and filmed and emotionally significant movie that deserves to be seen, no, should be seen by anyone who cares about compassion in a world which too often denies it.

history.review_title: Beautifully filmed, with a surrealistic look to it
history.text: Beautifully filmed, with a surrealistic look to it, dream-like and harshly garish, Bangkok Love Story is unremittingly, coldly violent and no love story save of the most brutal, death-obsessed, cruel kind, cruel both to its characters and to its audience. Much of the cinematography is haunting. Some, formalists say, might praise it for that alone. But its characters' motivations and actions rarely make much sense, certainly no consistent one. They are more like cinematic imitations, not based on life but figures taken, or stolen, from other films. Like them, the movie itself is painfully false, like a gay-themed, hyped up, ludicrously even more excessive Tarantino.

history.title: War & Peace
history.review_title: A dull, badly acted, and embarrassing mimicry of Tolstoy.s novel.
history.text: Though much briefer and far more of a condensation of the novel, the 2015 production with Paul Dano as Pierre is far superior to this 1972 BBC series from 1972. The earlier series brings to the screen far more of Tolstoy's novel, but the acting in it, by everyone in the cast from the most to the least significant character is excruciatingly amateurish and stiff. It is nearly painful to watch it. For all the consequences, narratively and psychologically, that befall a filmed so extremely condensed as the later one, it nonetheless contains far more of Tolstoy's spirit and essence simply because the characters are far more completely and complexly realized. The 1972 version is bad realization of the novel because it is so weakly, unconvincingly done, surprisingly so for a BBC production. The woman playing Natasha, for example, made me wince at her overacting and excesses, like a school girl acting for the first time in her life in a school play. Much of this film is like that: a lot of money spent on equipment and almost no thought going into the direction. The end result is that it turns one of the great novels of Western history into a dull and embarrassing mimicry of the real thing.

Franco's film version of Faulkner's As I Lay Dying was extraordinary for the ways in which its transfer from the page to the screen was handled. It was both respectful and innovative, creating a work of art inspired by but separate from the novel which was its source. The novel's images and story were metamorphically altered in the movie so that faithfulness was observed through transposition, not precise fidelity. It was in many ways an original work, if also obviously deeply dependent upon Faulkner throughout. The Sound and the Fury, however, is a novel even more resistant to filming. This time, though honorable, the movie fails. It is neither sufficiently faithful to the novel nor original enough to separate itself aesthetically from it. There are many problems. The most obvious one is the representation of the Compson mansion. When Dilsey speaks her famous lines, I have seen the beginning and I have seen the end, the mansion stands before us in all its stately splendor, nothing fallen or desolate about it. There is no sermon by the Reverend Shegog, a fundamental, even essential part of the novel. There is no turning of horse and carriage the wrong way around Jefferson's square. In fact, the square never appears. There's no Mottstown for Jason to race to to try to catch his niece and the man with the red tie. And so forth. Too much of the novel's fourth section has been omitted, both incidental and crucial, for the equivalent portion of the movie to succeed on any terms. The same is true in the Quentin section, though in some ways this middle section of the film is the best part of it, preserving as it does much of Jason Compson's, the father's speeches to his son, the epitome of romantic despair and ruination, undoubtedly contributory to his eldest son's death. But who would know, without having read the novel, why Quentin is with the little Italian girl? (He wants to protect her as he did Caddy, calling her "little sister.") Shreve, Quentin's roommate at Harvard, is in one brief scene. His absence, and that of Quentin's other friends at Harvard, eliminates a complexity in Quentin himself, one having to do with the confusion of eroticism and honor. The list could be endless. Yes, any adaptation has to cut, excise, eliminate. But the episode with the little girl isn't the only instance where, in the movie, that cutting results in a muddle. The most deplorable part of the movie, however, is Franco's own performance. I say that sadly, because I respect both his ambition and talent, at least during those times when he chooses to exhibit both. But his performance as Benjy is both self-indulgent and grotesque, hammy in the worst sort of ways (is there a good way to be hammy?). Not only is his acting self-indulgent, but Franco also films himself self-indulgently as well. Some of this might be owing to a need to save money, like many films made with a lot of close-ups. Yet every time Benjy is onscreen, I wince. Franco plays the role like a man making fun of a Benjy in order to elicit laughter. I don't mean he has done so deliberately. Far from it. But that is the consequence of a performance so lacking in subtlety. Even Benjy's more "lyrical" moments in his inner monologue in the novel are erased, just one of them preserved and often repeated. Since Benjy dominates the first section of the film and is frequently present in the third, if less so in the second, Franco's one-note bad acting by itself defeats the film. His casting of Seth Rogen in the small role of a telegraph operator, by the way, smacks of the same sort of narcissism, not a good trait in an actor. Nonetheless, I think those who know the novel might want to take a look, just for curiosity's sake. Certainly it is far, far superior to the crass, absurd, utterly unfaithful film produced by Jerry Wald and directed by Martin Ritt. (To see how bad movies could be in the '50's, take a look; to read how bad film criticism could be in 1959, consult Bosley Crowther's review of it in The New York Times, available online.) It is, as I have suggested, an honorable failure in many respects, but fail it does, despite moments in it where one can catch a glimpse of what might have been a far better film if only it had been more thoughtful, more observant, more careful with detail and substantive accuracy, and, if not more respectful to its source in the usual sense, more truly original and risk-taking, like Franco's As I Lay Dying, for an example. Otherwise, anyone attempting to film The Sound and the Fury, a work of serious literature if there ever was one, is doomed to failure.

history.title: Ararat [DVD]
history.text: Arafat changes historical horror into pretentious melodrama. The basic conceit of the film is that of a film about the Armenian genocide, directed by a man played in the movie by Charles Aznavour in the only plausible performance in it, within a film about the Armenian genocide. That conceit is supposed to make one think about the relationship of art to historical truth. It does no such thing. To that complexity is added, among other excesses, a love affair between a young man and his step sister who is also a drug dealer and more than a little crazed about her father's death which she blames on the young man's mother, a purported art historian and expert on Arshile Gorky who does not seem to know much about the complex reasons for Gorky suicide and blames it solely on what he witnessed in 1915. (Gorky was ill and poor and his studio with many of his paintings in it had burned down shortly before he hanged himself. By the way the scenes in which the young girl appears, full of rage and excoriating the mother, are wince-inducing.) A father, who is also a custom's inspector, implausibly played by Christopher Plummer, who is deeply uncomfortable, it seems, with his son's homosexuality. That son, who is as implausibly a guard at a museum which is showing the Gorky painting of himself and his mother (a key image in the movie) and prevents the young girl from slashing it with a pocket knife. His lover, who is half Turkish, playing a Turk in great part among those responsible for the genocide who, in his, the actor's, real life, expresses the Turkish justification for what the Turks refuse to acknowledge as a genocide. (That line between life and art, history and its portrayal, is blurry, you see.) I could go on. The movie piles one plot device upon another all in search of some deep meanings which get more and more muddled as the movie progresses. Arafat has so many themes running through it that the important one often gets lost in the thematic mayhem. There's something despicable about this film. The same sort of overbearing pretentiousness and ethical confusions undermined The Sweet Hereafter as well. One of the many problems in Arafat is the way it uses people either to give lectures on the genocide that don't sound at all like dialogue or to turn them into allegorical figures, as the movie itself abuses Arshile Gorky by turning him into an image (as well as an image maker) it uses to make points. That is, it disregards any sense of characters and how they might in certain circumstances actually behave in order to lecture its audience. In this way, reality in the film is continually cheapened, including the genocide itself. The film pays at lot more attention to itself than it does to the genocide and is in this sense appallingly self-serving. It also often makes little or no sense. I don't want to spoil the plot too much. But one does wonder how the young man with his films cans full of heroin ever made it through Turkish customs which are famously careful to such abuses. And one also wonders how the custom's inspector, before his unbelievable reconciliation scene with his son at the film's conclusion, was able to dispose of so much dope without its and his being discovered. This is a movie, though, that despite all its pretenses toward profound thoughts cannot bear much scrutiny. The more complex it becomes the more absurd it is. That is more than too bad. The Armenian genocide of 1915 happened. It is one of the great horrors of the last century. But, like the Shoah, it must be thought about in art with great tact and sensitivity. Perhaps, as some would claim about the Shoah, it is too terrible for art. Perhaps. But certainly a self-regarding, self-important, and preposterous film like Arafat is a betrayal of it.

history.title: Barcelona (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Barcelona: a phony, self-satisfied, overly clever movie from beginning to end.
history.text: Snarky, smug, self-satisfied, Barcelona lacks any grounding in what might be called the real world. Its dialogue sounds completely written, much better, perhaps, for its writer to read on a page and smirk at how witty he is being, than it is coming out of the mouths of the film's characters. None of it rings true, not one line, not one word. Like the film itself, the major characters, especially the cousins, are inordinately self-involved and far too confident in their own cleverness. In fact, they are irritating. The sailor is especially annoying, like an overgrown prep school boy who has never overcome his undeserved delight in his own presence. Without a doubt, he seems always to be saying, I am fine fellow when in fact he acts and speaks in ways that are appallingly insensitive and oblivious. The movie ostensibly touches on some serious themes, but them undermines them by its characters' behaviors. There is a scene after a sailor's death in a terrorist incident which is one of the most heartless moments I have seen in a film, though it seems to have been staged for its insouciance and ironies. That is perhaps what is most troubling about Barcelona. The film, in its phoniness, is also utterly heartless and cold. It is the chill of a supposed wit that fails because it is do disconnected from reality. Wit, Nietzsche wrote, is the death of feeling. So it is in this often cruel movie. But the worst of it is the artifice of the movie's dialogue, its archness and smirking pretension to cleverness. It is a hollow movie without one incident, one bit of conversation that seem to have begun in observation of reality, of what real human beings really do and say. It is a phony film from beginning to end.

history.title: Do You Take This Man
history.review_title: Watching this movie is like being stuck with people who won't stop talking in ...
history.text: Excruciating. Watching this movie is like being stuck with people who won't stop talking in clichés or being made to listen to conversations that seem never to end, repetitive, boring, annoying, stupid, and embarrassing. About a third of the way into it, sensing it was the only way out, I fast forwarded it to its predictable conclusions and felt, just by seeing all those lips moving and faces mugging, that I had heard every trivial, monotonous word.

history.title: You Can't Escape Lithuania
history.review_title: Like so many films promoted as "gay" themed movies
history.text: Violent, ill-written, badly acted, this intolerable movie seems to have no core of any kind, moral, aesthetic, political, you name it. Two of the main characters (there are only three) are people whom, if you ever had the misfortune to meet, you would, I hope, immediately turn your back on because of their obvious heartlessness and cruelty. The third is merely an inane stud from a hustler's ad with all the character and complexity of that sort of photo, a mindless body to keep the plot moving. This is the sort of film that should make one angry at the people who sold it to you, misrepresenting it in every respect while certainly knowing what a vile mess it was. Like so many films promoted as "gay" themed movies, it is a waste of time. I wish I'd been warned. It is despicable.

history.title: Veep Complete Seasons 1-4 Set
history.review_title: A mean-spirited, ugly, witless, vulgar show.
history.text: Veep is an intermittently funny show. I have the complete 6 season set which I don't see currently listed on Amazon. We were able to watch about half of the series and then gave it up. All the characters in it, including the V.P., are so relentlessly stupid, dumb in almost everything they do or say, that none of them would have been able to keep their jobs for a day. I know the show is meant to be a wicked satire, so to speak, but if satire is to work it must have some grounding in plausibility. This show lacks that altogether. As a consequence, it is far more often irritating than funny. Unless you are a fan of the Stooges, dumb deeds don't make for good wit. Furthermore, everyone in the show, no matter the character is, as relentlessly, vulgar. The number of four letter words per sentence is astonishing and grows very quickly boring. The remarks they all make to one another are usually sexual in one way or another, mostly aspersions and innuendos of various kinds, often homophobic and always degrading. There is nothing intelligent or witty or perceptive about any of this. Veep is throughout mean-spirited and ugly. The characters are not only stupid in everything they do and say. They are also quick to betray one another whenever they can. There are no morality or ethical principles in sight anywhere. Perhaps politics is a vile as this show depicts it to be. But, even if that is so, to watch it is to feel, far too often, corrupted by it. If there were deeper perceptions or underlying cogent motives to it, Veep might be better. But it is a mindless show that relies nearly all the time on the worst of what people are capable of in politics to make its puerile points.

history.title: Rossini: Mose in Egitto
history.review_title: Once more, a post-modern minded director runs amuck
history.text: By attempting to impose the significance of contemporary history, notably the Palestinian/Israeli conflicts on Rossini’s thoroughly ahistorical Mosè in Egitto, Graham Vick, its director, succeeds in rendering both absurd. Rossini is not a composer of depths. If there is profundity to him, it is a profundity of surfaces, of a classical idealism contained in Romantic guises. Vick’s production, however, attempts to render the opera as a pondering on recent Middle Eastern wars and conflicts. In his peculiar, perverse understanding of Rossini, it ends with a Palestinian child suicide bomber about to blow up an Israeli soldier. Imagine that, if you will, and try not to be horrified at the many other violences Vick brings to bear upon an opera that simply will not tolerate them. Post-modernism has a lot to answer for in all the arts. Perhaps, currently, it is in opera productions where it still holds, crazily, most sway. The madness of this production is clear from the start in the incongruity of almost every detail, no part fitting in with any other or seeming to belong to the same world. The stage is constantly active. So is the theater itself with chorus members and others drenched in blood, carrying dead children, posting photographs of the missing on walls. But, save for the abuse of history for the purposes of theatre, none of it makes any sense. What are all those computers being used for? Why are people being filmed? What are those kitschy Egyptian statues and enamel gold throne doing there? And soon and on. It’s all a hodgepodge, a farrago, a mess. History, especially the history that this production attempts to impose on what is a most fragile libretto, is a complex, ambiguous, and difficult record of often great cruelties. To use those cruelties as a way of giving weight to a work that cannot bear it is to ruin the work and to violate history. Terrorism is not what Rossini’s opera is in any shape or form about. There is something disturbingly immoral about suggesting that it is, immoral, abusive, and offensive to the very history it pretends to evoke. The only way, I think, this opera can still live on an operatic stage today is for its presentation to be as close to its own era, the early 19th century, as possible, not to ours. It is a strange piece, untrue to the bible, untrue to any known history anywhere, anytime, yet still possibly valid if its peculiar musical position between classicism and romanticism is observed. It contains far too much recitative, but its best moments remain moving and frequently beautiful, though not as sung in this self-important and disastrously overburdened production. The worst thing about post-modern productions of opera is how its directors impose their politics on a work they are in no other way responsive to. It is the vanity of the director one has to suffer from, time after time, while the true, real creators are betrayed, here none more so, of course, than Rossini. What one hears is so inapt for what one sees that the music becomes not deeper but seemingly more irrelevant, arbitrary, and even trivial. And that is perhaps the worst sort of betrayal. Rossini’s “serious” operas are not any of those things. But what they are and why we should pay attention to them are not easy to discern. A truly great production would show us the way. Where are they?

history.title: Wild Wild West
history.review_title: NOT THE WILD WILD WEST. NOT EVEN WILD. LAME.
history.text: THIS IS NOT THE WILD WILD WEST. THIS IS FAKE HOLLYWEIRD REMAKE GARBAGE. WILL SMITH SUCKS.

history.title: Frankenstein
history.review_title: AAARRRGGHHHH! one of the worst monster versions ever made.
history.text: As a big fan of Universal and Hammer and classic horror I have almost all Frankenstein movies even Abbott and Costello meet Frankenstein and most are good but this version is probably the worst! The writing acting directing is horrible. I could never get thru an entire viewing. If you want a good version the 73 version Frankenstein the True Story is far superior and one of the best. this is one of the worst.
what's to say other than one of the best TV comedies ever made.

history.review_title: Fatal Mission is fatal for the Nazis. Good TV movie.
history.text: Okay it's not as good as the original movies but this was a TV movie and pretty damn good not great. It moves along at a quick pace and there is plenty of action and shooting especially for a TV movie. The Nazis are made to look as stupid and evil as they were. Telly Savalas is great as the leader of the mission and the cast is many well know actors of the 80's. The ending is great with the explosions and train wreck but then they just walk off. What happened to the dirty dozen after the mission? oh well it's still better and more fun than any of the garbage made by the networks today or even on cable. Just a good action packed fun war movie.

history.title: The Rockford Files: Season Six
history.review_title: The end of the best detective show of all time.
history.text: This season ended early as Garner was in hospital and wanted out so they cancelled with only 1/2 season done. Some of the episodes are as good as any season but has a few clinkers like the Lauren Bacall episode. There are two shot on location one in Hawaii and one in a fishing town both are two of the wildest episodes with lots of ridiculous plots but both fun as usual. My favorite is Tom Selleck episode as the bumbling detective Lance White is back. It's a real good one. If your a fan you have to have the last season of James Rockford.

history.title: When a Stranger Calls
history.review_title: when a stranger calls don't answer! but watch this movie.
history.text: As a kid I loved the old suspense mystery TV and horror movies. I don't remember seeing this one but I had seen it a few times and thought it was one of those newer graphic blood gore horror movies. I got this at a discount store when I saw who was in it and when it was made. It is one of the better suspense mystery movies. The beginning of the movie is done very well with the baby sister getting phone calls and then find out the person is in the house and the kids are dead. But then it drags a little with Durning chasing after the escaped mental patient with some scenes that just seem like a waste of time that have nothing to do with the story. It gets back on track and the ending is very good. I won't ruin the ending. If you live 70's tv movies and horror you will like this. and there's no blood and gore to ruin the movie.

history.title: Man on the Moon
history.review_title: Man on the Moon is a wonderful trip into the life of the brilliant mind of Andy Kaufman.
history.text: As a kid I saw Kaufman do all his famous routines and thought he was hilarious but my dad and family didn't get it at all. I thought he was great on Taxi too. Not a fan of Carrey but I went see this movie when it first came out and thought it was good. Now I think it's great. I have had it on VHS yes still have it and dusted it off and it gets better with each viewing. The entire movie is incredible from the writing to directing to the acting by everybody. DeVito is great as the manager. I had forgot he was on Taxi with Kaufman. Hollyweird could not make a movie like this today. It would have to have all their leftist propaganda added. Those who say this is boring or bad need CGI special effects and blood and gore and sex and violence to get their attention span activated. This movie is for those who have a attention span and sense of humor.

history.title: Madhouse
history.review_title: Dr Death is in the Madhouse! A lost horror Classic!
history.text: A Horror Classic! Those who wrote negative reviews obviously don't like movies with great acting and story and without CGI graphic blood and gore even though this one does have some gore. Vincent Price and Peter Cushing are great in this together. Price plays it perfect as the horror star who has a nervous breakdown after his girlfriend is murdered and he was the main suspect but can't remember if he did it or not. Cushing plays his former writer of Dr Death series who brings him back to restart the series for the BBC but Price is not thrilled with reviving Dr Death from the Dead. The story has twist and turns and it's obvious the movie points the finger at Price as the killer but ? is he? The ending is especially good and done very well. A masterpiece of horror for Price and Cushing. A must see for all classic horror fans.

history.title: The Big Bang Theory: Season 2
history.review_title: Season 2 as good as 1 better than 3 and after that no more.
history.text: First and Second Seasons are the best. The 3rd is good but after that I was done. It began as a geek version of the Odd Couple with 2 other geek couple involved but then the additional of all the other characters except for Stewart the comic book owner and a few others it lost charm. But this season still held up the first season.

history.title: The Monster Club (remastered widescreen edition)
history.review_title: Come inside The Monster Club and have a ghoulish time!
history.text: Another lost gem! It's the way horror movies should be made! Great story telling and acting with humor and little graphic blood and gore. Price is a horror writer who gets bite by a vampire Carradine who brings him to The MOnster Club and gives him a history lesson in monsters and tales of terror. The stories are so good and fun to watch. If you like Thrillers and Suspense you'll love this movie. This was made in 80''s when new wave and punk was starting to get popular so there is music in the MOnster Club but it's actually pretty good and doesn't ruin the movie. A must have for Price fans.

targets.title: Starsky & Hutch - The Complete Fourth Season
The Twilight Zone: The Complete First Season
The Streets of San Francisco: Season 2 Volume 1
The Dan Curtis Macabre Collection (Dracula (1973) / The Turn of the Screw (1974) / Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde (1968) / The Picture of Dorian Gray (1973))

history.title: Beauty is Embarrassing: The Wayne White Story
history.text: Terrific gem of a film about Wayne White, an artist best known for his contributions to PeeWee's Playhouse and rock videos for Peter Gabriel and the Smashing Pumpkins. This is an incredibly entertaining documentary, and one that really demonstrates the joy of art and creativity. Five stars...I have watched it three times already.

history.title: Flight (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Although this was a courageous film role for Denzel Washington to take on, I wasn't that impressed by this one-note film. Not one of director Robert Zemeckis' better efforts. The first half hour (including the crash) is quite good...then it starts to lose itself.

history.title: The Heat (Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD)
history.text: I was hoping for some great character interaction, and a bit of physical comedy similar to "Bridesmaids" (also with Melissa McCarthy). I don't think I laughed once. Shrill, screamingly unfunny...avoid at all costs.

I enjoy Paul Williams as a songwriter, singer, actor and talk show wit. I noticed this film making the festival rounds and thought it seemed like a great subject for an offbeat documentary. What you get is a smug, rather mean-spirited look at Williams after the parade of fame has passed him by...all told in a very annoying way by a director schooled in the Morgan Spurlock school of "let me make this as much about ME as possible." A huge disappointment.

history.title: The Office: Season 6 [Blu-ray]
history.text: I have tried two sets of this season on blu ray and both share EXACTLY the same defects... Disc one freezes up continually, starting with episode two of the season. Buyer beware! There are many warnings out there about this being flawed...and you should believe every one of them. Set two going back tomorrow.

history.title: Moonrise Kingdom (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The usual amazing Criterion job of finding rare behind-the-scenes "making of" films
history.text: The usual amazing Criterion job of finding rare behind-the-scenes "making of" films, screen tests, set building, outtakes. I'm thrilled with this release.

history.title: Eclipse Series 31: Three Popular Films by Jean-Pierre Gorin (Poto and Cabengo, Routine Pleasures, My Crasy Life) (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.review_title: Buyer Beware... One of Criterion's Most Disappointing Releases
history.text: Three painful films (to sit through)! I usually trust Criterion to choose worthwhile films, but I have been burned a few times by the films they release in their lower-budget cult sets under the Eclipse subsidiary. These three films are the worst set that I have purchased so far. The director utilizes amateur-looking title and comment crawls across the screen in two of the films that lower the level of the work to that of a cheesy Power Point presentation. I made it through all three... But I certainly regret buying this set.

history.title: The Friends of Eddie Coyle [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Interesting film. Good performances and direction. Terrible score!
history.text: Fair film, but nothing outstanding. I think it suffers from being elevated too highly on these boards. Mitchum is quite good in this, but I couldn't get beyond the dated, inappropriate score by Dave Grusin (a composer much more suited to lightweight films like "Tootsie" than gritty crime dramas). Perhaps if there was an option to shut the score off and just watch the film without it, I would have enjoyed it more.

history.title: The Marlon Brando Collection (Julius Caesar / Mutiny on the Bounty 1962 / Reflections in a Golden Eye / The Teahouse of the August Moon / The Formula )
history.text: Defective discs! I cannot get Reflections In A Golden Eye (the reason I bought this set!) to play in any DVD player (I own three). Buyer beware!

history.title: Eclipse Series 35: Maidstone and Other Films by Norman Mailer (Maidstone / Wild 90 / Beyond the Law) (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.review_title: I love most of the films that Criterion chooses to release
history.text: Sheer torture. I love most of the films that Criterion chooses to release, but I found these three impossible to sit through. This set of three films is released on their Eclipse label.

history.title: Silver City
history.text: Add this to the list of "movies that could have and should have been great but weren't". Richard Dreyfuss is just not slimy enough to play the campaign manager. Sorry, Richard. Chris Cooper is great as the dimwit candidate, but doesn't have enough material to work with. The plot drags, and overall, it's difficult to care what happens to whom. Don't waste your money. If you've seen the trailer, you've seen all the good parts already.

history.title: FDR: American Badass
history.text: I watched this movie expecting it to be bad. My only question was, how bad will it be? But it wasn't! It was great! Sure, in a few spots it was a little off, but for the most part it was rolling-on-the-floor funny. And the acting was top-notch. Not A-list actors perhaps, but certainly some of them deserve to get there. It had a bit of history in it too. Not a huge amount of detail, but what was there was surprisingly accurate - aside from the obvious departures from reality. Definitely not PC, so if you're squeamish or easily offended, watch something else. But if you're looking for a good time with some friends, check it out.

history.title: Fairy Tales [DVD]
history.review_title: Light-hearted and fun, with better than expected music
history.text: This movie is great fun. Slightly titillating, surprisingly good music (and that coming from someone who usually dislikes musicals), and tolerably funny. Really very little nudity, just enough to keep one's interest. (I wonder what was in the six minutes that got cut out?) Fun and light-hearted; no violence or other unpleasantness. The barker/salesman fellow was a real crack-up. Not the best movie ever made, but it's really a shame that more movies aren't like this. Worth watching.

history.title: How the Earth Was Made
history.review_title: One of the best. Don't miss it.
history.text: Great. Very interesting, very informative, beautifully shot. The age of the earth is truly immense. This documentary brings that home in ways I haven't seen before. Don't miss the DVD Extra on volcanoes. Again, interesting and informative. This beats the pants off the TV series of the same name.

history.title: How the Earth Was Made: Complete Season One
history.review_title: Does not measure up to the original
history.text: It was good, but not good enough. Disappointing compared to the original feature documentary. Not that this was terrible; it wasn't. It just didn't measure up to the high bar its predecessor set. Lots of repeated (and repeated, and repeated, and...) short video clips. Lot of repeated CGI, lots of flash and noise, overly dramatic music clips and narration. Lots of whiz-bang, but short on substance. Rather reminded me of a late-night used-car commercial. They mentioned the Loch Ness Monster more times than I can count. Really?? Who gives a ... ??? Yes, they finally admitted that no, there are no leftover dinosaurs in Loch Ness (for one reason, the loch is only 10,000 years old), but COME ON! That "monster" never deserved a mention in the first place. All part of the attention-grabbing nonsense that this series has so much of. It was still informative, but overall just too TV-like.

history.title: The Day the Earth Nearly Died
history.review_title: Definitely worth watching; hate the commercials
history.text: Very interesting. Fact-based. They do go off on a tangent or two, but that's OK - science does run into dead ends on the way to knowledge. It's also interesting and different to think of things that happened 250M years ago as being "recent", but compared to the age of the earth, they really are recent. Quite a different perspective. Minus one star for awful non-skippable commercials in the beginning. I really, really hate those.

history.title: 8 Minute Buns & Legs [DVD]
history.text: Good workout, results as expected. See also Eight Minute Abs.

history.title: How The Earth Was Made: The Complete Season 2 [Blu-ray]
history.text: Very good, though doesn't quite measure up to the original (pilot?). Informative and interesting.

Interesting story about an interesting woman, an intelligent, very likable and ambitious person, from her childhood through her sad and untimely demise. She got into the sex business as a way to care for her ailing mother, and became a huge star. She became, uh, "close friends", with several famous people, including prime minister Harold Wilson. Unfortunately, when her mother finally died, it seems like Mary Millington stopped trying to care for her own life. She committed suicide as a result of being hounded for many years by the police and the tax man, and generally falling apart due to drugs and bad companions. Lessons learned: One, learn to properly handle your personal finances (for example, she was known to keep large amounts of money in cash), and two, don't do drugs! Also of interest was the view of English prudery. Wow, that place was even more messed up than the US.

history.title: Sex and Lucia (Rated Edition) by Palm Pictures / Umvd by Julio Medem
history.text: Whoever thought that this was sexy? Some 20-somethings trying to find meaning in their meaningless lives. They could start by growing up. What a snorefest. I watched the "unrated" version and wonder what all the fuss is about. There's not much sexy in this movie. I don't know what the censored version cut out. There was about three or four seconds of a beej, that's about it. Nothing to get excited over. Maybe there's more to this movie. Maybe it has a point. But I couldn't find it, and I'm really, really not willing to endure it again looking for profundity.

history.title: Company of Heroes
history.review_title: NONSENSE, ON ALL SORTS OF LEVELS.
history.text: I really like a good war movie. I didn't like this one. That's because it's not good. It's not even merely okay. It's trash. Don't get me wrong: my judgement doesn't have much to do with the fanciful plot ("Hey, guys! We've stumbled onto a Nazi super-bomb test site!!) I've got a pretty well-developed suspension of disbelief, if other things--dialogue, action--hold up, I'm there. Nope, not this time. The tip-off was the name of the director, Don Michael Paul. Who?? A little after-the-fact research reveals Paul's the director of a clutch of grade B horror movies and a Steven Seagal action flick. (Uh-oh.) Which means Company represents either his "big break" or "just another clunker" After about half an hour, the verdict is in: klunk, klunk, klunk. Hey, Jurgen Prochnow (Das Boot) is here. Great. Neal McDonough from Justified and Band of Brothers. That's good, too. Tom "Saving Private Ryan" Sizemore. Now, I know Sizemore's had some tough times recently, but I figured, what the hey, he's good. But I was misled. Turns out all of them were slumming and had to know it. And now you do, too. Sez Don Paul in the Special Feature about Recreating WW II, "You don't realize how many people out there are World War II fanatics!" Yeah, Don, I would. But you don't have to be to punch the eject button on this one. It pains me when I hear 1944-era characters saying "boots on the ground," and "kick some Nazi Ass." Then, a Brit introduces himself as a pilot from the "British Air Force." No officer in the ROYAL Air Force would introduce himself that way! I mean, I know it's tough to recreate Tiger tanks, but script changes are quick and easy. The kill rate--and the manner in which the bad ol' Nazis die, and most yanks don't--reminds me of the silliness of the old 60s TV series Combat. Which makes this movie a throwback, as well as a throw-away. Save yer time and money.

history.title: EXODUS: GODS AND KINGS
history.review_title: GOOD ONE, FROM THE DIRECTOR WHO HAS GIVEN US GREATS...
history.text: I'm not interested in whether or not this movie is "true to the Bible" (one review's headline reflected this idiocy: "A Secular take...well made but take with a grain of salt." Well, when dealing the Holy Book, I bring along a massive salt lick anyway.) So, I'll concentrate on the story and story-telling, the performances and what the camera (and computers) capture. It takes a lot to make these movies today. Not one, not two, but sometimes the budgets of three studios--such collaboration was unheard of even twenty-five years ago--and ARMIES of people each painstakingly included in teeny tiny font on the credits crawl on and and on and on...almost like the 40 year trek the Hebrews endured after they left Egypt. Now...how does this movie compare with what came before (Cecil B. DeMille's 1956 feature, The Ten Commandments)? There is no comparison at all, in story, performances and visuals. Not to denigrate this "masterpiece" (although the temptation is there), but how could there possibly be? Time, attitudes, story-telling forms and technology race on, and CB's "masterpiece" is simply left in the dust--at least in my mind, but not, I suspect, in most of the minds of the most of the 1,500 (!) people who posted reviews of the mid-50s biblical epic. The story and story telling: very good. Immediately, we go inside the palace in Memphis, and within a few minutes have a pretty good take on the (aging) pharaoh and his two "sons"--one legitimate, the other adopted--and their relationships, set up in short, punchy scenes--pharaoh Seti and Moses; Ramesses and infant son; Moses and his wife. Within minutes of the start, the boys are off to do battle with the Hittites. From a pure story-telling strategy, this is great, because action breaks up dialogue scenes (one thing I remember from the 1956 version: talk, talk, talk! This movie...moves) but also because it sets up the major premise of the greater conflict. Moses' conferences with "God" are handled in an intriguing fashion (no spoilers here) and the various plagues are executed in more-or-less plausible ways (including the "parting" of the Red Sea) and explained that way to Ramesses. Anyway... Nice touches with Moses and his "other" family, too. So, the human side is reflected AWAY from Egypt's palace and into a distant, dusty village of the time. And Moses--what a difference from the stiff, formal, pontificating presence of Charlton Heston. (Forever intoning, Let My People Go!) No, this Moses is much more the man of action--as is befitting a former general of the Pharaoh's army. His strategy--or, if you will, his fate--is rationally explained. The action, the events and most of all, the MOTIVATION...makes sense, and that kept me watching. Performances: uniformly good. Unexpected casting, with John Turturro as nicely understated Seti, Christina Bale does well as Moses, and Joel Edgerton (Animal Kingdom, Zero Dark Thirty, Great Gatsby) is very good in a very difficult part of the lackluster new Pharaoh--born to the battlefield, but not the throne. Thanks also to Director Ridley Scott, for keep the performances simmering, but, thankfully, a long way from the hard boil of Yul Brynner's 1956 grand-standing. What we see: the movie is a delightful spectacle, full of sweep and truly epic "showcase" scenes, the LEAST of which is the Hebrews' exodus from the city. This is a good one--not "great," as some of Scott's previous works, but solid entertainment...and worthy entry from the 77-year-old director who has given us so much: Thelma and Louise, Gladiator, Blade Runner and Alien. Nice to see that, after 40 years in the biz, he's still reaching and striving.

history.title: Fury [DVD]
history.review_title: ONE OF THE MOST MEMORABLE WAR MOVIES
history.text: This is a very good one, by any measure. It was of special interest to me: as a pre-teen baby-boomer in Vancouver, I was fascinated by the Sherman Tank displayed at an Armouries building on Beatty Street. The tank that thousands of Canadians fought in, on, (and behind!) during that incredible year in Europe after D-Day, and, not so incidentally, as the Canucks, Americans and British fought their way up the boot of Italy. That Beatty Street Sherman is still there, I've learned, one of less than half a dozen that still exist in Canada. (The fact that the movie utilizes 5 original WW II tanks--4 Shermans and a German Tiger adds to the realism.) How furious was the action? By the end of the war, only ONE Canadian Sherman that had clanked ashore during D-Day was still moving about a year later, by war's end. Amazing. I'd never seen the inside of a tank, so that was a major motivation for watching the movie. Great--and unexpected--movie experience, far beyond the hardware. Interesting story structure--we can only guess at the horrors this crew had ALREADY seen, in years of combat, prior to when the tale begins. The story is, in fact, the sad, tragic finale to their military service. Clever, too, in that we see war's horrors, not only from the tough perspective of hardened veterans, but from the perspective of the new crewman--a clerk-typist who, by his own admission, had never seen the inside of a tank, either. That's not all he hasn't seen, as we soon learn. It's not just the horrors we are reminded of here, but--unlike most other war movies, especially most made before the 1960s--the EFFECTS of the horror on those who fought, and, also, here, the effect on civilians, the "collateral damage" of combat. To say more would spoil the viewing experience of others, but be assured, this is one of the best. Happily, others think so, too. The movie has made almost 4 times its budget as of this writing.

history.title: I'll Follow You Down
history.text: Captivated by the concept of time travel since a teen, watching Rod Taylor click the decades by in George Pal's original movie, The Time Machine. Read even more on it, too (The Butterfly effect) Must say most have faded from my memory, except the Pal feature film, Time after Time, and the Time Traveller's Wife. This one will stick in the memory, though. It's not really "about" time travel, but the choices men (yeah, men) make chasing ideas, (wars, money, you name it) at the expense of love and family. Good performance by Haley Joel Osment (the psychic kid in Sixth Sense) as the son who lost his father...and has a chance to reclaim him, ahhh, but the cost! Nice turn by X-files' Gillian Anderson as the grieving widow and also Victor Garber as the young man's obsessed grandfather. Nice build-up, great ending, and, as always with time-travel stories, a sense of, "yeah, but what if..."

history.title: Harry Tracy: The Last of the Wild Bunch [DVD]
history.text: This movie died when it was first released, for unknown reasons--at least, for me. See the guy in the beard and bowler on the cover of the DVD case? Guess who? None other than Gordon Lightfoot (yeah, THAT Gordon Lightfoot) Filmed in part in and around Old Town Victoria, B.C., too.

history.review_title: DOES WHAT ALL EXCELLENT TRAGEDIES ARE SUPPOSED TO DO
history.text: Says one reviewer (who gave this movie one star): "we kept watching in hopes that it would end happy...nope couldn't even do that." Ahh, expectations. Watching a movie=enjoying happy endings. Which is why, I guess, Netflix viewers gave this phenomenal movie an average of just two stars out of five. Few films merit 5 stars, but this one comes close. Is this movie entertaining? Not in the usual sense, although I got supreme pleasure from watching inspired performances from all three leads under what I suspect was the incredibly talented direction of Bennett Miller, (Capote, Moneyball) who won Best Director honours at Cannes for his work here. Is the Bible entertaining? The question is not out of context here, for the movie really is a classic tale of temptation (with the Devil cleverly disguised as a wealthy man. Foxcatcher also has elements of the Cain-and-Abel saga, too (with a similar tragic conclusion.) And it begs the age-old question: Am I my brother's keeper? OK, like other tragedies (from Romeo and Juliet to Apocolypse Now), not "entertaining" in the strict sense, but very insightful about the American psyche, very instructive about human nature. If a tragedy does what it's supposed to do (offer insight, instruction--and make you feel very, very sad, as this one does, and move you to say, "If only...if only...) it's an artistic success. This one does it all.

history.title: The Enemy Below
history.text: As of 2015 (close to 60 years after this feature was released): 600 reviews. Amazing, especially when the movie is--at this point--somewhat dated and quite "typical" of the late-50s hollywood war movie (meaning, fairly predictable.) The original story--a British novel written by an English WW II naval officer--was a lot more hard-edged (in the climax, when seamen of both sides share a lifeboat, the Brit Captain takes a swing at the U-boat Captain). However, Dick Powell made the movie during the Cold War era and Germany was a good ally, hard up against Russia's Iron Curtain and so there's a brothers-in-arms "respectful adversary" feeling at the end. Dated, too, are the Oscar-winning special effects, with the (predictable) miniatures and rear-screen projection use during final combat scenes. No matter how clever the effects are (and they are) they just couldn't fake water, resulting in drops of water that are as big as...well, one of those three-inch guns mounted on the little destroyer escort. Excellent performance by Hollywood newcomer Curt Jurgens in his first screen appearance, as the U-boat skipper, and a solid one by Robert Mitchum as the American commander.

history.title: Fortress
history.review_title: Wasted opportunity, but for the chance for computer jockies to play aerial warfare.
history.text: Three stars, two for the effects. .5 for the idea. .5 for performances, None at all for the script. So it's effects over cliches, spouted by the crew of a B 17 flying off from Tunisia to bomb Sicily during Operation Husky. "Husky" is mentioned in passing, but never explained (a major pre-Normandy invasion of the island by Canadian forces, mainly, supported by, Brits and GIs.) Historical Note: the invasion was a hell of a lot more successful than the bombing missions, which, according to the movie, took out 8 of 10 men in the bombers. Great stuff...but this movie doesn't do any of it justice, and the aerial combat between what look like Mustangs and MI-109s (Hey; where'd the Fortress go?) start to resemble video games. Too much shine and sheen, not enough grit and guts.

history.review_title: BETTER TITLE: WILD WEST WOMEN FANTASIES.
history.text: Says one reviewer, “If you can’t handle the reality of it...” Sadly, reality is in really short supply in this new western series. Once upon a couple of times, the western was kiddie fantasy fare. The first time was during the era of quick, cheap B movie theatrical releases. Then, in 1939, John Ford made Stagecoach and, later, the Cavalry trilogy; the Ox Bow Incident was released and—while still steeped in mythology—the western, to a great extent, grew up. It grew up even more in the 1950s with Shane, The Searchers, High Noon, the Naked Spur and a host of other adult dramas. Kiddie fantasy westerns came back with a vengeance in the 1950s as producers filled TV airtime with quick-and-dirty “western hero” series: Hopalong Cassidy, the Roy Rogers Show, Wild Bill Hickok, the Cisco Kid and the most legendary of them all, The Lone Ranger. Imagine my surprise—and disappointment—when I began to watch Strange Empire and found that the fantasy western was back. I watched 1.5 episodes. That’s all I could take, folks. The name is wrong. First, it’s not original; it is borrowed. Strange Empire is the title of the finest non-fiction book about the REAL Canadian/US west, and tells the story of Louis Riel and his rebellion. Second, there is no discernible “empire” here at all. Quite the contrary... the settings don’t even pass for “towns.” The producers even get the name of the location wrong, calling it “Montana”, when the place was still Montana Territory (statehood not arriving until after the wild west was over.) The series is certainly “strange,” alright, but not in a good way. The most fitting title I can come up with: Wild West Women Fantasies. The series is fantasy because the women think, speak and act like 20th century women. They are a “force to be reckoned with.” Very, very few women were a “force” in the frontier west. The very few who were (Bill Hickok tag-along, Calamity Jane, outlaw Belle Star and Annie “Little Sure Shot” Oakley), were all seen as oddballs. The first two were mostly ridiculed and/or reviled. If you’d like a “reality” glimpse of women in the west, put yourself in front of the movie, The Homesman, wherein a man (Tommy Lee Jones) and woman (Hillary Swank) are charged with transporting a number of women back to their families and homes in the East. Why? Because the stark Prairie, impoverished lifestyle and brutal men they lived with have driven them stark-raving mad. Only in a politically-correct CBC drama would you have mid-19th century feminists (one of whom is obviously of Native parentage,) hobnobbing, in two back-to-back scenes, with an African-American (in Canada, no less) and a Chinese, who looks like no Chinese ever did in the 1860s-1870s. Well, there you go! The Canadian mosaic at work! When the gun-totin' heroine comes to the rescue out of nowhere just when another woman (female doctor) is about to be raped, well, it's straight out of B-movie kiddie fare of yore. Give this one a pass.

history.title: Fiend Without a Face (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.review_title: A rarity: Criterion Collection Does B Sci-Fi!
history.text: Wow...the Criterion Collection, no less! Surprising, but well-deserved. Remember seeing this run on Canadian as a teenager in the mid-1960s. Not only did the movie have a decent story and script, (decent, but not great), which in itself, was unusual for a B horror movie, it had terrific stop-motion special effects that brought the "fiends" to life. from Wikipedia: "...the film an "X" certificate, but newspaper critics were still aghast at its horrifying special effects." I bet. Beat out a lot of hokey US B-movie competition, for sure. This is a good one. For another one (although the plot's a little thin), see This island Earth.

Wonderful acting by every actor, many wonderful scenes. That does not always constitute a great movie - though I think any movie derived from a dialogue heavy play has serious challenges . The play is a finer work of art - but hell, movies have closeups! It's 1957 Pittsburgh and we have 53 year old Denzel , former Negro League star now working for the sanitation dept w a close buddy. Only 18 years of his life have been *settled* - now about to be unsettled by his sons interest in professional sports and a bigger issue (see the movie). He is obsessed about past and present fences - those he cleared w a ball and bat and the one he builds around his house . Who knows why? Some great writing here but 95% is philosophical , reflective ...and "Preachy". No spoiler intended but don't wait for Denzel to say "where's my coffee?" Picture runs too long and is quite convoluted . Worth seeing, in bits and pieces, especially if you enjoy anything with Denzel .

history.title: The Fate of the Furious
history.review_title: Robbers vs robbers old school - new school
history.text: This series is new to me . This genre is not my cuppa tea. But I found it very entertaining to a point ....and very well cast . All actors get the most out of the tight, taught , funny script. Obviously the audience is perceived to be graduates of the home video game college , where young people are taught to enjoy crash , bang , boom , hard edit effects for hours a time . Re "hours ", thus one runs almost an hour too long ; an extended explosive series of shots in New York is okay for about 7 minutes , not (apparently )about 20 minutes . You see a taxi ...gone ! See a bus ? Gone ! Metal , glass, rubber flying around as if a nuclear blast occurs. Anybody over 50 who loves The Rock or Kurt Russell might want to buy the DVD on Amazon so he/she can fast forward from the repetitive violence.

history.review_title: Some like it Hot , Tootsie, and The Birdcage ...mixed w a whole lot of Robin Williams
history.text: Some very long drawn out , draggy patches, and awkward mix of real and surreal but wonderful acting from all , especially Sally Field . Williams is Williams but the director keeps him just a little low-key. Too bad. Hippie daddy and pragmatic wife have grown apart, divorce, and a kind of role reversal scenario sustains the family ( and an hilarious denouement ). Daddy is a genius voice over artist who finds he can apply his talents to playing a "Mrs." - *acting * as the hired housekeeper , able to get a full week with the kids ,as opposed to just a lousy Saturday. He /she also gets a chance to watch the new suitor , Pierce Brosnan, and we are treated to a screamingly funny poolside scene. Brosnan , looking like Gentlemans Quarterly in his bathing suit and Williams sits off to the side, dressed in his English maid attire, muttering to himself! See the flick!

history.review_title: Great bits And pieces and occasionally brilliant script - but inconsistent and flawed . DeVito fans go for it.
history.text: Deck The Halls ? Not much going on I dude the house st Christmas time here, it’s all about the antagonist (why ? Who offended him?) Danny DeVito , a blue collar guy with a few bucks and plenty of debt , who moves into a very quaint Massachusetts town to settle down - but first he must “out -Christmas “ Matthew Broderick , the neighbor next door . Why ? The movie doesn’t explain the “challenge “. The premise is really cool . Danny DeVito is excellent . He’s not as engaged as he could be but he acts very well. A lot of Louie DePalma going on which is just fine with him. His straight man, if you will , is Matthew Broderick , and he plays it too straight . This dude can act if he wants to but the script too often gives him fluff to sort out - or maybe the director is at fault for not putting more nuance in the character . The frantic DeVito and the milquetoast Broderick . Good casting . But I think the latters best work was decades behind him - to wit, the naive college kid in The freshman (1980). I think Tom Hanks would have been a better choice than MB. I think back to the great The In Laws w Peter falk and Alan Arkin, the fbi guy and his brother in law , the mild mannered account (as I recall). There was rhyhme and reason to all the shenanigans . I want to say this movie would have been very good if the powers that be shaved off about 12 minutes and capitalized on three or four great set ups for hilarity which fizzle . One glaring : at the winter fest the two rivals take a breather from all the contests and sit down to watch three hot dancers in short skirts do naughty holiday numbers . Turns out that two are DeVito’s tall sensuous daughters and the dancer in the Middle is Broderick’s rebellious teen . I guess her new friends got her out of her shell ? The script doesn’t support that. Anyway , it was a good chance for another DeVito prank on his competitor , get him to call out lecherously to his own kid ....but no, both daddies are schocked sbdcrun to church to wash their faces in absolution water . This picture is very reminiscent of the 1980 “neighbors “, w ackroyd and belushi . This 2006 flick is funnier . But to think what a first Class comedy director could have wrought with *those* two .

I love this show. I love the characters and the way that they interact. I love the leads and the supporting characters, each has its distinct personality and many have quirky idiosyncrasies. This a good drama as few exist anymore with a focused storyline. I love how family oriented the secretary is and how devoted she is to her husband and he to her in a very balanced and normal way. It is a great example of real leadership and partnership in parenting. LOVE BlAKE, the secretary's assistant. It doesn't get any better than he. Lilith from Frasier continues to re-invent herself and with more and more likability. She played a role for a season in Blue Bloods that I liked very much and here she equally does a great job. You see her character grow through the seasons as she becomes convinced of the Secretary of State's capabilities, she too becomes more authoritative yet balanced. JUST a GREAT SHOW.....one of my favorites I've seen since the good old West Wing days.
