history.review_title: Big Like Me comes up short
history.text: I watched this whole documentary, so I can't say I wasn't entertained on some level. However, I didn't really like it. The main star (Greg Bergman) has extremely low self esteem due to his "insufficient" penis size. He pursues multiple avenues to try and rectify the issue, and as one might expect, most options are a complete waste of time and money. Throughout the film we're subjected to Greg's stand-up comedy act, and unfortunately I didn't find any of it to be funny. It's more angry rantings than jokes. I won't spoil the ending, but I didn't like the overall message of the documentary. It was also painful to sit through the Online dating portions of the film (where Greg's sole source of conversations with women consist entirely about penis size... obviously not good first date subject matter, unless you're TRYING to look like a creep). This doc may appeal to some, but it was a complete miss for me.

history.review_title: Firehead... an inaccurate title for a horrible film
history.text: If you like really bland and forgettable action flicks, then this is the movie for you! Firehead is the story of a man who can shoot blue laser beams out of his eyes. He can also create a personal deflector shield of some sort with his mind... but these super powers are rarely ever used (for budgetary reasons I assume). Most of the time the action is limited to boring gunfights. Christopher Plummer makes a sad appearance in this rubbish, along with Martin Landau. Both actors are far too good for this movie. Chris Lemmon (Jack Lemmon's son) is right were he belongs however, in all his cheesy b-movie glory. He'd go on to co-star in Thunder in Paradise a few years later (playing second banana to Hulk Hogan). The Rifftrax crew makes this trash fun to watch, just be ready to crank down the volume when the LOUDEST, most obnoxious child actor hits the screen. Her piercing shrieks might blow apart your speakers! Thankfully she's only on screen for short periods of time.

history.review_title: Not enough focus on Lenny Bruce
history.text: This is an interesting documentary, but it feels like a very brief introduction to Lenny Bruce himself. Majority of the time is focused on the evolution of show business AFTER Lenny's untimely death. I wanted to see more on Lenny's life, and hear about his various legal battles in greater detail. Instead disgraced entertainers like Michael Richards and Don Imus stole a lot of the spotlight. I didn't feel like I wasted my time watching this documentary... but now I'm in the mood to watch a substantial doc on Lenny's history. Unfortunately, I'm not sure if one of those exists at the moment.

history.review_title: Susan. Susan. Susan! SUSAN!!! Susan! Susan??? Susan! ...Susan? SUSAN!!!
history.text: A young girl who's totally obsessed with spiders grows up to become a crazy social outcast. Big surprise! Around her late teens or early twenties she starts using spiders like deadly weapons, sending them out to attack anyone she deems an "enemy." It's not long before her law enforcement uncle uncovers this madness... and promises to keep it a secret, IF she'll become his lover! It's a deadly web of spiders and incest, accompanied by a killer Rifftrax commentary. What more could you possibly need?

This movie has one incredibly misleading title. There's no actual "puppet people" and they never mount an "attack" of any kind. Still, it's quite entertaining in its own special way. A mad scientist /slash/ doll maker shrinks real-life people into personal doll-sized minions. The minions are forced to sing and dance at the scientist's request... or face punishment! The minions attempt to escape multiple times, and strangely there's no real resolution. The movie closes with a weird open-ending, as if the filmmakers simply ran out of time (or money) to finish the story. The special effects are great (in a super cheesy way)... NOTHING is set to scale. Also, there are plotholes a'plenty! For example, the minions are too small to be heard by anyone... yet they regularly converse with the full-sized mad scientist without any difficulty whatsoever. It's a mess of a movie, but fun to watch, and the Rifftrax commentary makes it twice as entertaining.

history.title: Zoo: Season 1
history.review_title: Nice scenery, but they're getting a D in science from me - and lucky I don't give an F ..
history.text: They need someone to explain science and biology - and animal identification - to the writers and directors ... There is a global genetic upgrade among the animals - somehow they're changing genetically, upgrading their consciousness, intelligence, cooperation and, in some cases, physiology and it's all caused by some bacteria included in a widely dispersed chemical that has been delivered to darned near everywhere on the planet so that the start date of this global change is about the same time....... everywhere. That all by itself is fairly unbelievable, but let's say we go with it. But then it hasn't affected leopards in one valley in Africa where the chemical was never used - and, no - don't think about rainfall or birds or wind drift - just go along with this... So our heroes dash off to Africa to acquire a leopard - preferably a baby one - so they can cook up the cure using T-cells from the baby leopard and bits from some mother cell that looks oddly like a piece of amber ... Anyway - off to Africa and straight for the baby leopard - except the cute little cat they pick up is a baby Serval - not a leopard at all. ... but - nevermind - we're off to make the cure - and they grind up a bit of this amber stuff and a tooth from the baby ... um .. Serval ... and they get the cure. .. They try it out on what looks like a purebred Belgium Shepherd that some poor villager in Africa has in his backyard. An injection in the rump doesn't work - though a mist in the mouth works like a charm. One of the actors assures us that the injection did not disperse the cure throughout the dog's body . ... um ... wait ... how does that happen? ... And then the big company who created this problem to begin with interferes with things and the piece of amber - or whatever that was - is destroyed ... So they send the dog - who has the cure inside him - back to his owner and they dash off with just the baby Serval to make the cure somewhere else... How are they going to do this without the key mothercell? ... Oh - never mind that ... Surely you've been carried along with the story by the grade B and C acting ... What are a few facts here and there? And how do they expect to deliver the cure to all the animals of the planet? Mosquitoes!! That's according to one of the grade B actors - and you'll have to buy Season 2 to see that charade carried out. Never mind the shaky fact that the injection doesn't work - only the oral mist of the cure. Somehow, they're going to get all the mosquitoes on the planet to carry the cure and deliver it to all the animals .... I cannot bear to watch the second season to see how all this turns out ...

history.title: Limelight
history.text: Thanks, Rudy. I'd love to still be able to go to Limelight (now a shopping mall, in a church), but all I've got left is the Lion King. Nice legacy. That said, this movie is a great reminder of NYC's nightlife in its heyday, albeit one that's a little one-sided (the movie is produced by Peter Gatien's daughter, after all), but even so, still entertaining and full of 90s nostalgia. I grew up right across the street from the Limelight in my early 20s, so I lived and breathed this scene. Still great to see so many quotes from all the people they included in this documentary, including Michael Alig. A good documentary in general, but more specifically for people who witnessed firsthand the nightlife of NYC in the 90s.

history.title: Back to the Future: 25th Anniversary Trilogy [Blu-ray]
history.text: This review is about the packaging, not the movies (which are great to meh in descending order). Why does Every studio that creates multi-disc box set have to pack them in customized, horrible, difficult to use, damaging to the discs-packaging? Back to the Future Trilogy is no exception. What's wrong with disc spindles? It's only six discs (including digital copy discs), not twenty, so why Universal felt it was necessary to lodge these discs in inflexible, brittle, plastic side-tabs is beyond me. In order to pull the discs out you need to wedge your fingers under the sides of the disc, on the disc-read side, and unsnap it from its housing. Same goes for the digital copy discs although those come out more easily. Putting the discs back in is a mysterious process that involves unnerving amounts of plastic grinding against plastic, and 'pinching' of the disc to get it to fit back in under the tabs, none of which is good for the longevity of your remastered blu-ray collection. I wish movie studios would get over trying to innovate with standard boxed collections like this and just stick with what works. I give the collection four stars because the movies shouldn't be penalized for bad packaging, but it's really the first movie that's the winner in the bunch. The second movie was decent, but it doesn't age as well. The third movie, like most third movies, didn't really need to happen, and is just a poor postcard of its era. Great to have them all in one place, so I'm glad for that, but these movies are not created equally.

history.title: Don't Think
history.review_title: The Best Thing Next To Being There
history.text: If you've ever seen The Chemical Brothers in concert, this is as faithful a representation as you can possibly get without being there. The audio quality captures the thrill of a live show, with the appropriate aural ambience, crowd noise, and bassy, thumping beats. If you've never had the pleasure of seeing the Chemicals in person, this is as close as you can get, with both the CD and DVD providing great audio and video quality. This is basically a run-through of their greatest hits (of which they have plenty), with the minor quibble that 'Galvanize' is relegated to a small but familiar sample, while the entire song is omitted. Besides this minor gripe, it's a seamless set that sounds great both in the car or home stereo, and in headphones.

history.title: Wicked City (Remastered Special Edition)
history.review_title: Fun movie, excellent picture quality. One of Madhouse's best.
history.text: In lieu of a blu-ray release, anyone on the fence about picking up this dark Madhouse cult classic should purchase without hesitation. Despite the fact that this is only on DVD, the image quality is fantastic, clean and with minimal artifacting. If you don't already know, Wicked City is from the same makers of anime classics like Ninja Scroll and the more recent Redline. Wicked City is one of their earlier works from the late 80s, and is rich with violence and over-the-top Japanese sexuality, but if a NSFW anime movie isn't a problem for you, this is film belongs in any serious anime collection.

history.title: Gaiking: The Movie Collection
history.review_title: The best mech from the halcyon days of early 70s giant robots meets TERRIBAD dub quality
history.text: I love Gaiking, I grew up with it. But I made the mistake of thinking this movie set would be on par with the vastly superior TV series published here by Discotek. Instead, this 3-pack of Gaiking movies features what might be THE worst English dub (no Japanese audio here, sorry) I've ever heard in my life, and that's saying something. I mean, it's so bad. It's soooo bad. It sounds like something some students did as a home video editing project for their junior high video editing class, which is to say it sounds like something I'd have done when I was 13. It's terrible. The animation is also pretty spectacularly bad as well, but chalk this up to early 70s Japanese animation techniques. It's terrible in a charming, low budget way. The voice acting, however, is bad bad. Like, "you hate your children and let them watch this DVD set" bad. I took one for the team so you don't have to. Avoid at all costs.

history.text: The UK version is about the same price (MSRP) and comes with the 3D version AND the soundtrack on CD. The 3D rights may be tied up with the distributor, since the 3D version in theaters displays that "the 3D conversion was made possible by Studio Canal" which is publishing the film across Europe. Since they're not the publisher in North America, it's possible they're the ones preventing the 3D version from being released here, OR Lionsgate just didn't want to pay Studio Canal for the rights to the 3D version for North America, knowing that it's kind of a niche market for 3D fans (like me). Whatever the reason, it still sucks. They should just sell the arm separately to be honest.

history.title: Ted
history.review_title: Teddy Ruxpin he's not, but kids don't know that
history.text: The idea of a talking teddy bear that remains long after the novelty has worn off is a clever one. The story of a boy that needs to grow up when confronted by adult life and crises is a time honored tale. The animation and voice acting was fabulous. So, where did the story go wrong? I appreciate Seth MacFarlane's sense of humor (and his singing voice, check out [[ASIN:B004T5IW2K Music Is Better Than Words]]). He has been willing to gore sacred cows in many walks of life. MacFarlane's irreverence is refreshing, and like [[ASIN:B005CHTXWC Robot Chicken: Season Five]] about 10% of his jokes are pants wettingly funny, 80% are amusing, and 10% just fall flat. Those are pretty good odds for humor across such a wide front. Unfortunately in the case of Ted, there was about 25% that were just horribly offensive. I'm no prude and can certainly laugh at myself, my culture, my religion, etc. "Family Guy" and "American Dad" have their moments, but generally there is only one or two missteps an episode. In Ted, the level of callousness and crudity were past the line enough to make the film unfunny. I'm not talking about political correctness. When Ted tells his manager that he used produce to fornicate with and then sold it to an indigent family, it does not come off as funny. And, the examples are legion. The other major issue I have is that Ted drew in a fair number of kids. It is a movie about a talking teddy bear after-all. I heard a couple of boys that appeared to be between 9-10 talking about Ted on the Metro last week. Sure, sure, where are the parents, but I could imagine some parents screwing up by letting their very young kids watch a movie about a talking teddy bear. You don't want to know which parts the boys were hooting about. :-( I just watched a new episode of Family Guy last night and mostly enjoyed it. Seth you let me down on Ted. Sorry, I cannot recommend this movie.

history.text: There have been many versions of this classical tale done over the past four decades, some live action, some animated, but this is my favorite. Chris Walken is simply amazing in this film. He dances, he sings, and delivers an amazing performance. (Honestly, I cannot shake imagining him as Gabriel from his most notable role, but he is great in this movie.) Also, the film is very true to the original tale. (Some of the other versions embellish quite a bit.) One caveat, this is not done in HD. It is clearly a VHS quality video transcribed to DVD, but for the little fairy tale lover in your family will not mind.

history.title: Killing Hasselhoff [DVD]
history.review_title: My Gosh it's full of stars ...
history.text: This movie was done by a number of stand-up commedians and consisted of a very fun (if wildly silly) plot. Ken Jeong stars as the very unlucky night club owner who has everything fail on him at the same time. Unfortunately, our night club owner has borrowed money from a Zen, Brooklyn, ... guy who is deadly serious about getting his money back. Where does the Hoff fit into this? He has a cameo at the beginning (as do about 700 Hollywood A & B listers), but the main connection is that Ken's character has been entering the Hollywood Death List every year for years. The idea is that if you pick the celebrity who dies that year first then you win the pot. By the time our movie story starts the pot is up to $500K, slightly more than our Zen friend cum loanshark needs. Ken finds himself in an increasingly crazy set of plot twists until ... (it is shown in the opening scene so it is not really a spoiler) Ken actually saves the Hoff's life. Roll happy ending. If you do buy, rent, or watch this movie, you should watch the end takes as there is some funny stuff there. It also demonstrates that this movie was largely ad lib by some highly trained professional comedians. (Justin Beiber is even in it!)

history.title: Lucifer: The Complete Second Season [DVD]
history.review_title: The show has hit its stride
history.text: The first season of Lucifer was a surprise hit. The chemistry between Tom Ellis (Lucifer) and DB Woodson (oldest brother Angel) was palpable. This season builds on the good points and keeps the chemistry going strong. Second season introduces a complex character, sometimes villain, Tricia Helfer,, as the “supreme goddess of creation/God’s Ex.” Truth in lending. This is completely recast as her role as the lead, evil humanoid Cylon from Battle Star Galactica. She did a great job in BSG, and she does a fantastic job in Lucifer – sometimes provocative, sometimes evil, and sometimes genuinely caring, but always with an undercurrent of conniving treachery. My favorite new character is Elle, God-fearing, Hispanic, forensic pathologist. She self describes as spontaneous, un-self-aware, and fun. Elle is a fantastic foil to Lucifer’s brooding and Chloe’s relentless responsibility. If you’re a Lucifer fan already, then the new season won’t disappoint, and if you are a newcomer then you can jump right in without fear of getting lost. Two nits – one of the fun things about season one is that it held to commonly held views of angels and devils in Judeo-Christian theology. Alas, in season two, the theological train leaves the rails. The introduction of a co-creator leaves monotheism in the dust. The second nit is that Tricia’s character felt a little muddled at times. By episode four, it was clear that she was very conniving and capable of killing at a whim. Then, there were attempts throughout the season up to the final episode to make her appear more sympathetic. That didn’t work as well as a might’ve. All in all though, a very nice outing for the Lucifer crew, and we’re all looking forward to seeing season three.

history.title: The Big Sick
history.review_title: Interesting premise, but falls downs based on two unlikable protagonists
history.text: I watched the DVD, not through Amazon Prime. The movie has some positive points. It shows the dynamics of a family from Pakistan that are religiously devote, but struggling with the assimilation of their youngest son, who wants to be a stand-up comedian rather than a doctor or lawyer. He also struggled with his views on the familial religion. Throughout the first half of the movie, his mother brings over a string of good Pakistani, unmarried ladies to see if there is a good fit for an arranged marriage. Some of the humor performed by the stand-up comedians is kind of funny. Some of the jokes were abysmal. In other words, the stand-up routines felt real. That said, it was hard to relate to either of the main characters. ** Beware Spoilers Follow ** Our stand-up, male protagonist lies to his family and his would be friend with benefits (several conversations early on in the film make it clear that he intends on pursuing an intimate relationship without ever becoming more than ... I'm not sure what a good phrase is. He is asked by Emily "can you imagine a world where we get together permanently?" His answer, "no." OK, so, maybe he is a schlepp, but Emily is nice, right? Um, no, we find out that she has been hiding the fact that she was previously married and divorced. OK, that is a common thing in modern America. What makes her tough to relate to is that she left her husband, because the sex got boring. He did not cheat. He was not abusive. He was not a drug user. By all accounts he was loving and supportive. Emily left him simply because "life is too short for boring sex." After the couple breaks up and our stand-up friend sleeps with another woman almost immediately, he is called, because Emily is in the hospital. He pretends to be her husband and signs for a dangerous medical procedure, and then, at last, he contacts Emily's parents. The middle third of the movie is about him coming to terms with the parents who know about his background, lies, etc. Ultimately Emily's parents are much more accepting that his are, and they come to like him. Emily however is not so easily convinced. They break up again, and he moves to New York City. They could have ended there, but there is a scene at the end that makes the audience believe they might get back together, but ... it might not be so. The premise of the movie lead me to believe that there was going to be an exploration of cultural integration on all sides, but in the end he is kicked out of his Pakastani family and left to go to New York as a sexually promiscuous comedian with low prospects for ever making it big.

history.title: The Exception [DVD]
history.review_title: A very well done film that is 9/10 love story and 1/10 moral dilemma
history.text: I really enjoyed this film. This review has the benefit of seeing previous reviews. Yes, as stated, there is some relatively obvious sex and nudity. This is not a movie for the kiddies. If you were going into the film expecting an expose of the deposed Kaiser (which, honestly the trailers do kind of imply) then I could see those aspects being undesirable. The movie actually revolves around two characters, and the Kaiser, the Princess, and their entourage are bit players to bring out the main plot. ** Beware Spoilers Follow ** The main characters are Hauptman (Captain) Brandt and an attractive, female member of the house staff. We find out almost immediately that the maid is actually a British spy, and Brandt figures it out pretty rapidly too. By the by, so does the Kaiser who is still a very cagey person despite his staff's feelings about his capabilities. She is also Jewish, something that she reveals to Brandt almost immediately. So, the story really revolves around what to do with conflicted loyalties and what does devotion and honor mean when your country has devolved into a despicable morass. (Just to be clear, there were no parallels either obvious or even implied with history after World War II - in other words, this movie steers well clear of any current controversies, and for one this viewer appreciated that.) The Kaiser, the Princess, their Aide de Camp, Brandt, and the love interest cum spy were all very well developed characters and all of them were appealing in some ways -- and clearly not in others. All in all, a very good film about a difficult period in human history.

history.text: Let me say right off the bat that I am a huge Kurosawa fan, but I have to write that this is probably the best Samurai film ever. The usual great swordplay scenes, but the film takes off from there. There is a scene half way through of folks sitting in a house listening to the rainfall outside. The flashbacks make it one of the great Japanese Movie scenes (and this is really saying something!) and there is the thing with the linking of the film score and the working of folks...every thing they do is in rhythm with the sound track music and really cool once you tumble to it. Every stroke with a plane or strike on a chisel or slash of harvesting a rice crop is all done as part of the music...perhaps unique in cinema. Not to be missed if you are a student of film! I had resisted watching this for some time, having seen many of the earlier Zatoichi films and not realizing just how different it really is. Be sure to watch to the very last second...there is a twist!

history.title: Matagi JAPANESE EDITION
history.review_title: aka Forest Of The Little Bear: One of the least known and greatest Japanese films
history.text: This is one of the most difficult DVDs for an American to find or even watch. It is the story of an old bear hunter who is a master of his craft. He only takes one bullet as he hunts in the beautiful snow covered mountains. On one such excursion he accidently kills a mother bear who has a cub. He is absolutely stricken as he has violated one of the prime rules of bear hunting. He takes the cub in and raises it. The cub reaches maturity and the old hunter releases it into the mountains so it can fulfill its' natural role. He and the bear love each other. A hard time comes and the bear starts to hunt humans, for he has no natural fear of them because of his raring. The old man knows full well what he must to make amends...it is, after, all his responsibility. Thus is set in motion the culmination of a tragedy of positively shakespearean proportions. The nobility of both the bear and the hunter will moisten your eyes One of the better Japanese movies, I have no idea why it has never been distributed here. One of Toshio Goto's greatest films..And nearly unobtainable. Here's hoping for a Criterion release soon!

history.title: Bobby Deerfield

history.text: This is a weird movie by director Sidney Pollack, featuring Al Pacino. (SPOILERS BELOW). The racing scenes are reasonably good. There are two Grand Prix featured: France and Jarama (Spain). The car used by Pacino character is a Brabham-Alfa Romeo, driven by the late Brazilian driver Carlos Pace. There are two main plots: in one of them, Pacino is trying to figure aout, together with the team's engineers, what mechanical shaninigans may have caused the fatal accident of his team mate, The other plot is the most important. Pacino goes to clinic in Germany to interview a survivor of the above mentioned crash, looking for clues. There, he find a mysterious and highly uptight woman. She asks him for a ride out of the clinic, and their relationship blossoms, with Pacino cheating on his girlfriend/wife whatever. But the woman is terminally ill. The movie portrays Bobby Deerfield as egocentric jerk without heart, and being in love with such a terminally ill lady makes him open up a little and be less self-centered. But the woman dies soon after, and Pacino ends the movie alone, withou any inch that he has changes or not. After the Dark is so ridiculously stupid that you'll be wondering if this is actually supposed to be a comedy. The plot assumes the event of a global nuclear war in which 20 highschool students are trying to decide who gets the right to live in a quarantined environment with only enough living space and resources designated for 10 persons for a span of one year. The decision of who gets to stay and who gets culled from the herd is decided by classist and sexist decree. Once the tally is in, the others either get shot like cattle (to spare them from suffering in the wilderness) or they try to outrun their fate. Selection for living in the bunker is most preferential to females because they can breed and thus eventually re-populate the earth .. that is, after they leave the bunker when the food and air goes out. No one ever factors in that even a year after worldwide nuclear detonation, life on earth would unbearable and so incredibly contaminated with radioactive waste that it would not be possible to survive. After the Dark is nothing more than a sarcastic take on an otherwise frightening reality. If you're interested in seeing realistic view of nuclear warfare than I suggest you track down the film, 'Threads'.

history.title: Dogfight
history.text: The premise sounds so cruel....a group of Marines each try to find the ugliest girl as a date for the dance, aka,"dogfight", and the one who's date is voted the ugliest (unbeknownst to the girls) wins the $50 prize money. The story is about the two main characters, Eddie and his ugly date---Rose, on the last night before he and his buddies ship out to Viet Nam. I don't know how they were able to make this movie so touching, so human and so funny when the subject matter, on the surface, is so offensive. The scenes with Eddie's three best buddies are filled with youthful male humor---vulgar, crude and immature--- yet it rings so true and really is just plain hilarious. You love these guys. They don't know where they're going when they ship out, but they're together and nothing else matters. And the friendship that develops between Eddie and Rose also rings completely true. I like the way the "ugly" girl turns out to be so witty and interesting and how the cute guy, over the course of the night, is so affected by her. The whole movie is just a wonderful surprise. From beginning to end. I still laugh whenever I think of one of the guys looking for ugly girls at the bus station and finding Miss Two Bears. This movie doesn't hit you over the head with anything and that's one of the best things about it...it unfolds gently, with humor and grace.

history.title: Children Of Heaven [DVD]

What we see on the news and read in the paper is so narrow. This is a window to a world that, in one viewing, taught me what I should have already known. It's a beautiful movie with such brilliant colors I couldn't believe it, about the simple predicament of a brother and sister. It's also a real eye-opener that shows us we are all the same, with the same struggles and hopes for our loved ones. With this one movie, I stopped painting with so broad a brush as far as Arabs go. I wish everyone in America would see this.

The family abuse just doesn't come across well especially in her character. The ending was just a little unlikely. Even taken as a fairy tale there are a lot of holes in the story.

Overall a little clumsy but entertaining. Difficult to decide which is imagination and which is reality. If the fantasy was all in her head then to suddenly recover her mental health after finishing a graphic novel doesn't quite make sense. On the other hand, if the graphic novel part actually happened, then everyone was too nonchalant about the occurrence. And what really happened to her doctor, killed by whom? So it's worth seeing and so much better than the usual stuff in this genre.

Look up the village of Capel Celyn after you finish the movie and Stanly's line of 'we had to go' and the police search will become clear. Entertaining with major flaws. The flaws are in the story itself and the characters actions.. The story? Where is it going and what is it trying to tell us? As is, it isn't much more than a campfire tale of curiosity. Most of the characters seem to act, excuse me, out of character. How? Well, an old woman kills herself horrifically in front of the one she has taken care of for almost a century. Yes, she is tired, but this is the act of a cruel or selfish person, which, she clearly is not. The Sheriff, (well played by David Elliot) who seems to be a reasonable, thinking, conservative person suddenly decides to take in an obviously neurotic teenager. Aaron von Dusen (Kim Contes) who is well aware of the danger, ignores it. Then there is Rufus, who has apparently lived for a long, long time but acts pretty much like a typical teenager with all of the experience of the typical teenager. A predator like this would have to have a descent memory in order to survive and yet this kid can't remember anything about his origins.
Hmm, Not much to say, Trite story lines, mediocre acting, weak directing.

history.title: Sanctuary: Season 4
history.text: My family and I loved seasons 1-3, but after the first few episodes of season 4 we quit watching. The story lines towards the end of season 3 were becoming increasingly ridiculous, which was frustrating after the excellence of seasons 1 and 2. However, we were willing to keep on just to see what happened. When the lesbianism and similar fare reared their ugly heads towards the beginning of season 4, though, we were done with "Sanctuary." Had Tapping et al simply continued to focus on making a fun sci-fi show instead of trying to make stupid political statements, I imagine Sanctuary could have had a much longer run. I didn't watch the musical episode, thankfully, as we quit watching before that. But even without these other issues, we found the minimal presence of both John Druitt and Nikola Tesla in season 4 to be hugely disappointing. They were two of the best characters on the show, but were essentially dropped or minimized towards the end of season 3. Bad move. Anyway, that's my 2 cents. Others may still like this season, but our family decided it wasn't worth the bother anymore.

history.title: Kitchen Stories [DVD]
history.review_title: I don't know what it is about this movie...
history.text: I first saw this movie around 9 years ago when I rented it on a whim. I wasn't expecting a whole lot, but I enjoy foreign films and immediately fell in love with this one. I honestly don't know what it is about this movie for me. It does have some funny parts, but it also makes me feel a little bit melancholy too. I still adore it. In a nutshell, a Swedish company is researching efficiency in kitchens and heads to Norway to study the kitchen habits of Norwegian bachelors. One researcher's assigned bachelor isn't very happy about the study and refuses to allow the man in his house, let alone in his kitchen. Add to the mix the bachelor's long-time friend who becomes unhappy about the situation himself. To me, it's both a funny/sad and touching story. The actors are perfect in their parts and I especially enjoy the character of the Swedish researcher--Folke Nilsson (portrayed by Tomas Norström). However, I think both he and Joachim Calmeyer as Isak Bjørvik are excellent. It has a small bit of swearing, for those who are concerned about such things, but it is definitely worth watching more than once. I was beside myself with joy when I came across it in my local thrift store for only $3.00. I immediately purchased it and have not regretted the buy. "Kitchen Stories" is a definite keeper in my book.

history.title: Gravity
history.review_title: Most irritating movie I've seen in a long time
history.text: Giving this movie one star is being pretty generous, as I can sum up my opinion of it in two words: deeply annoying. Looong shots of earth from outer space and looong segments of Bullock spinning in space while breathing heavily had me desperately looonging for the fast-forward button. SO boring and frustrating. But the single most irritating thing about this film for me was Sandra Bullock. I've seen other reviewers complain that she was miscast. I'm not sure if she was miscast or if the script and fleshing out of her character are what led to the major "suck" factor. Either way, I couldn't stand Bullock/Dr. Ryan Stone. I found myself repeatedly wondering how in the world such an utterly useless and incompetent idiot would ever end up on a space mission in the first place. For the majority of the film she was grunting, swearing, and panting/hyperventilating. Frankly, it sounded like somebody with painful constipation. Between that and shouting "no, no, no, no, no!" ad nauseum, I began to think it would be a great service to humanity to just leave her spinning forever in space. I honestly haven't had a movie character annoy me this deeply since Jar-Jar Binks. Seriously. Anyway, clearly some folks enjoyed this movie. Sadly, I was not one of them. If someone is contemplating whether or not to give this film a try, here's something that may help.....if you, like me, absolutely hated "2001: A Space Odyssey" but loved "Darkstar," then you will probably hate "Gravity." Alternatively, if you're a "2001...Odyssey" fan, then we have nothing to discuss, but you'll probably like "Gravity." Good luck.

I picked this up at the library because it sounded very similar to "Criminal Minds." I guess in some ways it is similar, but this show just goes several steps beyond what I'm willing to watch. There are some "Criminal Minds" episodes I have to skip as well, but the bits of nudity, gay stuff, and occasional strong swearing in "Wire..." were especially off-putting to me. And when a modified version of the horrific Judas Cradle torture device made its way into the storyline, I was done. I think the show had potential, but was just too vulgar and nauseating for me. It is definitely not my cup of tea, so went right back to the library. And what is the deal with the title? "Wire in the Blood" makes absolutely no sense and does nothing to reflect the show's subject material whatsoever. Big thumbs down.

history.title: Last Man Standing Season 2
history.text: We loved season one of "Last Man..." but were really, really disappointed by season two. Yes, there are a few funny jokes, but there are also a lot more in-your-face political episodes that feature more and more of the obnoxious liberal character Ryan Vogelson (Boyd's natural father). I absolutely despise the character and thought the show was infinitely better before they included this stupid and annoying jerk. We deal with enough Liberal idiots in real life that I certainly don't need a fictional TV show to further elevate my blood pressure. And the way Kristin (Boyd's mother) constantly caves and caters to this idiot after he ditched her for three years is completely implausible. Another problem I have is the cast change that dumped Alexandra Krosney in favor of Amanda Fuller for the role of Kristin Baxter. Fuller is immensely annoying and hard to watch. I thought Krosney did a better job playing the part and think replacing her was a big mistake. Finally, I was not at all happy to see a lot more dishonesty and immorality in the episodes for this season. The two oldest daughters act like complete whores and constantly lie to and undermine their father--with their mother's blessing, no less--and it's all played for laughs. It may be the norm today, but I don't find devaluing and disrespecting fathers to be the least bit funny. The immorality isn't funny either and it's pretty disgusting that the show could only manage one season of decent writing and episodes before devolving into offensive drivel. We finally quit watching part-way through. If subsequent seasons are this bad, I don't think we'll bother with them either.

history.title: Librarians, the - Season 03
history.text: Our family loved the first two seasons of "The Librarians." Noah Wyle is one of my favorite actors and I was especially impressed to read comments he made about wanting to make a "family friendly" television show. So we were excited to watch season 3 of the show. Unfortunately, it looks like "family friendly" has kind of gone by the wayside. Most of the episodes are as good as they were in season 1 and 2, but then they decided to include a revolting lesbian attraction and kiss between Cassandra and a female vampire. It was disgusting and offensive and certainly not something my husband or I wanted to see. And we definitely didn't want our children to see that garbage. But even without that, the whole thing with Flynn and Eve messing around together is annoying and drags down the story lines--particularly since I can't stand the character of Eve anyway. I also dislike how the stories, overall, don't focus on Flynn as much since he's the main reason I started watching it in the first place. The only other character I like is Jenkins, so episodes that primarily focus on the other librarians are a real drag. So, sadly, it looks like we're through with this show. It's really disappointing that they chose to include gay trash, but at least I didn't waste our hard-earned money on this season and just borrowed it from the library.

This would have added to the excitement of the film. Also, the art of disguise is much overlooked (the Bourne Identify overlooked this too--their writers didn't follow the book). When Wick walks into a party and the protector of a target he is hired to kill recognizes him, that was illogical! He should have attended the party in disguise and cleverly escape and maybe a security camera would reveal he did the killing and then plan a Wick search party and another big fight. history.text: This series split my opinion between the serial killer and the police. What will repetitiously catch your attention is the long delays between the police personnel responding to each other, it was like they were buying time to stretch the series timing because their scripts were so poorly written they compensated with silence--that made this a two for me--don't bore your viewers. Those long blank looks they give each other did not resonate logically! Gillian Anderson was too old for this part as a promiscuous predator with her peers. When they tried to make her look sexy in segments she actually looked repulsive--the shower profile scene for one! The other downgrade for me is that this whole series was filmed too dark--it was gloomy most of the time and you find yourself straining to see what is happening! There are ways to adjust cameras to allow viewers to see things happening in the dark of night--maybe the sets were so cheap they darkened backgrounds so you could hardly enjoy the series. I think a more optimistic person should have had some license to give hope to the script of the wife and children of the serial killer--that was so lame. Anyway, I will not watch this again or recommend to potential buyers.

history.title: Food Beware: The French Organic Revolution
history.text: Every farmer/rancher out there should be made to watch this documentary, as well as every school kid & parent. Want to know why the cancer rate is so high these days? Pesticides & synthetics in our food. This doc is packed with info. See it. Read labels on food products before you toss the item in your shopping cart. Don't be lazy like I was for years & would not take the time to read the label. Don't assume, like I did for years and years, just because the product is on your supermarket shelf that it is safe to eat. So many food manufacturers just don't give a damn about you or your family; you are nothing more than a number, a way for them to make money. Whether you or your kids come down with cancer, whether your kids are born deformed or autistic and/or with bi-polar disorder means nothing to them. It's about $$$; it's about the profit margin. Nothing personal at all. It's always been that way. Get this: farmers who use cancer-causing pesticides will not eat their own produce. Why? Why would they endanger their own? On the other hand, it's perfectly fine if YOU purchase this poisoned product. You don't matter. Note: I did not say all food growers are this way. Not all food manufacturers are money-grubing entities without a conscience. Some actually do care. Buy organic. Buy food that is free of synthetics; buy gluten-free; buy high fructose-free. Make the effort. Support the organic food movement. Stop consuming sodas. Don't let your kids near that stuff.

history.title: IMAX: Rocky Mountain Express [4K UHD]
history.review_title: I have a Lot to Learn!
history.text: 20 years ago my young son and I used to ride our bikes down to the train station in our little California town of Moorpark. We would wait to watch for the freight trains come through as they rumbled through the station. Sometimes on a rare occasion an old steam engine would come through. He had g-scale trains and an electronic sound station train whistle played through our sound system. His older sister did not like that one bit! We had lots of train videos and watched them frequently. Today he is grown and I am an old guy, but I love technology. I saw this video and I had to have it to view with my son on our LG UHD TV through our nice sound system. I bought the 4k version that comes with a regular blu ray. I found out the hard way that my Sony and Samsung 4k upconverting blu ray players will not play the 4k disk. I was disappointed, but the blu ray was beautiful with great sound. So when the actual 4k players become more reasonable price wise, I'll get one. The history lesson and beautiful scenery was worth it! Update: 9-10..I finally bought my 4k player and it is certainly worth it. Everything is crystal clear and the sound is incredible. I can't understand any of the less than 5 reviews. If you don't like trains, buy it for demonstration purposes! The price has come way down too for the player and this documentary .

history.text: I kept comparing this to Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey -- more specifically where Keir Dullea is stuck in a small pod outside the main spaceship -- after having retrieved the corpse of his fellow astronaut -- murdered by the onboard HAL 9000 computer. This movie comes nowhere close to recreating the sense of desperation and daring that was demonstrated in a film originating from the 1970's. In this sense, we don't really see anything new (although, thankfully, it's not just a special effects-type film). George Clooney just plays his usual self, so we get nothing new there. But, we do get to view a higher level of dramatic acting from Sandra Bullock. Overall, despite the tremendous hype, the film is really just above average, so if you rent it, don't be expecting too much.

This film is a continuation of the semi-interesting "Hunger Games." The original film was a rip of "The Running Man" and "Logan's Run." Since the first film was so successful (although I couldn't see why), I decided to rent the sequel. I thought, well, it's bound to be distracting at the least. It wasn't. It added nothing to the original film in terms of originality and even lost points because it just re-purposed a hackneyed concept. The first half of the film is excruciating. Nothing (I mean nothing) happens other than as a predictable set-up for the second half, which was just a less exciting recycling of the first movie. With judicious editing, the first half of the film could have been reduced to about 12 minutes. After the second half was completed, you are left with nothing but a teaser for a third film. At that point I felt that this whole enterprise might have made a second-rate mini-series for TV. The only positive thing I can say is that I think that Jennifer Lawrence has actual talent. She under-plays her character in a professional manner, and has the look and style of an actress who needs a better forum to show off her abilities. Otherwise, save your cash and just buy a bag of Doritos.

I didn't find much originality here. It seemed like every panic scene from every sci fi movie spliced together. The characters reminded me of that classic Twilight Zone episode where a group of people (including a clown) are trapped inside some kind of tall cylindrical enclosure, without knowing why. Though the production values are fairly good, it's not enough to make an appealing series. Most of the problems with modern TV programs of this nature are displayed here in abundance. Unlike Chris Carter's successful "X-Files," this thing is devoid of any adroit ad libs, humor or self-deprecation. I wouldn't have the patience to sit week after week to find out bits about the stock characters represented, nor would I be enthralled sufficiently to find out (or care) about the mutants/aliens/monsters that have rocked the world. And I can imagine all the spin-off story-lines that might try to link these birthday-centric characters. My first overall impression is that any series based on this premise would be tedious and redundant.
A "let down" from the original but still full of blood-and-guts entertainment.
Instantly forgettable but good material if you just feel like going mindless for a while.

history.title: Non-Stop
history.text: Better than expected. The plot is actually absurd, but you don't realize that the basic premise of the whole calamity is based on an absurdity until somewhere near the end. Lots of holes throughout, but the action moves forward at a steady clip, so the viewer doesn't have time to contemplate how a lot of the storyline doesn't hold together. Some scenes actually build up a respectable amount of tension. Good acting and direction.

history.review_title: If You Don't Already Know and Enjoy This Kind of Film, Just Move On
history.text: Not nearly as good as "Machete". The film is designed to entertain a very limited audience that enjoys trashy, cheap, B-level movie re-creations. In this sense it does an okay job. The ending "trailer" shows a "Machete in Space" sequel, which I really hope was just a joke because two Machete films is more than enough. I fear a third film may be inevitable, however, since there were several major loose strings left untied at the end of "Machete Kills."

history.review_title: It was fun to see Mickey Rourke as his Marv character again
history.text: As most would agree, the sequel is not nearly as interesting/compelling as the first film. Nevertheless, Eva Green (as Ava) really carries the show. She is the centerpiece of this movie, and moves it along with her shifts from a complete bitch to someone with a hidden heart. Beyond that her performance is memorizing and stunning. She exudes raw sexuality that completely manipulates Josh Brolin (Dwight), and it's hard not to fall into Dwight's weaknesses. It was fun to see Mickey Rourke as his Marv character again. I missed seeing Clive Owen, but you can't have everything. Powers Boothe is outstanding as the big bad guy. All in all this presented a pretty entertaining film for me. I didn't expect as much as from "Sin City," so I didn't cry about some of the let-downs. As a sequel it still had plenty of punch, so I didn't find myself terribly disappointed.

history.title: The Devil's Rejects (Unrated Widescreen Edition)
history.text: I was told to watch this by a friend. I thought this movie was really stupid. There is not one character I liked. I’m not sure if the viewer is suppose to root for the main characters at the end but if so that’s completely ridiculous as they are terrible people who do horrific things. They are psychopathic murderers not anti-heroes. I literally didn’t care what happened to any of them. The only good thing I have to say about it is that the movie has some good music. That’s it.

history.title: Cult of Chucky (Unrated)
history.text: The first Child’s Play will always be the scariest. Like the first Nightmare on Elm Street it can’t be outdone by a sequel or remake. I found Seed and Bride to be cheesy and corny. I hated them. Like Nightmare on Elm Steet the franchise of Child’s Play became more comical with each sequel. That said I was pleasantly surprised to watch Curse of Chucky. It brought back the scare so I was looking forward to Cult of Chucky thinking hopefully that the franchise had been revived in a good way. I was wrong. The overt gore and subpar acting by some of the cast was bad. The whole storyline was a letdown. I was excited to see the Andy Barkley character back but he was never utilized to his full potential. He’s in maybe a total of 20 minutes of the movie if that. The plot with the multiple Chuckys and stupid jokes made this movie more like Seed and Bride. Overall I was pretty disappointed. I watched this while I was still riding a binge-buzz having just finished the awesome second season of Stranger Things on Netflix. This movie pretty killed that. I realized quickly I should’ve just started rewatching ST or went to bed. I will say that Jennifer Tilly was great as always and I really enjoyed Fiona Dourif’s acting and character. She looks so much like her dad that at times, especially at the end, I thought I was looking at Brad Dourif.

history.title: Jaws 3
history.text: The first Jaws was the awesome. The sequels of course weren’t as good. I remember watching this as a kid and loving it just because of the underwater tunnel and restaurant scenes. Watching it again as an adult I can definitely see it’s more of a fair movie. It’s pretty unbelievable to me now. It does have a great cast. This is one of those movies you really just watch for a little fun or as a time killer. I’ve definitely seen worse but I’ve also also seen better. My baby cousin who is 20 years younger than me had no idea there was even a Jaws 3 made. He thought they stopped at 2. He’d never even heard of it when I told him and thought I was pulling his leg. Made me feel kinda old ha ha.

history.title: Jaws: The Revenge
history.text: In my opinion this is the worst of the sequels to Jaws. I still don’t understand why Michael Caine and Lorraine Gary chose to be in it.

history.title: Fear, Inc.
history.text: The acting is so bad. The main character is incredibly annoying. I didn’t find it funny or scary, just really stupid. I can’t believe anyone rated this movie 5 Stars. Just watch The Game. It’s soooo much better.

I thought this might be a decent time killer but I hated this movie. The main character is a victim of his own very bad decisions. Watching someone make such stupid choices is hard to watch. It starts to feel ridiculous. There’s a twist but I had it figured out long before the end. Watch Fatal Attraction instead. It’s a much better movie. I feel like I wasted 6.00 on this one.

history.title: The Box
history.text: I couldn’t get past the terrible southern accents. I’m from the Deep South and it’s laughable how bad some southern accents are in movies. Ask other southerners. They will say the same thing. This is supposed to be based in Virginia. The accents portrayed here are way too thick to be believable. I have family in Virginia and they do not have accents like those who live in the Deep South, like those portrayed in this movie. It may be a minor thing but it was off-putting to me and made it hard to even watch or take the movie seriously.

history.title: Flatliners
history.text: It was ok. The original is a really good movie with an amazing cast. I had no real bias going in because I was actually looking forward to the movie since it isn’t a total remake per say. Yet something was missing. The story just didn’t grab me like it’s predecessor did. I didn’t care for the characters like I did the first either. There isn’t really much of a climax here. Especially if you’ve seen the first one. There is a lot of partying and it didn’t really go into as much depth of the characters’ backstories as the previous one did. The first is one I’ve watched again from time to time. This is one I won’t be watching again. I also feel like Keifer Sutherland’s role was wasted here. I don’t understand why they didn’t have him play Nelson like he did in the previous movie. That would've made it more interesting to me. Even a small, little Easter egg would’ve been a nice tip of the hat to the original. Instead he plays just an everyday ordinary doctor/teacher with no real purpose other than maybe putting pressure on medical students. I don’t even remember his name in this film. I feel like that was a bit of wasted potential. Ellen Page was great but why they chose to go the route they did with her character so soon in the film is beyond me. Especially since she is the most well-known actor (other than Sutherland) in the film. She was pretty much the only character I really cared even a little bit about. I feel like the first movie had more of a lesson about forgiveness than this one. The first was about asking forgiveness for the sins you’ve committed against others. This one supposedly is about forgiving oneself but you don’t actually realize it till a small scene which is thrown in near the end. Overall I give it 2 stars instead of 3 because to me it’s more of a meh movie than a good one.

history.title: The Dark Tower
history.text: I thought it was ok. I haven’t read the books yet and even I could tell and wished the story had been more fleshed out. I felt like a lot was left unexplained about the entire story and the Dark Tower world. The good thing is that this has made me want to read the books as I find the story very interesting. I know that this is an entire series of books written by King who is one of my favorite authors. I wished maybe that they would’ve went the route of several sequels like LoTR to give us the entire story instead of trying to explain everything in one film. I can see why book readers would be disappointed here as I find the lack of depth portrayed here disappointing myself and I haven’t even read the books yet. As a stand alone movie I think it is good but definitely not great. It had a lot of potential and could’ve been better. It was rather short and I was surprised at how quickly it was over. I read recently that a Dark Tower series is coming out soon. I’m looking forward to seeing that. In the meantime I plan to start reading the books.

Good but not great. For me it was more of a fun movie than a scary one. There wasn’t as much gore as I’d thought there’d be considering that a lot of movies these days go that route. There is a lot of language though. In my opinion I feel like it didn’t go into enough depth with the relationship of the losers. The bond of the kids wasn’t explored as much as I would’ve liked and it seemed to barely scratch the surface of their fierce loyalty to one another. It left me feeling as though they weren’t that close. The CGI in my opinion also wasn’t that good. There are a couple scenes with the woman and the leper that I thought the CGI was pretty sloppy. There was plenty of source material from King’s book so I have no idea why they chose for Stan to be afraid of a painting. In the book he gets locked in a building with 2 dead boys. That would’ve been much scarier in my opinion. My biggest disappointment was the way Mike’s character was handled. In the book he’s the son of a very kind and loving family who happen to own a farm. The family including Mike experience racism firsthand. His father was one of my favorite characters in the book even though he wasn’t a very big one. It’s from him that Mike gets his love of history and learns how to handle the discrimination he experiences. Mike’s love and knowledge of the town history is taken away and given to Ben in this film which serves no real purpose. Ben is already suppose to be the engineer of the group and Mike the historian. Instead Mike just becomes a stand-in character in this film. The other character change I didn’t like was Bev. She comes across as older than the boys to me. I don’t know if it’s her make up or personality but she certainly seems more like a teenager than a middle schooler. In the book she is also the one whose aim sends Pennywise scurrying back to the sewers. In the film she becomes the damsel in distress which needs to be rescued near the end. It somewhat took away from the independence of her character. I did like how the relationship with Bill and Georgie was more fleshed out. You get a real feeling of how much Bill loved his brother in this film. Overall I think it’s a pretty good movie but not flawless. People online seem to have very strong feelings about this film. If you criticize it whatsoever some people seem to become very upset. I don’t understand why people take the opinions of others so personally these days. Especially over something as trivial as a movie.

history.title: The Starlost - The Complete Series
history.text: This was a Canadian video-taped science fiction series featuring a pretty well-known cast to sci-fi fans: Walter Koenig (Chekov from Star Trek), Keir Dullea (2001: A Space Odyssey), and Alexandra Bastedo (The Champions), but that's about all it has going for it. Makes Space 1999 seem like Shakespeare, and viewers might find the short-lived "Quark" sci-fi comedy more entertaining. Despite the fact that this remastered set includes the entire series 16 episodes instead of the initial 10, "Starlost" still comes up short--despite some interesting guest stars, Sterling Hayden and Frank Converse to name a few. The series apparently had a lot going for it even with noted science writer Ben Bova as a technical consultant, but alas, the show is still a yawner. Fans would have to wait yet another two years, until Gerry Anderson's "Space 1999" made its debut in America's living rooms re-igniting the excitement of big-budget science fiction. Rumor has it that the series was so poorly done and so utterly dull that its creator, the respected Harlan Ellison, disowned it and signed the pilot to the series wth his pen name "Cordwainer Bird." The series seems more appropriate as a cure for insomnia and was thankfully terminated after one season. The premise of the show revolved around a group of survivors from the destroyed planet Earth who were on an endless journey thru the farthest reaches of space in a huge spaceship consisting mainly of plastic, mod, circa early 1970's furniture and cardboard sets--not unlike seen on "Moonbase 3" which debuted the same year. For sci-fi purists only...

history.title: The World in Conflict
history.text: Once again the Timeless Media Group takes relatively old newsreels and calls them "rare archival footage" and attractively repackages this content to resemble documentaries into two DVDs for the unsuspecting history aficionado who, thinking he will be getting something truly unique, ends up with nothing more than old WWII news footage accompanied by bland and uninspiring narration. Don't bother paying the Amazon price listed here, or even $4.99 at the Ross-Dress-for-Less where you can usually fine such sets. You would be better served saving your money and investing in a far superior documentary series like the expertly assembled boxed set of the classic (and, in my opinion, the finest WWII documentary series ever made), Thames Television's "The World at War" or the more recent alternative, "BBC History of WWII"--both remarkable in content and depth and far more engaging for the armchair historian or casual viewer.

history.title: Secret Agent AKA Danger Man: The Complete Collection (Slimline Packaging)
history.review_title: Your ticket to danger and action...
history.text: discovered this series on KTEH 54-San Jose, a local PBS station, and I was astounded by the quality of the acting and of the writing. The dialogue is simply outstanding and far outpaces anything you will see on primetime tv today featuring the work of many well-known directors like Peter Yates (Bullitt), who are well-respected in the UK and abroad. I think John Drake is the epitome of cool--examine the icy interchange between Darren Nesbitt and McGoohan in "Sting in the Tail" for example--you will be riveted to the screen. Supporting cast include reliable, stock actors from the ITC stable and some notable British film stars like John Fraser, Bernard Lee, (M from the James Bond films) and Finlay Currie. Personally, I never grow tired watching these expertly written episodes over and over again--a product of Great Britain's when it still had something resembling an empire. The strength in Secret Agent lies in the scripts, characterization of the lead (McGoohan), and the gritty realism portrayed. In fact, McGoohan directed several of the episodes including "The Paper Chase" which has some whimsical, if not humorous, elements to it--I won't spoil it for you, but let's just say Drake's means of eluding the bad guys in this installment is a go-kart! Drake is not infalliable and does not always win the day: watch the episode "Judgment Day" and see why. Personally, these hour long episodes are far superior than the 30 minute "Danger Man" episodes that were produced a few years before. Secret Agent is played seriously--not like the candy coated sci fi James Bond "espionage entertainments" served up by Brosnan and Co. ridiculously replete with cars that fly or laden with machine guns and death rays. No, here is an agent that, although an expert marksman, refuses to use a gun, but instead relies on his wits to get the job done. Take my word for it, Secret Agent Mega set is the ticket to hours of viewing pleasure and an interesting window into Cold War politics and intrigue--Enjoy!

history.title: CALLAN, SET 1
history.review_title: And you thought LeCarre's "Spy Who Came in From the Cold" was dark and bleak?
history.text: Exceptional drama from Thames Television from the late 60's-early 70's starring the late Edward Woodward, more familiar to us here in the States as the principal character in "The Equalizer" series that ran during the mid-80's. Woodward plays Callan, a spy for a secret arm of the British Secret Service, so secret in fact that the his boss, William Squire, is identified not by name but by his code, "Hunter." Callan, middle-aged and more comfortable discussing the rudiments of Napoleonic warfare and collecting toy soldiers and wargaming, is reluctantly the "top man" takes "all the dirty jobs" with an eye on his target and other on his ruthless colleagues--expertly played by the duplicitous Anthony Valentine as Toby Meres and the impulsive Patrick Mower as Cross--who are more likely to twist a knife in Callan's back than provide the necessary back up on a mission. With that said, the episodes are tremendously entertaining if short on action by American standards. The scripts are superb, as the writers have clearly disposed of the "champagne and caviar" adventures of James Bond, but instead present a terribly complex but realistic portrait of cold war espionage in all of its ugliness--the deception, torture, duplicity, and divided loyalties that characterize spying at it's most ruthless. Supporting cast is also excellent with the late Russell Hunter as the not-so-bright Lonely, Callan's only friend, informant, and freelance accomplice in his nefarious deeds. The episodes are presented chronologically, so it's important to watch them in consecutive order--references are made to former characters and events in a consecutive timeline as Callan's cynicism towards the Section, his superiors, and his colleagues virtually reaches a boiling point at the close of Set 1. All in all, a most enjoyable set as is Set 2 (although the second set is noteably darker in tone) but just as engaging to the viewer. If you're looking for a James Bond adventure replete with bullet-proof cars and femme fatales who look like they just stepped off the pages of a Victoria's Secret catalog, look elsewhere. Callan is the real spy deal in all its gritty ugliness.

history.title: Van Der Valk Mysteries, Set 2
history.review_title: More great stuff from Barry Foster and cast....
history.text: Set 2 obviously carries on and completes the First, and arguably best season of Van Der Valk. Cast regulars are all present: Michael Latimer (Kroon) and Susan Travers (Arlette) and round out a very satisfying conclusion to Season One of Van Der Valk. Perhaps not as edgy as the first installments at the beginning of Season One, this set can hold its own for suspense and broader character development between Van Der Valk, Kroon, and Arlette, Van Der Valk's intelligent and introspective wife. Those who prefer prodding detective stories a la "The Last Detective" and "Midsommer Murders" with John Nettles will find lots to like here. Piet Van Der Valk,(Foster) is the primary focus of this detective series that is entertaining and uncompromisingly realistic for 1970's era Amsterdam. Van Der Valk, unlike Columbo, is more apt to trust his own intuition and buck his superiors in a case than applying simple logic making for a strong, appealing central character---emotional, shrewd, and tough when the situation demands it. Suporting cast are never less than adequate, and the draw of the characters and the interesting and unusual array of crimes they solve will compel you to watch again and again. Those wanting the entire series will need to purchase the Network DVD set of the entire series with Region 2 encoding from Amazon's UK site. Just make sure you have a multiregional DVD player to view it.

history.title: The Big Red One - The Reconstruction (Two-Disc Special Edition)
history.review_title: Before "Saving Private Ryan," here is the definitive film about the American GI in WWII
history.text: Before Steven Speilberg earned accolade after accolade for his D-Day opus, Sam Fuller's "The Big Red One" was probably the most telling movie ever made about the American GI's experience in the European Theater during WWII. Here Fuller offers a sprawing account of the First Infantry Division's slogging through North Africa, Italy and then onto Germany after D-Day and eventual liberation of the Nazi camps. Uncompromisingly realistic and, at times, unflinchingly compassionate, Fuller depicts the American GI not as "hero" but as ordinary men thrown into battle--Fuller clearly sees the psyche of the American GI--warts and all--his hates and prejudices, his loves, and the trivial. Most intelligently he conveys his fear with sentimentality put aside for a naturalism rarely seen in war films up to this time. Although a difficult actor to work with at times who often found solace from a bottle, Marvin, like Richard Burton, Peter O'Toole, Oliver Reed and Richard Harris, was the consummate professional before the camera. This is one of his finest films. Supporting cast is also superb including Robert Carradine and a post-Star Wars Mark Hamill. One of the final scenes with Marvin and a young boy who he has liberated from the death camps is virtually impossible to forget and a credit to Fuller's direction. This film is a testament to his talent.

history.title: The Laughing Policeman
history.review_title: San Francisco-based police drama offers chilling opening but little else...
history.text: A native Bay Area resident, I love to watch movies filmed in 1970's San Francisco. The Laughing Policeman offers a chilling premise of eight passengers gunned down including one cop on a MUNI bus with Matthau and Dern as the two detectives charged with the task of investigating it. Quite graphic in nudity and violence for it's day, what follows is an interesting police procedural that recalls some very strong similarities to Peter Yates' Bullitt made in 1968; for example, scenes on uncompromising realism in SF General Hospital's emergency room as doctors and nurses attempt to revive one of victims from the shooting massacre. From then on the film seems to meander from suspect to suspect without much resolution or direction as each lead Matthau and Dern uncover provide yet another red herring. The film is punctuated with a few tense moments in the middle, but action fans will be disappointed with the car and bus chase on the Embarcadero (circa 1973) that pales in comparison to McQueen's tense and edge of your seat Mustang vs. Challenger duel in Bullitt (1968). Marvel at Bruce Dern's remarkable range in this picture as a optimistic and happy-go-lucky detective who is involuntarily partnered with the sardonic Matthau who is obsessed with the case and dealing with a broken marriage. It's quite a change from Dern's typical characterization as a psychopath in most Westerns and other dramas he's been in. Matthau's lifeless performance is clearly a disappointment, and he delivers his lines as if he'd rather be somewhere else. Supporting cast Joanna Cassidy and Cathy Lee Crosby, with the exception of Lou Gossett Jr, and Val Avery (a staple from Peter Falk's original Columbo) are wasted in this police drama which begins fairly strong, retains a very slow middle, and carries with it a predictable and somewhat unsatisfactory conclusion.

history.title: Combat!: Fan Favorites (50th Anniversary)
history.text: Yes, a great series and a memorable one. Morrow was a fine actor and exceptionally well-cast for his role in the series. A sad and unnecessary loss in the '82 Twilight Zone Movie movie set accident. The series' gritty realism and superb performances by many guest stars were a welcome antidote to the hi jinx from the usual historical Hogans Heroes or F Troop fare broadcast at the same time--even more so than other realistic war dramas like "Rat Patrol". Before films like "Saving Private Ryan," Combat presented heroism and serious human dramas in a tight, yet exciting fifty minutes that keeps the viewer's attention until next week 's adventure. Few shows broadcast today can even manage that.

history.title: Dark City
history.text: As an example of early Noir, Dark City has several things going for it: an interesting story, good use of cinematography and lightning, and two talented leads--Heston and Scott. While Dark City may not have all the qualities inherent in Welles' "Touch of Evil" Heston made seven years later, but demonstrates his strong commanding, masculine presence that would dominate the screen in a number of historical and biblical epics throughout the 50s and 60s.

history.title: The Final Countdown (Widescreen Edition)
history.review_title: An Irwin Allen's Time Tunnel adventure takes to the Big Screen.....
history.text: When it comes to science-fiction, time travel is always a fascinating theme. Here we have the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz transported back to Peal Harbor, December 6, 1941. Of course, the premise is fantastic and resembles the science fiction more appropriate to television a la Rod Serling's Twilight Zone, the Outer Limits, or Irwin Allen's campy but fun Time Tunnel; nevertheless, director Don Taylor manages to pull it off successfully for 100 minutes. Part of this must be attributed to the acting by Sheen, Farentino, and Douglas who look and sound credible throughout. There is an authentic feel of earnestness and veracity to the film, owed in part to the enormity of the subject and the men who work and live within the Nimitz and, of course, a most tempting proposition: suppose you could change history? Would you? Of course, there is the guilty pleasure of seeing two Japanese Zero fighters literally obliterated by an F-14 Tomcat and an intriguing "what-if" storyline spoiled only by a lackluster and unsatisfactory ending which disappoints

history.title: Backfire
history.text: There appear to be several different versions (or packagers) of this fine little film. Mine is the Platinum Disc one, which is 90 minutes, full-frame, and uncensored. The timing and A.R. are not those given for the original production, but, if anything is missing, I didn't notice (relative to the version that shows on HD cable channels). The image is rather soft in places, like a 480i picture, but not in every scene; most of the movie (and, yes, the fleshy bits) look like a 480p DVD. I think the bit rate got up to 7.5 Mb/s in places, which is excellent detail for a DVD. Go figure. Being a rather intimate mystery story, the reduction to full-frame doesn't really hurt so much. Worth watching.

history.title: Big Bad Mama [Blu-ray]
history.text: The Blu-ray is a definite upgrade from the DVD, although not as much as one might expect. Much of the film, though not all, seems to have been shot with long lenses, low light and/or cheap filmstock. It almost looks blown up (enlarged) in places. Still, it's the best version I've seen since the theatrical release. What I didn't recall was how unusual Wm. Shatner's performance was; note the economy of gesture when he lets Joan Prather escape. A fun film.

history.title: Little Fauss & Big Halsy [Blu-ray]
history.text: The film is entertaining enough, but nothing special. However, Redford gives the most clinically exact portrayal of a full-bore psychopath (not a slasher film serial killer) you'll probably ever see unless you actually meet one. I think it takes him about 10 minutes of screen time to wangle food, shelter, sex and money, starting with nothing but his shirtless body. He uses people relentlessly (like an untalented version of Rip Torn's character in Payday). It's interesting that Fauss's mother distrusts him from the time they meet; most people don't know they've been with a true psychopath until he's gone (and taken what he wants).
