history.text: I give this two stars because I love Katherine Heigl and I give her credit for risking looking bad in a movie. She really didn't do her career any good making a movie in which she plays a lesbian. That said: just watching the trailer (I won't watch the movie but I did watch the trailer), it's surprising how unappealing lesbians can make themselves, and how one always looks better, more attractive, softer and more feminine than the other. Again, Heigl does the very difficult thing and makes herself the less-attractive one. This took guts, as an actress. My heart went out to her screen mother. The trailer was painful to watch, knowing that poor woman would have to see her daughter, who she hope can be a good mate to a husband and mom to grandkids, who has all the resources for success as a mother and wife (doesn't Katherine Heigl always deliver those things?) prove to be otherwise. A good roommate? Maybe, for many years. I hope the movie makes money just based on drawing lesbian audiences. For Heigl's sake. She's a good actress. Another bad thing: you look at this movie and amazon assumes you're a lesbian and want to see films about lesbians and their sexual involvements. Not so, amazon! It could be you just wanted to see a film that gives you the Katherine Heigl you've liked in other (heterosexual) films!

history.text: There just seem to be too many stereotypes bouncing around this drama. The Nazi angle - phttt. The family who look like they blew in from the Dust Bowl - sheesh. My dog has been long gone (died years ago) but my cat is alive and snoozing at the foot of the bed right now. It is the perfect time to watch this movie. When I first saw 'Unleashed,' I thought: this is so 'indie.' Now, I appreciate that it is not a big budget film with a great publicity campaign - although, if it were that, a lot more people would be watching! Instead, it's an imperfect little gem of an pet-lover's film. I say imperfect because there are some plot twists that are awkward only because they are so difficult to resolve. Yet, the movie does wind to a satisfactory conclusion. Anyone who has ever lost a cat will know what I mean! I watched 'Unleashed' again and it was more delightful the second time around. More time to appreciate the nuances of a dog or a cat. I especially liked the way the cat moves once he becomes a human. Not just graceful. Cat-like! This is a sweet, lovely, funny movie. I will save it for a rainy day and watch it again.

Chopped continues to excel in showing the challenges that not only chefs but ordinary cooks face every day. You must improvise! Maybe the combination of food ingredients tossed to these competing chefs is not the usual experience for a cook. But the push and the need to improvise are always there. The problems with an oven, the ice cream maker that doesn't give the right consistency to the product, the simple mistakes of adding too much salt (how to fix that!) are common enough for anyone to sympathize. This is by far my favorite cooking show because cooking dinner is a lot like 'Chopped' - unless you are a person who has planned every purchase and every step down to the smallest detail. At that point, something doesn't work as planned - and we are once again back to improvisation. I learn so much from listening to the chefs' and the judges' comments. This season, Amanda reminded me that it's important to salt the water when you cook pasta. Does every cook not know that? Apparently not, because some chefs have been known to omit this step in the process of cooking pasta for the competition.

I'm so glad I took a chance and watched this movies. I was surprised to learn that Hayley Mills played Mom, later when the credits rolled. The actors were just so dead-on right for their parts and played their comic roles with just deadpan demeanors. I suddenly realized where the plot was going quite far along into the movie when the mildest slapstick started to creep in to the steady plodding pace of the movie. After that turning point, it was if the box was opened and the contents a total surprise. It has been many moons since a movie did that for me. Very very satisfying. It's just great when you find something different AND entertaining AND a hidden gem among the other offerings in Prime.

I was entertained, i laughed, and it was not entirely predictable where the plot was headed. That's enough for me to recommend this movie. So low budget! Yet, so funny and really well-written. Not the wittiest or most clever dialogue but very appropriate language and thought for this particular group of people. Almost all the action takes place in the narrow confines of one floor of an apartment building. I love that idea - who has not had their world shrunk to the floor of a building at some time in their lives? This, and the array of characters that surrounds the star, Mark Ruffalo, who truly shines in this role. My favorite scene is when he meets his sexy neighbor while emptying his garbage. She reduces him to a giggling schoolboy and he really succeeds in being so un-charming, so un-sexy, so un-Mark Ruffalo!

Such fun! This series reminds me of why I enjoy 'Hotel Babylon' so much. A hotel is a buzzing hive of activity, no matter how serene the ambience. 'Hotel Babylon' is entertaining because of the plot and characters. This series is good for how much it shows of the operation of a large refined hotel. As in Hotel Babylon, the concierge is a key person. Denis seems to be the wizard here, helping people get what they want when they want it. I have seen this in my own travels. I once called the concierge of my hotel when i was lost. He gave me excellent directions for navigating the transportation system after he understood where I was standing. That was challenging. I love the way a room is described in this hotel: like a package that has never been opened. So clean, so untouched by human occupancy, and yet you know it's been crawling with maids and maintenace workers to make it look that way! So much fun watching this - and i love listening to the Irish language when it's spoken by various employees or visitors. So beautiful.

history.title: Coming To America (1988)
history.text: Is enough to make me break out in a big grin and feel a rush of expectation that this will be one VERY FUNNY movie. How do I know? Because I saw it when it first came out in theaters, years ago. What a gem! It is easily as funny as 'Trading Places,' perhaps even better. I'm so glad it is available on Prime. My kids have never seen this. It's a must-see. They are of a generation that thinks Eddie Murphy is a good comedian because he was Dr. Dolittle. Little do they know...

since I have seen such a sweet simply told story. I was surprised that the pace and the characters worked so well. I expected one of the characters to be revealed to be a former tech mogul or perhaps a disillusioned famous heart surgeon. Spoiler alert: these are people you can identify with. You feel like, despite the secrets, what you see is what you get. What you get are appealing singles who take a chance on love. In the nicest possible way, with little fanfare and no Tinder! I think anyone can watch this film with kids and not have to cover their eyes or answer questions about the motives of people on a date. Little boys will enjoy knowing that the main character spends all this working hours saving lives or being part of the fire brigade. Exciting! He describes riding on top of a firetruck as 'similar to sitting on a pilates ball,' which I found very funny. Appealing and heartfelt dialogue that sounds pretty much like what real people might say. This is a bonus. Five stars!

just what others have reported: good feelings. It's a feel-good movie. The pace is slow and even for most of the movie and then it delivers. This is definitely worth waiting for. The scriptwriters hope that you like Uncle Nino by then and you do - what's not to like? I am vaguely reminded of a movie that was one of my favorite italian language films years ago: Lo Zio Indegno. It was a much darker film, if you can imagine that (think of how the title translates: The Sleazy Uncle). Vittorio Gassman played the uncle of the title (Giancarlo Giannini played the nephew) and it truly challenged you to form an opinion of him. But it was very very good. Unfortunately, it's hard to find these days! Worth looking up and watching if you can - but keep the kids away even if they want to test their Italian skills! I don't know that this film was inspired by that but it could have been. There is no mention of Lo Zio Indegno anywhere, so who knows?

history.title: John Adams
history.text: I know mine is a minority opinion but I think this was a missed opportunity by HBO. Some of the acting was outstanding and the costumes were great. But the writing, pacing, cinematography and direction were below HBO standards. The history and timeline were a little dicey too. They couldn't include every detail, but that doesn't excuse inaccuracies like all 8 of the Brits charged in the Boston "Massacre" being found not guilty. Two were found guilty of manslaughter and branded, a scene Irving Stone used to great effect in his wonderful novel about John and Abigail, [[ASIN:0385001576 Those Who Love: A Biographical Novel of Abigail and John Adams]]. The courtroom scenes in the first episode are absolutely leaden as are the scenes in the Continental Congress, which should have been brimming with passion and debate. Also, I know that hand-held cameras are the rage now, but using a constantly jiggling hand-held camera during intimate scenes like the one in which Abigail tends to her dying son was maddeningly distracting and a very poor directing choice. John and Abigail were New England Puritans with a strict moral code who demanded a lot of their children, their friends and their colleagues. But they were also revered among the same for their wisdom and generosity. They had a huge and loving extended family of Adamses, Smiths, Quincys and Boylestons, all of whom, at various times, took in each others' kids, bailed each other out when debts mounted, held family holiday celebrations, etc. What I found saddest about this series was how it depicted them as utterly isolated from any larger social network. The old PBS series [[ASIN:B0013NAML0 The Adams Chronicles]] is available on DVD. The production values are stiff but the writing is better in that 1970's series. PBS's American Experience episode [[ASIN:B000BMSU9K American Experience: John and Abigail Adams]] is on DVD. It contains more depth and detail in two hours than the entire HBO series. And watch [[ASIN:B001TDS2SY 1776 Director's Cut]] sometime. It's a rather corny musical but the debates over independence in the Continental Congress crackle with intensity.

history.title: Affinity
history.review_title: Didn't Work for Me At All
history.text: This film version of Sarah Waters' brilliant novel "Affinity" seemed rushed and muddled and had very little emotional impact on me. I recognize that it must have been challenging to adapt the book, whose strengths are its detailed character development and slow ratcheting up of psychological tension. Although the book has action scenes and dialogue, much of the story is built on the internal thought processes of characters which cannot be as easily conveyed in a movie. The film's use of flashbacks to show the backgrounds of the main characters (a device used effectively in the book to slowly reveal character and keep you on edge) were too fleeting and, even for someone who has read the book, confusing. Two other weaknesses undermine it. The lead actresses, altho lovely to look at, are sort of one-note, not very subtle actors and I didn't feel any chemistry between them that would support them developing a real passion for each other (which is rather crucial to the concept of "Affinity"!). There is also a third character who plays a critical role in the story who is only brought in minimally at the very end of the movie. If you haven't read the book, you are likely to wonder where the heck she suddenly came from and what her motivations are/were. I wonder whether they shot additional scenes with her that maybe ended up on the cutting room floor, because her placement in the movie just seems so clumsy. The special features section of the DVD includes interviews with the director, producer and screenwriter (the great Andrew Davies, who penned the excellent screen versions of "Pride & Prejudice," "Bleak House" and "Little Dorrit"). I couldn't help thinking as I listened to these three men repeatedly refer to the women characters as "girls" and make simplistic statements about female needs and desires that the whole project would have benefitted from having women at the helm. Sarah Waters' book "Affinity" is a really gripping, emotional story. Skip this video and read the book. The film versions of Waters' [[ASIN:B000A4T804 Fingersmith]] and [[ASIN:B00011Y1QC Tipping the Velvet]], both produced by the BBC, are MUCH better and highly recommended!

history.review_title: Pristine Versions of Menzel and Current "Wicked" Cast
history.text: I had to have a pristine version of Idina Menzel's jaw-dropping performance at the 2014 Tony Awards singing "Always Starting Over" and then splurged by getting the performance of "For Good" by the current cast of "Wicked." They are available for viewing anytime in my Video Library on Amazon or for download. It was worth it for me to own the original stellar performances rather than watching grainy versions on YouTube. For Broadway fans, I think this is a good deal.

history.title: The Pianist
history.text: This gripping Holocaust saga is outstanding from start to finish with great writing, smart directorial choices, and an Oscar-winning turn by Adrien Brody as pianist Wladislaw Szpilman. It is based on Szpilman's memoir of survival in the midst of the Nazi extermination of Poland's Jews. It is both a tear-inducing tale of horror and death and a hair-raising adventure story about clinging to life. I like most of all that this is a Holocaust movie that actually focuses on Jews (are you listening Steven Spielberg?). In one of the extras on this DVD, director Roman Polanski talks about his own lucky escape from the Nazis while the rest of his family perished. It's clear that his own memories enhance many of the details of the film. The writing is efficient and powerful. The very first scene shows Szpilman playing piano in a radio studio as German bombs fall in September 1939. The next 10 minutes take us through the next two years and the increasing restrictions imposed on the Jews, ultimately leading to their slave labor and transportation to death camps. It propels you into the heart of the story. The pace is riveting, and I found myself rooting for Szpilman all the way. As played by Brody, Szpilman is a charming, lovable guy whose brilliance as a pianist inspires others to help him escape death. The horrors he witnesses as his family and community are destroyed are vividly portrayed in scenes where people are forced to bargain for life and face casual cruelties. As Szpilman avoids "deportation" and hides out in Warsaw, he witnesses the Warsaw ghetto uprising by Jews (1943) and the general Polish uprising (1944). I really appreciated how these stories of resistance were included. Szpilman is also aided along the way by Christian Poles and a German captain with a love of music. His encounter with the "good" German offers a little uplift at the end of this very dark story. The musical score, including several gorgeous Chopin pieces, complements and enhances the story. Highly recommended.

history.title: Civil War: The Untold Story
history.review_title: Excellent Docudrama for Civil War Buffs and Newbies
history.text: I so enjoyed this documentary on the Civil War when it ran on my PBS station that I bought the DVD set for future viewings and to share with friends. It focuses on the major battles of the western front -- Shiloh, Vicksburg, Corinth, Stones River, Perryville, Chickamauga, Chattanooga, etc. -- and shows how critical the western battles were to the outcome of the war. The clear writing and chronological progression made the 5 hour-long episodes flow very well. The story is told at a level basic enough that young viewers and those new to the Civil War can follow it. Yet there is enough action and interesting perspective that Civil War buffs should enjoy it as well. Many other pluses: The participation of hundreds of soldier reenactors, whether nervously waiting to fight, engaging in battle, or resting or mourning afterward, gave a real "You are there" feeling to the dramatic events. These guys are not professional actors but they sure took their work seriously and put their hearts into the fight. The cinematography of battle sites and the re-enacted battle scenes were awesome. The computer graphics that showed the positions of troops during battles were helpful. They were easy to follow and made me understand the movements and tactics better. I also liked the many personal anecdotes that were included, showing how people, from humble privates to generals to wives at home to slaves, all got caught up in the life-changing events. Some of the personal dramas are acted out, giving the series a kind of docudrama feeling. Included in the usual comments by historians are US park rangers who oversee the historic battle sites. They are very well-informed and skilled at sharing battlefield stories. Finally, I enjoyed the narration by actress Elizabeth McGovern. She seemed an odd choice for a war documentary, but her voice was consistently clear, strong and engaging. I guess sometimes it's good to have our expectations upended! I highly recommend this series. It's outstanding all around. Congrats to Nashville Public TV and Great Divide Pictures for producing such a quality series.

history.title: American Masters: Dorothea Lange: Grab a Hunk of
history.review_title: Captures the Life of an Outstanding Artist
history.text: I saw this documentary about photographer Dorothea Lange on PBS’s American Masters series and decided to buy a copy to view again and share with others. Lange’s b/w photography is framed beautifully in this video about her life and work and legacy. I was a little surprised that the presentation of her photos in this documentary had a more powerful effect on me than my last viewing of them in a book. It’s largely due to the filmmaker’s skill in setting the context of Lange’s life and struggles and placing them alongside the struggles of the many Americans she photographed. I sure wish we had more photographers of Lange’s caliber and social conscience working today. This is a slow-moving documentary that builds in power and ably captures a great artist at work. I recommend it to all viewers although I think lovers of photography, American history and women artists will find it most resonant.

history.title: American Experience: Rachel Carson's Silent Spring
history.review_title: Short, Illuminating Documentary on Carson's Work and Legacy
history.text: Rachel Carson’s life, work and legacy are covered succinctly in this documentary, first broadcast two decades ago as part of the PBS series “American Experience.” In less than an hour, we learn the essential facts of her life as a woman dedicated both to her family and to the natural environment. Carson conducted limited field work as a marine biologist but distinguished herself as a writer and editor for the US Fish and Wildlife Service’s scientific publications. She gained initial fame for her natural history, “The Sea Around Us,” published in 1951. In the late 50’s and early 60’s she turned her attention to the widespread aerial spraying of pesticides and wrote “Silent Spring,” a cri de coeur that woke people up to the thoughtless way we spread chemicals around our environment. One segment vividly captures the contrast between Carson’s environmental spirit and the attitude of the chemical giants. While Carson speaks about understanding how all species are interrelated and the necessity for greater care in our interactions with flora and fauna, a chemical company scientist bluntly dismisses that as nonsense because in modern times “Man controls nature.” Carson’s writing was a major influence in the emergence of the environmental movement. How powerful was her message about man’s responsibility to nature? Over 50 years after her death, chemical companies still pour millions into campaigns to discredit her. The fact that she was dying of cancer during the years she defended her thesis before the public adds a poignant element to the story. This documentary shows Rachel Carson to be a woman of courage and integrity whose writing continues to inspire many today.

history.title: Oscar & Lucinda [DVD]
history.review_title: Oddball Dramedy with Blanchett Lighting Up the Screen
history.text: “Oscar and Lucinda” is remarkable for early career performances by Ralph Fiennes and Cate Blanchett and lovely cinematography. The story, not so much. Based on a novel by Peter Carey, “Oscar and Lucinda” is the far-fetched tale of two compulsive gamblers, an ambitious Aussie woman who becomes a glass manufacturer and the repressed son of an austere fundamentalist minister in Britain. The two oddballs meet cute and spark over their gambling ways. Ultimately, they make a big wager that leads to a cross-country road trip from hell in which Oscar is determined both to win the bet and expiate his guilt over his sinful habit. The ending seemed over the top to me with heavy-handed symbolism and a quirky sense of both irony and wistfulness that kind of reflected the unevenness of the film. I first saw “Oscar and Lucinda” in 1997 and will never forget walking out of the theater with a friend and saying “Who WAS that woman?!” With those gorgeous cheek bones and a smile that lit up the screen (it doesn’t hurt that Lucinda’s character is a total charmer), it was pretty clear that Cate Blanchett was going to be a big movie star. Director Gillian Armstrong used the same cinematographer she did in her beautifully realized 1994 version of “Little Women,” Geoffrey Simpson. His work in both films is outstanding.

history.title: The X-Files: Season 4
history.review_title: Great Disks for Fans or Newbies
history.text: These "X-Files" DVDs are of excellent quality with many extra background features that will enhance any fan's or newbie's viewing. I purchased seasons 3, 4, 5, and 6 because I think they were the strongest, with the most diverse story content and fantastic guest stars. It's hard to ID the best episodes because there are so many but "Jose Chung's From Outer Space" with Charles Nelson Reilly (season 3) is certainly the funniest and "Tithonus" (Season 6) still gives me the creeps after four viewings. There are 20-22 episodes on each disk. I got them for about $15 bucks each. Given how much I will view them and lend them to friends, I feel like I got quite a bargain.

history.review_title: Tense Tale of Espionage and Conscience
history.text: This is an intelligent, tense tale of espionage and counterespionage during World War II with wonderful performances by William Holden as a Swedish industrialist and Lili Palmer as a beautiful resistance fighter. Unlike some WWII movies that seem kind of hokey and dated, this one stands up well. The cat and mouse spy games and the struggles with conscience are really well done. The European shooting locations are eye-catching. There are at least two escape scenes that take your breath away. Highly recommended.
I'm not sure what else I can add that hasn't been mentioned. This movie is just great. Funny, action packed, heart warming, sad, dramatic, it has everything that makes a movie good.

history.title: Sinister 2 [Blu-ray]

It’s not gory at all. Slightly disturbing, yes but unless you’re raised in a convent this movie isn’t that bad. And it’s not meant to be scary, it’s a super natural mystery. It’s a very good mystery and great storyline with some nice creepy elements.

The humor was there, slightly. The story was a little out there. The minions are barely part of this movie. It’s definitely not worth buying so I would recommend not doing that. I wouldn’t even think kids would like this that much. If someone who actually spent money on it invites you to watch it or it ends up on Netflix then watch it. The minions are happy Gru was fired and wants Gru to return to evil but refuses and the Minions all quit but two and they later end up in jail for breaking into a Tv studio. Meanwhile the Minona start to miss Gru and break out of prison. Drew helps Gru near the end, the Minions show up to help as well and right when you think Drew is good he runs off with the Minions leaving Gru and Lucy contemplating when they’ll go after him leaving room for, I really hope not, a fourth movie.

history.review_title: 'Red Dawn' Meets 'Falcon Crest' Meets a Lobotomy
history.text: The plot revolves around a supposed takeover of Norway's remote oil fields by the Russians as the behest of the EU. In the abstract, the plot is good and shows how Russia uses its soft power in support of its military occupation. Unfortunately, the plot is stung together by meetings, government official A meeting with government official B who walks out of that meeting into another meeting with government official C. It is so tedious. The combination of bad acting and bad dialog makes every moment spent watching this show painful. The male lead, the secret agent, is one of about ten people who work for Norway's security agency and he is the only one who leaves the office. He kisses all the girls, he is in every gunfight, he leads all the raids, he makes all the arrests, he does all the interrogations and single-handed, he does all the hostage rescues. So tedious. Many of us enjoy shows like 'The Night Manager', 'CSI, and 'Berlin Station' because they show realistic tradecraft but not this show. In most respects, this show is as bad as anything that has ever been produced.

history.title: Israel: The Royal Tour
history.text: I bought this video to plan for a trip but a large portion of this video is Netanyahu propaganda spoon fed by his biggest fan. For instance, this video shows the Netanyahu's home and tells about their trip to Disneyland. I wanted to see Israel, not the inside of a limo or an interview with the PM shot inside a nondescript office. The documentary shows the old Jewish cemetery but only to show the grave of Netanyahu's grandfather.

This video was recommended by the moderator of a PBS current affairs program. It is quite disappointing. It is a almost entirely an incoherent series of 15 to 30 second sound bites. Many people who were said to be scientists were interviewed but they did not present arguments or facts, only opinions. I don't want to suggest that this movie is inaccurate but in its demo of 3 card monte they use 4 cards. I am not really sure why 3 card monte was demonstrated but that's the kind of information presented in this movie. A scientific fact presented by this movie: because the Y2K bug didn't cause a crisis, climate change won't either. As a computer programmer I can report that companies recognized the problem of Y2K and addressed it so it is hardly reason to ignore other problems. There is bad science on both sides but presenting bad science and arguing against bad science is not a good basis for our decision making. These climate change deniers present the "fact" of climate cooling that was reported by Leonard Nimoy in the 1970s. Leonard Nimoy was not a scientist so it doesn't matter if he is right or wrong, he is reading a script, not presenting science. This movie has several scientists (or talking heads) state that the planet is currently starving for CO2 but they present NO INFORMATION about this claim. Something they did not address was the largest known instance of climate change was accompanied by CO2 changes an order of magnitude smaller than what man is responsible for today. One lie repeated by many of the talking head scientists, apparently in film from the 1980s, was that arctic and antarctic sea ice is constant or growing. The science presented here is bad on both sides. Idiots debating idiots is what passes for informed dialogue when the lobbyists want the public to just surrender to inertia.

history.title: National Geographic - Lewis & Clark - Great Journey West
history.review_title: Half As Good As Ken Burns
history.text: This is 42 minutes (not the three and a half hour Ken Burns Lewis and Clark documentary) and relatively lame, like a 1950s Disney after school special. The video of the scenery shot from helicopters is good but the narration and the voice actors are dull.

Having watched recent productions from France, Germany and Sweden, I thought this highly rated movie would offer a similar experience but in terms of many production values, it is almost a live-action cartoon, like a poorly produced 'Roger Rabbit Meets Maxwell Smart and Agent 99'. The Allied spies broadcast their location & intentions over the radio and then wonder how the Germans seem to always know their location & intentions ... I guess that the Germans knowing your plans doesn't matter when your kill ratio is 1000 to one. Why did the movie waste two minutes just to show Eastwood traipsing thru the castle to lock a door and return to the cable car? Pacing is often bad and continuity skips around. The cinematography is very good. This might be Richard Burton's best film since he seems to walk thru his part rather than aggressively overacting as he usually does.

history.title: The Voice of Merrill
history.text: The beginning of this movie is horrible but it slowly gets better. It first seems that plot and continuity will never make an appearance in this movie. The movie begins with a murder and the police investigation then, for the next hour, the murder is forgotten about and we are presented with a love affair. A married woman starts an affair the moment she meets a guy and immediately her Svengali-like husband has figured out what is going on and has his wife invite the her lover to dinner. I suggest skipping this movie because the first half is quite bad but, if you do watch it, don't stop halfway through because it does get much better. It is odd that there are no young actors in this movie. The male actors in this movie appear to be past 60, especially the cops.

Not much of a movie. Just an hour of sad boredom followed by 30 seconds of violence then some macho stuff. The video quality is so poor that the outdoor scenes aren't very good. If you saw Russell Crowe in Gladiator or one of the sniper in Iraq movies then you've seen this movie. I'd have much rather seen Zero Dark Thirty again.

Nothing of any interest about the inception and design of the machine. Although the Amiga's engineering team was interviewed, from the stories they relate you would think that the machine was manufactured without it ever being designed. After seeing the movie, I know nothing more about the Amiga than before I saw it. On the other hand, in some interviews of Wozniak he talks about the problems he was confronted with and how he solved them. I'm sure the Amiga people had similar issues but you wouldn't know it from this movie.

history.title: Hot Tub Time Machine
history.review_title: Not recommended for Noel Coward fans or those with a more refined sense of humor
history.text: 2.5 stars for this sophmoric tale of 3 schlubs (and a nephew) who were buds in the 80's but now have drifted apart leading miserable lives. An event triggers a reunion back at a ski lodge where they used to party back in the day. Alas, the resort has fallen on hard times and isn't the happening place they remember. The crew indulges in a wild night of drinking in their condo's hot tub and a spilled beverage shorts out the tub controls resulting in time traveling back to the 80's. Vulgar zaniness ensues. Call me a tradionalist but to me time traveling conveyances should be something more like H.G. Wells imagined, or at the very least a DeLorean but a hot tub seems to push the limits of belief. I have fond memories of the 80's and picked this up in a bargain bin for $5.00 though not sure why it was ever released in Blu-ray, it's no cinematic masterpiece. So, I'm no stranger to low brow humor and thought "Animal House", "National Lampoon's Vacation", and "Blazing Saddles" were all quite funny and cleverly written. They say humor is generational and to me at least contemporary films like this or "The Hangover" and it's ilk and other raunchy comedies prove the point. I just don't get the appeal of these flicks. It's unclear how John Cusack wound up in this farce lampooning all things 80's when he is something of an icon of the decade playing Lloyd Dobler in "Say Anything". The rest of the cast is largely forgettable. There are a few chuckle provoking moments but most of it's just profanity and vulgarity with some scatological and homophobic humor thrown in. It's amazing this mess garnered so many 5-star reviews on Amazon and that it even spawned a sequel in 2015. Oh well, to each his own and if this your kind of thing then dive on into the tub but if your tastes are a bit more mainstream than "Hot Tub Time Machine" is not recommended.

history.title: Bewitched: The Complete Series
history.review_title: Delightful trip down memory lane with Samantha and 'Derwood'
history.text: If you’re a heterosexual male of a certain age then there’s a very strong likelihood that your personal preferences in women were in part shaped by two TV shows; ‘Bewitched’ and ‘I Dream of Jeanie’. ‘Bewitched’ premiered to strong ratings on ABC in 1964 running for eight seasons and starred Elizabeth Montgomery as Samantha Stephens, a witch married to a hapless mortal and the challenges which follow. Darrin, her spouse is an advertising exec for a New York firm called McMahon & Tate and bears the brunt of trying to have a normal life while his wife and her meddling relatives magical powers wreak havoc on his existence- comedy mayhem ensues in every episode. The series was so successful the following year NBC decided they needed their own ‘magic blonde’ so Sidney Sheldon cooked up ‘I Dream of Jeanie’ about a gorgeous genie in a bottle discovered by an astronaut after landing on a remote island. The cast is superb starting with Montgomery; stunningly beautiful and incredibly charismatic you can’t take your eyes off of her. Two actors played her husband Darrin, Dick York and later Dick Sergeant who replaced York in Season 6 as a severe back injury forced York to quit the show. Agnes Moorehead is marvelous as Samantha’s mother Endora who is not thrilled with her daughter’s choice in spouses and David White as Darrin’s boss Larry Tate is a dependable straight man for all the antics. Of the recurring players Paul Lynde stands out as Samantha’s snarky warlock Uncle Arthur and can always be counted on for plenty of laughs. The show ran for 8 seasons and ratings began to decline in 1970 and frankly the cast looks pretty fatigued with it all at this point. All said and done ‘Bewitched’ holds up 45 years later although the plots become quite repetitive after awhile. Supposedly set in commuter town Westport, CT (a place I know very well) it looks nothing like Westport. Also, somewhat surprising for the period Samantha and Darrin are shown frequently occupying the same bed which network censors of the day might have been expected to balk at. Given it’s the ‘Mad Men’ era cocktails are constantly being imbibed, Don Draper would have been right at home. Also, it seemed strange to me that for a family show aimed at kids the final season Ms. Montgomery is clearly braless for virtually every episode…but it was the 70’s I guess. The show ends without fanfare or any closure for its audience and there are no special features of any kind with this box set. You'll be enchanted by ‘Bewitched’ even after all these years.

history.review_title: 'Tin Star' is an unsatisfying, bloody mess
history.text: "Tin Star" is an Amazon series that’s desperately trying to be a little bit ‘Twin Peaks’, a little bit ‘Fargo’, and a little bit ‘True Detective’ and failing at all three. Starring British actor Tim Roth whom I’ve never heard of before (but apparently has a fan base from the film ‘Reservoir Dogs’ which I’ve never seen) as London police officer Jack Worth who takes a job as police chief in a remote Canadian village called Little Big Bear along with his wife and two children. He’s got lots of baggage and struggles with alcohol dependency. This is a show where most all the central characters all make astonishingly poor decisions and exercise appallingly bad judgment straining the viewer’s credulity. None worse than Chief Worth (Roth) who falls off the wagon in spectacular fashion, gets in drunken brawls, has sex with strippers two at a time, taunts a biker bang and is savagely beaten by them, alienates himself from his family and subordinates, oh, and commits murder among other things. It was impossible for me to muster up any sympathy for this loser. How this guy doesn’t get fired or locked up or both is beyond belief. The supporting cast is largely an ensemble of unknowns with two exceptions. Christopher Heyerdahl who’s best known from his role as the murdering sociopath “The Swede” on ‘Hell on Wheels’ essentially plays a 21st century version of the same character here. Christina Hendricks of ‘Mad Men’ fame is totally wasted as a big oil company PR hack and is given little to do but slog around in unfashionable clothing until the last few episodes. Everyone else is largely forgettable. The plot gets darker and darker and Chief Worth's behavior completely goes off the reservation (no pun intended- the village has a local First Nations reservation nearby) and it all ends in a bloody mess that provides little satisfaction for the viewer. "Tin Star" is billed as "Season 1" but given how things conclude it's hard to see how a second season would really be possible or why anyone would care enough to watch. Personally I'm done with it and can't recommend you waste any of your viewing time when there are so many other options available.

history.title: Wonder Woman [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: You don't need 2 X-chromosomes to enjoy 'Wonder Woman' (contains few SPOILERS)
history.text: Like many the Lynda Carter portrayal of DC Comics superhero Wonder Woman is the one that I most identify with. When this current film version was announced and it was revealed that relative unknown Gal Gadot was cast in the lead I had my doubts about the Israeli fashion model’s ability to convincingly fill those red boots. Gadot’s quite pretty and charismatic but on the face of it seemed to lack the physicality to convincingly play the part compared to the statuesque Ms. Carter but honestly she pulled it off. Clearly for director Patty Jenkins as evidenced in the over two hours of bonus features this film was a labor of love and she had a specific vision. Incredible amounts of planning went into making this feature and it shows in the extraordinary level of detail; a simple daguerreotype photo seen for seconds in the beginning was made using the actual old time process to produce the image as an example. ‘Wonder Woman’ was more coherent than some of the big blockbuster Marvel outings where there’s just so many characters and so much going on that you can hardly keep track of what you’re watching. Not so in this case, all the central roles are well drawn and defined but most except Diana Prince lack much if any back story. It hardly matters as she’s the star of the show and it’s all about her. The pace was brisk, there are a few humorous moments such as when they take Diana shopping for street clothes at Selfridge’s department store in London but for the most part things are all business. It was fun to see Robin Wright take a break from the rigors of “House of Cards” and play something different in the part of Diana’s warror Aunt Antiope, too bad she didn’t get more screen time. The climactic big battle in the end goes on and on and is an orgy of CGI effects but delivers a satisfying conclusion. Less crowd-pleasing is the fate of Chris Pine’s Captain Steve Trevor who undertakes a suicide mission and flies off with a plane load of chemical bombs and proceeds to blow himself up. Given this film’s box office success it was surprising to see so many 1 and 2-star reviews here though many of those relate to grievances about the digital copy included with the Blu-ray packaging and not the movie itself. Some viewers complained ‘Wonder Woman’ was too “cheesy” which is comical if you go back and watch the old TV series and compare the two. Other unhappy reviewers didn’t like the abundance of CGI effects which for this genre are pretty much inescapable; heck they even had CGI in the latest rendition of “The Great Gatsby” and I don’t recall him being in the Justice League. And then some negative comments were focused on Ms. Gadot’s perceived inadequacies as an actress or felt she was too slight for the role. What can I say, to me she was convincing and I found her charming overall. Others took issue with Wonder Woman’s abilities to leap tall buildings and dodge bullets and other superhuman feats, they must have missed the part that she’s an immortal demi-goddess so none of those things would be outside her skill set. Also among the haters were a number of Greek mythology enthusiasts who took umbrage with apparent inaccuracies in the script. I would ask those folks to consider the source material was a comic book not a scholarly text so lighten up. In summary, ‘Wonder Woman’ was a pleasant surprise brightening the otherwise dark DC Comics universe. The trailer for the upcoming ‘Justice League’ looks pretty impressive so we can look forward to seeing more of her.

history.title: Major Crimes: The Complete Fifth Season S5 (DVD)
history.review_title: Season 5 of 'Major Crimes' does not disappoint
history.text: As I’m writing this the internet has just announced that ‘Major Crimes’ will be ending after it’s sixth season which is currently in production and due to air this month. It’s a befuddling decision by TNT given ‘Major Crimes’ still was the network’s highest rated show and the cast, and creator James Duff seem dedicated to continuing the series. Season 6 then will be the last and it’s been chopped from the usual 21 episodes to a mere 13 with which Duff & Co. will attempt to wrap things up for fans. Season 5 is solid and it’s hard to see any reason for the cancellation decision. Yes, there’s still too much Rusty and his tiresome relationship with Gus. How this young man regardless of who his adopted mother is manages the access to sensitive information inside the LAPD is beyond belief. Also this season the increasingly cloying romance between Capt Raydor and Lt Andy Flynn is taken to the next level- no chemistry between these two. Sharon remains a cold fish and seems like she might have more emotional investment in the copier than Flynn. These complaints aside the crimes are still cleverly conceived (for the most part) and watching the team go through their paces in solving them makes for enjoyable viewing. A major character is killed off this season that’s quite a shock if you didn’t read about it first on the internet. There’s a department shake up and a long overdue promotion for the finale that will satisfy long term fans. When “Major Crimes” sticks with its strength (which is dealing with ‘major crimes’) this series is one of TV’s best procedurals. The personal lives of the characters for me make less compelling viewing but that aside I’m disappointed the show is ending and like many hope for an eleventh hour reprieve from another network or alternate content provider.

history.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
history.review_title: A lighthearted take on the Spiderman saga that may annoy purists
history.text: After a dismal summer at the box office Hollywood’s few bright spots came from Marvel and DC (“Wonder Woman”). Spiderman’s long been a fan favorite in the world of superheroes and thanks to advances in film making we’ve been treated to some spectacular versions of Spidey’s story over the past 15 years. Starting with the Toby Maguire version directed by Sam Rami in 2002 which captured the origin story perfectly the series lost steam when the fairly abysmal Spiderman 3 ended things before Maguire started looking he was eligible for AARP. Then the “Amazing Spiderman” reboot starring Andrew Garfield as the webslinger debuted 2012. Not surprisingly most viewers found it to be mediocre by comparison to the Rami productions and this edition ended after a fairly incoherent sequel. Naturally news that once again Spiderman was hitting the big screen so soon after the last film was met with skepticism. The preview of the new Spidey in “The Avengers- Civil War” assuaged much of the concern and “Spiderman- Homecoming” is one of the best superhero films ever decisively ending any doubt. Tom Holland is well cast as Peter Parker and captures the right feel of the character as a very young, still immature teen. Director Jon Watts wisely skips the origin story that’s already been told in the last two generations of the franchise so we pick up shortly after “Civil War”. Bringing in Tony Stark (always terrific Robert Downey Jr.) as Parker’s mentor was a great addition to the tale and their interactions are very entertaining. I do agree with some viewers who felt Peter was too reliant on Stark Industries tech and lacked the skill and abilities he's had since day one in the comics. There are plenty of laughs as Peter’s very nerdy friend Ned discovers his powers and they try to leverage his secret identity to help in their popularity at their STEM high school. It goes without saying that we get tons of action and watching Spiderman try and perfect his skills and master the augmented suit given him by Tony Stark (including the AI assistant, a female Jarvis) is realistic and fun. Noteworthy supporting cast includes Michael Keaton as our villain and Marissa Tomei as Aunt May. I’m not sure why but since the appearance of the age appropriate Rosemary Harris as May in the 2002 film this character keeps getting younger; Sally Field played her in “The Amazing Spiderman” and now we have Ms. Tomei. Normally I’m not a fan of this sort of revisionist casting but it works here and Tomei is always a treat to watch. Sadly missing from the mix was M.J. Watson, Peter’s love interest and instead he’s pining for an African American young woman in a casting move that seems a contrived deviation from the source material. In summary, “Spiderman Homecoming” is a solid hit and the inevitable sequel will likely be eagerly anticipated by fans everywhere.

history.title: Supergirl: Season 1 [DVD]
history.text: This Supergirl update has much to recommend it to superhero fans. This reboot is clearly aimed at a youthful audience featuring primarily very attractive young people in tight clothing. The show nicely pays tribute to the past featuring Dean (‘Lois & Clark: The New Adventures of Superman’) Cain and Helen (‘Supergirl’ the movie) Slater as Kara Zor-El’s adoptive parents. Blake Neely’s triumphant theme music brilliantly captures the same spirit of John Williams’ iconic “Superman, The Movie” score that fits the positive mood of this new series. Melissa Benoist strikes the right vibe as Kara/Supergirl, cute and spunky with an unlimited sense of optimism. Just like her famous cousin Superman her disguise is a pair of glasses which wouldn’t seem likely to fool anyone. Her boss is media mogul played by talking stick figure Calista Flockhart as Cat Grant. Cat suspects that Kara (or ‘Keira’ as she calls her) is really Supergirl (maybe if Kara didn’t wear the same earrings when she’s in her cape?) but is eventually dissuaded though she doesn’t seem that gullible. Supergirl has help saving the world; fellow Catco employee “Winn” Schott who’s an IT wiz, her adopted sister Alex (beautiful Chyler Leigh) who works for a secret government agency (the DEO) that hunts alien bad guys, and Hank Henshaw (David Harewood) DEO chief who ironically happens to be a super powered shape shifting Martian . Like other reboots of the superhero genre “Supergirl” indulges in some revisionist casting. The most obvious is Jimmy Olson who has always been a geeky, bow tie wearing, freckle faced, red-haired white guy. In this new version Jimmy is now “James” and is a tall, strapping, bald headed African American model and Supergirl is smitten with him. Purists will find this change hard to swallow and though Mehcad Brooks is a likeable actor and tries his best he and Kara don't have much chemistry. A minor complaint on wardrobe, there are a number of military characters in “Supergirl” and for the most part the uniforms all look correct with one exception. Lucy Lane (yes, Lois’ sister) is an Army JAG major and when she’s in dress blues her service cap is for a company grade officer not a field grade officer and the eagle device is for an enlisted person not an officer. Also, she keeps her headgear on indoors although she’s not carrying a weapon, I know, nit-picking. My problem with the show is that it’s incredibly sappy constantly dwelling on themes of love, family, and inclusiveness ad nauseum. Considering the target demographic it’s hard for me to imagine jaded millennials not rolling their eyes as the super friends wallow in sentimentality. I got pretty bored with it all by the time the season ended. That said, I smiled at the end when Cat Grant promotes her long-suffering assistant and finally calls her ‘Kara’. Considering that “Supergirl” has three seasons under its belt my concerns clearly aren’t shared by the audience at large. If your looking for female empowerment I suggest the latest "Wonder Woman" film that came out earlier in the year. One and done for me.

Season 2 of this splendid PBS Masterpiece series based on Winston Graham’s novels does not disappoint. “Poldark” is an engaging period drama set on the coast of Cornwall and chronicles the frequently calamitous life of Captain Ross Poldark (Aidan Turner). In the first season Captain Ross a veteran of the war in the colonies returns to his home to find his girlfriend Elizabeth (Heida Reed) engaged to his cousin and his business affairs in shambles. He marries his scullery maid Demelza (Elizabeth Tomlinson) and makes various attempts to resurrect two copper mines that he owns that have fallen into decline. All the while he maintains a feud with the nefarious George Warleggan (Jack Farthing) a wealthy self-made man with a chip on his shoulder and a great dislike for Poldark. If this show is an 18th century version of “Dallas” then think of George as J.R. Season 2 picks up where things left off and provides plenty of twists and turns with the scenic Cornish coast providing a beautiful backdrop to the often soapy action. Fans of Jane Austen and “Downton Abbey” will likely find much to enjoy with this show with its lavish sets and costumes. A notable addition to the cast for this season is the love interest for Poldark’s friend Dr. Dwight Enys (Luke Norris). Heiress Caroline Penvenen (the stunning Gabriella Wilde) meets the good doctor while visiting her uncle and the two begin secretly meeting because her uncle doesn’t think Dwight’s good enough for her. Ms. Wilde in one scene enters a tavern and literally brings all activity to a standstill; wearing an ice-blue gown and long blonde curls she looks like Queen Elsa from Disney’s “Frozen”, she is a sight to behold. Highly recommended.

history.title: Elementary: The Fifth Season
history.text: Season 5 of “Elementary” returns to its roots with each episode’s primary focus being on Holmes and Watson solving specific crimes as consultants for the NYPD. Personally I found the past few seasons sub plots with Holmes’ brother Mycroft, father Morland, and protégé Kitty Winter (Ophelia Lovibond) all to be more of a distraction than anything else (lamentably Kitty makes a return visit for two episodes, I for one wasn’t missing her). This season introduces Shinwell Johnson (the late Nathan Ellis) a former gang member whom was saved after a shooting by Joan when she was still a practicing surgeon. This ongoing Shinwell storyline is interesting and occasionally takes center stage in some episodes but does not degrade the overall viewing experience. Johnny Lee Miller and Lucy Liu continue to have strong chemistry and watching them work as the modern day Holmes and Watson remains enjoyable. The supporting cast of Aidan Quinn as Capt. Gregson and Jon Michael Hill as Detective Bell are quite good and are a pleasure to watch. The mysteries are quite creative and clever keeping viewers guessing most of the time. Sometimes things don’t make much sense such as Holmes and Shinwell boxing in an NYPD gym. Shinwell is supposedly acting as a CI for the police and has integrated back into his old gang so why would he risk being seen at a cop gymnasium? In another episode Joan is awakened by gun shots in the brownstone; her reaction is to hop out of bed and run downstairs unarmed potentially facing death (it was Holmes playing a recording loudly), she seems smarter than that. Also notice that the detectives and CSI folks never wear shoe covers at the various crime scenes, the writers should watch a few episodes of “Major Crimes”. More unlikely is how much leeway Sherlock and Joan have with the NYPD, being permitted to lead interrogations in particular. I don’t know how ‘consultants’ work with law enforcement in reality and I realize they are the stars of the show after all but these two seem to get away with quite a lot. Hard to believe Captain Gregson and Det. Bell would be so passive and let civilians usurp their authority. Sadly it appears that “Elementary” is on borrowed time, initially CBS only renewed the series for a short 13 episode run and scheduled it as a mid-season replacement instead of a fall release…not a good sign. Just recently it was announced that the network expanded their series order for another 8 episodes bringing the total closer to the usual number. Despite this news the internet has many rumors that the sixth season will be the last and it won’t be aired until spring of 2018. I for one hope the rumors are wrong, this is a quality program and they haven’t ‘jumped the shark’ yet.

history.title: Simon & Simon: Season One
history.text: It’s been almost 38 years since “Simon & Simon” debuted and despite the long time since this series hit the small screen it holds up well. Rick (Gerald McRaney) and his younger brother A.J. (Jameson Parker) are struggling P.I.’s in San Diego who seem to spend entirely too much time with their mother. They have an office across the way from a competing mega Peerless Detective Agency headed by Myron Fowler (who looks like a used car salesman) and his very attractive daughter Janet Fowler (former "Miss Texas" Jeannie Wilson). The Simon’s are kind of like Oscar and Felix from the “Odd Couple” and the contrast between the two is a constant source of amusement. They poach clients from Myron on occasion while enlisting Janet’s assistance on more than one occasion. Cases feature many special guest stars from the era who are fun to see again. The boys spend a lot of time in Mexico which is depicted as a relatively carefree place whereas today their beheaded corpses would be found in a shallow grave first time they go south of the border. It’s all pretty light stuff and fun and still enjoyable entertainment. The first season theme music is not the one most viewers will recall, and in fact there are cringe-worthy lyrics they play during the closing credits. Thankfully, they got a new tune starting in season 2. It’s odd that the series isn’t available in a box set and you have to purchase each season individually. Also, the prices are what you’d expect to pay for the last season of a contemporary hit show and not one that’s almost 40 years old! I’m on board for more of “Simon & Simon”.

history.title: Uncorked
history.review_title: Odd movie. Good performances. Stick with it to the end, this quirkiness has a charm
history.text: Extremely well done but at the same time very Odd. Some of the cinematography is distractedly quirky & unexpected. Every once in awhile there is a narrative that seems a bit strange but the performances ,the pacing & the spaces of time when the camera just let's you look at what's going on & let's you watch the people not talking, are just as powerful as if there was engaging dialogue. We almost didn't stay with it till the end but I'm glad we did because it really was well worth it.

history.title: The Answer
history.review_title: One of those movies you're embarrassed to admit you watched
history.text: This is not the most terrible movie & the acting isn't the worst, BUT it is not something I would watch again. or recommend.. it didn't cost me anything which is why I watched it which makes me embarrassed to admit !

history.review_title: Typical Hyper active Streisand & bland O Neal drown in a sea of endless tedious lame humor
history.text: Streisand here seemed alot like her character in Hello Dolly. Ryan O Neal is wasted (totally bland) this is a reworked version of the Old Black & White film Bringing up Baby but has more slap stick gags than a vaudeville show....my nice way of saying that this is really stupidly done. If you are a Streisand fan then you will want to watch, but if you find her a bit hyper active, then you may want to pass. The lame joke & sight gags were just pounded in too hard for me.

all star cast is the only thing that saves this movie from being a clone of all the other movies out there just like it. The soundtrack is dated , distracting & does not enhance the movie. highschoolers talk more like college students & there is a whole lot of crude jokes that are almost middle school level. Ironically, the over protective father seems to have just cause for his fears as it turns out one of his daughters has already had (probably unprotected) sex.Predictable plot & as I said, only worth watching because of the cast. Fast forward 10 years & see how they have changed (or died)

history.title: Love Is A Ball
history.review_title: Decent forgettable passtime if you don't have to pay for it
history.text: Glenn Ford is about 46 in this movie which may explain what looks like a heavily shoe polished hair styling (combed forward even !) Hope Lang is a good 16 years younger so the romance between them isn't completely believable. The tone of the movie wants to be modern but carefully teeters on the edge of it as Lang's belly button is covered even when she wears midriff baring outfits and it's implied that she & Ford sleep together but nothing is said or shown. It's unclear why Ford falls for her but since she's set her sights on him he gives in rather easily. OK entertainment if it's free & you don't expect to much from it

history.review_title: Above average Hallmark-ish movie has characters work through issues & insecurities before you get to the happy ending
history.text: Rose (from the Haven T.V. series) & Watson's (From 7th Heaven T.V. series) acting is better than the material & soundtrack they are given. on a Hallmark movie scale I would rank this better than average though. I liked that the characters didn't resolve things instantaneously but needed space & time away from each other to conclude that they liked each other enough to put in the effort to try to have a relationship. It was also nice that both characters shared the blame equally for things not working out smoothly.. I would have preferred Barry Watson be more clean shaven but the scruffy look seems to be the Look now , which makes it all the less appealing as it's rather cliche. B+
