history.title: Peter & The Magic Egg
history.review_title: Disappointed in the VHS rip that this DVD is
history.text: This was NOT what I was expecting from Paramount/CBS! Unlike their Puff The Magic Dragon triple feature, the source material for this DVD was a VHS release of Peter And The Magic Egg. It has the Family Home Entertainment logo at the start of it, which means it's a rip of the FHE VHS release from over 25 years ago! The VHS to DVD conversion is typical of VHS to DVD conversions. The video is bright. The Liberation Kids DVD from about 10 years ago has a better video quality. The biggest selling point of this DVD release over the older one is this one has subtitles. Shame on Paramount for not using an original source print and going for a cheap VHS rip.

history.title: Rocky & Bullwinkle & Friends - The Complete Second Season
history.text: The contents on this DVD release are not why I give this such a low rating. It's the quality control of the production. To save on costs, the manufacturer put the episodes on flipper discs. Flippers are notoriously bad quality products, which is why they hardly use them any more. If you get this set, be sure to test EACH side of all 4 discs. This should have been released as 8 DVD-9's, not 4 flippers with DVD-9's on each side. With flippers, you're lucky if they arrive from the mail playable at all. The Outer Limits Season 1 came on flippers and out of 8 sides, only 2 were readable. The other 6 wouldn't even recognize as playable at all! Wonder Woman also had a season released on flippers and one of its discs wasn't playable. The Universal Monsters Legacy collections were initially released on flippers and there were tons of quality control issues with customers trying to play them. Universal eventually finally got it through its thick head and last year released a new version of the Legacy collections on DVD-9 non flipper discs. Bottom line is the episodes are as good as they used to be, with the odd edits here and there to change the title card of the show and the new voice over that announces the show's name. Stupid edits, but it seems that everyone who owns DVD content thinks it's their right and duty to make stupid edits to the contents on the DVD's they release. However, be sure you can read ALL the contents on all 8 sides. Otherwise, you're probably in for a long series of sending your DVD's back and hoping you'll get a release where the discs are all playable, but you most likely won't.

history.title: King of the Hill: Season 6
history.text: To save production costs, Fox made these discs as single layer flippers. There is a DVD on each side. Flippers are notorious for being extremely poor quality technology. They damage far easier and often times they leave the factory unplayable, even before they get scratched during shipping. On the copy I received, Disc 1 Side 2 had 2 large scratches on it that rendered the disc partially unplayable. The discs were damaged during shipping because there is not a label side to protect them from being jostled around. This is a shame. King Of The Hill is a good show and Season 6 contains one of my favorite episodes, Bobby Goes Nuts. However, Fox must be faulted for doing this DVD set on the cheap and should be punished for it. Punished by not roping in anyone else into buying this inferior release.

history.title: Return Of The Living Dead 3
history.review_title: Avoid DVD version! It is the R rated cut!
history.text: This review is for the Lionsgate DVD version. Don't waste your money on this DVD release. It's the watered down R rated cut. Get the Blu-Ray instead if you want this film as it was originally intended to be. That's supposedly the uncut, unrated version of the film.

history.title: Digimon: Digital Monsters - The Official Second Season
history.review_title: Cheap production values on the DVD set
history.text: There is next to no quality in the production value of this DVD release. The set uses DVD-5's instead of DVD-9's to hold its episodes. A DVD-5 will hold 4 episodes without quality loss through compression. There are 7 episodes per DVD-5 in this set. That means they used an awful lot of compression, so these episodes are not presented in the quality they should be. DVD-5's are cheaper to produce than DVD-9's, which is why this company went this route. I'm surprised they didn't even go cheaper and use flippers. Flippers reduce the number of discs but are notoriously cheap and too often arrive unplayable. If you're going to go cheap and use DVD-5's, then, by all means, increase the number of discs in a set and only put 4 episodes per disc. To nearly double the number of episodes that will fit on a disc is simply cheap, to reduce production costs while still charging the maximum amount for the DVD set. This DVD set is simply cheap and should be avoided.

history.title: DC Super-Villains: The Joker [DVD]
history.review_title: Appears to be the same disc as already released in the seasonal sets
history.text: Do not buy any of the DC Super-Villain series if you already own the complete season sets of Batman: The Animated Series. This series of discs appears to just be the same discs already released in those sets. They do contain an episode featuring the villain on the cover, but the rest of the episodes are simply other episodes from Batman: The Animated Series. For instance, the Joker's disc label is BATMAN_ANIMATED_SERIES_DISC_4. This indicates it was disc four of season 1 of Batman: The Animated Series. Or Disc 4 of seasons 3 or 4. Season 2 discs had V2 in their labels, so it's not one from that boxed set. Also for an example, these episodes also include ones featuring the Clock King and the Mad Hatter. This series appears to just be Warner Brothers recycling their existing content, double dipping the public without even going the extra mile to double dip by offering new content. If you already own the animated series seasonal boxed sets, skip these discs. If you're looking for more than one episode featuring the villain on the cover, then also skip these discs as you most likely will only get 1 episode featuring them.

history.title: The Waltons: Season 9
history.text: Be aware that the copy I received were flippers. They put two discs onto one for each of the 3 discs in this set to save on production costs. Flippers are notoriously cheap, hence why hardly anyone uses them anymore. So, be sure to check your set when you get it. If it's flippers, be sure to scan through all the contents of each side to make sure the disc can play. Flippers are notorious for arriving damaged in the mail and, because they are cheap, for sides that simply will not play shipped right out of the factory. Also be aware that Side B of Disc 3 was apparently intentionally left blank and unplayable. The information on Amazon.com for this set says there are no special features. So, there is the final episode of the series, The Revels, on Disc 3, Side A and apparently nothing on Side B since there are no special features listed. WHY Warner Brothers insisted on making a flipper with nothing on Side B and simply not use a single layer DVD-9 for Disc 3 is a mystery. As using a single sided DVD-9 would have saved production costs. Anyway, the bottom line is if you can't get Side B of Disc 3 to play, it's probably because there was intentionally nothing put on that side.

history.title: Alfred Hitchcock Presents: Season One
history.text: These discs are flippers. Very cheap production quality on the part on Universal. Disc 2 Side A arrived with 2 big scratches on it rendering it unplayable at that point. That's the problem with cheap flippers. They almost always arrived damaged or simply unplayable. They either get scratched in shipping or their cheap production quality means they're rendered unplayable straight from the factory. Sides that won't be recognized as playable DVD's in any player. Universal, of course, has the right to be cheap in production. And I have the right to tell you not to waste your money on their cheap product. EDIT: Further reasons not to buy. No scratches on Disc 2, Side B: not fully playable. No scratches on Disc 3, Side A: not fully playable. See? Flippers are trash! Do NOT buy!

history.title: Freddy vs. Jason (New Line Platinum Series)
history.review_title: Watch the full screen version over the widescreen one
history.text: You should probably watch the full screen version of this movie over the widescreen one. It seems the widescreen version is just the full screen version with black bars added to the top and bottom. This obscures some of the video data so you don't actually get a widescreen version where you see more visual information. This is best noticeable if you compare a scene near the beginning. When the woman gets out of the water, runs down the dock, and puts her shirt back on. There's more visual data in that shot on full screen than on the widescreen version. So, this leads me to think the widescreen version is just a matted full screen version, instead of a true widescreen version. As for the movie itself, I found it to be okay. Not great, but not bad. Not the best entry in either franchise, but a nice enough crossover between the two. It delivers what you would expect from movies of their kind. A mixture of standard deaths and some creative ones. Could have been better, but could have been worse, too.

history.title: Challenge Of The Gobots: The Original Miniseries (Remastered)
history.text: There are a few odd editing choices made to the episodes on this DVD. The ending credits are missing the classic swirling Hanna-Barbera logo they used in the 80's that were at the end of the syndicated version when the show originally aired. Episode 2 is missing all audio from the commercial bumpers. No music and no voice of Dick Tufeld saying the show would continue after these messages/back to the show. As for the content, the original miniseries of the Gobots was okay. It was a decent enough introduction to the series. The show definitely got better when the show proper started airing about a year after this miniseries did. Why do the producers of DVD material insist on making stupid edits? Wouldn't it be far easier to just take the original source material and convert rather than take the time to make stupid editing choices that the viewer didn't want?

history.title: Agatha Christie's Partners In Crime
history.text: I guess here that the second go round with attempt #2 was meant to be great. Rebecca Annis' and Robert Warwick's performances were exceptional but they were exceptional actors and had a natural acting-partnership together. But Walliams and Raine bring a freshness to Agatha Christie's favorite detective, barely known by the general public. I am not going to review the story and give it away as one needs to read it first, but both the book and movie are top-notch and great Chistie mystery.

history.title: Father Brown: Season Three Part One [DVD]
history.text: Far better FB than the one from the 70s or early 80s played by KM. These have some humor, a nice change of the characterization of the ongoing archenemy, and NC and her driver are a hoot. Getting part 2 of Season 3 this week and Season 4 is preordered. I hope there will be at least 8 seasons. It's really ashamed that the Blu-ray are not made for Region A/1 (NA AND CANADA).

history.title: A Murdoch Mysteries Christmas
history.review_title: A really one-DVD Christmas Special of snow, love, mayhem, murder and a dead body or two.
history.text: Another great story of a murder and Murdoch's brilliant mind and a blending of the Christmas holiday making it a real (Helene) "joy" to watch. Can't wait for season the next season to come out. Thank you Canada for bringing this super series for us in the US to see and hopefully many more seasons to come. But, where was the Path for the Toronto Constabulary? She was very much missed.

history.title: Masterpiece Mystery!: Endeavour Series 3 (UK Edition) Blu-ray
history.review_title: Great Series 3 of Endeavor. Hurry up, 4!
history.text: Another season of top-notch English policing drama. Once this has come to an end, I am afraid the Morse machine will have come to an end. Thankfully, I have everything of Morse and after Morse on DVD/BVD. This is as good as Lewis and better than Morse itself.

history.title: Father Brown: Season Three, Part Two
history.review_title: Another Season (or 1/2) of a Great Mystery with Humor from England
history.text: This is a continuation of the best presentation (video) of the Father Brown stories with a superb cast that leaves the audience feeling they really are the people they are playing. Other than Mark Williams, my favorite is Nancy Carroll who plays the Baroness of the area. She's a hoot and ends up doing things she would never have dreamed of doing like getting her Chanel dirty, all with a very dry wit. The writing is very well written, and in this set unlike those with Kenneth More of the 1970's in the role of Father Brown, John Light plays Hercule Flambeau when he is still a rogue rather than after his reformation which makes for a nice difference between the two series. Thankfully, this series is being made at least through 2017 and hopefully for even longer. Nothing against Kenneth More, this production is better produced, better acted, more lively, and just plain great as most English series are today. Were it not for English productions put to DVD, or shown on DVD our TV and DVD player sales would plummet.

history.title: Masterpiece Mystery!: Inspector Lewis 8 (Full UK-Length Edition) (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: The Climax Season of a Great Series--unusual for a spin-off series. Thank you, England for More Great TV.
history.text: This is the climex of one of the best Copper shows to come out of England and as a spin-off from another great for its time, Inspector Morse. In the series, it was satisfying that Lewis accepted Hathaway, or vice versa as it were, and equally so that he learned who killed his wife. It was interesting to learn why Hathaway became a cop and left the Catholic ministry (pre-seminary at Cambridge). Throughout the series, poor Lewis, with a consolidated school education through high school, learned his skills the hard way, with Morse being worn down by Morse his boss, always correcting his grammar, and who attended Oxford, and then Lewis his Sergeant, quoting to him Shakespeare or some other poet or writer or philosopher, below him and educated at Cambridge. But, he took it as he had to and learned to get it right. And learn, he did. It was a great run for Kevin Whately, from the mid 80's to the mid teens in a new century, about 30 years and his early role in Miss Marple A Murder is Announced playing a cop guarding the door of the home of the murderer. A lot of copping for Whately.

history.title: The Agatha Christie Hour: Complete Collection
history.review_title: So so Christie stories, if they really are based on Christie stories which is doubtful.
history.text: Very much dated 80's English TV stories supposedly from Agatha Christie. In my opinion, the stories were average as was the acting. As was typical, English TV had not come into its greatness until the mid 1980's with some exceptions. Recommend only if you have nothing else to watch and you collect anything Christie.

history.title: Murdoch Mysteries, Season 9
history.review_title: Super Series 9 as All Previous Series with One Exception
history.text: Nothing much more to add than what has already been said except that one series ends and can't wait for the next season is coming out which happens to be this August as memory recalls. I starts with the newly promoted Inspector being jailed for Murder, losing his position and after being found not guilty of the crime, so to speak, he was allowed to rejoin the ranks of his fellow officers but back at square one. However, to Murdoch, he considers his lowly title really "in name" only. Unless I was dreaming, this was the only season that did not leave us hanging on a Hitchcockian 'top of Mount Rushmore', or on the 'top of the Statue of Liberty' before the last salvo of being saved. Sadly, there was no season ending cliffhanger leaving us with baited breath. Other than that, we have lost the beautiful medical examiner (Coroner) to her 'new' LGBT lifestyle. The other Mystery were typical Murdoch.

history.title: Agatha Christie's Poirot: Complete Case Collection
history.review_title: SHAME ON ACORN FOR SUCH LAZINESS
history.text: Of course the Suchet performances are 10-star, par-excellence, will never be repeated to this level; but I wish to rate this one-star only because of the mix in sound. This set has so many various sound outputs; i.e. PCM, Dolby and DTS. Why not make all discs in all three audio formats and allow the user the option to choose which one to use. In my particular case, my audio output is a Bose Solo and anything Bose (almost anything) will not support DTS or Dolby Atmos or TrueHD only Dolby 5.1. When there is no option as the later discs in this set which are many as are the latest output of another long running English murder mystery series running beginning in 1997 and since switching to Blu-Ray in the past few years, I have to switch over to my horrible internal TV speakers. Bose simply will not support high-end Dolby or more frustratingly DTS of any type. So, Acorn, how much trouble would it have been, as do most movies, have a setup option, and allow us to decide which audio format we would like to hear it under? Thankfully, another reviewer went to the trouble to detail which discs had which type of audio for which I am eternally grateful. I won’t make this purchase which would be quite expensive especially since I have all the DVDs already.

history.title: Ruth Rendell Mysteries Collection
history.text: The real problem with this series and any other regarding Ruth Rendell is that Acorn or any other has not put any Wexford Mysteries except for three: Road Rage, Simisola, and Harm Done—the last three Inspector Wexford Mysteries that were filmed. And from what Acorn told me, there are no plans for the remaining Wexford mysteries to be put to DVD much less to BVD. At least not any time soon. My guess is that Acorn does not believe that the demand across the pond and in the US would not be high enough to cover the cost of paying royalties, etc.

history.text: Under unfortunate circumstances I did not get to see this movie in theater because it was only playing in “select” movie theaters as I was told, so I was pleasantly surprised to see it on Amazon Video yesterday. Jake Gyllenhaal is a phenomenal, underrrated and very versatile actor so he played an amazingly good Jeff Bauman. I cannot, however, understand the need for as much vulgarity as was used in this film. I’m not sure if it’s just true to real life or what, but the “f” word is used a profound amount of times. Other than that, this is a very captivating and heartwrenching catch on the real story and the main focal point of this movie is set AFTER the bombing to show what life was like for Jeff - which was very tear jerking at times. But in the end it can truly be a lesson for those of us who take life and all of the little things we have for granted - not to mention the good and evil that surrounds us. I definitely recommend this movie!

Over a decade ago I went to High School with a boy who dressed up like Eric Draven on a normal basis. My clothing and lifestyle (goth) were questionable to most from the outside looking in and despite regrettably not having seen The Crow when my friend would take bathroom breaks at school just to apply his Eric Draven look - it was years later that I realized why. And looking back, I wish I’d have paid more attention to his love for Eric and The Crow because this old friend of mine deserved praise for the excellent job at portraying him that he did. This film certainly uses some differences than the graphic novel but it doesn’t take away from the perfection or ability to appreciate the differentiations that the movie crew decided to use when planning and filming the movie. It’s a dark movie that someone with a truly deep personality can appreciate. At times the script is laughable (and not in a comedic way, but a way that will make you say “did they really just say that?”) but with such a strong backbone to the story and factoring in the few instances in real life that occurred to inspire this story I can overlook the flaws and not flinch when rating this movie a full 5 stars. Brandon Lee passed away while this film was still in production but I imagine he would’ve been proud. I wish he were still here and had retained the chance that he deserved to go on as a young, upcoming and talented actor as well as achievements he would’ve made in his own personal life. If you’ve yet to see this movie I fully encourage it. It’s one I’ll always kick myself over for not having seen it earlier in my younger years.

I was undoubtedly wrong. Seeing this movie in theater was merely because it was by invitation from my brother to get out of the house, plus he'd offered to pay. 20 minutes into the film is when the true action really began and it didn't stop until the ending credits began rolling. It's an absolutely well put together movie with a mix of well known and not so well known actors but it truly panned out. There is an extremely high amount of funny parts in this movie but not to the point that it overwhelmed the actual plot or purpose to the movie. And the small homage they paid to Robin Williams in the middle of the movie I was appreciative of. I can't say enough good things about this movie other than you should see it!

history.title: Peter Pan - Starring Mary Martin
history.text: When Captain Hook Intends to poison Peter, but poisons Tinkerbell, Peter asks children "Do you believe in fairies? This is faith in humanity. Though the years that faith has been tested, through "Peter Pan Live!" (which I reviewed) though the Election of Donald Trump, which made me feel the same way that "Peter Pan Live!" did, as the Ringling Brothers And Barnum and Bailey Circus draws to a close. As an adult, it's hard to believe on fairies, especially when you see how horrible humanity can be. But you must believe! Especially if you believe in youth, joy, and freedom for all. I LOVED the fact that Mary Martin was a women, because I was a six-year-old girl. The Musical defined me as a Feminist, even if I was too young to know what Feminism was. "Peter Pan Live!" took the two most powerful women in my universe, the women that played Peter Pan, and Tiger Lily, and SEXUALIZED them! NBC's power-trip of changing "Ugg-A-Wugg" because it was racist, was a miserable, and isolating experience. How could they claim not to be racist, and then, sexualize Native American women through Tiger Lily? The song is still followed by "Distant Melody" and the lyrics became PAINFULLY RELEVANT. The saving grace of "Peter Pan Live" was "When I went Home" the song that Peter sings about feeling abandoned and betrayed. It was no surprise that this was the song cut from the Original Broadway Production, It sounded like it was from the writers whose Musical I loved. Their last gift to me was making it ok to cry. I was sad, because up until that point I HAD believed in fairies, and that Mary Martin, my role model, had never done anything wrong. Plus NBC had done "Peter Pan" with Mary Martin, and a fair number of children, and had denounced them as racist. Social Justice Warrior that I am, I think the media could have handled it better. Like copying and pasting the Lyrics to "Ugg-A-Wugg" INSTEAD of posting videos with children in them. and NOT saying "Ugg-A-Wugg" was meaningless simply because you can't understand them. As a person with a disability, people can't understand me a lot, and at the time I first saw "Peter Pan" I was in speech therapy, so when the tape would come to "Ugg-A-Wugg" I would watch the brilliant Jerome Robbins choreography, and I would listen. I came to the conclusion that it meant "help" except "Ugg-Ugg-Wah" which meant "I Promise." ( Ableism is more of an undertone in this conversation) That "I Promise" was powerful, because with it I swore my loyalty to the characters, and the cast. When the lyrics were changed and NBC broke their loyal bonds by saying that everyone who worked on, or loved "Peter Pan" is o horrible racist, Sondra Lee, came to my rescue like she promised, just by giving an interview saying how sad she was, because she had happy memories off "Peter Pan" just like I did. The happiness it brought me was nothing to feel ashamed of, Sondra Lee is the hero of this story for relieving my isolation just enough, so I could watch "Peter Pan Live!" so I could tell people NBC is an EVIL HYPOCRIT! No, I couldn't be a Social Justice Warrior if I didn't believe in Fairies.

history.title: Annie [Blu-ray]
history.text: My dad died when I was 12, and within the first two months of his death I came across a video of "Maybe" the song where Annie is hoping her parents would come back for her, and feeling the same way myself, I loved this musical. The main characters gusty optimism matches my own, and traits like her race, didn't really matter. Of course, having an African American Annie is a loving gesture, but with Black Lives Matter having to continue, it had no impact at all. Sia wrote the new songs for this version and she has a love for "Annie" and the new, and edited songs match what the original writers intended, to see the opposite, check out "Peter Pan Live!" This version addresses inequality caused by the Foster Care System, the fact that Annie isn't able to read isn't because she's African American, it's because she's a foster kid. Having an African American Annie is probably more tokenism than anything else. My advise, appreciate how similar this contemporary version is to the Broadway Version.

While it might be helpful to address why shows starting female doctors revolve around sex, I LOVE that "House M.D." can star a brilliant male doctor, because if that's what it takes to NOT talk about sex I'm all for it. House's two romantic relationships end. The writers have the common sense to take both of those females off the show, one of those relationships most likely lead to the shows cancelation. The show reminds me of a Crime Drama because of how much focus the put on the Mystery illness of House's patient. There is a lot less focus on character development, so when House's staff gets switched out, you feel nothing. When the series was nearing it's end, they developed the character of one of House's staff, why they didn't develop the one with the terminal illness is beyond me, because it would kept the focus on Medicine. There were only two episodes without cases, and that constituents a bad episode. I wish they would have ended the series with one final case, and the death of Wilson from cancer, because that's a really good reason to quit being a doctor, you couldn't save your best friend. Despite his horrible bedside manner House really does care about his patients, because most of them survive. If House can't save you, who can?

history.title: Superman: The Movie [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A great sci-fi classic brought to Blu-Ray quality
history.text: If anyone out there has not seen this great film yet, I'd be surprised. So, we are talking about seeing it again, or seeing it on Blu-Ray for the 1st time. Either way, it's worth it and this is one film you will see at least once a year and not put it in perpetual storage like the rest of your library. This film had been long awaited by fans of the comic book. It came out in true Hollywood style, where even the film credits were awe-inspiring, let alone the Sfx, the stars( Marlon Brando, Gene Hackman, Christopher Reeve, Ned Beatty, Margot Kidder, Glenn Ford) and of course the story. As we all remember, the story has the people of the planet Krypton facing doom. Marlon Brando is Superman(Reeve)'s father and tries to rally the people to act before the planet is destroyed. Noone has the integrity to agree so he and his wife will send their child to a distant planet: Earth. Thereafter, Superman has a 'normal childhood' with Glenn Ford(a rural farmer); a transformation into Superman at a fortress of solitude; his newspaper job with the Daily Planet in Metropolis(New York?); and so the legend grows. The film was made with a sense of humor(Gene Hackman and Ned Beaty), drama, and pathos. It's more than just a comic book brought to life. In many ways, it was 3 films in one: the first part was true science fiction, with weighty themes presented by the lead marquee star: Marlon Brando. The 2nd part was a family story, childhood on the farm(briefly told). The 3rd and final part, the only part that was Superman as we know him, had him in Metropolis, fighting 'bad guys' and doing super things. All in all, it will seem like you've experienced all the wonders of the world in just 146 minutes of screen time...

history.title: Giorgio Moroder Presents Metropolis: Special Edition [Blu-ray]
history.text: More than any other film out there, Metropolis requires a careful consideration. Because it's so old and there are missing elements to it, the version you get will doubtless be different from versions sold elsewhere. THIS version is unique as the producers chose to add a film score, and one contemporary. SO, you must choose to have the traditional presentation, perhaps with more original footage, or this one, with an application of music. TO ME, the choice is clear. Though Metropolis might've been great at the time, in its complete form(now lost?), seeing the versions in silent film form leaves you 100% unmoved. Catharis...emotional feel...to a film is essential and the rock score adds just that element. I strongly encourage you to view film history via this version. The film itself concerns the struggle of labor versus management, with an intermediary(the hero?) who joins those two worlds. In this odd plot, there is a cyborg(female) that's created in order to control(or free?) the servile workers. You must see it to appreciate it as descriptions fail. The director, Fritz Lang, was so valued by the Germans that a certain 'German leader' offered him almost anything if he would stay in 'that Germany' of the 1933-45 period. Fortunately, he chose otherwise.

history.title: Papillon (DVD)
history.review_title: An adventure and quest from history
history.text: First things first: Some films are mostly dialogue or film noire; this film has vistas and big skies. The point being, you should spring for the Blu-Ray edition if you can afford the extra green. OK, the film itself is about Steve McQueen and Dustin Hoffman. They are 'doomed men', sentenced to the penal colony of the republic of France in French Guiana, in South America. There is some interplay between the mainland and the offshore facility, infamously known as 'Devil's Island'. That storied prison(actually several small facilities) existed for a century, amazingly not closed until 1953. What important is we experience the quest of the men to escape the confinement and conditions and make it away, freely, to almost anywhere. What is great in this film is that it allows you to understand somewhat the more famous case of Captain Dreyfus, the French officer wrongly convicted of treason(to France) and exiled to Devil's Island until a reprieve and exoneration. Whether you look at the film in this vein, or as the more simple story presented, you will be overwhelmed by the concept and challenge of oceanic voyage by people equipped with only courage. The film is not a simple 'escape film' but instead was almost a detective story, with a labyrinth of confidence placed in persons, some paid and some merely sympathetic. The problem was that it required 100% reliability and in real life, nothing works that well...

history.title: Deal of the Century
history.review_title: War and peace and other things...
history.text: Chevy Chase, Sigourney Weaver and Gregory Hines This now overlooked comedy featured Chevy Chase as an arms dealer in a world awash in military hardware sales. He is not the worst person out there, but when a questionable sales deal falls into his lap, he takes credit for it and becomes a new star. His friend, played by Gregory Hines, is a pilot who will do anything to be in the air but also a realist who has qualms about aircraft sales to countries who can barely afford school books. Now there'd be a moral dilemma as to doing the sale, with the requisite reward, or to do the 'right thing'. Vince Edwards is perfect in his role as the corporate president selling an advanced drone (remember this was years before the current age of real-life drones and robotic aircraft.) Although this film has an obvious political slant, it is so well-done and nuanced, you can overlook that. The basic questions of military budgets and the nation's needs have been at the forefront since this nation was formed, trying to defend us against the Crown... For a good comedy and one that is thoughtful, I recommend this little film...

history.title: Platoon
history.review_title: For once, a realistic war film
history.text: Tom Berenger, Willem Dafoe and Charlie Sheen starred in this brilliant tome about war, in particular Vietnam. Unlike the larger than life Apocalypse Now or the other Vietnam films that seemed to either overstate or understate the travails of war in 'Nam, Platoon seems to have tried to steer right down the center, showing war unvarnished or gussied up. We see Charlie Sheen as the newbie cleaning latrines, given the worst assignments, and given the usual (good and bad) advice by people about to end their tour of duty. The film takes us on a tour of duty with Charlie Sheen being 'everyman' thrust into the seemingly endless and pointless jungle warfare against an enemy, unseen normally. We go on night sentry duty, cave or tunnel rat work, etc. There is very little that is sentimental or romantic about any scene. Sheen is forced under the cirumstances to interrogate innocent (sic) citizens who might be harboring the VC(Viet Cong) or even actually be them. What is implied for the educated viewer is the fact that this was tough but actually might have been warranted; in other words, these innocents farmers could be, and were in fact, loyal citizens by day but VC supporters and suppliers by night. Oliver Stone, the director/auteur of the film, indicated that this was a personal journey for him, partially or totally basing it upon his actual experiences. We can't be sure of that, but the film is very personal, visceral, and affecting. I strongly recommend this as the definitive Vietnam film, showing the range of soldiery conduct that was, in the end, wasted by political forces beyond the scope of the men in the field...

history.title: Air America [DVD]
history.review_title: As much fun as we can associate with Vietnam...
history.text: The film is a brilliant add-on to our pantheon of films in re the Vietnam era. It is very much like Apocalypse Now insofar as the operatives that hire Sheen in that are similar to the mysterious agents that hire Downy to fly for 'Air America' (unofficially) in a field of battle that we(America) are not officially fighting. Gibson is brilliant as a self-absorbed pilot/operator who is out for himself while (co-incidentally) helping his country by flying supplies to our 'friends' in the region of Vietnam(i.e. Laos and Cambodia)...He(Gibson) is confronted by moral dilemmas, like Downy's questions about their helping control the poppy fields for related 'trade', or a friend's charitable activities which will ruin his(Gibson's) huge payday before retirement. Gibson has to decide whether to do the right thing(sic) or cash in. The choice is clearcut...or is it? Anyway, this is a brilliant semi-realistic rendition of the air war that we fought for the 'hearts and minds' of the area people around 'Nam. Best of all, it's funny and engaging while showing historical events.

history.title: The Errand Boy
history.text: This is quite simple: The Errand Boy was almost 100% Jerry Lewis, with him as star, director, and co-writer. If that intrigues you, then this is a must-have. If you are of the group that either dislikes Jerry or has pretty much forgotten him, then you might want to keep on truckin'... The Errand Boy was a wonderful family comedy about the movie studios of the time. You have to remember that the studios of the time had had 50 years of dominance; they were factories for movies with massive numbers of actors, extras, and management. That studio system is pretty much gone with the wind so this entire concept is dated. Nonetheless, it's a fascinating and amusing look at the arrogance of management, and you can relate to that for any industry. I'm not totally unbiased here; when Jerry came to Miami on vacation, he would always visit my father who was his personal physician down there...

history.title: Bat 21
history.text: Gene Hackman and Danny Glover star in this air action drama set in the Vietnam war epoch. Having read some of the reviews, positive and negative, I will say that the film, whether 100% accurate or not, is a riveting drama. Bat 21 is a perfect follow-up for you if you like Air America or any of the other Vietnam great films (Apocalypse Now, Platoon, etc.) Gene Hackman plays a specialist who goes out in the field by air and is brought down by enemy action. Suddenly, the war is not an intellectual pursuit for Hackman but is tangible; he has to fend for himself: evade the enemy and contact our forces to arrange a rescue (evacuation). It's touch and go whether he can make it out and you really experience how narrow an escape it will be...if he makes it home.

history.title: Poverty, Inc.
history.text: Outstanding documentary. Highly recommend it. Its theme is the old adage: "Give a man a fish, he eats for a day. Teach him HOW to fish and he eats for a lifetime." And one can extend that aphorism to include "give a man a net and he can feed himself, his family and the village! " This documentary shows how charities can make people dependent on outside agencies. And this aid, despite good intentions, can inadvertently eliminate jobs in the very communities they are serving. Many international experts in the field are interviewed. There is also remarkable comments by former President Clinton and the singer Bono in this film. Immediate aid after a natural disaster is fine but to continue doing so for years and years afterwards indicates something is not working in the economy. Long term aid fosters a "nanny state" and indigenous people lose their incentive to improve. The film also addresses corruption which is rampant in the charity business and poor countries. The rule of law MUST be implemented in many nations in order for the economy and social conditions to improve.

history.title: Apocalypse - World War I
history.text: WOW! Fantastic documentary. I cannot recommend it highly enough. The narration and the colorization of archival black and white film footage really brings history and war to life. It was so interesting seeing the key political players and members of the monarchies at work and play, e.g. Wilhelm II, Nicholas II and King George V. I think the writers, producers and director did a great job. I learned a lot, too. This film reminded me of Ken Burns' production, the "Civil War," except this pertained to WW I. Some reviewers have given this a one or two stars because they were unable to configure the dvd/blu-ray disc for English. I was able to select English easily using the "Setup" drop down list. It is shaded when selected. Their problem was "operator error" not a problem with the disc. I loved this documentary and am going to purchase "Apocalypse - World War II" now!

I would have enjoyed hearing more quotations from those letters and seen more of her personal mental difficulties she faced regarding her faith in God. Other than that, the movie did provide a brief overview of her vocation and I thought the actress who portrayed Mother did very good job.

history.text: This movie shows its age, there is no doubt about it. It is however, even now, nearly 15 years later, a good heist flick.

The first xXx was a low budget thrill ride that fit right in with the times, good music, stupid stunts, and Vin Diesel playing the stunt junky-turned-super-agent with a heart of gold, saving the world one kick-flip at a time. Yeah, nostalgia, I was still wearing Jnco's and running the streets back then. This continuance doesn't hold up as well, and suffers from a staggering underuse of the talent pool they tapped. I mean seriously, you have Donnie Yen and Tony Jaa in the same movie and there's not one really, really awesome fight scene? And I don't get the sudden obsession with this Ruby Rose chick/dude/whatever, he/she isn't a solid actor, in this or the new John Wick, the inclusion feels like when they put "Zombie Boy" into "The 47 Ronin" just because he'd been in a music video. All and all, the story itself is so transparent and redundant there's nothing to enjoy there, the opening got a laugh out of us, the Ice Cube cameo was cringe worthy, but I think that's just "The Cube man" himself, and the action feels like it should be intense, but the effect is lost somewhere, like watching explosions with no volume, there's a depth that's lacking regardless of the energy in the visuals. I have been really disappointed with movies in general lately, none of them have really been "good", much less "great", but this is at the bottom of the pile. Skip it.

history.review_title: Best King Kong movie to date
history.text: I saw this in theater, and it was much better than I expected. Much, much better. Kong Skull island has a plot that can interest you if you let it, a wonderful sense of "awe" instilled even though gorgeous island visuals and giant creatures are pretty par for the course across films, television, and movies these days. The fodder creatures are as expendable as can be expected, they don't make much sense in the vein of the "all these other monsters are monstrous versions of known animals or chimeras thereof" kind of theme the first portion of the movie has going on. But even I have to say, Kong himself looks gorgeous, the animation is so fluid you'd think you could touch him. I mean it's genuinely amazing. The ending and post credits scenes gave me goose bumps. Out of all the movies that have come out int he last 6-9 months, that I can think of, this is the best of them we've seen (we didn't see guardians 2 in theater, so I can't speak to that, wonder woman is on the agenda); definitely it's the best of what we've seen that's set to release soon. Don't hesitate if you're on the fence, it's a fun little watch, I'd suggest buying it, not renting, if you're looking forward to the Godzilla vs King Kong movie, though, I'm sure they'll offer it on sale by 2020.

history.title: Once upon a Time in Venice

history.text: The movie is mildly comedic, but really, really stupid. I'm not even going to bother explaining how/why.

I've seen some bad movies, and this one is way up there. The film tries incredibly hard to tell you a quiet tale of hardship, redemption, forgiveness, and making it work under less than ideal circumstances. However, even with such a star studded cast, this film comes off like artsy garbage. You know, that kind of film where you know actors love it, you know "artsy" types are going to tell you how much they loved the "subtle message of the film" and the "sense of conveyed blah blah blah"... In reality, it's just a bad movie. We made it all the way through it because we were hoping it would pan out to have some big reveal or a sudden upswing in tempo and a message we could decipher that made the trip worth it. That never happened, because this is just a weird, stupid movie.

history.title: L.A. Burning: The Riots 25 Years Later
history.review_title: We can't all just get along, as evidenced by the time between then and now.
history.text: This was an amazing documentary, it was also a little short, and certainly resonates with you after it ends. This was all happening when I was a kid, it was above my pay grade at the time, no way I could comprehend the severity of the circumstances or injustice of the entire situation. I lived in Texas where everyone just inferred Rodney King deserved what he got. Through the looking glass, while the severity of the beating was over the top, he did, of course bring the situation on himself as he was speeding, led the cops on a high speed chase, was high and drunk by his own admission, and did in fact resist arrest, in a manner that led the police he was dealing with to assume he was dangerously high on PCP. A drug which was common inside of the black community in L.A. at that time, and often led to violent encounters with the police. Again, I'm not saying the severity of the beating was warranted per se, but just like some of the cases lately, it was latched onto by the community and propelled into an event that had little to do with the reality of the situation that spurned it. In this case, like some of the ones recently, what it did was spark a violent outburst that turned into rioting. They briefly cover the fact that the violent reaction was contagious to other ethnic communities as well, and that the Chinese population in L.A. in particular was victimized as a whole. The racism on all sides of the spectrum was illuminated by the Reginald Denny beating at the hands of the notorious L.A. Four, which IS covered in this documentary; though they leave out the rapes and murders that happened, nearly all of which were racially motivated, perpetrated by the black mob and inflicted onto the white and hispanic men and women just trying to flee the mayhem. It's hard to watch this documentary without feeling the messages and threats aren't still relevant to this day. Hate cops if it makes you feel better, but you need to realize what your fellow people are like when lawlessness and insanity ensues.

JW2 loses all the empathic draw that the first one had, and seeks to make up for that with a stark increase in absurdity based gun-kata-esque violence. I was not as drawn into this second installment as I was the first, though it starts off very fun, it loses steam quickly and never builds up enough inertia to blow through the less entertaining parts without causing the viewer to lose interest. Something I've noticed as of the last 10 years or so with movies, is that people will rate a movie 5 stars that they only half paid attention to, or will never watch again; on some arbitrary principle that you show your allegiance to an actor or franchise your support by being overly generous to it in ratings and defense. I am not one of those people. John Wick 2 is a solid 3.5 star movie. It's largely uninspired, I found myself unengaged and unsympathetic to Mr. Wick and his antics/plight. I did enjoy some parts of it, some of the dialog was slick, some of the circumstances were highly entertaining, seeing Common pretend to be a super smooth bad @$$ again (Smoking Aces) wasn't really high up there on my list of missing ingredients in movies these days... And Mr. Reeves, despite being one of my favorite actors, delivered a largely lukewarm performance. I will not be watching this movie again, until the third one is set to drop, where I'm sure I'll revisit the previous installments to prepare for, and hope it's better than this one; which isn't bad, but isn't as good as the first. Empire this is not.

Please understand that my 3* review is not a slight, the movie is just very "average". Other people have given large and in depth reviews, given how rude people are on the amazon comments regarding reviews they disagree with, and how disgustingly arbitrary amazon is in their punitive actions towards your reactions to people being rude and condescending... I will simply state that by far and large my wife and I were underwhelmed with the film. It does some things pretty well, you can feel the film building inertia at several points, only to find that energy dulled by the friction of a bad script and completely average at best action sequences. The final fight in particular is an area of contention I have with the film, as it feels less epic and at the same time four times as corny as the TV show's final fights. Yes, Rita is sufficiently grotesque, the rangers are all young pretty people, the depth per character is on the level of the source material, and the new uniforms look great... if you haven't gotten enough of this new fad in "tactical power armor" appearances pushed by the recent explosion of comic book movies (which are all better than this). I stand hard on a 3 star rating, because the movie isn't terrible, but it's not really engaging or even enjoyable otherwise.

history.text: I rented this because of all the hype, I expected something interesting and given the material shown in trailers, kind of a similar production value to 13 Assassins. I'll forego a long, detailed breakdown of all the faults in the film and just say this, "it's not that". The movie is boring, I had to watch it in parts, the action is really sloppy, it's not "brutal" or "technical" or "anything" that would make such a lackluster offering entertaining. Some of these mid-to-low budget samurai flicks make up for weak plots and underwhelming production budgets with copious amounts of erratic sword play and buckets of that super red fake blood the Japanese love so much. This however, doesn't do anything of the sort. The action in the movie is the best at the beginning, and goes sharply downhill afterwards. I'm not sure where the 4-5* reviews come from, honestly. I can't imagine I'd have liked this much in my youth when Anime was still "fresh and cool" to me and Sonny Chiba was one of my idols. It's really just not a very good movie, that's based on a really mediocre manga. If you don't like my review, keep it to yourself. The toxic Amazon community cost me my commenting privileges with all the name calling and insults coupled with my inability to not respond to people pretending to be doctors or making disgusting comments about my children over an opinion that differed from theirs.
