history.title: The Beverly Hillbillies, Vols. 1 & 2 [DVD]
history.text: This 2 DVD set, courtesy of the now defunct BCI/Eclipse company, is simply yet another sloppily remastered public domain DVD release where the original theme song, The Ballad of Jed Clampett, is missing and is replaced with the same old shoddily performed banjo riff that has been on several other public domain releases. There is nothing new here. It is simply the same old-same old public domain rehash of select first season episodes that had fallen into public domain after the copyrights on the entire first season episodes expired. Again, as I said in another review, I understand that The Ballad of Jed Clampett is under copyright. BCI/Eclipse still could have had the copyright to that wonderful theme song loaned to them so it would have been wortwhile. What you simply get is simply the same old sloppy rehash of all other public domain DVD sets of this wonderful and still funny as heck show where it is simply a repeat of the last other issues of these first season episodes. If you want a more remarkably remastered collection of the very first season episodes and the first half of the second season episodes, then get MPI's The Beverly Hillbillies Ultimate Collection Volumes 1 and 2 and also, MPI's The Beverly Hillbillies/Petticoat Junction Christmas Collection. Those sets are authorized by the estate of the late Paul Henning and are remastered from the original negatives that were owned by the estate of Paul Henning for superb and far more superior quality.

history.title: The Beverly Hillbillies Collector's Edition, Vol. 2
history.review_title: Yet More Public Domain Sloppy Rehash
history.text: Once again, we are treated to a sloppily remastered public domain DVD set. This time, it is the Diamond Corporation/TGG Direct reissuing basically the same old thing that the other DVD companies did with many other previous editions regarding the episodes from the first and second seasons that had fallen into public domain. Likewise with those others, they simply replace that much loved theme song The Ballad Of Jed Clampett with the same old shoddily played banjo riff that the other companies who issued these same episodes that fell into public domain once their copyrights had expired. The show in itself is still wonderful, classic and still as funny as heck, but these sets leave so much to be desired. One more time, I understand that The Ballad of Jed Clampett is protected under copyright. But this company could have simply asked to be loaned the copyright to that much loved and much familiar theme song. I know that it isn't that simple, but still, the copyright owner probably would have loaned it to them if they asked. It would have made the issues of these episodes more complete and for nostalgia reasons. It would have been much better if they could have had the original theme music. One more time, if you want more remarkably remastered DVD sets of these first and second season episodes, then your best bet is to get MPI's The Beverly Hillbillies Ultimate Collection Volumes 1 & 2 and MPI's The Beverly Hillbillies/Petticoat Junction Ultimate Christmas Collection, which has the episodes digitally remastered using the original negatives, which are the property of the Paul Henning estate and are the only sets approved of by the Henning estate. Those sets are much better than any of these public domain DVD sets any day.

history.title: Mother
history.review_title: Another Winner From Albert Brooks And His Best Film To Date
history.text: Mother, a 1996 film by Albert Brooks, who also stars in this film, is another winner by him. This comedic and dramatic tale about a son moving back in with his mother is a wonderful film from start to finish. It also shows that there are still some great filmmakers in the good old USA. Brooks directed and co-wrote the script with Monica McGowan Johnson(may she rest in peace). The whole things starts with John Henderson(Brooks), a successful science fiction writer, who is going through his second divorce. He decides to move back in with his mother Beatrice(Debbie Reynolds)and decides to re-occupy the same room that he had when he was a child. John does this in hopes that by repairing the somewhat broken relationship that he had with his mother, he can also have better success with women. Soon, as John is settled in, he starts to make himself at home and helps his mother out whenever she needs it. The only problem is that it is causing some strains in her own personal life, especially where her relationships with other men are concerned. Plus, John can't seem to understand that his mother has since changed her lifestyle around starting from when he initially moved out. Also, he is soon in competition with his brother Jeff(Rob Morrow)for mother's affections as Beatrice is now reliving those days when both of these sons of hers were living in the house when they were still real young. Later on, while doing some checking around, John finds some old writings of hers that she did many years ago and reads them and thinks that they are really great. John soon discovers that this is why he feels that his mother hates him, though he does later learn that he is wrong in this assumption. Of course, his mother doesn't like him going through her personal things and such, but she doesn't really seem too mad about it with him. As usual, I won't give too much away as I don't want to spoil it for those who haven't seen this wonderful film as of yet. Mother became Brooks' highest grossing film to date. It made 19.1 million dollars at the box office. Like many of Brooks' previous films, it was also well received by critics. This is Brooks' best film to date. Brooks again really works wonders in front of and behind the camera. Mother is funny, poignant, bittersweet and has a lot of heart and soul. The film is very enjoyable and entertaining from start to finish. Mother is a rare film treat that can be enjoyed again and again without it ever getting dull or too boring. The chemistry between Brooks and Reynolds is really overwhelming and it works on all levels. They do make a wonderful team together as mother and son and that chemistry is what keeps the film alive and kicking. Originally, Albert Brooks wanted former US First Lady Nancy Reagan to portray the title character and she was contemplating coming out of retirement to portray the title character, but later had to back out as a result of her husband, former USA President Ronald Reagan, being sick and suffering from Alzheimer's Disease. Brooks also offered the role to Kathryn Grayson, but she turned it down thinking that the title character was, in her humble opinion, brain dead. Doris Day was also offered the title role, but she also turned it down. Nancy Reagen recommended her close friend Debbie Reynolds for the role and after Brooks talked with Reynolds' daughter Carrie Fisher, Carrie brought the script to her mother and she agreed to play the role. Debbie Reynolds was nominated for a Golden Globe award for "Best Performance by an actress in a Motion Picture Comedy/Musical" but won a Golden Satellite Award for the same category. Mother did win awards for it's script, which were the NFSC and NYFCC Awards respectively. I watched this film with my mother on Mother's Day 2012 and my mother enjoyed the film very much as much as I did. I advise all of you kids out there to watch this film with your mother any time that you wish. I hope that you and your mother enjoy this film as much as my mother and I did. Update: My mother died on September 21st, 2012 of cancer. May she always rest in peace. Whenever I decide to watch this film again, it will bring back the wonderful memory we had of her enjoying this movie. Overall, Mother is Brooks' best film to date and a film that still remains as wonderful no matter how many times that it is watched. It is also a very entertaining film by the one and only Albert Brooks. If you are a fan of Brooks' films like I am, this film should be in your DVD library. It is enjoyable from start to finish and never gets dull.

history.title: Mission: Magic! - The Complete Series [DVD]
history.review_title: Wonderful Cartoon Show Is Finally On DVD!
history.text: Mission Magic!, a cartoon show that was shown on Saturday mornings on the ABC TV Network during the 1973-1974 TV season, and was repeated again the following TV season on the same network, is a wonderful and entertaining cartoon show. The cartoon show was a spin-off of The Brady Kids, which, in itself, was a spin-off of The Brady Bunch. The cartoon starred Rick Springfield, who not only provided his voice for his animated counterpart, but also wrote almost every song that he sang on the show, with the exception of the title theme song. The series would become very popular over the ensuing years as a result of Rick Springfield later becoming popular in the next decade. The cartoon show was about a group of junior high school(now known as either middle or preparatory school)kids, who called themselves "The Adventurers Club", that were lead by a teacher named Miss Tickle(a play on the word mystical)who was a very magical teacher who used her magic at times whenever the kids would meet every week after school let out. After summoning her cat named "Tut-Tut" by saying "Oh, Tut-Tut, cat of ancient lore. 'Tis time to draw the magic door." When the door was drawn on the blackboard, the door would open and whisk the kids, Miss Tickle and "Tut-Tut" into the realm beyond the black board to meet up with Rick Springfield and his sidekick, a blue owl named Ptolemy, in the realm. The kids and Rick would embark on many adventures in the realm and also would meet and learn about important historical figures in the process. They would also at times meet up against an evil force, such as a supposed wizard named Modran and his three midget sidekicks or a giant lady who hated anything to do with magic, especially when her magic was outdone by Miss Tickle's magic or when a nemesis named Dr. Daguerreotype and his partners in crime would use magic cameras to steal many of the world's wonders or when a villain calling himself the chameleon would make himself into Rick Springfield to get into the real world to later pose as millionaires to steal their money out of their bank accounts. Miss Tickle, Rick and the Adventurers Club would go on many adventures and would also learn a moral lesson or two in the process. The kids always seemed to be having fun in their adventures and enjoyed their learning of lessons in the process. The show was always entertaining from start to finish and was never dull. It was funny and was also much better than the cartoon that it spun off from. Mission Magic! is a wonderful cartoon show packed with music and comedy, which can be enjoyed by people of all ages again and again. Mission Magic! was also used as a vehicle to help promote Rick Springfield in the USA, as he was still a relative unknown to everyone living in the USA during much of the 1970's. Despite having a Top 20 (#14) hit with Speak to the Sky on Capitol Records, and releasing four albums on different labels for much of the 1970's(Beginnings on Capitol, Comic Book Heroes on Columbia, Mission Magic! on Wizzardo and Wait for Night on Chelsea and an unissued fifth album called Beautiful Feelings, which was recorded in 1978 for Mercury Records and finally released in 1984 by Mercury after some overdubbing was done on the master tapes without Rick consenting to it nor authorizing it), Rick really didn't become popular until the early 1980's, when he was a star on the popular ABC soap opera General Hospital as Noah Drake and would resume his recording career in 1981 with the Top 10 album Working Class Dog on RCA Records and a US #1 hit with Jessie's Girl. Over the 1980's, all of Rick's 1970's albums were reissued by their respective labels, with only one exception, which was Wait for Night, which was reissued by RCA as a result of it's original label, Chelsea Records, going bankrupt after Rick had an almost Top 40 hit with a song called Take a Hand(#41)and it's parent album, the aforementioned Wait for Night, selling modestly. Also, during that time, Mission Magic! was being rerun in select areas where Rick was the most popular and select episodes were also released on VHS over the years by it's company Filmation. Rick would continue to be popular throughout the 1980's and is still pretty popular today as well as highly respected by his peers and fans. I watched Mission Magic! every Saturday morning myself, but I discovered this show on the syndicated channel WUTV Channel 29 as I also used to watch the syndicated children's show Big Blue Marble, which proceeded Mission Magic!. I became a fan of that show and waited eagerly for a DVD release once the DVD boom was taking off and when it was finally going to be on DVD, I pre-ordered my copy through Amazon and received it on the day that the DVD was to be released into the stores. I watched the whole set and I still enjoy this cartoon show to this very day as it is still just as fresh and new as the day that it was originally shown on TV. Mission Magic! is a wonderfully fun and entertaining cartoon show that still stands the test of time. It still holds up very well after all of these years. I highly recommend Mission Magic! to everyone who is a fan of Rick Springfield as well as fans of classic cartoon shows or both. It is a very entertaining and fun show to watch and can be enjoyed again and again no matter how old you are.

history.title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (2-Disc Ultimate Edition)
history.review_title: It's Everything It's Reputation Says It Is
history.text: The original 1974 shocker film, The Texas Chainsaw Massacre, is everything that it's reputation says it is. This film was made by Tobe Hooper in 1974. Hooper set out to create a movie that would be the most shocking ever made for the big screen and IMHO, he succeeded. He produced, directed and co-wrote the film with Kim Henkel, who would later make another film entry in the series; Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Next Generation (a.k.a.The Return of the Texas Chainsaw Massacre) a little over two decades later. The whole film starts with a narration by future Night Court star John Larroquette, which tells the story of what will happen in the film as we watch it. After the opening credits, we see five youths, three young men and two young women, taking a little cruise out in the countryside to check up on a grave where the Hardesty siblings grandfather is buried to see if it had been tampered with as in the area, there was a rash of grave diggings and grave robberies done by a mysterious suspect, with whom the police don't know who or why they are doing this sort of thing. The main youths Sally Hardesty (Marilyn Burns, May she rest in peace as she died on August 5th, 2014) and her invalid brother Franklin (Paul Partain; may he rest in peace) are conversing with the other youths in their van and talking about numerous things as they are on their way to an old shack out in the countryside on a hill. Along the way, they complain about the intense heat and humidity and even notice the smell of the old slaughterhouse where cattle are sold and slaughtered for meat to sell to consumers. Along the way, they pick up a freaky looking hitchhiker(Edwin Neal), who later proves to be part of their undoing as he causes trouble for the youths in the van, which ends with him slaughtering Franklin's wrist with a straight razor and being thrown out of the van because of that, and he leaves a marking of blood on the van and that is where the story really starts to unfold. After stopping at a service station and finding out that they have no gas, the man who owns the service station (Jim Siedow; may he also rest in peace), gives them some fresh barbecue and they head out to the old shack and later find out about the blood smeared on the van earlier by the hitchhiker. The rest of the youths check out the old shack and Franklin gets disgusted with being left alone while they check everything out. It is then that the story starts to get interesting as Kirk(William Vail)and Pam(Teri McMinn) decide to head to the old creek to go swimming only to see that the old creek has dried up since the last time that the Hardesty siblings were there. They stumble upon an old isolated farmhouse and after Kirk goes in, he gets hit with a sledgehammer by Leatherface(Gunnar Hansen) and after twitching, he gets hit again and Leatherface slams the kitchen up with a metal door. Pam, getting suspicious as to why Kirk doesn't come back out, she enters the house and after seeing all the furniture made with human bones and a lot of feathers all across the floor, proceeds to run out, only to be stopped by Leatherface and hung up on a hook and while screaming in pain, she watches as Leatherface cuts up Kirk with a chainsaw. Later on, Jerry(Allen Danzinger)gets concerned and decides to go out and look for Kirk and Pam, only to also stumble upon the old isolated farmhouse, enters the house and heads for the kitchen, where out of curiosity, he opens up the freezer and sees Pam in it and she is still alive as she raises her hands in fear, and looks partially frozen, and in comes Leatherface with his sledgehammer attempting to hit Jerry with it, which he misses slightly, but Jerry narrowly and successfully escapes with his life and disappears mysteriously as we never see Jerry again for the rest of the film. Later on, as it is getting dark, the Hardesty siblings are concerned and worried about their friends and think of looking for them, but are also undecided if they should because they don't want to leave the van alone in case the others come back. When the night is starting to get closer, they start calling out the names of their friends, but hear nothing. They proceed to look for them in the woods only to come across an angry Leatherface who slashes Franklin with his chainsaw and begins chasing Sally all over the place with the chainsaw with the determination of killing her and using her body for food for his demented cannibalistic family. The chase takes them to the farmhouse, then back outside in the woods and ending at the very service station they stopped at earlier in the film, only instead of getting protection and possibly getting the police involved, she learns that the service station owner, who is known as "the cook" in the family, is related to both Leatherface and the hitchhiker that they picked up earlier. Unbeknown to Sally, this is the start of an unforgettable night of unimaginable horror as both Leatherface and the hitchhiker taunt and abuse her relentlessly and although the cook says that he takes no pleasure in killing, he really contradicts this when he smiles later on when they continue to taunt and verbally abuse Sally, scaring her and motivates her begging the cook to make it stop. It turns out that Leatherface, whose facial mask is made out of crude human flesh, is looking for a new face and wants Sally's face as his new face. Will Sally escape the torturous family's house?, or, Will she be a feast for this demented family? As usual, I won't give too much away as I don't want top spoil this for anyone who hasn't seen this intensely shocking and horrific motion picture as of yet. This film was released in 1974 with the publicity that it was based on an actual crime that happened in Texas in August of 1973. It was only 1/8th true. The film and it's main protagonist, Leatherface, was actually loosely based on the story of Plainfield, Wisconsin murderer Ed Gein (a.k.a. The Ghoul of Plainfield) who also robbed graves and also killed people, particularly elderly looking women, for pleasure. Gein also came from an abusive home life as his mother, a legalistic styled so called Christian lady, repeatedly abused him and forbid him from having any contact with the outside world and after she died, his whole personal world came crashing down on him and he would later become an unholy terror in his hometown that he would be locked away in a mental institution for the rest of his life until his death in 1984 of respiratory failure. The rest of the film is basically the pure invention of Tobe Hooper and his co-screenwriter Kim Henkel. Hooper also revealed that he was mostly inspired to create this horrific motion picture by seeing a display of chainsaws in a hardware store and the idea to create a movie about a homicidal maniac with an equally homicidal family to boot came at him in a split second. He and Henkel wrote the script and started casting immediately. The whole thing started in 1972 and was finished within a year and ready for release. Again, Hooper decided to play the publicity that it was actually based on an actual crime, though most of the film's story was fictional. This even had an impact later on as to this day, many college and university students who major in psychiatry, psychology, criminal law and even law enforcement still visit the Texas State Police to ask for any files on this crime, only to be told repeatedly by the Texas State Police that the story really never happened and that it was all a publicity stunt by the filmmakers to shock the daylights out of people seeing the movie and really scare the daylights out of them. The film received mixed reviews upon it's original release in 1974, but over the years, it has been reappraised by many critics when they discovered the film's hidden greatness. Rex Reed even called this film "The Most Horrifying Motion Picture I Have Ever Seen!" I have to agree with Mr. Reed here regarding this particular film as it is horrifying and really scary. IMHO, this is the scariest motion picture ever made. Tobe Hooper, when making this film, really overdid it with the realism that he was trying to convey with this film and it worked. The film really carries you over the edge of your seat and really grabs you and refuses to let you go until the bitter end. Not only that, each and every prop that Hooper uses in this film looks like the real thing and that is what contributes to the horror factors making this a truly scary motion picture that continues to shock no matter how many times it is watched. It's ability to continue to horrify audiences repeatedly remains intact that at one private screening, the viewers walked out of the theater in a state of shock. I have watched this film repeatedly myself over the years and it still scares the daylights out of me. I have never had any motion picture in the horror genre do that to me until I saw this one. I remember seeing The Exorcist and while that movie scared me as well, it doesn't come close to this film. Many people claim that The Exorcist is the scariest motion picture ever made, but IMHO, The Texas Chainsaw Massacre is the scariest motion picture ever made with The Exorcist ranking a close second to it. This is scary and then some. The film is also a cult classic and is widely hailed as a masterpiece of modern horror and has also been highly influential. This film passed through a few distributors over the years since it's initial 1974 release. The first was Bryanston, which was an independent distributor of pornographic films and was later passed on to New Line Cinema, who took over distribution. When the home video market took off in the 1980's, the film passed through a few more distributors with Media Home Entertainment initially releasing this on home video and later, MPI Home Video continued it's home video run and when DVD's became the wave of the future, Pioneer released the film with a few special features added to it and finally, this special edition steel box release by Dark Sky Films, which has the film looking more colorful, increasing the terrifying factors that this film is known for, with various special features, such as commentaries, theatrical trailers, TV spots, radio spots, two documentaries: Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Shocking Truth and Flesh Wounds: A tour of the house in the film with Gunnar Hansen leading the way and deleted scenes, outtakes and bloopers and a still gallery. Regarding sound options, you have a choice of three, such as Dolby 5.1, 2.0 Stereo Surround and Original Mono, with subtitles in English and Spanish. This film also has it's share of controversy as it was banned in several countries initially, mainly due to it's subject matter and it's overdone realism. In the wake of the film, it has spawned three sequels, a 2003 re-imagining, a 2006 prequel and a much recent 3D re-imagining of the film. It has also inspired copycat films where the main protagonist also uses a chainsaw in their murderous ways. Unless you have a strong stomach, I suggest that you don't watch this film as you definitely need a strong stomach to watch this particular film. If you do decide to give this film a try, I will caution you that you will be in for the most horrifying ride of your life as there has nothing been made like this before or after that will scare the daylights out of you, shock you, and also will grab you and won't let you go until the bitter end. Also, if you do decide to watch this film, don't ever say that you weren't warned ahead of time. It is truly a scary film and it is very horrifying and sure to leave you with chills that you will never forget. Overall, this original 1974 film is, IMHO, the scariest motion picture ever made and if you are a fan of the horror genre, it is well worth a look, but first make sure that you have a strong stomach before you even think of watching this film. I highly recommend this film to horror fans all over. It is a movie experience that you will never forget as it will leave an impact as well an impression on you that no other film has ever left before or after. It is scary and yes, it is horrifying, and yes, it is a shocker of epic proportions.

history.title: Class of 1984
history.review_title: Another Film That's Everything It's Reputation Says It Is
history.text: The 1982 film, Class of 1984, was directed by Mark L.Lester and was a very controversial movie back in the day. The film is known for it's notorious violence and realistic performances by it's cast. The film, though very controversial, was an eerie prophecy as to what would happen in the USA school system if school administrators did nothing to stop school violence and bullying. The film itself served as a warning that was never heeded by the USA school system as today, violence in school is now an everyday happening. The film is also thought to be a modern day updating and/or remake/re-imagining of the classic 1955 film The Blackboard Jungle. The film starts with somewhat rookie teacher Andy Norris(Perry King)starting his first day at Lincoln High School as the new music teacher. He meets with veteran teacher Terry Corrigan(Roddy McDowall; may he rest in peace)in the parking lot and sees that he has a gun in his briefcase and wonders if it is really necessary. As Norris and Corrigan enter through the faculty entrance, they see kids, mostly violent gang members, entering school through a metal detector to detect any weapons, though at times, weapons do get snuck in using other ways of sneaking. Norris meets with the school's principal(David Gardner)and is assigned to a music class replacing the previous teacher who got hurt, which is never revealed how he did and then Norris meets the school's tough guys led by an angry young man named Peter Stegman(Timothy Van Patten)and after a confrontation with the gang, which results in the gang leaving the classroom, Norris meets Deneen(Erin Noble using the stage name Erin Flannery)and Arthur(Michael J. Fox in an early film role before his days as Family Ties' Alex Keaton as simply Micheal Fox before he added the J to his name to honor Canadian actor Michael J. Pollard) and the rest of the class and Norris starts to settle in with his new job, but he also hopes in time to reach the school's bully Stegman and hopefully try to see what his real problem is. As Norris continues teaching at the school, he has numerous run-in's with Stegman's gang and also, as a result of these things, his home life with his pregnant wife (Merrie Lynn Ross who also serves as co-executive producer with director Lester)gets even more complicated. Arthur and Deneen also become the target of Stegman's gang as they are repeatedly harassed and taunted by them, only to have their inexcusable shenanigans broken up by Norris once he sees it. Norris also becomes the victim of Stegman's taunts and also hurts himself in front of Norris in the boys bathroom and blames Norris for attacking him, which gets Norris into trouble. Repeatedly, Norris tries to have the principal and a police detective(Al Waxman; may he also rest in peace) get involved to put a stop to this violence, but both the principal and the police detective feel powerless to do anything about it. Later on, a fresh gang recruit, as part of his initiation, stabs innocent Arthur in the cafeteria while the gang starts a fight in order to distract the cafeteria staff so the new recruit can do the job. When Norris tries to talk with Mrs, Stegman(Linda Sorensen), he learns too painfully that even Stegman's own mother is also intimidated by her own son. During all of this insanity, a kid dies after falling from the flagpole after overdosing on drugs supplied by Stegman's gang. The violence gets worse with Stegman continuing to repeatedly taunt Norris and trying to intimidate him, but repeatedly fails as Norris won't let Stegman do that. It gets out of control one night when the school decides to have the school band perform in the auditorium with the gang now forcing themselves into the Norris apartment, kidnap his pregnant wife and it leads to a showdown between Norris and the gang. I am not going to give too much away as I don't want to spoil it for anyone who hasn't seen this film as of yet. The film was made in Canada at a high school during the Summer of 1982 and was released in the Fall of that year. It was the number one film in New York City for five weeks and it received mixed reviews by the critics. The film's script was written by Lester, with John Saxton, Tom Holland and Barry Schneider(who requested to have his name removed from the finished product after seeing a rough cut of the film and was offended by all of the violence in the film that he wanted nothing to do with it, though he did write much of the dialogue)with a story credit by Tom Holland. According to Lester, the film was inspired by actual events that took place at his old alma mater in Sepulveda California called Monroe High School. When he visited the school, he saw that there was much violence happening there and he also visited other areas where there was rampant school violence and decided that he would make a movie as a warning to the USA educational system that if they didn't do their job to stop school violence now, it's going to get a lot worse and will wind up seriously out of control. This film was eerily prophetic in it's approach as school violence did get much worse with many incidents of school violence happening all over the USA alone, starting with the Columbine High School massacre in 1999 and all the subsequent school violence massacres in the wake of Columbine. The film was controversial back in it's day, but it did predict a future time where violence in American schools would get much worse and worse until it would go completely out of control. Class of 1984 prophesied this and that eerie prophecy did come true in more ways than one. The film has become a cult classic over the many years since it's release. This film is intensely violent and shocking and it hasn't lost it's ability to shock and stun audiences. The film is an edge of the seat thrill ride that will grab you and won't let you go until the bitter end. It is well acted, well written and is a technically well made film. It also has a lot of style and the shock factor remains no matter how many times it is watched. It has never lost it's ability to truly horrify and shock audiences, even though the eerie prophecy that the film made actually came true. The point is that it is still a shocking film that will make you shiver with chills that are unforgettable. The film's budget was just about 4.5 Million Dollars. The film made 15 Million Dollars in the USA alone, with an extra 35 Million Dollars from overseas. Overall, the film grossed 50 Million Dollars. The film was released by Vestron Home Video initially during the 1980's home video boom and was shown on syndicated TV lots of times. The film was later withdrawn from home video distribution and was out of print for quite a long time until Anchor Bay Entertainment decided to issue it on DVD. The DVD looks more colorful. The sound quality is excellent and the soundtrack sounds very crisp. The special features include commentary by Mark L.Lester, A featurette called Blood and Blackboards that features interviews with cast members, the films theatrical trailer, two TV spots, a Mark L.Lester biography and the film's script in DVD-ROM format. Alice Cooper sings the theme song I Am The Future, which was written by Lalo Schifrin and Gary Osbourne, who also co-wrote songs with Elton John. The film also has a cameo by punk rock band Teenage Head. The film's theme song is also on Alice Cooper's 1982 album Zipper Catches Skin. In the wake of the release of this 1982 film, there were two sequels, which were Class of 1999(It's ironic that the year 1999 is in the title of this sequel as the Columbine High School massacre happened in 1999), a science fiction styled sequel that was also directed by Lester and like it's predecessor, was also released on home video by Vestron that was released theatrically, though limited, in 1990 and Class of 1999 Part 2: The Substitute, which was a direct to video sequel made by different filmmakers through Cinetel Films and was released by Vidmark entertainment in 1994. There have also been talks of a possible remake or re-imagining of this film, according to the IMDB message board on the Class of 1984 page on that site, but so far, there has been nothing coming from Lester or anyone that was associated with him about this particular area. Overall, Class of 1984 is a film that is everything it's reputation says it is and is one of the most shocking films ever made for the silver screen with a prophecy that would later come true. This is a film that must be seen to be believed. This film is also bound to please anyone who is an aficionado of action films and teen thrillers. Again, this film must be seen to be believed.

history.title: Carrie (Special Edition)
history.review_title: Wonderful Adaption of King's Classic Novel
history.text: Carrie, a 1976 film based on the classic horror novel by Stephen King, is a wonderful adaption of the novel. This was also the first time that any of King's novels or short stories was made into a feature film. The whole thing starts with the girl's playing volleyball on the Bates High School volleyball court. The character at the center of all this, Carrie White (Sissy Spacek), is a girl that is shunned by the "normal" crowd and is the pet hate of all the kids at her high school. We see this later on as the film starts to unfold in the girl's locker room and when Carrie has her first experience of menstruation, she is taunted left and right by the girls and has feminine pads and tampons thrown at her. She then faces the terror of confronting her religious fanatic legalism practicing mother (Piper Laurie) who accuses her of sinning with the curse of blood and is thrown into her prayer closet. After a while, Carrie is let out and she goes to bed. As punishment, the girls who taunted Carrie are forced into a punishing physical fitness routine courtesy of their gym teacher Miss Collins(Betty Buckley), only to have the meanest of the rest of the girls Chris Hargensen (Nancy Allen in her feature film debut) want out and she is subsequently out of school and the upcoming senior prom. Chris later enlists her boyfriend Billy Nolan(John Travolta in his feature film debut)to play a prank on Carrie in revenge for her being kicked out of school and the prom. During this, Sue Snell (Amy Irving) feel remorse for participating in the locker room ruckus and decides to have her boyfriend Tommy Ross (William Katt) to take Carrie to the prom to make up for her part in the ruckus. Carrie tells her mother that Tommy Ross invited her to the prom and despite her mother's objections and wranglings, Carrie says that she is going and that is all. Billy, Chris and a few others go to a pig farm and slaughter a pig to get it's blood and they use the blood in their planned prank on Carrie. On the night of the senior prom, Tommy and Carrie walk into the gym where the prom is being held and things are going well for her and to the surprise of her and Tommy, they are elected king and queen of the prom and at that moment, the pig blood is dumped on her and it stuns everyone in the place. After hearing laughter in her mind, Carrie's telekinetic powers take over and all H-E-Double Hockey Sticks breaks loose and all the students and faculty at the prom wind up losing their lives and once she's out, she inadvertently gets her revenge on Chris and Billy by forcing their car to roll several times and explode. For those of you who haven't seen this, I won't give too much away as I don't want to spoil it for you's who haven't seen this wonderful adaption as of yet. Larry Cohen wrote a great screenplay for Carrie. He adapts King's novel well. I also give Brian DePalma credit for his direction as his direction keeps moving things along. The film is also technically well made and the film is also well acted by the cast. The film is an effective mix of horror and a touch of comedy. It will not only have you on the edge of your seat, but will also make you chuckle here and there. The film is very entertaining and it's never dull. It does keep you entertained and it doesn't let up until the bitter end. I read the novel of this in junior high school during study hall as I am a huge Stephen King fan as I have read many of his novels and short stories. I saw this film on syndicated TV when I was 14 and I enjoyed the film immensely. I would later buy a VHS tape of the film and I watched it and I still enjoyed it as much as I did when I first watched it. I also would later buy the special edition DVD when it was released as part of a three DVD set. The film never gets dull no matter how many times it is watched and it is still a very entertaining film. This special edition DVD has a lot of very good special features. We have a photo gallery, A documentary on acting Carrie, another documentary about the filming called Visualizing Carrie, King talking about his experience writing the novel and last but not least, a featurette about the Broadway flop "Carrie: the Musical" with Betty Buckley and Larry Cohen talking about the musical. The film spawned a 1999 sequel called The Rage: Carrie 2, which was both a critical and commercial disaster It also spawned the aforementioned flop Broadway musical that though a flop, has it's own cult following. There were also two more adaptions of the novel, the first being a 2002 made for TV film that was more faithful to the novel than the original 1976 adaption and a 2013 re-imagining where Larry Cohen also had a hand in the screenplay writing. If you have a taste for horror or comedy or both, the 1976 Carrie is right for you. It is a very entertaining film that not only will scare you, but make you chuckle a little. It is also a movie that you can watch more than once and never get tired of. It is also a movie worth owing and having in your DVD library.

history.title: Carrie
history.review_title: The Best Adaption of King's Novel
history.text: This 2002 made for TV adaption of King's bestselling novel is the second adaption of King's novel and also a re-imagining at the same time. This film stays a lot more true and faithful to the novel than the 1976 feature film adaption (see review). The whole movie is centered on the local police investigation of what happened on prom night at Ewen High School. The police interview students who were at or not at the prom. As the police interview the students and later on, the gym teacher, we watched the story unfold as we watch the events leading up to prom night. The girls are playing softball in gym class and when it is all over, we see them head for the girl's locker room to shower and change clothes. Carrie (Angela Bettis) showers alone and is scared when she sees blood and fears that she is dying while the girls taunt her by shouting repeatedly "Period!" to her and the gym teacher Miss Desjardan (Rena Sofer) intervenes and she is sent home. Carrie then faces her religiously fanatical and legalistic mother (Patricia Clarkson) and is forced into a prayer closet and not let out until her mother feels that she is truly sorry for supposedly sinning when she had her first menstruation experience. Later on, as the girls are getting ready for gym, Miss Desjardan shows how angry she is with the girls that she decides to punish them by having them do intense physical fitness in the gym everyday, with only Chris Hargensen (Emilie De Ravin) deciding that she won't cooperate and as a result of that, she is suspended and banned from the upcoming senior prom. Carrie researches telekinetics and other sorts of strange phenoma in the school's library because she really can't understand why she has this power and what she can do about it. Later on, Sue Snell (Kandyse McClure) talks her boyfriend Tommy Ross (Tobias Mehler) into taking Carrie White to the upcoming senior prom out of remorse for participating in the locker room ruckus with the other girls. At first, Tommy is reluctant thinking that it is a totally mean joke and that Carrie will see right through it, but subsequently agrees to do it. Tommy later asks Carrie, who initially refuses thinking that she is being tricked and after some nice persuasion by Tommy, Carrie accepts, which leads to her telling her mother that she was invited and that she is going despite her mother's objections. Carrie shows that her mother's reign over her is over and that she is going and that her mother can't stop her and that is that. Chris later asks her boyfriend Billy Nolan (Jesse Cadotte) to help her play a prank on Carrie White and when Chris later hears through her girlfriend Tina (Katharine Isabelle) that Tommy Ross is taking Carrie White to the prom by showing her a ballot with Tommy and Carrie on it, they decide to go to a pig farm to slaughter a pig for it's blood as part of the prank, with Jackie Talbot (Malcolm Scott) and Kenny Garson (Miles Meadows) also in on the prank. As they arrive at the prom, everyone is shocked to see Carrie walk in with Tommy and the first to come to them is Helen (Chelan Simmons) and Roy (Steve Byers) who compliments her on her dress and they start to talk and get along. They are also approached by Norma (Meghan Black) who sees that Carrie is glowing with enthusiasm. After a confrontation by Miss Desjardin, Tommy and Carrie share in a slow dance and are surprised when they are elected king and queen of the senior prom. Not too long after this happens, Chris and Billy dump the pig's blood on Carrie and the whole crowd is shocked by this happening and when Kenny starts shouting taunts in the form of pig calls, Carrie has a mental breakdown and hears imaginary laughter in her mind and this unleashes her telekinetic powers and all H-E-Double Hockey Sticks breaks loose on everyone at the prom. The frightened prom night goers run everyplace around the gym, but find no way out. Carrie starts leaving the gym and as soon as she leaves the school, which starts to crumble as she leaves as a result of the electrical fire that was started when the electrical mechanisms malfunctioned, Carrie leaves mountains of destruction as she continues to walk home in a telekinetic trance and inadvertently gets even with Billy and Chris by making their vehicle smash and crash into a pole. The town becomes a disaster area as Carrie leaves destruction and death where she walks. I won't give too much away as I don't want to spoil it for those of you who haven't seen it yet. David Carson does a terrific auspicious job as the director of this 2002 adaption of King's bestselling novel. Bryan Fuller also wrote a great teleplay for this film. The special effects are realistic and well done. The film is also very well acted for a TV movie as Angela Bettis plays Carrie White brilliantly and Patricia Clarkson portrays Carrie's mother with unholy relish. The rest of the cast also portray their roles in the film wonderfully. Each and everything about this film is great. It is an edge of the seat thrill ride when the mayhem really starts and once it has you in it's grip, it won't let you go until the bitter end. It is a scary and frightening film that sends chills up the spine.We get to see the story unfold as the police detective talks with several students and a faculty member about prom night and what had happened that night with a lot of unanswered questions. I watched this made for TV adaption when it premiered on the NBC network in November of 2002. Before I did, I re-read King's novel and when I watched the film soon after, I saw that this was a more faithful adaption of the novel than the initial 1976 adaption. I also felt that it was a much better adaption as well as the best adaption of the novel. It stays true to the novel and leaves you wondering what will happen next as you watch it. I actually enjoyed this adaption and I still enjoy it. It happens to be my favorite adaption of the bestselling novel. I still enjoy the original 1976 adaption, but this particular adaption will always be my favorite of all three, as the novel was later adapted and re-imagined again in 2013. The DVD has nothing in regards to special features. The only things that we get is the preview trailer for this particular adaption and a few other preview trailers of other MGM released horror films. We also get a recommendation page of other MGM release horror DVD's. The movie still looks as colorful and fresh as the day that the film premiered on NBC in November of 2002. It was also meant to be a pilot for a TV series about Carrie, but was later scrapped. I bought my copy used from a local DVD rental store that was going out of business.I still enjoy this particular version and I have watched it several times since owning it. If you have a taste for horror, this 2002 adaption of Carrie is for you. It delivers all the goods that you'd expect in a horror film and it also will frighten and scare you. No fan of horror should pass this one up nor forget to add to their personal DVD library's. It is truly a treat for any fan of horror films.

history.title: Mysterious Museum
history.review_title: A Fantastic Sci-Fi Fantasy For All Ages
history.text: Mysterious Museum,a 1999 direct to video Sci-Fi Fantasy flick is a fantastic fantasy film that not only the whole family can watch, but also people of all ages can watch. It all starts on a day in a museum when Kim,a teenage girl who works in the museum, brings her brother Ben and kid sister Casey with her to watch them. While Kim is working, she asks Ben to keep an eye on Casey but Ben does the opposite by riding his skateboard around and just being the fun loving teen boy that he is. When Kim decides to check up on them during an electrical storm, she is whisked away into a painting from the museum and smack dab in the 17th Century where she soon becomes the prisoner of an evil wizard named Falco. When Ben,Casey and the museum curator look for Kim, Ben now realizes that Kim is in the painting and is also whisked away into the 17th century to find her and bring her back to the present. But Falco has a jewel that will make him the ruler of the world and Ben must retrieve it in order for him and his sister to return to the present. With the help of a magical, clumsy but likeable helper who is a cross between the curator and Pee Wee Herman courtesy of Casey, who draws him and places him on the frame of the painting, alongside a midget whom Ben befriends on his journey, Ben goes on a search for the jewel and knows that he has to use everything in his power to rescue Kim, retrieve the jewel and defeat the evil Falco before it's too late and they are stuck in the 17th century forever. Can Ben rescue Kim and retrieve the jewel and get back to the present in time or Will they be stuck in the 17th Century forever where they will never see their parents or friends again? Watch the movie and find out. Mysterious Museum is one of those rare films that can be watched by not only the whole family, but people of all ages who wish to watch a good movie when they want to.It's also a very entertaining picture. One can only wonder what would have been the result if this movie were released in theaters and it became a success rather than release it straight to video. It's an amazing and magical ride that never lets up until the bitter end. Mysterious Museum is a fantastic Sci-Fi fantasy film that's fun for the whole family and for all ages. It's also a movie that can be enjoyed again and again.

history.title: Murdercycle
history.review_title: An Edge of the Seat Thrill Ride
history.text: This Sci-Fi/Horror shocker from 1998 is an edge of the seat thrill ride from start to finish. The action never lets up. It keeps up and keeps you guessing until the bitter end. It all starts when a meteorite crashes onto earth in a top secret government zone and possesses an innocent motorbike rider who has seemed to lost his way. He soon turns into an unstoppable killing machine and is determined on keeping it's immortality even if it means killing anybody who is intent on stopping him. A team of US marine soldiers led by a female psychic are using everything in their power to stop the reign of terror by this phantom motor bike rider. The psychic finds a way that this can be done,but she knows that she has to race against time to save herself and the soldiers. Will she succeed? Will the soldiers win? Can they together STOP the phantom rider's reign of terror once and for all? Never in the tradition of films such as Duel, The Car, Christine, Maximum Overdrive, Wheels Of Terror and Trucks has a movie had been able to carry you over the edge. While those movies are entertaining in their own right, none of them can even equal the power of this thriller. Murdercycle is strictly in a class by itself. Murdercycle is an edge of the seat thrill ride with non-stop action and thrills and some very good acting performances by the cast. If you are a fan of non-stop action Sci-Fi/Horror films, this one is for you. Murdercycle is an action packed thrill ride to enjoy again and again.

history.title: The Pirates of Penzance
history.text: Truly an unforgettable show, though it seems I have, since I saw it locally years ago and thought I had never seen it before. "(I Am the Very Model of a)Modern Major General" proved to me otherwise, as that was definitely familiar. So again for the first time I got to see this show and found it to be very fun and enjoyable. Kevin Kline; wow that man has a lot of enthusiasm, energy, agility, and comic timing - even in dancing. An impressive performance for an actor in a musical production. The policemen got a larger chance to shine than either chorus of daughters or pirates by having the goofier dances and songs, which they endearingly wobbled and trilled to and so are more notable and memorable than the others who can easily be forgotten. Vocal standout, aside from Kevin Kline doing remarkably well, was Linda Ronstadt. It's hard to imagine most popular recording artists handling the challenging vocals the way she did. Angela Lansbury was a comforting familiar presence; she seems to be cast based on being so ubiquitous. Though as someone I know said, she does sing better than most teapots. The sets were, well, a bit odd. Cleverly cartoon-ish to fit with the feeling of comic unreality, or cheaply designed and made so as to keep the budget low. May as well give them the benefit of the doubt on this. A great combination of intelligent and wacky humor all in all, and with a slightly more refined vocabulary than most musicals that come to mind.

history.title: Into The Woods (Theatrical)
history.text: It looks like the fact that Into the Woods is a musical took some people unawares. The premise of the plot also seems to be a point of contention for others, citing too many different stories and unhappy endings. If you can accept these things then you may enjoy Into the Woods if you aren't familiar with it. We all know what happened to Bambi's mommy and that was a Disney movie too. Some of the details also reflect the original stories more accurately. The changes from the stage production are probably meant to make a good movie and appeal to a broader audience without offending. You can get the gist of everything, but it also sounds like the theatre buffs are disappointed. The show in general is very clever and captivating despite being compromised of familiar ones. I missed the missing Agony part two. It presents an interesting message too, though I suppose people take what they want from it. The world may be fraught with danger, but I think that's the risk we all have to take, as children inevitably grow up and come down from their towers. The acting and singing were actually pretty good which was a nice surprise. Though while watching Agony I just couldn't figure out what I was being reminded of - my first thought was '80s George Michael, then I realized ... Sigfried and Roy. I was waiting for the white tigers. And Meryl Streep, she didn't do badly at all (oh right, Mama Mia). I enjoyed Anna Kendrick's voice quite a bit, and to find something negative to say, a bit more than her acting. It was a little too modern-teenage-girl with the head bobbing and pithy language. The children were good, but I think Red was channeling the Broadway cast soundtrack and Jack had a touch of something in there with his accent. Both kids showed exceptional talent and poise. It's a great story if you're not familiar with it, and if you like it you might want to explore other cast productions or recordings. Nice to see Mr. Depp as well.

history.title: It's a Very Merry Muppet Christmas Movie
history.text: Least Christmasy Christmas movie ever. This was not a child friendly movie and the adult themed topics and jokes seemed out of place in a movie that vaguely concerned Christmas as per the title. I think the biggest Christmas reference had the most to do with which calendar day the rent was due, for there was not a lot else that had to do with the celebration or meaning of the holiday other than biting some uninspired pieces out of other holiday movie fare and stitching them together for this debacle. If this weren't marketed as a Christmas movie it could be the average Muppet movie about the evil landlord who would like tenants to pay their rent and probably no one would have cared as much about the sex jokes.

history.title: Murder, She Wrote: The Complete Sixth Season
history.review_title: The missing persons case involving one J. B. Fletcher.
history.text: Season six is akin to ordering something at a restaurant and having your waiter bring you something else. When you ask the waiter why they didn't bring you the meal you ordered, the waiter tells you, "Well, we understood your order perfectly, but we thought you might like to try something else that you didn't order which we consider to be worth trying." Your anger has been replaced by dejection, and you sigh and say, "But I ordered the Angela Lansbury special because that's what I wanted." "The waiter smiles, "Ah then, you will be pleased to know that we have a short prerecorded description by Angela Lansbury of the thing we are serving you." You shake your head in disbelief and pick up your fork knowing that you have been defeated by Hollywood logic. I'm confused as to why about half the episodes of this season aren't actual Murder, She Wrote episodes starring Angela Lansbury. Hopefully there was a good reason and hopefully they don't (didn't) continue this on for the remaining seasons. I know I'm about twenty years late on this, but what were they thinking?

history.title: The Revenant
history.text: Good acting by almost everyone but goodness this was boring. Probably I will get lots of down votes for saying anything negative. It just seemed like a whole lot of nothing with some things that didn't make sense. The whole revenge theme drove the movie but really, the bad guy who did the bad thing is one of the more relatable characters, because what he did that was so bad made sense at the time and the rest of the movie the other guy is mad at him for it. Perhaps I need something less sophistimicated to watch.

history.title: Chappie [DVD]
history.review_title: They may have misspelled the title.
history.text: The high ratings from users seem to address the message the film maker wanted to share with his audience. The low ratings seems to address the manner with which and vehicle wherein he shared his message. So much of this storyline just doesn't make sense. Maybe everybody has to get high to understand what is going on so they can understand where the writers were coming from, because most rational beings don't act the way the characters did. Unless that's some nouveau art thing, to, I don't know, create a life, then drop it off at some thug's house and tell them you'll be back tomorrow to visit for a bit. It's nonsensical, and I'm not talking about cultural differences. The acting wasn't stellar either. Imagine being trapped in a world run by teenagers, where all values are topsy-turvy and everything is 'like, I don't know.' And you can't tell me that some guy trying to destroy a country because he loves his robot and really hates the other guy's robot makes a lick of sense to you. But, if it does make sense to you, then this movie is something you may enjoy.

history.title: Scooby-Doo & WWE:Curse of Speed Demon
history.text: Well, if you want to watch the Scooby gang sit and watch a car race, then don't miss this opportunity. Though Fred and I both slept through most of it. There were some weird problems with the movie for any Scooby Doo fan. The movie was not about the Scooby gang in the least. For some of the movie they 'go along for the ride' but that's really all. It's a movie about the guest stars, which I would think would have to interact a little more to have a better joint undertaking. There are also numerous wrestling characters involved, so introducing each and giving them something to do makes the story spread a little thin and come off as erratic. There's a lot of catch phrase usage, maybe the only Spanish word the wrestlers knew was "Ole," but there was not much story or much dialogue. If you went into this caring about both topics, then you'll be disappointed because the Scooby half is severely underrepresented. I don't know where Velma's voice actress went or if she plans to return, but I hoped that she was merely protesting the script with her absence. I think whatever contract they made with the wrestling franchise included a clause that stipulated the word "Superstar" in reference to the wrestlers be used a certain amount of times. No matter how many times someone insists that they are awesome I'd still make up my own mind, and it sounds like they protest too much. The wrestler who uses the "bell tolls" catch line must really be a fan of John Donne. Perhaps he truly understands how mankind is linked. My personal distaste for wrestling might not have been such an obstacle to enjoying the movie if it had been a better written story. I enjoyed the KISS Scooby movie despite not liking KISS. Basically this is a mash up of NASCAR and WWE wrestling - wrestlers racing cars and fighting as they do. Neither of these pursuits interest me much. There is an audience out there that is interested in these things. Not a problem, really, I could pass on this movie because I don't care about racing or wrestling, but here's why I think it's inappropriate. These entertainment forms are sort of the "everyman"'s entertainment. So it's unnerving that there is a repetitive and obnoxious theme about the wealth of the actual owners of the wrestling franchise. It seems like a slap in the face to have someone mention more than once that entertaining this particular audience and selling them merchandise and making them pay for events has rocketed the owner's fortune into the billions. This objection could have nothing to do with the movie, except for the fact that it is part of the movie. The dollar amount is mentioned more than once. Everyone has to spend their money somewhere, on WWE wrestling tickets, t-shirts, action figures, ... Scooby movies. Guess I regret contributing to this particular cause. It's a bit like musicians waving fists full of dollars around in music videos, they're really addressing their fans saying, "Thanks for buying my cd, do you like the new car I bought with your money?" But I digress. There is no wit, there is no humor, there is no Scooby in this movie. I hope the joint venture between WWE and Warner has come to an end and that Scooby will emerge older and wiser from this experience. You can be modern without pandering (What's New Scooby-Doo? comes to mind).

history.title: Scooby-Doo! and KISS Rock and Roll Mystery (DVD)

history.text: After seeing another new Scooby movie just prior, this was a breath of fresh air. This seemed clever, and warm, and funny - by comparison. Even on it's own it is an entertaining and coherent story. There are two types of Scooby mysteries: 1) There's no such thing as ghosts; 2) There are ghosts. The modern ones explore either option more than past versions did. I found the anime homages amusing. The strong Sailor Moon vibes had me giggling because it's big strong guys (albeit in high heels, spandex, and makeup). There may have been hints of Dragonball or X-Men cartoons too. As someone who is not a fan of KISS I could still enjoy the movie because it was a good story where the gang helped solve a mystery with their guest stars. I even recognized one of the songs! I can also appreciate the smidgens of science. The date of Halloween was only a plot device - like when your town permanently cancels Halloween because kids will want to dress up like rockstars and instead you just have a harvest festival where everyone is served squash drinks and no one has any fun ever again. Spoiler : How old is Daphne supposed to be? It detracted just a little that someone referred to as a kid in once scene ends up sharing her first on screen kiss with a rockstar instead of her boyfriend. Think that's why they named the movie Kiss? Science Spoiler: Carbonado may have origins in outer space.

history.title: 11th Hour (WS) (DVD)
history.text: Rather disappointing overall. No one watching this will be swayed if they don't happen to believe humans are capable of effecting climate change. Keep in mind that most who reject that idea do so from a religious doctrine that says we are utterly incapable of doing so. This might be good to educate or introduce students to a topic they had not considered in depth before. The intended audience may even be young teenagers. Just a few of the speakers offered insight that was informative or unique perspective. I understand that having all scientists from Stanford or Cambridge would make the discussion less accessible to the average or younger viewer, and it was supposed to appear as an everyman topic because it's an everyman problem (with or without an everyman solution). So in that aspect, though it made it less interesting or informative as far as I am concerned, it was nice to have random businesspeople and enviro-fans talk about loving the Earth. This was half stock-footage stark music video, half ominous finger wagging, and no one really likes to be scolded. One guy made the point that we're basically doing everything wrong. But don't despair viewers, that just means we have the opportunity to fix everything. Lucky us! Considering that humans are not apart from nature but a part of nature is something we should keep in mind. The way we deal with nature is a product of society (or culture as one guy said), because we deal with politics and consumerism. I'm sure we'd all love some Solar City roof shingles, since they're only going to cost what a normal roof costs, except if rumors are true, Musk's definition of normal roofs is 10x what a normal person's definition is ($10-15,000, not $100,000). Not that people need government subsidies, but as technology evolves it is adopted slowly as people learn about it or save money to afford it. Price decreases with demand and then supply increase and therefore improved means of production drive the price down so it becomes more accessible to a greater number of consumers. It's a little discomfiting to be lectured about my consumerism in a movie by one of the wealthiest people I've heard of, but I'll get over it. The psychologist was getting a little philosophical when he stated that humans are unfulfilled and that's why they shop. While he may be right, that is the basis for some religions, and ironically, the idea that religion as a goal itself has been surpassed by non-religion which may lead to the lack of fulfillment which drives some of that consumerism. I'd also suggest that spending is both power and expression, while we remain beasts of burden we have few ways to explore other aspects of our personalities, and with the removal of any significant binding moral or religious or scientific (or whatever) goal/theme, we have apathy and disillusionment. In some ways this video felt oddly un-scientific, so many speakers warned about the progress and acquisitive nature of humans, and how detrimental is has been to the environment, they seem to ignore the fact that those may also be the root of the solutions to our past mistakes, and that progress is not necessarily about a cessation of industrialization or a return to a certain perfect balance of human population to Earth creatures. Our desire for progress and growth won't allow us to head backward, no matter how many hippies say that's progress, but perhaps instead of hitting some upper limit of population which leads to some devastating event, such as human extinction, that growth will lead us over that boundary into, for instance, outer space? And the idea that humans, or human industrialization is (like) an infection on Earth? Well, there is a solution for that, but I don't think we'll get everyone to agree to it. Because we're looking at the snapshot in time, post-industrial society that is learning to be more self-sustaining, we look back at times of less prosperity and realize a generation ago people had so much less and re-used so much more, we can imagine a future (right, we're the only species that can imagine and plan for the future!) where we produce enough for everyone and without much waste. We can look at resources as an equation, nothing is really destroyed, even if it disappears to the dump instead of the recycling facility. If we remove carbon from trees or oil and put it into the atmosphere, doesn't that sound like it might effect how something else would work? Like keeps a little more heat in, so ice melts a little more, sea levels rise a little, storms become a little stronger and faster and more frequent, deserts become a little wider and dryer and hotter? It's sort of math-like, we're just shifting variables around. It's not climate change that we debate whether it is or is not happening, it's following where the variables go and realizing that must alter the equation. My rebuttals to individual speakers: Consumerism drives technology, which drives advancements in the quality and efficiency of technology from consumer pressure with consumer financial backing, which of course leads to the solutions that people are begging for. Frugality is not a goal you can place on an ever-growing human population, especially when that world has extremely varied levels of prosperity. Arguing for nature to be given legal rights is probably the type of ideological creativity that off-puts a lot of people from caring about environmental policy. While the idea is not repugnant, it certainly is probably not taken seriously by the average person at present. Perhaps we should be more concerned with the undue influence certain people with more self-interest than environmental interest have over environmental policy than whether or not nature gets to vote about its own future. The best advice from this movie, paraphrased from one expert: "People ask me what they can do. I answer, want to do something?... Get involved." That's not even a bunch of nothing, it's a very minuscule amount of nothing. Don't be so abstruse. Give practical everyday advice for the average person listening to you that they can achieve with their income, lifestyle, and amount of time available or when asked that question respond that you do not have any advice for them at this time.

history.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Chronicles of Narnia - Voyage of the Dawn Treader - The worst packaging ever!!
history.text: What is the primary and most important aspect of blu-ray disc packaging? To protect the disc(s) from damage while stored or when being removed from the packaging or returned to the packaging. Well, apparently Fox doesn't believe in that. This is the most pathetic packaging imaginable for a single title 3 disc set. It is cheap cardboard - and when Amazon ships it to you in an envelope, be prepared to find the top portion of the product to have been crushed. Then you can open it up to find 2 of the discs stored in flip out sleeves, so you can grab them with your grubby oily fingers to drag them out for playing. The 3rd disc is twisted onto a little rubber nubby glued onto a cardboard flap in the center. We've seen these before - they are pure junk! Can you avoid putting marks on the discs? Well, do not worry about it - because they already have marks on them from the Fox worker bees who put the discs into this awful packaging in the first place. Please don't tell me this approach to packaging was so Fox could include that pack of "collector postcards" in the package - the ones I just flipped into the recycle bin. Fox should fire the idiots who dreamed this debacle up.

history.title: Murder 2 Blu Ray (2011) (Hindi Film / Bollywood Movie / Indian Cinema)
history.text: This film has a very strong and intense climax. That said, be aware that "Bollywood" films are not like typical western films. Dramatic content is interrupted by song and dance numbers, which can be unsettling if you are unfamiliar with the genre. "Murder 2" has a pretty good storyline although it is uneven in several instances. The male lead seems too young for the role, although I am unfamiliar with Hindu actors and he may have been cast for his popularity. On the other hand, the leading lady is gorgeous, sexy, and vulnerable. The villain, also, is perfectly evil. These three actors do a very good job of driving the plot to its inevitable conclusion. As a final comment I would say that the cover art is misleading. Although there are a number of scenes suggesting nudity there is none. That shouldn't take away from your enjoyment of the film, but it should not be your reason to purchase the Blu-Ray.
