history.text: Good movie but brutal. It's not the kind of movie I want to watch again or own. It has the most satisfying scenes of martial arts that I've seen. Some scenes were too disgusting and brutal for me to watch.

history.title: Vice [DVD + Digital]
history.text: My friend picked out this movie to watch. This is pure fiction and pure filth. It's a story about evolving artificial intelligence who were given a sensitive heart, and it's about an immoral human being who got rich from letting other rich immoral people commit all kinds of crimes and abuse against them and get away with it. I'm exceedingly grateful I didn't spend a cent on this video. If I had, I would have used a sledge hammer on it and thrown it in the trash. Many scenes were highly offensive and I got up and left the room many times. There were scenes involving lesbians, a guy raping a woman and beating her up, and a lot of shooting, killing, bad language and using God's name in vain. I never understood the urge people feel to use his name in vain when some of them don't even believe in him. Why not use Buddha as a cuss-word or Muhammad? The actor on the right of the cover, played a hero police detective. And there were a few other decent people in the story. I became interested in the last thirty or forty minutes. The plot got interesting for me, when a mistreated female android, escaped the laboratory from a sadistic scientist. The chase scenes were too long and I lost my interest again.

history.title: Hwarang : The Poet Warrior Youth (K-Drama w. English Sub)
history.text: I love how this story plays out in the first five and last episodes. Although, it kept my interest throughout the entire drama. It was fun watching the confident skilled fighter who was carefree, funny, a little oblivious, yet protective and clever. And he was also nice to look at. This part was played by Park Seo Joon. He looked so different, that I thought this was a new face I hadn't seen before. As the story progressed, he lost his magnetic carefree manner. Though the PSJ character didn't stop being attractive, in the early scenes of the story, there was a suspenseful energy (like how you feel watching a leopard getting ready to attack) that got lost as more things happened to him. That was too bad because he was more appealing that way. Actress Go ah ra's role was lovable and funny too. Her expressions and manner were delightful. She was forthright, and was no respecter of persons, unless they were her dad, the king and queen. It was so funny how she sometimes spoke to the lords and those in authority. Her skills were medical and storytelling. And it was appealing to watch both sides in action. I missed watching her amusing energy while telling a story. PSJ's character was amusing in how he didn't always do what was expected. And she was like that, too. Her manner was appealing, sometimes even when she was crying. I'm glad I hung onto the end. While my mood was being affected by the story, I was asking myself why I was watching another period piece and ready to give up on it until I realized I was on the 19th episode. But the last episode had such a satisfying ending. All the actors were believable and sometimes funny, especially the lead trainer. The twists in the story were interesting. There were many good looking men in the drama. The queen was the prettiest female. Overall though, the men were better looking than the women. It was an entertaining twenty episodes and the time went by fast. I would love to own this video and watch it whenever I wanted, as I've already watched the drama three times.

history.title: Heroines Of F.U.R.Y.
history.text: The Super Sexy Heroines of Metro City join forces to protect their city. Although these girls are so hot the crime rate will probably go up just from guys wanting to see them in their alluring costumes. Beautiful actresses, competent special effects & a real plot line make this title easy to recommend. I swear 60 seconds can't pass in this film without an opportunity to gaze at one of these appealing heroines. All of the women due a fine job acting. They all handle their roles with real poise & look incredible while doing it. Especially Cosmic Girl played by Ashley Lane, able to be both sweet & strong effortlessly. I hope to see her in future projects. The brunette Supergirl (Mercedes Raquel)...I just hope to see anywhere. Quite a few of these Superheroine themed movies have come out from Brookland Brothers these past couple of years. As far as I am concerned "Agents of Power" can be retconned right out of continuity while this new title "Heroines of Fury" is the crowning achievement. I hope future releases follow this style of tone. If you watched The Avengers & thought - Wow the only way this could be better is if it had gorgeous women in revealing costumes - Your wish has been granted. Definite purchase.

history.text: This movie is the equivalent of going to someone's house & watching them play Call of Duty. Then that person playing completely sucking at it. For a movie shot entirely in 1st person, it is incredibly boring. There are couple of scenes in this movie where the gore is absolutely disgusting. No plot by choice. That was a bad choice. Acting was completely ridiculous. Worst Movie I have seen this year! One of the worst movies I have ever seen!

history.title: Heartbreakers [Blu-ray]
history.text: This oft forgotten comedy is a classic. Showcasing some great work by great actors. Jennifer Love Hewitt & Sigourney Weaver play a mother - daughter con artist team. Bilking rich marks using their god given gifts. E.G. - Sigourney's intelligence & Jennifer's amazing chest! This is a great comedy film with an interesting plot. Ray Liotta, Gene Hackman & Jason Lee round out the cast. Let me tell you, every one of them brought there A game! As great as they are, Jennifer Love Hewitt is phenomenal! This is Jennifer's best role! She has great comedic skills & when the script calls for more serious acting she nails that too. Ghost Whisperer was pretty successful in it's tv run but this is the role Jennifer truly excelled at. She looks incredible in all of her scenes! The wardrobe dept. definitely accentuated her beauty pageant queen looks & best assets. E.G. - As a said before her amazing chest! If you are a fan of JLH this has to be in your movie collection. If you enjoy great comedies or grifter style - heist movies then you should own this. Just like it's two leading ladies, this film is timeless. Great in any day, year or decade.

history.title: Arrow: The Complete Fifth Season [Blu-ray]
history.text: I have been a huge fan of this show since it began. After a couple of weak seasons. Arrow is back on top of the superhero tv shows. IMO this is the greatest season of Arrow! Even surpasses the amazing season 2. The season is filled with intrigue, excitement & great characters. The show that started the superhero craze on tv. Has now raised the bar for everyone else in the genre. Amell gets a lot of flack for his acting online. After this season, no one can question his acting prowess. The final episodes hinged a lot on his portrayal. He completely knocked it out of the park! Can't wait for this release! Highly Recommended!

history.review_title: Blue Eyed Bullet From The West!
history.text: Amy Johnston goes from stunt double to lead actress with a deft performance in this movie. Exciting fight choreography, attractive performers & a plot that goes in some unexpected directions make this film easy to recommend. Besides english not being the native tongue of many of the performers, the acting is commendable. Definitely inspired by Bloodsport. Honestly may be just as good of a film.

Critics online have been way too harsh on this one. Just as funny & viable as other films of this genre currently at the theatres. Doesn't cast the female leads in the best light. Although girls can be frenemies. Their competition was played for laughs. Not a social commentary. The work is the work. Alexandra Daddario came to turn in her best possible performance with what was given to her. I thought she had some truly funny scenes. Willing to bet, her performance elevated what was written in the script for her. Kate Upton doesn't seem to be acting as much as playing a heightened version of herself. Whatever, she also had some very funny scenes & one liners. Not great by any means. Good comedic elements & two attractive leads (very attractive in Daddario's case) make this recommendable. history.text: This is one of those movies that you'll see the cover, you'll see the title, you'll read the premise, and shake your head. Most of the time, the combo would be correct. You'd be wrong in this case. This movie is gold! Funny, gory, and well acted, it is a nice fun, rainy night movie. I totally recommend it.

history.title: Doctor Who: The Complete Fourth Series
history.review_title: The NOT so Complete Fourth Series
history.text: I loved the 4th series, don't get me wrong. It's great! It's marvelous. I adore Donna. So why the 3 stars, you ask? Because, IT'S NOT THE COMPLETE SERIES! If you went from this to Season 5, you'd have no idea why David Tennant is now Matt Smith. Why? Because BBC decided to have 4 episodes be "The Specials" and not include them. So you're forced to shell out more money to fill in the gap between Season 4 and Season 5. This is wrong, as far as I'm concerned, so it won't get a good rating (nor will I hold BBC in high esteem). But, it is a great season. =)

history.title: Doctor Who: Season 8
history.review_title: Dear Rachel Talalay, Dr. Who is NOT Nightmare on Elm Street!
history.text: I was surprised I would ever rate Doctor Who so low. So let me clarify why I am now. Peter Capaldi does a great job. He IS a great combination of the first and third Doctor with his own fun added in. Clara is fine, though she does get a little stale. And the series starts quite well. Magical actually. I really liked it. Then the third episode began. As it goes on, it gets darker and darker, both in the mood, the script, AND how it's filmed. (BBC, if you didn't have the budget for it, then spread the damn thing out until you DO!) I laughed at first when I saw it was directed by Rachel Talalay. I thought, "Wow, she did some of the "A Nightmare on Elm Street" sequels. This should be good!" I was wrong. It had the same dark, dreary, "bummer ending" feel of the "Freddy's Nightmares" TV show in the early nineties. When it reached the end, I was actually sick. This is not Doctor Who. Had I known what I was in store for by the time I reached the end, I would never had purchased season 9 (but I did). Mr. Pink, you deserved better. If you liked Season 7, end it there. You won't just cry with this. You'll be angry. It's just... terrible.

This is a dark comedy. Now, not sure if the producers had that in mind or not but that's what it is. At moments, it's laugh out loud funny, at moments it's cringe worthy. It doesn't get a 5 star from me simply because there are some parts that simply don't need to be there (funny as his cameo was, why do we need a "trailer" for "Fish Hunter"? It wasn't fun or funny.) or are things we've seen before (*ahem* Hollywood, please notice what was said, I down scored you for REPEATING yourself. Break New Ground). But worth a watch, you'll get a giggle out of it. But it's not a horror movie so don't expect many scares.

history.title: Under the Sun
history.text: It was as well done as could be expected. The filmmaker lived in a communist country in childhood. He was expecting to see same thing. He didn't find the same thing at all. I was concerned before watching I would see an image that would give nightmares, there are no worries.

history.title: Change of Habit [DVD]

history.title: Daredevils of the Red Circle (1939) (12 Chapter Serial) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Calling all cliffhanger serial fans -- BUY THIS NOW!
history.text: I was really looking forward to this blu-ray, as Daredevils of the Red Circle is one of my favorite serials. In my book, Daredevils runs neck and neck with Flash Gordon for all-time best cliffhanger serial. Daredevils has so much going for it. It was directed by my favorite serial directing team (William Witney and John English) and produced by my favorite serial studio (Republic). And it has the incomparable Charles "Ming the Merciless" Middleton as the villain. William Lava delivers and stirring and atmospheric musical score. Not only does Daredevils have great opening and closing chapters, the excitement hardly lets up all the way through. An all-time classic! Now that we've gotten my biases out of the way, let me say that the blu-ray offers an excellent presentation of Daredevils of the Red Circle. A great upgrade that represents an improvement in every way over my old Republic VHS copy (which I had converted to DVD for my personal video library and to avoid wear and tear on the tape -- did I mention this was one of my favorite serials?) The cleaned-up audio and video of the blu-ray release make this the best looking edition of Daredevils that I have ever seen. While not perfect, and therefore perfectionists may have some gripes that I am willing to overlook, I think the quality of the blu-ray gives us an edition of Daredevils that we can proudly show off to generations to come. If you are a fan of cliffhangers . . . Republic serials . . . William Witney and John English . . . or are just "serial-curious", add this to your cart and buy it RIGHT NOW -- you won't regret it! The only disappointment I have about this release, and it is a very small one, is with regards to the blu-ray chapter stops which only take you to the very start of each chapter of the serial. While serial chapters may be a bit short to deserve multiple chapter stops, that still would have been appreciated, perhaps to jump to the next action sequence. But what should be mandatory in a modern serial release is a blu-ray chapter stop immediately after the opening credits of each serial chapter. That way you can have the option to jump directly to the title card for the episode and not have to play (or fast forward through) the opening music for every chapter. Other than that very minor issue, which doesn't merit taking even a sliver of a star off my rating for this one, I am very pleased with the treatment that Kino Lorber gave Daredevils. A fine presentation as was owed to this classic Republic cliffhanger.

history.title: Danger Close [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Close, but no Citizen Solder (or Hornet's Nest)
history.text: Important Public Service Message, as an update to my original review: Before you waste *any* time on this film, including reading my review, GO DIRECTLY TO [[ASIN:B06Y4QZCV8 Legion of Brothers]] and buy that movie instead -- it is a great, high quality, authentic documentary that properly focuses on the heroes and their families, and REALLY takes you "inside special ops", unlike this lackluster product. If you want more details about the reason for the above recommendation, then please read on... but really, you should JUST SKIP THIS REVIEW AND THIS MOVIE and get Legion of Brothers instead! ----- First off, let me express my utmost respect towards U.S. Army Special Forces Staff Sgt. Pirelli and his family for service and sacrifice. I am puzzled by the lack of any mention of Pirelli in the Amazon description for this disc. Currently there is only a brief "editorial review" filling in as a description here. That one-sentence blurb just mentions Alex Quade, the journalist who shot much of the footage that makes up the film. The oversight of having no mention of how SSG Pirelli and his family feature in Danger Close reflects a general issue that some may have with the film -- the emphasis is skewed too far to the wrong side of the camera. Despite the sparse description, I pre-ordered this disc based on the strength of The Hornet's Nest and Citizen Soldier, the previous two films from this directing team. Unfortunately, Danger Close is not as good as either of those films. For those who thought there was too much focus on the journalists in The Hornet's Nest, Danger Close will definitely rub you the wrong way. I felt that The Hornet's Nest did a good job of balancing the story of the journalists with compelling raw footage that offered an on-the-ground soldier's perspective of Afghanistan. Danger Close, on the other hand, offers the viewer little to no background or perspective on the underlying subject matter. Far too often, Danger Close centers around how various incidents impacted journalist Quade. Early into the film she is shown being questioned in a static, sit-down studio interview. While I was hoping that the studio interview was just an opening set piece, perhaps to bridge the transition of the story from Afghanistan to Iraq, the static interview of Quade turned out to be a recurring part of the film. Further, given the film's lack of adequate background or perspective on the various military actors and actions it depicts, the documentary often presents like a mere piece of war tourism. This is not a deep documentary or one that will provide you with any meaningful insight into the conflicts in Iraq or Afghanistan. The units that Quade hop-scotches through get short shrift -- their missions and risks serving as mere scenery and footnotes for Quade's attempt to return to the base SSG Pirelli helped construct. Oddly enough, the special feature segments included on the disc are more informative and more in depth. A collection featuring more of Quade's short subjects may have made for a better disc. Indeed, someone who doesn't have a decent grounding in the subject matter might benefit from watching the special features first. And, to be fair, the film does go into more background with regards to SSG Pirelli -- which is why you would figure he might be mentioned someplace in the Amazon description... (ok, I've more than made my point on that issue). The Hornet's Nest was interesting in that it presented another perspective on the events portrayed in Restrepo and Korengal. Citizen Soldier gave a gripping and moving overview of the sacrifices faced by National Guard troops deploying to Afghanistan. Now comes Danger Close, which purports to take us "inside special ops", per the blurb on the cover. More accurately, Danger Close really just presents us with the perspective of a journalist working beside special ops. The term Danger Close refers to directing artillery fire or air support at a point that is in extremely close proximity to friendly forces. Hopefully this AAR of my experience with the film will help you decide whether it would be a danger close mission for you to drop this movie into your blu-ray player...

history.title: On Wings of Eagles
history.review_title: This one soars on wings of 80's made-for-TV, based-on-a-true-story drama!
history.text: "On Wings of Eagles" presents an inspiring story of courage and determination. I was glad to have found it, and it was definitely a better investment of my leisure time than spending three hours watching the latest set of Hollywood sequels or remakes! Although On Wings of Eagles has some of the typical deficiencies that one would expect from a TV movie of its time, overall I thought it was entertaining. It is worth tracking down if you are interested in military or special ops films drawn from true stories. I'd also recommend it to Burt Lancaster fans solely on the basis of his entertaining portrayal of Colonel "Bull" Simons! Also of potential interest is Richard Crenna's portrayal of Ross Perot, which incorporates some Perot speech patterns and mannerisms that probably would not have been common knowledge at the time the film came out. These should now be recognizable to anyone who was around for Perot's presidential run, and this gives some insight into the preparation that Crenna put into the role. All that being said, this is not a slam-bang film of constant action. It is a recounting of (mostly?) true events, and by remaining relatively faithful to how things played out it sometimes moves a little slow to fill out the running time. However, the filmmakers and actors bring a lot of sincerity to the production and the stories of the various characters will hold your interest all the way through. The character of Rashid, in particular, struck a chord for me by reminding me of people I worked with overseas. After watching the film I read the Ken Follet book for the first time. That caused me to appreciate the movie even more, as some of the incidents I had figured were simply manufactured by the screenwriter to jazz up the movie were actually adapted straight from the book. On the other hand, the movie also adds the obligatory Hollywood "based on a true story" (i.e. didn't happen) action and suspense sequences. That's too bad, because if they had stuck to the story as related in the book, I think they still would have had a great movie. If you are completely new to the On Wings of Eagles story, I'd say watch the movie first and then read the book. If you've already read the book, I think you'll still enjoy the movie if you keep in mind that it has some unnecessary additional drama added. (But hey, we experienced that with Lone Survivor as well, with its dramatic battle tacked on to the climactic rescue sequence!) One other notable fact to pass along. Most readers of this review will probably be aware of Bull Simons' connection to the Son Tay raid (an attempt to rescue America POW's during the Vietnam War). However, I was not aware that he also participated in the World War II Cabanatuan raid (depicted in the excellent 2005 film, The Great Raid) that liberated allied prisoners from a Japanese POW camp in the Philippines. Simons' involvement in those significant rescue missions, in addition to his status as a legend in the special operations community, only added to my interest in finding out about how he utilized a team of computer executives to orchestrate the rescue of their colleagues from an Iranian jail.

history.title: Airplane 2-Movie Collection
history.review_title: "Shirley" a seriously good deal - unless you picked the wrong week to stop ordering blu-rays!
history.text: Why so few reviews? Because we haven't stopped laughing yet! The original Airplane is still my favorite of the pair. This was the first big hit from the Zucker (x2) and Abrahams team that would continue to tickle our funny-bones into the nineties with genre homages like Top Secret, The Naked Gun, and Hot Shots. I think Hot Shots was where they finally managed to top the home run hit they scored with Airplane, but I enjoyed their other parodies too. Airplane is a send up of the classic airline disaster movies (such as The High and the Mighty and the Airport series). Along the way, other Hollywood classics and genres get the treatment as well (such as Saturday Night Fever). Airplane II then takes the airline disaster genre into "the future," with a space shuttle being the featured craft in jeopardy. Airplane is a mixture of movie buff in-jokes, razor sharp wit, goofy puns, and sight gags. What takes things over the top is the stellar cast that is involved in the shenanigans, including golden age Hollywood stars Lloyd Bridges and Leslie Nielsen who would go on to become gut-busting Zucker-Abrahams regulars. Also on board for Airplane are Robert Stack, Peter Graves, and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Barbara Billingsley, of "Leave It To Beaver" fame, has a hilarious and unexpected cameo, and somehow California tax activist Howard Jarvis even makes it into the mix! Airplane II has similarly inspired casting, with Bridges and Graves returning, joined by Chuck Connors, Sony Bono, Raymond Burr, and John Vernon. Plus there's William Shatner who shows up as the perfect candidate to play the commander of a lunar base. The star-studded casts of both movies reflect how disaster movies of the seventies used a cavalcade of stars as a selling point. This is a welcome, bargain priced set for fans and newcomers alike. Here you get two hilarious movies on blu-ray for under ten bucks -- who can gripe about that? Perhaps only someone who hasn't gotten over Macho Grande...

history.title: Legion of Brothers
history.review_title: Not perfect, but still incomparably great -- a moving and gripping SF documentary YOU MUST SEE!
history.text: I love these guys. Having only read about their amazing accomplishments, it was a privilege to see and hear directly from the Green Beret professionals who helped carry out one of the greatest special operations campaigns in history. If you read and enjoyed any of the books on the early campaign in Afghanistan (such as [[ASIN:1416580522 Horse Soldiers]], [[ASIN:0061661236 The Only Thing Worth Dying For]], or [[ASIN:0891418725 First In]]), then you will definitely want to see Legion of Brothers. Even if you haven't read any of these books, there's still just enough background information sprinkled into the documentary for the complete newcomer. (And then you should read the above books to find out more about these men and their accomplishments.) The only thing wrong with this film is that it should have been three or four times as long. I would have liked to see more of this important SF oral history documented in the style used by the filmmakers. Even so, despite its brisk 78 minute running time, Legion of Brothers accomplishes a lot. It humanizes these Green Beret heroes, highlights personal and family sacrifices, and touches on some significant events from the campaign that immediately followed 9/11. One of the all-around best documentaries I have seen on the war in Afghanistan, period. DON'T MISS IT!

history.title: 3-Film Action Collection [Blu-ray] with 3 Bonus DVD Features
history.review_title: 4-Star Action buoyed by an affordable Bravo Two Zero blu-ray -- but beware the poor quality DVD of Jackie Chan movies!
history.text: My rating is primarily for the overall value of the three movies on the BD (and overlooks the limited audio options and lack of extras, as this is a budget pack, after all). If I were rating the quality of the presentation of the movies included on the "bonus" DVD, this release would get no stars! First off, note that this is an unusual package in that three of the movies (Bravo Two Zero, Driven to Kill, and Super Cop) are on a blu-ray while the others are on a DVD. As noted in the tiny note in the bottom left corner of the cover, the "Bonus 3 DVD Movies" are Project A, Project A 2, and Dragon Lord. I had overlooked this fact when I ordered the combo pack, thinking that all of the movies were Blu-ray. The Blu-ray is a no frills disc, just the three films, no extras, and with English 2.0 stereo as the only audio option. The video quality on all three movies looks good to me. The main reason I got this combo pack was for the SAS Gulf War survival story Bravo Two Zero. The movie does a good job of presenting Andy McNab's book (which has taken some knocks for alleged embellishment over the years). This is a movie that deserves a decent solo Blu-ray release with extra features, like interviews with the SAS veterans who were a part of the mission. One exception to the decent quality of the video is that the televised Gulf War stock-footage looks really bad and pixelated. Fortunately these sequences are fairly brief and not central to the movie. Super Cop is presented in 2:35.1 widescreen, which is good news (compared to the previous 1.78 cropped blu), but it is the 91 minute US cut with only a dubbed English soundtrack. Still, I really like this movie, particularly Michelle Yeoh's impressive and engaging performance. This is another movie that deserves a decent solo Blu-ray release, with appropriate extras! Finally there is Driven to Kill, a 2009 direct-to-video Steven Seagal flick that makes me wonder what happened to this guy after his series of crackling eighties action classics such as Above the Law, Out for Justice, and Under Siege. Still, this is better than a lot of his direct-to-video efforts (although I know that isn't saying much), and oddly enough it is the headliner on the package. The other two movies are the real value here. Now for the DVD. It can pretty much be taken out of the box and tossed in the trash. Really! If you found this DVD sitting loose someplace and put it into a player to watch it, you would think it was a bootleg copy that came from an Afghan bazaar! The menu is even "less frills" than the Blu-ray, having just the three names of the movies in plain text. There are compression artifacts evident in all three movies, with Dragon Lord being the only one of the three that is viewable on a large screen in my opinion (but still not great). As noted, I missed the fact that these three movies were combined on one DVD when I ordered this. So while the poor quality was a surprise, it didn't really diminish from the overall value of the package, if you can find this set at the right price. Just be warned -- if you are thinking about ordering this for any of the movies on the DVD, don't bother! You will almost certainly be disappointed by the poor video quality on that disc in this two-disc set.

history.title: 6 Days
history.review_title: A surprisingly good treatment of the 1980 Iranian embassy siege - SAS aficionados take note!
history.text: I decided to give Six Days a try despite the lukewarm reviews for the theatrical release. It is definitely a lot better than the reviews indicated! Six Days strikes me as a bit of an old school presentation -- offering an interesting, well-paced story with comprehensible and realistic action sequences. I found the action sequences particularly refreshing compared to the standard quick-cut, blurred, frenetic action style that seems to be virtually mandatory these days. If this had been a big budget Hollywood release, undoubtedly the assault on the embassy would have been presented like a first-person-shooter video game. Kudos to the creators of Six Days for not falling victim to that overused trend! The movie is a dramatized account of the 1980 hostage siege at the Iranian embassy in London. I was interested in the Special Air Service (SAS) aspect of the movie, having read extensively on this particular operation for years now. Rather than solely focusing on the SAS, the movie centers on four characters: a police hostage negotiator, a BBC reporter, one of the hostages (Police Constable Trevor Lock), and Rusty Firmin, a lance corporal in the SAS who participated in the assault to rescue the hostages. While not a definitive film treatment of the SAS involvement, I thought the movie did an overall good job with the story of the incident, and did an excellent job of presenting the SAS assault. I'd recommend the movie on the strength of those sequences alone, especially because it is nice to see them presented in a comprehensible way. The film also manages to effectively intercut vintage footage to add to a documentary-style feel. Give this one a look!

history.title: Right Stuff (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The Wrong Stuff - inaccurate description - *NO* special features on single disc blu-ray edition!
history.text: The one-star rating is for the new, "not as advertised" blu-ray. The Right Stuff is a great movie (four to five stars for that) which is currently advertised here as a single disc blu-ray set containing the following features: "Additional Scenes Biographical Profile John Glenn: American Hero The Journey and the Mission: Scene-Specific Commentaries with Director/Screenwriter Philip Kaufman, Cast and Crew Members 3 Featurettes Featuring Cast, Crew and/or the Real-LifeHeroes Portrayed in the Movie: Realizing the Right Stuff, T-20 Years and Counting and The Real Men with the Right Stuff Theatrical Trailer" One BIG problem - this new blu-ray release ONLY contains the movie and not one of the above advertised special features. So count me as also feeling duped, along with the other recent reviewers who have posted the same complaint about this significant error.

history.review_title: Glass 1/2 empty, 1/2 full...or as I like to call it, Wax On, Wax Off
history.text: I'm just going to bullet-point the highs and lows of this one. For some of you, it's better than you think. For others, it's worse than you imagined. WAX ON (the "half full" review): 1). Hillary Swank is attractive and engaging as Julie, the tomboy with anger management issues. 2). Pat Morita. I'm sure he knew this was less than a 5 star flick when he signed up for it, but he deserved one final Miyagi-sized payday. No harm, no foul on his part. 3). I gave this one 5 stars for having the courage to break from the formula. WAX OFF (the "half empty" review): 1). The ice melts a little too quickly on Hillary Swank's character for it to b believable, especially in the romance department. 2). Michael Ironside. Neil Young made the one-note solo entertaining in "Cinnamon Girl." Ironside is basically playing the same role here as the one he played in "Total Recall" and probably every other movie he's been in. He just chews the scenery and isn't the least believable or entertaining while doing so. 3). The fight scenes. Thoroughly inept, stunt doubles punching and kicking empty air. Just awful. FULL DISCLOSURE: This has been showing recently on the Ion Network. I was too lazy to change the channel and welcomed the opportunity to satisfy my curiosity by watching it for free. I recommend you do the same. 2 stars, and I am being overly generous.

history.title: Live In Tokyo [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Same Jeff, but from a different angle
history.text: Given the fact that "Performing This Week ... Live at Ronnie Scott's" was such a high-profile and universally acclaimed live set (and justifiably so), it's almost impossible to view "Live In Tokyo" without drawing some comparisons. That doesn't mean you have to decide that that "Ronnie" is a "better" show, or vice-versa. It's still Jeff Beck, he's still at a peak in terms of prowess, it's still a nice career-spanning overview of his work. What's different is the band, for starters, as well as the venue. There was a certain level of warmth, from Jeff''s own stage presence to the interplay between the band members, to the obvious small club ambiance on "Ronnie" that you aren't going to find here. And that's OK...that show was a chapter, not the whole story. At the beginning of this show, Beck...wearing shades...struts out onto the stage, shredding as he goes. That's in stark contrast to the no-shades, smiling, greeting the audience Beck who opened the "Ronnie" show. We go from a small club to a mega-hall, and yes...let's get this out of the way up front...Tal Wilkenfeld created a magic in the "Ronnie" band that is replaced by the technically proficient but perhaps less charming Rhonda Smith. He's also got a second guitarist (Nicolas Meier) which is not the norm. Finally, "Cause We've Ended As Lovers" in "Ronnie" was a more soft-spoken performance, primarily offered as a bookend for Tal's fluid bass solo. Here, it's closer to the "Blow By Blow" original. When it comes to choosing material, Jeff's tastes can be hit or miss, buy boy, did he HIT when he decided to cover the Mahavishnu Orchestra's "You Know You Know." It's just killer, with its slightly menacing pacing...perfect for Beck. Jimi's "Little Wing" is a little tougher than Clapton;s version, but it also has a softer side. Because he was touring behind "Emotion & Commotion," you get some of his newer material, but he also serves up the creme de la creme like "The Pump" and "Blue Wind." The only thing that could possibly get in the way of your enjoying the daylights out of this is that if you insist on comparing it, unfavorably, to the "Ronnnie" DVD. Don't do that. It's too good to mess up with comparisons.

history.title: Machete Kills
history.text: This movie is everything it intended to be, and more. You can't judge a film like "Machete Kills" or a director like Robert Rodriguez using "current box office standards." first, Rodriguez...like his "sometimes partner in film" Tarantino...does what he wants to do, follows his own vision. Both directors obviously have influences up the wazoo..."Machete Kills," like Tarantino's "Death Proof," is more about cheesy retro exploitation cinema of the 70s or 80s than it is ANYTHING going on in 2015. But these influences are utilized at will, when they serve the greater purpose of the director. It would be the same as a musician in 2015 writing a song and saying "let's put a solo in right here like Jeff Beck would have done with the Yardbirds." It doesn't mean the song has now become a "tribute" to either Beck or the Yardbirds. It simply means the artist found that specific influence to be "useful" in the moment. What can you say about a film that features Charlie Sheen (under his real name, Carlos Estevez), as the PRESIDENT, with him playing the role in a way that gleefully exploits every square inch of the tabloid fodder he himself generated? Or crazed madman Mel Gibson in a role that followed his own media inferno that presented him as...well, a crazed madman? The scorecard: Danny Trejo is everything you would want or need him to be in this role, he just nails it. Amber Heard as "Miss San Antonio" is pure evil honey, a joy to behold. Michelle Rodriguez as "Luz" is a lot of fun, and she delivers some of the best lines in the script. Sofia Vergara as "Desdemona: is playing her role in a deliberately over-the-top manner, which...for my tastes...veers close to "annoying" at points. The "La Camaleón" role is a master stroke, jointly played by Walton Goggins, Antonio Banderas (amazingly playing the opposite of his "image"), Cuba Gooding Jr, and Lady Gaga. Cuba Gooding Jr.'s take on the role is especially tasty as he is often cast as the "voice of conscience" or the "stable" member of an ensemble cast, and here he is just cold and unrepentant evil. Tom Savini is always good for a laugh when he appears in these films. Put that together with Danny, Mel and Charlie, and you have a five-star stab at reliving the past while inventing the future.

history.title: Django Unchained
history.review_title: Suspension of disbelief equals greater entertainment value
history.text: A movie that examines the human condition through the bloody lens of over-the-top Tarantino bloodbaths like "Kill Bill," you might find yourself saying "that would never happen" more than once during this film. I make it my policy to not give up spoilers, so you'll just have to find those spots in the movie yourself. I'd say that "most mesmerizing performance" honors are a toss-up between Christoph Waltz as "Dr. King Schultz" and Leonardo DiCaprio as Plantation / Slave owner "Calvin Candie." DiCaprio seems to have really absorbed the essence of Jack Nicholson's 2006 performance as "Frank Costello" in the 2006 Martin Scorsese film "The Departed," in which DiCaprio also starred. Like Costello, Candie's evil is a sport...he relishes it, he rolls around in it and cannot be separated from its fulfillment. It's probably not a stretch to call at least a few of DiCaprio's character's outbursts "Nicholsonian." And the casting genius of the role is that they didn't offer it to Nicholson, or any actor like him...they handed it to Leo and let him take it over the top. It's a L-O-N-G movie...not sure if I agree with some of the "boring" assessments...and like pretty much every other Tarantino, it places equal weight on the moral ambiguities experienced by the good guys AND the bad guys. The "good" guys are never totally good, while the "bad" guys are never totally "bad." How can I say that? Well, Samuel L. Jackson plays something of a "Renfield" role to DiCaprio's bloodsucker. Jackson's a bad guy, no doubt about it, but his character is an African American who enjoys slipping into a big plush chair in DiCaprio's study and savoring a brandy while he tells his "master" that he's kidding himself. DiCaprio indulges Jackson because he knows Jackson is a sneak, a toad, an informant, the one guy on the entire plantation who knows that rewards come with watching his "master's" back. None of the relationships or character studies are simple or one-dimensional, neither are they completely believable, which is where "entertainment" comes in. Worth a purchase? I'd start with a rental first, because if you are a fan of Tarantino's films, and anything I wrote here captured your interest or curiosity, you will probably like it...you just may not watch it over and over again.

history.title: Rage
history.text: If it hadn't been for the "plot twist," I might have given this one three stars. Even with the plot twist, the first 2/3 of the movie or so is a three star movie. Without resorting to spoilers, here's why I gave it one star. 1). Danny Glover pretty much plays Sgt. Murtaugh in this one, but his performance lacks any gusto. He doesn't actually say his trademark line "I'm getting too old for this ****," but the tone of his entire performance is "I'm getting too old for this ****." He shadows Cage's character for the entire film, playing out that worn and tired plot of warning Cage that if he doesn't stop what he's doing right now, the consequences are going to be dire. Do the math, people. This isn't a Disney film. Take a wild guess at how things turn out, with or without Glover's stern warnings. 2). The first two thirds of the movie set themselves up and play out like a "good" Steven Seagal flick. I say "good" because I am sure that some of you aren't Seagal fans, and yeah...he's made more than his share of direct-to-DVD stinkers. Once again I won't spoil the film by revealing too much of the story but suffice it to say that if you have ever seen a "good" Seagal film, you will think you are watching one, UNTIL... 3). The PLOT TWIST. Ham-fisted, amateurish, a real "face palm" moment. The film telegraphs its punches early...YOU KNOW there is going to BE a plot twist...but when it comes, you almost want to stop the movie. But because you've watched 2/3 of it, you won't. 4). The exciting, dramatic, "didn't see that coming" climax. Of course, I'm being sarcastic. The ending spirals out of the plot twist, and it's pure garbage. It's what a screenwriter comes up with after he thinks he's crafted a clever plot twist but has then run out of ideas. ONE star, and I am being generous. If you want / need to see a Cage film that delivers, watch "Con Air," "The Rock," or for a double dose of fun, hammy overacting, catch the double threat of Cage and Travolta in "Face Off." "I'M CASTOR TROY!" But in THIS turkey, he's not. Caveat Emptor.

history.title: Would You Rather
history.text: From start to finish, the movie is laced with over-the-top sadism and cruelty. In some ways it's a throwback to the Vincent Price "Dr. Phibes" films, where the fates of the characters become a form of one-upsmanship...each more twisted as the film goes on. It's a pretty engaging thriller if that sort of film appeals to you, but it also telegraphs its punches...especially the ending...from a mile away. You'll either think "Wow!" or feel let down as the closing credits roll. good for a rental at best.

history.title: Fargo: Season 1
history.review_title: "Is this what you want? Yes or no."
history.text: As a fan of the movie, I didn't want to watch this. But as one other Amazon reviewer pointed out, it's less of a TV series and more of a movie played out over one season, and it's a GOOD one. There are "touchstones" to the movie all over the place (one of the most obvious being the bedroom scene between Allison Tolman (Deputy Molly Solverson) and her husband Colin Hanks (Officer-turned-Postman Gus Grimly), in which she calmly assures him "We're doing good," mirroring the Frances McDormand (Marge Gunderson) scene in the film. But this is by no means an "homage," a "tribute," a "rip-off" of the movie...all of the initial concerns I had when deciding not to watch it on its original release. This is a "movie"...a long, long movie...which channels the spirit of the original Coen Brothers film and stands completely on its own. ****NO-SPOILER ALERT***** That's right, I'm not going to give up any spoilers here, because half the pleasure of watching this is the joy of discovery, watching the characters reveal themselves, as well as the plethora of plot twists and shocking, unexpected moments. There are NO "filler episodes" in this 10-episode story arc. EVERY episode rewards the viewer with something new, something weird and wonderful, on a par with (and sometimes exceeding) the original film. It's also self-contained. Season 2 moved on to new characters, new story lines. So in order to give you something to work with while considering your purchase (and not ruining the experience by doing so), let's talk a bit about a few of the characters. Bob Odenkirk as Police Chief Bill Oswalt is 100% Odenkirk, a role that fits him like a glove, and you'll see shades of his Jimmy McGill / Saul Goodman waffling between right and wrong, cowardly and noble, victory and defeat. Time and time again he sees the writing on the wall and responds with an "I know that, BUT..." attitude. Billy Bob Thornton as Lorne Malvo takes every drop of malevolence expressed by Peter Stormare as Gaear Grimsrud in the movie and amps it up, because face it...Fargo without a STELLAR bad guy is Fargo Lite, and no one's going to want to watch that. This is an award-worthy performance as chameleon Malvo effortlessly shifts between pure evil and deceptive innocence. When he crosses paths with the main protagonist, Martin Freeman as insurance salesman Lester Nygaard, it sets the story in motion. Lester is a spin on William H. Macy as Jerry Lundegaard in the film, but with more depth, more development (he changes significantly over the 10 episodes, but remains weak and rotten at the core). Colin Hanks as Officer Gus Grimly was another exercise in character development. They guy is on top of the mountain and in the valley throughout the season, sometimes simultaneously. He never gives up, period...but he does NOT do it in a Hallmark Card / surface level manner. His "journey" is complex, and most of all, believable. I think that if you liked the movie, you will like this. I know people who were lukewarm to it, and if you're one of those people, you might be lukewarm to this as well. With the resurgence of "Twin Peaks" (similar in spirit, but David Lynch is significantly weirder than the Coen Brothers), it's an ideal time to sit back and enjoy a rich, well-developed, tense, and ultimately redemptive spin on a classic movie. Oh, you betcha.

history.title: Odd Thomas
history.review_title: I liked it, but then again, I've never read a Dean Koontz book.
history.text: Full disclosure: My girlfriend is an avid reader of fiction, I am not. I'm an avid reader of non-fiction. She spotted this one and was familiar with the Dean Koontz books. I'm familiar with the name "Dean Koontz." So I didn't walk into this one with any preconceived notions of it being "faithful" to the book, or "better than" or "worse than" the book. I just sat down to watch the movie. One of my favorite films of all time is the Christopher Walken / Al Pacino / Alan Arkin masterpiece "Stand Up Guys," which featured Addison Timlin in the pivotal supporting role of Alex the waitress, so that gave the film an instant "hook" for me. Also, I'm a Willem DeFoe fan (watch "White Sands," folks). So coming out of the gates, two actors already have my attention. I thought Anton Yelchin in the title role was likable. If they had cast someone like Ashton Kutcher, I'm confident that I'd have been wishing for one of the evil creatures to eat him about 15 minutes in. He plays the role along the lines of Toby Maguire in the Spider-Man films...equally goofy and heroic, never sacrificing one quality for the other. The movie is deliberately odd, in a sort of "Twin Peaks Lite" way. Some may find the unrelenting lovebird banter between Yelchin and Timlin to be a bit cloying after a while, but this isn't a movie for cynics to begin with. And the ending...well, that's another love it or hate it proposition as well. I gave the movie five stars based on what I like, not my anticipated assessment of what the mainstream might like. The special effects are computer generated...there is not a single second in which they will seem "real" to you. It's a little fairy tale, it's a little love story, it's a little slice of eccentric fun. Likable performers, a Koontz-based story (if that matters to you), and a film that is light years ahead of most of the films you'll find on the streaming services. If my idea of fun sounds like fun to you, you'll enjoy it. If it doesn't, you'll love it or hate it for multiple reasons. I'd leave it where it is, though...even though there are apparently other Odd Thomas books, I wouldn't want this to become another Harry Potter franchise. One was enough.

history.title: Longmire: Season 1
history.text: Come ON, November 17th and the sixth season of Longmire! I've given season one four stars, because I have binge-watched the available 5 seasons front-to-back at least twice. Several days ago, I went back to season one again. What I found is that the ensemble cast hadn't yet jelled, which is to be expected. It sounds more like actors delivering their lines and less of the "lived-in" feel that was to come later. There are more "one-liners" between cast members, where later seasons had more subtle, dry humor. The Branch Connoly running for sheriff thing gets a little overworked, too. Walt says "Do you know what time it is" and Branch replies "Saw one of your campaign signs out on the highway." Walt says "I need for you to do a background check on this guy and Branch says "I guess I'll do it because you have beer cans in the back of your truck." Those aren't actual lines of dialogue, but he's set up as a jerk from the get-go, whereas later in the series he becomes a dark, humorless, doomed jerk. The friendship between Walt and Henry, is also a little more superficial and less natural here. The whole first season has a degree of exposition that is necessary, in order to bring you up to speed on the characters, but when you go back to season one after seeing all five seasons, all of the things I've described here grow a little tiresome. No harm, no foul though...it was a good show on its way to becoming much, much better.

history.title: The Hateful Eight
history.text: It's long, it's Tarantino. That's going to pull you in or turn you off. It's actually a tense, well-played story, and the length is never an issue. The minute you see Samuel L. Jackson standing in the snow next to a pile of corpses, you know Tarantino's going to take you somewhere. And for me, as a viewer, I felt the time I spent was worth it when I got to the end. It's a pretty decent "ensemble cast," and because it's Tarantino, there are quirks-a-plenty. Kurt Russell is channeling John Wayne...you almost expect him to say "Pilgrim" at end of some of his lines. He's sharp as a tack when it comes to his chosen profession as bounty hunter, not so sharp when it comes to things like grammar. He trusts no one and tries to look at every angle, and Storytelling 101 dictates that a character like that is going to miss something eventually. Samuel L. Jackson plays Samuel L. Jackson, so if that's what brought you to the table, you may find the price of admission worth it for that alone. This is Jules from Pulp Fiction in another place and time. He's cold, smart, confident and ruthless...with a major cruel streak, just like Russell. Jackson wants his bounty..."dead or alive" means that a dead outlaw won't try to escape or kill him on the way to collecting his reward, but Russell brings 'em in alive because he relishes the sound of their "neck snapping" under the hangman's noose. Tim Roth is particularly interesting here, because HE is channeling Christoph Waltz's Dr. King Schultz from Django Unchained and Col. Hans Landa from Inglorious Basterds. His costuming and makeup appears to be ready-made for Waltz, and his speech about the nature of "justice" is so tightly wrapped around the essence of Waltz that you have to wonder if he was offered the role and turned it down, was unavailable, or Roth and Tarantino conspired to have the character "played like Waltz." I've now seen the movie twice. The first time, this was a bit of a distraction for me. The second time, I expected it and didn't dwell on it. For followers and fans of Tarantino films, it's especially enjoyable to see Michael Madsen as Joe Gage. As an actor, he's similar to Jackson in the fact that at some point he's going to flip the switch and turn on Madsen, just as Jackson turns on Jackson. It won't be a challenge for you to see that this is the same actor who played Mr. Blonde in Reservoir Dogs...he just dials it down a few notches, but it's the same guy under the skin. The other actor I'd like to single out is Walton Goggins. I've been a fan of his work since "The Shield." It's well know that he is a textbook "method actor" who immerses himself fully in a role, and it's said that he won't speak to or interact with his fellow cast and crew between takes for risk of "breaking character." In this film, you have no reason to suspect that the character is more than a one-dimensional idiot, and the audacity of an idiot on the way to Red Rock to become the new Sheriff makes you wonder "Who IS he, and what is he up to?" I won't spoil it for you, other than to say that the character has idiot tendencies, but that's far from the whole picture, and Goggins scores another major career notch in his belt with a masterful performance. This movie, to me, is "entertainment"...that's why I gave it five stars. In the realm of Tarantino movies, yes...he's made a few that missed the mark for one reason or another. This one shoots and scores.

Just as bad as I expected. But, rescued by bouncing boobies for a third of the film...so there's that.

Just a charming cast and well written.

history.title: The 13th Warrior
history.review_title: A treasure of a hidden film.
history.text: Based on the book "Eaters of the Dead" by Michael Crichton (oddly written on a bet w/ a fellow professor that he could not take the Beowulf story and make it interesting...) this movie is just solid viking entertainment. Based on real historical evidence of numerous Arab/Scandinavian trade stories, etc. Well written, beautifully filmed, and exceptionally "cool".

targets.title: Cabin In The Woods [DVD + Digital Copy]

history.text: Very good film. Nice cast. It's a true story, and it's nice to see it stick so closely to facts. The whale sinking the ship was only half the story - of equal value is their survival adrift at sea and near starvation. The only thing I quarrel with is that the actual whale was much larger than in this film: the book that Owen Chase wrote about their ordeal describes the whale as "about 85 feet in length". Imagine. Interestingly, the Essex was only one of several that were sunk by whales.

This is a film that aspires to be a sweeping saga but never quite gets there. It's a retelling of Shakepeare's King Lear, complete with the evil, jealous older sister and their scheming husbands, the foolish aging king, and the spoiled, unassuming, unfortunate youngest daughter. But this is set in Corsica, and that was the most fascinating part - the wild, French/Italian culture that survives into the 20th century with outdated customs like vendetta, local kings, and political weddings. A few people here complained about the English subtitles - one person even proclaiming that the translator doesn't know French. This isn't true. I am fluent in both French and English - the translation is competent, if not brilliant. The English is a bit awkward, but perfectly comprehensible. Don't let that deter you from watching.

Really liked this. Someone very young or immature is going to hate it - it takes some life experience, and some understanding of adult emotions and wounds, to understand this film. It's ultimately about not being able to rescue those we love, and accepting that somehow. And it's a deeply moving love story. Two very beautiful performances. Wow.

history.review_title: One of the worst I've seen in a long time.
history.text: Really stupid film. The storyline is okay, but the pacing is so terrible that by the end I didn't care; multiple flashbacks - badly placed with no logical sequence - make it confusing. Also, the acting is truly horrible, particularly that of the lead actress, who confuses perpetual pouting, canned reactions, and wooden silence, with drama. I really recommend people just skipping a film - few are that worthless - but this has little redeeming value. Don't waste your time.

Highly amusing. Good use of Austenesque dialogue. It is never less than entertaining and has some very nice performances. I couldn't shake the feeling it was done as a star vehicle for Kate Beckinsale, who plays such an annoyingly selfish and amoral character that she isn't funny - just infuriating. It's for that I dropped to three stars - plus the fact that it's rather shallow and silly - no higher meaning here. It's worth watching.

I really loved this series. From the script, to the excellent performances, to the lavish sets, it's full of period detail and technical merit. As an amateur medievalist, I was very familiar with the story, and the series sticks very close to fact as we know it, while giving a nod to the book on which this is based. Elizabeth was a fascinating, smart, engaging woman in real life (and reportedly quite a beauty) who well understood what she had to do in order for she and her family to survive in a tough society and era. The ad sells this as a story about "scheming" women - I find that really cheap and insulting, and frankly that isn't what the story is about. These women had enormous heart, did have morals, and also had the brains to play the games they were forced to play from birth. That isn't "scheming and manipulation", it's survival. I want to mention especially the beautiful performance of Rebecca Ferguson in the lead role - this series garnered her some well-deserved and overdue professional attention and led to other roles. The viewer will recognize the actress playing Warwick's older daughter as the woman playing a lead role in Poldark. And Max Irons is really fine - and great to look at - as the tempestuous, strong-willed warrior king Edward IV - the real man was as tall, as handsome, as stubborn, as impetuous, and Max nails it. Edward is remembered as one of England's most successful kings. Anyone who loves history, wants to understand the Wars of the Roses, and great historical drama, will like this one.

Disturbing. This documentary seems to have an agenda: selling anonymous, mindless, soulless sexual encounters and mainstream, hip, and healthy. It could have been really interesting subject matter, with a different (realistic) tone. But this "This is the wave of the future" message and "Isn't this fun and enlightening?" tone is really .... well, yuck. The people in the case studies are kind of odd in an unsettling way. Just really a waste of time.

history.review_title: OK if you're bored, but don't expect much here.
history.text: Mildly interesting, amateurish screenplay with a decent cast. Comparisons to a Bronte novel are unfounded; those were complex novels, this is a rather silly, immature story with a very predictable plot. All the moody cinematography in the world will not, in the end, cover a shallow plot and lazy research. Nothing is more annoying in an historical drama than blatantly bad research. This is apparent in the first minutes when the protagonist shoots an ailing horse. Anyone - man or woman - surviving on the prairie on a farm, knew how to properly kill a large animal, humanely. The way she does it - standing across the room and - good grief! - closing her eyes and firing, is not going to do anything but maim the horse and torture it. (You shoot in the middle of the forehead, up close, between the eyes - any vet will tell you that.) The male character does a lot of smoking of modern cigarettes - a particularly ridiculous sight. At one point he says, "I know I let you down" - a late 20th century phrase. These things may seem like nitpicking, but they matter - too many of them make the story unbelievable to the viewer and ruin the atmosphere. But the most frustrating thing is the characterizations. These women are too stupid to survive on the prairie. The hand-wringing and simpering presence of the female protagonist gets old after about 20 minutes. Someone this weak and insipid would simply not have survived in that environment - it's unbelievable. To add to the silliness, in this story the men are all either sinister or stupid. There is really no one to respect here. I would have liked women with some backbone and a brain, and men with heart. That would have rung truer. The most believable character is the 14 year old girl - who like most 14 year old girls is governed entirely by romantic fantasy, hormones drowning out any brain cells. At least that was realistic. But even she lacks anything resembling a fully fleshed-out, three-dimensional character. I didn't look up the filmmaker, but I"m 99% certain she is very young, and lacks experience with writing a screenplay. Give her ten years, some life experience and professional experience, and she may do something more skilled.

history.review_title: A Pleasant - if Silly - Foray Into Rural Wales
history.text: Older film, with a charming story and a lot of melodrama. Daniel J Travanti is very good. I want to warn horse lovers - as someone who knows them and grew up with them - this film will drive you crazy: the director obviously knew little about them. The lead character - although she is supposed to love horses - spends a lot of time yelling at them, slapping them, and pulling on their halters like a five year old. I wanted to kick her in the pants. This is exactly NOT the way to be handling horses. For people who 'grew up around horses' they do a lot of falling off of them and losing control of them. I found myself laughing out loud during the barn scene when the foal is born. Take it from me - you put your arms up a horses' vagina, you do not want to just put your clean jacket back on. Your arms - and everything else you have on - is covered with slime and blood after that. But THIS girl - she's spotlessly clean! Good heavens. So .... watch it with a grain of salt.

I appreciate this film so much - both as a film lover and as a pro writer/editor with a literature degree. These writers took the best of the novel and put it into two wonderful hours, while maintaining the theme Jane Austen intended - this story isn't so much a romance as it is a statement about social class inequities of the time. (The BBC series with Colin Firth, btw, is fun to watch, but they turned it into more of a soap opera romance - entirely dissing the novel in the process!) There are too many really wonderful performances here to mention. The set is an absolute feast, as is the cinematography. Period details are well-researched, from costumes to interior wall paints to the breeds of dogs running around. But the acting makes the film. For one example, notice the scene where Darcy first proposes and they have a fight - these are two amazing, accomplished actors. I've watched this scene probably ten times, and I get goosebumps every time still.

history.title: In The Heat of the Night Season 7

history.review_title: Crash course in traditional v. westernized Chinese
history.text: I felt prepared for Madam Xie from reading Amy Tan's description of her mother. (Of course, Amy Tan's mother didn't have her traditional Chinese values stretched as far!) I liked how much she accomplished with her restrained facial expressions. As much as the other characters talked about the importance of family, her face showed it as the family's secrets started to unravel in the course of criminal investigations. The bunch of them, including her, are treacherous people, so it's hard to feel sorry for any of them when they're unmasked. I don't quite believe the "we're all friends now" happy ending. The back story of Jo, the Chinese-American detective, is as interesting a mystery as the whodunnit. She looks Chinese, but she's not. She's enculturated in Western ways, brought up by a white, single, Canadian mother. I look forward to Season 2, when she'll straighten our her identity issues.

history.title: American Indian Collection
history.review_title: BASICALLY GOOD, SHAME ON THE FICTIONAL MOVIES
history.text: I bought this used because it was cheaper than the newer version of this set. Basically I am interested in Am Indian movies that contain true spirituality, visions and ceremonies etc or history. 1) "Great Indian Leaders and Nations", mentioned as -Winner American Indian Film Festival was the 1rst movie I watched. Part One of that called Great Indian Leaders I really loved with one exception. It seemed condensed and it threw too many facts at you too fast. I found myself rewinding a lot just to try to absorb what they were saying. The content was Excellent, no complaint on the amount of information, just too fast ! I wished they had seen a Ken Burns movie where you get to absorb and even Savor the content ! Part Two - Great Indian Nations did not have that problem of being condensed. It was good but Part One is my favorite so far. 2) I Will Fight No More Forever, which was 106 minutes starring Sam Elliott, James Whitmore and Ned Romero. It is a full length movie ( in reply to the other reviewer that said it wasn't), it is a bit dated, and " the Indians" had teased hair to make the tops puffy ! Ha, ha. ( I like old westerns too : ) By the end of the movie I give it a thumbs up. The back of the case says it "reenacts the heroic and tragic true story ". I especially like the true story Am Indian movies. 3) The Legend of Tillamook's Gold - I wish now that I knew there is " truly a legend on this dating back to the 1600s ", I googled it after I saw the movie. That said, this is a fictional rendition of the story, done in a made for teens movie. I didn't think I'd like it but actually I did, I am a 59 yr old woman without children. I dislike so much of the new movies because of all the violence and everything is darkness, I am careful what I choose to focus on or let enter my consciousness. I liked the movie as an adult except-the boy who likes her- his parents are played in a corny and goofy manner that cries " made for kids movie". They begin In the first 5 minutes with her having a vision, and the visions continue throughout the movie. It had my interest, too bad its fiction. I like true Am Indian spirituality as in Chief Crazy Horse and A Man Called Horse, The Return of a Man Called Horse, and Dreamkeeper are a few movies based true spirituality. 3) "Windrunner" A fictional teen or family movie about a boy trying to get on the high school football team. Because of the football theme I didn't think I'd care for it, but I did like it. 4) "The Sign of the Beaver" The good points are that it has real Indian actors. It also portrays the truth that the No. Easten Indians saved us by showing us how to make it through the winter or we'd have starved, and how we repaid them by taking any good land there was. The bad parts are that it's so bland, so literally "White washed" that the reason for the title is not included. It is an award winning 135pg book used by many teachers in school with rave reviews on how it makes history interesting. If you look up reviews for this movie as a single movie on a dvd, you will see that all the most important parts of the book were stripped out, including the reason for the title ! All the interesting things about the Indians are NOT included. THIS IS NOT A MOVIE ABOUT NATIVE AMERICANS AT ALL, BUT A TEEN MOVIE ON AN AMERICAN FAMILY. This movie is wasted film, a true travesty of "Whitewashing" an award winning book. Why did they bother ? THIS MOVIE DESERVES A REMAKE THAT IS TRUE TO THE BOOK ITSELF ! 6) "Sacagawea" is a fully narrated movie. Is is narrated by a young girls voice from the viewpoint of Sacagawea of the whole journey. The very end has a mans narrative voice summary after they all split up. I did learn a few interesting details. ADDED FEATURETTE MOVIE is about our national parks within the areas they traveled. It is 32 minutes but I thought it was longer. It was like a full 2nd movie to me. It was like a slow moving nature movie, unrushed, and a pleasant surprise ! It was mentioned in the reviews for that movie. I skipped any extra parts on the rest of the movies.

history.title: National Geographic - Lewis & Clark - Great Journey West
history.review_title: COST IS PROHIBATIVE FOR A 1 HR MOVIE.
history.text: Come on ! Copying discs is cheap now. How about passing that on to us !

This is not a "pretty Hollywood movie", in reference to some of the low reviews. It's not the highest quality film, YOU WATCH THIS TO BE INFORMED ! How long are we going to neglect these people of our country ? The myriad of problems they face is overwhelming. They are overwhelmed, point blank. This movie barely skims the surface. My first glimpse into Pine Ridge, SD was a Diane Sawyer 20/20 special hour long show 8-10 yrs ago. That's what got me interested further. Learn everything you can, the injustices go on and on. Even to this day with the pipeline our govt has forced on " their land". A new book is out (I haven't read yet) titled "The Killers of Flower Moon", get this - that is how our FBI began, because of greed and corruption and murder of Native Americans in Oklahoma. The chief picked the worst land he could find so he figured they could be left alone. Turns out there was oil on the land. There were blatent murders during the 1930 s(?). Our govt ruled they were not competent to handle their own money, appointed guardians who stole their money. Look it up. It just keeps going on and on. People donate for over in Africa or wherever, when these are the most neglected people here in our backyard. Many of the WHITE charities that claim to help the Native Americans are still stealing now. I wanted to help and had to research 2 weeks ! I was about to donate, and found that was corrupt too. I looked again, the next week. This time to make doubly sure, I looked up the name of the Pine Ridge newspaper - The Lakota Country Times and called them to ask if this one was legit. " Yes, I see their trucks delivering food all over the reservation ! ". Just out of curiosity I asked what the temperature was that day, she said " Zero". (They need wood, coats blankets, food and more) Finally I had found someone legit ! It's called ONE SPIRIT in Rapid City So Dakota, or www.native progress.org. READ, READ, READ, That website has a lot of information and projects. Look it up & get involved ! One Spirit asks them what they need and want. The residents do the work distributing food, firewood, what ever they can. One Spirit funded building an Art Center for the children to learn Native crafts. (There is no room in tiny houses with 15 family members living in one house) They are building the Buffalo Meat Processing Center so they can get back to their native diet. They are just beginning to fund another Food Distribution Center in Allen for fresh vegetables and meat. Pine Ridge is the size of Connecticut and its called THE BADLANDS because that's what we gave them. Give a hand up.

Though the story is fictional, the girls house really did burn down and the scene where she goes to view what happened is live, as it happened and true. The Asian woman wrote it in. I watched this on Sundance Now on Roku. It was featured as a now playing movie in my membership trial. I ended up searching for it to see it from the beginning. A great talent no one has heard of. Similar to Queen or Meatloaf, witty story type lyrics with good music but gay. A slice of real life's crapshoot, who succeeds and who fails. My afterthoughts were how could someone so talented have slipped through the cracks ? I think the right answer came to me. Someone mentioned "Needing to pay your dues." I wouldnt say pay your dues, he was a genius talent. What was missing was doing all the smaller club shows gives you live audience feedback on what works or what they will respond to and accept. Starting at the top with all the big promotion first denied him that necessary step and that honing his show to audiences response. A grassroots following whether by strictly gay audiences or as a crossover artist was needed as a testing ground on which direction to take flight. Yes, he was ahead of his time also. If he was born now with You Tube, he would have found a greater audience. Even at the end a University audience loved him with his stage show, but the bottom fell out too soon. Finally he ended up in small piano lounges playing Cole Porter and Irving Berlin music earning a living. Like a bright shooting star he faded out an early death. My last thoughts were... I'd so much rather watch movies about real life than all those action and fantasy movies they stuff down your gullet non stop. Movies about a slice of life, and European movies give you a chance to reflect and stay grounded instead of spinning in constant chaos.... ( Another similar movie about a 70s music talent unknown in America but had a huge following on another Continent that he never knew himself is "Searching for Sugar Man", also on Sundance Now. history.title: Boardwalk Empire
history.text: Typical excellence from HBO; excellent binge watching for me as I am coming to the series after its run ended. Have enjoyed the first 4 seasons and looking forward to the final season, #5. If graphic violence offends you, I do not recommend this series; it is terribly brutal and violent, but it is very realistic as well. I am from New Jersey and my elders all remembered many of the real-life figures in the show and the kind of world that existed during prohibition. Perhaps the real point of the series is to show how criminals can take defacto control of government and divide up territories, carry out wars among themselves, just as small countries might, with near-impunity. In this case, the problem was rooted in the highly misguided decision to adopt prohibition, something that a majority of Americans did not support, but which lasted some 15 years or so anyway. It opened a huge market in illegal liquor, which gangsters immediately took hold of, finding a nation full of ready customers. Very worth watching from that point of view, and to consider that most of these characters are real and did the vile, brutal things that are depicted. All that it takes for such people to gain power is the right conditions, which prohibition did.

history.title: Being There
history.text: I am a big fan of Peter Sellers and enjoy most of his films, and I realize that this film is highly regarded for various reasons, but it was a total misfire for me. The film is a one-joke work that wears thin very quickly. Just as quickly, it becomes less and less credible. It becomes not so much a matter of how obtuse the Sellers character is, but how totally credulous and unbelievable the rest of the characters are. Not for one minute did I believe any of their reactions to Sellers beyond the first few encounters. It's too bad, really, because Sellers was an amazing talent; a totally plastic actor who could literally become any of the characters he played. I will continue to enjoy most of his other work, but I could never sit through this again. It was boring and, after a while, excruciating. The two stars are for Sellers alone.
