When you start forcing people to give up their land and things, you are acting outside of free market capitalism. Authorian Socialism is clearly the more greedy of the two. These little bits of ignorance in movies used to try to sway public opinion only goes to show the cluelessness of the Hollywood elite, living in a fantasy land and thinking the few should rule the many, whose idea of everything being equal means that they should have more. history.title: Knight of Cups

If stream-of-consciousness experimental style films are your cup of tea, you'll enjoy this but it takes a lot of patience and a pretty open mind. Terrence Malick has always been an iconoclast and a visionary, but you must suspend expectation and have an open mind in order to appreciate. I was awe-struck by the imagery and imaginative filmmaking techniques but left cold by the characters, who all seemed very unfeeling and self-centered, which I believe was the point but a bit unsettling.

Still, I'm a fan of Hitchcock and Lynch so I stuck with it but it just threw every bit of logic out the window. I think it could have been a good movie has they structured it so the clues were explained and had given it a resolution but the way it ended up left me asking what the point of the movie even was? I give it two stars for at least the camera angles and sound design were good and definitely created a spooky atmosphere. There was a behind the scenes clip but it reveals very little and is short and not really worth the price of the DVD.

history.title: The Story of Robin Hood
history.text: For a non-Bluray, this DVD is sharp and clear and the audio is too. We loved the adventure and action that is so buoyant and breezy played by some terrific English actors in splendid locations. Unlike newer "epics" about the medieval age, the castles look new here as they would have been, with eye-popping color (admittedly my preference for swashbuckling adventure). The story gets in an amazing number of interesting ideas in between swordplay right away and never lets up: Why King Richard left for the Crusades, Why his brother gets in control, and why Robin, and who was that wandering minstrel anyway, all with a beautiful Maid Marian and very awesome locations and again, that story line is just enchanting even when you know the story or have seen it in other Robin Hoods over and over. AN epic with heart and enchantment, this is the best version of the story and one reason Disney became so great. So fun.

history.title: The Comancheros (50th Anniversary Edition) [Blu-ray Book]
history.text: BluRay Stars in Widescreen Adventure Comedy . I should have written this when I first got the Bluray a year back, but watching it again the other night reminds me of how great it is to have the BluRay format. This film delivers Westerns scenery in spades and it is dazzling in its clarity. HiDef transfers for BluRay can be made two ways: quick and dirty it just gets the HiDef transfer through the film chain. Really great BluRay picture comes when they stop each frame in the telecine gate and individually scan it for hi definition, which is how it appears they did this disc. Just awesome quality. Love the movie, no question there, and really enjoy this disc time and again.

history.title: Valley of the Kings 1954
history.review_title: Save the money and buy the soundtrack.
history.text: Boy, this one I really didn't like. And this from a diehard Robert Taylor and adventure movies of the Fifties fan. Seemed hacked together in the worst way with almost no plot, really padded out like they all went on a vacation trek though the desert and decided to film it and add narration later to make up a story about what you are seeing. The big action scene (at least until the end) is a "race" between lovers' carriages through streets of Cairo. Lackluster script and portrayals, a "no director" feel, topped off by a muddy, no-one-cared quality to the DVD (meaning scratchy, mushy picture with no restoration attempt). Maybe it was OK new on the big screen but at home what a dud from the start with a decent ending. Big disappointment except -- What is GREAT about this is the Miklos Rosza music score. It's out on CD and was actually the reason I bought the DVD sight unseen. Save the money and buy the soundtrack.

history.title: Cinerama's Seven Wonders of the World
history.text: No matter how much I heard about this movie before seeing it, and I had not seen it before, I still did not know how good it was going to be. And I have no other documentaries in my collection. This one is just so sweeping, from the languorous crisscrossing of New York in the Fifties, to the startling beauty and low aerial flyovers of the expanses of Rio de Janerio, this was a dazzling showcase of the times and format. The Cinerama Clipper seems to float over the desert but with great, swooping banked turns still showing the pyramids and famed places you've longed to visit. A review would be inseparable from the times and locals so long and far ago shown, and I am sure nostalgia is a part of it all, but somehow the film felt fresh and still in keeping with reality. If "Reality in Cinerama" is or could be your thing, there's an awesome globe circling feast in store for you.

history.title: NCIS: Season 11
history.text: My only complaint with the Season 11 DVD, is with the Ep.1 Commentary. While it is fair to assume that people listening to the commentary have watched the episode in question, it is not fair to assume that DVD purchasers have necessarily seen the entire season. It is highly irritating & annoying to us enjoying this excellent series for the first time on DVD, never having watched it on TV, for it to be revealed in an Ep. 1 Commentary that a certain character is killed mid-season! It is like the A-hole who goes to a movie a second time and starts revealing upcoming scenes in a loud voice to the audience, or plot points upcoming in a book you are reading. If you wouldn't say or show it in previews of upcoming shows on the TV broadcast, don't put it in a Commentary! Just common sense really. Up to this point, in prior seasons, the Commentaries have been very good with sticking to talking about the show in question. Otherwise, the writing, acting and direction are all still excellent.

history.title: 13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi
history.text: How can a movie about the Benghazi travesty not mention the name "Hillary Clinton?" Nothing about the numerous requests for more security, down-play of the requests for help during the attack and the numerous orders to "stand down." Nothing about the real story of Benghazi, the immediate cover-up by Obama and Hillary Clinton (yes the internet video is mentioned but not who was selling the lie of the video being the reason for the attack.) Luckily, the movie was made within recent memory of people who know what actually happened (from the interviews of the heroes involved and seeing Susan Rice and Hillary Clinton with their own eyes lie about the video) so that the complete story of the failure to order the rescue and the subsequent cover-up is known by at least some voters. Ask yourself, if the only thing you knew about Benghazi was from this movie, would you know that Hillary Clinton had any involvement at all in the Benghazi incident, before, during, or after? Simply a whitewash that lets her off the hook. (Pretty well done otherwise, thus the 3 stars.)

history.title: The Last Ship: Season 1
history.text: Makes you wonder how TNT can afford the production cost of making a series that looks as good as any major motion picture. Very much a showcase of U.S. military capability. Bought the first season at a Black Friday sale, never having seen the show. Finally watched it and was glad I bought it (and just ordered Season two.) Great cast, great writing, plausible plot. Lots of action and good guys making tough decisions, always striving to do the right thing. Reminds me of the many ex-military men who I have been trained by, unabashed patriots and heroes all. Probably has the worst possible time-slot on TV, Sunday night at the same time as AMC's Fear the Walking Dead, but that is what a second cable hookup, TV and VCR or DVR are for. You certainly do not have to dislike The Walking Dead to like this show. They are both top-quality shows, worth watching and buying. This one is based more in real, scientific possibility, but both are about what happens to humanity when social order breaks down, however it happens, which is always interesting to think about. If it happens, just be sure you are armed with plenty of ammo!

history.title: Matt Helm Lounge: The Silencers / Murderers' Row / The Ambushers / The Wrecking Crew [DVD]
history.text: Worst adaptation of a book series ever. Donald Hamilton's Matt Helm is a serious bad ass in the books, not in any way a clown. Only the first film, The Silencers, was done half-way seriously, and even it did not live up to the book. The rest of the films were simply farces and makes The Silencers look good by comparison, when it really isn't. Believe me, each film gets progressively worse after The Silencers. Read the books instead, starting with Death of a Citizen, and you will see what I mean. I saw all of the films in the theater when they came out, so would not waste 10 cents on this set, much less the outrageous asking price for some of the worst films ever made. (The Matt Helm book series deserves a real adaptation of the books, done with a serious Director and leading actor, remaining true to the books. If done right, they would make very good films, more in the nature of the Parker films.) Zero stars is the real rating, but apparently one star is the lowest you can go.

history.title: Banshee: Season 3
history.review_title: Annoying Commentary Spoilers, but Great Show
history.text: No complaints with the show itself. This season features two brutally realistic fights and a number of interesting new characters. My only complaint is that in the Episode 1 Commentary there are spoilers of two different deaths of characters later in the season. There is even less reason to believe that people buying a series on DVD that comes from a premium cable show have seen the entire season on TV than shows from network TV. I usually like to watch everything on a disc at one time, while the episodes are still fresh in my mind, so foretelling future plot points and character deaths in an early commentary is extremely annoying. It's called drama people! Let the story develop! Since the season is only 10 episodes, the best way to watch it and the commentaries, is to watch all the episodes and then go back and watch the commentaries. Yes, I do like the commentaries, but a comprehensive commentary discussing the specifics of the entire season goes on the last episode of a season, not the first.

history.title: The Man From U.N.C.L.E. - The Complete Series (Repackage/DVD)
history.text: This series is definitely a mixed bag. The first season is one of the best seasons of a spy series of all time: good writing, real danger, well acted, great guest stars. Napoleon Solo was truly cool under pressure. The writers proceeded to ruin the show after that season, (think the first Lethal Weapon movie vs Lethal Weapon 3 or 4 or Twin Peaks Season One vs. Twin Peaks Season Two) It is probably still worth getting the full series set to see everything, but you can see how they destroyed a show with an excellent beginning. If you just bought Season One and saw how good it was, you would likely want to buy Season Two anyway, so you might as well get the whole series at a pretty reasonable price. (Had this show ended after Season One, this show would have had the same, or better, cult following as The Prisoner; just an excellent show that inexplicably ended, leaving everyone wanting more.) As it is, it very much wore out its welcome by the end.

history.title: Melancholia
history.text: Slow, tedious, boring. Take a fairly simple Science Fiction idea of the earth under threat of being destroyed and make it into an uninteresting bore-fest. If a point can be made in 5 minutes, let's take 15 or 20 minutes to make it, and on and on. The entire first half of the movie (of 2 hours and 15 minutes) was unnecessary to the rest of the film. No explanation of what happened to her husband, in the second half of the film, after going on and on, and on and on, with the wedding party in the first half. The only redeeming part of the film is Kirsten Dunst finally getting topless in two scenes, and the last 30 seconds of the film, but, beyond that, this movie is a total waste of time. Very good actors are simply wasted by the Writer/Director of this mess.

history.title: Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection 'F' [DVD]
history.review_title: The best dragonball Z "Film" to date...
history.text: This is, by far, the best dragonball z film to date. Is it better than Cell games, or some of the heated battles or really messed up serious moments? No, but it is pretty excellent. "Ressurection F" may come off like any other DBZ movie: oh look, a villain is coming, we gotta stop him, fight, roll credits. Well, they went above and beyond to insure there would be more to this. Warning-tons of spoilers ahead. This movie starts off with the premise that Freiza being resurrected has been a goal for a while, but tracking down a safe place to get dragon balls has been difficult. So they take the risk, and they succeed. It is revealed, Freiza never trained for a single day a bit later on, and this comes as no surprise. Before that, we are shown a army and in addition, some humor with Emperor Pilaf making things all too easy. A rather disturbing scene of a "not completly together" Freiza follows, and I will say, to anime fans who watch shows like "Deadman Wonderland, "Claymore," etc, it may not seem so disturbing. But maybe it will. No worries, technology has advanced, and Freize is reassembled, no mechanics this time either. Revealing what Freiza's "Hell" was like was both hilarious and messed up. Not that he deserves better, but it's still like "yep." When Freiza decides to go back to earth with an army of 1,000, some great action and character fights follow. This is where a lot of complaints have come from, as many say it is ridiculous who is there and who is not, and also that Gohan is again basically sidelined. It's not untrue. For one, Krillin brings Master Roshi, but Tien doesn't bring Chaotsu or Yamcha? They were light-years beyond Master Roshi's strength. So that made no sense. That being said, they do a good job of making it obvious Master Roshi isn't keeping up, Krillin coming to his aid at some point, and on top of that, Gohan saves Krillin, and eventually Piccolo from Freiza's current most powerful fighter. Freize specifically points out that Gohan is not going full max (even with still being "out of the game"-no training), as he doesn't wish to kill, or the entire army would've been gone in seconds. Gohan would do that, he is not evil, he's not even Vegeta obviously. After this Goku and Vegeta (along with Beerus who humorously freaks out Freiza later and Wees) show up, and the "real battle" begins. For a rematch of what I believe is still the longest anime fight of all the time (30+ episodes was it), it was extremely well done. The Super Saiyan god form goes blue, Freiza mocks it as hair-dye, and Freiza goes golden. His colors alter as does multiple areas of his body: this is not just "Freiza is golden" as many like to say. Also, as far as a super saiyan form, i am not sure where fans wanted them to go after super long haired 3. Did they want them to have hair creepingly long and able to attack/choke people like say, Sailor Moon's "Mistress 9?" A cheap shot was also a big area of fans outcry. I think everyone who was so angered about the shot at Goku taking him down should go back and watch the series again. Krillin throws a rock and hurts Goku, and he also hurts his foot on a rock later, these are just 2 examples. They are not impenetrable, simply on their guard and thus maxed out. They can still be hurt easily, they are just smarter than that. It was unexpected and quite amazing. Vegeta swarms in to save the day, only for yet another extremely creepy scene to follow. And that is something that goes over this whole film. While it has it's light moments 4sure (Beerus eating Pizza, Wees and him eating other foods), it has some very dark tone to it. They aren't given five minutes, they are not easily all saved. HUGE SPOILER! Freiza takes out the whole earth b4 Vegeta even gets to finish off his big moment. Poor Vegeta...Vegeta fans, deal, seriously why would u want the movie to be predictable? It might help, that the special effects are so suberb, even though we know certain things (like, for instance, the hereos are gonna win the end), watching earth slowly crumble and being oblitered, Vegeta dying (again), and everyone aside from Goku, the gods, and those who fought the army (plus Bulma and Jaco-a cool addition who has his own manga-do check it out it's fun!), are alive and realize they lost. Fear not, time is reversed, and Goku takes out Freiza b4 this terrible event happens. It lasted just long enough to have a terrifying impact though. I think it was a good idea not to include too many characters as well, against other's opinions. We do not see anyone whose not going to fight essentially. I would've liked to see Andriod 18, Yamcha, and Chaotsu, but we really didn't need Videl, Buu, Mr. Satan, or others there, and it allowed for more of the stars and less of those who are cool, but don't need to be in every scene/film/episode/movie. Yes, this a "revenge-plot" movie and there isn't much more to the plot than that. But let's face it, Freiza was the one who set off every disastrous event since day 1, even Cell on some level (since his DNA was used in that concoction-can we get Resurrection-C next?). This "rematch" of sorts does not disappoint. Forgot to mention, Freiza's arrival involves blowing up an entire city in one hit. Fun right? Let this movie be fun, well done, with great special effects, excellent battles, many terrifying moments, and well done fight scenes. It was far more thrilling than battle of gods, despite Beerus being awesome, and far more engaging than most of the DBZ movies, even Wrath of The Dragon and yes, Broly: Legendary Super Saiyan. It definitely beats out many sagas of the series I'd say too: again, no comparison to Cell, or the namek-to-freiza saga. One more shed light on the humor: Goku and Vegeta both make jokes of their "fusion" multiple times, Bulma yells at Freiza calling endless names, and humorously sees him for the first time. This series knows when to take things seriously and when not too-most of the time-this is one time where it did better than usual (an example of failing to me is the entire Fusion Reborn movie, or Beerus vs. Vegeta in battle of gods, where it was a sushi joke the whole time). I'd reccomend this to even casual fans of the series, for as long as they know Freiza was a galactic nightmare of a being who, by all means, has done way more damage than perhaps anyone we've seen to date (all-right, Beerus-god of destruction, and Majin Buu was nasty as well, but time ((Beerus is mega old)), plus how far did Buu even get b4 being stopped?), there is nothing to not understand or not enjoy. 5 out of 5, as opposed to battle of gods, which I'd do 4 out of 5, Broly and Wrath OT Dragon would get 4.5 out of 5.

history.title: Once Upon a Time: Season 4 DVD
history.review_title: Overall a pretty great season, lacking some in the latter half....
history.text: The title may sound negative, but literally the unenjoyable part of this season is the latter half of the second half of the season. Get to that later. Following off the formula of Season 3, the show has taken an "arc based" storyline. Personally, I preferred the way Season 2 handled things, where there was a main evil villain (in that case, it was Cora/Miller's Daughter/Queen Of Hearts) while many events could take place for a few episodes without derailing to getting other from the main story. And like Season 3, this season does suffer a bit from things ending too fast. Unlike Season 3's beginning, it is not slow or boring in the least. The first "arc" is the "Frozen/Snow Queen" arc, based off the hot success of Disney's "Frozen." The acting, costumes, etc, are top notch and better than ever here. Doing a better job would've been hard. The story quickly excelerates from "oh look it's Elsa" to the introduction of Ingrid, the Snow Queen. A huge line of secrets kept. What makes this work so well in one episode, for example, has Anna meeting David, teaching him how to sword fight, which explains a lot. A big emphasis on family and a villain who is more misunderstood that actually evil, crazy, deranged, etc. Halfway through it begins to feel more like Hans Christian Anderson's "Snow Queen" story than simply Frozen, with an intersection of "Sorcerer's Apprentice" within it too. Highlights are "The Snow Queen" and "Shattered Sight," both of which showed us some top notch acting, and to be honest, sometimes the acting is not the best on this show. What also works so well is Ingrid/Snow Queen's connection to Emma, that she had love for her, and that also, Elsa is like an instant best friend forever to Emma, and it actually all works. Like the prior Oz arc, I felt it could've been longer, but it worked. Oh, and Belle actually had quite a good deal of involvement too. Onto the 2nd half, we get a plotline leading out from the beginning of the "Sorcerer's Apprentice" part in the background of the first half. Mr. Gold reunites the "Queens Of Darkness" which consist of Maleficient, Cruella, and Ursula. First off, finally Malificient is back. A past with the charmings really is very messed up, and makes more of Emma's backstory used in the first half add up to something. Strengthened is the amazingingly well played Cruella. Here she has the ability to control animals. They after the "author" as someone had to have written the book of Henry's. Ursula is a bit underwhelming, if only because her costume is kinda crummy, and that she really isn't given much of a role. Then Cruella is killed for no real reason whatosever. We find out Mal has a child, or rather, she's alive, and the whole thing is quite well done. Charmings vs...the Mal's? August/Pinnochio also returned for some enjoyment. What throws this off is basically introducing "the author" who has gotta be 100x more annoying, and 1000x more worthless than Pan from Season 3. He only has power because of really dumb circumstantial occurrences. His involvement is Cruella's backstory is silly to say the least, as was the "alternative" universe episode which felt more like self-parody then an effort to suprise anyone. It leaves Mal underdeveloped still. We get thrown a serious curveball, in "Zelena's alive!" Yes, the wicked witch sister. I thought it was obvious she didn't die in Season 3, but the way she is sprung is a bombshell. Seriously, though, between the author, the random spring of "omg the dark one" again, and lack of development of three great iconic villains, was kind of messy. I'd be giving this a 3 out of 5 overall for the 2nd half bringing it down, if not for the fact both Cruella and Mal are returning for the 2nd half of Season 5 (which, tbh, so far has been absolutely awful). Basically, shortened version. Love or hate Frozen, they couldn't really have done any better justice to it, the original Snow Queen source material, and making it work really well. We finally got Maleficent back (same actress from Season 1, Kristen Strauten) and involved, and who doesn't like Cruella? Points all have to go to Elizabeth Mitchell for her portrayal as the Snow Queen/Ingrid though, she did an amazing job.

history.title: Last, The: Naruto the Movie (BD)
history.review_title: The worst Naruto film, bordering on forced, out of character nonsense, and soap-opera quality, textbook plot+love....
history.text: All-right, and I honestly thought "Bonds" was rather awful, with it's paint-by numbers story of "oh that's actually a girl" "this old guy is pulling some stuff" (we've seen this like 5 times already), and cop-out easy to solve invasion ending. Having been off the tails of Blood Prison and Road To Ninja, I'm still not even sure what I forced myself to sit through with this one. People say "Lost Tower" wasn't good, with the time traveling and Naruto actually meeting his father and stuff. Ok, enough prior Naruto film comparison. This is, without the doubt, the worst Naruto movie to date. It's not even a paint-by-numbers issue. It literally makes zero sense. OK, I can handle them showcasing Hinata some in a plot-line, and having a little fun with her obvious "I have always loved you" thing for Naruto. But seriously, he never even acknowledged in all the years passed he even remotely liked her. There not even close. OK, I get it, Sakura is obsessed with Sasuke. But seriously. He lost his mind. It would've been more believable if she'd abandoned everything to be with him, then to believe that Naruto suddenly decides to play "oh i can get the girls!" This turns into a soap-opera/love story rather than shonen anime somewhere within the time frame of this film. They couldn't even have Sakura be a bit jealous of the Hinato-Naruto set up here, given her obvious close bond to Naruto? It's like they were not even trying to make sense, but just be like "ship these two and make a plotline around it!" There were better filler arcs in the series than this. Nevermind the fact that, like Bonds, this movie really didn't go anything to ackowledge itself as a "great story" of a film, unlike Road to Ninja, Blood Prison, Will Of Fire, the 1st Shippuden movie, the original 3 Naruto movies. etc. Even if they were like filler story arcs made into better animated feature length films, they were still trying hard to make us pay attention. Just for example, that gate thing in Blood Prison was really creepy, something feared by even chief toad. This movie has nothing whatsoever but the forced love story to hold it. Hinata's clan and past becomes an explosion of trouble and they have to take on another villain whose playing the "This is my right this is what is going to happen!" thing. I honestly cannot comprehend what anyone was thinking. And then they made a sequel to this where Sakura and Sasuke are together...after all the damage he caused? Seriously? Sakura practically has Stockholm syndrome minus the actually being held captive part at this point. She was always way stronger than that. Now I am not saying "she should've ended up with Naruto" 100%. Would it have made a lot more sense? Yes. Would it have felt far less forced? Definitely. Am I on that shipping team? Nope. It's not necessary for every character to get paired up with a lover. Especially on a show that acknowledges friendship bonds constantly as it's primarily focus of importance when it comes to character interaction. And that, is all one really needs to think about to judge this film. If you really wanted Hinata+Naruto, you got it. Otherwise, this movie is a mess, with forced love, Naruto acting like "hot stuff" when he clearly grew up from that, and a paint-by-numbers plotline with less action than former films. I think I'll just go back and watch the "power" episodes, cause as said, the series has better filler than this so-called "canon" film.

history.title: Captain America: Civil War [3D Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Honestly, the best MCU film probably ever made...
history.text: I had a few different titles I wanted to use for this, but went with the simple one. Others were "A movie that somehow manages to not only outdo WInter Soldier, but pretty much any super hero film with a large number of them in one film." The third was "A movie that is called Captain America that gives Tony Stark more plot development than he's ever gotten." And they are all right, in my opinion. Where to start. Don't be going into this looking for some super creepy, weird, "villain." Yes, this movie has enemies, and the title "civil war" yes means other superheroes too, but there are others. Let's start with the return for General Thunderbolt Ross. He is played really well, still really simply put, about as much of a villain while still being on the side as it gets. Showing unnecessary creepy footage to basically make the good guys feel bad. We also have a surviving now full-fledged villain who is only in the opening scene, which sets 1 of 2 needed stages of the film. The main one is someone whose motive is literally unclear til the very end of the film. You will not expect it, no matter how other things you might figure out or find obvious. Onto this film, after a opening fight scene, now "Avenger" Scarlet Witch, is the first to be distraught. Vision is also around, so yeah, you definitely had to see "Age Of Ultron" to get everything. Even if your watching a movie that is about 1000x what "Age Of Ultron" could really dream to be, "Civil War" sets up a 117 country act that will basically make the avengers a world owned, controlled organization. In a turn of events, Tony Stark actually is on board. Why? Because he seems to finally be feeling guilty for the chaos he's caused, namely creating Ultron, which, was pretty dumb on his part. Side scenes emphasize this. Others have different ideas, Captain America the freedom fighter wants the freedom. Cue a disastrous thing to make things worse when formed evil "Winter Soldier" Bucky Barnes seems to have blown up an embassy, killing what turns out to be the Black Panther's dad. And that's when it really gets insane. The introduction of the Black Panther was great-acting, movements, reasons, etc. For being a side character, he goes through an entire character arc and realization by the end. After a semi-fight, everyone is brought in, and our villain "Zemo" uses specific words to set up the winter soldier Bucky. I kind of expected something like this was going to be an issue, but all of the surrounding issues just makes it so much worse. What follows, is teaming up, including Spider-Man, which, I honestly loved. He's in the MCU now, he's got the signal, he's younger, he's still wise cracking like ASM2, but different enough. A humorous kidnapping of Ant-Man leads to the big "showdown. Or so you'll think. Sorry if I don't have the sides entirely right, but we got: Iron Man, Black Panther, Black Widow, War Machine, Vision, and Spider man. Versus Captain America, Falcon, Ant-Man, Hawkeye, Winter Soldier, and Scarlet Witch. Both dark and humorous, from Ant-Man going into a new mode, to Spider Man being in apparently his first real fight, to the accidental hurting of War Machine, and who does it as well, coupled with double-double-double agent Black Widow's actions. As said, this film has many surprises even when you think you've figured out 1/2 the twists. No, the real battle is still yet to be fought, but it was pretty epic. Honestly, nothing can really compare. It's basically the Iron Man, Captain America, and Thor scene from Avengers times 1000. There is an issue with their being more hydra winter soldiers (are you suprised or not? not sure if I was.). But this is not at all how this film will end. They show scenes of a car and hints all throughout that it was (MEGA SPOILER ALERT!) Tony's parents car. Who else has been waiting since like, Iron Man 2 to find out who did it and why? Captain America's darkest moment comes out. Tony Stark tried so hard to not act like a fool or pursue his own agenda, but no one can blame him for the massive battle that occurs. It's almost more epic than the big fight earlier on. No one really knows how to apologize, but everyone really does in some way or another. Now that I'm past the film itself, what's the damage? Well, for one, I was pretty worried the movie would be heavily overcrowded. I wasn't feeling them throwing Iron Man so heavily into the film. "Winter Soldier" had Black Widow, Captain America, Nick Fury, Winter Soldier, Frank Grillo/Crossbones, Robert Redford, that's about it. Avengers Age Of Ultron felt extremely overcrowded, Baron Von Struckner appearing for no real reason other than to throw in Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver, they basically just fight giant robots again. Yeah, wasn't a big fan of the later. This film does not suffer from the "too many characters" effect at all. One can say "spider man was unnecessary" despite how well it worked, but aside from that, I see this film only as "it would be less if it lacked anything else." Another thing, is a movie needing to be a "civil war" I would've thought needed to be a 2 parter, but truthfully, unless they were going to drag like 5 more heroes into this and change the ending to the cliche plot we thought was coming but didn't, it would've felt dragged out then. Another thing before being done is, anyone comparing this to BatmanVSuperman should just stop. This movie nor that movie would have any right to be anything like each other. Just because they set up versus circumstances means literally nothing. "omg superheroes fight" is the end of similarities. They are such different characters in different universes in totally different levels of events occurring. I am glad to see Hollywood didn't toss 2 versus films similar, contrary to what others say. In conclusion, whether you simply love Marvel, love Captain America, Iron Man, any of the others (honestly cannot wait for Black Panther after this), you want to see this. It has a way better plot, pacing, etc, than "Age Of Ultron" and doesn't play around. A sense of humor? Yes. Is it a goofball fest like Iron Man 3 with nonsensical plot points, or redundant and not in need of any team like Age Of Ultron? Absolutely not. The directors for this movie are doing Avengers: Infinity Wars 1-2, and this film proved they have the rights to do so.

history.title: Once Upon A Time: Season 5
history.review_title: 1st half is cringe-worthy, but the 2nd half was pretty good...
history.text: Where to start. Honestly, I love this show, but no idea what they were thinking in the 1st half. Like the previous 2 seasons, the show has been divided up into 2 "arcs" leaving the first half to have a different story from the 1st. Leaving off from the end of season 4, Emma became the "new dark one." The show goes back and forth on a six week timeline where "Dark Swan" is in storybrooke and there is confusion-Merida being controlled, Rumple is all over the place, Henry is betrayed, Regina trys to play savior. It's all downhill from there. Going to Camelot starts out interesting but leaves us with way too quick plotlines that go nowhere and are never resolved even at the end of the entire season. No Morgana, Mordred, Merlin dies way too quickly on a technicality basically, and Zelena whose back is mostly there to...well, act evil because dark swan fails. Then we get Captain Dark One, yes, guess what that means. It is just plain bad-camelot is not interesting at all, the main cast is wimpy and does really nothing to combat any threat. Things are really only interesting when Merida-yes the one from Pixar's Brave-is around, trying to get Rumple to beable to pull Excalibur from the stone, or her own backstory where it's revealed King Arthur killed her father and a lot goes down including the return of Mulan and Ruby in "The Bear King." The ending episode of the 1st half is really pathetic, a super let down of prior dark ones walking around doing nothing and easily ended. Zelena is randomly sent away. In the end, nobody was really that evil, and it wasn't fun at all, just another dark curse, a messy plotline more so than Season 4B, not sure what they were thinking. The 2nd part becomes somewhat of a quest to save Hook, but grows into something much bigger. In the Underworld, we get a lot of return characters. Cora, Henry Sr, Pan, Cruella, the blind witch. Storybrooke is eerily creepy looking for an unexpected reason. Emma is back to normal, and they find out everyone around has unfinished business. The sort of real underworld is underneath what they begin to call "Underbrooke." We have a lot of personal episodes, the first being "Souls Of The Departed" which was really excellent. It explains a lot of past season things and settles old issues. They wish to help others settle their unfinished business, which leads to coming accross Cruella putting Henry in a situation, and of course, Hades. Hades is pretty great, even gets involved with Hercules for an episode. We see who trained snow how to use the bow, more evil queen, funny Cruella moments. Gaston from Belle's past returns as well as Hook's brother, and Milah, Hook and Rumple's ex lover. Some characters go, some stay, the river of lost souls is creepy. Zelena returns and is accidently brought to the underworld, only for things to become way more complicated in a good way, as Hades had eyes for Zelena and her time travel spell. Eventually, when things settle down, they of course go back home, which leads to an extremely sad confrontation. It works very well. Things are also tied up from the 1st half with characters going home if they wish as well as good character bonding. The 2 final episodes seem a bit overblown involving a new plotline and were kind of slow, but interesting. In conclusion, yes, you want to buy this. It's no different than Season 3, one part is done poorly and the other is great. Or from Season 4 for that manner. Just don't expect anything too good out of camelot or dark swan. Hopefully they can be more consistent with a Season 6 coming. I honestly would've rather rated this 4 stars given more was good than bad, but when it's bad, it's really bad, the last 2 episodes were boring.

history.title: Ghostbusters
history.review_title: An enjoyable movie that honestly was a "hate-train" lover for people and honestly over-budgeted...
history.text: Said a lot in the title, but I will explain more as I review this film. As a reboot movie that shows an origin of a all female, new ghostbusters team, I am glad they retitled it "Answer the Call." I will say, the amount of hate for this film prior to release and those who refused to see it is childish nonsense. Be honest here, Ghostbusters 2 wasn't even good, so bad can a reboot be? The answer is, in the very least, much more worthy of the name and done pretty well. Yes, there are some moments that seem a bit drawn out. I'd honestly not reccomend the extended version, which inserts goofy dance sequences and adds nothing. The normal version however, despite probably needing to take a little rest on every character being comedic, manages to find a pretty good tone that we can feel there is a huge problem to call the assembling ghostbusters team for and route for them in a semi-serious manner. Hauntings are increasing everywhere. They bring in what can be called "fun science" that allows for some interesting concepts without trying to overexplain to make too much sense out of their weaponry, gear, the ghosts vomiting green stuff, etc. There is a villain who is setting up a massive device to have the undead invade essentially, making this not about "Zool" or any of that. So the plotline is also different, and going to say for the last time, at least better than that ooze silliness from the original ghostbusters sequel. It turns into an event that goes down and is less about the sky and more about what's coming out of a ground. The origin of the logo is fun, the action sequences are fun, everything about this movie is pretty fun. SPOILER ALERT! Partially through the movie the villain "dies" but possesses Chris Hemsworth, here seen playing not the wise cracking hero type but a really dumb secretary, and it works very well seeing him play the double roles of the secretary and the villain. We even see a latter monster and a few others. I wouldn't say they reach the creep level of those of said original film, in fact they are more akin to the cartoon "Real Ghostbusters" which they may or may not have been going for. In any case, it works. All of this movie works, and does a good job in entertaining and showing off chemistry and characters. I wish it would've done better, though I feel they wasted a lot of money (there are dance sequences that ate up reportedly $30 million plus that aren't in the 3D/normal cut, seriously?). I think the studio expected WAY TOO MUCH out of it profit wise. I'll end with the whole "song dispute." There are 3 Ghostbusters songs in this film, one is a japanese band cover of the original, another is my walk the moon-also a cover, and the fall out boy/missy elliot song. Honestly, all work, and you'll only hear the last one for about 1 1/2 minutes when they really first set up and get out there. Oh, and the hate-train. The original cast was all guys, was that sexist? I'm a guy and I was happy to have seen this be made. It's good, plain fun, done well. Enjoy it and go in with your mind open.

history.title: Underworld: Blood Wars
history.review_title: Excellent installment in the franchise, crummy format release...
history.text: I really enjoyed this movie. From the beautiful set pieces, to the interacting coven and death dealers, plotting against each other to become the new elders, how Selene become so important to change the future, only to go a step further...I think the only reason why it doesn't deserve a 10/10 more like a 9/10 is the lack of explanation of her journey, where she basically went from "vampire" to "vampire-immortal hybrid" to "vampire-immortal 2.0" version with the white streaks. With a sixth film already planned, I imagine it will be explored deeper. The spin and the plotline about Amelia was also way overdue and it delivered, with taking both Charles Dance character from "Awakening" and making him a lot more powerful in both acting and what he was willing to do (aka not be viktor), and whom his son 'really was" was ideal. The 2 stars are there because seriously, screen gems has got to be behind the no-3D release. Now, Allegedly, this movie is getting a 3d release on May 29th, 2017. It's a ridicoulous bs gimmick to confuse people as well as make them need multiple releases if they want all the platforms available. I for one, will just be waiting. I saw this in the theatres and this isn't one of those movies you see in 3d just because you wanted a sword or a random weapon or nasty gore shot to come at you for 2 seconds approximately every 20 minutes. No, this movie has depth with the people themselves even when talking, let alone the structures, the water, snow, ice, and especially all of the grand fight scenes. Movie-5 out of 5 stars, best film in the franchise since Underworld: Evolution (and tbh, I really liked both the prequel and awakening too). Release-1 out of 4 stars, it's screen gems, and I say that because they are doing the same with the not as good by a long shot, but shared property release of "Resident Evil: Final Chapter." AGAIN NO 3D? These kind of movies with the various set pieces, directors who care to put in the effort to do it properly, and the amount of fighting, rubble, etc, that comes towards the screen in any fashion is why 3d even exists.

history.title: Star Trek Beyond (DVD)
history.review_title: There's a reason for the "every other movie" joke and it seems to be fitting here...
history.text: Star Trek fans know full well of the "every other movie sucks" thing, even if some aren't looked so down upon, like "Star Trek: The Motion Picture" like they once were. I honestly wasn't a huge fan of this reboot series 1st installment, really just from the nonsensical moments like stranding Kirk in a place he'd surely die if he didn't meet old spock (watch that movie if you don't know what I'm talking about), or the amount of action scenes that were very unoriginal like J.J. Abrams looked like he used the star trek brand to make a star wars film. Hence why people started calling it "Trek Wars." However, it was hardly bad, and I think some fine tunning really worked with the huge theme of self-sacrifice, emotions, rebooted Khan being played by the amazing Benedict Cumberbatch plus the revamped plot of it going from a set up to start a war with the klingons to having to take down Khan. Thus was "Star Trek: Into Darkness" and I found it to be excellent. I cannot say the same for this movie. It was disappointing. The "five year mission to explore unknown territory" given to them at the end of "Into Darkness" feels like "to explore repetitive totally known territory." Complete with another "going to start a galactic war" plot, a "were all stranded and have to figure out how to get off this planet" plot, and other general drivel really brought this down. The stakes are also so dumbed down, ok yeah guy is threatening the galactic war but he's not menancing or downright creepy, like either version of Khan (from into darkness or the classic ST2: Wrath Of Khan). And there's no exploration of unknown territory besides a generic looking planet and some different aliens who get more screen time than the ones in prior movies. Who really cares? What would've been better in a run-in with the klingons if they were aiming in the action direction, or dropped this entire script in favor of something, say, more akin to "Star Trek IV: Voyage Home" where the plot was so out there, the movie was calmed down but still suspenseful and well done, taken to the modern day to retrieve humpback whales to save the future when a probe is transmitting a signal only they can respond too. It had many underlying themes, spock wearing a bandana to cover his ears was hysterical. That's the kind of sequel we were promised, and instead, what we got was basically a general episode of the original series, the kind where in 25 minutes, someone would be stranded and saved by the end and move on. Except it's just as long as Into Darkness! Watch it only if you like the new cast and don't mind if it's sub-par or just wanna go with the fact this is going to be the "ok/passable" sequel and that "Star Trek 4" of this new franchise will be the next good one.

history.title: My Little Pony: The Movie
history.review_title: Overrated and sub-par compared to most of the what the series has to offer...
history.text: Didn't they spend "years" working on this? This movie was nothing short of a disappointment. Of all the music that's been written for the series, the songs are really not memorable. I somehow ended up distracted during the film hearing "magic inside" when the birds decided to go back to their old ways, as it seemed more fitting and...way better written. Also, the animation "enhancement" really does nothing for the film. It's a little complaint, but true. In all honesty, the giant airships look a bit out of a place. Another problem is the beginning. First Twilight is just being ridiculous again and doesn't seem to be thinking. I get she wants everything to be perfect, but her "request" makes it seem like she hasn't grown a bit since day 1, and her concern has no real humor or feeling because there is literally no issue. Then we get to the film's set up and introduction of a pony with a broken horn. Who wasn't/isn't intrigued by what that means? It goes over so quickly. I get Tempest Shadow had a really easy way to trap powerful ponies, but this was a huge festival. Nobody put up a fight? The amount of spells out there, all the powers character's have, the shear amount that would've not just randomly stood by and did nothing. This movie completely lacks an opening fight scene of any kind, not even a poor struggle, just none at all. A few "out of the way" princesses and it's onto the next scene. And what is up with the "Stitch" goofy sidekick? It's so out of place, Tempest Shadow would've obliterated him way before this movie started. There are also a lot of rather goofy jokes, and not the kind we expect from this series. Not just pinky pie's goofiness or natural humor. There's a lot of out of the blue potty humor, including a litter box joke. This series is SO MUCh better than any of that. Did they just write this to try to appeal to a broader audience, as if 7 seasons, and a spin-off series with actual human girls with 4 movies and many shorts didn't skyrocket this thing to possibly an all time high? As it continues we simply encounter more random characters, such as a cat whom sings a random song-honestly the best in the film because it has a humorous tone, and the character is really the stand out. Ok, Tempest Shadow is whom we want to love villain or not here, but a kind gesture towards someone who never gets such things is shown and continues throughout. It was a good move, but ultimately we have seen way better in just about every 2 part season opener or finale that's had 1/2 the running time and told a story ten times better. We get into what's probably the best part of the film, involving seaponies. So obviously going to sell more toys, and up to this point, one thing interesting is seeing a lot more random species or different ones, but these are ponies, just seaponies. It feels more natural and honestly gets the whole film on a better track. Why didn't they just skip pretty much right to this part is beyond me, leaving about 10 minutes of film to this as they did makes me wonder if they thought cramming every idea (that honestly-all that we see, pass by, goes over in seconds, etc-could've made for an entire season on the show) possible into this film was a good idea. By this point yet another pointless issue has arisen. Only Twilight and Pinkie Pie are actually doing anything. This isn't like the episodes where they teamed up using all their intellect or skills to fight back or to figure out a plan, or recognize they left too much up to Twilight. They just randomly have lines and their dramatic moments and it feels like this film would've been better if everyone but Twilight and Pinkie Pie had gotten captured in order for it to move along more naturally, like how everyone was captured by the changelings and thus discord, starlight glimmer, and Trixie got involved in Season 6's ending. Back to the songs for a moment-they are also easily full length songs, where the series often has beautiful pieces cut down to anywhere from 2-2 1/2 minutes, or shorter. When they were written way better and had meaning. In this movie, they seem to be filler, in a film that could've spent a lot more time developing a coherent adventure instead of padding the run time. The main thing here is Twilight acts really stupid and as a result causes numerous issues. There isn't much tension in her exploding because she did something really dumb (SPOILER: tried to steal what could save them, not actually being kind just distracting others). It comes off really unnatural despite the heat of the moment seeming sad because she was honestly scared as anyone would be. Finally, the movie get's more real tension. We see Tempest Shadow giving Twilight more "yeah you lost" evil speeches. She is really the highlight of the film, you feel she's creepy and you know she's powerful, even if she is answering to someone else. Ultimately we are all so ready for the showdown here, and the only memorable song unleashed also comes out in the form of a misguided villain who only wants what was her's back and doesn't got a clue basically why she should care about destroying a friendship festival, what friends are, etc. The core of the series. "Open Up Your Eyes" is comparable to "this day-aria" not in that it's as good, but that it has that feel except you know this is about a hurt soul and not someone downright evil (like queen crystalis). The storm king doesn't even show up til the last 1/4 of the film, and he basically just spouts about not liking cute things and acting high and mighty typical cartoon villain. They had a chance to do something really creepy here, since he wasn't going to ever be a character in need of friendship or something. He could've been far creepier, at first he had me thinking back to the crystal empire with King Sombra and all that, instead he is a total toss-away joke, and the film knew it. The "save the day" moments come in with easy defeats that could've happened at the beginning of the film while Tempest Shadow is forced to 180 pretty much because the plot is so quickly tossed like that. In the end Tempest Shadow stops being evil though tbh is someone gonna fix her horn? And we have a giant "Sia as a pony" sequence which is something nobody is going to get in 10 years. zzzzzzzzz. All in all, they should've called this "My Generic Little Pony: The Mass Audience Film." I'd reccomend seeing it with low expectations, and enjoy Tempest Shadow. Oh, did I mention Starlight Glimmer isn't even in this movie? So when did this happen exactly? Now, normally I'd give "where does this fit in" a pass, like many anime films for instance, but, 3 seasons later and they can't even include Starlight Glimmer? The end credit's include yet another generic song and clearly was done last with little glimmers of characters not in the film. All in all, this was very dissapointing. And tbh, I watched it online, and I am really glad I didn't pay for a ticket to see this.

history.title: Barbershop: The Next Cut (DVD)
history.review_title: 15 years and they could come with was rehash and political crap...
history.text: I enjoyed the first two installments in this series. The cast is always good, even in this one despite many only making cameos, or not being in it with the time passed, etc. This one doesn't break the series at it's core. Unfortunately, it would seem the writing team knew the characters, but couldn't come up with anything for them to talk about but a bunch of political nonsense. The four 25 minutes of this movie glosses over key plot points like the beauty shop being fused with the barber shop, no development for new characters we want to like, etc. It's like a 25 minute discussion on "what's wrong with the world" except it's even worse than that. We got some indian guy saying "I don't like white people" and nobody even looks at him wierd. We have a guy who was totally ready to cheat on his wife and if he wasn't going to get caught he was going to do it, he even admits he might as well after being accused when nothing had started. This isn't "Barbershop." It doesn't work with the rest of the series in that instead of focusing on the characters and what they feel they need to make it in this world, admidst all the bad, and decisions made "with the best intentions" but not the right ones, is so in the backdrop. I thought it'd be pretty enjoyable to revisit the world made from the first two after so long, literally from my early teens to now my latter 20's. This movie is just not good. It's political speak for 1/2 the runtime and is also an extremely down in the dumps angle they doesn't make for better drama. If they were trying to make it "current" and believable, it goes the total opposite way. And if this is "realistic," than it's pretty pathetic. I'm glad I watched this for free on hulu, paying $4.00 for it would've irritated me. As it is I somehow managed to sit through it despite being pretty done 50 minutes in, it didn't do anything to want me to push it up to 3 stars, so it stays at 2. Why not one? Well, maybe people will go and watch the other two since Ice Cube's star power is clearly not letting up (Ride Along 1 and 2), and it did have stuff in the backdrop. If only they'd put all of that front and center, and made the movie about 20 minutes shorter, it would've been a worthy entry even if the "sell out the shop" angle was also used before. Don't waste your time-Ice Cube fan, looking to see why they made a sequel so many years later, heck tbh I never thought "Barbershop 2" was that great, not in comparison to the original. But this sequel makes it look great. Skip this one unless you can see it for free or a dollar, just for the sake of forming your own opinion. I really hope if they do decide to make another one they skip over washed up storyline and endless political talk.

He puts on a great performance as well as do the joke wanna be's, but they sadly didn't have much to work with due to a lame script and an unimaginative director who's obviously trying to be Luc Besson, the real ORIGINAL FILM director that France has ever turned out. This is a B-movie with an A-status look made with an F-ed up everything, but Mel. It was too short in the long scenes and even shorter in the scenes with a point to make. This is "Film 101" of what NOT to do when making a movie. Even the Michael Parks and William H. Macy parts were a disappointment. history.review_title: Get creepier the more you watch them
history.text: I can't believe that I have never seen any episodes of this show before. Granted a lot of the stories seem made up but even so they can get kind of creepy with their beyond the grave theme. If you are a fan of EC comics from the 1950's these are kind-of a milder journey but still good. The stories remind me of some of the ghost story comic books printed by Dell and DC in the 1960's. Certainly comparable to, if not up to the same quality as "The Twilight Zone". I really enjoy seeing all of the famous stars in their early roles. Cloris Leachman and Louise Fletcher (Nurse Ratched) used to have quite the curvy figure! Who knew? And it's great to see Suzanne Pleshette in one of her early roles. Babes and ghosts, what's not to like?

history.title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers
history.text: The dog with the human face still creeps me out.
Painful to watch.

history.title: Thomas Hart Benton
history.text: One of Ken Burns' first documentaries and it still is the best on Benton. Too bad he doesn't do a series on Eakins, Henri and "the Eight", Benton, and Marsh. I wish I had the connections to do a decent history of the precedents of modern art and art education in America. It is almost as interesting as the paintings. It is amazing how many American painters went over to study in France. Even good-old Robert Beverly Hale hobnobbed with the 1920's crowd in Paris. This video will also give you the basics on the teacher/student relationship of Benton and Pollock. Benton is very underrated and Pollock is very overrated in my opinion. Pollock was mostly a self-destructive drunk who belittled Benton's goodwill. Heck, Benton bailed Pollock out of jail and very often gave him a sanctuary to retreat to. Benton was actually an intellectual who tried to come across as a homespun tough-guy. His Memory needs an upgrade and this is a good start.

history.title: Tucker - The Man and His Dream
history.text: An entertaining look at automotive history. I missed it when it first came out. Glad that Amazon makes it available for those of us without Netflix.

history.title: Risen [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: At this point, any corpse could be the Nazarene
history.text: I was enthralled with this depiction of a Roman Tribune witnessing the origins of Christianity until the cure of the leper. I cannot "white-wash" the suffering of anything as profound as leprosy, especially with a miracle. Why can't people accept that metaphors, allegory, and parables can be their own truth? Other than the leper-cure everything else is first rate, truly inspired film making, even if it came out of Hollywood. Actually it is more of an Anglo-Italian-Spanish production. One of the best Biblical epics ever done. Fundamentalists and Atheists will have trouble with it, the rest of us just wish that we could break bread with Yeshua and enjoy God's blessings.

history.title: Carnival of Souls (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I love the scenes where a sparrow's song brings Mary Henry back from transitioning out of the land of the living. You will never take a simple bird's song for granted again. I know I don't after seeing this film.

history.title: Cutthroat Island [DVD]
history.review_title: Bring on the special features ye, stingy scallywags
history.text: I have wanted to see this for a long time as I missed it when it first came out and avoid watching it when I catch it half-way through on TV. I enjoyed it despite all of the negative reviews it has gathered over the years. Frank Langella steals the show as the villain. My only complaint is the lack of special features. Not even a dialog track with the director... just a trailer. Geena Davis appears to do many of her own stunts and is quite the athlete. Now I understand how she actually thought she could compete in the Olympics in archery.

history.review_title: Break the windows, then try again, then drive through them
history.text: I absolutely loved this movie. Elizabeth Moss, of Mad Men fame is wonderful, as always. The twisted approach of couples therapy via your fantasy date versus your significant other's worst side is nigh profound. My only complaint is that if I had been Ethan I would have busted every dang blanged window in that guest house. And if I couldn't break the glass then I would have gotten the heebie-jeebies out of there!

history.text: This movie is two parts Short Circuit to one part Robocop...both movies that were much more entertaining and believable than Chappie. After the wonderful District 9 and Elysium, I was excited to see Chappie...but it's incredibly weak, especially considering that studio's pedigree. From the AI programmer character to Hugh Jackman's over the top maniacal character, there are too many situations where the viewer has to suspend disbelief. The ending seems tacked on: Chappie is still a "child", yet he miraculously figures out how to transfer peoples brains to a robot's digital hard drive? To top it all off, between the south african accents and synthesized robotic voice, I couldn't understand what most of the actors were saying. Two stars just for the computer graphics.

history.title: The Maze Runner
history.text: If you're gonna title a movie "maze runner", there should be a lot more maze and a lot more running...instead, you get a lot of wall and a lot of walking. The acting is good and the creatures are well done, but the story within this chapter of the series is not very interesting and has no sort of resolution...it's just a blatant setup for a sequel. The entire series may end up being acceptable, but this movie, alone, is weak...I wont mind skipping the sequel.

history.title: The Divergent Series: Insurgent
history.text: Better than the first movie (Divergent), imo, because this one has many more sci-fi elements and the CG is more present. Like the first movie in the series, this one is a complete story with a strong resolution...not just a means to a sequel and no resolution (like Maze Runner). One thing that stands out to me is the lead actress is too frail looking for the character. Hard to believe this wimpy looking girl is an elite athlete...lift some weights, woman! It's a good a standalone movie for a series, but people who haven't seen the first move will be confused because they don't re-explain the factions. Also, the sound engineering is poor...there's a lot of whispering so, half the time,I could barely tell what they were saying.

history.review_title: I like this mature Keanu...a lot
history.text: John Wick kept my attention from beginning to end...and that's saying something due to my ADD. There were a few areas I didn't quite understand (coins, hit man hotel, etc), but it's a really good movie, overall. Ever since "Bill and Ted", I never took Keanu seriously...in fact, I haven't paid to see any of his movies since B&T. In "John Wick", Keanu looks exponentially more mature than any of his previous movies both in appearance, stage presence and believably. Based on his performance in this film, I definitely have a new respect for Keanu and will keep watching his material. WARNING: This movie is extremely violent with a lot of people graphically getting their brains blown out. I had a nightmare from watching it.

The 3D is first rate (Pixar quality) and so is the voice acting. However, the story is a kinda wonky...pretty sure 99% of the kids that watch this aren't going to have a clue whats going on (but the movie looks and sounds so good, they wont care).

history.title: The Martian
history.review_title: First decent Ridley Scott movie since Alien
history.text: Nothing not to like in this movie. The story is enjoyable (not predictable, but not convoluted), it's well acted, well directed and the CG is well done. After the god-awful "Prometheus", I had given up on Ridley Scott...but, with "The Martian", he's redeemed his name.

Cute movie that tugged on my emotions...but it lacks the seemingly spontaneous comedy Ellen DeGeneres developed in Finding Nemo. Also, many of events/scenes are so exaggeratedly impossible, I found my suspension of disbelief failing.

history.title: The Boss
history.review_title: starts out funny, but last half not so much
history.text: As far as Melissa McCarthy movies, I'd say it's somewhere in between "Tammy" (1 star) and "The Heat" (5 stars).

history.title: Valerian and the City of A Thousand Planets [DVD + Bluray]
history.text: I expected and received a good story (not too convoluted) and decent acting, but the glorious and practically continuous CGI visuals are what push the rating into the 5 star range. For me, Valerian ranks up there with "The Fifth Element" and "Avatar" and I actually liked it better than the non-original Star Wars movies. Valerian completely satisfied my sci-fi fix, but my friend didn't like it. Still, I think anyone who gives this movie a one star rating is just maliciously skewing the results.

history.title: Léon the Professional (Theatrical and Extended Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Was wondering if anyone would make a Ranzerox movie
history.text: So I just rented Valerian (loved it). Luc Besson directed both movies, so I thought I'd drop a review of The Professional. When I first started watching the movie, I realized the similarity to the "Ranxerox" comics I bought in europe during the early 80s. Besson definitely borrowed the round glasses, the pre-pubescent girlfriend, Gary Oldman's character, the over the top violence, etc from Ranzerox. Great interpretation, anyway, and great casting and story resolution. I'd still like to see a movie version closer to the original Ranzerox series; including the musculature, rampant drugs, punk rockers, hardcore "street-y" homosexuals, futuristic setting, etc. With CGI as developed as it is, it shouldn't that much of a stretch to bring a fantastic version Ranzerox's cyborg character to the screen.
