history.title: Interstellar (Blu-ray + DVD Combo Pack)
history.review_title: competently produced science fiction film but not the 2001 of this generation. (This review has spoilers)
history.text: I wanted to be blown away by this film but it simply wasn't to be. Perhaps I simply allowed myself to get caught up in the hype and overblown expectations. It has plenty going for it theoretically. big name director, well known physicist as a science consultant, decent enough actors, big budget and yet... It has impressive visuals but it feels like the story doesn't quite know where to go. Is the point that man must evolve to go off world or evolve to find other planets upon which to live? were the 5th dimensionals aliens or future humans? Other parts of the story also didn't make much sense. For somebody that grew up when the space race was still 'a thing' I was hoping to see a story about mankind's resourcefulness and desire to explore. I wanted a film that showed the development of practical interstellar travel by present human ingenuity and the first such voyage to another star and the adventure that would ensue. Instead, in this future, it turns out that mankind has abandoned the desire to pursue science and engineering due to an environmental collapse and the politically-correct socialistic group-think types have taken over and believe that the moon landing was capitalist propaganda.wonderful. To top it off the instellar part is thanks to a deus ex machina wormhole that shows up with no apparent explanation - and nobody really cares to ask why. But here is the part of the film that ultimately sunk it in my eyes: So here we are (once again) with the typical American trope of a kid growing up resenting their parent because said parent promised them something that they ultimately failed to deliver. It doesn't matter that any reasonable person once becoming an adult would realize that the promise their parent made was completely beyond their ability to guarantee. It doesn't matter that this parent was knowingly risking life and limb on a mission that might save not only the future of the entire race but the child's own personal future as well - pretty much the definition of the word 'hero'. oh no. we have to be mad at daddy because he couldn't buy you a pony for christmas or whatever. The worst part is that after all that heartache he comes back decades in the future and gets laughed at by the medics because he thought they named the space station after him. Hello. The guy just traversed time and space. Back from a suicide mission. Decades in the future. He didn't age. And they treat him like he's some dumb no-nothing shmuck from the boonies. Seriously? To top it off he finally gets to see his now aged daughter...and she totally blows him off...and all of these descendants of his that are around her - have absolutely no reaction to the guy! Anyway, like the title states, it's competently made even if the story isn't quite there and it's still enjoyable such that i would recommend someone watch it, if they hadn't already seen it. The banter with the robots was enjoyable - in some ways they were the most interesting and most developed characters in the film.

history.text: I feel like I wasted my time with this series. Watching the final season became a chore predicated only on the fact that I had already invested so much time into it that I felt i had to see it to the end. There was also the blind hope that maybe - just maybe - the show might actually fulfill its potential. Unfortunately it never did. The depiction of resistance against alien invaders is simply a cartoon version of war. Too many tricks and gimmicks and plot twists that made no sense all the way up to the finale. There was a lot of filler and dead time (which is terrible considering these seasons had only about 10 episodes a piece). It's a shame because I did like Noah Wyle in his role....

history.title: The Huntsman: Winter's War [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: If you are a fantasy fan then you might enjoy this film but on the whole I found it ...
history.text: At least they left Kristen Stewart out of it. People also seem to make a big noise about Charlize Theron but I just don't see why. She has a tendency to overact and really let's it go in the few scenes she has in this film. The other main players do well enough. If you are a fantasy fan then you might enjoy this film but on the whole I found it to be surprisingly dull.

history.title: Gods Of Egypt [Bluray + Digital HD]
history.review_title: Ignore the race police and just enjoy it for what it is.
history.text: This film had a unique visual and imaginative style that I enjoyed quite a bit. Sure the overall story was simple and generally predictable but it was still fun. All of the actors did a decent job with their roles. It's a shame that this film won't get a sequel thanks in part to the now never ending onslaught of the race baiters and PC Police.... Just in case it wasn't clear - this film is a fantasy based on concepts from the Egyptian pantheon - not a treatise on the life and times of tutanhkamen. The outrage directed at this movie over its perceived lack of diversity is the real outrage. No 'diversity'? Let's see: Chadwick Boseman (Thoth) - Black man Elodie Yung - (Hathor) - Half Cambodian and half French (presumably caucasian) Courtney Eaton - (Zaya) - Caucasian, Chinese and Maori descent. Yaya Deng ( Astarte ) - black woman Apparently this isn't sufficient for those keeping the books on 'diversity.' Oh well, I suspect such people would never be pleased regardless.

history.review_title: Both a sci-fi show and a documentary but does not shine in either role
history.text: The intermix of sci-fi and documentary elements is a fairly jarring melange of styles. The documentary parts don't offer very much that a space enthusiast doesn't already know so I found myself skipping those after the first few episodes. The documentary portions suffer from the same superficial style and content that plagues most of the documentaries featured on the science popularizer channels like Discovery, Science, National Geographic etc. in that they don't really offer anything new or compelling to the space enthusiast. The drama portion has a few highlights but falls flat overall with some very dry main characters and a lot of talking heads in monotone narration. Hopefully they focus a bit more on the drama and less on the retread documentary aspect for season 2.

history.review_title: Great atmosphere and sense of mystery!
history.text: A very intriguing start for a much needed original science fiction show - especially one that touches on spirituality in some form. The spooky and tense atmosphere is a nice switch from the usual fare and it reminds me of the series 'Outcasts' from a number of years ago (which sadly was cancelled far too soon). Amazon, please give this series the green light!

history.title: Brimstone [Blu-ray]
history.text: This film depicts violence and brutality to a level that goes beyond what is necessary to get any sort of larger point across; it seems more voyeuristic than anything else. From some online articles one gets the impression that the director and cast want this film to be seen as making a commentary on abuse against women and religious fundamentalism. I'm not sure what point they are trying to make. Do we really need to be shown the graphic flogging of a 5 year old girl after already having sat through numerous beatings, torturous killings, patricide, incestuous child abuse, tongues being cut and the murder of a child?

history.review_title: A mediocre Spacemonster movie with a twist ending that you can see from a mile away.
history.text: This is not a bad film, but it isn't an especially great one either. This is essentially an updated version of a 1950's 'monster from space' B-Movie ; one with modern A-grade effects work. Many have compared it to Alien which I suppose is valid but it doesn't provide the tension of that earlier film. Sadly there is nothing really unique here and even the 'twist' ending was easily intuited. Much of the plot is driven by character decisions and reactions that make no sense for a presumably highly trained crew entrusted with investigating the first known sample of extraterrestrial life. Examples include: There is no proper isolation of the organism. There is no emergency sterilization equipment for potentially infectious or hazardous organisms. Some characters at first care about quarantine and exposure and then alternately don't care about it. The ability to jettison such an organism out into space relies on a soyuz capsule that needs to be launched only after an emergency situation arises. Hopefully NASA and ESA are better than this in real life. All that said, if you just enjoy it as a popcorn monster movie then this film is can be enjoyable as a Saturday afternoon diversion.

history.title: It Came from Outer Space [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A great film that is not given the treatment it deserves.
history.text: This is one of the best science fiction films of the 1950s for it's thoughtful take on a first contact situation that does not ultimately fall prey to the usual bug eyed monster tropes. This one ranks up there with 'This Island Earth' and 'Forbidden Planet' though it is not as widely known as those others (perhaps because it is in black and white?) That said the transfer of this film is near appalling. There is far to much graininess and noise in the transfer. There are times where the background shimmers almost like old tv static - i wouldn't be surprised if they simply used the DVD transfer for this.

history.review_title: Just a Dull Mess of a Film
history.text: As huge fan of 80's slasher movies, "The Forest" was one I had never seen. I vividly remember the box art sitting on my local video store shelves, but just never bothered to rent it. I actually purchased this DVD a handful of years ago, but it just sat on my shelf until this past weekend when I finally decided to give it a view. I should have kept it on the shelf. "The Forest" is the usual, crazed killer stalking campers storyline you've seen before. This time they throw in a twist that there are ghosts tossed into the mix. Not for additional scares, they just provide additional exposition and backstory. There honestly isn't anything to recommend about this title. The score is okay, and the setting is great. You really wish that a good film had utilized this shooting location as it's beautiful, but the direction fails to really capture it fully. The acting is awful, the kills are tame, and it doesn't help that the killer looks like George Lucas?? Just a dull mess. Pass this one up.

history.title: The Guest [Blu-ray]
history.text: "The Guest" if a fun thriller, and even when you think you know where it's going, they change things up. "The Guest" takes a bunch of great ideas and tosses them into a blender, so you're never quite sure where it's going next. A family mourning the loss of their son while serving in the Army in the Middle East opens their home to David, a returning soldier and friend of their deceased son. David seems to be very helpful to the family, a shoulder to lean on and helping the family deal with day-to-day problems. But David seems to be hiding something from them. "The Guest" is just a bunch of fun, and try to read as little about the story as possible before viewing. You'll enjoy the film so much more if you just go along for the ride.

history.review_title: Worth a Viewing for Charlize Theron's Performance
history.text: I didn't really know what to expect from "Monster". I knew the story, but wasn't sure how it would play out. Gritty and disturbing like "Henry" or over the top splatter like "Confessions of a Serial Killer". While "Monster" is gritty, it doesn't really focus on the murders, the way the Henry Lee Lucas films did, so it's not nearly as disturbing. Actually "Monster" goes a long way in generating sympathy for Aileen. The film is actually kind of plodding and very slow, but the reason I stayed tuned into the film was the performance by Charlize Theron. After about 5 minutes you completely forget it is Charlize Theron. She becomes Aileen Wuornos. The facial tics, the way she talks, the way she holds her mouth, it's an amazing acting job.

history.title: Battlestar Galactica: The Complete Epic Series [DVD]
history.text: I vividly remember my older brother and I watching "Battlestar Galactica" when it originally ran, and we loved it. Children of the 70's and 80's we cut our teeth on "Star Trek" and "Star Wars", and to us, this was the weekly version of "Star Wars". The Cylons were the perfect blend of scary and flat out cool. The Galactica looked awesome, and the Vipers were just awesome. Running just 24 "episodes", the original series explored some cool ideas, and featured cutting edge special F/X for the time. It created heroes with "Starbuck", "Boomer" and "Apollo", and who didn't want a wise leader like Lorne Greene's "Adama"? And as cool as the heroes were, the villains were even better. The Cyclops-like electric eyed Cylons with their robotized vocals, and the evil human turn-coat Baltar, plus assorted other villains introduced throughout the show, kept me glued to the screen. I was a bit worried about re-visiting the show, as I had such wonderful memories of it from childhood, I hoped it would "hold up" to my adult viewing. It does. While a lot of praise was given to the ideas presented in the 2004 re-boot of "Galactica", quite a few of the ideas were presented here first. Granted, not in the same way, as the original series seemed aimed at a younger audience, but still the seeds were there. If you fondly remember this show, you owe it to yourself to give it a re-visit. If you're only familiar with the rebooted series, give the original a try. Yes, it has it's fair share of cheesiness, but the core of the show is so good, it should just add to the fun.

history.title: Galactica 1980: The Final Season
history.review_title: Just Search Out the "Starbuck" Episode, Skip the Rest
history.text: I just finished watching "Battlestar Galactica", and wanted to watch the further adventures of the crew I had grown to love. What a mistake!! "Galactica 1980" is just awful. Almost every choice made is not only the wrong one, but it's completely toxic. The Cylons couldn't have conceived a more diabolical plan to destroy "Galactica" than this show. While I would say the original "Battlestar Galactica" aimed at capturing the young fans of "Star Wars", I honestly don't know who "Galactica 1980" was aimed for? "Galactica 1980" finds the Battlestar orbiting Earth, but fearing that they've lead the Cylons to the small planet they want to avoid being detected, so they send down Dick Van Dyke's son and the guy from "Adam12" to get into wacky adventures with flying motorcycles. Yes...really. Toss in some super kids that pop in and out of several episodes and this show is just a mess. To make it worse they aren't even stand-alone episodes, it's like a series of 3 episode story arcs. Almost everything fans of the original series enjoyed is absent from the new show. I will say that the only redeeming episode of this show is the final episode where we discover the fate of "Starbuck" from the original series. But you don't need to watch the proceeding 9 episodes to enjoy that single show, so bypass picking up the entire series, and just seek out "The Return of Starbuck".

"Fear Inc" has a neat premise, but the film is an utter failure. Four friends are getting together for a Halloween weekend, when one of them contacts a company called "Fear Inc.". The purpose of "Fear Inc." is to let people face their biggest fears (which apparently means being chased by robed people wearing Greek theater masks?). As the terror is amped up, the group begin to question whether the events occurring are real or part of the company's service. The filmmakers try to blend humor and horror, and it just doesn't work, mainly because neither the humor or the horror is very good. As a fan of "Raising Hope", I enjoy Lucas Neff, and was interested to see what he would bring to the table. Unfortunately....not much. You have four people pushing 40 still trying to act like they're in their early 20's, and dropping movie quotes and "jokes" about genre films. "Fear Inc." thinks it more clever than it is, and you'll find yourself board. Worse, when they start dropping famous horror movie quotes, it just makes you wish you were watching one of those films instead. Dull film, that tries to patch together things which worked in much better movies. Re-watch "Scream" instead.

I just happened to stumble across this title on Prime, and saw Patrick Stewart and Anton Yelchin were part of the cast. As a big fan of "Star Trek" I had to give this a view. I went in without knowing anything about the story, and while not what I was expecting, found it very enjoyable. A punk band is on the last legs of a faltering "tour", having just played at a Mexican Food restaurant, they manage to land a gig at an out of the way club in Oregon. When they arrive at the club, they find that it's a bar for Skinheads. They decide to play the gig, grab the dough and get out, but once inside, one of the band members witnesses a murder. Pretty intense film, with a top-notch cast. The suspense really gets ratcheted up as the film unfolds. If you're a horror fan, this one is worth checking out.

history.title: Planet of the Apes - The Legacy Collection
history.review_title: Worth the Price for the First Film Alone
history.text: The original "Planet of the Apes" is a landmark film, and deserves to be part of any film collector's library. Sure, the story is so well known now, that the "twist" ending was spoiled even by the film's VHS box art back in the 80's. Re-watching the original film last night, knowing the ending, I have to say that it really doesn't matter. The story, the acting, the make-up, the characters, everything just clicks in this film, and you'll find yourself caught up in film. The other films in the set, provides some additional high moments; "Escape from the Planet of the Apes" and "Battle for the Planet of the Apes" as well as some low points; "Beneath the Planet of the Apes". In reality, just consider the additional films in the series as excellent "bonus" material to the original film. Nothing on the set compares to the original movie, but there is something to enjoy about each.

history.review_title: Just an Awful Film, So Dull it Makes "Unfriended" Look Good
history.text: Phew, this one stinks. I rented it from Prime so felt compelled to watch it to the end, but there is honestly NOTHING to recommend about this film. Horribly acted, horrible direction, (was there a score?) forgettable music, and just an awful story. If you're looking for something with even an eyelash worth of horror, please pick something else. The movie actually starts with some promise as some nutter goes around his neighborhood shooting people with a shotgun (in a completely bloodless way?). I was pulled right in...and then right out again as we meet three college friends renting a spooky old house. When one of the boring trio finds "The Bye Bye Man" written in the bottom of a nightstand drawer the "horror" begins. Don't worry, I hate spoilers, so I won't get into any detail, needless to say the tag line from the film is more than appropriate for anyone thinking of watching this movie "Don't Think It. Don't Say It" just turn away and watch something else.

history.title: Poltergeist [Blu-ray]
history.text: The "Poltergeist" remake fails on almost every level. I'm not anti-remake, so long as the people crafting the film have something new to say on a familiar story (Rob Zombie's "Halloween"), or want to pay homage to classic by updating the story while remaining true to the spirit of the original (John Carpenter's "The Thing"), but "Poltergeist" is completely pointless. As the film starts we meet a family moving into their new home, apparently a step down as the father is now unemployed, the mother is a wannabe author who doesn't write. So they have no income coming in, but are purchasing as house? We soon learn that the family is swimming in debt, credit cards are maxed (which is the true horror of the film), and there's some funky stuff happening in the youngest daughter's room. It's not long before the tiny tyke is talking and touching hands to the TV (now a flatscreen, but still showing static). I won't go into spoilers in case someone out there still wants to subject themselves to this movie (don't), but from there the remake hits most of the same beats as the original. There are so many problems with this film, not the least of which is that this family is TOXIC. I have liked Sam Rockwell since watching him in "Clownhouse", and this is the first film where it felt like he was just phoning it in. You don't really care what happens to these people because you don't like any of them. But the biggest failing of the movie is that lacks scares and suspense. This is a movie made by committee, and you can just see them checking off the boxes; the original did this, so we'll do it too, here mix in some "Paranormal Activity" and some found footage stuff to keep it current, and boom cookie-cutter, soulless entertainment. Just avoid this and re-watch the original.

The movie that answers the question for the ages: "What if Robin Sparkles had taken time off from cheesy music videos and sexually suggestive kids shows to make a movie!?" If you're of the "so bad it's good" philosophy, then this is a prime candidate. Otherwise it's just bad. Very, very bad. If you get the "How I Met Your Mother" reference, you might actually get a laugh out of this movie. After watching this movie (in fast forward obviously) I can only assume that Robin Sparkles and Jessica Glitter were based on Dru-Anne Perry and Gina Calabrese.

history.title: Passengers
history.text: I loved this movie because it is a sci-fi movie with high production values, two main actors that I really like, and two supporting actors that I really like, and because it was (sort of) romantic without being too over the top. But what really intrigued me about the movie was the underlying question of the morality of what the male lead did. Obviously it was bad, but just HOW bad. Where does it fall on the scale between really bad practical joke and murder?

history.title: Arrival [Blu-ray]
history.text: Amy Adams did a fantastic job as did Jeremy Renner. The story is very thought provoking. I confess I didn't actually figure out what was going on with the weird flashbacks until close to the end of the movie, but I loved it once I figured it out. I don't really buy the "aliens existing outside of the constraints of time" thing, but maybe that's because, as a Christian, that's essentially how we think of God. (Having created time, He exists outside of time.) But the exploration of the concept is certainly more entertaining in this setting. I also ABSOLUTELY LOVE the alien design. Virtually every creature on earth exhibits (external) bilateral or radial symmetry. I keep waiting for some adventurous designer to think outside the box and make a sentient life form without bilateral (or radial) symmetry. This one doesn't quite go outside the box, but it certainly gets close to the wall. I personally would have enjoyed a little more exploration of how they figured out the linguistics, but I suspect they would have lost a lot of the audience in so doing.

history.title: Live Die Repeat: Edge of Tomorrow
history.review_title: This Movie Didn't Get Nearly Enough Attention [Mild SPOILERS]
history.text: Great movie. I'm a big Sci-Fi fan and Tom Cruise fan (the actor, not the Scientologist) so maybe I'm a little biased. Like Oblivion, I always appreciate a high production value Sci-Fi movie, and Tom Cruise as the lead is icing on the cake. Usually, I'm not a big fan of time travel - time shifting - sort of movies, but this one (along with Arrival) is a definite exception to that rule. I also really appreciated the humor involved in his predicament, particularly when Emily Blunt's character almost shoots him in the head (for the umpteenth time) AFTER he has lost his reset button. EDIT: Sorry. I think she actually tries to STAB him, not shoot him.

history.title: Jack Reacher: Never Go Back
history.review_title: Um.... The First Jack Reacher Movie Was Great!
history.text: The producers should have taken their own advice from the title. This movie was pretty disappointing compared to the first one. Of course that statement applies to the vast majority of sequels. Even so, it wasn't awful, it was just... forgettable. UPDATE: I think one of the things that just kills this movie is the casting of Cobie Smulders as the female lead. Don't get me wrong, I loved her in the series "How I Met Your Mother", but that's part of the problem. I don't know if it's her acting or just my perspective, but in just about every scene I kept expecting her to deliver one of those priceless, unintended punch lines. Unfortunately, Jack Reacher being decidedly NOT that kind of movie, it makes every scene she's in kind of uncomfortable to watch. Add to that the fact that her counterpart in the first Reacher movie was Rosamund Pike and Cobie Smulders just never really had a chance.

history.title: The Magnificent Seven
history.text: Answers the age old question: "Can you really take a bunch of good actors and make a crappy movie?" Yep. Yes you can. Okay, crappy is a bit harsh. But when you start out with a budget busting cast, and some of the best source material around, you better make one heck of a good remake.

history.title: The Imitation Game (Blu-ray + Ultraviolet)
history.review_title: Watched a Movie, Fell Asleep, Woke Up to a Sermon About Not Being Evil to Gay People
history.text: Pretty interesting plot, but it does run on a bit. And then they just couldn't resist the ten minute sermon about how history has been so mean to gays... even the really smart ones! To be fair, it was pretty abominable at times, but I tend to watch movies for their entertainment value rather than their persuasive value. Maybe I'm just weird that way.

history.title: The Martian
history.text: Loved this movie... mostly because of Matt Damon (since he gets about 80% to 90% of the screen time), not because I'm some huge Matt Damon fan, but because his acting was just excellent in this movie in particular. And to be honest, the whole cast was excellent. Kudos to the director. One thing I really love about the movie is that, while the run time is not at all what I'd consider excessive, the story line is pretty epic, as in, it covers a lot of ground with great economy of time and yet doesn't feel rushed. This is just a beautifully made film and at least seems pretty realistic. It isn't one of those films which paints an overly rosy picture of Mars being made habitable. Side note: Personally, I don't think terraforming Mars is physically possible unless we figure out some way of partially melting part of its core. Without a partially fluid metallic core, there's very little magnetosphere to guard from solar winds. Without a fairly decent magnetosphere, most of the atmosphere that is present gets blasted away. So you can make atmospheric gases 'til the cows come home and you're not going to get an atmosphere that hangs around long enough to sustain much of anything. One might argue that you could create an underground ecosystem, but why go 34 million miles to do that when you could do that on the moon (with fairly epic advances in technology at least,) or for that matter, right here on Earth. But I digress. In other words, I like this movie because it has a gripping story line, is a high production value sci-fi movie (which are much too few and far between for my taste), and because, despite it being sci-fi, it doesn't overtax my suspension of disbelief for the most part. And especially because the acting is so darn good.

history.title: Hacksaw Ridge [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital]
history.review_title: My War Film Gore-o-Meter Just Got a New Number.
history.text: Pretty inspiring story. But WOW! They really turned the gore factor up a notch from level 10 (Saving Private Ryan) to 11. Made it actually kind of difficult to watch. Of course I grew up in the late John Wayne era, where many a brave actor fought and died though nary a drop of fake blood was spilled... 'cept maybe a little dribble from the corner of the mouth for the close-ups.

history.review_title: How This Movie is Like Going to a Prostitute
history.text: I suppose it could have been worse. I could be like some of these poor souls who actually read the books and so were somewhat emotionally invested. Stars the perennially meh Brad Johnson and discount Laura Dern (Emily Lloyd). The only actual halfway passable acting in it was Jonathan Cake as Nero. Each of the main characters except for Brad Johnson is some famous historical figure: Alice Liddell (Alice in Wonderland); Nero; Samuel Clemens. Not sure about the African Princess woman, (producers walkin' that fine line between cultural appropriation and full blown racism in that character) or the Nazi death camp NOT survivor (can we fit any more stereotypes in here?) Of particular note, acting-wise is Brian Moore as the alien Monat: His performance is particularly awful for a main character. I want to know why all the people come back with essentially perfect bodies, but the alien gets a perpetual head spasm for no apparent reason. It seems unlikely to be an evolutionary advantage, universal among his species. Whatever. Maybe he was just trying to distract us from the really lame make-up. He's probably one guy who was glad the movie didn't get picked up as a series. Could you imagine going to work every day having to pretend to have Parkinson's disease? That's what he was in for. Pretty much all the other characters just get grunts and grrrs or whimpers and screams depending on whose side they were on. I just watched this movie. It was bad enough that I had managed to block out the fact that I had already seen it a few years ago and didn't remember that fact until about two-thirds of the way through it. The story line actually does seem decent; I might even consider checking out the book series (although I suspect I'll just take a shower and try to block out the whole sad incident from my memory again.) The director has to feel a sense of accomplishment for this made for TV movie though - it seems like he managed to squeeze in every cliche from his list of cheesy movie cliches. Don't watch this movie unless you are craving the loss of two hours of your life followed by a deep sense of regret.

history.title: Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
history.text: This is a nice film that seems to accomplish what it sets out to do, but there are a few flaws. Perhaps it tries to do too much in too little time--the first half of the film feels very fragmented and disjointed. There's very little flow to it, and it sometimes takes a few moments to allow the brain to catch up with sudden shifts in the narrative. I would also agree with other reviewers who are disappointed with what has been left out--there seems to be a fear here of running too long, something that we learned with "Gandhi" isn't a huge problem if you have a truly compelling narrative. And the life of Mandela does provide that. They could easily have given us more details without spoiling the film. That said, it's still a worthwhile film to see.

history.title: Margot At The Wedding
history.text: This was really awful. Like some other reviewers, we kept with it until the end, hoping that something would come of the mess, but it never does. All the reasons for which it's horrible are in the other reviews, so I'll just say that none of the characters are sympathetic, none but Margot and her sister are developed at all (and they're developed poorly), and the cinematography is quite mediocre--some of the scenes are extremely dark and washed out, as if the director and the people on the cameras didn't understand anything about light or lighting while they were filming. All in all, a horrible waste of time.

history.title: Arrested Development: Season 4
history.text: This is an absolute travesty. Everything that made Arrested Development a strong series is gone, and is replaced by weak writing, contrived situations, lame characters, a ridiculous plot, and very weak editing. This last one is probably the biggest disappointment--the editing of the original three seasons was truly inspired, but here it's quite lame and very weak. It's evident from episode one that this is not the AR development of old. The horribly contrived situation of Michael living in his son's dorm and being so completely stupid that he can't see that his son isn't okay with it makes me cringe as a viewer. And when he gets in a public shower with his son when there's a free one right next to it, well, that's just creepy in many, many ways. And the creepy things continue all through the season. We felt dismayed after the first two episodes, but we decided to watch the whole season just to see if things get better. They don't--they actually get worse. This is a complete waste of time and effort and energy and money, and it all leads to one of the most stupid endings that I've ever seen to anything. I think the five-star reviews are from people who were so happy that the show was back that they didn't care about quality, but this is like a long-lost friend coming back into your life, only now he's into drugs and he smells bad and he constantly insults you and calls you names--he's not the same friend you used to have.

history.title: Before I Fall [Blu-ray]
history.text: I was fortunate enough to be able to see this on a plane, so there was no risk of wasting time on a movie I never had heard of before. It starts out a bit slow and seems to be heading in very predictable directions, and for the most part, that's true. In this type of film, the conflicts and opportunities for growth and change are set up very carefully in the first "normal" day, and this film isn't any different from the norm. There are, however, some rather consistent twists and turns that end up making this story different from the norm, and some of the twists work while others do not. The main character's "rebellious" day, for example, plays rather shallowly and annoyingly, though it also provides us with some interesting background that wasn't there before. The main actress (I've forgotten her name) is quite good, and all in all the acting, directing, and camera work are quite strong. The story is good, though again somewhat predictable most of the time. I think the most frustrating thing of the film is that the main character takes a lot of time to catch on to many things, and she seems smarter than that. Perhaps she's not, though. This is a good film and well worth watching.

history.title: Cowboys & Aliens Region Free
history.text: We just watched the Blu-Ray version, and the sound mixing was absolutely horrible--I had to hold the remote the entire movie because when people were talking, I had to turn up the volume, but as soon as any action or music started, it was incredibly loud and I had to turn it down again. While it was a somewhat enjoyable film in many ways and quite entertaining in a mindless way, I probably would go with such a low rating because they've done something that so many others do--they've made the aliens so strong and fast that it's absolutely ridiculous to think that they could be defeated by a ragtag group of outlaws and Apache warriors, along with a guy with a super-weapon on his wrist. It's just silly--you can make aliens strong to make the audience admire the victors for having defeated them, but not so strong that they're practically invincible.

history.title: Gattaca
history.text: This is an extremely slow-moving film that has some interesting moments, but that all in all turns out to be disappointing. It ended up being a very long two hours for very little that was enjoyable.

None of the characters are at all sympathetic, and neither of us watching it cared even the slightest bit for any of them. Simply a bad movie, one to pass on.

history.title: Bandidas
history.text: This was a lot of fun--it's not a great movie, by any means, but everyone involved seems to know that, and they're more interested in making a fun piece of entertainment than trying to create a work of art. And it works. Cruz and Hayek work extremely well together, the plot holds up fairly well, the supporting actors are all decent, and it's a fun way to pass an hour and a half. No one is taking themselves or their roles too seriously, and the result is very enjoyable. So if you want to enjoy the company of two very friendly ladies who are very good actresses, this is a good film to watch.

history.title: Modern Family: Season 9
history.text: Okay, so it's over. The last couple of seasons have demonstrated significantly diminishing quality, but this one is a pretty bad season by any standards. Especially poor are the scripts, which force the characters into some pretty stupid situations, which forces the actors to overcompensate, trying to make something stupid seem realistic. All in all, a huge disappointment--the actors are still good enough that if you were to get some fresh scriptwriters in there, you could make every season as good as the first. But this is Hollywood, I guess, so they'll just let it die a pitiful death several years after it should have been cancelled or improved.

history.title: The Revenant
history.text: In this film we have disjointed nonsense hung upon the framework of adventure, something like a drunken housewife hanging laundry all akimbo upon a clothesline. Rarely, expect in B-movies, have I seen so many improbabilities and inconsistencies. Hugh Glass, played by Leonardo DiCaprio, is a scout for a fur trading expedition that ostensibly is organized like a military unit, expect that whenever there is a crisis, anywhere in this film, good military discipline does not prevail. This coincides with left-wing belief systems about the uselessness and ineptitude of anything military, so this worldview is presented to the audience and is nonsense. Here is an example - central to the plot is the conflict between Glass and his antagonist John Fitzgerald (played by Tom Hardy) in which Hardy essentially blames Glass with being a dangerously (even treasonously) incompetent scout. Of course, this charge has to be false to maintain the hero status of the protagonist. In fact Glass's job IS security (and scouting) for the fur trading expedition. While he is away (within hearing distance of a rifle shot) hunting meat for the expedition, the expedition is attacked, and the majority of the party is killed. Straight-forward enough except that in the attack it is clear that the Indians have infiltrated into the treetops the night before, so Glass really is culpable of incompetence (or at least negligence). Later, as Glass leads the survivors of the massacre on an escape route, one morning he again goes out to scout, this time alone, and is almost mortally wounded by a bear. Anybody with any knowledge at all of basic military procedure (or common sense) would understand that for the key leader of the party to be out scouting alone in hostile territory when they know they are being pursued be enemies is ridiculous or utter incompetency. Oh yes, men do get mauled by bears but it becomes a bit more difficult for the bear when there are two or three armed men in the group than one. So really, Glass is an incompetent scout, but in this film he is the hero, and Fitzgerald is the deranged, despicable cad. Then there is the whole business in this film about white race relations with Indians. In this film, everything the white man does to the Indian is bad,, but everything the Indian does to the white man, no matter how barbaric, is neutral at worst, since the white man allegedly deserves what he gets. For this reason, it is "understandable" when blacks kill white cops in our society today, because at the end of the day the cops allegedly deserve it. In short this film serves up a confused mish-mash of politically correct vignettes in the framework of backwoods adventure. And by the way, apparently in the 1820's nobody lived beyond 40 because everyone in this film is 40 years old or younger, much younger, even the senior commanders of the fur trading expedition. This film was targeted at the millennial generation who actually believes the nonsense this film serves up. I gave the film two stars instead of one because the scene where Leonardo DiCaprio gets mauled by a bear is fairly realistic (well done).

history.title: Unknown
history.review_title: Left-winger Neeson Makes Fundamentally Dishonest Film
history.text: Oh yes, this is an adventure film and succeeds pretty well on that score, but if you have critical thinking skills this film is also a stinker. At the core of the plot is the premise that a scientist, described by Neeson's character as a "progressive", has developed, with the financial backing of an Arab sheik (also characterized by Neeson as "progressive"), a strain of corn capable of ending world hunger. He intends to offer it to the world for free, but greedy capitalists want to steal the science and make billions of dollars on it. Now in real life, Neeson is a flaming liberal, so lets examine the film for ideological soundness: 1) How many Arab oil billionaires do you ever hear of that are not greedy capitalists? Anyone ever heard of OPEC, the oil cartel that over the years has tried and succeeded in manipulating the world oil market to it's advantage, bilking working people out of trillions of hard earned dollars? 2.) In light of all the recent mass murders around the globe committed by Islamic terrorists, how likely is it that an Islamic oil sheik wants to feed the world rather than burn it down? It is well documented that Saudi princes fund education in radicalism in mosques all around the world. 3.) If greedy capitalists are so bad, then why didn't the producers of this film donate all proceed to charity, and why didn't Neeson donate his acting so the little guy consumers could get a price break at the box office?

Turns out this flick was made in Norway, by Norwegians, and is a high quality production in every respect, right down to the script. Granted there are some implausible aspects of this film (a unexceptional flashlight operating at length underwater, etc.) but these flaws hardly distract from the overall plausibility of the scenario. A good night's entertainment.

history.title: Shining Through
history.text: Don't be deceived by the positive reviews for this film here and elsewhere. This so-called drama is really a melodrama cum chick flick. Michael Douglas plays Ed Leland, a top level New York lawyer who is also a top level spy for the United States into Germany prior to and during WWII. He holds the rank of colonel. Nevertheless despite his elite education and high rank in the military intelligence, Leland can't read, write or speak German. You know, that's kind of like being Vice President of Ford Motor Company but not knowing how to drive an automobile - happens all the time. Melanie Griffith plays Linda Voss, a kid with no education from the Bronx who has no problem winning the affections of an elite lawyer and colonel in the armed forces. This kind of thing, too, happens all the time. Leland agrees to use Voss, who DOES speak German, in an covert operation into Germany to uncover the plans for the V-2 Rocket. Since in real life, Germany managed to launch over 3,000 V-2 rockets against the Allies, it is hard to see what Voss's penetration into Germany accomplished, even in fiction. Other incredible aspects of this film include Voss running through the deserted streets of Berlin at night in a full length formal evening gown,pursued by the S.S. and somehow escaping their detection. I live in a small town in the American Midwest and I couldn't escape detection from the police, let alone and elite military unit, if I was fleeing in blue jeans in the streets. Also at the very end of the movie it falls upon Leland to get himself, who can't speak German, without proper papers, and an unconscious Voss across the Swiss border at a regular German-patrolled border crossing. Another example of stuff depicted in this movie that happens all the time.

history.title: Arrival
history.text: Amy Adams plays the part of a linguist enlisted by the military to establish communication with space aliens, whom they fear may have hostile intent towards earth and her inhabitants. This film is deeply flawed in multiple respects: 1.) It has poor quality sound quality, ironic in a film whose plot is about good communication. 2.) The chief protagonist, our linguist, plays a cliché - the ubiquitous ( in Hollywood movies) single mom. Hollywood disdains to cast its heroines in any way dependent on a man; nevertheless there is always a child. Scriptwriters haven't yet crafted a way to get a woman pregnant without a sperm donor. 3.) Midway through the film the heroine's patient endeavors to find common ground with the aliens is nearly terminated, catastrophically, by soldiers who've been incited to violence by right-wing talk radio. It so happens I viewed this film one week after a real-to-life hard core left-winger, apparently incited by rampant anti-Trump hysteria in the mainstream media, and carrying a list of conservative Republicans in his pocket, opened fire on those same Republicans at a baseball practice for a charity fundraiser. Too bad Hollywood drama doesn't imitate reality a little more accurately. 4.) Now, Jeremy Renner plays a lesser protagonist - a scientist preoccupied with mastery of time through faster-than-light space travel. Never mind that in reality a particle has been discovered to travel faster than light, putting the kibosh on that nonsense. No, we have to endure a subplot about time travel because Hollywood types need to fantasize about living forever, and therefore escaping eternal damnation. And never mind that someone alive today, whom we can all befriend, with whom we all can communicate in any language, has total mastery over time and is willing to share that mastery with us - namely, Jesus Christ. Not too many Hollywood types are making movies about HIM.

history.title: Sleuth
history.text: This is a good movie, fun mystery, well acted. One needs to keep in mind the time at which this film was made - 1972. Social upheavals were rocking the West and this film reflects those upheavals. Laurence Olivier plays Andrew Wyke a species of man - an English country squire - that was in the crosshairs of angry socialists in the early 1970's, so in this film he is a target. Michael Caine plays Milo Tindle, a hairdresser embracing the casual social norms of his young, new, generation, and he pays a price for his nonchalance. In short you can't just watch the film for the mystery aspects; to understand it you have to have some understanding of what was going on in Western Civilization in 1972 - free love, long hair, bell bottoms, getting high, etc.

history.title: White Comanche
history.text: Over the years, William Shatner has become something of a phenomenon, and WHITE COMANCHE proves that the process started long ago. Here, the larger-than-life slice of Canadian bacon, on hiatus from STAR TREK, plays a dual role; Jeff Moon, a cowboy type who wears denim, boots, a Stetson, and a Captain Kirk haircut. Jeff, a half-breed, is constantly in the soup with just about everyone due to the shenanigans of his near-(their eyes are different colors) identical twin, Notah, a wild Comanche type who sports moccasins, a bare chest, war-paint, a headband and....a Captain Kirk haircut. Notah eats peyote, goes on rape/pillage/plunder sprees, and disappears into the hills, leaving Jeff to nearly get lynched. After a bit of this, Jeff gets tired of it, and decides to go after his psychedelically psychotic sibling. Joseph Cotton, looking somewhat in his cups, plays a sheriff, while a clowder of Spanish and Italian actors make up the rest of the cast. Shatner X 2 are in rare form, licking the paint off the flats like nobody's business; the two of them together are a near-meltdown. The music score alone is nearly worth the purchase price. For fans of drive-in brain-munchies, WHITE COMANCHE is primo.

As other reviews have noted, Garth is sent back in time to stop mind-control experiments which will aid the rise of a totalitarian world government. Nothing new here, but this is a fun flick, nonetheless. The mid-60's sci-fi sets, the technobabble, Mr. Rennie's stoic delivery, the two cyber-cops chasing him in their silver go-go boots, green jumpsuits, motorcycle helmets, and big clunky wristwatches that they stare at while they jog in step. As with many reviewers, I first saw CYBORG 2087 on a local Friday night monster movie show in the 70's. Buying a copy for your collection would be a good move.

history.title: Billy the Kid Versus Dracula
history.text: The late John Carradine, when asked what was the worst film he'd ever made, would often cite BILLY THE KID VS. DRACULA. Personally, I disagree (4-X, THE WIZARD OF MARS), But I can certainly understand the sentiment. The appropriately named Cheesy Flicks released this DVD, and it certainly is such; indeed, one of the classics of American cine-cheese. The imfamous William "One Take" Beaudine directed this horror western,with his usual stingy budget and thorough disregard for cinematic quality. John Carradine is in full turbo mode, playing the vampire (who, BTW, is never referred to as "Dracula"), bugging his eyes, rolling his R's, and chewing necks and scenery. The rest of the cast are pretty much holes in the screen, but they add to the fun in their own way. If you're a fan of Cinema Terrible, this film deserves a place of honor on your shelf.

history.review_title: A SHADOW OF ITS FORMER SELF
history.text: I didn't see this film theatrically in '94, based on the negative feedback I'd heard from friends who did see it. I ordered a copy from Amazon a week ago, and watched this evening, figuring it couldn't be THAT bad. Well, it wasn't....but it wasn't great, either. I guess it's tempting for writers and directors these days to try and jazz up popular, established characters to appeal to the nano-attention span audiences of the past thirty years, but it always winds up distorting and cheapening the mythos. The period look of the film is a plus, but the story? Why would Lamont Cranston be a warlord in Tibet? Since when is the Police Commissioner Lamont's uncle? There's a lot of these canonical hiccups in THE SHADOW, and they make as much sense as Superman knocking up Lois Lane and leaving the planet, Johnny Storm being black, or Lt. Sulu being homosexual. Three stars for the look and the atmosphere.

history.title: Pompeii
history.text: It never ceases to amaze me how the folks who make movies can take something completely fascinating from history and turn it into something either boring ("Troy"), stupid ("Gladiator"), or, in the case of this piece of silliness, downright painful. This movie is simply a comic book, and full of errors, some of which are howlers. The first of these is when the female love interest comes home to Pompeii from a year in Rome, which is to the north. As she was going south, and as Pompeii was on the west coast of Italy, the sea would be on her right. Not in this movie. In this movie, the sea is on her left so you can look at her wagon entering the town with Mt. Vesuvius (to the north of Pompeii) looming overhead. Geography? We don't need no stinking geography! Next, we have the slave who says "Okay" - not a word used in ancient Rome as far as I know. At that point in the film I was desperately trying to suspend my disbelief, but hearing an American colloquialism took care of that. You might as well have had two people greet each other by saying "Whassup?". Virtually every aspect of gladiatorial combat shown is incorrect, and, believe it or not, the director got pretty much the entire volcanic eruption wrong. When Vesuvius buried Pompeii, there was no lava, there were no fireballs, there was no massive earthquake that destroyed the arena, and there was no tsunami, all of which appear in the movie. Oh, and in the never-happened massive earthquake, Pompeii's gladiator arena did not collapse. I'm pretty sure of this, as I've been there and stood in it. Quite simply, the director transplanted the special effects from "2012" and put them in Pompeii, and incorrectly at that. I gave this movie one star based on the one aspect of it that was not only cool, but very accurate. The computer graphics showing Pompeii from the air were extremely well done, and gave a very good sense of what the place would have looked like. These shots take up perhaps thirty seconds of the movie. As for the rest - ouch! Update - I've tried to sell this to two used-DVD stores in the Los Angeles area. Neither one would take it. Again, ouch!

history.title: The Class
history.review_title: Very Good - Could Have Been Just a Bit Better
history.text: I teach 7th-graders from a poor neighborhood in a large American city, so I had a great interest in this film. I enjoyed the approach of the film makers to the subject matter, and appreciated that there are more similarities than differences between the American and French public school systems. I thought it was an effective film, and at various moments my heart ached for both the teachers and the students. That said, I did have a couple of problems. First, all of the students I saw in the film were, for lack of a better word, redeemable, even if they had issues. The violent incident in the classroom came about accidentally, and the other students themselves had sympathy for the perpetrator. There wasn't a single "bad" kid in this film. Given my own experience, I found this unrealistic. The sad truth is that by middle school, some children who have insufficient or poor adult influences are well on the way to becoming bad people. The lack of any really awful behavior also leads directly to my second quibble, which has to do with the scene in the teachers' lounge where a male faculty member practically has a nervous breakdown because his students are so horrible he describes them as acting like animals. The teacher's rant is spot on, but the student behavior I saw in the film doesn't even amount to a difficult day in the world in which I teach. In order for me to understand why this guy loses it so badly, I needed to see what he was talking about. I never did. Not even close. There are classroom fistfights in my world, and teachers are cussed out by 12-year-olds in the vilest possible language on a fairly regular basis. Their parents or guardians are sometimes impossible to reach, and some of them are unable or unwilling to be supportive of the children they made. This is a good and valuable film, and I recommend it. Then, for a reality check, I would recommend doing a week's worth of volunteer work at an inner-city secondary school.

history.title: Castle
history.review_title: Very Dated - Needs to be Redone
history.text: This DVD fits right into my curriculum as a 7th-grade teacher of History in California. The subject matter was very interesting to me as I grew up, and I had high hopes that this DVD would prove of value to my 12 & 13 year-old students. I was mistaken. According to their feedback, this DVD is slow, interesting only in small portions, and hard to hear. As the adult in the room, I'll address all three points my students made. First, the production values are pretty poor for this day and age, and the DVD is in fact difficult to hear. An option for subtitles would be a great help, but this DVD does not have that feature. The animated portion of the DVD is also pretty primitive, closer to South Park than Warner Brothers. I also have observed that for a contemporary audience of adolescents, the formula of Mr. Macaulay ambling around exchanging pearls of wisdom with a female counterpart is largely a non-starter. My audience would be much more interested if Macaulay were talking to a 12-year-old, or a group of them. A female partner would then be most welcome, as the role of women of all social levels could be better dealt with. At this point I'm running the risk of criticizing this DVD for wishing it were something else, so I'll stop. In conclusion, if you are a parent of literate, inquisitive children and want to show this to them at home, I believe it would work. If, however, you are a teacher and are looking for something to use in your classroom, my advice is to preview it first and to show only segments that you think might be of high interest (The garderobe, for example.). The production faults are the same for Macaulay's DVD "Cathedral", and his female sidekick in that one also has a French accent that has been difficult for my students to understand. "Roman City" works somewhat better in terms of the information presented, but the animated portion is so exaggeratedly cartoonish that it undermines the DVD as a whole. The material on all three DVDs is valuable, and could be presented in a much better way for public school students. I wish all three would be updated to do this.

history.title: The First Grader
history.text: This film tells a remarkable story, but oversimplifies it to the point of misinforming. The protagonist, Kimani Maruge, became famous for being the oldest person to enter primary school. He did so at the age of eighty-four, when the Kenyan government declared a policy of free education for all. He faced adversity in continuing his studies, but overcame it. Eventually his story went international and he spoke to the U.N. about the importance of literacy and education. In his earlier life, Maruge had been a member of the Mau Mau, the group of Kenyans (Mostly from the Kikuyu tribe.) who fought to force the British to leave Kenya. He was captured by the British, and tortured in their now notorious (And rightly so.) concentration camps. In the end, he and other survivors of those camps received compensation from the Kenyan government. That's the story the film tells, and it is genuinely inspiring. However, as films about actual events often do, this story is made simple in order to create a two-dimensional "feel good" movie. Here are some examples, all of which are shown through flashbacks of Maruge's days in the Mau Mau. The scene in which Maruge will take the Mau Mau oath shows a number of native Kenyans out in the country with a goat. The scene is quite pastoral. It is clear something important is about to happen, but the film doesn't show it. An adult might guess that the goat will be killed, but younger audience members will not. In actuality, the goat was going to be slowly tortured to death, with one bone at a time being broken with a club. While the goat was being slowly and horribly put to death, the oath-takers would state that if they ever broke their oath, the fate of the goat would be their fate as well. The whole point of a Mau Mau oath was to awe the oath-takers with its brutality. That scene might have made us less sympathetic to Maruge and the Mau Mau, so it was left out. The scene in which Maruge and other Mau Mau steal guns from a white Kenyan's farm shows several unarmed Mau Mau quietly sneaking into a house to find the guns. They do so, and while some run with the guns, we briefly see one of them hitting a white farmer with his fists. In reality, the Mau Mau weapon of choice was the machete, and they on at least one occasion hacked an entire family to death, including their children, one as young as six years of age. Clearly you wouldn't want such a scene in a feel-good movie. As Mark Twain said, "Never let the truth get in the way of a good story." Maruge's wife and child are murdered by soldiers of the King's African Rifles at the order of a British officer. Without actually showing the murder, the scene quite effectively portrays the well documented cruelty of the British in dealing with the Mau Mau and their suspected supporters. During the film Maruge mentions that he had a wife and child. In actuality, Maruge had more than one wife and fathered fifteen children, five of whom survived. He was actually enrolled in the same school as two of his grandchildren. By distorting the truth of Maruge's family, the film-makers once again cheated the audience. I think Kimani Maruge's story is an important and inspirational one. I would like to have seen him written and portrayed as a three-dimensional person. By simplifying his story to the point of two-dimensionality, the film-makers have deliberately dumbed it down as though the intended audience couldn't handle complexity. I'm sorry they did so.

history.title: Day of the Siege
history.text: This movie is a mess. In short, it takes one of the most interesting, important battles of post-medieval history and turns it into a tedious bore. There are some good actors in this film who simply can't rise above some of the worst dialogue ever committed to film. Some very interesting "real people" are left out so the film can be populated with more boring fictitious people. Much of the dialogue, most notably in the battle scenes appears to have been dubbed in later, by the same actors saying the same things. For instance, in one of the attacks, as you watch the Turks charge, you hear a voice yelling something like, "Quickly, quickly, out of the trench!" Ten seconds later, as you watch the Viennese defenders, you hear the same voice yelling something like, "Quickly, everyone, to the walls!" Same guy, on both sides. Laughable. The battle scenes, which could have been spectacular, are amateurishly put together, and the best part of the film is the end, which is at least based loosely on something that really happened. Skip this mess and read "The Enemy at the Gate", by Andrew Wheatcroft, for a much more exciting and involving account of the Siege of Vienna.

history.title: Last Kingdom, The
history.review_title: Happy to be Able to See This - Could Have Been Better
history.text: I've been hoping for this series for a long time - ever since the History Channel gave us their wretched "Vikings" series, to be exact. And now that it's here, I do like it, even though I think it could have been better. The good - By and large, I think the performances range from good to superb. King Alfred is particularly well drawn, as are some of the Danish adversaries and Father Beocca. The production values are excellent, and the show gets a lot of bang for the buck out of what I've read was a fairly low budget. The writing, based on some of the most vivid historical novels I've read, gets high marks from me as well. It's also beautifully filmed, with excellent, though infrequent, use of color. The not-so-good - I'm not at all drawn to Uhtred, the main character, and find myself wondering why the show cast the particular actor it chose. This series depends on Uhtred to move it forward, and there is more than one ensemble scene in which virtually everyone else involved is more compelling. It's a problem. Also, the contrast between the Danes and the Saxons is not as keenly drawn here as it is in the books. In the books, Uhtred is always comparing the joyous attitude of the Danes to the somberness of the Saxons. The contrast goes way beyond the difference between paganism and early Christianity, and was beautifully summed up in one brief scene that could certainly have been put in the series. When the Danes sail by Bebbanburg at the very beginning of Book One, their leader, Earl Ragnar, runs from one end of his longship to the other on the extended oars of his crew. It's a beautifully written scene, and establishes the Danes not just as ruthless plunderers but as joyous adventurers. This aspect of the Danes is pretty much lost in the series, which is a shame. It could have been there. The bad, but unavoidable under the circumstances - the series is monumentally slimmed down from the books. The books had a cast of dozens, all beautifully executed by Bernard Cornwell, who excels at character development. The series, by comparison, has a much smaller ensemble, and some of the best characters in the first two books have gone by the boards. Still, it's very rare that a film version of anything can stand up to the book or books that inspired it, so I can live with it. The inexplicable - Uhtred's weapons had names, and his sword, Serpent-Breath, is so anthropomorphised in the books that it is, for all intents and purposes, a character. Uhtred's seax, named Wasp-Sting, enjoys a similar stature. This is a wonderful bit of historical color that added tremendously to the books, and which would have added tremendously to the series. Why this was left out is beyond me. Still, I am such a devotee of Cornwell's Saxon Tales that I am happy to have this series to watch. There are nine books so far, so there is plenty more of Uhtred's story to tell. I hope the BBC tells it.

history.title: The Boys of Baraka
history.text: I teach young men in South Los Angeles whose circumstances are similar to those of the young men portrayed in this film, and it's fair to say that this film very much changed the way I saw the young people I teach. It also inspired me; broke my heart; filled me with despair; filled me with hope; made me very angry; made me very determined. The Baraka School was located in the countryside of Kenya, and served as a boarding school for some of inner-city Baltimore's most troubled male 7th and 8th graders. The boys who went there were not the "good" kids - rather they were the "bad" kids who kept the good kids from being able to learn anything. The documentary follows four of them for the one year they are at the Baraka school. Those four are: 1) a boy whose solution to every problem he encounters is to start a fight with another student; 2) a young aspiring preacher whose mother is an active junkie; 3) a 7th-grader functioning at a 2nd-grade level whose father is in jail for having shot his mother; and 4) his younger brother, who seems lost but who is academically capable. In the course of their year at the Baraka school, these four young men are able to experience something that inner-city Baltimore has taken from them: a childhood. They are taken from a world of drugs, guns, and concrete to the Kenyan countryside, where the electricity is turned off in mid-evening. They experience nature - one boy delightedly asks "Did we just see a lizard?" They are taught the old-fashioned way, in small classes, with patience, by teachers who are able to see them and care about them. One reviewer takes exception that the teachers are white. Really? Seriously? So what? As a culminating activity ending their first year, the young men climb Mt. Kenya. They return to Baltimore for their summer vacation transformed. Unfortunately, world events intervened to end the Baraka School after the bombing of the United States Embassy in Nairobi. The four young men, having had one year of a truly transformative experience are now thrown back into the Baltimore public school system, and there the film ends. We don't know what will happen to them; neither do they. One, Montre (The fighter.), discovered at Baraka that he is a math whiz. He gets the second-highest score on the Maryland State Math test, and is headed off to one of Baltimore's best high schools. He is clear - Baraka showed him what to do, and now it's up to him to do it. Another, Romesh (The academically capable younger brother.), is simply devastated, and says "I think our lives are gonna be bad now." The other two seem to be drifting and unsure when the film ends. A bit of research online can reveal what has happened to the four young men. The infuriating thing is that the Baraka school provides a model of something that might well work if carried out within the United States as a national program. Public education in our country is letting down the most vulnerable members of our society. This film clearly shows us a better way. It should be required viewing for every metropolitan school district superintendent and every candidate for Secretary of Education.

history.title: Masterpiece: Poldark
history.text: Remakes should be better than original productions, otherwise there is no point in making them. This is a comic book version of "Poldark". So much is left out that there's very little to it, and if I literally lost count of the times Ross rode his horse across one particular stretch of Cornwall's North coast. But please keep in mind that I'm prejudiced about Poldark. The original mini-series led me to the books, which in my opinion are among the best historical novels ever written. I was already booked that year to go to the U.K., and Poldark - the series and the books - got me to Cornwall, which I love to this day. The richness and depth of the books are incredible, and the original mini-series made a valiant and largely successful attempt to bring them to the screen. All that is missing from the new series, which is simply about a series of events, rather than letting us get to know the people who experience those events. It is shallow and rushed by comparison, and does not take the time to allow the audience to get to know the characters. In my opinion this version of Poldark was entirely unnecessary. To me, it can't hold a candle to the original.

history.title: POLDARK: THE COMPLETE COLLECTION
history.review_title: A Window Into A Different Time And Place
history.text: Of the two versions available on DVD, this is the one that makes the most effort to be true to the books. Yes, it was done in the 1970s and shot on video. Yes, much of it looks like a soap opera. Yes, compared to the new one it looks dated. However, if you want a much richer, detailed version of the story and a look at the rigid class system in place in England at the time, this is the series to watch. For me, I got to know and care for the characters over time. I felt that I was engaged in who the characters were, rather than just seeing a series of events to which the people reacted. Watching this series got me to Cornwall when I went to the U.K. in 1978, and I saw a number of the locations that appeared in the series. I love Cornwall to this day. Unfortunately, so does everybody else; it's been discovered in a big way since then. If you have the time to invest, and can put up with the factors that make it dated, this is the version for you. If you are a modern person in a hurry, and want the bare-bones version of a wonderful story, then you should check out the modern version. And if you're a reader, by all means go straight to the books. They are wonderful!

history.title: Small Faces
history.review_title: A Vivid, Haunting, Coming of Age Story
history.text: I saw this film several times when it came out in 1996, and found it unlike anything I had ever seen before. Set in Glasgow in 1968, the film follows the coming of age of two of three brothers being raised by a single mom. Glasgow itself is vividly portrayed, and the film gives the viewer a terrific sense of place. And as the mom tries to cope with safely bringing up her three boys, lurking behind everything is the tension caused by the presence of two adolescent gangs: the Tongs and the Glen. One of the sons is a member of the Glen. Gangs in Scotland had no access to guns as gang members do - and did in 1968 - in the United States. Instead, they wrought their mayhem with tools such as hammers, knives (Scotland has more knifings per capita than any other country in Europe.), and their signature weapon, the straight razor. They were terrifying, and their membership was huge. According to the head of the Glen, the Tongs had an active membership of over 300. "Small Faces" follows Lex, the youngest of the three sons, as he simply tries to get on with his life after a precipitating incident brings him to the hostile attention of the Tongs. It also deals with the sexual coming of age of one of his older brothers, Alan, an art student. The third brother, Bobby the gang member, achieves momentary glory in a rumble against the Tongs. I really can't say more without putting in a spoiler, which I won't do. "Small Faces" for me was a haunting film, and I have gotten a copy on VHS. Its lack of availability on DVD in the States continues to bother me, especially when so much trash is so easily available. I recommend this film very highly as a coming of age story set in an unforgettable milieu. Now, in 2016, Glasgow has cleaned up its act and is legitimately Scotland's second city in the sense that Chicago is in the United States. But in 1968, when this film takes place, Glasgow was a terrifying place in which to grow up.

history.title: Flight
history.text: I am getting tired of films and TV shows that glamourize and glorify alcohol and drug abuse. This does both. The film centers around Captain Whip Whitman (played by Denzel) who miraculously crash lands a jetliner that suddenly starts to nosedive. Before the plane takes off we see the Captain drinking and taking cocaine. Now the important thing is that the drug and alcohol abuse has nothing to do with the plane crash. After the plane crash the movie crashes. After the crash, Whip rids his life of alchol. This is a great series of scenes where he goes through his grandfather's farmhouse (which he owns but is trying to sell) and starts by flushing his pain killers down the toilet and then bottle after bottle and six pack after six pack. It appears that Whip is going to straighten out his life. But then the film starts down the wrong road. Whip goes to a meeting with his friend, now working for the pilot's union. When he gets there he finds a lawyer (wonderfully played by Don Cheadle) and is told that there is a drug and alcohol report that states he was three times over the legal limit for alcohol and he tested positive for cocaine. If these results hold up, this means jail time. My first thought is the film is going to be about Whip being railroaded and made the scapegoat. But no, what next happens is he gets drunk and picks up a recovering drug adict he met in hospital (another great performance). Before the big finally, he is once again sober, its the night before his testimony before the ATSB. He is in a hotel room, his mini bar is stocked with Coke products. He hears a knocking. He determines it the adjoining door. He opens his side of the door to find the other side unlocked and he finds an empty room and a full mini bar which he proceeds to empty. The next day, his friend and attorney buy him cocain to bring him around! Come on without you stupid ending there would be no consequences for his actions. How can you make this worse, start making it preachy. Whip and Nicole (Kelly Reilly) attend an AA meeting with an over the top preachy testimonial. Then another preachy scene is when he goes to visit his co-pilot in the hospital. And it ends with when Whip has a chance to escape it all with one final lie he decides he cannot and finally tells the truth which puts him in jail. Now Denzel's performance is be hailed by many but come on its easy to play a drunk. The better performaces come from Don Cheadle (and I am guessing many of his scenes probably wound up on the cutting room floor because he outclassed Denzel in every scene), Kelly Reilly who makes you feel that she is in love with Whip but will not let him bring her down and Tamara Tunie as the surving flight attendant who helps save the plane and then Whip. These are the reason that I gave this film three stars and not Denzel or the script. One final note, John Goodman is one of the greatest character actors around but this performace is one of his worst. So over the top (almost as bad as performance in A Christmas Carol at the Kodak Theatre). If you really want this film, I would say wait a few months and pick it up in the clearance bins at Big Lots.

YPM is about a hapless politician who is controlled by his staff. VEEP is about a hapless politician that has a staff even more hapless than her. I was so hopeful for this show but it really let me down. I am guessing that this show was a what if Sarah Palin got elected. And I think that is why so many people like it. I never found her laughable and making fun of her is not funny. There is so much that is laughable about Washington. I hope season 2 will get it act together. Despite the bad review Anna Chlumsky has grown into a competent comedian and Reid Scott of The Big C overcomes, for the most part, this mediocrity.

history.title: JACK IRISH, SET 1
history.text: This is the first two adaptations of the Jack Irish books. Set in an area of Melbourne at a time just before gentrification happened. Jack Irish is a successful lawyer. One day one of his unsuccessful defendamts comes back looking for justice and kills Jack's wife. This sends Jack into a tailspin and he gives up practicing the law and becomes a sort of private eye (note: this is the first 10 minutes of the first movie). In the first movie, he investigates the death of one of his old clients, which leads to other murders and a coverup. Guy Pierce, who came to America's attention in LA Confidential and Momemto, stars as Irish and brings life to this troubled character. This is an iteresting yet flawed pair of movies that are worth looking into. Making of documentary is included.
