history.title: Lucky Star: The Complete Series [BD Combo Pack]
history.text: I'm so glad Funimation got the rights to Lucky☆Star and The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya! Both are really great anime series that were extremely popular in Japan and released im the US by Bandai around a decade ago. It's great that Lucky★Star is gonna finally be rereleased. For those of you who don't know, Lucky Star is a slice-of-life anime that peeks into the lives of ordinary Japanese High School student girls while referencing many Japanese culture and popular Anime...as quoted by character Akira Kogami herself as she explains this in show to the Anime Store manager ;) It's really one of those "talking head" shows where you watch characters have conversations with each other about what's the end of a chocolate cornet. The fat end or the skinny end? Since we already know Lucky Star is a great series there's no doubt this rerelease will ALSO be great since Funimation is releasing it! We'll expect reversible cover art and hopefully bonus features... unlike Sentai Filmworks' horrible releases. Seriously, have any of you seen how they releases Clannad?? That big, tacky, bulky box with the discs stacked onto each other on a cheap spindle with a foamy sponge to keep it in place? Shaking my head. On top of that they don't offer ANY bonus features on their releases except Textless Opening and Ending Animations and other Sentai Filmworks previews...which is usually only just that series opening... so we don't actually get a trailer. Shaking my head again. So glad Funimation secured this and Haruhi and NOT Sentai Filmworks. I actually had a BAD dream that Sentai Filmworks got Haruhi and REDUBBED IT! The cast was awful: Kyon - David Matranga Haruhi Suzumiya - Brittany Karbowski Yuki Nagato - Emily Neeves Mikuru Asahina - Hilary Haag... I don't even know who do Koizumi's voice ans frankly I don't care. I'm not saying these voice actors are bad...THEY JUST REUSE THEM in every one of their shows! Clannad, Angel Beats and ef...BUT thankfully that was only a dream and Sentai will for sure NOT redub Haruhi. Lucky Star is one of the English Dubs that I truly love and prefer over the Japanese voices. Wendy Lee is amazing as Konata Izumi and so is Michelle Ruff, Karen Strassman, Kari Wahlgren, Stephanie Sheh and Sam Regal...all personal favorites of mine in the English dubbed world of anime. I REALLY hope Funimation includes a new English dub for the OVA episode! That'll definitely be a marketable feature and secure my decision to definitely buy this product!

history.title: Little Busters Ex
history.review_title: More secrets to the world after Refrain!
history.text: This was a great follow-up to the Little Busters anime series, Little Busters (season 1) and Little Busters Refrain (season 2). Little Busters EX is an extended release of the Little Busters visual novel but adds three new heroine routes for Sasami Sasasegawa, Kanata Futaki and the new heroine, Saya Tokido. All three stories are great and just as enjoyable as the other six girl's stories in the main series but for a precautionary measure, I do not recommend this OVA unless you've watched the first two seasons because you will be clueless as to what's going on. More importantly, their stories revolve heavily around "the secret of the world" that has not been revealed until the end of Refrain. EX is 8 episodes long. The first four episodes revolve around Saya Tokido, the next two, Sasami Sasasegawa and the last two, Kanata Futaki. As per all Sentai Filmworks releases, we can expect all Clean Openings, all Clean Endings and Sentai previews. With a character like Saya Tokido and with Sentai Filmworks' habit of having all similar characters be played by the same voice actor/actress, I would expect someone like Brittany Karbowski to play Saya, the only problem is, she already played Rin Natsume in this series. I pray that Sentai does not cast Shelley-Calene Black as her! Although Sentai Filmworks will not be releasing a DVD or Bluray for this series until 6 December, I will come back and review both the DVDs and Blurays once they are released. 10 DEC UPDATE: So I watched all eight episodes on a slow graveyard shift at work. I have NEVER seen the English dub of Little Busters or Little Busters Refrain but I did watch EX in English just because I've seen the Japanese version with subs dozens of times already. Riki has a girly voice as usual...I think the same person who usually does young boys voices him (Young Yuichi Aizawa from Kanon). Hilary Haag does...alright...as Saya Tokido. That whiny voice really shows when she does over the top lines (when they were scaling down the pyramind). There were a couple lines she shouted that I could not understand leaving me to say "what?" It's a really typical Hilary Haagish voice. Although she does dramatic lines really well. Saya's arc in the end made me teary eyed but that's it. Sasami's arc is the next two episodes. Her voice sounds good too...then...I heard Kud's voice... THEY FLIPPIN GAVE HER A RUSSIAN ACCENT!!!!!!! WHAT?!!!!! IT SOUNDS...no comment. It just threw me off. I knew what Rin, Komari and Yuiko sounded like from English promos but this was the first time I heard Kud's, Mio's, Haruka's voices in English. Haruka sounds very Peppermint Patty or a female character from Franklin the Turtle series... -_- This is why I don't watch English dubs. I have such high hopes only to disappointed just cuz my preferences want something better. Anyways... without spoiling Sasami's story...I balled my eyes out in the end. I cry at the end of episode 6 every single time I see this. Kanata's arc is just meh. Unlike the previous two, there are no supernatural elements to toss the story around, it is purely slice-of-life. Those of you who missed seeing the Little Busters all together doing missions like in the first season will surely enjoy these episodes because they are somewhat important in these episodes instead of having no lines in Saya's and Sasami's stories. The only thing I hate about Kanata's story is that sick, twisted family gets brought up again...but I'll get over it. Basically it's just a continuation of Haruka's story from season 1. Kanata's English voice...sounds very butch. With that I mean she sounds like she can play Riki's voice and come off as a guy. Overall, I'm more than happy that EX got an English release. That's all I've asked for from Sentai Filmworks for the past two years and my wish came true. Really, this is a great early Christmas gift to myself. I probably won't watch the English dub again though. One thing I really want to gripe on is the TV I was watching this on. I hope its just because of this TV's screen ratio, BUT I was disappointed that at the very end of episode 8, Saya was cropped out of the group picture... I need to rewatch this on my laptop or my TV at home to see if it was just the ratio aspect...but it's a really great scene showing all the Little Busters, Saya, Sasami ans Kanata all together. To recap, EX is a great follow-up to the two seasons of Little Busters and can be considered a love letter to the fans who wanted the EX routes adapted on screen. Saya's story is hands down the best out of the three stories, making you shed a little tear, Sasami's story will have you balling your eyes out especially if you love animals. Kanata's didn't have me feel anything but I still love her character and seeing the Little Busters go on missions to help their friends out is always fun. Thanks for reading this review and pick up this set if you watched the first two seasons!

history.title: Sailor Moon S:S3Pt1 (DVD)
history.text: The S Season is arguably the best of the five seasons of Sailor Moon and probably the darkesr with its themes of the Apocalypse and Sacrifice. The Outer Guardians appear for the first time (except Pluto who briefly appeared in R) and they steal the spotlight every time they're in screen! It looks like ViZ media is going for a "rainbow" theme with these chipboard boxsets. Season 1 was pink, season 2 orange and now we have yellow for season 3. By the looks of it, SuperS will be green and Stars blue. I like it! For those of you who preordered this Bluray/DVD Combo pack on rightstuf.com you'll also get an exclusive Cosmic Heart Compact coin! I think its cheaper there than Amazon. I preordered this back in July the day it was announced at the official Sailor Moon panel at Anime Expo and got a special screening of the English episodes "The Rod of Love is Born! Usagi's New Transformation, A Beautiful Boy? The Secret of Haruka Tenno" and "Bond of Destiny! The Distant Days of Uranus!" As far as what I've seen, the new voice actresses for Uranus, Neptune, Kaolinite (who did Usagi's mom and Temari from Naruto) sound great!! Special mentions go to Keith Silverstein who plays Professor Tomoe! He's one of my favorite voice actors and he's such a great guy too! The veteran's Stephanie Sheh, Michelle Ruff and Robbie Daymond all sound great and bring the characters to life too! I can't wait tk hear Christie-Marie Cabanos when she does Hotaru's voice in the next half of the series. Sob, that'll be such a long wait!! This uncut version will do this series justice unlike the previous Pioneer releases. I mean, I live that Pioneer used the original cover art and that they had English Subtitles for the Japanese voices, BUT they completed omitted the first and second opening songs and only used the third one throughout, spoiling Hotaru Tomoe's appearance much earlier in the series as well as hinting Super Sailor Moon is the messiah (she flies with butterflies and purges the dark clouds making way for light to come through). They also CUT the next episode previews. They were labeled "ORIGINAL UNCUT VERSION" but making edits like this doesn't say "uncut" in my book. But now with VIZ rereleasing the entire series, that shouldn't be a problem anymore. I can't wait to own the first part if this set this November, as well as the usual special art booklet and coin! Back when I became a Sailor Moon fan in 2005, it sucked because there was nothing! Sailor Moon's license in America had expired, the Tokyopop manga and DVD's were pulled from shelves and no one shared the same interest. Now is definitely the perfect time to be a Sailor Moon fan, with Kodansha's new English manga, its 20th anniversary, all the new products and merchandise appearing in Japan and American stores like Hot Topic and Barnes and Noble, ViZ media's acquisition on the license, the fan clubs and the new Sailor Moon Crystal anime! Sailor Moon is back and here to stay! "Crisis! Make Up!!"

history.title: The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya: Seasons 1 & 2 [DVD]
history.review_title: GREAT Re-release of one if anime's most popular franchises!!
history.text: I bought this at Fry's Electronics and I am absolutely happy with this product. Since Bandai's rights to the series expired a while back, finding complete sets of seasons 1 and season 2 and the movie were difficult! You wouldn't believe the crazy prices people and scalpers have been selling these for online! I own the Bandai set but I did not own season 2 until now. I'm glad Funimation decided to release all 28 episodes at once instead of dividing the seasons into two separate sets (really...would Endless Eight sell separately??). The DVD cover art uses the Anime Legends art from Bandai's season 2 set and the reversible cover is the Regular Edition of Volume 0 released in Japan. The disc art also takes the artwork from the Limited Edition DVDs from Japan for seasons 1 and 2. I watched the Sigh Arc already and I don't notice any frame issues. Everything looks great even for DVD quality. Funimation has the on screen text and Japanese subtitles at the top and bottom if the screen in a way that it does not obscure the image like Bandai's release. I notice the next episode previews are gone but I think they are included in the Extras disc. Speaking of Extras, I did not have the time to look through all of em yet. I'm assuming they're the same extras seen on Bandai's releases. I know the regular Bluray and the Limited Bluray sets come with 5 hours worth of bonus content though as opposed to this one's being 4 hours less. Anyways, I got this just to be able to own Season 2 and I couldn't be happier with this product. This is one of a rare select of anime titles where I watch the English dub. I love the English dubs to this and Lucky★Star! Crispin Freeman's voice as Kyons, Wendee Lee playing Haruhi, Stephanie Sheh as Mikuru, Michelle Ruff as Yuki and Johnny Yong Bosch as Koizumi. They're all great voice actors who play voices in multiple anime and video games and they really bring the characters to life. One small gripe I have is the simple cover art. I know the title name-drops the central character, I thought a little more creativity could've been used besides using Season 2's art and throwing it over a plain red background. But I gueas this is okay because there are too many group photos of cover art featuring many characters. What makes up for this is what I mentioned earlier: Funimation using Volume 0 of the Japanese Regular Edition as the reversible cover art. I flipped it around to that on my DVD because that just happens to be one of my favorite cover artworks, featuring Waitress Mikuru Asahina agaibst Witch Yuki Nagato. This is unmistakably a must-have for any hardcore anime collector. I totally reccommend it. However, if you don't have $35 to spare for the DVD version (Bluray is $55 and the Limited Edition Bluray is $139!!) wait for Funimation to release a S.A.V.E. version of this...if they're still doing that. But if you're an anime fan this show is one not to be missed. It was extremely popular with its original light novel series in Japan and is beautifully animated by Kyoto Animation, the studio responsible for shows like AIR, Kanon, CLANNAD, Free! and Full Metal Panic. It blends a bit of every genre into one and its funny and has a nice, casual feel, taking place in a high school setting yet being totally sci-fi at the same time. Haruhi Suzumiya has been an iconic character in the world of anime and in my opinion, her popularity continues to grow! Buy this set! You won't be disappointed and it's worth every penny spent!

history.title: Stephen King's The Shining (Two Disc Special Edition)
history.review_title: Annoying brat needs to be punished.
history.text: Terrible CGI hedge animals. Check. Seeing a hornets nest and make a stupid decision to try and grab it. Check. Stupid, annoying characters. Check. This mini-series was utterly boring and stupid. I watched it as a freshman seven years ago. I decided to watch it again because all I remembered were the hedge animals, the hornets nest and the grotesque woman in the bathtub singing "Old mac donald." Danny is such an annoying brat and reminds me why I don't have kids yet. The way he speaks is annoying, his ugly hairstyle and his inability to follow simple orders and expects to be forgiven. AND his constantly repeating "It's just pictures in a book" make me cringe and adds to the sheer level of disgust I feel for that pustule. No wonder the father wants to beat the crap out of him, I was hoping to see it. And the wife is just another stereotypical clueless house wife who tries to keep an otherwise disfunctioning family under control with ridiculous results. Give this garbage a pass. The effects are bad and the characters are unlikeable and you feel no sympathy for these stupid people. The characters and actors in the original 1980 Kubrick films may have been ugly but at least they had some charm and they weren't as unlikeable as the cast in this terrible remake.

history.title: My Little Pony Friendship Is Magic: Exploring The Crystal Empire
history.review_title: How many "Theme DVD's" will Hasbro dish out?
history.text: Wow! This is a great DVD! I started seeing it at Target. It contains two 2-parters, the Season 5 finale, "The Cutie-Remark Parts 1 and 2," the Season 6 opener, "The Crystalling Parts 1 and 2" and finally the episode "The Times they are a Changeling." I think its the 2nd Crystal Empire themed DVD. Now I know y'all adults probably think themed DVD's are pointless and would just wait for the season box sets, but Hasbro has to sell DVDs to the target audience, little girls, so they're always going to dish out themed DVD'S no matter what. The thing is, I've always had a problem with the themed DVD's, in that a handful of them don't have a themed episode centering around the theme the DVD is about. Make sense? An example I'll give is the 3rd official Mlp fis DVD, "Adventures in the Crystal Empire." Sure it had the season 3 opening, "The Crystal Empire," but the other 3 episodes? Not so much. We get a Rainbow Dash episode (probably best to be on the Dash of Awesome DVD), the Princess Luna episode (...prooooobably best to be on the Spooktacular stories DVD...oh wait, I think it is!) And the "It's about time" episode (huh?). I thought they could've put the "Games Ponies Play" episode there...BUT they placed it on the Princess Twilight Sparkle DVD. The Princess Twilight Sparkle DVD carries the same problem. We get that one episode where she becomes a Princess...and in my opinion, SHOULD have come with the Season 4 opener "Princess Twilight Sparkle Parts 1 and 2!" How awesome would that DVD have been? It would make sense since Season 4 hasn't aired yet I think but still...we get a crystal empire themed episode, a Trixie episode, which is alright, a detective episode which was more about Pinkie Pie than Twilight Sparkle, AND a repackaged episode "Lesson Zero" that can be found bundled with the Wedding Playful Ponies Brushables wave. In fact, I don't think the Season 4 openers have been issued on a themed DVD yet. The "Keys of Friendship" DVD is one I actually own and even reviewed here on Amazon. I thought it could have been perfect if they included the Applejack and Pinkie Pie "Key" episodes instead of putting the random "Pinkie Apple Pie" there. You get my point though, right? The only perfect DVD Hasbro put out in my opinion was the "Royal Pony Wedding" DVD. It had great episodes. The epic Canterlot Wedding episodes, "Sweet and Elite (shares the celebration theme with Twilight Sparkle's Birthday), "Hearts and Hooves Day (shares the wedding/trying to get two ponies to love each other plot)" and "The Best Night Ever (the great Season 2 finale, piggybacking off of the Canterlot Wedding celebration theme). This "Exploring the Crystal Empire" seems to be the newest DVD in the themed MLP DVD's line and if you ask me, Starlight Glimmer should be the focus...so why is she not on the cover? There were many themed DVD'S released since "The Friendship Express" and I've stopped collecting em after "Keys of Friendship." I own: - The Friendship Expess - Celebration at Canterlot - Adventures in Ponyville - Royal Pony Wedding - Princess Twilight Sparkle - Pinkie Pie Party and - Keys of Friendship Overall, I'm happy Hasbro tried with this DVD since every episode is indeed a "Crystal Empire" one, well...except the "Cutie Re-mark" but it still makes an appearance in it. Its just weird how Hasbro released 2 Crystal Empire DVDs and 2 Scary story themed DVDs. Since I have Netflix, I see no reason to spend $9 on this DVD. Only if your a collector, I'd reccomend it. Or else, just collect the season sets. Kids will probably enjoy the sing-along and forgive Starlight Glimmer's corruption. Hope this helps!

history.title: My Little Pony Friendship Is Magic: Royal Pony Wedding
history.text: Out of all the Friendship is Magic DVDs Hasbro dished out, they actually got this one right. We get the 2-part Season 2 finale "A Canterlot Wedding" which is one if the greatest stories in FiM, the Rarity episode, "Sweet and Elite" which carries on the celebration theme, celebrating Twilight Sparkle's Birthday, "Hearts and Hooves Day," a Cutie Mark Crusader episode that still shares the wedding theme of trying to have a couple hook-up, and finally "The Best Night Ever," the great Season 1 finale which is as good as "A Canterlot Wedding" and also shares the celebration theme. Not many special features. Just 2 sing-alongs and coloring sheets. I will point out the only two 1 star reviewers here. Uh, just what part of these episodes is dark and violent? There's not even any blood in this and its no darker than a Disney Movie. You crazy, sensitive parents have a really warped idea of what "scary" and "violence" really is, smh. If you can't even expose your children to a TV Y rated batch of episodes, what do you expose them to? Give me a break.

history.title: Sailor Moon S Part 2 (Season 3) (combo pack) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Another solid release from ViZ Media
history.text: As June comes in, here we have Sailor Moon S Part 2 Bluray/DVD Combo pack. I think this release was a shorter wait than Sailor Moon R Part 2 which is a good thing. As with the past Sailor Moon releases by ViZ media, I'll be comparing some good and bad in this release. Minor spoilers ahead, but I expect only fans of the series who have watched it already in subs and the Cloverway dub will read this. I also won't get into the plot because everyone should know it by now. If not, look online. I will only be reviewing the product. The box art is nice, continuing the yellow background used in S Part 1. Pictured is an S image if all 10 Guardians I've seen on a previously released binder as I expected I totally knew theywere going to use this image...). Same with the reversible image, utilizing a shot of all 10 Sailor Guardians. ViZ also distributed this image as a poster and post card during AX 2016 and Otakon 2016 so I have a lot of copies. Disc 1 has an image of Super Sailor Moon, Disc 2 Sailor Chibi-Moon and Disc 3 Sailor Saturn. This pattern goes for the Blu-Rays and DVD's. Bonus features include a standard art gallery, textless opening and ending, trailers and cast interviews. I have only seen the Keith Silverstein interview (he plays Professor Tomoe and Kenji Tsukino) but there are more such as a commentary and some convention stuff. If you really want, I'll reviewthe bonus features and rewrite them in this review. Now for the episodes. Obviously this set has the remaining episodes for the S season, starting out with "A time of shock! Secret Identities revealed to one another." As you can tell the series is halfway through and picking the plot up strong, showing the talismans, Sailor Pluto's return, the remaining Witches 5 and of course Sailor Saturn and Hotaru Tomoe's mystery. As usual, the English cast does a solid performance, sticking close to the original Japanese dialogue with minor changes here and there. Cristie-Marie Cabanos is amazing as Hotaru Tomoe/Mistress 9/Sailor Saturn. It takes a talented voice actress to play three characters' alternate personalities at once and she was great going from a cute, frail little girl to a menacing, evil she-demon, to a firm, solitary guardian. I had my doubts hearing her as the title character on Puella Magi Madoka Magica but rest assured, she did a great job (not that she did a bad performance in Madoka, I just didn't think her voice would fit Saturn's character). Funny how she and Cristina Vee (Sailor Mars) are nearly in everything together? ;) As for the other voices, Keith Silverstein as Professor Tomoe nails it compared to Jeff Lumby's voice in the Cloverway dub. Keith is one of my favorite voice actors I regularly follow on social media and I met him a couple times. He's a great, talented guy and when I first heard him do Tomoe's voice is the first S trailer and he did his menacing laugh, it sent chills down my spine! As for the Witches 5, I'm not sure what happened. Besides Eudial's deeper voice courtesy of Erin Fitzgerald, the remaining Witches 5, Mimete, Tellu, Viluy and Cyprine all sound the same and pretty boring. That's not to say they didn't to a good job portraying their characters, its just that there's no way to distinguish who is who. Cloverway's dub was good at portraying their voices. Eudial/Eugeal had a whiny, "I'm the boss" voice, Mimete/Mimet had a really strange, bimbo voice matching an idol-has-been that wasn't really high, Tellu/Telulu had a deep, sexy, but oddly older voice, Viluy/Byruit had a snobbish, valley girl voice and Cyprine and Ptilol had a haunting, creepy voice...if that makes sense. An example I'll give is the scream Cyprine and Ptilol make as they were vaporized by each other's attacks. The scream we hear in the new ViZ dub was just one generic scream that didn't linger. Cloverway's dub, they screamed for a while and we were able to notice a certain gasped-out linger which was great, showing thay dying by vaporizing is painful! And because of the similar sounding, generic women voices in the ViZ dub, it makes it hard to remember what kind of voice Tellu, Viluy and Cyprine had, whereas in the Cloverway dub, they each had a unique voice. Yes it sticks to the script, but I sorta missed Tellu's deep voice and Viluy being a snobby bitch to everyone. Guess they're just the Nostalgia goggles talking... -_- Other than that, the main cast do well for what they were given, especially Johnny-Yong Bosch as Artemis and Robbie Daymond as Tuxedo Mask who don't get much screentime this season. When the comedy is there, the voice actors and actresses deliver the lines right. When its dark and serious, especially during the final battle its all there and sounds fitting. One episode worth mentioning is "A Bright Shooting Star! Saturn and the Messiah." I can't tell which dubbed episode I like more, Cloverways or ViZ? Cabanos like I said portrayed Mistress 9 well, but the woman who did her voice in the Cloverway dub was very convincing! During the line when Hotaru was trying to take control of her body, she even added gasped chokes, when saying "This body is rejecting me! Remove yourself! REMOVE YOURSELF!!" It helps by the fact that that was the most accurate, dubbed episode Cloverway has ever gotten when comparing to its original Japanese one, meaning it wasn't a Lisa-Lumby Richards episode. She did the movies and directed numerous, poor episodes with bad dialogue -_- but I'll move on to picture quality before I get ahead of myself...bur first...shout outs definitely go to Stephanie Sheh as Sailor Moon who is able to sound convincing especially during the dark moment where she was trying to perform Moon Crisis Make Up. I instantly got chills and emotional as I heard how desperate she was trying to transform to save Sailor Saturn just like in the Japanese version, so bravo to Ms. Sheh! Returning to Keith Silverstein as Professor Tomoe, I was surprised that he kept his creepy scientist voice even after he was free of Germatoid the male daimon. I assumed he would use his Kenji Tsukino voice but I think its for the better. Picture quality. Ah, this. One of ViZ's most harsh criticisms when it comes to the Sailor Moon releases. I'm watching the Blurays on an old LG screen since I moved and my other TV is in storage. When sitting far away, the quality is...good at best. The lines are sharp and the colors are bright...but when sitting closer, you can see all the grain and ghosting. This is the only complaint I have because we should have the perfect Bluray transfers from Japan that Italy has received -_- Come on. The R Movie Bluray looks nice, so why can't we have it? If I were going to buy the Bluray/DVD combo set, I'd buy from Rightstuf.com because its cheaper than Amazon and they send bonus cards featuring the heroes and the Death Busters which is always nice. That wraps up my review for ViZ Media's Sailor Moon S Part 2 Bluray/DVD Combo pack! Hope it was helpful! --Sailor Orthos

history.text: I made it a point not to read reviews for Bone Tomahawk because I'm a long-time fan of Kurt Russell and also enjoy Westerns that offer dialog ripe with an authentic rural cadence. At first blush, this is an original and oddly compelling film featuring really enjoyable performances from Russell and the cast, especially Richard Jenkins who's never been better. As I'd hoped, the dialog sounds authentically archaic and manages to be witty and believable but as the film moves into some genuinely chilling sequences, the graphic violence just became too extreme for me. It's been a long time since I've looked away from a screen. I won't be watching this one a second time.

David Lean and screenwriter Robert Bolt re-imagine Flaubert's classic Madame Bovary in a wild and wind-swept Irish setting. In the hands of the lesser-skilled, compelling personal stories might get lost amid the visual grandeur but Mr. Lean always knew his way around the cinematic canvass. He knew how to reveal volumes about the lives of his on-screen characters. Sarah Miles was perfectly cast as a vibrant beauty who gives in to emotions as wild and stormy as the Western Irish coast. Robert Mitchum is surprisingly effective as the husband tag-teamed by a handsome but emotionally-tortured British officer played by another American actor, Christopher Jones. Then there's veterans like John Mills who is simply heartbreaking and even a bit off-putting as the mentally-challenged Michael whose misguided actions prove pivotal to every important turn of the plot. At the time of its release, the critics were brutally negative in their assessment of the film and Lean was so depressed by the reviews that he almost quit making films. Ryan's Daughter is flawed but wonderfully so. We watched Ryan's Daughter via Amazon On-Demand and the Oscar-winning cinematography held up very nicely. Recommended.

history.title: Special Effects Collection (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I don't think these films will ever grow old and this Blu-ray collection will keep them alive just a while longer. Son of Kong is the only dud in this wonderful offering of "monster on the loose" classics but at least it's an interesting dud. Pop up a batch of popcorn and let the nostalgia begin. Highly Recommended.

history.review_title: Plot Spoilers for a Spoiled Plot
history.text: It's hard to believe that John Cusack and Kate Beckinsale--two very talented actors--actually read the script before committing to play the leads in Serendipity. At first blush, the premise sounds slightly intriguing: two attractive people meet accidentally, experience a sweet and memorable evening but because they are already in relationships, decide to let blind chance determine if they should spend their lives together. You notice that I didn't describe them as intelligent. That's because the characters suffer from a lack of cognitive skills. There can only be chaos ahead for anyone who employs the serendipity model for potential life-altering decisions. Apparently, everyone connected to this project decided to use that same model for making this questionable story into a movie. Possibly, Cusack exhibited the same momentary lapse in judgement. There he was, enjoying a career high point while perusing a variety of scripts, spread around his coffee table. He took out his SAG card and tossed it into the air. The card landed on the screenplay for Serendipity. I knew the film was in trouble when Beckinsale's character, Sarah allows Cusack to write her name and phone number in a novel hoping that, somehow, should the book come back into his possession again, it will be a sign that they should be together. Would any clear-thinking woman inscribe her name and number in a book that will end up on the shelves of a used book store insuring that any random creep in New York city can ring her up? That's akin to scrawling someone's name on a stall in a public urinal. And here's the worst mind fart encountered in this forehead-slapping plot line, years later, Beckinsale is in New York with her best friend (played by Molly Shannon). Shannon just happens to run into an old friend who just happens to be getting married to Cusack. It gets worse. Shannon is then invited to said friend's wedding but never tells Beckinsale the name of the groom (Cusack). Even when the wedding is called off, it never occurs to Beckinsale's character to be curious about the identity of a groom who'd call off a wedding at the last minute. Actually, Serendipity could work as a thriller but only if the writer jettisons most of plot turns in the original narrative. Because the audience wouldn't buy it. In the new version, a beautiful but psychotic woman is smitten by a handsome New Yorker she meets accidentally, spends the evening with him and decides that chance will dictate their destiny. Somehow, they run into each other a second time and she sees it as a sign and begins to relentlessly stalk him.

Van Heflin, Everett Sloane and Ed Begley are typical captains of industry in this briskly-paced drama that details the intrigues and office politics of big business. This fine cast also includes solid supporting turns by Beatrice Straight as Heflin's supportive wife and Elizabeth Wilson as Begley's dedicated secretary. The action rarely ventures outside the confines of the company and the characters constantly skirmish over questions of ethics vs. productivity and at what cost of one's soul. Though Rod Serling's dialogue crackles, the overheated boardroom exchanges often lapse into the melodramatic shouting matches.

I had high hopes for GOLIATH. It came with a great pedigree thanks to creator David E. Kelley and a stellar cast. Despite a promising set-up, the narrative stalled. Midway through the series only had it's eccentric characters and pithy dialogue to carry it along. Where the show really stumbled was on its most vital plot point (SPOILER)--William's Hurt's character's unyielding hatred for his former law partner(Billy Bob Thornton). This was never fully explained or developed. Ultimately it made Hurt's character appear not simply eccentric but certifiably nuts. I don't know if Amazon ordered another season but by the final episode I simply didn't care to wade through anymore.

history.title: The Infiltrator
history.text: Taunt, engrossing true-crime drama about the team that delivered a major blow to drug kingpin Pablo Escobar by gutting his money-laundering operation. Though Cranston's character (based on real-life U.S. Customs agent Robert Mazur) faces moral dilemmas we've already seen in many similar films, the mix of great casting and Brady Furman's skillful direction makes for an entertaining and often tense narrative. Definitely worth your time.

For years, broadcast television provided a steady diet of cop shows and for the most part, shot on the streets of LA but Amazon's BOSCH looks and feels more like the real Los Angeles than anything in recent memory. The show's production design seems to incorporate a lot of actual locations (especially the eateries), too. In addition, the cast skillfully conveys that LA attitude which seems to be an uneasy mix of laid back and quietly judgemental. I agree with others, Season 3 was the best thus far. Better writing. Tighter plotting. Titus Welliver manages to make Bosch--if not likeable--at least sympathetic. Thanks Amazon.

history.title: Island Of Terror [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: One of My Favorite SBIG Films (So-Bad-It's Good)
history.text: The four-star rating isn't because Island of Terror is that good. It's because it's so bad--that it's good, chock full of requisite cheezy rubber monsters, thespians who stoically deliver genuinely bad dialogue with completely straight faces and a plot that challenges the viewer not to hurl choice one-liners at the screen. My admiration has grown for actors Edward Judd, Peter Cushing and really the entire cast who managed to sell every ridiculous bit of dialogue with genuine conviction. Terence Fisher directed the film with lots energy--as if pushing cast and crew to get on with it, so as not embarrass themselves any longer than needed. Thanks to the efforts of Shout Factory the Blu-ray disc is superbly encoded with crisp 1920x1080 resolution that even allows you to spot the wires used to wrangle the tentacles of the rubbery creatures who terrorize the island. I first saw Island of Terror years ago at the old Gemini Twin in Dallas but I didn't recall the film being so absurdly entertaining. If you want to have your own Mystery Science Theater Movie night, I recommend Island of Terror, a generous helping of sci-fi movie cheese.

history.title: The Lost City of Z
history.review_title: Please Mr Bezos, More Films Like This
history.text: Full disclosure, I haven't purchased the Blu-ray but I did see LOST CITY OF Z during its initial theatrical release and thoroughly enjoyed it. LOST CITY OF Z is a fairly faithful adaptation of David Grann's exceptional book of the same name. The style and narrative is reminiscent of the kind of adventure films I've always loved. Sadly, the genre has fallen out of favor with mainstream audiences who, again, stayed away. Since the film fared poorly at the boxoffice, studios will likely shy away from the genre. Despite this, everything about the LOST CITY OF Z hits the right notes--casting, cinematography, production design, etc. It's all quite compelling. And though we still don't know the fate of explorer Percy Fawcett and his companions who went missing deep in Brazil's Matto Grosso, the film attempts to supply a dramatically satisfying answer. I'm a Prime member and genuinely looking forward to watching LOST CITY OF Z again when it hits Prime status. Hopefully, the wait won't be too long since the film was an Amazon production.

history.title: Island of Lost Souls (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.text: I've been anticipating this release for years, so I'm glad to see it finally appear. The Paramount VHS version looked pretty darned good (for tape), so I have high hopes that the Criterion DVD has a top-quality source and will do this masterpiece justice. Definitely get the Blu-Ray version. As for the movie itself, Laughton couldn't be better. He owns Dr. Moreau the way Sean Connery owns James Bond. No one could do effete aristocratic evil better than he. Yes, the panther woman is made up to look a little nightclubby, and Stanley Fields (the drunken captain of the ship) and Paul Hurst (the garrulous captain of the rescue ship) ham it up a bit in their character parts, but was there ever a more terrifying scene than the one in which Richard Arlen first lays eyes on the animal-men? I haven't seen every remake of this story, but the Burt Lancaster (1977) and Marlon Brando (1996) versions aren't in the same league. In fact, even without comparison to the Laughton version, both of them are pretty bad. I've seen this film fifty times and look forward to watching it again when the disc arrives. I'll be sure to invite my dad, who saw it when it came out (at age 7) and now (at age 85) says no other movie ever filled him with such profound fear. Look for the theological themes. It has only been in my more recent viewings that they manifest themselves so clearly to me. Bela Lugosi should have won an Academy Award for his portrayal of the Sayer of the Law . . . "Are we not MEN?"

history.title: Change of Habit [DVD]
history.review_title: The very worst in a pile of stinkers
history.text: I have been a fan of Elvis Presley's music since the King hit like a bomb in the mid-1950s. I bought all his early 45s and then the LPs, and by now have collected the best CD masterings of all his good songs (not the movie filler). Some of his movies were mildly entertaining fluff (Follow That Dream, Kid Galahad); some were talky bores (Wild in the Country, Love Me Tender, King Creole); and Blue Hawaii spawned a dozen copycat color travelogues with thin plots and often thinner songs. In many of his movies, it was obvious that the producers couldn't decide whether they were presenting an actor or a singer. Eventually, Elvis sank to making sitcom-level, low-budget dreck like Kissin' Cousins and Harum Scarum. "Change of Habit" is perhaps Elvis' worst movie: a shallow, confused, cliché-ridden, cardboard attempt to be "relevant." Virtually every scene is sickeningly bad, and that is coming from a lifelong admirer of Elvis Presley's talent. I guess the movies made a lot of money, but overall they were a detriment to the man's career. Thirty-five years after his death, his star still shines bright, but it might have been brighter had he never made a single movie.

history.title: The Suckers / The Love Garden [DVD]
history.review_title: Get this "roughie" to see Laurie Rose
history.text: Almost 40 years ago, I took my date to a drive-in to see some forgettable artsy foreign costume period piece whose title escapes me. When "The Suckers" appeared on the screen, I assumed it was a preview, but it in fact went on for an entire reel. Wrong movie or not, it was actually kind of interesting, so I was disappointed when it was followed by the second reel of the costume drama. My date and I, seemingly the only people in the place to notice the incongruity, suffered through the rest of the scheduled flick. So ever since, I've hoped "The Suckers" would appear on VHS or DVD so I could find out what happened. I found a trailer for it from Something Weird Video, but imdb.com didn't list the movie, and several inside sources stated confidently that it had been forever lost. From seeing the trailer, I am quite sure that my date would have been horrified had "The Suckers" continued past the first reel. It is a fine example of what was called, in those days before hard-core porn, a "roughie." Such pictures had no outright sex, but their plots did supply plenty of excuses to tie up girls and/or get them naked to kidnap them or punish them or make them talk. Believe it or not, most of the old "roughies" ("Love Camp 7," "The Pick-Up," "The House Near the Prado") could not be made today, when graphic sex and graphic violence are OK, but sexual violence is taboo. So if it sounds like your kind of movie, the evidence from the trailer is that it will deliver. Regardless, men will enjoy seeing one of the most appealing and attractive women of early 1970s sexploitation cinema: the lovely Laurie Rose ("The Abductors," "The Hot Box"). Also on display are sexploitation queens Sandy Dempsey and Barbara Mills, who, like Laurie Rose, showcase glorious "real girl" natural beauty. Note: "The Suckers" is a (loose) remake of Richard Connell's famous story "The Most Dangerous Game." "The Woman Hunt," which was made the next year and also stars Laurie Rose, is a remake of the same story. Update April 13, 2013: Picture quality is variable but overall quite acceptable. A few vertical lines here and there, and two places where both audio and video suddenly deteriorate, but briefly. Color is a bit washed out but much better than would be expected from a film that sat around for 40 years. Clarity is good. "The Love Garden" is a slow-moving, insipid excuse to get a little nudity on the screen. The color is weak; the story is weaker. Camera work is amateurish. It is purely a curious relic of a bygone era.

history.title: The Invisible Ray
history.text: Boris and Bela appeared in the same movie only six times. In one of them (Black Friday), they did not share a single scene, Bela ludicrously played a mobster, and Stanley Ridges, as the dual ghoul, stole the show from Boris. In another (The Body Snatcher), Boris dominated the picture while Bela again had a small, lousy part simply so they could put his name on the marquee. In yet another (The Raven) the roles were reversed, with Bela the main character and Boris thrown in to boost attendance. In "Son of Frankenstein," Boris played a rather uninteresting, one-dimensional monster while Bela created an immortal character as the crazed Igor. But in two movies, they each succeeded in substantial roles: the ultra-baroque "Black Cat" and the underrated "Invisible Ray." I'm a bit puzzled by this release, though. "The Invisible Ray" has been and is available in a studio-produced multidisc set of 1930s flicks that costs about the same and includes the aforementioned Raven, Black Cat, and Black Friday, as well as Bela's "Murders in the Rue Morgue."

history.title: Classic Monsters (Complete 30-Film Collection)
history.text: I've been a lifelong fan of the Universal horrors (bad as some of them were), but I see no point in this release. I suspect that most people who would be interested in this collection already have these films on DVD, and the real fans have picked up the Blu-Ray set, probably (like me) at low price from the UK. Just how long can something be recycled? Does the world need yet another version of Elvis's 1950s hits? The Wizard of Oz? Gone with the Wind? Snow White? Chuck Berry's greatest hits?

history.title: The Big Noise (Blu-ray/DVD Combo)
history.review_title: Not interested in their later stuff.
history.text: There is no greater fan of Laurel and Hardy than I. If Blu Ray discs ever become available for the terrific material they produced from their last silent shorts (e.g., Big Business, Two Tars) through about 1935 (Thicker than Water), I would snap them up immediately, despite the age of the films. Unfortunately, the full-length movies L&H made after they left the Roach studios are artistic disgraces, with screenplays written by Hollywood hacks who had never seen a L&H film. Stan and Ollie themselves were well aware of the dismal product being produced, but they were well paid for their work, and needed the money. In my opinion, "Saps at Sea" was the last picture Laurel and Hardy made in which the characters we loved in the old shorts are recognizable. "Great Guns" was on TV a while back. I saw a little of it, and it was WORSE than I remembered it to be—actually painful to watch. As far as I'm concerned, it and "The Big Noise" and everything the boys made afterward should be burned out of reverence for the two funniest guys who ever lived.

history.title: The Wolf Man: Complete Legacy Collection [Blu-ray]
history.text: For those (like me) who bought the first set of Universal Blu Rays and already have Frankenstein, Bride of Frankenstein, and Wolf Man, either the Wolf Man or the Frankenstein Legacy Blu Ray fills out collections with monster-fests: Frankenstein Meets the Wolf Man (the Universal horror that falls the farthest from beginning (the superb graveyard scene and a tidy if obvious mystery) to illogical and chaotic end, the C-grade House of Frankenstein and House of Dracula, and perhaps the best of the four, Abbot and Costello Meet Frankenstein. If those four will do it for you, either the Wolf Man set or the Frankenstein set will do. But if you want Werewolf of London or She-Wolf of London, you'll have to go with the Wolf Man set; if you want Son of Frankenstein or Ghost of Frankenstein, it's the Frankenstein set. To me, both She-Wolf of London and Ghost of Frankenstein are throw-aways, but the spooky, atmospheric, and neglected Werewolf of London is well worth having on Blu Ray, and so is Son of Frankenstein, with its great cast, especially Bela as Ygor. So I guess I'll have to buy both sets. I don't like the duplication, but at these low prices for Blu Rays, I can't complain.

history.title: Dracula Vs. Frankenstein [Blu-ray]
history.text: "So bad it's good" can legitimately describe some movies (The Devil Bat [1940], It Conquered the World [1956], Showgirls [1995], Gung Ho! [1943]), and some are so bad they're just plain bad (Plan 9 from Outer Space [1959], Snuff [1975]. Dracula vs. Frankenstein falls squarely into the latter category.

history.title: THE BEST OF LAUREL & HARDY: Premium Collector's Edition with Laurel & Hardy and Friends Featuring 'Our Gang' 8-DVD Bundle
history.text: The best of Laurel and Hardy? Just the opposite. Almost all these titles are of value only as curiosities. Virtually none of L&Hs best work is included. The non-L&H stuff is pretty much worthless, too. Wouldn't take this collection free.

history.title: The Sea Wolf [Blu-ray]
history.text: The long wait for this classic was well worth it. For some reason, "The Sea Wolf" never made it to VHS (that I know of) and had appeared on DVD only in an undesirable, heavily cut, wrong-aspect Spanish version. When I was young, it was on TV every once in a while, but never in its full 100-minute form. (Because TV stations wanted movies that could, with commercials, fit evenly into slots of 60, 90, or 120 minutes, the studios supplied versions in which anything not crucial to the plot was often excised. In "The Sea Wolf," these included scenes of the alcoholic physician trying to recover some self-esteem, of the lead-up to the blood transfusion that saved Ida Lupino, and of the time in the dinghy during the attempted escape.) It's great to have the high definition of Blu Ray, but even more important is the restoration of the 16 minutes that, before now, were known only to people who had attended a theater showing three quarters of a century ago. Those 16 minutes supply background, develop characters, and clarify otherwise inexplicable dialog that occurs later. Those who appreciate fine acting will also enjoy this movie. Instead of the quick cuts among short lines from talking heads who are simply spouting from a page of script, we are treated to long scenes that demand the intelligence and skills of real actors, and of those "The Sea Wolf" has an abundance: Edward G. Robinson, John Garfield, Ida Lupino, Barry Fitzgerald, Alexander Knox, Gene Lockhart, and even the lesser-known Stanley Ridges, whose film resume includes high-quality performances in a variety of roles. This release is a real treasure.

history.title: Days Of Thunder [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Days of Thunder on blu ray….They thundered past a remaster
history.text: This review is about and based solely upon the transfer of the film to Blu Ray and does not provide the 100th summary of the plot or my opinions on the movie's quality, acting or storyline. VIDEO…. I watched on a Panasonic ZT 65" plasma and an Oppo 103 Blu Ray player. Do not think that this film has been remastered in any way. It is rare that I actually see artifacts on a blu ray, even a bad one, but Days of Thunder does have them in the form of white dropouts. Granted, I saw them only once around the 20th chapter and went back and confirmed them as well. The imaging is not terrible but not great either. The film has a relatively soft focus with a smoothing out of small details. It's not that you don't get used to seeing what your watching but this film was probably transcoded to Blu Ray from an old mother copy and was not cleaned up at all. Deep blacks are not deep and the warm color grading is pretty lifeless. Despite the dated soundtrack, I like the film but this transfer doesn't cut it. Glad I bought it cheap at BB. 2 stars for the video. AUDIO…. You'd expect the audio on a film about car racing would be incredible but it isn't. While the lossless Dolby True HD 5.1 soundtrack provided clean and transparent dialogue they could have done so much more for those who's home theaters are just waiting for a film like this. While better than the video imaging, a disappointment for me in the holding back of what should have been much discreet directionality from the surrounds. Bottom end for the LFE channel gets some use but is not anywhere near as deep as it should be for those who have ever been around a race track. 3.5 stars on the audio Extras…. There are none, not even a commentary. They do include the movie trailer but I hardly call that an extra. All my reviews focus solely upon the quality of the transfer to blu ray and I do hope that this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

history.title: Starship Troopers: Invasion [Blu-ray]
history.text: I enjoyed the original Paul Verhoeven's live-action version of Starship Troopers for its thrill ride action, outright humor and satire. This sequel, Starship Troopers: Invasion, was a huge disappointment to me in almost every way. Usually, for my reviews of films on Blu Ray, I focus only upon the actual quality of the video and audio elements of the BR disc and leave the plot summaries and opinions on acting et al to the many other reviewers but this review will deviate somewhat from my past reviews. Please do keep in mind that what you see and hear at home is dependent upon the TV monitor and home theater equipment you are using. My system is a fairly high end esoteric(and costly) system. VIDEO QUALITY..... I felt as if I were watching a video game throughout the entire film. The whole movie is CGI animation and not very realistic at that. Desaturated color palate, smoothed out faces with no details really at all. Since it is all CGI, there were obviously no dropouts or grain, no artifacts or aliasing but just plain Japanese style animation. The so called nude scenes served no purpose at all in this confusing cast of characters. I have no issues with nude sex scenes in films but these were absurdly placed in the film. Dialogue was entirely cliché and syncing of lines to the characters mouths often seemed very off...like the old Godzilla movies of the 50's. Much of the battle action scenes were confusing as you couldn't tell what characters were doing what as there was little distinguishing who was in what 'power suit'. Video Stars....Zero AUDIO QUALITY.... The audio quality was an uncompressed (actually it is all compressed but this lossless audio codec is much less so) DTS HD MA 5.1 which I listened to on a 7.1 system. The dialogue, though poorly synched to the character's mouths, was clear and transparent. The audio is not bad at all and fairly immersed you within the film utilizing your entire audio system. There was not a whole lot of front to back or visa versa panning, nor left to right(and visa versa) panning of the sound stages and almost no discreet directionality of audio foley effects, but the overall audio came through strongly through all speakers with the LFE channel getting a decent workout. EXTRAS... There were a few blooper scenes with the voice actors ad libbing some dialogue, a couple of deleted/extended scenes and the director's commentary which, while somewhat interesting, seemed too much to me as if he was patting himself on the back for his excellent (in his opinion) job of staying true to both the real movie and Robert Heinlein's novel. One thing I truly hate on either DVDs or Blu Rays are the extras called ' previews'. This disc had an ad telling us how wonderful Blu Ray discs are and about 5 or 6 different previews of other films. Basically, you are paying for advertisements that take up some of the very limited room on these Blu Ray discs causing for more compression and reduced resolution of the movie you are actually paying for. This was one Blu Ray disc I wish I had not gotten. Just terrible for me but it might suit the tastes of a 12 year old. I do hope that this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. All my movie reviews are of this nature and focus only on the quality of the transfer to BluRay so check them and see if they are of help as well. Thank you for reading.

The monitor I use is a fairly new Panasonic ZT 65" plasma and the amps, speakers, cables, OPPO 103 BluRay player and AVM-60 7.1 Atmos enabled Surround Processor I use are hi end esoteric gear to provide me with a more realistic and objective perspective. The Oppo player is not enabled to transcode Atmos audio so it will default to the next best audio coded, in this case, DTS HD MA 7.1 I am not trying to be a snob here, but just pointing out that what you see and hear is very dependent upon the quality of the gear you are using. VIDEO QUALITY..... I had not seen this film in the theaters nor read about it so I bought it on a blind gamble and won. Very well done film in most respects with a very credible storyline. The film's video quality rates a 4 in my mind. Colors are deeply saturated without over popping colors as you might find in a Transformers movie. Skin tones are normal and natural with clarity to small details even in the darkest of scenes. No artifacting anywhere was noticed, which having been shot in video rather than on film would be expected. A great many of the scenes were done in CGI and, to my eyes, some of the CGI was less than perfect. The CGI apes, while appearing to be well done were nowhere near as natural looking as the apes of the recent Planet of the Apes films were. You could see the CGI of them pretty clearly. I wouldn't call them poorly done, just not as good as other CGI I have seen. The CGI of Tarzan and the natives running along the tree branches was dizzying but not as obvious. Mbps rate appeared to average in the mid 30's. This could easily have been increased if it weren't for the several ads for other films that the company calls 'extras'. They just take up room on the disc calling for more compression of the film you are paying for. AUDIO QUALITY...... The Atmos 7.1 lossless codec is the default audio but since I do not have an Atmos player, it defaults to the lossless 7.1 codec and does a good job with that. All audio levels were properly set so even quiet dialogue was clean and discernible. The surrounds are used primarily for an immersive ambient experience and does so respectfully. There was not a whole lot of discreet directionality from various front, side or rear channels for various foley fx but the overall audio experience was a good one. Left and right pans across the front stage are few but effective. While the audio quality is good, why the audio editors do not put effort into utilizing the 7.1 codec is disappointing but is due probably to budget reasons. Audio gets cut first. EXTRAS.... No deleted scenes or gag reels but some good docs on creating the many CGI effects as well as the training the actors needed to go through and the development of a excellent story line that easily could have gone awry and turned into a cheapo storyline. As it is, the story was very well done. The Standard Def disc is included as well as your ability to download it from UltraViolet but not iTunes which I prefer. I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

This is a film where the audio engineers really put some thought and effort into creating a seamless audio soundtrack with breathtaking use of both pounding and subtle foley fx. EXTRAS..... Audio fx from pans back and across the front and rear sound stages are put to the test with a great number of foley fx for both the front sides and rear speakers. history.title: Independence Day Resurgence(Bluray+DVD+Digital HD)
history.text: All of my many Blue Ray reviews focus solely upon the actual quality of the film from Standard Def DVD quality to the higher standard set for Blu Ray. This film was roundly criticized for its weak rehashing of the original Independence Day and in my opinion, deservedly so. Many hole plots, some weak and obvious CGI along with the good CGI as well. Never the less, the Blue Ray deserves its 5 stars strictly for the excellent quality of the discs video and audio which could easily be used as a demo disc to show off the quality of your own home theater set up. VIDEO QUALITY.... Independence Day Resurgence displays some of the finest video quality you will find anywhere. Colors are true and bright with color correction doing nothing to take away of the imaging. Skin tones are very natural and contrast is excellent throughout the film. Small details such as hair and skin pores are easily seen and are not blurred into mushiness. While several 'previews' ,which add up to nothing more than advertisements for other movies and take up room on the disc's limited room causing for greater compression of the film you are paying for, the video quality remains superb. Average bit rate appeared to be 30 Mbps which is not very high but better than those with those low 20 rates. AUDIO QUALITY.... While there is no Atmos 7.1 format on this disc, the lossless DTS HD MA 7.1 codec is utilized to its full potential. Not only is the audio totally immersive, the audio engineers use the surround channels for a lot more than simply spreading the musical score around. There is a ton of discreet audio foley fx spread across and around the different sound stages. These fx come from all directions so you are in the battles from all angles. Your LFE channel will also get a great workout throughout the film's many action sequences. 10 stars on the audio for sure. EXTRAS.... Aside from the completely unnecessary ads for Blu Ray and other movies, the disc has several decent extras. The bloopers, which I usually enjoy when they are included, are not the funniest and are often redundant. They are all shown with the blue screen in the rear as almost all the CGI was done with blue screen rather than green screen. You are also provided with the typical directors commentary which I never listen to. Additionally, there is a typical 'making of' documentary. One extra, 'It's Early, ABQ" is a hilarious spoof that is not to be missed and a wonderful addition. Still another extra is entitled 'The War of 1996' which could have been a part of the film serving as a prologue but would have made the theatrical release far too long. Never the less, it takes on the appearance of a news report going back to the original Independence Day. There is also a concept art gallery which I didn't look at and the Standard Def disc. The UV download process for this Fox movie is horrible. The redemption code has far too many letters and numbers that could be interpreted as something else. I tried every possible alternative for S that could be a 5 and B that could be an 8, G that could be a 6 but I still cannot have the code verified. There is no way to contact customer support other than by email which I have sent. I have no idea how long it may take for them to get back to me on my inability to redeem the download and there is no phone number to call on their website. A real pain in the butt and inconvenience. So far, I have heard nothing back. The movie deserves the negative reviews it received on many levels, however if you can get past the holes in the storyline it remained an enjoyable evening with popcorn at hand. The real value of the film on blue ray is the excellent transfer for both the audio and video. I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

The Oppo player is not enabled to transcode Atmos audio so it will default to the next best audio coded, in this case, DTS HD MA 7.1 I am not trying to be a snob here, but just pointing out that what you see and hear is very dependent upon the quality of the gear you are using. VIDEO QUALITY..... Video quality is completely free of any artifactting or visual defects. Color grading has been deliberately colorized to be on the warm and slightly desaturated side. I would not call this color grading to be completely normal or natural as things colors did not look any different in 1952 when this real life story takes place than it does today. That said, the color grading does provided that feeling of age and naivety that permeated the 50's, Mbps rate appeared to average at about 32; not too shabby. Black levels are decent but do not get too deep and small detail visuals rate about the same, a 4. Nothing bad at all but nothing terribly great either. Details of rain and snow drops towards the film's end are pretty discernible and that is always a good thing. AUDIO QUALITY.... No new Atmos soundtrack but we are provided a very decent lossless 7.1 DTS HD MA soundtrack that brings with it very transparent dialogue even with a cacophony of storm noise behind it. The audio is really quite immersive throughout the entire film and this aggressive surround approach does put you front and in the very center of what is going on, especially so during the scenes when you are on either the stricken vessel or rescue boat. Unfortunately, this very immersive audio does not provide much in the way of discreet channel directionality. You won't hear too many waves hit you on the left while your right is quiet or doors slam behind you, pans across left and right, front and rear sound stages. You are in a storm and it is all around you. Bass reproduction is solidly handled and very natural sounding, so that when a wave hits a bar, it sounds as it should. I have spent enough time at sea to know reality when I hear it. Good job here. EXTRAS....I really liked that Disney used real photos of the actual characters and placed them side by side with the actors. I love historical events and took pleasure in seeing these real life survivors and heros.
