history.title: MALEFICENT [Blu-ray]
history.text: I first saw the reviews, and the trailers. Plus it's Disney, so I figured it should be at least good. The second thing, I love movies based on "myth" and other such things. So I watched the Blue Ray thinking this would be a different version of the old classic, (which as a kid the dragon scared the heck out of me). What I saw was so different then what I thought it would be. It's has the basis of the original story, but made it much more "dark" yet not as terrifying. Even the soundtrack matched the moods of the movie so well. In short, I loved it. Malificent was as much a "dark" angel as a faerie. The special effects and computer animation drew you in and was done so well you didn't question it. Even the colors and hues of the scenes were excellent. Angelina Jolie did a superb job, so different from her norm. The rest of the cast did quite well also. There are flickers of humor throughout, which I liked. No spoilers here. A recommended movie.

history.title: Interstellar (Blu-ray + DVD Combo Pack)
history.review_title: Great SCI FI, with outstanding cast
history.text: I don't usually review movies, but being a Sci-Fi nut and seeing all the build up for this, I waited for the price to drop and bought the Blue Ray. ( a week later price went up again). I really only knew about the two lead actors, and was surprised at the level of the rest of the cast. Michael Caine? YES! To me the movie started up a bit slow, but I like character building and showing the scenario. It did this very well. As they went into space, the effects and such, I definitely got a Stanley Kubrick "Space Odyssey" feel too it, Which I Liked. I did get really engrossed in the movie. The reason? This is a very true Science Fiction Movie, not a "shoot em up got to have a laser in every shot" movie. Independence Day it is not, but it's not supposed to be. The science that goes through the discussions in "Interstellar" are reminiscent of the works of Asimov and others..very hard core. Thus the five star rating. I like science fiction! Note that this isn't for the 13 year old "Mom where's the funny aliens and stuff" movie. I believe that if you like sci-fi, you will like this.

history.title: Victory at Sea - The Complete 26 Episode Series - Plus 6 Bonus War Documentary Programs - Collector's Tin
history.text: To start off with, I remember watching this as a child. My father loved this show, and he loved the soundtrack, and as a result, so do it. Still have the original soundtrack albums. The songs " Beneath The Southern Cross" and "Guadalcanal March" are worth the listen. The show itself was done in the fifties, not that far removed from the war itself. "The Greatest Generation" was riveted to it on their black and white TV's..ours was. The narration is stirring, they used actual footage throughout, and its episode sequence built up to the finale. If you wish to expose children or teens to the history of this time, this is a great way to expose them to the feel of the time. This and the other excellent series "The World At War" are excellent ways to do that. This is highly recommended, and at this price, you simply cannot go wrong. I while back, I got this as presents for my relatives, (father, uncles), and they were astounded. At $5??? No better gift for those who lived it.

history.title: San Andreas (Blu-ray)
history.text: I remember the Charleton Heston "Earthquake" back in the day. This beats it hands down. The special effects are spectacular, some of the best ever. It's like taking "2012" and doing it on a larger disaster scale. People must realize that this is a disaster epic pure and simple. This is not a "art film", (which few make blockbuster money anyway). The kids loved it, (it was intense so not TOO young). I had my Surround System on, and boy did that ad to the effect. I rate it a five because, 1) it is entertaining 2) Special effects are excellent 3) It could happen 4)the Family loved it and "The Rock", and 5) I will see it again. I though the actors used were excellent choices also.

history.title: Seeking a Friend for the End of the World [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: It's The End Of The World As We Know It
history.text: Very unique movie. A typical love story I guess, with appealing actors and supporting cast. But the premise makes the movie. The end of the world as a backdrop just made the story. I have now seen it twice and would recommend it. We had a discussion after the movie, "what would you do?". You can feel the end of the movie coming, and even in "success", the ending was bittersweet and sad. I just bought it for my collection on Blu Ray on sale. I will see it again.

history.title: Passengers [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A Great Sci Fi Love Action Thriller
history.text: I have read many science fiction books, and a few were similar to this. To me, this is a classic science fiction movie, dealing with interstellar travel and many of the themes science fiction writers use. (The sling shot manuever, food dispensers, etc). While the movie starts off a little slow, it does accelerate. What is amazing that much of the movie is only four actors. But great actors they are, well cast, and the chemistry is obvious. The acting is frankly superb. Yes a love story, a good one, set with action especially in the last half. A sort of "romantic science fiction action thriller". Great special affecrs, well thought out, and not over the top. Highly recommended for stream viewing, and if you like, then add it to your sci fi collection. I did.

history.title: DOCTOR STRANGE
history.text: I will not delve into the detailed review as others already have. The 5 star reviews are entirely justified. The addition of Dr. Strange into the Marvel Studios "canon" is a great missing piece now filled. I have read the comics since the beginning and knew how difficult it would be to do this in a movie. But now, movie "science" has caught up. and here we are. The casting of the movie was brilliant. Watching Cumberbach change into the Final Dr. Strange was a highlight. In Comics, his look is do unique, and they caught it here. I loved the movie, I loved the special affects, and the acting drew you in. The action accelerated and grabbed you. Well recommended.

history.text: This is one of the great movies from my childhood. Seeing it then on my Black and White TV with massive commercial interruptions. I have been carefully selecting these moves for myself as I see them, and this was a great choice. Watching it in color, in it's entirety on the wide screen was just great. A great western.

history.title: Spin Out
history.text: Spin Out is about racing with cars in the Australian Outback in an attempt to outmaneuver each other by spinning round and round until one is declared the winner in a kind of "game of chicken". It really isn't that clear. But that's only the backdrop for a film that moves at a snail's pace towards finding true love and reconciling one's feelings that seem to have been submerged forever. The box for the disc proudly proclaims: "An affectionate fusion of Project X and Love Actually". Actually, it's more like Animal House meets The Dukes of Hazzard. Trite and predictable don't begin to define this movie which plods along to its inevitable end. All the standard jokes and gross outs are there - from a portable worker's outhouse that explodes with someone in there resulting in..., grown men dressing in drag, binge drinking contests, mud wrestling, nude flashing, etc. The only bright spot is to see the incomparable Xavier Samuel (Twilight, Adore, Bait, Drift, Anonymous, Newcastle) who must have had some free time on his hands to make this film and earn a few extra bucks. It does not help his career. The idea for this movie must have looked better on paper than in the final outcome. The last extended scene in the film reminds one of that found in Grease without the great music, production values, and dancing that we see in the latter. Ironically, it is Olivia Newton John, an Australian, who is one of the two major stars of Grease and is responsible for setting up the entire finale of that film. Maybe they should have borrowed her to make a cameo appearance in this one. Forget Spin Out. It will only make your head spin!

history.title: Kong: Skull Island
history.text: Theatre Review: This film is far more than a mere reboot or remake. I saw it in 3-D and I as well as the people around me were jumping and flinching throughout the movie as object after object came zooming out at us. The film has a solid script, fine acting, and CGI effects the likes of which stand at the very pinnacle of this genre. This may be the most credible and "three dimensional" Kong ever presented from the standpoint of his size, strength, actions, behavior, and appearance. While the story does follow several tried and true as well as predictable paths, the way that many of the would be hunters are dispatched is brought to a new level of gore and, combined with the intensity of this film, is not for the squeamish.The movie begins with same kind of rationale that was seen at the beginning of the Godzilla reboot for the South Pacific atomic testing of the early 1950s. But, from then on nothing is like the latter. Indeed, Kong makes a very early appearance and one need not wait until you are 60% or more into this film for it to happen. The setting on Skull Island is far superior to the California civic setting of Godzilla and far deadlier and forbidding. Kong's creature opponents alone make this film more sinister and exciting - and help to elevate the special effects to a whole new level. The balance between Kong's "humanity" and his "monster side" is perfectly done. While Samuel L. Jackson's character does tend to chew up the scenery he is necessary as the usual human foil for Kong. As a deranged soldier who, in 1973 (the chronological setting for this film), still cannot accept the end result in Vietnam, Jackson's attitude and emotional posturing make Kong appear that much more human. One disappointment was the way the "WALL" on Skull Island was introduced and the reason given for it even though it was intended to fit the storyline of this particular Kong. In the end, it was basically a mere homage to previous Kong movies and something of a throw away. For those who have never seen it, this Kong movie was far more reminiscent of a 1948 film titled "Unknown Island" with Richard Denning, Virginia Grey, and Barton MacLane. That film even had a most threatening oversized prehistoric sloth which even does battle with a T-Rex near the end. (A DVD of the film is still available on Amazon.) Another surprise for me is the fact that Kong: Skull Island is not doing as well by some $30million so far in the US and Canada compared to Godzilla even though IMHO the former is a much better film in every way. However, overseas business is very brisk so far and should well exceed Godzilla when the final tally is made. A final note: For anyone who has yet to see Kong be sure and wait till the end of all the end credits. People always leave the theatre as soon as the credits begin to roll. I don't. And a key Epilogue scene was missed. Serves them right.

history.title: The Great Epochs of European Art: Early Christian and Byzantine Art, Romanesque Art & Gothic Art
history.review_title: A GOOD VISUAL INTRODUCTION FOR STUDENTS AND LAYMEN ALIKE
history.text: Despite the broad range of its coverage (some 1000 years of Eastern and Western Christian art), I found the section on Byzantium in this DVD to be quite helpful for my students in a course on The Art of Byzantium & Russia. In itself, it is not the be all and end all but does complement the basic textbook(s) that were being used. The neglect that is given to the art and architecture of the above mentioned two cultures makes any available visual material especially worthwhile. Just glance at the listings in art history for any number of universities and colleges around the country to see what I mean. The importance of Russia and contemporary Istanbul (formerly Constantinople) in the present world absolutely demands more material on Byzantium and its heir - Russia. There is a more comprehensive approach in John Romer's "Byzantium: The Lost Empire" that comes in a 2 DVD set and is also available from Amazon. However, his approach is a bit heavy and a bit breathless in its subjectivity and, at times, rambling nature. Nevertheless, for the inquisitive layman and student alike who have any interest or curiosity regarding Byzantium (a modern appellation applied to the Christianized Eastern Roman Empire that survived its Western counterpart by nearly 1000 years) and its art, this is highly recommended.

history.title: Hercules Reborn
history.review_title: SHOULD HAVE BEEN SMOTHERED IN THE CRADLE
history.text: Worse than DeCoteau's "1313: Hercules Unbound". The gag reel had more substance. (What could one expect when the film supposedly takes place in 13 BC when 1300 BC might have been somewhat more accurate. Perhaps someone saved the remaining two zeroes for the number of stars this movie really deserves.)

history.title: Half Light
history.review_title: IS THIS THE SAME AS THE TWILIGHT ZONE?
history.text: In case anyone hasn't noticed it, this movie has MUCH in common with GHOST including the fact that Demi Moore appears in BOTH films (which I believe to be deliberate in its casting).1) A loved one is killed off early in both films; 2)Demi Moore (aka Rachel Carlson - NOT Carson which is the name used for her character on the DVD cover [doesn't anyone proofread anymore?]) is left alone to grieve and resolve the fall out from the deaths;3)I'm not entirely sure who left the deadly gate unlocked in HL since DM's husband (her second) possesses the key and lock for said gate to use later on (the movie is not totally clear on this point despite a brief conversation early on regarding the unlocked gate). Thus, both deaths may be deliberate; 4)The ultimate baddy turns out to be a relative, business associate, and/or best friend; 5)A psychic helps to bring about a positive conclusion in both films - remember Whoopy Goldberg; 6)Supernatural forces help to bring about justice in the grand finale. In any event, HL holds your attention and plays well when it comes to the hallucinatory/reality conflict. There are indeed many loopholes. But this genre always has them While the musical score for HL is well above average, it cannot compete with the tear jerking strings courtesy of Maurice Jarre; and the love relationship between DM and Patrick Swayze in GHOST is hardly comparable to the emotional ties that are established in Half Light despite the sad and moving tragedy contained in the latter. But, all in all, this is an interesting twist on an old theme. An afterthought: What is the significance of the Lighthouse if any?

history.title: Vera - Series 7 [DVD] [2017]
history.review_title: she is like a general based in a war room
history.text: Season 7 is another triumph for Vera. Four engaging murder mystery episodes on 2 discs comprise this latest offering which follows the format of the six previous seasons. Vera is once again the energetic relentless detective determined to get her man or woman no matter what. With her most able minions, she is like a general based in a war room, planning her strategy, connecting the dots, and pressuring her associates to get the job done. This latest season, like its immediate predecessor, is much brighter and more colorful (literally) than the first four seasons. Filmed in Newcastle and the Northumberland countryside, we have a ringside seat to the action which requires as much physical activity (if not more) than the intellectual side. Based upon characters created by noted mystery writer Ann Cleeves, we are led through a maze of tantalizing clues up to the final denouement. No two episodes in all seven seasons that I have seen are alike. The brilliant originality of the writers stands out on this point. And everything is fully explained and makes sense in the end even if we are thrown an occasional "red herring". I won't repeat any discussion of the individual episodes here which one fine reviewer has already done. Suffice it to say that the fun in watching VERA is not the solution but how she gets there. Indeed, while the episodic conclusion may be an "Aha!" moment, it is the journey that grips our attention. Knowing the outcome, one is often tempted to view an episode again to see how deftly it all comes together. One last caveat: USE THE SUB-TITLES! VERA may be in English but the pronunciation of a number of words is quite different than what an American audience is accustomed to hearing.

history.title: Kept Boy
history.text: This story of a "kept boy" has more substance than one might think when considering the title on its own. It is a real "human" story that shows how true love can manifest itself even though the beginnings of a relationship were based upon monetary considerations and sexual usage. Once again, the complexities of bonding between two people is revealed to be something that is far from simple, and things are not always what they seem. The concern over the possibility of being tossed aside for a younger replacement, the fear of losing what was once bought and now is more meaningful, jealousy, and misunderstanding are all well presented without being trite. The star of this film and its subject, played by Jon Paul Phillips, has the necessary good looks but also has depth. One feels that you are watching the unfolding lives of real people who are relatable and can conjure empathy. While there is nudity (no frontal) in this film and the sex is not hard core, both have a relevant place in the story it is trying to tell. I would give it a soft R. My only criticism of this film is that it seemed rushed and could have been fleshed out more prior to what turned out to be a somewhat surprising but not necessarily unexpected ending.

history.title: Rift
history.text: The jewel case for this DVD, compliments of Iceland, proudly proclaims: "...A Mesmerizing Exercise in LGBT Horror Done Right" and "...An Atmospheric Thriller...". What it really is is an incoherent mish-mash involving two young men whose relationship is on the rocks trying to resolve their differences while occupying an isolated cabin in the Icelandic wilderness. Someone appears to be lurking around. A knocking on their door reveals no one is there when opened. Like a merry-go-round revolving endlessly, this is what this puzzling story seems to feel like. The English sub-titles are so small that this only compounds one's ability to figure out what's going on. In the end, it makes no difference. The only horror here is this piece of trash masquerading as a "horror" film. The LGBT twist is only there to ensnare the unsuspecting LGBT audience. Beware of this "Rift". You might fall in. Caveat Emptor!

history.title: EastSiders Season 3
history.review_title: A ROAD TRIP OF DISCOVERY AND AFFIRMATION
history.text: This season completes (one is tempted to say fulfills) what has become a trilogy in the lives of gay couple Cal (Kit Williamson) and Tom (Van Hansis). From the outset (Season 1), which depicted uncertainty, betrayal, a sense of disconnect, and lack of firm commitment in their relationship - thereby leading to an eventual (and temporary) separation - through a reunion and the rebuilding of trust and acceptance ultimately achieving a positive resolution (Season 2), we are now shown the two as a legitimate intimate loving couple (Season 3). This current "Season" comprises an actual road trip from NY to CA - a return to their original home in more ways than one - which serves as a kind of metaphor for this couple's relationship. Along the way that relationship is tested by a variety of mishaps, challenges, and revelations which inevitably leads to a new understanding, a sincere expression of love, and genuine commitment. This Season is divided into 6 stand alone Episodes that are also interlinked in one way or another. The campiness and shrillness of previous Seasons has been replaced with a much more serious and mature air. (This also applies to all the original characters from past Seasons.) But it is not overbearing and has many a laughable moment. Indeed, it is far more true to life than what you might find in comparable films of this genre. The dialogue (thanks to Kit Williamson) is credible and the behavior is quite natural. As is the case in other movies that revolve around a "road trip", this is also one of discovery. (As an aside, the titles of some of the Episodes is a humorous double entendre.) The acting is uniformly excellent and the entire story is most satisfying and never preachy. There are a couple of noteworthy "cameo" appearances and Traci Lords makes a brief but critical appearance as Cal's mother. With Season 1, I felt that the story of Cal and Tom was a work in progress. I'm happy to say that this work has now been satisfactorily completed. Bravo!

history.title: Downton Abbey: Season 4
history.review_title: Downton Abbey is a Dopey soap opera set in a phony world accompanied by sawing violins
history.text: The sets are great. Some of the acting is good. The depiction of many aristocrats is believable in that they exhibit their naive ignorance of "real life". Is this supposed to be a sociological look at the difference of classes, acceptance of people in an era when there was little acceptance of outsiders? Is it supposed to be a fairy tale world of people getting along across the barriers of the crippling conventions of the British Empire? Is it supposed to imply that the favored rich of that world have big hearts and are just ordinary folk who can accept the chauffeur with no demur? To show how the Americans appeared to underwrite many of the great houses of Britain but were generally still looked down upon for their differences? Anthony Trollope may have been able to do justice to this group of people, but I think the story as it is goes nowhere. With all real soap operas too many characters get into the stew as they are introduced to keep the story going, and then there isn't time to develop anything very deeply. Too many cameo parts, and no cohesive story. The last episode was the worst of all, leaving everything up in the air with no resolutions. Julian Fellowes just seems unable to let go of all this panorama of people moving around, dancing, being presented at court and almost always punctuated by that MUSIC. Who wrote that theme song? We are subjected to that putrid music constantly as well as all these unlikely relationships. Granted there are some stand-out characters such as Maggie Smith and some of the other women, but compare it to the old Upstairs Downstairs where every episode really had some sort of genuine social or political issue and the class thing was so much more in the open? Or Brideshead Revisited for its ambience. Both of those works had a beginning middle and end and both of them were well written. I vote no on Downton Abbey. I really hoped it would improve, that there would be some actual depth in the story, that something would happen--- but it just floated out on that never ending theme song of sawing violins.

history.title: THE PALLISERS: 40TH ANNIVERSARY EDITION
history.text: Although this is a very loose adaptation of 5 thick and satisfying novels by Trollope, it stands alone in many ways. In the novels, although characters such as Glencora and Planty Palliser do not appear so often, they are created as the main characters in this adaptation, around whom the action evolves and thus it makes a cohesive story. If you have read the Palliser novels you will probably be appalled at the omissions of so much which was essential. However, this does not diminish the acting and ambience of this rambling but at the same time interesting look at the 19th century world. Trollope presents a view of that world which I believe is both believable and at the same time often humorous. Susan Hampshire shines in this, the costumes and sets are wonderful, and many of the characters unforgettable, such as Phineas Finn, the Duke of St. Bungay, and the wonderful Aunts trying to rein Glencora in when she is going astray with her handsome and penniless suitor. The Dukes of Omnium both uncle and nephew Plantaganet, are both beautifully drawn, the older one an old roue who lives for pleasure, and the younger husband of Glencora serious, good, and somewhat of a fool. There are 16 episodes in this set, and they only cover the tip of these interesting novels which present yet another view of the Empire and of Victorian society at the height. The character of Lizzie Eustace is sadly miscast and her story is misrepresented the most in this production, but I still recommend this screen version with five stars.

history.title: The Horse's Mouth (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.text: Alec Guinness not only starred in this but wrote the screenplay. It is adapted from the book by Joyce Cary which is far more rambling and which I finally had to skim to finish as it just went on and on. This version is I believe one of the great pieces of all time, not only a comedy but a true "portrait of the artist." The art depicted was also done by John Bratby, an eccentric London "kitchen sink school" artist, and it goes so well with the special personality depicted by Guinness. I can only say, don't miss watching this movie at least once!

history.title: The 1,000 Eyes of Dr. Mabuse [DVD]
history.review_title: Not as good as the first two Mabuse films
history.text: Not as good as the earlier German masterpieces, Dr. Mabuse der Speiler and the Testament of Dr. Mabuse. This version was more expensive to buy in the German with English subtitles. I had bought the English dubbed version first, and it was terrible, the voices loud and jarring. However, getting the German version didn't do much to make it better. I believe not having Thea von Harbou as part of the production may have been part of the problem. (note Lang always seems to have taken full credit for his films but von Harbou was I believe his muse in the early days and her contribution has often been overlooked. But having read more of Lang's biography it is clear that his style of running things did not jibe with Hollywood and his eyesight was failing badly from his glaucoma and a botched surgery, so he was prevented from being able to do as much as he might have otherwise. But no matter, the story falls kind of flat, even with the references to the earlier films such as shooting the victim on a busy street in an almost exact configuration of the earlier works. I definitely recommend the first two as well as Metropolis wholeheartedly.

history.title: Rocko's Modern Life: Season 1
history.text: When I first started watching Nickelodeon, there were the "Big Four" Nicktoons. Doug was flat-out garbage. Rugrats was amusing at first, but became garbage when it was retargeted at an audience about the same age as the main characters. Ren and Stimpy was funny when you were 8 and thought that anything disgusting was funny, but it's not funny for anyone with a shred of maturity... and then there was Rocko's Modern Life. I saw it as a kid, and liked it, but wasn't capable of appreciating it as much as I should have. Later, when I moved into my own apartment and got a free trial for the Gold cable package, I found a channel that showed old Nicktoons, and started religiously watching Rocko again. That was when I made a startling discovery: "OH MY GOD! That's my life right there!" This show is truly brilliant as a satire of how ridiculous life in general is, especially when you're first living on your own. We did not get another Nicktoon of even remotely comparable quality until Invader Zim, which was everything that Ren and Stimpy tried to be, but done in a tasteful, brilliant way. I will be proud to have Rocko in my DVD collection.

history.text: Easily the best kids' show of the early 2000s. Not quite on par with the serious dramas like Gargoyles, Exo Squad, Batman Beyond, or Transformers Prime, and not quite the comic brilliance of Invader Zim, it's still original, funny, action-packed, and often surprising, with a wide range of great characters played by some A-list vocal talent including Patrick Warburton. The opening music is pretty catchy, too. Overall, Kim Possible was a bright spot in the cultural wasteland that kids' TV has become.

history.title: Once Upon A Time: Season 3
history.text: Honestly, I was hoping that this season would be split into two boxes in accordance with how it was broadcast. This is the season when OUAT "jumped the shark" by taking a story that could be told in one episode and dragging it out into 11 episodes. This causes the stories to move at 1/11th the speed while also making them 11 times as complicated and hard to understand. However, the Neverland episodes are chock full of enough high-octane nightmare fuel to make that not really matter. That's why I wish I could buy only the first half of the season. Everything afterward is a confusing slog.

history.title: Once Upon a Time: Season 4 DVD
history.review_title: The season that killed the show
history.text: This is the season that killed the show. If it hadn't jumped the shark before now, then it definitely did in this season. I'll discuss the two story arcs separately. First, the Frozen arc. Up until now, a huge part of the show's charm and appeal was how it put radically original spins on many of its characters. Rumplestiltskin goes around telling everyone his name instead of making them guess. Prince Charming is an impostor and the real prince is dead. Little Red Riding Hood IS the wolf (which I guess makes it a werewolf rather than a wolf). Pinnochio is all grown up. Peter Pan is a sociopath who murders people by stealing their shadows. Stuff like that. The Frozen arc, however, retains so much of the source material that it might as well just be the 8-hour extended cut of Frozen... except that Frozen was actually good. The plot of this arc, however, moves at a glacial pace, pun intended. And it's ridiculously convoluted. And half of it is told through flashbacks, which aren't marked with stuff like "30 years ago" or "present day". Because none of the characters have aged and the settings all look so similar, this makes the plot almost impossible to follow. It's just painfully boring and inexcusably confusing, except for the last few episodes, which I confess had me wiping my eyes and insist that I was just cutting onions. Nonetheless, a lackluster arc will not kill the show. The second half of this season is where the show completely self-destructs. This arc is such an incoherent mess that I honestly don't even know what to call it. There's not even an identifiable "big bad". At first, it seems to be the trio of Cruella De Vil, Ursula, and Maleficent. I confess that it's actually kind of cool to see these different Disney villains teaming up. Then Rumple joins them, and appoints himself leader, making it seem like he's the main villain, especially as Ursula and Cruella get bumped off. Then The Author is introduced. At first, he seems like a good guy, until he teams up with Rumple to write a book in which the villains get their happy endings. If that wasn't cluttered and rambling enough, his pen and ink are the MOST OBVIOUS DEUS EX MACHINA IN TV HISTORY. It should also be pointed out that the show throws away its own internal logic by simply including this character and his godlike abilities, a point which is made obvious when everyone enters the new book. Except that it's not really a book where the villains win and the heroes lose. It's just a book in which the heroes and villains have swapped places, allowing the show's writers to carbon-copy their previous plotlines instead of actually doing something new. The first two and a half seasons of this show were brilliant. The Wicked Witch arc was tolerable. This season was just a lazy pile of moldy cheese ass with a few great episodes in the middle. Like a moldy cheese ass sandwich.

history.title: Defiance: Season 3
history.text: Defiance was a brilliant show for precisely two seasons. By the end of the first episode of season 3, it had jumped the shark and turned into a godawful pile of crap, primarily for three reasons: (1) the pre-planned story arc that had propelled the first two seasons of the show had run out of gas and the writers had absolutely no idea where they wanted to take the show next. A similar thing happened to Prison Break. In both shows, the first episode gave us the first piece to a huge puzzle that would take two years to solve... and in both cases, once the puzzles had been solved, the shows lost most of what made them interesting. (2) Irisa was absolutely RUINED as a character. The "Lost Ones" webisodes, which were made between seasons 1 and 2, very firmly and clearly established Irisa as being even more quick to violence than Nolan; as a character who would not hesitate to plant a knife firmly in anybody's neck at the first sign of trouble. Nolan has to RESTRAIN her on several occasions throughout the first two seasons. But in Season 3, she is unwilling to fight even in self-defense; about halfway through the season, the writers pretend that she was never comfortable with violence and it was Nolan who desensitized her to it. She eventually gets her act together, but then the writers move on to ruining Nolan... (3) the worst, most nonsensical, most disappointing series finale since Battlestar Galactica. Now, this season did have ONE good... nay, BRILLIANT episode. For people who've already seen it, I shouldn't have to say which one. To avoid spoilers, I'll just say that it involves a major character surviving a suicide mission in the most theatrical and awesome way possible. However, it does not justify suffering through the entire rest of the season, or even the first half. As far as I am concerned, Defiance ended with Nolan and Irisa in that stasis pod underground at the end of season 2.

history.title: The Dark Knight Trilogy 2005
history.text: Let me explain exactly what I want. I just want the two-disc special edition DVDs of all 3 movies in a single box, in a format playable on NTSC region 1 television sets. Instead, these are my choices: I can buy the two-disc special edition DVDs separately like a loser, I can buy the 3-DVD box and miss out on 3 whole disks' worth of special features, I can buy the Blu-Ray box and lose the ability to back up the movies to my USB hard drive via Smartripper, or I can buy some Region 2 PAL nonsense from Europe and lose the ability to play the movies on an actual TV set (and that's not counting the AVIsynth filtering and other tweaking that I'd have to do in order to restore the movies to their original 24 frames per second for proper viewing on my computers). THIS IS NOT ACCEPTABLE, WARNER! I ultimately settled for buying the two-disk DVD editions separately because practical concerns outweighed packaging preferences, but I shouldn't have been forced to make that decision in the first place. I'm genuinely going to send Warner an e-mail about this, or call them or something. If they can release a proper 6-DVD boxed set for the Europeans, then they can make one for North America.

With the advice of his friendly doctor (Burl Ives) he gets in over his head by "pulling the wool over his superiors eyes" when he begins recruiting other agents "that are never quite recruited." Not knowing the first thing about the dangers of being a secret agent he bumbles along until things take a serious tone and he fears for his life, following the murderous death of his doctor friend, his fellow agents try to poison him and he gets the hint to take his daughter and return to England. Better than your average 3 star movies so 4 stars.for Our Man In Havana.

history.title: The Silver Fleet
history.review_title: ANYONE FOR A NICE BOAT RIDE?-- NAZIS ONLY PLEASE!
history.text: Nicely done WWII movie about a Dutch boat builder who becomes part of the Dutch resistance when his community boat company is taken over by the Nazis. Good suspense and action as we watch him slyly becoming a friend of the Nazis, to the point that his friends and employees believe he is a "quisling" or Nazi collaborator. But don't believe it for a moment. He is secretly the head of the resistance and realizes that he must cooperate or watch his loved ones suffer under Nazi rule. But as he cooperates "his" way, we soon realize that it is not important that he builds boats for the Nazis, but it is important, "how he builds them" The last scene is indicative of just how much courage and determination it took to defeat the Nazis.
One of the best war movies I have seen. Originally shot in Black and White it seems more like you are actually involved in some of the horrific naval battles of the time period.

This actual strip was similar in many ways to Bloom County by Berk Breathed but was totally unique to its author, Brett Merhar with the characters taken from his friends and relatives. Perhaps the most endearing character was Angus the caffeine addicted ferret who it seems everyone loved. The other characters Brett actually knew, especially Johnny Jenkins, his best childhood friend and Paula Wisconsin, modeled after his sister. This collection of episodes, first aired on Showtime goes deeper into Bretts life experiences, again using and exaggerating members of his own family. I always looked forward to reading the nationally syndicated strip and while the show is definitely more like South Park than Bloom County it still retains cutting edge humor. Recommended!

history.title: Air Force
history.review_title: Long Lost Gem Reconstructed on DVD
history.text: Excellent WWII movie showing the trials and tribulations of a bomber crew as they are ordered to fly across the Pacific just after the Japanese attack Pearl Harbor. The script is tight and does a good job of character development, The acting, especially by Harry Carey who steals the show, is what acting should be, and the story line is believable and realistic. Directed by one of the all time great, war- time directors, Howard Hawks, this is truly a gem from the past. Exciting action right to the end makes this one of the best wartime movies of the 40's.

history.title: Spark: A Burning Man Story
history.review_title: Burning Man as Social Experiment between Safety and Freedom
history.text: Recommended for all types of anarchists to meditate on the nature of infrastructure in a gift economy and voluntary society. This was a documentary of the history and development of Burning Man as Utopia for creative energy from its birth in San Francisco in 1988 through the philosophy of safety concerns that skyrocketed with the population increase in 1996. The explosion of anger from participants when the organizers resorted to a lottery to manage population numbers was a conundrum that tested the courage of the organizers to continue with their social experiment. Burning Man is now a non-profit; as you watch this story, decide for yourself how it contributes to the ongoing discussion about how public safety and freedom mix.

history.review_title: Fun, Funny, creative, endearing and enduring

This show rates as high as Firefly for Science Fiction because of the relationship between all the characters. I love steampunk, alternative history, public service, mystery, heroes and heroines so this was my escape world. It was obvious the actors enjoyed each other, even Orson Wells.

The character development and how each deals with the choices of their "time" are intellectually stimulating, challenging and rewarding. The sex is absolutely romantic (except the violent episode). Instead of sending a poor young man to a prostitute for his "education" let him learn how to love a woman by watching these orchestrated scenes of gentle manly lovemaking.

history.text: Daniel Craig was great, but the performance by flawless beauty, Yekaterina Rednikova, was amazing. Starts out slow to build the backstory, but picks up quickly. Gabriel Macht also turns in a believable performance as a relentless journalist willing to go to extremes in pursuit of a story.

I really liked this movie for a number of reasons. First, the father and son interaction reminded me of my close relationship with my own father. We spent a lot of time together and often worked side by side. Emjay Anthony, who plays the son is an incredible actor in that he was on camera for long periods of time and had some complicated fast paced scenes. Second, it was as if Jon Favreau told his actor buddies that he was writing, staring in and directing a movie and they all asked to be in it. Actors who usually are stars and carry movies seemed happy to take bit parts and not overact. Scarlett Johansson kept her attractiveness under wraps. Sofía Vergara as hard as it is to believe gave an understated performance. Still latin. Still hot, but more mother and supportive cheerleader than an object of men's desire. John Leguizamo was the friend everyone wishes they had. Funny at times, reflective at others but always on your side. Finally there is the food, music and scenes from Miami, New Orleans and Austin. Also thought that social media was used as a vehicle to convey a message and not, as it often has become, a story-line crutch. However, with that all said, if strong language, especially when spoken by a preteen bothers you, be aware that this movie has its moments. The young man is often treated like an adult so the language is not out of character for the roles. But, it still might be a bit strong for some people's liking.

For these kind of revenge films to work you have to hate the bad guys and care about the good guys. The Hunter's Prayer tries to mix it up a bit with a bad guy (assassin, junkie) who is trying to be a good guy. The other good person, a young woman is cute but not all that loveable. The real bad guy is bad enough, he feeds a no-one-will-miss-villager to his specially trained to kill dog, but we don't get to know him well enough to really hate him or his henchwoman and henchman who looks too much like our maybe not such a bad guy assassin. In the shadows, it often is difficult to tell them apart. The reason I did not give one star has nothing to do with the story or acting but special effects. Without giving too much away, there is one scene where a bad guy gets run over by a car (in reverse) that comes out of nowhere. You are going to want to watch this scene over and over again and in slow motion if you can. Oh, and there is a chase scene where the chased car strikes another car in just the right place to spin it around to hit the chaser vehicle. Pretty clever. I like a good revenge movie. Bad guys getting their due and good guys coming out on top. I like the predictability. Here, the sappy ending is too little and far too late. You feel like you got to the bottom the Cracker Jacks and instead of a surprise you found a coupon for a free prune juice.

Other than number of viewers, there are two strong indicators whether a show is successful. Are those viewers anxious to see what is next and do they talk about the show with others? Designated Survivor has two actors who starred in their own shows and is smart enough to give them about equal screen time doing what they do best. Then you have a strong supporting cast who get enough screen time that we have gotten to know them. It also is good to see a chief executive portrayed as other than a self-important arrogant jerk. Sincerely hope that Designated Survivor becomes one of the most successful series ever. Maybe then the content providers will take note that this is the quality of programming that viewers want and will pay to watch.

This review is about the Salvation TV series and not about how Amazon did not initially make all episodes available for free. Santiago Cabrera, as the billionaire, Darius, is incredible. His looks, his movements, the delivery of his lines are flawless. He is believable in the role. And, there lies the problem. All the other actors don't even come close. Jennifer Finnigan, was barely tolerable in Tyrant but is downright annoying here. Ian Anthony Dale is not as macho or attractive as he thinks he is. Again, annoying. Tess, the omnipotent virtual assistant, probably gives the second best performance. Erica Luttrell who plays the president's advisor is not listed in the main cast but should be. Beautiful, bright, sexy and devious. She hits the mark with all of them. The storyline is a simple one -- asteroid is on its way to destroy earth and must be stopped. How that should be accomplished and by whom is a source of friction between the various factions. Without a scorecard it is hard to tell the good guys from the bad guys at any given moment, especially because it seems the good guys may have been bad guys in the past. The visual effects and cinematography are fine. Get rid of a few annoying actors and this show could be watchable instead of cringe worthy.

In its place are deep friendships, loyalty, empathy and compassion even when romantic relationships end. In that sense, it brought back fond memories of my youth. And, that seems to be what Red Oaks is all about. Each episode is only about 25 minutes, so take a couple of hours and give it a chance. We only need to know which ones. Therein lies the "trick." The two main characters function in an upper middle class ambience of NYC cafe society. They reside across Central Park in one of the precious buildings with a view, have sent their children to highly selective Eastern boarding schools, and now to Harvard. history.title: Cloverfield
history.text: If the camera person had not tried so hard to be a bad camera person, this would have been a lot more enjoyable. But they tried so hard to show that the guy didn't have a clue how to film that that was additional torture the audience needn't have been subjected to. Having filmed excursions/events hand-held, I speak from experience. The guy was relentlessly clueless. As were the characters. A few reviews have said how they related to the characters -- I found them brain-dead 20-somethings who didn't seem to have any experience outside of a very limited social scope or reality, involved w/themselves and the next relationship, no matter how shallow. As such, it was hard to get involved in their experiences from the beginning, and then, as one critic points out, the guy goes into the electronics store to find a battery and people of color are ripping the store off -- another brain-dead cliche, as if your life is worth less than that new TV you've been drooling over in the window display -- while a battle is raging outside. So the director seems cut of the same cloth. So from an interest stand point, between the characters being/acting brain-dead/narcissistic/shallow/ or shell-shocked, it lacked a bit of pull. I think losing the hand-held, while still being in the room w/the characters would be a step up, so we see what they see, not what some camera being flailed about sees. And then, of course, creating characters w/a bit more depth to them would up the empathy level a huge amount. At least 10 Cloverfield Lane had those points going for it.

history.title: Agatha Christie's Partners In Crime
history.review_title: A slog in slow-motion wooden direction and single-expression acting
history.text: I have to agree w/all those who couldn't stand the agonizing pace produced by this paperweight. As I mentioned in a comment, it was as if the director was completely stoned and loved to watch water boil, and decided to drag the audience along for the ride. Situations arose filled w/dead air where nothing happened and for a moment one could confuse the characters in the scene w/manikins. And decisions sometimes were agonizingly not appropriate to the situation, leaving this audience confused and shouting at the screen. The male lead playing Tommy had one, and only one expression to cover the gamut of his character. He was in scenes w/other characters who were playing unsavory chaps who in real life would have seen Tommy for the rube he was, yet somehow they actually thought he was clever! More confusion, more shouting at the screen. It was truly painful and agonizing to slog through the first story. And I don't recommend you attempt it. If it is available at your library, my advice is to check it out there. Jessica Raine, who plays Tuppence, was the only bright spot in the effort, and near the end of the first story, even her character was becoming annoyed at Tommy's behavior (which was so nonsensical and cast Tommy as a moronic bumbling statue).

Some of the reviews are particularly harsh. But, in a way they are deserved. The actors seem to do OK with what they're given, but the writing is stupendously bad. Not that I could do better, but, well, an IT woman -- ie, a person who is versed in tech and computers, wakes up w/amnesia and can't remember anything about herself or her circumstance. Sounds interesting. Might be good. But . . . . . the writing given her makes her seem like she possesses an IQ of about 80 -- she can't seem to fathom what a ship's computer is or that it watches continuously everything on the ship -- in fact, at first, she can't even fathom a ship's computer, but soldiers on nevertheless, walking down the 20 foot hallways so slowly as if sleepwalking -- dreaming she was in a minefield. Seems to me anyone who had risen in tech before losing their memory would be a little quicker on the uptake than this character is. Her expression hardly changes, which lends to the low IQ impression. But it's the dialogue that keeps her there. If the dialogue -- writing -- had been a bit more active and clever, the obvious low-budget, but attractive set, would have melded into the background and we would have been given a story worth watching. As it stands now, it stretches credulity past the breaking point -- at least, for me. The appearance of the show, costumes, actors, space ship, all are fine AFAIC. It's the writers I blame. (and second time attempt, I didn't get far enough to be affected by overbearing music, so can't comment on that).

history.review_title: Brilliant by Clémence Poésy, and excellent effort by Stephen Dillane -- keeps you on the edge of your seat!
history.text: This show is another takeoff of The Bridge, a Danish-Swedish endeavor, with its own twists and turns. I have not seen the D-S effort, but I have the American version, put out by FX @ the same time as The Tunnel. Both the female leads have a form of autism or something similar, but the French girl is much more approachable to my mind than the American girl is. They are both social misfits and awkward around others, and neither can understand why everyone hasn't seen what's clearly right there for everyone to see, but I found the American version's character to be colder and less sympathetic than the French, played by Clémence Poésy. Ms Poésy plays her role so well, it makes you just want to run up and hug her! (Even tho she wouldn't understand why.) Anyway, of the two takeoff versions of the original Danish - Swedish offering, I enjoyed this one much more. The teams on both sides of the Channel were likeable and intelligent -- I just wish they had had more to do than forever stare @ computer screens. It would have been more interesting to see all of them in the field, not just the two stars, but that's not the way they were written by the writers. Highly recommended.

Wow... it's definitely amateur hour with this movie. I decided to change it based on some of the reviews. The acting is bad, the scenes are bad. It's like someone took an adult movie and edited out the sex scenes and just left the bad acting scenes in. Or similarly, it's what a 10-yr old would have come up with and had family members act in; that's the quality of this movie. Over acting and wooden acting aside and ignoring the long overt scenes to show you a stone, or someones feet it a little too much. Cut to scene with empty carpet and count 1... 2...3...4...5... and feet appear and count... 1...2...3 ...4 feet disappear. So we have carpet again...1...2...3, cut to next scene. Lastly, the plot is fairly empty, it tries but it's too contrived and again, much like what a child would have made. Entertaining if you know the kid, not so much if you don't. SPOILER: It starts off with a little boy and girl find a magic mushroom that turns into a jewel box. They take the stone from inside and the little girl moves away. (no context given to that). A writer gets hurt, an suddenly an unseen person gives him the stone, but it's not the girl, she's a helpful nurse that's oddly ever present even though she's not his nurse. The writer decides to become a super hacker. I love that he can't talk and type at the same time. I've never seen anyone try so hard to spill coffee while supposedly not trying to spill coffee (on a keyboard). There is more with the pill fiend wife, the frustrated married friends, and the shark spirit, but I'll leave that for you to chance watching to learn more. I'd say you probably need to be stoned for this movie to have a good pace and make perfect sense.

history.review_title: it's more of a collection of stories you'd tell around a campfire - like the story of the name with a hook for ...
history.text: This isn't a fancy show, it's more of a collection of stories you'd tell around a campfire - like the story of the name with a hook for a hand. So if you like small tales, this is a good show for a handful of small local tales. If you want large grand stories and a Holly like production, then this isn't for you. The stories range from old tales of dragons to explain a landscape feature all the way to an old lady some locals thought were a witch in the 1890's. Again, think campfire stories. It reminded me of the radio shows my Dad used to listen to where they narrate a story. I gave it a 3 star because the stories weren't as epic as others I know and it isn't high quality. But it is was still nice to listen to each narrator tell a story for 12-15 mins at a time. To me it was good; not great, just good. It reminded me of someone reading paraphrased versions of Grimm tales.

history.title: Who Is Jesus?: Building a Comprehensive Case
history.review_title: I loved series 1 and 2 as they were well represented ...
history.text: I loved series 1 and 2 as they were well represented and provided a good arguments backed up with facts. This one had too much bias and misinformation that I was annoyed with it. For instance, the lecturer said that,"Jesus was pierced in the heart..." No, the Bible says he was pierced in the side, not the heart. And he uses baseless arguments such as people rally against Jesus's teachings, but never against other historical figures such as Plato. That is absolutely not true; just got to a college and study philosophy not to mention you can find periodicals and Google around to find articles discussing the merits and dislikes to Buddha, Freud, Adams, John Locke. Basically, if you made history, there will be someone to critique every nuance of what you said and what you might have meant. Another point he makes is that people question whether Jesus was real, but no one questions whether Julius Caesar was real. You can say the same for Confucius and Buddha, and many historical figures. My problem is that he makes claims and does not back them up with facts, and his claims are actually his assertions which can be misleading. I give this 2 stars because he still does touch upon good points of discussion, but I just wish he did more research and less preaching. Season 1 and 2 made me sit up and say 'wow', Season 3 not so much.

history.title: Stories We Tell
history.text: This is a thoroughly engaging film. I love the narrative voice and think that it is way underutilized in straightforward, dramatic films. This piece is nothing but narrative voices against an excellent visual background. These are real people, sometimes struggling, telling the story of their mother/wife/lover. It is a complete success in drawing you into their world and holding your attention. I considered giving it five stars. Its limitation, I think, is that the mother's secrets were not all that remarkable, far from it, actually. Most of life is, I suppose, not all that remarkable -- the familiar dramatic themes of domestic life tend to play out again and again, which is not to say that we ever should or ever will lose interest in them. But I was somehow set up for some more surprising events that became secrets. I also thought that the film was not really successful in the effort to demonstrate the familiar phenomenon of different observers coming away with different stories -- there was not much disagreement. What we have here is unremarkable human drama in slightly exotic lives told very engagingly and with a lot of feeling. Pretty much anyone raised in a family has equally compelling family material although few would be so successful in bringing it to life on the screen.

What was magic in the "The Company" is ho-hum here, and it may still have been the best thing in the production. Otherwise, it was just a less tasteful and much less convincing swirl of the off-stage lives of the mostly young, sexy artists. history.title: The Appalachians
history.review_title: So much ~bigger~ than I first imagined
history.text: I stumbled on this series as it aired on my local PBS station and ordered it after watching the first episode. I have not yet gotten around to watching my own copy but I keep stumbling across it as it continues to air. Every episode startles me just as the first one did -- it is one majestic story piled upon another. In the beginning, of course, I did not know what I was watching. I first thought it was about the folkways of improvised American religion in the hinterlands. But then it morphed into the wonderful story of Appalachian music, which I supposed to be the wrap-up. Only slowly did I grasp that it is an epic history of a region and its people, profound and heartfelt at every turn. This is a wonderful series; I hope that they are watching it in Manhattan, Hollywood, and wherever clueless elites gather.

history.title: Charlie Rose (February 18, 2005)
history.review_title: Exploitation of the American story...by Charlie Rose
history.text: The asking price for this DVD is obscene. Charlie Rose has a right to be paid for his work...we are not communists, after all. But this strikes me as egregiously exploitative and greedy. Arthur Miller was a profound voice in his literary critique of a certain aspect of American life in the middle of the last century. But that was a half a century ago, and I resent Charlie Rose, Inc. bottling up the later-life reflections of this man and making them available only at an extravagant price. It is Miller, after all, who was an important figure, not the shallow and posturing Charlie Rose. I do not at all deny that Rose -- in his best moments -- has a great interviewer's instinct for going after what is important. But he is very well paid for his work without treating a national treasure as his own property.

history.title: Bicycle Dreams: A Cycling Film [DVD]
history.review_title: Helped me redefine my attitude toward the bike
history.text: I found both this film and the similar "Race Across America" boring and unpleasant. I cared about no one in the films, there is no story nor is there any sense of the magnificent panorama of America rolling by. At some point, grit and heroics (in a pointless endeavor) reveal the tedious characters of the participants. I recognize that with distance cycling -- as in other endurance sports -- the capacity to tolerate the suffering is a big part of the endeavor. Folks who need this are welcome to it, but it is uninteresting as they flatten themselves into this blinkered, one-dimensional obsession. I have recently returned to cycling as a senior citizen after a half dozen years completely off the bike. The recovery of fitness is exhilarating, and I find myself beginning to think about more modestly demanding cycling adventures like a 500-mile, non-competitive tour across my own state. For me, an endeavor of a mere 500 miles (including a couple of mountain days) would be fanatical and desperate and dangerously unhealthy endeavor, although I recognize that it is not at all an unreasonable thing for very fit cyclists who routinely put in a lot of miles. But I turn away from the siren song of the irrelevantly heroic. I will challenge myself within reasonable limits and try to extend myself on the bike, but I will not get crazy. And this RAAM thing is a crazy stunt for anybody. Anybody who could do it is not someone whom I would like to have a beer with or even care about (or want to watch a film about). (All of this cannot help but make me reflect on the Tour de France, which I follow and enjoy. I must say that I have thought a few times that many of the TdF stars are essentially uninteresting and one-dimensional. The Tour, though, is somewhat redeemed for me by the team aspect and all of the complexity and the various goals within the race short of being the overall GC winner. And then there is the fact that the athletes do, at least, sleep at night, eat well, and get a lot care. So it is not like watching to see who can hold his hand in a flame for the longest time.)

Don't know about that but he certainly is a grand storyteller. I saw part of this on PBS and instantly came here to order it. As I write this review, it is due to be released next week. Edit: Saw more on another PBS showing, the story -- in some detail -- of how a young Chinese seeker (monk?) sometime around the fifth century CE set off on foot to travel west through China skirting the Himalayas, swung around them through Afghanistan, and then trekked eastward into the heart of India. He was after knowledge of Buddhism. After many years he returned bringing many scared scrolls and introduced Buddhism to China. Had adventures, etc. The Emperor was intrigued.

history.title: Life: Season Two
history.review_title: Not as good as it should have been...
history.text: After watching all of Season 1 over the course of two days I was eagerly awaiting the Season 2 DVD set to come in the mail. Alas, what a letdown! I don't know if the writers changed but Season 2 just doesn't come close to the first season. Crewe's search for the answer to who framed him and slaughtered his friend's family takes a backseat to a series of quite mediocre murder whodunits. The stories meander all over the place and the writing just isn't close to as crisp and believable as Season 1. Just a sample of silliness: 1. In one episode Crews fires four shots from his service revolver into the wall of a cop bar to demonstrate how cops are trained to shoot in the academy! Come on! Did he think what might be behind that wall. This is gratuitous and reckless firing of his weapon. One of the major themes of Season 1 was Crewes being careful not to give the department heads a reason to relieve him of duty. Here's a reason in a gift package tied up with ribbons and bows! Yet, that whole idea of the homicide department trying to get rid of Crewes, an integral part of the background mystery in Season 1, is no longer even a minor theme in Season 2. 2. Reese and Tidwell as "an item"?? Totally and completely unbelievable. There's just NO connection there. I would have better believed Crewes and Tidwell's female predecessor in Season 1! 3. Crews pretends to be the chauffeur for the rich guy who's become one of the suspects in the "big mystery"? Cmon, how many ways does this not make any sense? 4. Crews' Zen banter... wow, it's bad now. It had some depth and meaning in Season 1. Now he's dropping such useless garbage as "Did you know figs are 55% sugar?" Reese now has good reason to question his sanity. 5. Storyline is very "jumpy." Reese & Crews will be dealing with the current murder investigation and then with no smooth transition Crews is following up some lead on his own mystery. It's like they filmed the two storylines entirely separately and then spliced them together without any attempt to integrate them into one episode. What heightens this disjointedness is that the characters in the current murder investigation aren't involved anymore in Crews' mystery. Tidwell doesn't even appear to be aware of the issue and Reese, who would clearly have an interest since her dad was involved in the sinister events, never even asks about it. Totally unbelievable. There are many more but I'm depressing myself listing them. I haven't finished Season 2 yet because, unlike with Season 1, I can't bring myself to watch more than 1 or 2 episodes at a sitting. I understand with gratitude that the series does resolve Crew's mystery by the last episode. If this resolution is truly satisfying I may modify this "2" grade. But I have a bad feeling about that. Will post a followup when I'm done.

history.title: The Bridge: Die Bruecke
history.review_title: As war movies go, not bad...
history.text: This isn't a bad war movie, especially considering when and how it was made. It has an evocative atmosphere, with fog and smoke swirling about, especially at night, adding to the terror of guarding a bridge waiting for the enemy to show up. The first half hour is decidedly tedious. Yes, it's true the story needed to establish the background of small-town German youngsters being dragooned from their semi-idyllic into becoming cannon fodder for the Nazis to slow down the Allied advance. But it went on too long. The movie redeems itself with the battle scenes, which are nicely done, although I've never seen American tanks who look anything like the armored vehicle used here. The premise behind the battle is hard to understand. Evidently to protect these youngsters, who were drafted literally the day before and received almost no training, they're assigned to an experienced corporal who is told to have them "guard" a small bridge (in their own hometown) which is going to be blown up anyway in 24 hours, right after the first American tanks have crossed over. Presumably this will minimize exposing them to danger at a time when the war was fast approaching its end anyway. First, I don't get why you'd blow the bridge AFTER some of the enemy has crossed over. This isn't sound defensive strategy. Second, assigning these 7 "kids" to a bridge which is known about to be approached by substantial enemy forces, including armor, is hardly keeping them out of harm's way. Third, evidently they gave no written orders to the corporal, who is waylaid in the town when he goes looking for "coffee" by military police who are probably going to execute him, so he runs and then gets shot down dead. If the corporal had written orders he would have avoided these consequences, which left the 7 kids entirely unsupervised. Fourth, there is a demolitions unit assigned to the bridge but they're hiding in a basement in the town, watching for the first Yank tanks to cross, and while they know the kids are guarding the bridge, they do nothing to try to communicate with them. In fact, they express frustration during the valiant fight between the kids and the Americans, lamenting that the Wehrmacht WANTS some Ami tanks to cross but the kids are doing such a good job fighting they're holding up the enemy advance. Fifth, it's unreasonable that these youngsters would handle themselves so well. Sure, they might have had the spirit and boldness of youth but where did they learn to shoot automatic rifles, machine guns and panzerfausts? There's no indication they could have learned all this in their ONE AFTERNOON of military training. (It's mentioned repeatedly they were all called up just the day before.) The acting quality is mixed. There's a bit too much melodrama at times, especially in scenes involving soldiers being injured or killed. A couple of the scenes are laughingly bad, as when one boy discovers his father in bed with the fraulein that he moons over himself. All in all, well worth watching once, and certainly notable when considered in context of when and how it was filmed.

history.title: Crime Scene Cleaner: Season 1
history.review_title: Not all that much "crime scene cleaning" but still enjoyable---and funny!
history.text: Interesting series, about as good as I hoped it would be. Surprisingly, there isn't really all that much about crime scene cleaning. Each episode is primarily a discussion between the "star" and various people he runs into---friends and neighbors of the deceased, and others, a shaman and even the murderer at least once! It's actually a very "TALKY" series, with almost no action. I thought maybe our hero would sometimes solve the crime but actually he has no interest in doing that: he wants to do the job, eat his baloney lunch, get paid and go home and watch football and drink beer. The funniest episode is the third, which also features a cameo from Burkow & Koenig. He's cleaning one victim's apartment when a call girl makes her scheduled visit. A very cute encounter ensues, only interrupted when B&K show up to collect the "evidence" that was left behind in the bloody bathroom. I enjoyed the 10 half-hour episodes in the box. I do wish I hadn't watched them back to back within a couple of days. A bit too much dosage of an amusing and interesting, but not awe-inspiring series. This is one show that would be more enjoyable watched at the half-hour a week pace, since there is no continuity to speak of and each episode stands alone.

history.title: Beck: Episodes 16-18 (Set 6)
history.text: I wouldn't have rated this 5 STARS from the start, but as others have stated, the series has improved dramatically---and in comedic terms as well---over the years. history.title: Horatio Hornblower - The New Adventures (Loyalty / Duty)
history.review_title: Cheap enough, but only 2 "movies" and not that great either---where is the closed captioning??
history.text: I enjoyed the earlier DVD, which had a lot more content---PLUS English subtitles (for hard of hearing.) The menu here lists CLOSED CAPTIONS but when you click all it tells you is check your DVD PLAYER to see if it can provide. How can the DVD PLAYER provide subtitles without the content already being on the DVD? SPOILER ALERT for below: This is swashbuckling story-telling but I expected a bit more believability. Hornblower never gets shot or sword-cut, even when fighting masses of Frenchmen at point-blank range. His ragtag band of sailors never get hurt either, at least not the ones who appear in every episode. He and a tiny band of men are always able to sneak into castles and forts, blowing up cannons, rescuing prisoners and just generally running around at will while the stupid enemy is without a clue. In one of these episodes Hornblower and crew slaughter a French artillery unit firing cannons on one level a fort while the French troops on the next level down notice nothing and just keep firing their own guns. This enables Hornblower to lower the aim of one of his captured cannons and wipe out the entire lower level of French soldiers! Yeah, sure. Correct me if I'm wrong here, but he marries his former landlady's daughter just so she'll accept the money he gave her to get her and her mother out of debtor's prison? Isn't that going really above and beyond?? Hey, they're enjoyable to watch once when there's nothing else on TV. Unfortunately, that's a comedown from the earlier movies which were quite engaging.

history.title: A French Village: Season 2
history.review_title: Superb series about France under the German occupation during WW2
history.text: SPOILER ALERT ahead! I'm proud to be the first to review this excellent program! Superb series, engrossing, exciting and intriguing. Almost never any dead time or slow spots in this engaging drama of a small French village under the German occupation during World War II. The tensions between the French who collaborate in the interests of protecting their friends, family and neighbors, and those who resist---mostly for political reasons (a lot are Communists) is explored in a serious, non-trivializing manner. For example, the doctor/mayor struggles mightily with his dilemma: he cooperates with the Wehrmacht leadership in order to protect the citizens who he has lived with all his life. But he gets grief for it from some people, because it requires him to make decisions which hurt the very same people. Like at one point the Germans plan to execute 20 hostages because of a Resistance attack on a German officer. He is able to negotiate this down to 10 hostages---but HE must decide which 10. You sympathize with his agony over deciding which of his neighbors will be killed. These are decisions which will surely plague him the remainder of his life. The series offers a great deal of historical realism, from my reading of true-life accounts of the Occupation. Plus my mother and grandmother, along with their relatives, lived 4 years in Paris under the Germans so I have some direct familiarity with people who lived under the experience. However there are some incidents which strike me as rather incredible. I don't consider them to hurt my enjoyment of the series and I doubt they would yours. Unfortunately, they want the "heroes" of the show to do heroic things and survive to appear in the next episode so some incidents stretch credibility. Like when the mayor aids his brother's escape, after the brother is being pursued for direct involvement in the cold-blooded shooting of a German officer. The German secret police, the SD, arrest him and start to even torture him but the local Wehrmacht commander, who has a cordial working relationship with the mayor, intercedes and frees him. He also arranges to send the SD man to the Eastern Front! This strikes me as incredible in the extreme. Sure during the initial months of the Occupation the Germans tried to tread somewhat lightly ON the French in the hope that they could eventually bring Vichy into the Axis as a full-fledged member. But surely a small town mayor who assists the escape of an assassin is going to get some kind of punishment beyond a few bruises. A similar incident occurs earlier where a woman is tortured into providing the name of her Communist cellmate and then released. She quickly tips off her comrades who take action to avoid capture. Surely the Germans at least would have kept her incarcerated until they rounded up the members of the cell. What I also like greatly about the series is that most of the characters are complex... not the usual black-and-white paintings typical of war movies. The Commandant is a human being; the German sergeant is an artist who falls in love with the French school teacher;, the mayor's brother, albeit a communist, questions the mindless orders that come down from headquarters; Schwartz, played masterfully by Thierry Godard (Spiral) is torn about keeping his business alive (and his employees working) by providing lumber and concrete to the Wehrmacht; even the SD chief, Muller, while reprehensible in the end, is shown as a creature with a human side, a very rare fictional depiction for a member of the Gestapo/SD. In some ways the worst-behaved person in the entire show is the mayor's wife, played by the delectable Audrey Fleurot (of Spiral), who cheats on her saintly spouse repeatedly, finally sleeping with the SD officer and even going beyond the pale when she uses information obtained from her nephew to tip off the SD that her hunted brother-in-law will be visiting the mayor's home secretly that night. This is a betrayal so palpable that the mayor's decision to divorce her finally comes as a relief. The series shows its stereotypical French origin in the number of instances of adultery, fornication, pregnancies outside of marriage, etc., which only adds to the intensity of the stories! More seriously it also addresses the complex and sometimes deplorable attitude French people had/have toward the Jews who live in their communities. Highly recommended! I only hope they rush out Season 3 through 6, with English subtitles, since it will be frustrating to have to wait months or years to see how the series advances.

history.title: Parade's End
history.text: Tedious beyond tolerance. I watched the first one and a half episodes and just had to shut it off. It's not as if I don't like British dramas, even slow-paced melodramas focused on the elite of early 20th century or 19th century British society. But this one crawled and truly had stretches which were apparently intentionally incomprehensible. Like what's the deal with the minister who starts talking about self-abuse right in the middle of mixed company in the dinner party? Was he nuts? What's the point? The cuckolded "hero" has zero personality and one has no sympathy for him since he seems to create, or at least aid and abet, his own problems. His fornicating cheating wife, she's cute enough but she's one-dimensional as a classically jaded useless member of the British upper crust. Rather than evoking a sense of sympathy for the destruction the coming World War will inflict on this class of British society you, or I at least, find myself thinking it to be a fortunate event if it leads to end of this kind of uselessness. I suspect the books are better, as is often the case, but I think I can find about 1000 novels to read before I test this thesis. I'm certainly glad I paid only the "used" price for this.

history.title: Better Call Saul: Season 1 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Good not great but worth watching if you can stand the slow pacing and if you resist comparing it to BB
history.text: Takes a while to get "into" but I find Better Call Saul to be an enjoyable show to watch. It suffers by comparison to Breaking Bad, for sure, since the pace of Saul is glacial compared to BB---except for very brief spurts. The law firm stuff is generally boring but I do greatly enjoy supporting actors like Mike and the crazy drug dealers. It's very interesting to see the old guy before he became crippled and his whack-a-mole nuts nephew who, one wonders, how he survives the 6 years until he encounters Walt since his behavior is so over the top even his underlings want to assassinate him. I'd have gone with 3.5 stars here, if I could, since 3 stars says "mediocre", which it isn't, but 4 stars says excellent, which it probably isn't---quite. No way 5 stars, which I reserve for a series that held me riveted and which I could watch time and time again. Saul ain't that good. If you watch the first 2-3 episodes and think it's too slow-paced and offbeat for you, the best I can say it does get better but THIS IS the pace of the show so if you really don't like that you probably won't ever really enjoy Saul.

history.title: A French Village: Season 5 [DVD]
history.text: Once again I'm proud to be the first to post a review here and commend this fantastic series. Despite 5 seasons' worth of episodes the quality remains high, the drama intense, the acting superb, the realism----well, very real, and the plot twists and turns unpredictable, engrossing and fully believable. This series is so superb that I'm going to buy the 6th season in the French-only language release, even though my French isn't that strong, and hope that enabling the French-language subtitles, and having a French-English dictionary handy, will enable me to absorb the 6th season, because frankly I don't want to wait for them to release it with English subtitles! A series to recommend heartily and unreservedly to anyone who is interested in history, and indeed to anyone who is interested in human drama.
