An actress who, unfortunately had been caught in that bizarre thing called "Mommie Dearest" plays a wonderful character here, RUTYANA _________ (I am embarrassed that only two hours have gone by and her last name escapes me......) The other is Meryl Streep, in all the naturalness of her youthful acting before she became the queen of the MIMICS, of MIMESIS.........Not of Interpretation, no, but of copying a personality's voice, movements, gestures and offering them to us as some sort of extraordinary performance. The Meryl Streep we see here, and a bit later in that harrowing film "Sophie's Choice" has left us long ago. The ravages of war in a personality before Psychiatry had invented the term "Post-traumatic-stress-disorder" (remember "Shell-shocked"?) are rendered, well, let's just say that although they are there, they do not satisfy. A director's mistake, perhaps? Do see the movie. Nothing to do with Vietnam, and only thrilling enough for all you "sado-Masochists" out there (in here too) in the viciousness of that monstrosity that society's structure keeps in check for most of us. A warning: those with upper-class pretensions should skip the first ENTIRE hour or they will start having too much guilt, or too much boredom and sneering at the antics of a bunch of people who even in a wedding can behave like animals.............

history.title: The People vs. Larry Flynt
history.text: Given all those negative words, the positives are impossible to forget-------and the fact is that that REPULSIVE woman by the name of Courtney Love gives a fantastic performance that perhaps------only perhaps-------manages to eclipse the GREAT performance by Harrelson. Or was Ms. Love simply playing herself?, as my companion wisely noted! Has she done any more acting? I do not know whether this was filmed before the death of her husband, but tell me if I am wrong-----I believe she became a very wealthy woman after that since she inherited most of Cobain's estate, so arguably because of that she never pushed herself----- and nothing to deter talent (very broadly speaking) than being very wealthy. Where do you think some acquaintances of mine ended? Not as leaders and great successes, but "losers" that quietly pursued "careers" that were purely imagination------aaah! those days when in certain circles nobody asked you "What do you do?". But perhaps we are better off today. The director carries us on a rollercoaster ride that can't stop or slow down since perhaps there wasn't a good screenwriter to give the movie depth. The film remains basically a "telenovela" (our new preferred way for "soap opera" that-----no offense to fans of "Days of our lives"--------begin and end within six months or so.......and the HEAT they emanate!!) But I digress----forgive me. Everything is just about "by the book", so to speak, but there's a lifeless quality to the structure of the whole act. Again, performances are STRONG, and they help us along the way, but then all this "OPERATIC", ridiculous music in so many scenes give a cheap grandiosity to the whole thing. Ludicrous----- just as ludicrous as the idealized portrait of Mr. Flynt himself. Basically a repugnant human being, Harrelson is here to give us a glamorized, falsified version of Flynt. Can you tell me how is it that in Bio-pics the protagonist is always so good-looking next to the real thing? Can't they find UGLY people just as in this case? Well, the fact is that there is a moment when FLYNT himself plays a very conservative, bloated judge that must have been a fantastic time for him (and US as well!). Of course, you need to recognize Flint, and this is roughly 20 years ago. Not to forget! Edward (?) NORTON, looking fresh as a kid out of High School, already had the wonderful skills that he was to prove to us over the years again and again. The movie's CORE and ------mistake?-------is the issue of the First Amendment. The reason why Flynt wins the case, at the Supreme Court no less, is because of a fake advertisement on his HUSTLER magazine in which that master of reincarnation of Jesus Jerry Falwell appears having sex with his mother. It is something ugly that you or I would not want to be humiliated by in our own lives. But the First Amendment, that mostly dormant one (?) in our magnificent constitution until, perhaps, "Larry Flynt VERSUS....." (or is my history correct?) brings Flynt to triumph when invoked convincingly enough so that what is basically a parody can be protected from Libel, etc. That has come to have serious positive (and not so positive) changes in our society's freedom of speech. The perplexing thing is that to a great extent that has nothing much (please tell me otherwise) to do with Flynt's dramatic fights with Justice over PORNOGRAPHY. Of course, the first amendment has, perhaps since then, opened the door to free distribution of Porn all across America (not to mention the NET and its intractable "problem" over whether we can limit or not the gigantic amount of PORN that has become the norm, and for which, quite seriously speaking, has made Flynt's publications almost a work of literature, no?). The movie simply shifts course and from Pornography itself it jumps to the protection of parody and anything you want to say about any public figure no matter how disgusting AS LONG as you inject some kind of tongue-in-cheek. Am I right that a program like "Saturday Night Live" was greatly improved by this decision? Perhaps you can guess that one subject follows the other, but it is an obscure connection that perhaps someone reading this can illustrate for us. For that, Mr. Flynt will be remembered------surprisingly enough that the decision was unanimous, in a court eternally divided 5-to-4. That is perhaps too much "thinking" to try to inject into this, again, failure of a course on LAW, but even without it the film remains a mash-up of biography--------not to mention that this "moderate" (your writer) found it extremely celebratory of its liberal viewpoint, unfairly leaving us in the dark (irresponsibly so) about the counter-arguments. Mr. Norton exudes wisdom in his defense, but NO ONE does for Conservatism. Terrible history, moderately exciting entertainment.

history.title: Repulsion (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Deneuve in a MAGNIFICENTLY MAGNETIC Performance......
history.text: Deneuve literally CHEWS up the movie. And that brings us to consider the role of a director when it comes to a movie like this. Clearly, being her second role since being catapulted to stardom with that ridiculous "musical" The Umbrellas of..........( the French NEVER understood the meaning of a Musical), she must have been "directed" for this by Polansky, the EPHEBOPHILE. But how much credit should a director take when having cast such a superior actor as MS. Deneuve? If there is any honesty in him------very LITTLE. A marvelous example is BRANDO-----perhaps the epitome of "self-directing"-----you did not direct Brando, and you knew it from the beginning. She, clearly, so early in her career was not Brando, and some actors, no matter their brilliance rely on their director to act in whatever way they "should". But, again, with work such as this one I don't believe that such a performance was "created" by Polansky. Do you find that this opinion is mistaken? The movie has dated a bit. Scenes like the one where arms come out of the walls made us (the group that were watching it at home last night) titter and snort. This only happened once, Thanks be to the Gods. But it is borderline-farcical. What is curious to me (will you call me a Macho misogynist?) is that up until we see the deterioration of her character into what is clearly a sad, pathetic psychotic, deluded victim I have a great compassion for her, but after the first killing my heart grows cold and I no longer have the slightest pity for this poor woman. The fact that it is the (beautiful) man in love with her contributes to this, and the fact that she kills the landlord in such a vicious way renders her repugnant to my VISCERAL MIND-------let us stress visceral, since my intellect recognizes the hopelessness of what drives her to this. Her profound depression leading to this is heartbreakingly sad. For a while we played with motive, until we "patched it together", so to speak, and kind of convinced ourselves that those scenes in which she clearly is being raped are the key that Polansky offers us as perhaps rather simplistic an answer as to WHY. What is not so easy to interpret is the monster behind it all. Polansky gives you a SLY moment that, indeed, had us recoil and be surprised and, yes, REPULSED at that grotesque smile that only appears on the sister's lover for a moment. And so you have to, perhaps, come to the conclusion that HE is the perpetrator of these repugnant acts. BUT IS HE? We will never know---I doubt that Polanski has "confessed" it during an interview, He need not have been---------he may have lusted after her for long, she ignoring him, and he, a piece of filth, enjoys her tragedy. By the way, the woman who plays the sister offers us an unforgettable performance to rival Deneuve, particularly when she falls apart upon the discovery of the corpse. Why 3 stars instead of 4? A kind of stingy "It's Okay"?..... I hesitated with 4, but there is an element of "terror" film, of "HORROR" genre that robs the film of the potency of Ms. Deneuve 's performance. Perhaps the movie needed RESTRAINT, from which he could not, well, RESTRAIN himself so that thinking of MONEY he "sells out" to a mass audience. A great work of "entertainment" that fails to uncover the PROFOUND issues that can destroy a personality, a human being's core to, as in this case (by no means, as we know, the response of the majority of women that are raped) to its disintegration. The film tries, but perhaps it is to a certain degree an impossibility. I have been pondering what my very greatest GENIUS of film, Bergman would have done with the subject. Still, to be 19 (as she was at the time) and give as difficult and complex a performance as this is to be remembered for always. She must remain proud over this achievement. NOT SO with Mr. POlanski.

history.title: Callas Forever [DVD]
history.review_title: Mr. Zeffirelli's failure of a Paean to CALLAS..............
history.text: It is fascinating to find that 94% of the reviewers of this film here at Amazon rate it 2 to 4 stars (from "it's OK" to "I love it") to a movie that is a dull travesty, a ludicrous film, 120 minutes of which only the last 30 approach anything remotely to be considered inspiring. And remember that Ms. Callas was Zeffirelli's best friend, or one that bewitched him. The grotesque joke is that the premise of the film is based on what can be magnificent fuel to all of Callas' enemies----and they are infinite. The basic "contraption" is that Callas is despondent, a recluse, it is 1977 (the same year that she dies) and her close friend, a film director, convinces her to go into the studio and lip-synch arias from "Carmen" as an actual cinematic story (not a concert). She goes along with the concept, very reluctantly for a long while. The "joke" as I say, is that Callas was, and continues to be considered an ACTRESS, not a great singer by any possibility, by many, many people who do not understand and cannot recognize the profundity of her art. I myself, a great Callas fan since I heard her voice in film (cannot remember) where she was singing "Addio del Passato" from Traviata, recognized a voice that was not, decidedly the beautiful voice of Victoria de los Angeles, by any chance, and yet moved me to tears with her delivery. A friend and I have had countless arguments about this. And people continue to. The FACT is that, yes, the voice was imperfect, and she was an actress (and what an actress, from what I read, and snippets that I have seen that do not exactly convey this reasoning) but more than an actress thanks to her physicality, her acting was the VOICE itself. The greatest of opera singers are not the ones who deliver the highest notes but those that can simply utter a phrase with so much humanity, so much wisdom that they are incomparable. That was Callas. With this lip-synching that she is convinced to do Zeffirelli, again, is telling us that, after all, we can unite the recordings with her great acting, which she purportedly still has and presto! we have a magnificent movie. But Callas was an artist of the greatest dignity and standards and this whole thing would turn out to be a ridiculous pantomime. It is even "sadder" since you have three actors of very high caliber: Joan Plowright, Fanny Ardant, and Jeremy Irons. All of them go through the paces with the most ridiculous of screenplays. Ms. Plowright has to deliver lines like: "This is 1977----Satan is redundant". The mediocrity is everywhere. Perhaps it isn't surprising, as I just discovered that, along with some great moments as a director, hideous things like "The Blue Lagoon" with Brooke Shields are part of his "repertoire"---not to mention a rather recent fiasco with his staging of "Tosca" at the Met in NY. No, I think that Callas would have been deeply dissatisfied with this "paean" to her: he certainly could have thought something better. Not to mention that Fanny Ardant does not look AT ALL like a woman who is about to die of a heart attack within months! She looks magnificent, the very portrait of health, and by then Callas was a broken woman. Of course, it is all fantasy, but you are stretching the truth with this. As well, this man does the very unimaginative thing to act as if this is the 1950's, when every movie had to have a love affair inserted no matter the subject, and so does he, showing his lack of imagination: Irons is gay, but being 2002 Zeffirelli decides NOT to have Irons' young male stud even share a kiss, and Callas herself has a tentative moment with her lead from the picture---this is all thrown in as nothing more than filler. Again, it is simply unimaginable that any great artist, as dignified and with an ego the size of a supernova (which she has been since, say 1950) would have in any way accepted the ludicrous project of acting out a movie moving her lips to the recordings that made her the international star she remains, without breaking down. Let me put it to you this way: the GREATEST moment in the film is the credits as they slowly roll by........why is that??? Callas sings "Vissi D'Arte" from Tosca in the background and it is a moment where you know that every Callas fan remained seated unlike all the other movies where everyone, rather rudely, runs for the door. That hands it to you in a nutshell.............

history.title: Hello, Dolly!
history.review_title: Aaah, the MUSICAL, that "forgotten" art now called "Spiderman"...............
history.text: I did not grow up with the Musical.....I am 52, but my partner is 64 and he has beautiful memories of going to Broadway in the mid-60's and early 70's UNTIL Mr. Stephen Sondheim appears on the scene, RE-CREATES, contradicts, re-invents, and some say DESTROYS the musical. My partner does not have fond feelings for him. For Rodgers and Hart, oh my! For Cole Porter, wow!-------and then there's Jerry Herman, perhaps the last gasp of the old wonderful, tender, silly musical that runs from, say, the 1920's to the 60's...... That "last gasp" would more or less be this......... You have very probably heard a teenager see any of these DINOSAURS and cluelessly say: "How ridiculous! People breaking into song in the middle of a conversation?!". Perhaps we should blame so-called "modernism" for its death-------among many other things that modernism has left us with---- like.......architecture?.......Well, I am NOT in any way against modernism---certainly not of "REALISM"-----neo-realism, or else---------those that taught us that "suspension-of-disbelief" was to be given in very minimal dosages..... Ad so we come to Ms. Streisand with those last gasps, indeed: "Funny Girl", a beautiful achievement, "Funny Lady" (not yet seen by me, but generally considered a mediocre product) and this...... I have never liked Streisand, never cared for that "Brooklynese" chatter that she displays here in all its glory, which we must assume that she simply decided never to "clean up" and be what she was. BRAVO for her! Bravo for that nose! (By the way, do you know the amount of talent that Brooklyn produced in the 20th century? It is staggering----all magnificently talented jews). But I think that rare is the person who will not warm up to this woman's tender voice. It is a voice where, interestingly, all that "vulgar" chatter and accent disappears, and she delivers her songs in a wonderful diction to begin with, extending all her SSSSS's to the infinite, and every word carefully enunciated. Her voice is beautiful, unique, humane, needful, sober, honest, heartbreaking...you can go on and on.....The arrangements are too sentimental a lot of the time, but even then she pierces you with that magnetism, that slow manner that sings truth. Here, the subject which I tried to present to you is in full display. It is exquisitely SILLY, a "turn-of-the-century" story in NYCity that is simply an excuse for Streisand to show us what a wonderful poseur she was in the sixties at a time when Rock and Roll was changing the culture, the very essence of music, coarse and revealing, vulgar and profound, and I don't know who went to these movies but I can safely assume that the audiences were mostly post-30's in their age?, certainly not teenagers and certainly not people listening to the Stones or Hendrix, or the Beatles' late work. The illusions were dead, the "suspension-of-disbelief" was no longer possible, broadly speaking, and again, the ridiculousness of dancing in the middle of a conversation, of a thin plot that demands very little attention defy your temper-----I left the room a number of times, coming back to the words of "don't worry, you did not miss anything"....Ha! And yet, it is moving in its own "passe" way----for us getting older it is almost more of a testament to the fact that everything will change and not even our own genres will subsist and time is pushing us away.....Don't talk to me about J-lo and Beyonce and even PATHETIC Madonna (who I grew up with!) at the age of 56 unable to transition into middle-age and showing us a sad human being trapped in a hollow image that insists on being sexual and "depraved" and all anew, ready to devour.... But...the movie. Again, depending on who you are, you may or may not have a good time. It is NOT the musical as an example of greatness, certainly not an example of the embodiment of the musical genre. There's a tiredness to it, an absurdity that wants you to say----"all right, enough!". It is, I believe, 2+ hours and yet as I write that I realize that it rarely lags. Walter Matthau is not my idea of a great leading man, unlike Rex Harrison accompanying Audrey Hepburn in "My Fair Lady", but it will have to do, no? There are almost no exceptional numbers, EXCEPT....yes, "Hello Dolly", but it is my confusion on whether "Hello Dolly" the song was a huge hit for Streisand, because for two decades I have heard it sung (not to mention "trumpeted"?) by Louis Armstrong in a marvellous way, an unforgettable way, yet here he is, thrown in awkwardly in the middle of a long musical scene and an audience who wouldn't have known him would be perplexed (not to mention that he is not playing) of the two of them together, he the ONLY BLACK person in the entire movie to be given anything of a role (historically correct, but also making you wonder whether this was done so that the segment could be excised in the south? In 1969?----I have no idea). Again, listen to Armstrong's version and the pure, sheer JOY of his delivery shake you to the core. I believe this was Armstrong's LAST hit (and a super-hit that topped the charts---in the middle of all that Rock and roll revolution) before his death. Watch the movie. But you will not be missing much, to be brutally honest, if you don't. A fan of Streisand? By all means. She delivers. For a "girl" in her late 20's to show so much poise, so great an amount of sophistication, class, acting skills, singing, of course----it makes you realize what a great talent we had here and how much we have descended to forty years later. Or is it old age slowly creeping up on me, and the pull of the past?................

history.title: Bonnie and Clyde (Two-Disc Special Edition)
history.text: For a long while you fear sitting down to watch this movie, since you have been (mis)led to believe it to be a work of consummate ART (caps required). You need not fear. Tonight I sat down to two hours of magnificent VACUITY that ends up with that closing shot which makes you laugh out loud, since it is considered to be the "breakthrough" moment in american cinema which led to the explosion of all that violence which came to be necessary to attract middle-brow audiences thirsty for blood, and you realize how out of proportion such a statement is. Well, good for all those "scholars" who find such a trajectory an action of great importance. But the movie ITSELF is a complete disappointment. The first thing that came out of my mouth while quietly at home with friends and not having to be pestered by "Sssshhh"s when at the theatre was "What an irresponsible movie!". But that soon led to the exquisitely TEDIOUS scene after scene of the same cheap stuff. Again and again, poor sad human beings are subjected, during the Depression to the indignities of being robbed of their pennies (and lives, as it progresses). Mr. Penn proves himself to be exquisitely unimaginative with his constant rat-tat-tat of bank after bank, with blood delightfully presented in "joyously" cosmetic form. True, what could he do but film the pathetic story of these two white-trash individuals, who just happen to be made beautiful by Hollywood (who wants to see UGLY people when dealing with a "fun ride" in which you need as much aesthetics (very minor ones---let us not confuse the word with that seriou and rich area of Philosophy)--------as possible? So B. & C. are offered to us in the panoramic pair of beauty by the names of Warren Beatty (who, unimaginatively uses the same slow-motion cheap ending of this movie when many years later directing and starring in "Bugsy"---true genius, eh?) AND that great unique beauty Ms. Faye Dunaway-------and watch her mannerisms closely to realize the short range of this actress as you are remember again and again that those same moves are in full bloom 12 years later with "Mommie Dearest" (unquestionably, and bizarrely so the best acting job of her precarious career). If we are to have trash occupy space it better be beautiful and stylish. That SOIGNEE "Park Avenue" hair on Bonnie, a hick that barely can speak a proper sentence! Those magnificent eyes and smile in that nobody named Clyde! It is true that both offer us a pleasurable ride throughout more than a bit of the film, acting that is mannered and self-conscious (read: impossible to suspend disbelief), and that to be honest everyone behaves beautifully in their acting jobs. It is also true that, new to me, the idea of a man suffering from impotence during his "best" years, especially one who is to be such a "lady-killer" as Clyde, suddenly brings to us a moment of deep reflection on what agonies such men must have gone through. And it is very tender to watch Bonnie embrace it all after an initial disappointment---not to mention his "triumph" in finally being able to "perform" for once towards the end----his ego seemingly so inflated that at last he can sustain an erection---power, as we know, can activate hormones that have perhaps been blocked by trauma for decades, even. In that way, the director (but really Clyde's story itself?---or just another intent in humanizing his characters?) offers us an opportunity to feel deeply (those who will) for such YOUNG men suffering from such a sad condition, and when considering that Cialis, Viagra and that incredible injection (mmmm....) were not around then. But we were not able to feel anything for Clyde---the physical condition displayed makes all of us highly successful men in such matters (allow me.....ha!) feel great compassion. But the plot cannot go anywhere---it is simply, and unbelievably TEDIOUS to watch robbery after robbery and have us lose our patience as we start counting. No matter the distractions and shallow changes from bank to bank, no matter the thousand chases and stolen cars---------whoever is enlightened by such a plot is to be commended..,....... The characterizations, as much as the acting is brilliant in its own way, are EMPTY, SHALLOW, deeply STUNTED throughout------throw the book of synonyms at it. You won't be wrong. The iconization of violence while insisting that these are "good" human beings takes us nowhere. We learn NOTHING whatsoever about Bonnie and Clyde--------perhaps their true story is the real thing, so to speak. What Mr. Penn tries to convey, it clearly comes across is that every "monster" inside of us is also a human being. Well, we know that from having read history and realized that even grotesque "heroes" like Napoleon and Alexander were ALSO human. I won't go as far as Mr. H..... (in the 20th century) because I have too much respect for my Jewish friends, but the truth is that what Penn tries to convey and HUMANIZE but fails UTTERLY is really, ultimately, alas......an empty PAGEANT of people going nowhere AND developing not one single bit. This is a magnificent example of what has repeatedly happened again and again throughout history: a few people cluelessly offering pathetic opinions metastasizes into a gigantic metaphor for something that carries no substance whatsoever at its core. It is, to an extent, if a bit much here for the term, a sort of minor propaganda. And it works so much of the time as it has here. Mild entertainment, especially for its ridiculous "slow-motion" ending which brings laughter and titters to all in the room........

history.title: The Gospel According to St. Matthew
history.review_title: Neo-Realism at its crudest, most stilted, ineffective, indeed irresponsible manifestation.....
history.text: If all the actors in this ridiculous movie were indeed non-actors, this time it did not work. To counter critics of the severity of my review, you find elsewhere, if you care, my review of Mamma Roma.....I consider it a 5-star masterpiece. The greatness of neo-realism resides in its combination of great acting skills (the great Anna Magnani in a heartbreaking performance) and a myriad of non-actors that give a certain curious challenge to the portrayal of everyday.life. Having said that, we know that most of can sustain, given the right direction a scene or two in a role that is not too demanding. That is because we spend our entire lives ACTING, whether consciously OR unconsciously, and to different degrees of narcissism (not to mention success!). Even the homeless person on the street has "memorized" his "stump speech"----let us not go there what with the present endless debate in America and its "artful" politicians. In this case, out of sheer arrogance or some stupid idealism Mr. Pasolini decided to dedicate more than 2 hours to one of the most taxing, cheaply pseudo-intellectual of all films in memory----and I have watched the very finest in the long history of American and international Cinema. The movie was clearly made on pennies (not in itself a liability), and the direction is appalling. One sad thing that comes to mind, heartbreakingly so is that all of these peasants ( were they all?)---apart from the figure of Jesus must have unquestionably been paid a pittance for their work-----and of course, Pasolini went on to reap the rewards and not give one single thought about sharing any proceeds with these poor souls.. Aesthetics: Surely, 2,000 years ago there were no dentists, but the fact that Mr. Pasolini chooses the most grotesque of "smiles" is an act of manipulation and nothing else. The fact that PIER selects the UGLIEST of faces (or more to the point the lighting that makes them look monstrous) is yet another manipulative effect, all in the name of "realism"........This is no critique of beauty versus ugliness, this is about steering your audience towards shock value. I grew up "catholic" (big quotes) and every Good Friday we were given the same ration of Hollywood, Cecil B. Demille drivel (not without its cheesy pleasures). I cannot say these were not at least VISUALLY beautiful (say, "Song of Songs"), but that ends the whole of the aesthetics problem. On to the REAL merits of a film like this.... "Actors" begin by staring at the camera endlessly---------let us emphasize endlessly, but with the important caveat that NOTHING, virtually NOTHING offers us expressiveness. Indeed, what we contemplate are faces that are CLUELESS and baffled----baffled we start becoming as more and more of this develops. If you have no idea of the life of Christ, you will be given a greatly distorted view, Pasolini "artfully" rendered. The movie that I saw, om TV and pay-per-view was DUBBED, but I seriously DOUBT that the original italian was delivered in any different way (an analogy is Fellini's films, which are given a disemboweled feel to them, but mostly those from his "depraved" period where anything goes, the antithesis of this film). The lines are recorded in the studio, in a magnificently stilted way, virtually READ, and during all the passages where Jesus is to be at his most charismatic you know that NOBODY would have followed this FOOL. (We will not go into issues of historical revisionism since then there is no reason for this movie, as it has been proven quite effectively that Jesus is a figure of lore---indeed one of the greatest, most perplexing events in human history---and I am decidedly NOT a conspiracy theorist------but being an agnostic, none of that matters at all. The fact is that the Gospels are filled with an amount of humanism that unquestionably changed the world-------if taking centuries for such a thing to happen.. There is no doubt on my mind that Pasolini had seen all that Hollywood "trash" and decided to go to the opposite extreme. But when, not only do you have performers read their lines in a studio, BUT you leave large chunks of the story out, not to mention its greatest and most dangerous flaw, you know you are dealing with an inflated ego that wishes to supersede the historical cinematic past. The VIA CRUCIS (also known as the seven-stations of the cross---and I don't mean Mal Gibson's grotesque blood-fest!) is, perplexingly, left out entirely. This is one of the most beautifully humanistic moments in the history of Christ. More importantly, shiveringly so, is Pasolini's COMPLETE lack of nuance when dealing with the extraordinarily subtle issues that go into the outcome, which is that the Jews "kill" Jesus. To make it short, Jesus is a jew and the small jewish community is terrified of its master, ROME. Anything can tilt the events against the Jews. And suddenly this RABID, angry, violent, exquisitely megalomaniac man appears before them, creating mayhem. And...he refuses to show his main card, his miracles, to the Jewish establishment. I think that most of us, given such a context, and hanging by the skin our teeth, would have had him killed. The Jews are portrayed in the least sympathetic of ways. By the way, I am NOT Jewish, but have the greatest respect for them. ONCE AGAIN, in the history of so much media, an uncultivated person leaves the theater with the clear idea that the Jews killed Christ. Well YES, they actually convince the Roman authorities to kill one of them, a madman for all they know. A fellow JEW. Pasolini was a devoted Catholic------the magnificently bizarre contradictions of this film if he indeed was NOT an anti-semite prove THE FILM to BE anti-semitic-------not in any way blatantly so, but what do you get when growing with Mussolini?.......perhaps more than a few "snatches" of that monstrous' "intellectual" propaganda. As we have come to know more and more, a Marxist's agenda differs very little, ultimately, with that of a fascist's one...It took many of us to figure that one out, no? Castro, anybody? Pasolini was one more phony "Communist" reaping the benefits of very generous materialist comforts while spewing "equality" from a very safe place. It takes quite a compartmentalization to separate the artist from the BUFFOON. Finally, right after Christ's death there is no "recorded" earthquake that destroys the "favela" built on a hill. It is only a darkening of the skies which lead Roman soldiers to be perplexed and suddenly turn "Christian". Finally, those that will try to defend the film by way of insisting that this is the ".......according to St. Mark" and no more miss the point. When you align all four gospels---one next to each other------you can see that the differences are in NUANCE, not plot. That this work of UTTER MEDIOCRITY has been lauded over the course of 50 years or so, remains as problematic as Bunuel's "...discreet charm.........". This is an exercise in hubris, an amateur work, irresponsible, sadly anti-semitic, but most importantly when looking for inspiration from christianity and his leader will find you confronting, alas..........absolute STERILITY........... ASIDE: the movie contains, at different moments, the most beautiful seemingly African/Brazilian music. It is spellbinding, and I would be honored if anyone will send me a note telling me what it is if they know!

history.title: Malcolm X (Two-Disc Special Edition)
history.text: No question about it........ Yet, it is clearly an act of RACISM and, we must accept, perhaps Mr. Lee's "arrogant" ways that offer us the humiliating fact that the film was ignored for Best Picture OR Best Director............The brilliant, stunning performance of Denzel Washington/ Malcolm X (because he seemed to transform himself into X without the silly mimesis of that great actress who first gave us "Sophie's Choice" and then slowly descended into PARODIES) was the only nomination among the top--and he lost to "Mr. Scarface" for "Scent of a woman" or some sort of insignificant reel when compared. Angela Bassett is simply heartbreaking as his wife, and the very moment of the killing offers us a haunting display of agony, characterized by her cries of sorrow that are so chillingly extraordinary that they have haunted me to this day--------TWENTY-FIVE years later. The entire movie captures X in all the many shades of his persona and inner being. What may be considered controversial by some is Lee's exquisite handling of the main dilemma that remains: WHO killed Malcolm X---and he does it with great fairness, but leaves little doubt of the fact that although the FBI persecuted him, the ultimate responsibility is in the hands of that repugnant group "The Nation of Islam" and its magnificently corrupt leader ELIJAH MOHAMMED, with whom X bravely parts after finding the truth of HIS leader's own phoniness. The movie is a beautiful testament to Malcolm X's profound honesty and searing search for truth, culminating with the change that comes too late for the "world" to acknowledge---even to this day, when particularly white people (but I would bet that, alas so many BLACKS as well!) have no clue as to his transformation from his "hatred" of whites and his loud, damning speeches and reputation as a horrible counter-racist and even violence- inciting man of "God" (his ...."by any means necessary...") to a preacher, a humanist almost in tandem with the great Martin Luther. Not so arguably, every white American should see this film, to penetrate the very many layers of RACISM that to this day continue to haunt this nation-----------but, as well, what is a historically almost exact record of the life of this extraordinary person. Alas, not only should every White American, BUT every BLACK person, indeed among MANY who, as most people in America seem to regard History as unnecessary to their lives, living literally more and more detached from everything that has molded us. This is, I believe a 3+ hour film, yet it NEVER slows, never has us praying for it to end. BRAVO to Spike Lee for his gargantuan efforts, to Washington for his immersing into a complex character and capturing his many "selves"---------and ultimately, if outside of the film, of course to the great Malcolm X himself for his transforming being that leads to his own liberation and forgiveness, to whatever extent, of the generations of Americans who shared (and continue to!) the guilt of participation in what remains the greatest STAIN of this extraordinary nation.

history.title: Insidious
history.review_title: If they'd just stopped about halfway, this would've been decent
history.text: Worth a rental, no way you're paying moviegoer fare for this. Starts off well enough, using the ole' less is more formula of haunted houses, but that's the essence of fright - letting the audience scare itself by leaving out concrete details such as the true appearance of ghosts/demons. Paranormal Activity used the less is more formula to great effect. Amazing how scared you can get on a budget flick. Anyway, Insid builds it up but lets it down in the end, where the film just implodes, turns on itself and removes any sense of fright created so clearly in the start and middle. The most frightening film since The Exorcist? Demon, please. The most terrifying film since Poltergeist? Shame on you, promoter-voice guy. A two-star one-night rental to enjoy and forget? Right on, daddy-o.

So - many people are giving Spiel & Co. the finger over Super 8. Here's my finger back at them, plus support for my gesture: 1. Likable characters 2. Decent plot 3. Righteous FX But the biggest reason I liked 8 was the sentimentality of it, something Spiel is a master of. He makes me remember being a kid and having dreams, biking around and thinking about nothing except the moment, wishing for the pretty girl to say hi, the posters and models - it just touched my heart. So thanks, Spiel and Abrams. You guys made me remember. It's a perfect summer film. Not taxing on the mind, just a slice of "Ah, I used to be like that."

Lantern's got some good and some bad. Lantern resides among other tier-two superheroes like DareDevil, Ghost Rider and Thor. It's always a hurdle for filmmakers to dish all the backstory so they can get right into the action since the majority of viewers don't know GL's origin. We have to learn some history about him before he faces the Ultimate Bad Guy. Goodwise, Reynolds has stepped up in acting ability as of late. He moderated the wise-ass routine enough here to let his character come through, but it's still Reynolds. CG is passable, and very emerald. And there's Blake Lively - just another pretty face, but oh what a face (and everything else). The guy who played Sinestro did a wonderful job, and Peter Sarsgaard (another top talent) did well too despite the giant head. Badwise: CG is sometimes low-grade, as would befit a movie like this. Superman and Spiderman get the best CG treatment. Rushed story. There's just not enough time to define the character, explore his motives, understand the supporting characters, introduce a superhero universe of galactic cops, narrate the bad guy's motives and origins, and wrap it up in 180 minutes. Your brain can't process all the changes quick enough.

history.title: Man of Steel (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: Hollywood getting closer to a great Superman movie
history.text: Getting closer, not there yet. Supes always gets the highest budget and the cutting edge CG. The actors do their thing well, and I liked the film on the whole. Some things annoy me about Man of Steel (and Spidey and Bats as well). First, WE DO NOT NOT NOT NEED TO SEE SUPERMAN'S ORIGINS ANYMORE. SAME GOES FOR SPIDERMAN AND BATMAN. Please, dammit, please stop telling us where Superman comes from and that his parents were torn to pieces leaving their only child to the fate of human beings and that he fell in with the nice Clark people. We Got It. It's burned into our brains forever. Second, and last, the film does go overboard with the building destruction. At certain points it's eyeball zapping, brain-numbing shlock. In all, MOS is good - not yet the awesome thing it should be, but good.

history.review_title: So Much Less Than Meets the Eye
history.text: I was pleasantly surprised when I saw Transformers 1, terribly disappointed at the blatant racism, sexism and U.S. flag-waving (as perpetrated by the Autobots)of T2, and turned off T3 near the end. I thought, just finish watching the damn thing, but no - I'd had enough. Enough of excellent actors (Malkovich, McDormand, Turturro) speaking horrible lines w/a straight face, the obligatory Bay-girl who'd replaced Megan Fox and was there only for teens to pitch a tent to. Advanced robots from another world that think just like humans, have blue eyes to denote "good" (just like people think) and red eyes to denote "evil." Evil Decepticons robots that are animalistic in appearance because, as humans know, animals are savage and stupid. Lots of phony baloney, albeit veiled, grandstanding about U.S. values as said by the Autobots ("Humans love their freedom" and other crap-worthy, trite sentiments about individualism and sticking up for each other). The orchestral music and other pop music tracks that pipe in to underscore the drama. I was cringing at that so much, and I was sitting alone in my living room. A plot about some nonsense that will end the world, but who cares amidst the ear-rupturing clanging of robots and explosions. Everything's exploding, the sidewalks, the sky, the flowers. Bay can't tell us enough how much he covets the fine art of blowing s*** up like a madman every ten minutes. If you're under 14, are male and have an average or less IQ, then you definitely need to invest some time here; everyone else, Transform and avoid this POS movie.

history.review_title: The sequel we didn't need but got anyway
history.text: Chronicles of Riddick is one of those sequels like Highlander 2: The Quickening, where you wonder why they needed to make a sequel. After all, Pitch Black was never anything great. It was a sleeper hit that they should've let alone, or at best, if they had to make a sequel, why did they have to make Chronicles? Chronicles is watchable in a tongue-in-cheek way. The dialogue, costumes, names and plot are silly. The film tries so hard to be cool: "Necromongers" "Lens him out and cleanse him" "You keep what you kill" "Quasi-Deads." You laugh and cringe when the actors have to say their lines without smirking. Chronicles also suffers from the fatal error of more is more. Hollywood decided to give Riddick the huge budget it supposedly deserved, based on nothing more than the mild cult status of Pitch Black. So here we go: make it all bigger, badder, over the top. Instead of a tight, focused flick like Pitch Black, let's expand this thing into a galaxy-sized smorgasbord on par w/Star Wars and Star Trek. Include an array of races and tech and some kind of abstract concept like Underverse, tons of locations, ships, people. Chronicles gets out of hand fast and is crushed by its own weight. If you happened to see the third and final Riddick (creatively titled "Riddick") you will be pleasantly surprised. It's entertaining, worlds better than Chronicles, because it keeps it tight and falls back to the smaller structure of Pitch Black, fewer characters, one planet, one plot. It's well done. Despite my complaints, Chronicles is decent. It's pure escapist shlock I'll probably watch again if it's on tv.

history.title: Hobbit, The: The Desolation of Smaug (Special Edition) (DVD)
history.text: Desolation is entertaining enough. Three hours is unnecessary, let alone three films, but that's greed for you. I like the cast, but too much silliness undercuts the story. Elves (Legs and Tauriel shouldn't even be there) can do such amazing, supernatural fighting moves it becomes a joke to watch. A visually and audibly grueling, one-hour long encounter w/Smaug wherein main characters jump and duck the dragon over and over when Smaug, an ancient and wise being, could've easily smoked all of them in seconds. After the LOTR trilogy The Hobbit just seemed like an unneeded series that probably should have waited longer, had a new director and a new film location. I think Hollywood should've put The Hobbit out first, as is chronologically correct, because the series is so much like watching a football game well after one team has a huge lead over the other and there's no reason to watch anymore.

history.title: Godzilla (2014)
history.text: This is the first film I've seen where the star of the show is relegated to a cameo. I'm speaking of that force of nature, Godzilla, everyone's fav beast from the east. On the positive side, the film has class. Cranston does well for the short time he's in it. It's not like some stupid Transformers flick. I think they captured the feel of the old Godzilla films. The negative? I don't know why but Godzilla is rarely seen in the film. He screams a few times, we see his massive legs, and one time, just as he's about to kick ass, the film irises-in. Very disappointing. After seeing Pacific Rim, a guilty pleasure, I would've thought filmmakers would follow their lead and create some stunning fight sequences, but they didn't. Instead, I watched humanity track the evil MUTO's for eighty minutes and philosophize about their presence and Godzilla's role in the affair. Finally, for the final five minutes, there's a titanic Godzilla-MUTO throwdown I'd been waiting for. Five minutes. That's it. So a huge chase-the-monster scene and people tripping over themselves to get out of or into Godzilla's way, and that's it. Godzilla wins. Blasts his nuclear breath once. Then he goes home.

history.title: The Hobbit: The Battle of The Five Armies
history.text: Rotten way to end a poorly executed trilogy. If you watch it knowing it's going to stink then you can probably enjoy it. What killed it for me... 1. Legolas - why is he there again? soaking up screen time, doing things so beyond superhuman abilities he's invincible; firing arrows at a mile's distance and hitting his target, jumping and catching ledges and branches from hundreds of feet 2. Minor characters with too much screen time. Someone thought it was time for Alfrid to be the comedic center in the film. He shouldn't have even been there at all. 3. Computer graphics that suck: it's the poorly made film where the designers don't know when to add CGI and when not to; ex. a rolling cart nearly kills Bards family but the cart is so easily noticed as CGI it takes you out of the tension; also, plenty more battlefield CGI so dwarves can ride hogs, elves who spear five orcs on the horns of their moose mounts, really stupid looking stuff that again undercuts the attempt to immerse the viewer 4. Bilbo? the book's called "The Hobbit," but B is an afterthought, walking around as the moral and ethical center of the violence he sees, grimacing and fighting, running and pondering, but never truly being the front of the film 5. Far too much of the book was changed to fit Hollywood's need to turn classics (like Disney does to classics) into marketable, mindless crap, insulting Hobbit fans' intelligence and pissing on Tolkien's grave all to make a video game type movie in time to capitalize on the holiday movie run Sum: a bad ending for a fairly weak series. The one good point is a well done fight scene between Sauron and the council members.

I dislike when you have a character of such legendary reputation as Apocalypse, a being of such power and rage and mystery, and then portray him as an almost human, bland and lifeless character. Where's the beef? This flick goes on for 2.5 hours but it's just so much dead air and the Big A pontificating his philosophy of having to remake the world in his image. Blah blah blah. And of course they have to further confuse me by throwing a Wolverine cameo into the mix. Most unncecessary. Come on, man. I'm here for one thing: to see mutants kick ass, show off their powers and dance within a tightly wound story. Apocalypse missed the boat.

history.review_title: What in the world were the writers thinking?
history.text: What in the world were the writers thinking? Everything was fine with me up to the last episode. There was some confusion on the killer was thought to have been killed earlier and it turned out to be another person and they did not address this at all, but I could tolerate all this. So here comes the final episode. They didn't have much to do for the final episode. The next to last episode ended great, but I guess the writers are attention deprived pansies who have to "shake things up" in the end. So what do these guys do? It was fine half way through but in the last 20 minutes or so they kill off a main character, and then change the ending completely. There's nothing wrong with guessing how it will end and getting it right. The writers just HAD to make it so that no one would have guess how it would end. There's a reason no one guessed how it would end: IT SUCKED! I have watched this show from season 1 and feel like this was a cheap way for it to go out. There seemed to be such growth in Dexter, then they take it all away. This was an utter disappointment.

history.title: The Magnificent Seven
history.review_title: Depthless Fun - As in Fun Without Depth
history.text: Although I'm not normally a fan of Antoine Fuqua - who can forget his King Arthur, apart from everyone - I enjoyed this film. It was depthless, in that the characters have no depth, but some very good performances make up for this. Denzel Washington never gives a bad performance. Vincent D'Onofrio portrays profoundly eccentric characters extremely well. Even Ethan Hawke's turn as PTSD suffering Civil War veteran was convincing. They make up for a so-so script filled with cliches, contemporary figures of speech, and no apparent character motivation apart from Washington's Chisholm, and only at the very end. In fairness, the western has been dead for awhile. Its core themes don't resonate today. Plus few people would find Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai from 1954, much less John Sturges' Magnificent Seven from 1960 very gripping today. Kurosawa's original was meant for a post-war Japanese audience after all and, although its characters and underlying message are as timeless as they are universal, this was not the mission of this particular motion picture.

history.review_title: One Delicious Hot Dog, But It's Still a Hot Dog
history.text: As a superhero movie, it's entertaining in many ways. Art direction here is outstanding while paying homage to its comic book origin. Gal Gadot wonderfully conveys an otherworldly presence. Plus she plays her role of someone who knows what she believes but does not know who she is quite well. A superhero must command the screen. She does. She lacks physical presence owing to her fashion model physique but her power has nothing to do with muscles. Nor is she, say, Linda Hamilton from Terminator II whose developed and sharply defined muscles expressed the driven, tortured nature of Sarah Conner. Forget the faux feminism. There's nothing of that sort here. The ideal woman is still disturbingly thin. She dare not have muscles or else risk turning off the men and frightening the women. Or give her muscles, as James Cameron did in T2, but you'd better have a good excuse. In short, there's nothing truly daring or socially conscious about this film. Some call this the perfect superhero movie. But that's a bit like the best imaginable hot dog - delicious, of course, but still a hot dog. My problem was with the period used. World War I actually happened, Erich Ludendorff did not die in 1918, this was not a good versus evil war, though it was an extremely evil war. Due to the deeply flawed nature of the armistice, the film portrays as Wonder Woman's triumph over an evil god, an even more evil war followed. Bad history, even in a fantasy film, is a bad idea for many reasons unless it's merely a backdrop. They should have stuck with the Crimean War, as they'd planned, with no harm done. That was not among history's most pivotal conflicts.

history.title: Arrival
history.review_title: A Skillful Retelling of Plato's Allegory of the Cave
history.text: A skillful retelling of Plato's Allegory of the Cave, this film explores themes we normally associate with philosophies of the east. Specifically, living with less focus on self, not turning all our attention to our individual lives and feelings, moment to moment - what social media too often is: The daily me. In the west, we often regard abandoning focus on the self as a mental disorder. For a Buddhist monk, it's the highest state of enlightenment: Nirvana, meaning living suspended between fear and desire, accepting suffering as a necessary condition of being alive rather than living life with the aim of avoiding suffering. We believe that if we get it right, we can avoid suffering entirely. Suffering is for losers. "I prefer people who don't get captured," for example. Yes, I know this interpretation can seem like a whole lot of new age hooey. And I'm certainly as far from being a Buddhist as you can get without a prescription. I can't live that way. What makes this film interesting is that it took nearly unimaginable, earth-shaking events and traumas for the hero of this story to achieve this. All science fiction is allegory and metaphor, usually dreadful. This one, however, is brilliant.

Splendidly executed thriller with marvelous writing, acting, plot twists, the works. Plus it deals with an extremely uncomfortable subject - the Iraq war: easily the most profound foreign policy blunder of this century thus far. It does so, though, more as allegory than direct criticism, touching obliquely on the misconceptions and abuses of power evident in 2003 which resonate to this day. The story craft employed here is that the case seems, at first, far, far from any event larger than the murder of a teenaged woman. Not that such things are trivial. They're not. Thus the series can capture our attention, setting us up for misdirections and surprise plot twists. Helen McCrory's performance is flawless and captivating. That alone made this series memorable for me. Three instead of five stars, though, due to the myriad plot improbabilities which I won't detail here, as they'd serve as spoilers.

history.review_title: Splendid Propaganda Parody That Runs a Bit Too Long
history.text: A stranger premise for a comedy would be difficult to find: a "discovered and remastered" Romanian cop show from the "'80s." They really put some work into this. All the actors are Romanian and the series was filmed there. Even if you remember the Cold War (I do) Romania is one obscure place to most Westerners. Few people even know that Romanian is a Romance language. But state propaganda is always with us. Here it's silly and easily parodied. But it convinced no one, not ever. It was an extremely repressive state, not shared Communist conviction, that ruled that country. Romanians revolted in 1989 and killed their ruler, Nicolae Ceaușescu and his wife, Elena, by firing squad after a 90 minute show trial. Romanians viewed the video replay of their execution over and over on television with visible joy. So, how can this work as a comedy? Watching people pretend that soup is a feast, say, with pride, that their primitive hospitals are the best in the world, their miserable cars that can barely start are world-class too while spouting stilted, slogan-filled dialog will either make you laugh or drive you to seek something - anything - else to watch. Hence the 5 star and 1 star reviews here. Mostly I laughed until the core joke got old.

Walt Disney is often dismissed now as a cultural relic. Nonsense! He was a technological and entertainment innovator surpassing the likes of Lucas, Spielberg, Steve Jobs and many contemporary luminaries. The first episode touches on this. He invented the concept of motion capture, revolutionized animation, attracted the best people, gave them room to innovate, and was always in pursuit of the next thing. He understood the importance of fantasy and myth. He knew that evoking emotion was independent of photographic realism. This is why many cutting-edge video game developers continue to admire him today. There are better documentaries on his early years in business. Part of the problem is that the showrunners here don't use interviews with people who are now deceased. Yes, he was difficult to work with at times and, for a creative person, an extreme social conservative. But he was never the monster that some later Disney CEOs, such as Michael Eisner, were. But this is, nonetheless, a splendid two-part documentary series.

Another short attention span style history documentary. There are NO static shots. The camera is ALWAYS moving and at variable speeds as it pans and zooms, drops in and out of timelapse to make the clouds overhead and people on the ground move with unnatural speed and stutter to a stop - all of it set to a techno beat and plenty of forced hyperbole. The entire series reeks of raw fear that you might turn away for even a moment. No, that's not it. What the showrunners here fear most of all is that, if they give you a moment, you might think. There are two, perhaps three, interesting findings here. Problem is they're buried beneath hours of bull manure. And don't expect to actually see Egyptian pyramids, St. Paul's, or Petra. All you'll get is a frustrating montage of glimpses delivered as if intended to give you a seizure.

history.title: UNDER THE GREENWOOD TREE (FF)(DVD)
history.review_title: Enjoyable Period Rom-Com With Hardy Depth and Charismatic Casting
history.text: A lighthearted, high-spirited, and comically earthy yet not raunchy treat filled with Thomas Hardy's multi-generational life and romantic challenges and catalysts including caste inequities, enjoyably whipped up with olde world fairytale-like Ye Olde Village charm, electric romantic charisma and likeable other characters casting intimately filmed and satisfyingly reverberating with more thought-provoking depth than lighter fare period rom-coms yet surprisingly lighter than Thomas Hardy's usual, though still telescoping his large life macrocosms into small and deceptively simple microcosms. My only critiques the dreadfully painted fake snow drifts (filmed in England, why couldn't this heavily English garbed period piece in four-season setting have used actual winter?) and the director's shift from Hardy's awakening young male hero to the young female's perspective emancipating them from rural into turn-of-the-century industrial Britain but this detour from Hardy's too much the director's proudly admitted copying Bathsheba Everdene and "Far From the Madding Crowd" instead of being true to Hardy's, making me want to read his novella and to look for an older version of the film to experience this idyllic time in England from a coming of age young Hardy's horizon. Still, Hardy could not but be pleased by the beautiful and irrepressibly hopeful expectation of love, joy, and fun of youth and other passions too--surprising how rich the lingering takeaway, though should not be since it is after all a Thomas Hardy.

history.title: Lost in Austen
history.review_title: Lost in Austin must have lost their script writer
history.text: I will admit that the idea of a modern girl going back in time sounded like a great story line. But "Lost in Austin" re-writes the story of pride and prejudice is poorly done. It starts off great and it seems wonderful, but slowly the script becomes messy and the story line is messed up. I tried to think of ways to fix the script and came up with a few improvements, but in the end the story line is weak and not enjoyable. I hate to say this but it kind of ruined pride and prejudice for me. Overall it's an okay movie. I would not recommend it for pride and prejudice fans. It almost came off as a mockery of pride and prejudice. The acting is a bit over done, but believable. The costumes are well enough and the locations are beautiful. The lighting is okay it could have been better in a few scenes. The director did a great job with the camera angles and the editing is fast past. Overall, I think most people will be happy with this movie. I was hoping for a more gentle version, such as the girl that would go back in time would be of the gentle type and would fit in more naturally, but than we would lose the comedy. I do believe that some pride and prejudice fans will find this movie enjoyable. That is they will like the oddities the movie shows and the odd plots twist and turns. But in my opinion i thought the script predictable and a little vulgar. I'm not trying to hurt anyones feelings. If i was the script writer; I would focus the story line to be more comical and romantic. That no matter what the character would not interferer with the story of Dacey and Lizzy, but would add to it, by falling in love with another character within the story that could be introduced as a brother or a friend for example the cousin of Mr. Darcey. Please don't send me hate mail, because i didn't love this movie. I wanted to like it, but i couldn't because of how predictable it is. But I'm sure that many people will enjoy this movie sine it has a fun twist to it. Faithful Austin Fan

history.text: I love movies like this, but somehow I felt like I've seen this before. It's RoboCop meets anime, meets Scarlet Johanson. There was nothing wrong with this movie. They did a fantastic job with everything about it. The cover to the menu inside. Kind of wish it would have been a little bit more in-depth. If you liked the anime then you'll feel like this is a quick version of the same thing. Nothing new added, and more condensed. I wanted to love it but as a movie snob, I didn't. Kudos to the amazing director and actors that did so much fighting and special effects department. Flawless animation and beautiful cuts and transitions. With the lack of human to the human connection, it falls a bit short. We really want to care for these characters and the anime explores more and has more time. So it is not fair the compare them. But where the anime gets to explore and dive deeper this version is flawless, but essentially rushed focusing too much on action-packed scenes, and forcing us to lose the human touch. Hey, But we all like Scarlet Johansson. Except for a few people... hey quit complaining about their acting. Scarlett is amazing... complaints about acting should be kept to the director. She did a fantastic job. I can't think of another actress that could and would pull this off.

history.title: The Greatest Story Ever Told (Special Edition) [DVD]
history.text: Let me say right up front that I am not a particularly religious person. Even with that being the case, I have to admit to being touched by this film. I cannot imagine a better portrayal of Christ than that by von Sydow. The portrayal of Mary Magdalene by Joanna Dunham, though limited to only a few minutes on the screen, made me understand why the men of that time would have been tempted by her. The production values are superb. I have yet to bite the bullet by buying a widescreen TV so the letterboxing proved a nuisance. The cinematogpraphy simply blew me away. The lighting director deserved an Oscar (he might have won one but I haven't checked) just for the scenes involving the cruxificion. I played that portion over and over again and couldn't help but think that this is how a great painter would have interpreted that event. It's a rather long film but I didn't find one scene that I would have wanted cut. The icing on the cake is the great soundtrack. The transfer to 5.1 is excellent although, at times, it was a bit difficult to hear the dialog over the score. Anyone with the slightest interest about the origins of Christianity should at least watch the film and it belongs in the library of anyone interested in the cinema in general.

history.title: Sherlock Holmes
history.text: I've been a fan of the Sherlock Holmes stories, both in book form and on film, my entire life. The films starring Basil Rathbone and Nigel Bruce didn't require special effects and blaring noise to hold their audience's interest. Having read every book and seen every movie involving Holmes, I don't recall much in the way of gunplay or any other form of violence. The essence of Holmes was his brain....not his brawn, but you would never know if from this trash. This piece of garbage may appeal to people who know nothing of the original stories and therefore might enjoy the overblown antics in which Holmes and Watson are involved. Frankly, this is one of the few movies I've ever paid admission to and walked out on. I do not own the DVD and would not accept it if it were given to me for free. Obviously, a large profit was made on this film as there is a sequel to be released shortly. I now know enough not to waste my time and money on that one.

history.title: The War File: Tanks! Barbarossa
history.text: As a World War II buff and fan of German Armor, I was really looking forward to viewing this DVD. What a disappointment. Granted, some of the historical footage is decent enough, but that's about it. Descriptions of the tanks (especially the Russian T34) are either incomplete or incorrect. For example, no distinction is made between the original T34 (with the 76mm main gun) and the upgunned version (T34/85) with its larger turret. Worst of all, the DVD does not bring Operation Barbarossa to its conclusion. It ends at the first German retreat without so much as an explanation of what happened after that. Did the Germans win? Did the Russians? Of course we all know how things turned out, but you would never know that from this movie. Save your money.

Although you can certainly call this a "football movie", it's really a lot more about boys coming of age. Jim Caviezel does his usual fine acting job and Michael Chiklis could easily qualify for a "Best Supporting Actor" Oscar. Laura Dern's part is small but she also comes across as genuine. The film crosses racial and economic boundries and some characters were a bit stereotyped. Yet, these same characters were all believable and elicited the appropriate emotional response from me. targets.title: Did You Hear About the Morgans?

history.text: This is not like the novels. Bosch was a Vietnam vet; this character apparently served in Afghanistan. That's presumably to save money - easier to use current everything than make it true to the period in which it was originally set for the earlier novels. The original Bosch was getting over a break with his wife; this guy has a long, unnecessarily drawn out and boring sex scene by episode two. Not true to the Bosch character. The actor playing Bosch is wooden, flat and expressionless - the whole show, actually, is the same. None of the acting rises above average, and there is little in the characters or plot (so far) to encourage further watching. Having bought and read every one of the Bosch novels, this is very disappointing. Michael Connelly has had little luck in terms of transferring his work to the screen - the movie "Blood Work" was horrible, and bore little resemblance to the novel. Perhaps he'll make a lot of money from this Amazon tedium, and that'll be OK for him, but I wonder if he agrees with all the glowing reviews here (I also wonder how many of the reviewers have read the series from the start). Amazon are to be appreciated for at least bring Harry Bosch to the screen, but if this and "Transparent" are anything to go by (I haven't watched their other pilots) they have a lot to do if they're to catch up to the quality of NetFlix's own productions. P.S. To people who rave about this being a great cop show, it isn't: try watching something that really is good, such as "Spiral" ("Engrenages"), or, for all those who can't read subtitles, "The Shield". There are a lot of others that are far better than this one.

history.title: Edge
history.review_title: but that's a poor excuse for the whole mess

I guess some would say it's a "homage", but that's a poor excuse for the whole mess. The characters are cartoon-like (it reminds me of recent Hollywood crap made from comic books, but with lower production values). The ending -I hope it is, and there won't be more - is unnecessarily gruesome, too. Overall, horrible - a sixth grader's version of a western. Considering that westerns are one of only a few true American art forms (others ; blues, jazz), it's a real shame to see them pissed on like this. It's getting to be that if it's an Amazon production, it should be avoided.

history.title: Wind River [DVD]
history.text: I do understand that the writer/director wanted to make a point about the fact that Native America women's missing person status is not quantified by the federal government. However, I am absolutely sick & disgusted with so many films that include non-stop shootouts with blood & gore all over the place. Shooting the wolf was bad enough but I do understand about sheep herders/cattle owners wanting predators killed (my mother grew up on a ranch in Wyoming). But the rape/murder scene was too horrific & went on Far too long. I sped through it, hoping to see that all the evil men (also predators) would be devoured by mountain lions. The repeated reference to a mother mountain lion & her kits made me Hope that the evil men (or at least one of them) would be eaten by lions. It would have been a pure Chekovian moment. I won't do a spoiler but this didn't happen. It was all too severely depressing. I am starting to realize that Sundance movies are Not for me. It's important to know facts like how bad it is on reservations & how Native womens' disappearances are not noted. But TOO MUCH VIOLENCE.

Way too much violence. I am so sick of shoot outs with blood & guts flying. Horrifying. I realize the writer/director was trying to make a point Native women disappearing & no one investigating the disappearances. However, why show so much horrific violence. The wolf being shot, the woman being raped, sodomized, her boyfriend being murdered (I sped through all that). Just horrible. Done for shock value, like Peckinpaugh. The acting is very good but the violence is over the top.

Moody atmosphere. Sad time period, the fall of The South. A group of women in a Young Ladies' School are trying to survive this harsh time in the south. A badly injured soldier is found by a little girl picking mushrooms. I immediately thought "Chekov! Mushrooms on the mantlepiece!" It was quite dark in most scenes. But I do understand the director was setting the film in a time when there was no outside lighting, everything was candles or the muted sunlight coming through huge oak trees covered in Spanish moss. I did have to put captions on, as some actors mumbled. This is a problem with films nowadays. The women take care of this soldier & complications ensue. Everyone does a great job of acting. Colin Farrell as the soldier is brooding, tempting, furiously damaged. Nicole Kidman is erect, noble, competent & brave. Kirsten Dunst is lovely, vulnerable, intelligent. Elle Fanning is a cat-eyed hussy, fun to watch her. The younger girls are all talented. Especially Addison Reike as Marie.

history.title: Tutankhamun [DVD] [2016]
history.text: I absolutely loved this mini-series. All the acting was brilliant. It followed the lives of archaeologist Howard Carter, his benefactor Lord Carnarvon, Carnarvon's daughter (the first woman to enter the tomb of King Tut, Carter's competitor & eventual friend (Herbert Winlock), a woman archaeologist (Maggie Lewis) and many others. The setting is gorgeous. The excavations are believable. The anticipation & excitement as first the steps are found (by an Arab boy) & then the chamber, still sealed. I well remember reading about all this when I was 10 years old. To this day, archaeology excites me. My husband & I have done expoloring (not excavating, though) at many neolithic sites all over Europe. It was fascinating to follow this story of the most amazing archaeological find in history.
Depressing, dark, endless torture. Hellish. I usually enjoy Scorcese films but this was warped.

My husband & I had watched "How to Be a Latin Lover" starring Eugenio Derbez and Loved it. Hilarious all the way through. This film is more serious but also has a lot of hilarious scenes. This film shows how a Latin Lover becomes a single Dad. He is such a loving father. Then the mother (who deserted her daughter as an infant) comes back, demanding custody. Complications ensue. It is a beautifully realized story with Excellent acting by all. The little girl is phenomenal. The ending is sad but strangely uplifting (I do believe in Heaven so this is the hopeful part). Throughout, Eugenio Derbez directs with care and love. The colors are absolutely beautiful: tangerines, golds, bright reds, verdant greens.

history.review_title: Confusing: no real sense of a satisfying ending
history.text: My husband's mother is British. We love British/Irish/Scottish movies & tv shows. I adore Jim Broadbent & my husband is a huge fan of Michelle Dockery. So we were drawn to this film. We do not require car chase/shoot 'em out movies whatsoever. But this film was too long & drawn out with no real "sense of an ending." First of all, why are all the young men (Broadbent's youthful friends & himself) sandy-haired fellows? It was difficult to keep them apart. My husband kept thinking the young man playing the young Broadbent character (Tony) was Adrian Finn (his best friend) in the flashback scenes. The music really brought us back to the 60s (Psychotic Reaction in the scene where Tony meets Veronica, with her Leica camera). All the scenes in the 60s were so spot on. The cinematography was wonderful throughout the film. Every actor in this movie did a wonderful job, young & older. But the film was based on an extremely enigmatic book. There really is NEVER a sense of an ending. No information is given to explain why Veronica burned the diary her mother had bequeathed to Tony. Or who the father of Veronica's "half brother" might be. Is it Tony? Did Tony sleep with Veronica's mother? If I rated this Only based on the acting skills, it would get 6 stars. But based on the fact that we are left mightily confused, it gets 3.

ZERO stars. I think highly of Nicole Kidman & Colin Farrell as actors. But this writer/director must have some form of serious mental illness. He has now made 2 films which are horrifically sadistic, monotone, meaningless & cruel. Actors think they are doing something highly unusual/artistic. Sorry, it's just balderdash.

history.title: I Don't Care Girl
history.text: I'm sorry to have to agree with the negative reviews of this film. I love Mitzi Gaynor, but in this movie she is poorly directed and choreographed. For example, her ability to show anger or hurt is to shout with a dead looking expression---high school play level. When she's happy, she gives us the dance-number smiling face, and that's it. Even singing the words "I don't care," she lacks any liveliness of tone and timing. Compare her performance here to the one in Les Girls. In the latter she is much more alive and varied in her expressions under director George Cukor. As for the choreography, she doesn't do much in any of the numbers but prance around on those cute legs and shake her voluminous skirts. Hardly any variety of steps and body language. The songs, also, are fifth rate, and the lead singer has a foggy uninteresting voice. If you want to see how good this girl was, check out her "It's De-lovely" routine with Donald O'Connor in Anything Goes. But sadly, I'd suggest you skip IDCG. . . unless you like Oscar Levant who does some excellent piano work, as usual. All in all, Mitzi deserved better, dang it!

history.title: Anything Goes [DVD]
history.review_title: Go with it! It's worth the trip.
history.text: Not the greatest movie musical but up there with the next tier of thoroughly enjoyable examples of the genre, this one rich with performances of delightful Cole Porter songs. And in the "It's De-lovely" number, Mitzi Gaynor and Donald O'Connor get pretty close to an Astaire-Rogers performance. Finally, as a swan song for Bing Crosby, it works just fine. He leaves us with the inimitable style that he brought to so many musical films and not once does he seem to be pushing it or lacking in full enthusiasm for this happy farewell. Highly recommended!.

history.title: Les Girls [DVD]
history.text: As a lover of classic movie musicals, I wasn't quite happy with this film when it first came out, if only because it was to be Gene Kelley's last dancing role, and felt like the end of a stunning era. But as the years have gone by, I've come to love Les Girls, and it has held up beautifully. All three ladies are marvelous, and Cukor's direction is up to some of his best. This is one of the rare musicals that could stand as a rich, witty comedy without the music. But happily the Cole Porter score is just perfect for the story-line of this oh so high quality piece. In short, it's a real winner . . . a joy from another time. And lucky you if you still have the chance to see it for the first time.
What Phantom is this? I didn't recognize any of the music. Very strange approach to what I thought would be a performance of the great musical.

history.title: The Rainmaker
history.review_title: The bestest rain you ever saw!
history.text: I first saw this film years ago as a young man. I was crazy about Katherine Hepburn and thought her outstanding in the movie. But both Burt Lancaster and Earl Holliman seemed maybe too much over the top. But that was then! Now, after a life that has made me a bit less know-it-all snobbish, and tiring of the "life is crap" message in too many recent films--- I am totally delighted with this gem. The energy, the verve, the fine script, everybody just right for the parts . . . It's a life-enhancing, life affirming movie and I urge you to watch it. Also, my copy of it is very reasonably priced for a film with such a fine picture and sound. You just can't go wrong with this one. So beat that drum and draw that big arrow and just have a hell of a good time.
