history.title: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull (Single-Disc Edition)
history.text: When did Spielberg start going downhill? I'd say some time in the late 1980s. You can see signs in The Last Crusade: the stunt-casting of Sean Connery, the silly scene with Hitler, and perhaps the over-extended tank chase. Since then, I haven't enjoyed anything he's made (except Jurassic Park), which is remarkable considering how wonderful his earlier films were. We can gauge his fall by comparing Kingdom of the Crystal Skull with the earlier Indiana Jones movies. First, despite what the cinematographer says (in a featurette) about duplicating the look of the old films, this sequel is visually much less interesting. Do a direct comparison: the early films have tight compositions, lots of interesting movement through the frame, and dramatic high-contrast lighting. Kingdom's shots tend to be excessively wide, boringly composed, and overlit, making the image look flat and bland. I thought the absolute worst moment was the diner scene, which was awkwardly set up, mostly stuck in one long shot, and with a deep focus that brought out every detail of the busy background and was painfully distracting. You'll also notice, throughout the action scenes, not one close-up of Jones looking frightened, in pain, flustered or relieved, whereas in the early films these shots helped us empathise with the character, adding to the drama and being really a signature of the series. Kingdom unfortunately models its structure on recent action movies, which means action, action, action, always at the expense of character. The problem with this is that if you don't care about the characters, you don't care about the action. Also, the application of modern techniques eliminates the rough-and-ready quality of the action in the old films, which made them wonderfully believable. The use of motion-controlled cameras, the obvious CG clean-up, the flow of unbelievable stunt after unbelievable stunt, all these make action scenes look slick and fake. That we are supposed to believe a 65 year old man could do all these things (including things much more difficult than in any of the previous films) is the final dealbreaker. Probably the worst offender of the action scenes is the jungle chase, which is ten or fifteen minutes of pure fantasy, most notably Mutt continuing a sword fight for five minutes while astride two speeding jeeps. With so much silly Stuff happening during this scene, it quickly becomes a bore. It's directly followed by the army ant scene, which did have the potential to be a classic Indiana Jones moment, but was undermined by immediately following the exhausting jungle chase, and by being boringly directed. There's some running around and screaming, but our heroes hardly feature. The story is not bad in itself, but is spoiled by various silly things, such as: Jones walking TOWARDS the mushroom cloud of an atomic bomb; Mutt wanting to rescue some old guy for no compelling reason I could gather; Jones mispronouncing "libary" (though I'm sure everyone on set thought it was hilarious); cunningly evading the Russian spies by going home and staying there; Inca ninjas (totally unexplained); reintroducing Marion and then not giving her any decent scenes with Jones; a middle and last act with five potentially interesting characters (six including the villainess) and no interesting dramatic scenes at all; more ninjas; an elaborate gate-unlocking scene which was done for real but LOOKS computer generated; Jones rushing into the skull chamber when a tentative creep would've been more dramatically interesting (but hey, why start now?); the portal to other dimensions looking like a big extractor fan; the villain dissolving in a CGI haze when we all wanted to see her head explode; Jones's "surprise son" looking nothing like him; and the groan-inducing applause at the wedding (a moment which the film had definitely not earned). So what's GOOD about Kingdom of the Crystal Skull? Well, most of the actors do what they can with their underwritten parts (though I still think Cate Blanchett is overrated), and the production design, costuming, etc, are of a high standard. (John Williams' music sounded good in its featurette, but I hardly noticed it in the film.) There were a lot of good IDEAS in the story: retrieving an item from the mysterious government warehouse, the atomic test village (though it seemed to belong in a different story), the return of Marion, the South American setting. I even think the "aliens" plot had potential. It's just that in almost every case the execution of the idea failed to deliver. Let's just be thankful they won't be making any more of these.

history.title: Jyu-Oh-Sei: Planet of the Beast King - The Complete Series S.A.V.E.
history.text: I bought this because of all the positive reviews, and I'm afraid I have to say I was disappointed. Near the beginning, things picked up after a certain annoying character died, and I had expectations of a reasonable experience. Sadly, in the last few episodes, believability in terms of character and plot goes right out the window. I can't go into detail because I don't want to spoil it anymore than I already have, but I found the sequence of "twists" and "exciting moments" in these last episodes to be ridiculous, to the extent that it ruined the show for me. I wish I had watched something better, and not wasted my time.

history.title: Shigurui: Death Frenzy Complete Series (Anime Classics)
history.review_title: Beautiful but flawed ultraviolent samurai drama, not for the mainstream
history.text: I'm reviewing this because I thought people might like to know what the show is like! Shigurui is an historical samurai drama, but it's not exactly comfort TV. The style is extremely arty, especially during the first few episodes - many many shots of dead cicadas, etc. The pace is also extremely slow, and the ending won't make much sense unless you paid attention to one particular line from the narrator in the middle of the series. You should also take care not to be confused by the flashback near the beginning (it might be more accurate to say the show starts with a flashforward). At the same time, this show is extremely violent and depraved. Apart from various people having their guts spilled and many different body parts chopped off, there are sex scenes, including a senile old man trying to seduce his daughter, and, laughably, one instance of autofellatio. There is a serious point to the shock value, which is that the absolute obedience demanded of dojo members, combined with an obsession to be the best swordsman, leads them to make themselves into something ultimately much less than human. But the execution of these themes is always over the top and exploitative. All this means that this show is for a particular audience, and not for the mainstream. You'll know if it's for you from the above description. Even allowing for the specialised tastes this show caters to, it is less than perfect, particularly in its pacing. It could profitably be cut down to a 2-hour movie without losing anything important. All these factors considered, it's still worth a look.

history.title: Sucker Punch
history.review_title: A tricky mix of blockbuster videogame and arthouse angst & weirdness - or a modern-day Scheherazade?
history.text: I think that Sucker Punch is a much better and more interesting film than many critics give it credit for. I don't, however, think that the subtle machinations of the plot layers are the point of the film, or should be used to intellectually justify it by saying "complex=good". For me, this film is less an intellectual exercise than a stream-of-consciousness expression of emotion; it's about feeling powerless, and escaping that feeling through fantasy. The mechanics of the plot are just there to support the emotional content. After the plot's complexity, the most controversial part of the film is the "video game" action sequences. Honestly, I am a bit iffy about them conceptually, as their relationship to the main plot is extremely tenuous, but to my surprise I found these sequences mostly very engaging and even moving. The exception to this was the sequence that most needed to be emotionally engaging - the train heist. It might have been because it was poorly directed, or because I was worn out by the preceding action scenes. Whatever the reason, I found this part just didn't work. It's the one big flaw of the piece. Another controversial element often mentioned is the skimpy outfits the heroines wear. I don't think the allegations of sexism are valid as generally stated. If women are working at an exotic dance club, it is natural that they would "hang out" in their costumes or in their underwear - this is pretty much standard for back-stage behaviour. I didn't find the photography at all leering. What might be questionable is the fetish outfits* the heroines wear during the "video game" sequences. This is part of a wider argument about the double-image of feisty female protagonists, going back at least to the Alien movies, and I don't think Sucker Punch will solve the argument conclusively for either side. Maybe these diverse criticisms are inevitable if you try to combine accessible contemporary action with arthouse explorations of plot and emotion. But Snyder deserves points for trying, and succeeding as much as he has. 3.5 stars (*And of course by "fetish outfits" I don't mean kinky leather, but outfits containing certain elements which have become iconic to the video game-playing, anime-watching generation (i.e. sailor suits, samurai swords, aeronautical goggles, etc.). Failure to comprehend the iconic nature of these and other elements is the main reason older critics disliked this film. The question of what meaning these symbols possess when stripped of their original context is an issue so big I won't even attempt to deal with it here.)

history.title: Supernatural: Anime Series
history.review_title: It's not Supernatural, and it's not good anime
history.text: As a major fan of both anime and Supernatural, I had high hopes for this series. I sat down to watch it with a smile on my face and hope in my heart. I held onto these as long as I could, but after a few episodes I had to be honest with myself, and face up to my disappointment. This anime doesn't capture anything of the feeling of Supernatural. The colours are garish. The music is cheesy and inappropriate. The acting has no subtlety (unlike most reviewers here, I listened to the Japanese audio). There is none of the affection for the characters that you'd expect from the live action series. There is no wry low-key humour. Dean is now a cry-baby, and Bobby, for no good reason, is a short fat clean-shaven nebbish instead of a cool cracker with a beard. John is a mean SOB, with beard and hat. Only Sam still resembles the live-action character. This isn't just a case of me not being able to accept Supernatural in a new format. Purely as anime, this show is also mediocre. In the featurette, the Japanese directors say they hired a TV writer because they didn't want the usual anime writing. Cut to a story conference in which the writer is fighting to get in ONE LINE that will give the monster of the week some sort of motivation. If you watch that episode (Alter Ego, the remake of Skin), you'll see that he did not get the line in. But the writing in general is poor. The plots are simplistic (and the plots of the "anime originals" are in fact mostly derived from pre-existing episodes). The directors say this is because of the short episode length, but anime fans will know that plenty of story and character can be fitted into the standard 23 minutes. When the dialog is not just blandly generic, Sam and Dean engage in awful gag-based banter (apparently cartoon Sam just HATES being called Sammy - hilarious!). Thankfully, the wacky attempts at humour mostly disappear about halfway through the series (after the one effective episode, which doesn't even feature Sam and Dean), making the show more tolerable, but still not actually good. What would a better anime version of Supernatural have looked like? Maybe a bit like Stand Alone Complex, or Witch Hunter Robin, or even Boogiepop Phantom, but obviously with a bit more ironic humour. Instead we get something that can only only lower the reputation of anime in the West, and of Supernatural in the East. A stupid, cheesy cartoon for kids. An embarrassment to both Kripke's show and the anime industry. I realise that writing such a negative review will garner a few unhelpful votes. I thought long and hard before writing this, and giving what I believe is my lowest ever Amazon review score. I'm only doing this because I want people to have an alternative to the relentlessly positive reviews here. Obviously, if you are a hardcore Supernatural fan, you will have to buy this series. I understand that. I just want you to be aware of what you are getting into, before you get your hopes too high, like I did, and then suffer a terrible disappointment.

history.title: Tokyo Underground (Complete Boxed Set) [DVD]
history.review_title: A solid shonen show that ended before its time.
history.text: The anime Tokyo Underground hasn't had much luck, and has largely gone unnoticed. Nevertheless, it's a fun shonen series that will reward viewers who have a bit of patience. The premise of Tokyo Underground is cool: hidden beneath Tokyo is an underground city many levels deep, which has been cut off from the surface for years, and our heroes have to go questing through it. The problem with the execution of the show is that at the start it takes place mostly ABOVE-ground, with more of an emphasis on comedy (from the hero's dojo-running grandpappy). My theory is that the ratings dropped because of this misdirection, leading to the show being cancelled even though it gets better after this weak start. And indeed it DOES get better. There is a good variety of likeable characters whose agendas slowly become known, and although the show was made on a TV budget, you really get the sense of a vast mysterious labyrinth. The ending is undeniably a bit rushed - you can tell they had a lot more story and exploration planned before the climax, but they manage to tie things up in an acceptable fashion. It is a shame this show was cancelled, as it had potential for a couple more seasons. It would be nice if someone tried remaking it, maybe with a slightly grittier, more realistic feel (not too gritty, or it would end up being like Texhnolyze). In the meantime, this is a great investment if you can get it at a reasonable price. I've actually watched it three times so far.

history.title: Monthly Girls Nozaki-Kun
history.text: One of the best recent animes I've seen, and much better than I expected. It makes the old anime tropes seem fresh, and has some really endearing characters, despite a focus on comedy. Very enjoyable and highly recommended. Monthly Girls Nozaki-Kun is a high school comedy about a genki girl who loves a very tall boy who is a manga artist on the side. Once she gets involved in his work, their friends and associates are quickly drawn into a series of off-beat antics. This show looks a bit like a reverse-harem, but as there is no real plot, I suspect it was based on a four-panel gag manga. There is a good variety of characters, all normal at first glance but kooky in various ways. I laughed out loud a few times, which for me is rare. There's also some clever insight into the workings of shojo manga (romance comics, basically), and a clever bit where the silly conventions of shojo manga and computer dating games are compared. The only real downside is that the main character is bland, which is typical of harem shows. I'd love to see another series of this, but they'd have to introduce some sort of plot to maintain interest. BTW, the Australian edition (if you can get it) includes three soundtrack CDs. That's good value, but the music was probably the least interesting part of this show....

history.title: Resident Evil: The Final Chapter
history.review_title: A solid conclusion to the series, spoiled by weirdly terrible editing (contains SPOILERS!!!!!!!)
history.text: I enjoy a lot of this director's movies, because they are extremely stylish, and because they push my sci-fi/horror nerve just right. Back when the first Resident Evil movie was made, at a time when rapid-cutting "MTV style" editing was in vogue, Anderson went the other way, with a lot of medium-wide angles with wide lenses, and the shots being held for longer than was the norm. The result was quite theatrical in effect, and had a characteristic grandness and eloquence. He went even further in the later RE movies, as a consequence of shooting in 3D. But while this approach for fantasy action movies has become mainstream (see the Marvel movies), with this film Anderson has gone in the other direction, embracing a rapid-cutting "impressionistic" approach. (I suspect this is due to Anderson distancing himself from the editing process, due to painful memories of the shoot, during which the lead stunt woman was badly injured and another person died.) Undoubtedly this editing style creates a feeling of tension, and arguably gives a sense of the chaos of battle. The problem is that it also makes it hard for impactful shots to "land", and makes it hard for viewers to get a sense of the geography of the scene. If this approach was only used occasionally, it would be effective. Unfortunately, the entire movie is edited in this way. There are a lot of good things about this movie: the main acting performances are strong, with Iain Glen (who you might know from Game of Thrones) as Isaacs being the stand-out - if this was a "serious" movie, I'd say he should be in line for an Oscar. The music is good, the design is good, the photography is excellent. The story is fine, though the siege section in the middle of the movie feels like it should have been explored more fully (this problem due at least in part to the editing). Will there be an extended version that fills out areas that seem to have been glossed over? We can only hope so. The religious motives of villain are an interesting change. Other complaints I've read about this movie: > "There are a number of likeable side-characters in the previous movies, but only Claire reappears for the finale." - I'm sure they would have liked to bring back other characters, but scheduling conflicts probably prevented this. If you want to see a bunch of popular characters brought back for one movie, that was done in the movie before this one (RE 5: Retribution, which I think was underrated). > "The movie is too dark." - I find a lot of movies are too dark in the cinema; home viewing is better for light balance and shadow detail. Besides, I found darkness was not a problem, except for the scene where the Ruby Rose character (Abigail) dies. I think a lot of the complaints about not being able to see what's happening are really due to the editing issue. > "Side characters don't get enough development." - This is true. This is partly because, as the last movie in the series, this is very much Alice's story rather than a team-up. Also, due to the editing issue, we don't get a sustained view of any of the side characters in order to observe their character. There is a nice exchange between Alice and Abigail, but it's short, and not developed further. As I said, I hope there is more of this in the home release. (OTOH I thought the villain's henchmen were developed as much as was necessary.) > "How come Alice (plus some monsters) survives the T-virus antidote?" - There are two alternate answers for this: 1. It's explained in the aftermath that saying Alice would die was a lie, told for "reasons". Also, there's no reason the antidote would kill anything living, because a cure by definition would make them better. It would only kill the undead. 2. It's arguable that Alice DID die, and what we see at the end is only a dream before her death. > "Alice's aged makeup looks crap." - It looks fine. Stop bitching about nothing. So what are we to conclude about Resident Evil: The Final Chapter? It's a solid movie spoiled by a new stylistic approach. Sadly, this is not the sort of issue that can be fixed with a fan edit. Possibly watching at a slower frame rate would help? It would be good if the home release was an improvement, but it's unlikely they'll re-edit the entire movie. We can at least hope that the side characters and the siege sequence are filled out a bit. And at home it will be a bit easier to see what is going on. I'm sad that this enjoyable sci-fi/horror series has ended on this sour note, but I'm glad that Alice's story has been allowed to reach a solid conclusion. I'm looking forward to buying this whole series as a box-set on blu-ray (or whatever the next format is), and I'm sure I'll watch all these movies many times in the future. To all those RE fans out there: cheers, and keep slaying those zombies!

history.review_title: Terrible writing, mediocre directing, not worth watching
history.text: I like the first three Underworld movies (I think 3 is underrated). 4 had some good action moments, but was mostly forgettable and a bit silly. It also abandoned the gothic style and feeling of deep lore that characterised the previous films. Those elements are brought back in 5: Blood Wars, but in other respects this is by far the weaker film. The big problem is the dialog. It aspires to Shakespearean grandiosity, but is stuck at the teen fanfic level. The results of this is that the good actors seem as bad as the worst actors. (I thought the worst actors were the two main villains, though in contrast their two henchpersons (played by Bradley James and Daisy Head) came out of it very well, perhaps because the writer put less "effort" into their dialog?) Bad writing is also the reason this movie suffers from boring exposition, unbelievable characters, and dramatic moments that fall flat. The directing is mediocre. The director's first language is not English, which might partly explain why the dramatic performances are so lack-lustre and awkward. The colour palette is grey grey grey, the most uninteresting of the series. There are no impressive visual flourishes except for a couple of shots of a train in snowy mountains (which I presume were CGI). The werewolf transformations look cartoonish. The use of music is weird: there is virtually no music during the battle sequences, when the drama desperately needs bolstering. I could also point out some oddities in the plot (especially concerning the "Sacred World"), but those problems are small compared to the ones I've mentioned. The Underworld series is dead (unless it falls into radically different creative hands). Stick to the original trilogy.

history.title: GF Girl Friend Beta Complete Series DVD
history.text: Perhaps you are wondering if you should order this DVD? The short answer is no, you should not. If you thought the problem with K-on was that it was too good, this show may be your thing. This high school moe show is completely mediocre. The backgrounds are all simple and cheap, the character designs are generic and not especially attractive, the directing (frame composition, lighting effects, colour design and editing) has zero flair and imagination. The voice acting is bland; the combination of vacant-looking generic face design and mediocre voice work makes it seem like most of the characters are heavily medicated. The writing is weak. Four episodes in, most of the characters still have no personalities (i.e. an emotional viewpoint), only external characteristics (the athlete, the foreigner, the model, the reporter). Also, most animes might have a "girl worries about gaining weight" story towards the end of the season when they are running out of ideas. This show does that story in the second episode. The OP/ED themes are sung badly.

history.title: Knight of Cups [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Dont listen to the negative reviews
history.text: A beautiful psychedelic journey, a bizarre mind f*#% experience. Not your average movie, most people unfortunately wont realize what an irreplaceable treasure this film is, Terrence Malick has created a wonderful masterpiece. I litteraly felt like i could die in peace after watching this film because i was fortunate enough to witness such a grand essence of perfection. Im a huge Christian Bale fan, but that doesnt mean i like all his movies, but this seriously is one of his greater films. Just as good as the dark knight trilogy, the prestige, american psycho, the fighter, the machinist, the big short, american hustle, flowers of war, public enemy, the new world...well yeah you get what i mean, Christian Bale does it again big time, what a huge success Knight Of Cups is. I loved how they played such beautiful mesmerizing music from the begining to the end of the film, the sound track was just perfect. The orchestra music in Knight of cups has a sort of psychedelic sound to it in my opinion, which the movie wouldnt be complete without. Roger Ebert gave the film a 4/4 but i was still amazed how many people gave it a poor review, had to watch it for my self to be the judge. A simple minded person who likes going to the movies to see only action, horror or comedy will never understand this film. Truely a film for the greatest of minds. Christian Bale, Terrence Malick and everyone responsible for the making of the soundtrack and film are Gods in our time. If i can relate this movie with another, it would be Michael Fassbender's Shame, which is another film Roger Ebert rated 4/4. After watching the Knight of Cups trailer and watching the film, the only movie that came to my head with stricking similarities was Shame, i highly recommend that film aswell, its a grand masterpiece.

Saddly i couldnt get passed the 6th episode, i kept watching in hopes it would get better but eventually i had to thow in the towel. There are very few animes ive come across that i actually couldnt finish watching because they where just so dull, this is one of them. The only reason i gave this anime 2 stars is because the main character is always flashing her underwear, but thats hardly a reason to view kiddy grade. This is a great cartoon for babies, but a huge failure in my opinion for adult viewers, there is no real violence or drama displayed. In one scene in episode 5, the main character breaks the cock pit of a jet, and throws the pilot out in mid air. When im FINALLY thinking im viewing a scene of violence, the producers made damn sure the audience views the pilot pulling out and using his parachute to ensure no real harm was caused to the bad guy pilot. A great way to describe kiddy grade is, well it feels like its an anime from the 60's or 70's. Yes there is light nudity like the animes back then, but like most animes 5, 6 decades ago, they failed to "hook in " their viewers. To sum up my overall review, this anime is too childish and boring, its much too tv friendly... i mean come on the main character's only weapon is a magic lipstic.

history.title: Grizzly Man
history.review_title: Not a documentary about Grillys - but a tribute to a kind-hearted Delusional man who gets killed by one. : ( Scott M.
history.text: By the cover of this DVD I assumed it would be an interesting documentary about a guy and what he's learned about Grizzlys. I was right about the documentary part - but this whole DVD is just a tribute to a guy Timothy Dexter - who changed his name to Timothy Treadwell. I have some mixed thoughts & feelings about Timothy. In some ways a highly sensitive person. Probably got teased as a kid for being such an open heart. Also an alcoholic and drug user - who stopped - but apparently without the help of AA (etc) Some footage shows Timothy ranting and raving - and swearing with awful language. Clearly in some ways a kind heart - and mentally ill too. He basically moved to the wilds of Alaska - and 'thought' of himself as a friend to Grizzlys (and other critters) He wad Delusional in his beliefs that he assumed the Grizzlys were his friends too. In Oct 2003 he and his girlfriend were ripped to shreds by a grizzly - and partially devoured. This DVD does not show his death (thank God) - but made me cringe to hear how they went. They were alive an conscious through much of their being killed. A Very tragic life. Ultimately pathetic. Most of my DVDs are 'Keepers' - Not this one. Watching it Once - was Two times to many. : ( Scott M.

history.title: Robin Williams: Live On Broadway
history.review_title: I Can't watch this without seeing the Tormented person he was. No entertainment in watching someone implode. Scott M.
history.text: (Review date 3-23-2017) long after Robin's passing. I can understand the sides that people love Robin Williams. I too am a stand up comic (not famous - yet). Many were shocked by Robin's suicide. (I am a self-help person) - I saw years before - that his psychological unraveling was right out there to see. Though most seemed to think it was all pure talent. I saw a person Desperate for help and really struggling. Talent?? Sure - plenty of it - but even more he was mentally unwell. I know an actor who starred in a movie with him - and has lots of good things to say about Robin. And I'm not just speaking in general about him - my focus Is on this DVD. I Can't stand (or sit) watching Robin going off on his tangents. Rambling - shouting - Swearing!! Beyond obscene. In Robin's performances - more is Lost than Gained. Comedy is an art form - and is therefore subjective. I know most love Robin and miss him. I get his 'comedy style' - it's Not for me. 85% of what I see - is a tormented person who was imploding. I know from interview - he had a kind heart - and meant well. - It's just that when someone is ill like this - it jumps out at me - and I Can't pretend it's not there and not killing them. I Don't find it entertaining. Whatever happens in the afterlife - I hope he is well and at peace. - And has the Love he deserves. Scott M.

(My mistake) It's basically just about them. 1st part is about Sinatra. I'm not a Sinatra fan - and Much time is Wasted with people commenting that he was great. I found the Marilyn Monroe thing more interesting. I learned some things I didn't know - like she converted to Judaism for her husband. But - currently I'm 56 years old. If you're around my age or older - and you had access to a television in the past 40-50 years, - you probably or should know most everything that is said on this DVD documentary. As a psychotherapist, I can appreciate this study of grief and loss. As a movie watcher, I thought it fairly dismal. In this day and age it's mind boggling to think the main character would not be in therapy. I'm not saying therapy can extinguish the level of grief he was dealing with. It can't. But it can help. This would be a great teaching tool for a psych course, or a homework assignment for someone whose grief is stuck and needs a catalyst to be set free. As a movie it's simply depressing. history.review_title: Just horrible, and it completely misrepresents the correct treatment/therapy for deep grief.
history.text: I really liked the cast, which is why I actually paid to watch this...most of it. As a therapist for over four decades who specializes in grief, this is absolute rubbish. If you’ve been married for 33 years and your spouse dies, which is not a spoiler since we all know that from the beginning of the movie, you are not going to get over it quickly. And taking years to re-ground, regroup, and re-center is normal. Yes, there are those prone to say get over it, even in the face of huge losses, but they are misguided. Furthermore, most people do not need an antidepressant for grief. Grief, even deep grief after a major loss, is normal and healthy. The thing to do with feelings is to feel them. If you’re not feeling you’re not dealing and not healing. The messages in this movie, at least through the first hour and 15 minutes that I could stand watching, Are extremely unhelpful. They pathologize a normal life reaction to loss. Grief is not a disease. Grief is what we feel when the ground beneath our feet has turned to quicksand.

history.title: Ultraviolet [Blu-ray]
history.text: My comments only concern the DVD versus Blu-ray issue. I have the unrated extended cut of the DVD version and the PG-13 theatrical cut of the Blu-ray version. My experience has been that DVDs mastered in high definition look identical to the Blu-ray version (either on a Blu-Ray player or an upconvert DVD player). Ultraviolet is no exception. Moreover, the look of the film seems to soften details, which really defeats the point of Blu-ray. Aside from no improvement in the look, the Blu-ray version has no more special features than the DVD, and the extended cut DVD has seven additional minutes. Go with the DVD version on this one.

history.title: Hart's War [Blu-ray]
history.text: My comments only concern the DVD versus Blu-ray issue. I have the the DVD version and the Blu-ray version. My experience has been that DVDs mastered in high definition look identical to the Blu-ray version (either on a Blu-Ray player or an upconvert DVD player). Although the DVD version has a very good transfer, I could see slight improvement in the Blu-ray version. (The branches on the trees in the first scene had slightly better definition.) On the other hand, it really didn't matter for most of the movie. The real problem with the Blu-ray version was the lack of special features. The only feature was the trailer. In contrast, the DVD version has two commentary tracks, deleted scenes, and a photo gallery. If you don't care about the features and are willing to pay a bit more for a slightly more defined picture, then go with the Blu-ray. If you want the extras, go with the DVD.

history.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Blu-ray much better than DVD version
history.text: My comments only concern the DVD versus Blu-ray issue. I have an older version of the DVD (Stanley Kubrick Collection, white box) and the Blu-ray version. My experience has been that DVDs mastered in high definition look identical to the Blu-ray version (either on a Blu-Ray player or an upconvert DVD player). In this case, the Blu-ray version is MUCH better. The differece is much like the samples used in stores to show the difference betwee regular and high definition--you know, grainy on one side sharp on the other. Although my DVD version is widescreen, it is old enough that my TV thinks the width is full screen. With the 2.2:1 aspect ratio, this makes it look like a postage stamp in the middle of the screen. Even worse, the transer is very poor. A good comparison is with the sunrise scene at the start of the movie. On the DVD, the colors run together and the clouds are indiscinct, even at the small size. On the Blu-ray version, which fills the screen, the colors are fantastic and the detail in the clouds is great. That would be enough to recommend the Blu-ray version, but it also has several special features, including a commentary track, a documentary, four featurettes, artwork, photo gallery, and an audio interview with Kubrick. The only extra on the DVD version is an interview with Arthur C. Clarke. In this case, the Blu-ray is definitely worth it, even if you already have the DVD version.

history.title: A Clockwork Orange [Blu-ray]
history.text: My comments only concern the DVD versus Blu-ray issue. I have an older version of the DVD (Stanley Kubrick Collection, white box) and the Blu-ray version. My experience has been that DVDs mastered in high definition look identical to the Blu-ray version (either on a Blu-ray player or an upconvert DVD player). In this case, the Blu-ray version is MUCH better. The differece is much like the samples used in stores to show the difference betwee regular and high definition--you know, grainy on one side sharp on the other. Although my DVD version is widescreen, it is old enough that it is not enhanced for widescreen TVs. As a result, it is only as wide as a full screen version and with widescreen aspect ratio it looks like a postage stamp in the middle of the screen. Even worse, the transer is not very good. In general, the colors are brighter and the details sharper on the Blu-ray version. This may not matter as much as it does for 2001 (where, again, the Blu-ray version is much better), but the better picture using the whole screen is so much better! That would be enough to recommend the Blu-ray version, but it also has several special features, including a commentary track, a documentary, and a featurette. The only extra on the DVD version is the trailer (which I don't even consider a special feature anymore). In this case, the Blu-ray is definitely worth it, even if you already have the DVD version.

history.title: CHAMPION ACROBATS OF CHINA: Flying Lotus
history.text: I am always amazed at the things acrobats can do in terms of balance and flexibility and the acts on this DVD are no exception. The program runs only 40 minutes and includes six routines by female acrobats. The six include: plate spinning (multiple performers), kicking bowls (while on a unicycle), balancing on benches (stacked nearly 30 feet high), flying plates (basically just catching them with some comic relief thrown in), stunt cycling (multiple performers), balancing on a stationary bicycle, and Pagoda of Bowls (balancing bowls while performing with amazing flexibility). All the performances are accompanied by English narration/commentary. Although the performances are very good, the production values hurt the presentation. The DVD is copyright 2008, but the material is copyright 1992 and some of the comments give the impression that the performances might have been filmed in the early 1980s (and look like something from the 1970s). Not bad, mind you, but they do have a dated look and some of the editing is less than smooth. Overall I thought this disc worth the price, but those who aren't already fans of Chinese acrobatics might enjoy it less due to the quality of the production.

history.title: Yellowstone: Battle for Life [Blu-ray]
history.text: I'm writing this before the Blu-Ray is released, but I happened to catch this program on Animal Planet yesterday and was very pleased with it. The program contains the usual stunning scenery and animal video you would expect from this type of program. The basic theme of the program is to follow how various animals survive in Yellowstone throughout the year. I missed the first part of the program, but I believe it starts with summer and then flows through the seasons to summer again. There seemed to be particular emphasis on the Yellowstone winter given its harshness. (Of particular interest was the fact that winter is when wolves are at their strongest as their prey animals become weaker.) The program also spent some time explaining how the geology of Yellowstone affected its climate. They explained, for example, how it can snow in Yellowstone any month of the year. (Something I found interesting given that I got caught in a snowstorm there in late July one year!) The TV airing was 120 minutes, less commercials. The Blu-Ray description indicates a run time of 150 minutes. That might include extra features or it might mean additional footage not included for broadcast. Either way, and given the price, this seems to be a good deal. UPDATE: The program actually includes three 50-minute episodes (Winter, Summer, Autumn). I must have missed part of the Autumn as part of that episode has a bit more of the man versus nature theme than the other episodes. The episodes are presented in widescreen (and look great). Three short features on "The People of Yellowstone" are included.

history.title: Wallace & Gromit: The Complete Collection [Blu-ray]
history.text: I'll leave for others to talk about Wallace & Gromit themselves and focus here on the Blu-Ray offering. There are four "movies" included on the disc. Each of these is about 30 minutes long. The first three were previously included on the DVD, "Wallace & Gromit in Three Amazing Adventures." Also included on the BR disc are the features that were on the DVD. New to this release are the short "A Matter of Loaf and Death," the episode of Shaun the Sheep, "Off the Baa!," and at least one of the short features. A game demo is also included, but you need a BR player on your computer (PCs only) to play it. The first two features are full frame and the second two are widescreen. The features all look great on BR (though I don't know if they were remastered for this release). The disc doesn't include "The Curse of the Were-Rabbit," so one might quibble that it doesn't include all the W&G material, but it does include all the shorts (including the two that won Academy Awards). Overall, I thought this was a very good presentation for a very funny duo and well worth the price.

history.title: Top Fighter 2: Deadly China Dolls [DVD]
history.review_title: Interesting, but likely for fans only
history.text: Top Fighter 2 is essentially a documentary highlighting several of the women who broke ground or rose to fame in martial arts movies. I was only familiar with two of the women highlighted (Michelle Yeoh and Cynthia Rothrock) so I welcomed the opportunity to learn more about other female stars. There are plenty of action clips and short interviews with the stars. Unfortunately most of the interviews are not as informative as they could have been. A bigger problem, however, is that the quality of most of the clips is rather poor. In part this may be due to the use of clips from older movies that may not have been remastered, but the entire movie seems to have just been copied to DVD from a VHS tape. Aside from these problems I did enjoy the interviews and clips. Documentaries such as this give me an opportunity to learn of other movies that I might like. Unfortunately, although the narrator often noted the name of a particular film, the names were not put on screen at the start of particular clips. This made it difficult to know whether the clip was from the film mentioned or another that showcased the actress's skills. I think casual fans will find less value to this film than fans who are already familiar with the featured actresses and who would enjoy a highlight reel of their fight scenes.

history.review_title: An excellent look into the Iowa Caucuses
history.text: I found this to be an excellent peek into the details of the Iowa Caucuses. Many outside of Iowa really don't understand the process and what's required of the candidates--and that includes many of the national reporters who come to Iowa to cover the process. Those outside of Iowa often only see the candidates on TV or in large venues, but those in Iowa (and New Hampshire) get to see them up close and often in small venues such as local diners and even people's living rooms. In these venues the candidates have to interact with average people. They can't just give scripted, impersonal speeches. They must answer real questions that are on the minds of voters, including strange questions on obscure topics. The ability of the candidate to handle such situations is an important part of him or her understanding what issues are on the minds of "regular" people. The film follows the various Republican candidates (President Obama was unopposed in the Democrat's caucuses that year). That may turn some off right away, but it shouldn't. As I said to someone at the time I first saw the film, both Democrats and Republicans will find things to laugh at in the movie, though not likely the same things. Also, aside from the candidates, the caucus activities are the same regardless of political party. This film helps one to understand an important part of the presidential nomination process and I strongly recommend it.

history.title: The Giant Behemoth VHS
history.review_title: "And The Lord said, Behold now.....The Behemoth"
history.text: One of the last in "the giant monster from sea" genre of the 50's "Gorgo" officially being the last in 1961 before the japan imports came in. The story concerns that of a mysterious radioactive force that not only seems to wash up mountains of dead fish on england shore but infects one man's hand & kills another. An investigation by Marine biologist uncovers the radioactivity's source from that of the titled creature, a huge brontasaur left over from "King Kong" who proceeds to stomp London and burn all within it's radioactive range. Another of my favorites from the creature feature era This film was probably Willis O'Brien's swan song as his creation stirs the streets of Merry old in all it's glory one would tend to think on life had come full circle from his brontosaur of the "Lost world" made some 30 years earlier,Unlike "The beast from 20,000 fathoms" This film takes on a darker tone focusing more on the science and the aftermath of radiation (showing burn victims, fishing market slumps etc)& in addition a memorable score. Gene Evans in one of his few goodguy roles accompanies Andre Morell as Prof. Bigford Special effect range from a wonderful entrance by the creature on the docks to the quickie shot of the beast's wooden head on a makeshift raft. You wouldn't see this sequence on warner bros.vhs version of The giant behemoth though. I wouldn't believe that the company responsible for so many classics like "The African Queen" & "The Roaring 20's" would be too cheap to use a 90 min tape. The picture quality is great but I hope the dvd will be more complete "Thy own right hand shall save thee"

history.title: The Land Unknown
history.text: I can't imagine Universal's logic for rereleasing 1950's sci-fi films that were already released as a boxset in a single no frills dvd disc except that they're strapped for cash. and for a near twenty dollar a pop tag you can just break down get the boxset. I have broke down and bought a few Vault titles like "The Black shield" just to see what an $20 Vault disc experience was like and frankly "eh" For a bare bones non remastered version of vintage film that reloops itself after that end credit. I think Universal,Fox,MGM,Columbia and WB should"Archive" "Vault"and "Choice collection" their way to lowering their price tags to more affordable standard hence increasing sales I know I would buy more titles. does this mean that these titles are going to be release again in the blue-ray format as well?......Ga ching!

history.title: Those Redheads From Seattle
history.text: Nice old fashioned entertainment from a bygone where the movie industry had to fight for the public attention over television with gimmicks that you Couldn't get on television namely 3-D. This family friendly story finds Agnes Moorhead and four attractive daughters heading from San Francisco to The frozen Yukon to find where abouts of her husband who may have met with foul play due to his unpopular newspaper articles.memorable songs Are few in this entry (with exceptional stand out 'chicka boom") but we do get the lovely Rhonda Flemming who looks stunning as always along with Gene Barry and Teresa Brewster. Fairly good print (some footage darkens in spots) Kino is on a role with their vintage film releases hopefully these Will lead to other Paramount 3D thrills like "Jivaro" and "Sangaree" includes Rhonda Flemming interview at a 2006 public showing +Original Trailer

history.title: Ben (Bluray/DVD Combo) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: "Ben....and his army of rats are on the way!"
history.text: Ben the granddaddy of rat army movies and a direct sequel to Willard is alive and well and officially on disc. I missed seeing this in theatres by a hot Minute in 1970's because of my young age but my older brother came back with tales of how epic it was. Now that I see it again decades later it still holds up but plays more like a "Made for television" movie with a bit of bite (excuse the pun) but still all the fun that you expect from a film from this Genre. Picking up at the last few minutes of "Willard" this sequel has the title protagonist befriending a young boy with heart problems while causing Assorted mayhem in supermarkets etc searching for food for his ever growing army now living in the city's sewer system. Although this movie will be Remembered mostly for its downbeat ending song "Ben" sang memorably by Michael Jackson for me the meat of the film will always be the work of the rat wranglers who with limited optical effects truly delivered in the scenes where hordes of these rodents were needed to make the film a staple. Hard to believe the studio could lose original negative to a widely distributed 1970's film.( I'm betting some dumpster diver has a print somewhere.) Fairly decent print just the same (1.85 ratio) comes with trailers both theatrical & Television, plus interview with kid star of the film lee Montgomery

history.title: Journey to the Far Side of the Sun [Blu-ray]
history.text: Gerry Anderson comes thru again with another production that reaches out of the box with this his only "live" theatrical release after his success of 'Thunderbirds are go" and "Thunderbird 6" This movie centers the euro space programs race to investigate a strange planet similar to earth directly Behind the sun with nevertheless strange and disastrous results. This film plays like a twilight zone episode but with that late sixties charm that only The brits could pull off. Fans of the Andersons will love Derrick Medding magnificent miniature work and set detail along with a beautiful a film score By Berry Gray. With a capable cast including Roy Thinnes,Ian Hendry and Herbert Lom. My one complaint is why didn't Universal release this movie In its original letterbox format of 2.33:1 instead of 1:85? I still have my old copy (pictured) which I believe was transferred from laserdisc and kind of heightens the true scope of the film.

history.title: Drive-In Delirium: Hi Def Hysteria - 60s & 70s Savagery
history.text: Wow! First of all I'm a trailer freak. So you had me at "drive in" 'Drive in Deliruim 60s & 70's' is nothing short of a great purchase for everyone who loves a good coming attractions collection. Close to 200 trailers are provided here on a single disc divided by part 1: "the 60s" and part 2: "the 70's" Menu allows you to watch either part separate or as one massive trailer show complete with retro preshow introductions / ending and intermission. Titles included are a sorted selection of genres (mostly horror, sci-fi, action adventure) many things seen before but lots of surprises but the quality In picture and sound are the main attractions here as the high def ups the game and makes many of these trailers look as clear as the actual films Themselves! My only gripe is that menu won't let you find your favorite trailer unless you go thru entire list which is thankfully printed on the inside Insert. That aside umbrella entertainment is definitely a name to look for in quality and production

history.title: Drive in Delirium: Maximum 80s Over Drive
history.text: Then you'll love this complication of 80's themed coming attractions from "the rad" era only 156 trailers on this volume which is less then The that of 60's / 70's Volume but excellent quality in picture and sound never the less. Once again the single dvd separates the titles into two parts the first part Titled "the crackdown" (covers mostly revenge / action-adventure / sci-fi) while part 2: "Stalk n' slash" pretty much describes itself. Also as with vol 1. You can watch the two parts separately or as an entire show complete with ads, intermission etc. from the main animated menu you can tell that the folks at Umbrella entertainment actually care about their product and the collectors of this obscure genre. like the films that they represent the trailer Is an art form in itself and needs disc like this to preserve (and enhance) it.

history.title: Gorgo (blu-Ray)
history.text: One of U.K. Few entries into the giant rampaging rascal genre (Konga ,The giant behemoth) but a great production never the less telling the story of the capture of Large sea monster found off the coast of an Ireland fishing village and brought back to jolly old London and put on display in a circus. It's captures are unaware that this creature is the offspring of a 200 ft adult creature that will prove itself unstoppable in it's search the young one. Works in all directions for those who like their monster mayhem with a little heart in center. The blueray release definitely a step up from earlier dvd (I'm not talking Spartacus restoration or anything but it is Brighter clearer and eliminates most the annoying browns and greens). My only complaint Is I was disappointed that the film was released 1:78 instead of the print widescreen of 2;35 but still lot of great extras including a new documentary which covers everything you could ever want to know about the film production and is worth the price of the disc by itself!

history.title: The Thing [Collector's Edition] [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: ‘Definitive Classic.... made even more so by shout factory”
history.text: If you haven’t seen this film by now your officially one of the 2% as this one is required viewing for any horror/sci-fi cult film fan. I had the privilege of seeing this in the theatre on its original unappreciated 80s release (and I was also one of first to purchase it on VHS before films were economically priced) that being said its comes a long way to be finally giving the respect it deserves in this blueray release. The folks at shout factory once show their love toward the collector by not only providing smooth pristine picture and sound but packed this two disc edition with all the bells and whistles Of the previous sets plus more features including a new and much awaited cast interviews by “the men of outpost 31” and of course the only thing more horrifying than “the thing” itself is watching a really bad copy of the heavily butchered television aired version which is also included as a well And reminds you how grateful you really should be for remastered editions

history.title: Trailer Trauma 4: Television Trauma
history.text: Okay to the collectors of these trailer compliation dvds like myself you know the drill. For those just joining in this entry is a first as it concentrates on The television versions of those same grindhouse movie trailers. These trailers are short ringing in between 20 seconds to a minute per preview and In most cases since they were aired on prime time television edited to pull the viewer in without revealing too much offensive material as shown in the full film versions. (There’s a few exceptions that I’m presuming were aired in the wee midnight hours) these trailers are all square screen ratio at 1;33.1 as seen on pre-flat screen televisions but your current flat screen tv should be able to pop up image to fill screen with ‘pic size’ button located on your remote. As for the trailers themselves the single disc contains 264 of them. they’re clean, sharp and loud (with the exception of a few toward the end that may have been pulled from a video source) these trailers are mostly 70’s and 80’s with a occasional 60’s Black & white and are mostly Random covering sci-fi / horror, slasher, prison women, high school hijinks, blaxploitation, chopsocky nature amuck..the gangs all here. There are a lot of rarities as well at least to me (fly me, Zaat, Solomon’s king, folks at red wolf inn, stud brown, Love life of a cop) to name a few. There’s also a entertaining commentary by grindhouse pros Chris poggiali and Michael gingold to speed you thru the shinanagans..”at a flagship theatre near you”

history.title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars (Two-Disc Special Edition)
history.review_title: Pilot film for the animated Clone Wars series
history.text: As a fan of Star Wars overall, I've read many of the books from the now non Canon expanded universe, and the prequel films were ok, the main trilogy remains a classic and I kinda dig the new Rebels series and was amazed by Force Awakens. The Clone Wars series was something I watched occasionally but never had time to watch it. I have the box set now and making my way through it. This film sets the stage for the series and while it's not perfect it's still very entertaining and it holds your attention with the action as well as the character dynamics and politics. Not bad for a cartoon show for kids. I love how this film and each episode of the series kicks things off with a montage of images with a voiceover bringing people up to speed on what is going on, much like a wartime newsreel. You are invested in the characters even though in the back of your mind you already know that things are going to end badly for a lot of them given what we know from Episode 3 and so on. The sight of seeing our heroes onboard star destroyers with an army of storm troopers is a bit weird a tad unsettling. But it is still awesome seeing Anakin in his element as someone who clearly cares about the lives of his men and about living on the edge in the heat of battle. The relationship he forges with Ahsoka is a bit prickly at first, the disrespectful little know it all snot that is teamed up with a brash and somewhat overconfident warrior. Its a great pilot film, and as a lead in to the rest of the series it sets up what the series is all about... Showcasing the wider scope of the war and the various people involved. Its an epic space opera, which is exactly what star wars is meant to be but this series takes that concept and pushes it further. Highly recommended

history.title: Ben 10: The Complete Season 1
history.review_title: No ordinary kid, no ordinary cartoon
history.text: I came across this series when it was on Netflix and was hooked. As a fan of cartoons, I was blown away by how well crafted this series is, along with it's subsequent sequel series Alien Force and Ultimate Alien (not counting omniverse or the reboot series). This series is very well written and constructed overall, as it taps into that essential element for young kids that dream of being superheroes, here is ben Tennyson getting that chance largely by accident. I love how as the series progresses the mythology of the universe od this series builds and builds as we learn more about Grandpa max and his time as a 'plumber'. Ans also see Ben still be your typical 10 year old but also learn about doing the right thing and about his responsibilities, even when he isn't constantly bickering with his cousin Gwen. That was one thingbthatnalways kinda bothered me watching many of these epusodes back to back , hearing the sniping and bickering and gwen calling ben a dweeb a doofus a dork all the freaking time got really tiresome. Im grateful that by the time Alien Force was made they made the characters older and pretty much had the antagonism between Ben and Gwen replaced with genuine familial affection. Anyway, I loved how the people taht made this aeries were clearly comic book fans cu with the omnitrix and its abilities, it reminds one of tue Dial h for Hero, where the special dial allows the user to transform into different types of heroes for different types of situations. I especially love how Ben tries to go for one alien hero and ends up with a different one by mistake, which is funny but also Aids in teaching ben to think on his feet and make use of powers and abilities at his disposal. Also the fact that the omnitrix is green and even the symbol on the chest of each alien, and even the corps of plumbers being galactic defenders.and policemen, brings to mind the green lantern Corps. This first season sets the tone and also sets things in motion rather nicely.

history.title: RuPaul's Drag Race: Season 4
history.text: I have enjoyed this series largely because I am a fan of drag, even though I am a straight man, I have nothing but respect and admiration for these very talented men who express their artistry, creativity and femininity through the art and illusion of drag. I've watched each season since the beginning and have been pretty impressed by the challenges, the drama, the hilarity, the ingenuity, and so on demonstrated by each queen. Season four is without a doubt where this show began to hit its stride by demonstrating true diversity in the world of drag, particularly with who eventually won this season. The challenges this season were pretty awesome and showcased some great branching out, building upon what they were doing in previous seasons. One thing that is usually still very cringe inducing for me is watching the preparations for the filmed acting challenges, cuz you do have a tendency to see the whole warts and all elements with them either screwing up their lines, complaining about how they screwed up, or showcasing that they just really suck at acting. Now, there are moments that occur in this season that are infamous and still remain in Drag pop culture, like the first appearance of Sharon Needles, in all her gothic glory! I loved Sharon Needles even before the season started, and the fact that she went on to win the season was fantastic. Sharon Needles is essentially the Marlyn Manson of Drag, a true entertainer that is more than just a spooky and shocking exterior, and holds within the heart, soul, and brains of a fearless and inventive performer that takes calculated risks as opposed to some that take risks without putting any thought behind those risks. Her rivalry with Phi Phi O'Hara is a major source of drama (but not only source) this season, as Phi Phi showcased right off the bat when she entered the competition a sense of arrogance and superiority (overshadowed only by Willam's supreme arrogance), and looked down on Sharon, and even underestimated her abilities and more often than not made no secret about how she felt about what she thought were Sharon's limitations as a Drag Queen (even though Phi Phi at times showed herself to be just as weak in certain areas, like her performance as Gaga in Snatch Game or that ridiculously annoying Sarah Palinesque caricature during the Frock the Vote challenge). And that whole 'Party City' insult she threw at Sharon, it pretty much exemplified Phi Phi's whole attitude during that season, plus how quick Phi Phi is to tell people to kiss her ass, telling people to 'shut up before I smack you', showcases how thin skinned she can be. I have been told and have seen evidence that Phi Phi is actually really nice, and as a child suffered from a great deal of abuse for being gay, and she has my sympathy, but being abused as a child is not an excuse for having a stank ass attitude to all and sundry, and treating nearly all and sundry with derision and contempt (I'm still not convinced her giving Chad Michaels her phonecall home during 'Sntach Game' wasn't just a ploy). Willam was just.... irritating. Willam is a professional actor but brought that Hollywood arrogance into the show, and it showed. Willam was certainly clever in certain areas, but her arrogance and snobbish superiority complex was not cool. So it's no surprise that her sorry ass got disqualified when she decided to break the rules (which apparently involved having her significant other visit her at the undisclosed location where the queens are sequestered to during their time on the show). Milan, I did no care for Milan. Milan was just not interesting and had a tendency to make some really dumb mistakes, and also had a tendency to not take direction and not really listen to criticism. Milan is a fierce performer, no doubt, but not one that I would go out of my way to see. Kenya Michaels, I have a soft spot for her, given that is Puerto Rican, just like me. She did have some flaws in her abilities as a performer, but I was still sad when she was eliminated. Latrice Royale, large and in charge, chunky yet funky. Latrice definitely elevated the presence for plus sized queens on the show, and was definitely one of my picks for top three, since most plus sized queens tended not to last beyond the middle of the season. I love Latrice, she was awesome. Chad Michaels, phenomenal! Its Cher Bitch! Jiggly Caliente, sweet but insecure. LaShawn Beyond.... unremarkable. Madame LaQueer.... okay. The Princess... sweet and zen, and possessing of untapped potential that I was sad that I didn't get to see. Dida Ritz... okay. Very sweet, and very likeable, but at times was just... there Alissa Summers... wonderful queen from Florida (where I live), and definitely gone too soon. Sharon's win showcased that Drag Superstars come in all shapes, sizes, personalities, and abilities, and Sharon's win also opened the door for other unconventional queens to enter the competition in the seasons that came afterwards (for better or worse).

history.title: RuPaul's Drag Race: Season 3 (4 Discs)
history.text: I remember when this season came out, and this season is still pretty solid for me because of the various queens, the various challenges and whatnot. Many of the queens that were on this season were awesome but there were some I wasn't too keen on, but that's usually the same with each season. The surprise twist at the start of the season with the return of Shangela was pretty neat, but it also did cause an imbalance in the competition and allow me to explain. I am all for giving people a second chance, and Shangela was someone that got eliminated in season two in the first episode cuz she was unpolished, but had a ton of personality that was just begging to be showcased. And it was cool to see that play out as the season progressed, but I did not like that having Shangela back meant that someone else had to be sacrificed, and that unfortunate person was Venus Dee Lite. Venus was someone I was looking forward to seeing compete, and if Shangela had not been brought back, my feeling was that the bottom two that would Lip Sync would've been Venus and Phoenix, and I think that Venus would've been saved and Phoenix sent home. The fact that Phoenix got sent home in the next challenge just showcased how unimpressive she was as a performer while Venus a lot more to show and would've grown in the competition. but Shangela once again was unpolished, but Ru did not want to send her home in the first episode AGAIN, and so Venus was sacrificed just so Shangela could have her chance to compete. I've got nothing against Shangela, and I'm sure she has learned a lot over the years since season three, but here is something I just have to know. In the time Shangela got eliminated from season two to the time she came back for season three, couldn't that bitch have taken a damn sewing class!?! Because another aspect of Shangela highlighted in season three was that she couldn't sew and needed help from others in order to make stuff. The acting and the creative challenges were awesome as they always are, the Christmas challenge, the money dress challenge, the Sci Fi movie challenge, the Snatch Game, the Totally Leotarded episode with Susan Powter, the QNN challenge with Debbie Matanopolous, and I could go on and on. it was just a fun season. Now, the queens featured this season: Alexis Mateo, one of my favorites cuz Alexis is from Florida, like me, and I was already familiar with Alexis' style of drag and performing and knew she would be a top contender, and the fact that she was in the top three was great, but I was sad Alexis didn't win. Carmen Carrerra, she could be kinda polarizing, because on the one hand she was absolutely gorgeous and was creative, and was clearly smart, but also seemed a bit vain and kinda clueless. Manila Luzon, one of my personal favorites, gorgeous, witty, funny and just an absolute delight, was also a favorite of mine to win. Raja... FAN-TAS-TIC!! Smart, beautiful, charming, witty, and talented, and I was very happy when Raja won. Mariah.... she was ok. Very pretty, but also kinda vain and a shallow. Phoenix.... blah. Yara Sofia... another favorite cuz she's a fellow Puerto Rican. Gorgeous and hilarious, struggled a bit cuz of the language barrier, but fought through it, although that breakdown she had on the runway during the lip sync on the money challenge broke my heart. still, her Amy Winehouse was freaking hilarious. Mimi Imfurst... tried waaaaaaay too hard to be the Pandora Boxx of season three. she was clearly talented as a performer and a comic queen, but seemed to go so far over the top that she ended up crashing into a satellite and burning up in the atmosphere. and what she did during her lip sync did her no favors. Venus... lovely and talented and gone way too soon. Shangela,.. hilarious, charming, and talented, and utilized her second chance well. Delta Work... lovely and talented, but seemed very standoffish at times, especially when she joined up with the 'Heathers' clique, which I will talk about soon. Stacey Lane Matthews.... such a lovely southern creature, and many is the time I just wanted to hug her. she has talent, but also self-esteem and confidence issues. Her Monique on Snatch Game was amazing. India Farrah... was just kinda... there. Now, the Heathers Clique.... much as I love the queens who were part of the clique individually, it created this unnecessary schoolyard mentality and this ridiculous class system of an 'us vs. them', that we are so much better because we are prettier than everyone else. What really annoys the crap outta me about the Heathers thing was the fact that all of these queens probably at one time or another have suffered from being humiliated and ridiculed and were probably bullied and abused for being gay, and yet here these bitches go excluding themselves and being all snobby and snooty in their mentality, essentially making the other bitches feel humiliated and ridiculed, essentially doing to others what they have experienced in their lives, and for what?!? And another thing that annoyed me was Delta's comment in that stand up comedy challenge, she got eliminated in the lip sync cuz she lip synced against Manila and Manila won. Delta's parting words were like 'I'm glad that I lost to a Heather rather than one of the Boogers', what the hell!?!? and then her bullcrap explanation during the reunited episode was exactly that, bullcrap, and Delta didn't even apologize to Stacy or any of the other queens, it was Raja that had the balls to try and make amends. despite these gripes, its still a wonderful season that I really loved.

history.title: Angie Tribeca: Season 1
history.review_title: It's kinda like Sledhge Hammer! But more on par with Police Squad for the modern era.
history.text: I came across this show on TBS and was very intrigued. I have been more or less disappointed with most comedic programs that tend to think that awkwardness is a reasonable substitute for humor. This show brings humor back to where it belongs, at least in my opinion. Everything is done very straight laced and po-faced, and the humor is essentially derived from the fact that there are all of these insane things going around and none of the characters comment on it, they just go with it or just accept it as normal. The Carrels I think are more than likely influenced by the likes of the Zucker brothers, who created the Airplane films, Police Squad, the Naked Gun films, and so on. Its all there in the dialogue as well as in the multitude of sight gags on display. Its utterly brilliant, and long may it continue.

I really enjoyed watching the show, but then when season three came around they did so really unthinkable things... New York, the seat of government for this post apocalyptic world is destroyed... the human family that was part and parcel of the town of Defiance... ALL WIPED OUT!! I couldn't bring myself to continue watching because so much of what I liked was changing far too drastically to the point of being completely unrecognizable. I mean, i can understand sometimes when people kill off certain characters in order to emphasize the dangers of certain circumstances, but it didn't feel this way at all, it just felt like a cheap ploy to be shocking and daring in the short term without really thinking about how this would shape out in the long term, because if all you do is make things bleak without any sign of hope, it doesn't make your show daring and envelope pushing, it makes it downbeat and depressing because you suck out all of the things that made it enjoyable and entertaining in the first place. its a real shame cuz i really enjoyed watching this show considering there aren't that many shows with such a lived in universe filled with alien species interacting with humans and each other like its no big deal. any TV show that deals with living in space nowadays have ALL HUMAN CASTS! The current hit on SyFy now is Expanse, and there aren't any aliens in it! its a great show, but it just seems to continue to emphasize this ridiculous notion of humanity essentially being the center of the universe, because if they go out there and all they find is a whole lot of nothing and humanity spreads out and encounters no other life aside from themselves, it makes the universe rather lonely if there is nothing else out there aside from us. sorry, i got off track, but i really enjoyed Defiance in the first two seasons, but by season three i couldn't bring myself to even watch the rest of the season despite it having some really interesting story arcs because i couldn't get over the bleakness and the downbeat nature set down by the season three premiere.

history.review_title: Enjoyably entertaining mashup of sci fi action, police procedural and domestic family dramedy
history.text: The 1990s was definitely filled to bursting with a wide variety of genre programs sold into first run syndication, some obviously having longer runs than others like Star Trek and it's numerous spinoffs, and of course the absolutely epic Babylon 5. Space Precinct was one of those shows that unfortunately slipped through the cracks and ended up lasting only a season, largely due to poor scheduling (many US markets scheduled this show either really late at night, 12 am or 1am, or really early in the morning, like 4 or 5am, on weekends). It's a shame because this is a quite enjoyable and entertaining. Although the storytelling does try to walk a fine line between gritty, hard edged sci fi action with the police action and lighthearted humor usually brought about by the domestic stuff centering on the Brogan family, or Lt. Haldane's numerous attempts to woo Lt. Castle (which invariably fail until... well you'll see). This is probably what got station affiliates.confused, as they were uncertain how it should be marketed, cuz it was at times too hard edged for kids, but also a little too silly at times for adults. This series was the last production by genre icon Garry Anderson to feature live actors mixed with his impressive model work often associated with his puppet programs. I rather enjoyed the mix of sci fi action, police procedural and domestic stuff, it gave things a rather unique flavor and an identity all of its own. While the series did not have a proper first episode to set up the show and it's plot, the series has a good lived in universe with some nice background details sprinkled throughout with dialogue that feels natural. Credit where it's due, the actors involved do a great job with the material. And while Ted Shackleford will probably be forever known as the lesser Ewing brother, Gary Ewing, from.Dallas/Knots Landing, he does quite well as Patrick Brogan, an NYPD cop now serving and protecting tarns and creons, and dealing with humans and other species of ne'er do wells, all while coming to grips with having uprooted his family from Earth to live out amongst the final frontier. Haven't seen Rob Youngblood in much else aside from this, but his character of Haldane is awesome, cocksure swagger, wisecracking, a ladies man, and always flirting with Castle (and always getting shot down... most of the time). Simone Bendix I haven't seen in much else either, but she is great as Jane Castle. Beautiful, smart, tough, but compassionate. Her banter with Haldane is awesome, and over the course of this series, you do see her softening towards him until it reaches it's natural conclusion in the series finale Deathwatch. Things seem fairly pedestrian in its pacing, and I swear there is one scene of the female lead speaking with a former astronaut, played by Ian McCulloch, about a previous failed mission that reminded me of a similar dialogue exchange featured in an episode from Space: 1999 called 'Dragon's Domain'. What suffers the most has to be the fact that the film front loaded its best stuff at the beginning of the film, with the eggs exploding causing chest bursting for some reason. Other than that, the film itself is fairly unremarkable. As a knock off of Aliens, it's also not worth your time as there are many other films that are better executed.

history.title: Super 8 (Two-Disc Blu-ray/DVD Combo)
history.text: Great movie. Can't say enough positive about it. If you were a super 8 filmmaker in the late 70's this movie is for u !!! Tons of great movie moments. This film is almost autobiographical about my teenage days in the 1970's. Masterfully accomplished film with J.J. Abrams using the town of Weirton, WV as a character - even down to the caretakers storage building in the actual cemetery where Joe visits his mother's gravesite - which is a real treat to find if you re-visit the filming locations. I found the spot - but they used a fake movie prop tombstone and placed it between existing and real headstones. I had a blast on a few occasions visiting Weirton and finding almost all of the movie locations from the film. This film captures the pure essence of the late 1970's - it's almost magical - and you can certainly tell that Larry Fong and J.J. Abrams were childhood friends and young filmmakers as you notice the passion they put into the film. Most of the actual 70's props came from the basements of businesses that once were during this period. If you were a kid of the 70's, you won't want to miss this film.
